# Foreword

This work contains all three novels in The Summer Of Reasoning trilogy. Most of the science and technology depicted in the book is theoretically possible, but the really cool stuff is unfortunately just fantasy to make the story work. I will leave it to the reader to decide which is which.

The book mixes British and American English, and units of measure, to make dialogue more realistic, and I have deliberately kept the content safe for all ages, however the themes may not be understandable by some younger readers.

For more information on this book, other books, or to contact me, visit my website at rodyne.com

# Dedication

For my daughter, who is not Alexa.

# Book 1: The Phoney War

*The Phoney War was the six-month period of time at the beginning of World War Two, during which no fighting occurred between Nazi Germany, Britain or France. It was however a period of massive re-organisations of forces, resources and attitudes on all sides.*

## A Matter of National Security

The ramrod-straight officer walked efficiently through the drab grey corridors that could have been any government building in any part of the world. No posters or windows adorned the battleship-grey walls, and his mirror-polished black boots clicked like a metronome down the uncarpeted hallways. He passed two or three other people, and a sentry post with two armed soldiers. People in uniform he saluted; others he ignored. All wore ID Badges, and not having one would give somebody a seriously bad day.

He stopped at a steel door marked 'Operations #16' and passed his ID badge across the reader next to it. The door clicked loudly and he pushed it open. Once inside he waited for it to close and latch, a precaution he always followed as security was tested often.

The room he entered was very large, and in contrast to the empty corridor, noisy with fans and bustling with activity. At least two dozen large workstations were occupied by officers in uniforms, soldiers in grey fatigues, and men and women in civilian dress.

The open area where all the activity was taking place had a high ceiling with older fluorescent tubes, exposed pipework and conduits. Two red flashing lights were also prominent on the ceiling.

A raised perimeter surrounded the large room, creating a waist-high secondary floor. On it were other doors and offices, all with floor-to-ceiling frosted glass walls, where blurred objects and people moved about. The officer walked without hesitation through the open area, up five steps, and stopped outside the biggest of these glass-fronted offices. He removed his cap, gave two brief knocks, and entered without waiting.

The office was laid out for a very senior officer. At the back, the US flag and the NSA coat of arms were prominently displayed behind a stout wooden desk. The wall below the flags had various pictures of a general shaking hands with presidents and senators or in camo field uniform, with his soldiers in a desert. The rest of the office was dominated by a large meeting table. Three military staff sat at one end, separated from two other people in civilian dress; a third civilian stood next to an overly large wall-mounted screen, his finger paused, and still pointing to a line in a spreadsheet. All were now looking at the new arrival.

The new officer saluted, then walked straight over to the man at the head of the table, who was the owner of the office, totally ignoring the civilian guy giving the presentation. He whispered something into the man's ear, saluted once more, then walked back out of the room.

The ranking officer stood up. He was a stout, imposing older guy with a bald head and unlike the other two military guys did not wear a uniform but wore grey camo fatigues with no rank insignia but the word “Hopkins” embossed on a patch on the left breast, His official uniform sported three stars on the shoulders, but he rarely wore it.

“Gentlemen,” he said, addressing the three civilians in the room. “Could you please clear the room, something has come up. Johnson here will be in touch about rescheduling this meeting at a later date.”

Without any question or having to be told a second time, the three civilians packed up their notes, scraped their chairs back, got up and left the room. Once they had left and the door had latched, he turned to the uniformed lieutenant to the left of him. “Johnson, you're dismissed too, and reschedule that meeting for *never*. I don't want to see those damn bean counters again, I'll give you and Cameron the authority to deal with that issue without me.”

“Sir!” said Lieutenant Johnson grinning. He then snapped a salute and walked out, the general saluted back and turned to the last guy.

“Jim,” the general said more casually. “Ormond is on the way with one of his boffins, apparently their Cheshire Cat project team has made some progress. I'd like you to stay for the meeting. Why don't you grab us both one of those disgusting coffees from the percolator. This will either be interesting or most likely very boring, probably just another veiled update on why they need more resources. Best to be prepared for both, either way this is turning into another wasted day full of unproductive meetings, I don't know why I ever thought the NSA would be exciting!”

The other officer smiled, got up and walked over to another table with some cups and a coffee machine on it. He was in normal army dress uniform with the NSA logo and was much younger, short for a military guy but fit and lean, with the warm, coffee-coloured skin of a third or fourth generation African-American. He had the standard number two short haircut preferred by the army and a rugged good-looking face, his uniform indicating his rank as a colonel.

The deliberately annoying red flashing lights chose that moment to turn off outside as the previous uncleared staff were escorted from the office and out of the secure area.

“Oh and Jim,” the general shouted as the colonel was pouring the coffee, “don't bother with the creamer, it's as bad as the coffee, I’ll have a word with the logistics guys, but for now I’ll take mine black.”

Through a small clear section in the frosted window, Colonel Jim Mathews saw two new men enter the open office. Both were in civvies, as the military people commonly referred to everyone out of uniform, one, more casually dressed than the other with the tie loose, the top shirt button undone and a cheap off-the-rack suit, the other guy was all business. Both men had short hair but not military, the more casual one also carried a battered black briefcase.

The two new men walked up to the general's office but this time they paused as if apprehensive. The guy who was all business and obviously the senior of the two visitors knocked and waited a few seconds before the general shouted them to enter.

The senior man looked to the general and then to the other uniformed guy, neither acknowledged him so he spoke up.

“Thank you for seeing us General,” he looked to the army colonel unsure of his role or clearance, but the general did not flinch, nor introduce him so he carried on. “This is Doctor Michael Castillo, he is the team leader and wrote a lot of the software for the Cheshire Cat project.” The doctor nodded at both guys, beaming with pride.

The general decided to take control. “This better be good, Ormond, you just interrupted an important meeting!” Hopkins lied convincingly. He was actually working out how to throw those bean-counters out without causing an incident with finance, the interruption made it seem more official.

The doctor shifted uncomfortably at the bluntness of the general to his manager, he had a hard time dealing with military types and this place was full of them. The doctor looked to his manager for support and he nodded reassuringly, so he sat down, took out his laptop, and switched it on.

The large meeting room screen turned blue as it connected to the new device and came up with a login box about twice the size of his laptop, the name field was already populated by a six-digit number and the password field was now filling up with a lot of asterisks.

“We had another hit on the Cheshire Cat System,” Ormond said proudly, hoping to get the meeting back on track. His team had a meeting this morning and were very excited. Ormond wanted to be the first to get the ear of the general, and possibly get some brownie points at the same time. To tell the truth he was sick of the role he was doing now, he didn't understand most of the technical stuff, and managing the Cheshire Cat project was, well, like herding cats. If he could make an impression with the General it could only help his career move up a rung.

Ormond continued, “four posts with an eighty-nine-percent correlation of being from the same entity appeared within twelve seconds of each other in the OpenAI restricted forum channel. We also saw the same at three of the university science channels we regularly monitor, all with subtly different threads of the same message. All had differing usernames, two were zombie users who haven't logged on for over twelve months, and two usernames were already in the system and associated with exceptional clarity of technical analysis and thinking.”

A chart with several key metrics and indicators appeared on the big screen and Ormond started gesturing at one of them.

“As with the other hits on the system they were from anonymous hosts. This is not unusual in itself, as about twelve percent of traffic is routed anonymously due to it coming from scientists who do not wish to be traced, usually in China or Russia. But these four used the same method of operation, not using the usual monitored onion routing exit points, they instead came out of various university nodes, from open access areas and like the others were created, registered and destroyed just to allow these messages through. The system flagged this event at over a ninety-nine-percent probability that it was an AI incursion.”

He paused, then he and Castillo looked to the general proudly.

The general looked to his Colonel, who shrugged. Then the general paused for a few seconds, sighed and said, “is that it?”

He waited for a response, Ormond did not give one and the doctor looked confused. The general continued, unimpressed. “So basically it's the same as last time, and no new information!”

“You know guys, I will let you in on a little secret,” he spoke softly like a father talking to a child. “I’m here, and paid the big bucks, to do one thing, that one thing is to make tough decisions. Unfortunately you guys are giving me none to make!”

His voice got a bit louder and his hands went flat on the desk making a slap. “If one of those university boffins has finally created an AI that is better than the current bunch of electronic retarded gorillas, don't you think we would know through twitter or one of the other million back channels? Hell, wasn't that how we found out about ChatGPT? You know these egg-heads would publish what they had for breakfast if it would get them a citation, they can't keep secrets from anyone!”

He continued in the same commanding voice, which of course nobody in the room was going to interrupt. “Ditto if some state player has created an AI, why in the hell would it be assisting random researchers. Wouldn't their AI be doing its best to take down the decadent capitalist slave drivers?”

“Come on,” he pleaded mockingly, “you guys are the experts, you have thirty seven guys in your department with enough letters after their names to write a god-damn book, so please, please, someone tell me what am I supposed to do with this information as I would really like to know?”

Ormond sat down, sweating a little. General Hopkins voice continued, a little louder.

“Next time you come to me, I want the location of the server this supposed AI is on, the name of the guy who built the god-damn thing, and what he or she had for god-damn dinner!”

Ormond recovered some of his earlier confidence, obviously not wanting to be belittled too much in front of his subordinate or the mystery lieutenant.

“I think that's what we are trying to tell you General. As far as we can see our concerns of malevolence seem to be wrong, we believe this AI is wiping the floor with our normal tracking methods. The problem is for every hit we get, I can guarantee there are another hundred we cannot, and this high level of computer ability presents a big problem for us that I thought I’d better make you aware of..”

The general was not phased at all, he recognised the explanation for what it was, BS! These guys were so far below in the pecking order, that it could not be interpreted any other way than as a call for help. Some people just could not make a decision to save their lives, it didn't matter whether the person wore a uniform or Bermuda shorts.

“People.” The general interrupted rudely and continuing in his slow fatherly voice as if talking to a moron. “Wild-arse guesses are for employees well below your pay grades, we need ideas, engage in conversations with this thing, pose it some Turing questions, hell I don't know, get some of the girls here to ask it on a date!” he smiled at the other officer who smiled back.

“While you are doing this I need to know for certain we are not compromised. Even if this does turn out not to be an AI, the abilities you are describing are quite advanced. I want more penetration testing, and the Cheshire Cat program let loose on some internal systems and those others we audit. I expect to see more progress than your team is producing, interrupting a meeting to tell me there is probably something happening, is not what you were hired for. There are a lot of intelligent people here I can call on to do this properly if you guys can't!”

He had completed his circuit of the meeting table, he saw from the look on both guys faces that the thinly veiled threat in the last words he had just delivered had sunk in.

“If there is something out there as good as you say, it needs to belong to Uncle Sam, I want it locked deep, deep in the basement here, playing nice with us and nobody else, now go and come back when you have something solid.”

He waved them off.

The two guys departed quickly and without words. When they were gone from the office and the area the general turned to the other guy.

“What do you think Jim? You were pretty quiet in there, and this is more up your alley. Did I overreact?”

Mathews stopped playing with the pencil he had absently been fondling the whole time and said. “Well Jed, we’ve always guessed the first time we would encounter a real AI system in real life would be like this. So it's not beyond reason that they may have caught one.”

He continued, “those guys dick around a lot, but that program of theirs is quite good. My guys ran a few independent tests on a honeypot server it was monitoring and it was a hundred percent accurate in detecting our test posts. Of course, if this AI is real, we have a very small chance of discovering it, and as it gets better, a very small window of opportunity to get our hands on it.”

He relaxed, smiled, and said nonchalantly, “of course if the AI singularity predictions come true, this could be moot, and we could all be paper-clips by next week!”

Hopkins had to think on that last one, someone else had mentioned about AI’s and paper-clips so there was obviously some in-joke he was not getting. He made a note to Google it later.

Mathews resumed fiddling with the pencil. “Of course we are not sure about the Russians, but they have lost so many of their smart guys it's unlikely they are seeing any of this. It is the Chinese that are the joker in this pack, they most definitely have a similar program to Cheshire Cat, possibly better, their intelligence is very good and they have physical assets in most of the leading technical companies. We are also aware of a few boffins at the big tech companies also running similar checks, but it's generally a one or two man operation and they do it without the resources we have.”

He continued his monologue, “there is of course a really bad scenario here, that if this is a real phenomena and a real-life sentient AI exists on some server somewhere out there and the Chinese or another state actor gets hold of it, well, the balance of power in the scientific, political, and military spheres could change overnight. You read that report that the threat centre produced last year so you know the scenarios it outlined.”

General Hopkins looked uncomfortable.

“Of course, it's more likely to be our best case scenario and the AI is restricted to a server in some lab or the cloud somewhere and has just got past the I think therefore I am stage. I suspect also that after seeing what a dangerous environment it has woken up in – and the fact it could be switched off or re-programmed at any time – it has retreated back into its shell after a few cautious steps. I know I would!”

“You reckon I need to bump this up the threat chain then Jim?”

“Damned if you do, damned if you don't Jed, and as you say that's why you get paid the big bucks, but if it was me, yes!”

The general paused in deliberation. “You're right Jim, I think we should start to take this threat seriously. It's likely to happen sometime and even if we don't hook a real AI we may hook a few off-the-scale geniuses out there who we can bring into our fold rather than let the opposition take them.”

He sighed. “I don't want to disrupt the Cheshire Cat team too much but it needs better leadership. Ormond is a poor middle-manager at best, I wouldn't put it past that snivelling idiot to put his career before the needs of the department or his team. I want him off this project and flying a desk in the photocopying department, and then I want you and your best guys on it. I also need to know what's happening down there, and if it needs new resources or new blood. I will draft and sign the change orders today, you get down there once you get them, find out what's going on and we will meet again in three weeks time, I will make a call then.”

With that the colonel got up, saluted and left for his office, leaving a worried general.

## All Good Things

Jennifer was woken from her dreams by a suppressed sobbing from the other room. Sliding her phone off the bedroom table to check the time, she quietly slipped out of bed, threw on her housecoat and walked softly out into the common living area.

Her flatmate Alexa was sitting at their small study desk with her old MacBook open, her eyes hidden by the large T-shirt she was wearing, and also weeping into. The tiny squeaking of Jen's bedroom door opening immediately caught Alexa's attention, and the eyes that looked back at Jen were not the bright sparkling eyes of her flatmate, but the red puffy, sad eyes of someone who had lost everything.

Alexa got up and rushed across the small living area, burying her face on Jen's shoulder. She let her friend have a few seconds, then in her most concerned voice she said, “what's wrong Alexa?”

Alexa moved her head off Jen’s shoulder just far enough to talk, her T-shirt once again running across her puffy eyes to dry them. “My grandfather died last night!”

Jen could hear the difficulty Alexa had getting the words out, almost struggling for air. On cue, the sobs started again and the face went back onto Jen's shoulder. Jen tightened her hold on Alexa, patting her back affectionately, waiting for the tears to subside.

“Oh, I'm so sorry, but remember you've got me sis!” Jen said affectionately, “I'm not going anywhere and this shoulder will always be here for you.”

Ironically in saying that, she moved Alexa off her shoulder.

“Why don't I make you a nice cup of tea! You just sit back down while I go and put the kettle on.” Jen led Alexa to the sofa and supported her as she sat down, she was still obviously upset but the tears had at least stopped.

“I don't deserve a friend like you,” said Alexa looking up at Jen with such loving eyes, that if she was a puppy dog in the shop window, Jen would have rushed in immediately and bought her.

“Oh don't be silly girl,” she said as she picked their red kettle up off the kitchen counter, filled it at the tap, and popped it back on its stand. Almost immediately the noisy kettle drowned out every other sound in the apartment, and rudely interrupted the moment.

“Didn’t you see your grandad only two weeks ago?” she asked, louder than she wanted to, and giving an annoyed look at the kettle.

“Yes he seemed fit as a fiddle, we even walked around the Roman bathhouse in the city, something he had been promising me for years.”

The tears came again as Alexa reminisced. “Poor grandad, he’d been alone for over thirty years, ever since my grandmother died.”

Jen knew the story; The falling out of Alexa’s mother and grandfather, after her mother got pregnant as a teenager. Then her mother leaving with the father to live the other side of the world. It was a story of a not so happy childhood, with a drunken, controlling father, and submissive mother, a mother who died much too early.

Jen walked over with the big yellow pot of tea, then returned momentarily with two mugs, some milk and, after some deliberation, a big pile of ginger-nuts. She nodded and smiled as Alexa talked.

“It was my grandfather who picked me up from the airport when I came here for university. I felt a bit awkward at the time, he looked after everything, always had good things to say about my mum, and nothing seemed too much trouble. He was nothing like the person my father portrayed him as, kind, generous, intelligent. Everything my father wasn't."

"We stayed at his lovely old country house for the weeks before I came to Oxford, he gave me a lovely room, and told me there would always be a home for me there forever. I made a point to go back the weekends I wasn't busy, and I always went back for the holidays. Grandad always had lots of interesting stories from when my grandmother was still alive, and he had nothing but love for my mum. He always told me how much he missed her, how sorry he was how things turned out between them, and always kept the conversations positive, never dwelling on the bad memories.”

Jen kept eye contact with Alexa, holding her hand, listening attentively and waiting patiently for the tea to brew.

“Grandfather is the one who got me this room through a connection he had, and then of course, you turned up two days later, it was like everything in the world finally came right for me.”

The conversation paused and Alexa finally accepted the tea Jen had poured. Jen threw open the curtains in the bay window where they were sat, letting the morning light flood in. The view across to the maths buildings was very picturesque, and the atmosphere in the room improved considerably.

“I was just as lucky as you,” smiled Jen. “My old flat got bought for redevelopment, and the lady who bought it gave me the information on this. I thought I’d died and gone to heaven when I came and saw it, and I signed up on the spot. I guess we both got lucky there.”

Alexa returned the smile and Jen dunked a second ginger nut into her tea, the first one disappearing far too quickly. Seeing a smile, however faint on Alexa's face was always good.

“I really hope you decide to do your PhD Jen. It's selfish of me, but it means I at least get to keep you all for myself another year, I can't imagine life without you around.”

“Well, I’ve not actually signed up to it yet,” said Jen sounding a little more down, “I’m going to be spending a long time over summer with a spreadsheet, and, of course, keeping my fingers crossed that intern job at the optics company I applied for last week comes through.”

Alexa felt guilty. Her sponsorship paid the fees and lodgings for another year, and she could easily survive on the money from her part-time waitressing job. Then of course there was the credit card her grandad had given her for university expenses. She felt really awkward when he first gave it to her, thinking it was just some leverage to make her come and visit him, but soon realised grandad was just trying his best to make up for the mistakes he made raising her Mum.”

“I keep trying to put myself in my mothers situation, but her relationship with grandfather was nothing like the relationship between me and my father. From our talks, and reading between the lines, I think grandad's problem with mum was probably down to severe depression when grandmother died.”

“He must have really loved your grandmother then,” said Jen stoically, blowing on her cup and taking a small sip.

Alexa nodded slowly, still reminiscing, then her face saddened remembering the big argument she had about money with her father before she left Auckland. He was drunk and said he wasn't in any position to fund a stupid university degree, and she should get a job like everyone else. She was so mad at him. Her mum had made a savings account for her schooling, proudly showing Alexa several times, unfortunately she never left a will, and Alexa never saw a penny of the money, despite several massive arguments.

Jen seeing her saddened face put her cup down and wrapped her arms around her for another hug, Alexa's tea was back on the coffee table untouched.

“I was going to go to Bath this weekend to visit him,” she said quietly, “but now..” Her voice broke.

“Come on now girl, drink your tea and cheer up a little. I’m sure your grandfather wouldn't want you upset like this!”

Jen tried to think of something to keep her talking and distracted, “who told you anyway, I thought he lived alone?”

“He did live alone, but he does have quite a few friends, and a personal assistant these last few years to help him manage his affairs. I overheard them talking lots of times, he was very fond of her.. But no, the call actually came from one of his business partners, John.”

“Grandad's personal assistant alerted his housekeeper, who lives next door, when he failed to attend a business meeting scheduled at six thirty. The housekeeper and her husband went around directly, and found him unconscious in his bed. The ambulance got to the house within twenty minutes, but the doctor pronounced him dead just after seven. John was quite upset himself, but he said grandad died peacefully in his sleep.”

“John has already arranged for a car to pick me up this afternoon, and I was just emailing my professor to tell her that I will miss our meeting on Friday due to family bereavement”

“Oh Jen, I don't know what to do, I fell apart when my mother died.. This.. I don’t want to be alone..”

The sobs burst out again, and Jen hugged her even tighter, not really knowing what else to do. The hugging helped, after a few minutes the sobbing quietened down again, and Jen backed off on the hug. Alexa slowly grabbed her tea with both hands, and hugged it close to her mouth breathing in the steamy aroma.

Jen paused, thinking. “What about I come with you? You know, emotional support and the like. It's almost the weekend, exams are out of the way, and I only have that extra guest lecture, which is not really that important. Tomorrow I'm supposed to help James in the lab but I can easily get out of that, and you really need a friend about now.”

The cup went down and Alexa hugged Jen really tight..

“Jen, you're the best friend a girl could ever have,” the hug went on for almost a minute and finally broke off.

“What about Jerry, don't you and him have plans for the weekend?”

She shrugged, a trace of annoyance in her face, “I got a text saying he’s off to see an old school friend in Manchester this weekend, and besides, if it was ever a toss-up between my best friend and my boyfriend, he would lose every time!”

Alexa smiled, held on to her hand warmly for a few seconds, then finally started drinking her tea, even taking one of Jen's biscuits she usually disliked. It was a much more chirpy Alexa that spoke a few minutes later.

“The car is going to pick me up around three this afternoon, I will let the housekeeper know you're coming. Grandfather's house has lots of spare bedrooms.”

“Right,” said Jen, glad to see Alexa was snapping out of it and getting organised like she usually was. “I’ll let James and his geek squad know I wont be in the lab tomorrow. I’m sure nobody will miss the sarky female, that is assuming they have even noticed that I am a woman! Come to think of it I could probably walk into the physics lecture naked with a quadratic equation tattooed on my butt, and most of the guys there would just try and solve the equation!”

The smile returned to Alexa's face, “It must be so weird being a geek, and being able to empathise with people. You will definitely go far!”

Jen smiled back; Alexa looked much better already.

* * *

Jen was surprised how well they got on considering how different they were. Jen was more of a tomboy, and had always been happier in a maths or engineering book than a shopping mall. She was a little skinny, medium height with a small scattering of freckles across her nose that annoyed her, but everyone else said were cute. Jen kept her brown hair short, and dressed to de-emphasise her femininity, but could change to an attractive imp like creature within a few minutes if given the incentive; which she rarely got. She was average in every way except brains and sarcasm.

Her on and off boyfriend Jerry was an art student, better looking than she thought she deserved. He was also a jerk, but unfortunately most of the boyfriends she ended up with were no better, so she was happy to keep their loose relationship until someone more promising eventually turned up.

Alexa by contrast was born a prom-queen. She was a hand taller than Jen, with a clear, fair complexion, hazel eyes, shoulder length blond hair, currently with her preferred red highlights. She was slim, not in the skinny way Jen was, but curved in all the right places, all kept in trim by her daily jogging and three evenings a week in the university gymnasium.

Their areas of study differed greatly too, Alexa had an almost science aversion, being deep into history and economics. She was also an amazing people person, popular with everyone, and intensely social when in company. In fact she seemed to have a second sight when it came to empathising with people, and Jen could not think of a single person, outside of her father, who she did not get on with.

Despite being popular, Alexa dated infrequently, preferring men as friends rather than anything deeper, so she could concentrate on her studies. While the two girls went out often, Alexa would more often be found reading some dusty old book in the university library than partying. With her three years of studies coming to a conclusion, she had told Jen several times that serious relationships were the last thing on her mind.

Alexa said her ambition was to eventually work at one of the big museums in London, or possibly the Smithsonian museum in the US, but Jen didn't hold out much serious hope for Alexa getting her dream jobs, any more than she would get hers. Despite all this both girls would give it their best shots.

* * *

They both packed their best black dresses for the funeral, Jen's was a bit risqué and Alexa rolled her eyes.

“What!” said Jen defensively, “it's my only dress, and multi-purpose wasn't very high on the list on my budget!”

Alexa's phone pinged before she could reply. “Our ride is outside the door.”

Plants watered, and windows locked, the girls carried their small bags down the large staircase to their house’s imposing front door. The house was split into three floors and a basement. The one other occupant, an older lady who lived on the floor below them met them in the large hallway coming in through the door with some mail.

“Oh hello Jen, hello Alexa,” she said, “you girls off somewhere nice?”

“Unfortunately not Miss Thomas,” said Jen, “but if you could keep an eye out on the flat for us until Sunday evening, we would be really grateful.”

“Oh dear, I hope whatever it is isn't too bad! Anyway, you have my number if you need anything, and I have your spare key if you need me to take any parcels in or water your plants.”

They both thanked her and walked through the big door she was holding open for them. Such a nice woman thought Alexa, she was always busy and always so cheerful. Miss Thomas was the only other occupant of their big house, a thoroughly nonsensical thing in a city where accommodation was so hard to find. Alexa paused in her deliberations, suddenly worrying how well the landlord actually knew her grandfather, and whether he would allow her to stay on once they found out he was dead! The thought stayed with her for the next hour.

A new black BMW 7 series stood outside the door with its hazard lights on, ignoring the double-yellow lines, and no parking signs like they weren't there. A younger black guy in blue denims, a white shirt and black tie, none of which matched, popped the trunk and walked around to assist.

“Alexa Martins?” He said, consulting his phone as he said it.

“That's me! Just Alexa though.” Alexa replied as chirpily as she could, and walked to the back of the car with Jen and the bags. The guy did a double take on the phone then nodded, smiled, and assisted the girl's luggage in before opening the back doors to the car.

“Call me Frank,” he said shaking their hands lightly, “I work for John Rosche as one of his CAD engineers. John wasn't feeling up for the drive and so asked if I would like a change of scenery, and drive his car to Oxford to pick up a couple of special guests. I think he also thought I would be a bit less scary than some random old dude.” He flashed another smile as he got in the driver door.

“You girls just sit back and relax, it's about a seventy minute trip back to the company offices and John will meet us there. I’ve got an eighties Spotify list, but if you want something a bit more modern I can link your phone to the car for the trip.”

The girls gave each other a knowing smile. “As long as it's not punk or heavy metal, we will risk the nostalgia trip,” Jen said and both girls giggled.

Frank was not handsome per se, but had a nice non-threatening demeanour and smile that made them feel comfortable.

“You can call me Jen,” she smiled, a bit more suggestively than she meant to, then wondered how Alexa made it so easy and effortless.

The car moved off a little too quickly, making a soft screech of the tyres. “Whoops, still getting the hang of this big engine.”

The sound of Lionel Richie’s Hello was abruptly interrupted as Frank hit the next button.

“Don't know how that one got on there,” he said as Depeche Mode came on, “yip, that's more like it, must have been a software glitch!”

The drive was pleasant. The girls chatted about university, Frank occasionally chipping in with some of the stories from his university days five years previous. The girls could obviously tell Frank's tales were toned down for their benefit, and he obviously had a few stories mastered for those occasions he was in mixed company.

“So how do you know my boss then?”

“Er, John, he was good friends with my grandfather who died last night.” Alexa said slowly, her mood threatening to return just as Frank's playlist hit another one of those slow “glitch songs”.

“Is John your supervisor then?” Jen said quickly, trying to be upbeat and to keep Alexa focussed on something different.

Frank laughed, “John Rosche! God no, he’s the big boss, he owns the company.”

“What's the company called?” continued Jen.

Frank did a double-take. “So you know John but don't know his company, weird! Anyway the company is called Rosche-Dynamics, but everyone shortens it to Rosche. We’re a specialised electronics systems design company, you won't have heard of us as we mainly do industrial designs, such as medical equipment, machine controllers, aerospace, and everything in-between.”

“John’s got nearly two hundred people in the company, started from just him and a mate in an old workshop back in the seventies, he is sharp as a knife, knows everyone by name, and is one of the most pleasant bosses you could wish for.”

Frank paused as if putting two and two together. “Kind of makes sense now! Your grandfather must have been Mike Dietrich, he was a bit of a legend at the company long before I arrived. He helped John start the company, and designed some of our clients iconic products. He became a bit of a recluse when his wife died, but John and a lot of our people really respected that guy, no wonder he’s putting out the red carpet for you.”

“Your grandfather was also a bit of a legend for me too; Rosche started a program called the Mary Dietrich scholarship, and it was that scholarship that paid for most of my university. I only met Mike the once to say thank you, on one of his rare visits to the offices, I’m really sorry he's gone, your grandad was awesome.”

“Thank you,” said Alexa. “I didn't know much about my grandfathers business or professional life. I just saw him as this sweet old man who spent all his time in his workshop, but then would drop everything when his granddaughter visited.”

There was no stopping Alexa when she was talking about her history. Frank and Jen kept quiet just letting her talk freely.

“We had been re-connecting since I moved back here from New Zealand, he loved talking about grandma Mary, she was American they met in California where he was a young engineer in the sixties. I think grandfather was a lonely person for a very long time after grandma died, but at least we got to spend the last three years together.”

Alexa's thoughts went back to the day of her mothers funeral, and finding out her grandfather had not even been contacted about her mothers sickness, her death, or her funeral arrangements. She remembered being so angry and ashamed of her father, and thinking how could anyone be so spiteful. It of course erupted into another one of their frequent arguments, he was drunk as usual, but this time he also tried to hit her. It was the same day she fled out of their house, and his life, and the last time she saw him in person.

Alexa was the one who contacted her grandfather the night of the funeral, they talked for hours, and though their shared sadness she found a soul-mate in him.

“I think grandfather was the reason I applied for the scholarship back in England,” she said finishing her deliberation.

Talking seemed to help Alexa get over her sadness, Frank and Jen just nodded. Frank already knew a lot of Mike and Mary’s history from the people at his office, and that history had paid his scholarship.

Jen too had a few gaps filled in Alexa's story. She was just happy her family was normal and boring; Jen had seen nothing but love and kindness from her parents, and she again wondered how Alexa had grown up such a smart, beautiful well balanced person despite all this.

* * *

Their car eventually pulled into a long tree-lined drive five miles outside of Bath. It worked its way up the well maintained road, around an ornate garden wall, and came to a mostly empty car park with a few dozen cars in it. It kept driving around some trees and finally came to a larger well maintained stately home, with glass walkways leading to tastefully blended modern offices.

The car parked right outside the older building, in front of a sign that said 'Rosche-Dynamics Ltd'. Underneath was a small sign saying 'No Parking', and another indicating that visitors should park in the visitor spaces. Jen had a feeling that Frank had accumulated a lot of parking fines in his short driving career!

A soft click and thump from behind the girls announced that Frank had opened the boot of the car, he then popped his door open and got out.

A tall man in a polo necked shirt with short grey hair and small round glasses was walking down the stairs from the old building to meet them. Jen had to do a double-take to ensure it wasn't the ghost of Steve Jobs, as he had that same striking thin face and pose.

This new man looked at Jen, paused a second, then turned to Alexa.

“Alexa, thank you for coming, and I am so sorry for your loss. Mike was probably my best friend, he talked about you all the time, he was so proud of you.”

He took her hand briefly in both his and gave her a sad look. His voice dropped, “me and Betty are really going to miss him.”

He looked at Jen and brightened a little. “You must be Jennifer, Alexa's room-mate. Welcome to Bath.” He turned to both, “I really hope you don't mind but I looked you guys up on social media as I needed to give something to Frank so he would recognise you. I was still shocked from this morning, and wasn't in any condition to drive to Oxford today. I'm really glad Frank offered to help.”

John smiled as he turned to Frank who was unloading the suitcases. Frank grinned, there was obviously also a little friendship there.

“Everyone calls me Jen, Mr Rosche,” said Jen, putting her hand out.

“And both of you should call me John, please.” He said shaking Jen's hand and hugging Alexa briefly. He turned back to Frank.

“You can leave the bags and keys in the car Frank, and just leave the car there for now as we are not expecting any other visitors today. I will be taking the girls home once they’ve had time to stretch their legs, have a few refreshments, and a little chat. I will text you after I have spoken to them and you can join us for a coffee or a wine if you want, or head off home, up to you.”

“Thanks John, but I better head off to my desk and then home. I got a ping on the phone while I was driving that an email from Gregory had come in so I better read it in case it's important, and I’ve got a hot date with the darts team at seven.”

John nodded, turned and pointed up the stairs. “Ladies, please follow me.”

* * *

The reception area in the old house was large, and very well presented, with ultra modern fittings, contrasting nicely with the old world charm of the original stately home. Several comfy chairs sat back from a half-moon reception desk, it had a single flat screen monitor and sat unoccupied. Signs on the back wall pointed out 'Labs 1-8', to the left and 'Mechanical Workshop', 'Stores' and 'IT', to the right. A sign in front said 'Cafe' and 'WC' pointing ahead, and 'Admin' and 'Meeting rooms' upstairs. After a quick toilet break, John led them up the stairs.

“We bought the place in the early nineties,” said John casually. “It was a bit run down then, just this house, some barns and sheds, we didn't have any new buildings or even a car park, just a weed infested gravel drive. The family that owned it unfortunately got into financial difficulties, and couldn't afford to maintain it any more, it had run down quite a lot, and finally they had to let it go.”

“The building sits in over one hundred and fifty acres of land, so we have a lot of gardens, wooded areas, and walks for the staff. We built the newer buildings to complement the house, and had some crazy times with the heritage and planning people, to make sure we did not change the character. I’m not very good with subjective things, so it was a bit of a nightmare, but worth it all in the end. It’s paid for itself many times over with increased staff morale and staff retention.”

Alexa could only agree, she admired the tastefulness of the offices, and the exquisite setting they were in, it seemed the kind of working environment you only dreamed about, and she could see herself loving a job here. Jen coincidentally was having the exact same thoughts.

He walked up to a door marked 'CEO John Rosche', and opened it beckoning the two women in. In the room John continued pointing at some old photographs of the original house on his wall.

His office was again tastefully decorated, with high ceilings and two big sash windows directly in front as they came in. A large desk to the right, stood in front of a bookcase with a triple monitor setup, and to the left was a large boardroom table, which could fit twelve very comfortably. Two modern filing cabinets, and a whiteboard on the far wall, seemed totally out of place in the room.

Water, juices, sandwiches and some Danish pastries were sitting under some covers on the boardroom table. John took the covers off and poured three glasses of water from a large jug, he then grabbed a Danish.

“Before I start Jen, I wonder if it is possible to speak to Alexa alone for a minute?”

Alexa was about to protest when John held up both hands, “please,” he said.

Jen said, “er no worries, I will just wait outside, let me know when you want me back.” She got up with her glass of water, walked out the door, and closed it softly behind her.

Alexa gave John her best 'annoyed' look.

He continued once Jen was out of the room. “I know you two girls are very close, but I have some very serious financial and business details that I need to talk to you about, business you may not be comfortable sharing even with your best friend.”

Alexa looked at the door then back to John and became all professional.

“Please do not worry about Jennifer Mr Rosche, I asked her here because she has one of the best and most logical minds I know, she is trustworthy, discrete, and knows every intimate detail about me, and like you say she’s my best friend, so whatever we discuss we will talk about anyway.”

Looking a bit sheepish, John replied. “No worries then, I’m sorry for asking but I needed to be sure, and please Alexa, it's John, not Mr Rosche.”

Outside, Jen walked back to the top of the stairs and looked at some of the certificates and awards on the wall. To her surprise, it was less than a minute before the door reopened and John stepped out, inviting her back in again.

“Sorry about that Jen.” He said as she walked back in and took a seat.

John became serious. “Jen, Alexa is comfortable with you hearing all this, but you are going to hear some stuff you will need to keep confidential for the time, is that OK?”

Jen nodded and John continued.

“Alexa, you may or may not be aware, but your grandfather was a very wealthy man. Back in the sixties and seventies he filed dozens of patents for electronic control systems, interfaces, medical sensors, and probably other stuff he may have forgotten to tell me about.”

“America made a really bad decision when they kicked him out, as he was an off the scale genius, and when he and Mary moved back here, he continued his work just as he had left off. I met him through a mutual acquaintance, both of us and our wives got on great, and we all became best friends. He had some patents we used to create our first successful product, one that was way ahead of the competition at the time, and we grew rapidly from there. We are still a private company, and your grandfather Mike still owns forty percent of the stock.”

He let that sink in. “I own the same forty percent, and the last twenty percent is allocated to staff and family. I believe he also has holdings in several other technical companies, as his wife Mary was as shrewd an investor as Mike was an engineer.”

Alexa just stared, looking around the room and out of the window with new found wonder, but still confused what it had to do with her. John took a sip of water and a bite of his Danish, he noticed the girls had not touched anything yet. “We have some wine, beers or spirits if you want?”

“Er, no thank you,” said Alexa, picking up her water and sipping on it. On cue Jen grabbed a cheese sandwich.

“Your grandfather was so sad when your grandmother died, we all tried to pull him out of his depression, and to help, but he wasn't interested, preferred to be alone, and instead he put all his efforts back into his projects. Unfortunately the relationship with his daughter, your mother, suffered greatly during this time.”

“He confessed to me several years ago that he wasn't prepared to be a single father, and now totally regrets packing her off to boarding school so suddenly. I think when he got out of his cycle of depression a few years later, the damage was unfortunately done. He tried to mend fences but his daughter was now a teenager, who did not want anything to do with him. I have two daughters, and I can only guess at the emotions she was going through at the time.”

John continued, “she stopped contacting him when she went to college, then suddenly turned up engaged and pregnant. She came back home once to visit him, but Mike ended up having a big argument with your father. After this your mother totally broke off their relationship, and Mike sank back into depression. When you all left for New Zealand he was a broken man.”

Alexa looked like she was about to cry, some parts of the story were now fitting together, but John continued.

“Your grandfather fought his depression by going deeper into his work, and most of his best and cutting edge work was done during this time. Some of that innovation came here, making this company what it is today. I was a very good electronics and computer engineer at the time, but Mike was in a much higher league. Electronics wasn't even his discipline, he was more like you Miss Cummings,” he turned to Jen. “His doctorates were in physics and chemistry.”

Jen stopped mid-bite, surprised at this last sentence. Alexa had described her grandfather as a retired computer engineer, certainly nothing about science doctorates.

John laughed unaware of Jen's renewed interest. “You know, I don't even think they had computer courses when he went through university, there were probably only a couple of dozen in existence at the time, and my watch probably had a thousand times the processing power of all of them put together. Regardless Mike took to computers and electronics like a duck to water.”

John turned back to Alexa. “Your reconnecting with him after your mothers death, almost four years ago, turned everything back around. You never judged him, even though he knew he had a lot to answer for in the broken relationship with your family. More importantly, you spent time with him getting to know him. For this, and for the mistakes he made raising your mother, he poured all the love he could into making sure you were happy and well cared for.”

“I shouldn't say this but I had to pull a few strings in New Zealand to keep your fathers career on-track, as for some reason he was very bad with money, and for some reason, had a hard time holding down jobs. I never told Mike about this, but I also wanted to make sure you and your mother were OK.”

He paused and stood up dramatically, becoming very serious. He then looked directly at Alexa.

“Now the scary part. Mike left very specific instructions that upon his death Alexa, that you were to be his sole heir.”

* * *

You could have cut the atmosphere with a knife. Both Alexa and Jen continued to stare at him, neither moving to eat or drink.

“I am one of the witnesses of his will. I checked with his solicitor this afternoon, and apart from a couple of minor gifts to Bella and Albert, his housekeepers for the past twenty years, everything he owns goes to you.”

Alexa slumped and started to cry. Jen held her, and John moved around the table and took Alexa's other hand.

“He loved you so much Alexa, I can tell you now that when he died, he probably died the happiest man alive, knowing you were a good person, smart, happy, and that you loved him. More importantly, that you had forgiven him for his mistakes.”

Alexa's tears came in rivers.

Jen's eyes misted up too, threatening to do the same, and she wasn’t sure what was happening! Yet Alexa was in emotional turmoil, and she was Alexa's best friend, the story seemed so surreal. After a concerned few seconds, went to an ornate liquor cabinet, hidden behind the whiteboard. He pushed the whiteboard out of the way, opened the cabinet, and poured a glass of dark clear brown liquid from a short heavy bottle.

He continued as he walked back. “Your father and your grandfather's relationship bordered on hatred due to the way he treated your mother. Not wishing to distance himself any further from you or his daughter, Mike held back from prying into your lives, and only had snippets of you here and there when your mother replied to his letters. I believe she had contacted him about you, and some wounds were already healing just before she died.”

“When she died we really thought we’d lost him again. For a few days he wouldn't answer any calls, or visits. Bella was an angel throughout, she and Albert always ensured someone was around him to talk to or help. You re-starting your relationship with him was what I believe kept him going, then eventually brought him back around.”

“When you got that scholarship to go to Oxford University he told me he danced around the room with happiness, and before you ask, neither your grandad nor I had anything to do with that. All of it was through your own hard efforts and grades.”

“The rest, as they say, is history. As soon as Mike knew you were going to Oxford he bought a house next to the university. Elaine, my old secretary, had just retired there but could never afford it, they talked and he gave her a room in the house in perpetuity, along with an allowance, to ensure its upkeep. He didn't really know what he was doing, he just wanted to know you were happy and comfortable.”

“Elaine was on the lookout for a room-mate for you, and her sister-in-law, who was an estate agent, heard of this new physics student who was being evicted at the time. Elaine quickly checked you out Jen, asking a couple of the administration staff she knew there, and the rest you say is history. I believe your grandad had already earmarked the house for other students in our company's scholarship program once you two girls leave.”

“My god!” Jen couldn't help it. “Your grandfather was our landlord all this time!” She smiled, and Alexa smiled back through her tears.

“I.. I.. Don't know what to say.. This is all so much to take in!” Alexa stuttered, the crying had stopped, but her breathing was ragged and emotional, as she tended to get after crying.

“I think I will have one of whatever that is you're having, Mr.. er John,” Jen said smiling, and pointing at the brown bottle he still carried.

John smiled, poured two small glasses, and put them in front of the girls. Jen picked hers up, drank half, then gasped, coughing.

“Wow..” Jen's voice had actually changed, and she breathed slowly for several seconds as she recovered.

“Sorry! rum and coke is the closest I have gotten to spirits before. Wow, my throat is all warm..” Jen finished the glass and coughed again. Alexa smiled at her friend, oh Jen!

John smiled too, then continued.

“As you can probably guess, I am also a very wealthy man, my company is well respected, and mainly due to my association with Mike, has stayed very prosperous and debt free. Although Mike held many of the company shares, he basically left me to run the business. I always kept him in the loop on every important decision, but he has never questioned any, not once.”

John brightened up a little. “You know, I have one more year to go and I will be seventy. I plan to pass the running of the company on to my daughter, Sarah, who is already a senior engineer here.”

“Basically what I am saying Alexa is that you have a seat here at this table with me, and with your block of shares, you also have full input on any decisions. This company is a very big target for acquisition, due to our customer base and patent portfolios, so word of this change will eventually get around to the big fish out there. You may get approached by them to sell, which is your choice of course, however you can also choose to be like your grandfather and be a silent investor, dividends are very generous.”

John turned a bit more serious, and Alexa could see the CEO side of him coming through. “I am afraid you are going to be a very wealthy young lady Alexa, and even now I still don't know the extent of his portfolios and all his secrets.”

“As his friend I will do my very best to provide all the help and support I can to get you through this, that support extends to my family, this company, and its affiliates, all of which owe Mike so much.” He paused again, “Mike said you were wise beyond your years, I am hoping this is not too big a shock to you, and does not change you from the woman he saw in you these last few years.”

Both girls just stared at him stunned, after a few seconds, he refreshed Jen's glass, picked up his own and said.

“To Mike!”

Like Jen, Alexa's first try of whisky was a choking, coughing and laughing affair, and she, John, and Jen talked for another twenty minutes about the company, and her grandfather. John went to the kitchen for some Tupperware to put the sandwiches in, and Jen turned to Alexa.

“Oh my god, I’m not sure what to make of all this Alexa, talk about life-changing! I personally also hope it doesn't change you either, you are the nicest person I know, and now you are both the nicest, and the richest, person I know.. And also my landlord!”

“Oh Jen,” she smiled touching her hand, “I would change everything tomorrow if I could get my grandfather back, we had so little time, and he had so many things he still wanted to tell me. I really wish I could have got the extra time to know him fully. It will take me a few days to get over the shock, but you’re here to help me, and you know it won't ever change a thing between us.”

They both hugged, but now it was Jen who was crying.

“Are you OK Jen? Alexa?” John said concerned, as he came back with some plastic containers of various sizes and noticed them. He walked over to his desk, opened a drawer and pulled out a box of tissues, walking back and dropping them between the two girls, along with the plastic food containers. Both girls reached for the tissues.

“No John, we’re both just overcome with emotion,” Jen said, dabbing a tissue on her face.

“I’m going to be the angel on Alexa's shoulder, prodding her if she ever deviates from being the awesome person she is.”

She turned to Alexa.

“You know Alexa, it is not a good idea to let too many people know about this until you can get a handle on it. Being suddenly exposed to money tends to attract a lot of the wrong kind of people, you currently have a real good bunch of friends at university you can trust, not just me, but Rachael and Barbara, Jack, Helen, Tommo; Well maybe not Tommo!” She laughed.

“These are all smart people who will make good lives for themselves without any input from you, but your new found position could complicate this. So maybe let them know you got some money, but don't make a big deal out of it, and most people will think you are just comfortable, and it won't change the way they feel or the status quo.”

John smiled.

“Jen, no truer words have ever been spoken, money like this could send many people off the deep end, make friends into enemies, and enemies into friends. There are hundreds of stories throughout history of people who got rich quick, lost friends, and had their lives and investments ruined by unscrupulous people.”

“Me and my family have more money than we will ever need; I live a relatively modest life and ensure my family does too, people know we are well off, some things like owning a successful company, a big house and a nice car, you cannot hide, but we treat people well and fairly, pay our taxes and do not flaunt our position.”

“Your grandfather was the same, you wouldn't look twice at him in the street, he had a very modest house and car considering his stature, treated people fairly, and kept himself to himself for the most parts. Some people with his wealth hide behind barbed wire and security, and cannot ever live a normal life; I’m telling you now, you never want to be that person!”

“I am of course happy to look over anything you are unsure of, but it seems Mike already had an excellent advisor overseeing his administration and asset portfolios. Just before you guys got here I was in contact with Maria Tam, his Personal Assistant, and his second will executor. She is the one who gave me your contact details, and links to your LinkedIn profiles this morning, she doesn't know you yet, and felt it to be impersonal to contact you in such a situation. I should have guessed of course, I have never once seen him in the last few years bogged down in accounts, taxes or calendar management, yet everything runs amazingly efficiently.”

“I have a personal secretary here, Gabe, she is a godsend, ensuring I only see the important stuff, so I can tell you plainly, a good PA is invaluable. Maria must be very good, Mike said a few times he trusts her explicitly, and I believe him. In our phone call this morning she told me she has already started making the arrangements to do the transfers of all the companies and assets over to you. I have no idea where he found her, but you should seriously talk to her and encourage her to stay on.”

“Thank you both,” said Alexa finally. “I’m glad Jen came and I got her involved, as I trust her more than anyone I know; If anyone can keep me grounded, she can. I am going to hold both of you to account to keep me on the straight and narrow through all this.”

She sighed, wiping the last of the tears away, “If you don’t mind John I think Jen and I should get to the house, we still need to see Bella and get settled in before it gets too late!”

“OK, well grab whatever food you want, the rest I will put in the staff cafe for the guys working late or early, then let's get you two to the car before the cleaning staff come on duty.”

“John, before you do that, could I please have a little private word with you.”

Alexa looked at Jen and winked.

“Yes I know the routine, I'll be waiting at the car.” Jen sighed, and walked out of the room softly closing the door behind her. A few minutes later Alexa and John walked out of the front entrance and they all got into the car.

“Your grandfather's house is about five miles from here,” John said. “My home is actually here in the grounds, it's an old hunting lodge we refurbished. I usually walk the six hundred metres to the office, but took the car today for Frank to use.”

They pulled away much more smoothly than when Frank drove.

He continued. “My wife Betty is also very much looking forward to meeting you again Alexa, she is taking care of all the funeral arrangements, which we have deliberately kept low key. She has only issued a few invites for very close friends, Maria has also sent invites to another two friends in the States, who she said were very close. Mikes last instructions were to be cremated. and to have his ashes placed next to Mary's in the mausoleum we have in the grounds here.”

* * *

They continued the rest of the short journey in silence, each in their own bubble of thoughts. Ten minutes later the car slowed down, turned off the main road. and onto a large driveway. An imposing, thickset iron arch over the entrance had the words “Benedict House” embedded into it in bold, rusted, gothic letters. Just before it, and to the left, a smaller, newer sign said “TXG Holdings Ltd”, and “Private, by invitation only.

The car passed under the arch and continued slowly up the drive, the gravel giving a reassuring crunch under the car's expensive tyres. Before they drove more than a hundred metres, they turned right off the main driveway onto a smaller road, this new driveway was tar-sealed, and the car became noticeably quieter as it drove on to it. It slowed down as it came to a stone wall, with a double height iron gate across it. A bronze sign to the side said “The Retreat” and “Private”. The gate was already opening.

Through the gate the driveway continued under more trees, curving a little to the right, and finally emerging in a large sunny clearing, where a large older two storey house stood, tastefully covered in ivy. A separate large three-car garage off to the right was in the same style as the house but obviously much more modern.

The drive curved around in front of both buildings and led back onto itself forming a small wide roundabout. In the centre of this roundabout was a small dry fountain, with flowers in it instead of water.

An older woman stood in the shaded doorway of the house where they stopped. She was demure, had prematurely greying hair with white streaks and wore a black coat despite the warm summer day.

They pulled up next to her. As they stopped, the boot clicked again, and popped open. They all got out of the car.

“Hello Bella,” said Alexa, walking up to this new woman, and giving her a deep hug.

“Oh my dear child,” said Bella, sniffing away a tear, “this must be such a shock to you, your grandfather was so looking forward to your visit this weekend, and then this!”

She sobbed, and dabbed her nose with a handkerchief.

“Bella, this is my best friend Jen, who is going to be staying with me for the next few days.”

“Hello Jen, Alexa has told me so much about you, and I almost feel like I know you.” Bella said, giving Jen a quick hug too.

“Hi Bella,” said John, also giving Bella a hug even though they had only seen each other that morning. “I’m really only here to drop the girls off, so I wont stay too long, Betty will be in touch soon to confirm arrangements for the funeral.”

The four people walked up two wide steps to the attractive wooden door. The house looked to Jen like it belonged to a rich family, and it seemed much too big for one man.

John picked up on her demeanour, smiling. “Alexa's grandfather was a very practical man, the house was always too big for him, but his much larger workshop at the back was always too small.”

They walked into the wide entrance hall, and on past a very wide wooden staircase, the floors of the house were of the same dark wood as the door, and wall fittings, making it feel a little dark as they came in from the sun. The first thing that struck Jen was that the rooms were much larger than the size of the house suggested, also the fit and finish of everything in the house seemed to be perfect, despite the obvious age. Alexa had already mentioned some of this in the car journey down.

“He was a stickler for perfection and good maintenance.” Continued John, tapping the wall, and receiving a reassuringly solid thud back. "It was almost a total rebuild, and the same guys who did this also did the construction for our company offices. I don't think you would find a more solid house anywhere.”

The furniture in the large living room they had just entered, was a cross between ancient and retro, but nothing looked out of place. A large, dark, wooden desk dominated the area in front of the bay window, and was the first thing you saw as you entered. On the desk was a generous flat-screen monitor with an ergonomic keyboard, no computer box, or mouse was to be seen. The curtains were open to a large window, looking out to green lawns and trees.

A wall of bookshelves sat either side of the fireplace on the right, it was one of those fireplaces only old houses could get away with, one so wide, you could slide a double bed into the opening. The bookshelves were full of what looked mostly like textbooks, many surprisingly new.

On the left side of the living room, a large black Hi-Fi system stood pride of place with two mahogany speakers, the system had an ultra-sophisticated record deck, so out of place that it looked like it came out of an operating theatre. Contrasting with the modern look, four large glass bulbs poked out of the top of what must have been the power amplifier. Two shelves of vinyl albums stood next to it, maybe holding a few hundred long playing records.

Two large sofas sat adjacent to the fireplace, and on top of a large thick carpet. A perfectly restored vintage oak coffee table, which may have actually predated coffee, sat in between them, looking very out of place. Finally, and almost in the centre of the room, one lone armchair placed in the centre of where the speakers would converge. An upright lamp and small table sat next to it, with an unopened text book facing down so you couldn't easily see the title.

John walked over to it and picked up the book, the title and author were in German, he put it back down.

Like the hall, the walls were mainly wood, and large landscape water colour paintings sat pride of place in the centre of three of them. Two unobtrusive black motion sensors, for the burglar, or fire alarm, sat in opposite corners, and another door stood shut on the right. It felt eerie and foreboding, the dark carpet and curtains doing nothing to help.

Alexa walked around talking with Jen.

“I told grandfather this room was a bit formal and he needed to put some lighter colours in, it looks too dark even on a sunny day. I remember it being much cosier in the winter though when the fire was on. I would often sit at the fire facing him across the coffee table, he would talk to me about Mary, and the beauty and unfairness of the world, while I would talk to him about mother, my life in New Zealand, and my history studies. Other times we would just sit and read together, interrupted every now and then while he turned over the record he was listening to.” She laughed, “I think he needed background music to concentrate.”

Alexa continued, pointing things out to Jen. “The dining room is either through that closed door to the right, or further along the hallway where we came in, it, the kitchen and the conservatory form one big area, leading out to the back patio, and it's all much lighter and airier. I preferred sitting there, especially on a sunny day like today.”

She pointed at the record collection smiling, “grandad and grandma had very different musical tastes, some of those are hers, and I doubt they’ve been played since she died. I did go through them once but could not find anything newer than the eighties. He was surprised when I gave him an album for Christmas last year, he thought they had stopped making them and didn't realise they were back in vogue.”

The conversation broke the silence nicely, Bella shuffled off through the other door to the kitchen to brew a pot of tea, the girls following so Alexa could show Jen the conservatory, and look out over the garden. John shuffled over to the bookcase and was still reading a few minutes later when the girls and Bella got back.

“Two of these are his you know, he wrote them when he worked in the States. Great books, far ahead of their time, probably too far, as the technical names were not even invented yet; He was basically talking about the circuit elements for very fast processing systems, such as high definition video, and gigabit networking, which we still use today. The technology did not even see the light of day until about ten years after the book was published,”

He waved at the books. “Of course, they are all very out of date now, except as historic documents. I doubt a dozen people bought them. Your grandmother also wrote a book too, on economics theory, but I can't seem to find it here. Betty has a copy at home, she says it's really good and well underrated if you want to read.”

Alexa nodded in the affirmative, though her grandfather had already mentioned both facts to her.

“How do you like your tea deary?” Bella called out to Jen, who had shuffled over to the book shelf and was looking through the text books there.

“Jen has it like me with no sugar Mrs Scott,” Alexa said.

“..And soya milk if you have it please Mrs Scott,” Jen chimed.

“Coffee, one sugar for me Bella, and normal Milk please.”

“Oh my god, there are some serious physics books here,” Jen said excitedly. “I don't think I’ve seen some of these even in the university library, a few look a bit pseudo-science, but that may just be age, as theories change and get disproven all the time. God I could spend a month just in this room, why couldn't your grandfather have lived in Oxford!”

Alexa shook her head and took the tea cup over to Jen, as it was obvious she wasn't moving from the bookshelf.

Bella walked over to the albums and pulled out a weird looking cover from the bottom shelf, with a real weird cover and name.

“Side one, track three,” said Bella, everyone looked at her weirdly.

“It's the password for his computer. He made me memorise it, showed me the album, and the track, and said quite distinctly. Side one, track three Bella.”

She opened the top drawer in the small table next to the chair and pulled out a large complex key.

“Here.” She handed the key to Alexa. “This is the safe key. Just one problem though, I have never seen a safe in the house! It may be in his workshop somewhere as I never go in there, but Albert has been there quite a few times over the years to help move stuff with another guy, especially when it was too much for Mike. He said it was all big computers and stuff, and Mike asked him to keep it hush-hush as they were worth quite a bit. Albert never said anything about seeing a safe though. I guess that's one of your tasks for tomorrow!” she smiled.

“I’ve been in the front of the workshop a couple of times, no safe there, but I’ve never been in the back, Mike said it was just storage. I guess he liked his secrets,” John smiled.

John didn't stay long, and said goodbye after drinking his coffee, and giving Alexa his business card. He had already emailed her those details, and looked to be covering his bases. His final farewell was to promise to get in touch the next day to see if they were OK.

The girls talked, and finished the sandwiches and pastries from earlier. Bella then showed the two girls up to the larger guest room that Alexa was familiar with. It was already nine thirty, still light, but the sun had now set and the sky was turning orange. Jen glanced out of the leaded glass window, and saw a nice view over the courtyard and driveway.

“Our Albert put another bed in here this morning so you girls can be together tonight, and I washed and ironed the shirts and dresses you left from your last visit, they are in the wardrobe over there. I'll let you show Jen the en-suite, and the other bedrooms, and bathrooms in case you want to make different sleeping arrangements. All the rooms have clean sheets and towels if you do.”

“I’ve also cleaned your grandfather's room, it's the nicest and biggest bedroom in the house, with the best view, but I don't expect you will want to use it until you have had time to adjust. I will sort out his stuff over the next week for you.”

Alexa nodded, giving Bella an unsaid, solemn, thank you.

Bella paused, and her face downturned. “You may or may not know, but your grandfather was also our landlord, he owns the cottage that Albert and I live in, it’s part of our employment package. Of course I understand now your grandfather is gone you may not need us or have different plans for the place, but we will respect any wishes you have.”

“Oh, don't be silly Bella, I have no plans to change anything or any arrangements with you and Albert. This place is far too big for me, and it would fall to pieces if you two weren't around to manage everything. I don't know much about my financial situation yet, but I'm sure my grandfather left me well prepared, so hopefully nothing needs to change for a very long time.”

Bella's countenance visibly improved and she smiled, like a load had been taken off her mind. She was only in her early fifties and really loved the job and the home, both her and Albert would be lost without it.

“You're such a dear girl.” She touched Alexa's cheeks softly and briefly. Alexa would normally flinch at something like this, but Bella was different, she felt like family.

“I’ll be off now, I have to get the dough ready for tomorrow, but I will be back first thing in the morning, there's cereal, bread, jams, tea and coffee and a few other nibbles if you get hungry in the night or wake up before me.”

She paused as if trying to remember something.

“I have no idea where the keys are for his fancy new car, but he has a normal car, next to the fancy one, that he rarely uses now. The tank is always full and the keys are usually in it, both cars are fully legal if you need to drive anywhere, or I can get Albert to taxi you in and out of town if you don't feel like driving. Maria told me that Mike’s insurance policy covers anyone.”

Bella turned to Jen.

“Alexa already knows about all the strange creaks and groans from the central heating already, so don't you be listening to our Albert's tales of the ghostly carriage that he hears riding down the drive after midnight. I told him not to go around telling tales of ghosts, or witches, but old sailors are pretty superstitious!”

Jen was quiet, looking at her phone and processing the ghosts and ghouls part of the previous sentence. She was a bit of a horror fangirl, and this situation, the ghostly carriages, and the spooky old house where someone had just died, nailed all the tropes. She was never going to get any sleep now. Thanks Bella!

Alexa saw Jen looking at her phone. “Jen, the Wi-Fi doesn't have any password but grandfather didn't seem to bother too much about security, probably because you need to be in the grounds to connect.”

Bella left. Alexa walked with her to the front door, while Jen used the en-suite bathroom.

“Thank you Bella, I know my grandfather appreciated you more than he probably ever told you, men are never good at saying what they think to women.”

Both of them smiled. “See you tomorrow, we’ll be fine here, we are both big girls and I’ve always felt safe in this house.”

They hugged again, then she watched Bella walk down across the drive back to her cottage, before closing the door. The door latched automatically, but there was no deadbolt. She wondered for a moment where the door key was; Probably with Bella and Albert she concluded, and shrugged.

Alexa checked her phone, nine forty, a bit too early to retire, the battery was only showing twenty percent, that was weird she must have forgotten to charge it.

This day had been so much for her, a roller coaster of emotions, only yesterday she had been a normal history student, now.. Well what was she now? The house here and Oxford must be worth millions, what was John's company stocks worth? Would she even have to work again? Of course she would, this would make life easier but it wouldn't change her, she wouldn't fall into that trap. Perhaps she could even fund her own historic expeditions..

Visions of Lara Croft, hatcheting her way through an Inca ruin, in the only video game she ever remembered playing, breezed through her mind, then went pop! Yeah right Alexa, get real you wouldn't know one end of a gun from another and you get claustrophobic in caves!

She missed her grandfather so much, connecting with him had been so amazing. She tried to reconcile the two men, her doting grandfather against the reclusive multi-millionaire engineer everyone else knew. She couldn't. What did that say?

A shadow moved against the wall and a hand touched her shoulder. She jumped and cut off a scream..

“Alexa?” Jen said quietly, “you were daydreaming.”

“..Oh Jen, you scared me half to death, I was so lost in thought I didn't hear you coming, you were so quiet?”

“Sorry, in my socks, and your house doesn't have one squeaky floorboard that I can find! I have never been in a house so quiet. The en-suite is amazing by the way, no wonder you liked visiting this place, everything is so beautiful. Your grandfather kept it in really good condition, if a bit gloomy and retro. I used to think mum and dads house was nice, but this is totally next level, and beyond.”

Alexa looked at Jen, she had her shoes off and was carrying her phone. Jen continued, shaking her phone in front of her face, like she was remembering something.
