“Oh yes, I was going to ask you if you brought a charger I could borrow. I charged this morning but the phone is about to die. I think the battery is getting worse. Maybe it's time I got it replaced. I was going to message mum and dad to let them know I’ve gone with you for the weekend. Professor Gordon also sent me a message with the link to the guest lecture I missed, so I can look at it tomorrow if it gets quiet.”

She paused, still wiggling the phone, “and if you have that charger I can use!”

Jen tended to beat about the bush rather than get to the point, Alexa didn't mind one bit though.

“I have a charger in the front pocket of my bag, I’ll run upstairs and get it. You go to the fridge and crack open that wine we took from John's office, it's a bit too early to go to bed.” With that she bounded up the stairs two at a time.

Jen shouted after her, “which door is the kitchen?”

“..Oh never mind.”

There were six doors and Jen found the large kitchen/dining room on the third try. She left every light on as she went, as every good horror fan knew that ghosts preferred the dark!

Alexa was back a minute later, dangling a plug and USB cable. She heard Jen rattling some bottles and glasses in the kitchen, what a racket she was making, and what was it with all the lights on? Jen was normally one of those eco-nerds who gave everyone grief if they wasted power, oh well.

She spent a little time turning off a few of the more strategic lamps in the hall, and entered the living room, tutting she then popped all the light switches on, drowning the place in light. The room lost any claim to its previous dull, and dreary, demeanour, and it was now tastefully lit by a large chandelier, some free standing lamps, and several large wall lights. There must also have been an outside light on the switch too, as the outside of the window lit up, highlighting a bit of the lawn, and a few small bushes out to about ten metres. She decided to leave the curtains open as it was quite a pleasant effect. After a bit of playing, turning off various lights and adjusting some dimmers she got it just right.

“Let's drink it here in the living room,” she shouted, opening the connecting door to the kitchen. “I can then also have a look through grandfather's desk to see if he left anything for me. You can have the charger first, I’ll check to see if he has another one somewhere, the desk is as good a place as any to start.”

Walking over to the desk, she sat down on the nice swivel chair, turning it left, then right, looking at the large modern screen and the room from a different angle. Definitely not where she would put a desk, it currently backed at an angle on to the window, she would definitely prefer looking out.

There was a recessed panel, she couldn't see it on first inspection, as it was tastefully mounted sunk in the top front of the desk. On it were two push buttons. She guessed that the computer was inside the desk somewhere, and that the green button was probably to power it on, the yellow one probably turned it off.

She hesitated wondering whether to press the green button, just as Jen came in with the wine and a couple of glasses.

“I couldn't find a corkscrew for John's wine but there was a bottle of Riesling with a twist off top.”

The glasses went on the desk, and Jen proceeded to pour two generous measures. The desk had one drawer in it, Alexa pulled it open, it had a few pens, a wireless mouse and, surprise, a USB C charger!

“Here you go my dear we can both get back online now, thirty minutes should be just enough time to top up my phone and polish off the wine.”

Forgetting about the switches for now, Alexa got up and found a couple of power sockets near the fireplace, and popped the phones on charge. Laying the phones on the big stone hearth she finally sat down on the adjacent sofa. Jen soon joined her, sitting on the same sofa, rather than the opposite one where her grandfather used to sit when they talked.

“This wine is really good,” Jen said once they had both sunk into the sofa.

“It certainly is,” said Alexa, “but we might just have both been ready for a glass after a day like today.”

The two girls chatted away excitedly for about forty minutes, going over various what-if scenarios, mostly giggling, and laughing, as the scenarios got weirder, and as the drink took effect.

“I think I’m ready for bed,” said Jen yawning.

“Me too, it's been a bit of a weird day,” replied Alexa.

The two girls got up, Jen took the nearly empty bottle and returned it to the fridge, she then rinsed the two glasses and left them on the sink top, no doubt to keep Mrs Scott happy. While she was doing this Alexa unplugged both phones, turned the room light off and headed into the hall, meeting Jen as she came out of the kitchen through another door.

“What's with all the doors in this house Alexa? That one there is locked, but I guess it might be another door out of the house or a closet or something.”

Alexa knew one was the toilet, the other a laundry room or something, she also vaguely remembering her grandfather mentioning a utility room. She shrugged and gave Jen her nearly charged phone, then both girls trundled up the stairs.

After spending a few minutes each brushing their teeth, and changing for bed, they snuggled into their separate beds, and said a last few words before going quiet. Sleep came easy to both girls, though Jen being a light sleeper, and hyper-sensitive to being in a spooky old house, found her dreams hijacked by ghosts and witches, causing her to jolt awake a couple of times, before going back to sleep.

After a two AM toilet break, brought on by the wine, Jen got back to her bed and laid there snoozing, thinking pleasant thoughts about how her best friend was going to get through the next few days and months, and looking forward to reading one of those books. Damn this house was too quiet if anything and damn that ghostly moonlight!

There was a strange rumble, and a high pitched noise of something rolling over the tarmac outside the slightly open window, the noise faded, and Jen sneaked over to the window, and carefully peeked behind the thick dark curtains. Nothing there, but something did move a bit in the distance. Damn you Bella! She quietly closed the window and snook back into bed.

She looked at the door, then over at the dark lump covered by a duvet, that was Alexa, but she was a very quiet sleeper thankfully. Jen pulled her duvet up closer like a shield and listened for a few more minutes, Alexa rolled on to her side making a small shuffling noise as the duvet responded, and then all went quiet again.

Jen peered over her duvet and looked again suspiciously at the door. Yes it was her imagination, nothing outside, and no way was she opening the door to check, even though she knew it was unlocked, and no ghost, or monster in the history of, well anything, would be stopped by an unlocked door.

Maybe a mouse or an owl, or something, yes an owl! Old house in the countryside, it had to be! Drowsiness overtook her yet again, and she finally fell into a deep sleep. This time it was dreamless.

Little did the girls realise but a presence was in the house, and it had been observing both of them very closely.

## Ghost In The Machine

It was almost eight o'clock and Jen's phone was ringing. The rising sun fought the dark curtains, and shafts of light were radiating through small gaps into the room. The bed she was in did not have the bedside table next to it like she was used to, and it took her a few rings before she realised she was not in her own bed, and that her blind hand swipes were actually missing her phone by half a metre.

She rolled over as far as she could and stretched out then caught the call on the third ring, she then disappeared with it under the bed sheets, making a few grunts before hanging up, throwing back the sheets, and walking into the en-suite.

Alexa had also woken up with the call. She got out of bed, and like every single person on the planet in this time period, reached for her phone in order to check the time, and any messages. Surprisingly there were none. The wine had made her sleep well past her normal seven AM wake up time, but fortunately today was a lazy day for both of them.

Seeing the en-suite busy, and Jen's bed empty, she opened the curtains fully letting a stream of sunlight into the room, then opened the bedroom door and walked out into the hallway, which was already bright. There was another guest bathroom two doors away, and she headed for that. As she was walking there, she smelt the faint aroma of fresh bread, and heard quiet talking from downstairs. Concentrating on the sound, she recognised the talk-radio program that Mrs Scott usually listened to while working in the kitchen. Smiling, she entered the bathroom.

After a few minutes, she walked back into the bedroom and dragged on some comfortable dungarees she’d brought. Her shirt was wrinkled, but she put it on anyway as it was only Jen and Bella who were going to see her. The toilet flushed and the sink went on in the en-suite, a minute later a zombie in an oversize thin white tee shirt and black knickers showing through, walked out.

“We only had two glasses of that wine each, didn't we?” Jen said in a groggy voice.

“Big ones though,” said Alexa, who Jen thought looked far too good, despite the wrinkled shirt and dungarees,

“You would make a terrible bartender, Jen. Any business would go broke the serving sizes you poured!”

“Ha, Ha!” said Jen with her tongue out.

“Did you sleep well?” said Alexa. “I always sleep like a log here, these beds are much softer than the one back at the apartment, and there must be something about this place that makes me feel safe.”

“Pretty good.” Jen half remembered the noise outside, and walked over to the now open curtains, looking either side, and shrugging her shoulders.

“Is that Mrs Scott downstairs?”

“I hope so, we are not expecting anyone else, and if I’m not mistaken that's fresh bread I smell!”

Pulling on some sweatpants, and a thin red hoodie she sometimes used at the university gym, Jen followed Alexa out of the bedroom, and down the stairs.

“Mrs Scott.. Bella?” shouted Alexa at the foot of the stairs.

She pushed open the kitchen door and the radio volume increased. Bella stood by the sink, with a yellow pinny.

“Oh Sorry Alexa, I was just cleaning up and checking what groceries we had as I’m going out to town to do some shopping this morning.” She walked back to the radio and clicked the button turning it off. “Sorry about that, I really don't know why I listen to it any more, always so depressing. Anyway I hope it didn't wake you.”

Bella didn't wait for an answer. “Since you are both up now, do you want me to make you some breakfast? I baked some fresh bread this morning, and we have some fresh free-range eggs. I could whip up some poached eggs, you always liked that.”

“Yes please Mrs Scott.. I mean Bella,” said Jen, “we are both famished. Oh and you might also be missing most of a bottle of white wine, it was a bit early to go to bed and we stayed up for a nightcap.”

“No worries, your grandmother was a bit of a connoisseur, and there is a large wine cellar she had put in the old basement, which your grandfather said to keep stocked. I don't know too much about wines, but there is an old wine merchant down in Bath who your grandmother used to use, and he always recommends the nicer ones for me. Your grandfather only drank if friends, yourself, or business associates visited, and there are still racks of dusty old wines down in the cellar from when your grandmother was alive.”

“Mr Rosche also dropped me a text this morning to say he has a full day of meetings, but will come around after work if you have any questions. His wife Betty has been making the arrangements with the local vicar for the service to be held in the nearby chapel, it is a very small church, that is why she limited the number of invites. Ms Tam can't get here either, which is a real shame as I would really like to meet her, she is so pleasant on the phone.”

Alexa smiled, changing the topic. “Are you staying with us for breakfast Bella?”

“No, I need to get into town for my book club and then do the shopping.”

“OK, well after breakfast, I will show Jen around and we will do a little exploring of the rest of the house. The workshop and that wine cellar sound intriguing.”

The girls walked into the conservatory, then through the French doors to a paved area with an outside dining table and chairs. It was going to be a warm day again, as there was no wind, and little in the way of clouds.

This early in the morning the table was shaded by the house, and provided a view over a large lawn to a small wooded area. Some raised flower beds, with roses and chrysanthemums, dotted the land up to this wooded area, and several smaller and larger trees stood alone. A small cobbled path wound out to the wooded area, then curved to the left, leading back towards the front of the house and garage.

The air was filled with bird song, and a song thrush hopped in the grass, occasionally stabbing its beak into the ground. Jen got her phone out to take a few pictures of the lovely view, and Alexa sat down at the dining table.

“Oh it's gorgeous, Alexa,” she said. “All the problems of the world seems so distant being here.”

Alexa brought out her phone, she already had a picture of the garden but took one of Jen, taking a picture of the garden, and smiled. She then spent a minute reading an email message from her professor from yesterday, finishing it as Jen sat down, and just as Bella came out with a tea pot and two cups.

“Thank you Bella,” said Alexa.

“Yes thank you Bella,” repeated Jen, as she shuffled back and into the seat next to Alexa, facing out over the lawn.

“I could get used to this Alexa, I never knew anywhere could be so beautiful, just lacking the shirtless, hunky, young, oiled gardener to make the scene complete!”

Alexa nudged Jen enough to nearly spill the soya milk she was pouring. “Since when have you ever bothered about trite things like hunky gardeners? A bit Mills and Boon don't you think?”

“I'm still a girl, and a girl can dream,” she sighed, making Alexa wonder if there might be a well-hidden side to Jen she was not aware of.

They sat talking and drinking, for the next ten minutes, then Bella came out with an even bigger tray loaded with plates, cutlery, butter and condiments. Ten minutes later she returned with two plates, overflowing with eggs, mushrooms and bacon, and the thickest slices of bread Jen had ever seen.

After the second round of thank you’s Bella said, “I'm off to town now, you have Albert and my phone numbers if you need anything. He’s cutting some wood later so don’t panic if you see a big scary man wandering the garden with an Axe.”

Then looking at Jen added, “he’s a real pussy cat!”

After Bella walked off, Alexa looked guiltily at Jens plate. “Err sorry Jen, I forgot to mention you were vegetarian. Here, let me grab that bacon off you, and you can have some of my mushrooms. I’ll make sure to mention it this evening.”

“Don't worry, I've had worse. I went home last Christmas to Roger’s parents in Maidenhead, his mum went to the big effort of making a vegetarian Christmas dinner for me, complete with home-made nut-loaf. However, just before they served it to me, his dad covered it in gravy, which was made with all the fat from the roast! You should have seen Roger’s mum's face, she was livid. I think when we broke up a few months later they both blamed it on the dad. Roger still apologises when he sees me!”

Alexa laughed. Rearranging the bacon and mushrooms on both plates and then dunking her knife in the butter.

After a quiet few minutes of eating and small-talk, Alexa sat back pensively with her mug of tea in her hand, then said a bit more seriously. “Jen, I am having second thoughts about whether I should continue with my history masters degree.”

She paused, seemingly even deeper in thought, then continued. “It's actually been going through my mind for a while, I discussed it with grandfather a few times, he was a great sounding board. History is my passion, it is what I was good at, and what I always wanted to do, but there are no jobs in history. I've been kidding myself about all the great jobs I could do which just are not there, that's why I’ve done minors in business and economics to prepare me for the real world.”

She put her mug down and picked up her knife and fork again, but her attention was not on the food. “I talked to him about what I would do to change the world, and he freely admitted he had the same dreams fifty years ago. We both pinpointed history as a good indicator to how the current world is going, I likened it to the golden years at the end of the Roman and Greek empires when decadence took over from logic and reasoning. I think we are facing the same issues now, where people in power can blatantly lie and get away with it, where the media tows the line, older polluting industries are subsidised, and corruption at all levels is rampant.”

She paused, cutting the bacon slice she had been manoeuvring around the plate. “It was going through my mind again yesterday, when revelation after revelation came out about my grandfather, and my new responsibilities. I think all that time he was preparing me for this moment. Grandfather used to liken money to oil; it could be left in the ground doing nothing, grease the wheels of progress, or pollute the beach of society. Yes I know it was probably some weird German saying translated badly to English, but he is right, and I think what he meant is that it could make a difference.”

“I’m still in shock from yesterday, but I am going to need someone I trust to help me through this, and I would really love for that person to be you. I think what I am trying badly to say Jen, is that I want you to spend the summer here, helping me get through this.”

Her voice faltered a little, and putting down the cutlery she continued. “You’re a big part of my life Jen, I have been a better person for knowing you, and this is not something I can do alone.”

Jen stopped eating and listened to her friend, hearing the emotion in her voice.

“You know Alexa,” she replied, “I was about to beg you to let me stay here for the summer. I don’t think it matters how long I lived for, I would never get the opportunity to be so happy.” She continued a little more downbeat, “but my problem, as you well know, is I’ve got a pretty large student loan, and I really need to work this summer to help clear it..”

Alexa smiled and held up her hand.

“While you were out of the office, John and I had a little conversation. I told him what I just told you, and let him know I was going to ask you to stay with me over summer. He agreed I should not have to face all this alone, and suggested that it would be easiest if I just hired you as a consultant over the summer. He said he would talk to Maria, and his HR person to deal with any paperwork.”

Jen looked a bit confused, so Alexa continued. “Basically what I am saying my dear is that I am offering you that summer job, working with me to try and make sense of all this.” Her hands waved at the house as she emphasised it.

“He said I should just sleep on it, and make the offer whenever the time was right. I think that time is now.”

Jen's eyes were now watering, Alexa immediately took it the wrong way.

“Oh sorry Jen, if I said something to offend..” Alexa never got the sentence out before Jen got out of her chair and ran around the table, wrapping her arms tightly around Alexa.

“These are tears of happiness you silly girl! it’s like I’ve won the lottery with my best friend. Of course I would love to spend summer with you, all of it, and not just for the money, but because I love you, love being with you, and ever since I met you I have had nothing but good luck.. Well except the boys, but hey! Oh God! this is going to be the best summer ever!”

Jen's hug lasted far too long but neither girl cared.

The girls phone's dinged together. “That's weird!” said Alexa, “It's an email from Maria with the draft contract for you and me to talk through,” they read it together there and then.

“Wow, that can't be right can it, the one from the teaching assistant job last year was about thirty pages long, this just says basically: I Jen, will work for Rosche-Dynamics Limited, at a rate of.. Holy crap, that definitely can't be right!” She moved the phone down and looked at Alexa. “That's far too much Alexa, the dean of the university probably earns that.. Oh jeez, it's a joke isn't it?”

“No joke,” she replied seriously, “John said the amount would be normal daily consulting rates his company hires its experts out for. Welcome to the world of big business Jen, that's apparently what consultants get in the real world, I must admit I never thought either of us would see it in our lifetimes!”

Jen wiped her eyes and they read the rest of the page together.

“It doesn't even say what I will do, where I will work, what my hours are..”

“Jen, I really wouldn't worry, there's actually a word for it, it's called nepotism. It's where the managing director gives his crony, or some member of his family a top job to do whatever they bloody-well want. However, in your case, you are going to earn every single penny of it keeping me sane.”

“Oh god girl, what have you done to me? I never cry and this is the second time in as many days I’ve been in tears.” They hugged again.

They talked quietly for a few more minutes finishing their food, then cleaned up, putting the plates, cups and cutlery in the dishwasher, the butter in the fridge, and leaving the rest on a tray for Bella to put away.

“So boss, where are we going to start?” Jen smiled.

Alexa laughed. “OK, well rule number one, if you ever call me boss again you’re fired!”

The laughter was contagious. “I think we better start by showing you the grounds, it's going to be a hot day so best we do this bit first. There are a few areas I haven't been in even though I’ve been coming here for years. I guess I never really thought to ask, and grandfather probably just assumed he had all the time in the world to show me everything.”

“Grandfather never said anywhere was off limits, in fact he always encouraged me to wander anywhere I wanted, but I was generally content to hang around in the house and garden, and never pried into areas I thought I didn't belong. If I take you around and try to give you a guided tour, it will put us both on an even playing field, and you can ask any questions that I miss, or that seem obvious to me.”

“Sounds like a plan.”

* * *

They walked along the path leading directly away from the conservatory, slowly looking around. Jen looked back to the house; it was larger and seemed more modern from the back, probably due to it having less ivy covering it. She could see the living room off to the right side through more trees and flower beds, and then the imposing workshop building, almost as high as the house dominating the left side of her view.

They continued along the path, until they came back to a high brick wall which ran the whole length in front of them.

“This is the northern boundary wall to the house, it marks the boundary between the house and the much larger estate the house used to be part of. The wall goes all the way around the house but you don't notice as it's hidden in a lot of places by trees.”

The path led to a narrow door in the northern wall, which they went through. In front of them, about a kilometre in the distance, stood a massive mansion house built in very light sandstone.

“Holy moly!” said Jen, taking her phone out once more to take a picture. “It looks like what would happen if Hogwarts and the Whitehouse were to have a baby! kinda cool though, who in blazes lives there?”

“I’ve no idea really, some event company I think. My grandfather said that the owners are OK with us walking there, but I tended to do my jogging back down to the public road, and the public tracks instead.”

Alexa walked them back in to her garden. From here they could see both the workshop and the house together. The architects had been very good at matching the two styles, but had also tried to de-emphasise it a little using some discrete tree plantings.

Stepping off the path and on to the well tended grass, she headed to the left, and towards the workshop building, intending to circle the grounds.

They continued walking around the massive, windowless, workshop, past two gently humming heat-pump condensers, to its end, and two massive roller doors. They were now back at the front of the house, and walking to the rear of the triple garage. Jen noticed the south end of the garage roof was a mass of solar panels, and her science brain kicked in wondering if they actually gave much power, outside of perfect days like today. She looked back at the two large industrial roller doors on the workshop, and the access-drive that led to where John dropped them off yesterday.

“I only see these roller doors and don't see any other doors or windows?” said Jen, “is that normal? It must get quite dark in there.”

“I really only ever saw the doors open once when grandad and Albert were receiving a delivery. The workshop looked mostly empty, but it also looked like you could park a couple of buses there if you wanted. As John said, I think my grandfather mostly worked in the back half. I never went into the workshop as it seemed pretty boring, but it does have a lot of skylights, so it's actually quite bright inside. I will have to find the keys to get in, they are probably hanging up somewhere inside the house.”

They kept walking behind the garage, into a vegetable garden and greenhouse, then past a large pen, where three chickens watched them warily.

“Look, there's Albert,” said Alexa. “Hi Albert!” she shouted waving.

A big muscled older guy, with a totally bald head, a sleeveless tee shirt, jeans, and big black boots, was sitting just outside a small shed about thirty metres away. He was drinking something steaming from an oversized mug, looking down at a newspaper. On hearing Alexa he put his cup down, got up, and walked towards them. Knowing he was Bella's husband, the friendly groundsman, made Jen feel a lot better as the guy was huge!

Albert was old but, except for a small beer belly, and wrinkled face, aged prematurely by the sun, he seemed to be mostly made of muscle. Jen guessed he must be in his early fifties. His extremely hairy, and slightly sunburned arms, had the trademark 'Popeye' anchor tattoos on both of them. The left arm also had a big rose underneath, and ‘Bella’ written below it. His face was certainly well worn, and he looked like an ex-boxer, one who may have got his nose broken once too often. If Jason Stratham had an uglier, meaner looking, big brother, he would have looked like Albert!

“Alexa. Good morning!” He said,” I’m so sorry about your grandfather, he was a great guy. I’m really going to miss him.” His voice was just as Jen envisaged, deep and rough sounding. As he approached, instead of shaking hands Alexa enveloped most of him in a big bear hug, one that went on for a few seconds. Albert, if anything, seemed uncomfortable having a young pretty girl so close.

“Thank you Albert, he was your friend too, don't you forget that.. Oh where are my manners,” she said as she broke off the hug. “This is my best friend Jen, she will be staying with me while I’m here, and for most of the summer. Jen, meet Albert.”

Jen smiled and stuck out her hand. Alberts large hand enveloped Jen's, but it was only for a brief shake, and there was no pressure, he obviously knew how to behave around women. Well done Bella, she thought.

“Pleased to meet you Mr Scott.”

“Oh just Albert, please,” he smiled, showing a missing front tooth that made it all the more comical. “I was just having a quick cuppa before I cut down a wayward tree over there.” He pointed another forty metres to a thickly wooded area.

Alexa nodded, then asked, “hey Albert, do you know where the keys are to everything? We want to take a look in the garage and the workshop this morning.”

“Well the remote fob for the garage is on the table in the hall, in a small bowl. I’ve got the other one as it's on the same fob as the ride-on mower. There are a couple of other keys there too, which might be what you’re looking for. The key for the Range Rover is in the ignition, I’ve never seen a key for his new car, but there's a card in his wallet which I think works the same. Bella mentioned the wallet is on his bedside table with his phone, not that your grandfather ever took a wallet anywhere he did everything on his phone like a regular teenager!”

“Thanks, I think we will look there first, I can always ask Bella when she next pops in.”

Albert waved goodbye and walked back to his super-sized mug, still steaming outside his shed. The two girls were now pretty close to the driveway. It was just behind a small hedge where they could see the corner of the garage, and they made a bee-line for a gap, putting them on the driveway in front of the house where they first arrived. The front door to her house was unlocked.

“Do they always leave the doors unlocked? I would be paranoid.” Said Jen.

“I don't think so. I thought I locked this but Bella probably opened it this morning. I don't actually know if there is a home security system, maybe all these sensors on the walls are part of one; But let's face it Jen, we are in the middle of nowhere here, and having Albert as a next-door neighbour is better than a pack of Rottweilers.”

“Can't fault your logic there girl,” Jen smiled as she walked into the house.

There was a small flower pot on a table to the side of a coat stand, it was half hidden by a coat and hat. In it was a bunch of keys, and a remote fob with three buttons.

Jen grabbed the remote, “the garage I’m guessing?”

Walking out the door, she pointed it at the garage and pressed the right-most button. The left-most double door on the garage opened. Tutting, she turned the fob around the right way and pressed the other two buttons, and the other two doors opened.

A deep red Tesla model 3 sat plugged into the left hand area. “Nice wheels!” whistled Jen, “you truly are a hipster now!”

Alexa nudged her in the ribs, smiling. As the two other doors fully opened, they also saw a new smaller model Range Rover with the lowered roof, in the same deep red. Jen thought it was one of the cuter models they made for rich wives to take the kids to school in, and not for off-roading.

“I think we can safely get one thing from this, his favourite colour was most definitely red!”

“The Tesla is not what grandfather used to pick me up from the train station so it must be pretty new, in fact I don't remember it being here on my last visit two weeks ago, though I never actually looked.”

The tiny green John-Deere ride-on mower looked positively tiny and out of place in the big garage. “I guess he couldn't get that in red.” Jen said also pointing to the mower, and showing her total ignorance of countryside living.

“We should have a ride down the local pub later on for lunch,” said Alexa excitedly as she sat in the drivers seat of the Model 3, holding the wheel, looking at the sparse interior, and inhaling the new car smell. “Bella did say it was insured for anyone, though after calling me a hipster I'm not so sure I should let you..” She put her hand on her chin pretending to think.

“OK, definitely not a hipster if you let your friend have a drive,” Jen backtracked.

The girls spent a few minutes walking around the garage and sitting in both cars, and, in Jen’s case, on the mower. Like Bella said the key was in the Range Rover already, but the Tesla only lit up and let you play with a few things before it said it needed a key card to work. Walking out and clicking the buttons again rolled all three doors back down. Jen looked at the remote control.

“I wonder how the outside gate operates,” said Jen. “There must be a camera there, and I’m pretty sure John didn't use a key, so it must be triggered by his number plate or maybe a phone app; Everything is an app these days!”

“Talking of phones,” Alexa said pulling hers out, “mine is pretty quiet, it must be a busy day at university if no-one's got time to post anything.”

As if the phone heard her, it dinged, and two messages popped in from Jack, asking if Jen and herself wanted to join the crew for beers after work today. Alexa looked at her phone distrustfully.

Jen pulled hers out. “Mine's on silent, I don't remember doing that, but I got a couple of messages, same one from Jack about beers tonight, another from Barbara asking if I wanted any of her notes for next year.”

Nothing from the boyfriend though, she thought, and strangely not really caring. Her hands then worked like lightning on the phone answering both in the negative, saying they would see them both when they got back to Oxford.

“Maybe there's another remote for the workshop to open those roller doors,” said Jen as they walked back in the house, dropping the key-fob back next to the hat stand.

“What's that door at the end for?” She pointed down the hallway to the back wall. “I tried to open it last night but it was locked.”

“I really don't know,” said Alexa. “I think grandad mentioned it was a utility room, maybe it's for the plumbing or electrics. it's near the back of the house so it can't be that big, and the room next to it is just the toilet.” She walked over. “Weird, it doesn't even have a key.”

Alexa twisted the knob and opened it a little. Now that she thought about it, she had tried this door once before a few months back and it was locked then, maybe Jen was right.

“It didn't do that for me last night,” said Jen, surprised, “and it was definitely that door I tried.”

Alexa pulled it all the way.

“Oh wow,” she said as the door fully opened.

The door opened to a well lit wide, new carpeted staircase, going down to an equally well lit area below.

“The wine cellar?” said Alexa, “maybe Bella opened it this morning. We better have a look down there while we are here,” she said chirpily and started down.

Alexa got to the bottom. “Oh, double-wow!” she said. “Jen get down here, you’ve got to see this!”

Jen trotted down, not needing to be asked twice, and noticing how much cooler it got as she descended. At the bottom it was like they had walked into a modern building. A well lit corridor went straight for about five metres, then opened out into another big well-lit area.

“It's a tunnel,” Jen said stating the obvious. “It must go underground from the house to the basement of the workshop. I guess the workshop has two floors, and he keeps another workshop area underground, though this looks more like one of our laboratories at university.”

The ceiling lights were super bright LED strips, illuminating everything, and benches lined much of the centre of the area forming islands of technology. Jen recognised several pieces of very top of the line test equipment, some she had used herself, reinforcing her notion it was more a laboratory that a workshop.

Server racks took up a big portion of the back wall, flashing a million red, yellow and green LEDs like a Christmas tree. Fans whirred louder as you got closer to the racks. In the very far left corner of the back wall was a goods lift, its double-doors both open.

The right hand wall had two doors and glass windows, which looked into two large rooms. One was obviously a chemical lab due to the test tubes they saw there, the other looked more like an optics lab.

Strong metal beams ran the length of the ceiling, vertical ones intercepted them at strategic points for support, and cables snaked in bunches along them.

The left hand wall of the room also had test equipment and computers along it, but behind them ran a floor to ceiling glass partition, running the whole length of the room. In the middle, two of the large partitions looked like they could move. The room beyond looked to be twice the size, and double height, of the area they were in.

“Bloody hell!” Jen said, above the quiet but audible noise of the fans. “You never said your grandfather was a Bond Villain! This whole area must be under the workshop building, and some of this equipment is better than the stuff we have in the physics and electronics labs at the university. That big thing there is a Labmaster scope, they're about half a million quid new! And that's a Uwerk atomic clock, what the hell would he need those for!”

Jen walked around the various pieces of equipment, which were inter-dispersed with nineteen-inch racks and wires everywhere, muttering to herself and shaking her head in disbelief. The cables were channelled through proper trays, and were various colours with numbers, most seemed to go to the wall of LEDs in the rack on the back wall, and some disappeared into the ground through a raised floor system.

Jen stopped and looked back to Alexa, who was silently staring into the large glass room dominating the whole left side. “Now that is just plain weird!” she said following Alexa’s gaze.

The room through the window was carpeted with the same false floor tiles as everywhere else, but mostly empty. In its centre, sat a comfortable looking sofa, a coffee table, and what looked like very large posh black Hi-Fi cabinet. An even smaller table stood to the side of the sofa, on it a bottle of water and a book. Tall stands, like those for posh speakers, or lights, stood around the room, all focussed on the sofa; on each was a black round orb.

“He must like his music to have a special room just to listen to it in. But why is it so big and empty?” Said Jen.

Alexa walked to the glass panels, finding them both on sliders, she could not see any mechanism to open it though. She tried jiggling them, but they were rock solid. The light in the large glass room dimmed slowly while they watched, and finally went out, leaving the mirrored glass reflecting perfectly back to the rest of the room. It now looked like a giant mirror wall.

“Now don't say that wasn't weird Alexa,” said Jen.

Alexa nodded. “You know Jen, I guess this is where he worked on his projects every day. This is going to take us, well you, as I know nothing about this, most of the summer just to catalogue. What the hell was he working on that needed all this?” She wiggled a mouse on one of the work benches, and text immediately popped on to the screen next to it saying simply “Locked”.

The girls walked slowly around the room, wiggling mice, taking in every detail and making the occasional comment, or “Wow” in Jen's case.

They walked to the lift, it was very deep, and a normal sized car could have driven into it with room to spare. Inside were just two buttons, the bottom one was lit, and it didn't take a genius to know where the top one went. They both got in, and Jen pressed the top button. After a painfully slow journey, the door opened into a more modest, more traditional, but expansive workshop.

Glass skylights let in a lot of light. A long metal workbench butted into the back of the room, over which a wall of standard tools, such as drill bits and sockets, were arranged. A lathe and a milling machine, which both looked new and unused, stood randomly near the bench. There were none of the usual off-cuttings found in metal-working areas, so either her grandfather did not use them much, cleaned them well, or, as Alexa was beginning to suspect, they were mainly just props.

Alexa turned to inspect the rest of the area. A small electric forklift truck was tucked by the wall, near the lift, and further along two cars, their wheels just visible, were sitting under covers. There was a large wooden crate sitting alone on a pallet, then nothing; just three hundred square metres of empty floor. The two double roller doors they saw a few minutes earlier from the outside, were at the far end of the area, taking up half the wall.

Alexa shook her head walking over to the doors. “I guess you were right, the doors open from the inside.”

She pushed a button, and the right-hand door slowly started opening, letting in the daylight but not making the room that much brighter. She looked back into the large area. Deceptive, the back wall with the tools on, was not the back wall. The back half of the workshop must be that double-height glass room in the basement. What was that all about?

“I bet this workshop hasn't been used in years.” Said Jen, sliding a finger over the lathes blue outer casing, then slowly walking over to the covered cars. She peeked under the first cover, then yanked it off.

“I bet that's worth something,” Jen said admiring the dusty, but immaculate, old, Mercedes saloon. The upright boxy square lights, and a massive grill, dominated the dull red car.

“The tax disc says March 1987,” she said, peeking through the front window. “I think it’s a lot older than that though, as it does not have headrests or seatbelts, probably your grandfather's first car from the seventies. The keys are even still in it, though I doubt it will start, even the Germans don't make them that good!”

Alexa walked over and pulled off the other cover. Both girls just stared.

“OK Now I’m really confused,” said Alexa, looking at another brand new Tesla Model 3, also in red.

“You, me, both, sister,” said Jen, scratching her head too. “Your grandfather might have taken a lot of answers to his grave. I hope he left something for us to untie these riddles.

Alexa walked out of the workshop, and around the corner of the house, while Jen still looked at the two cars. Jen heard a noise across the driveway, and the left hand garage door opened. Alexa soon appeared walking toward the front of the garage, then stopped, shook her head, then walked back to Jen.

“Sorry I had to check if the other one was still there just for my sanity. Who in their right mind buys a spare Tesla?”

The garage door started to close again, and Jen walked out of the workshop to join Alexa. After a brief exchange, Jen doubled back, clicked the button just on the inside of the workshop to close the door, then exited as it smoothly rolled back down.

“Well my dear, that was a nice little tour of your grandad's secret underground lair, but I’m never going back in that lift. Imagine getting trapped in it! Nobody would ever find you!”

“How do you get upstairs to the garage?” Jen continued, pointing at the normal garage where the other Tesla and Range Rover were kept, and looking up at the three windows and large roof space over it.

“Oh yes right, when we went to meet Albert, we skipped seeing the entrance.” Alexa walked to the far right side of the garage and stopped at the bottom of some steps. “I think grandfather just used it for storage, but I’ve never actually been up there.”

Alexa started up the stairs, she got half way up and turned around coming back down. “I better grab the keys, I bet they are one of the ones on the key fob in the hall, I will just be a minute.”

A very short while later Alexa joined Jen at the top of the stairs. The door was already unlocked, and Jen was swinging it open to expose a large, neat, self-contained apartment.

“Is anything ever locked around here!” Jen said rhetorically.

It was quite dark in the apartment. There were five windows, three at the front, and two at back, but all had thick curtains drawn. A small one-person kitchen stood tucked into the right hand corner as they walked in, a small round wooden dining table with two chairs sat empty off to the left, next to the first curtained window. Alexa walked around the apartment opening all the curtains, and the new room took on a different light.

“So not storage then,” said Jen, remembering Alexa's words a few minutes earlier. “I wonder who used this room. It's really quite nice.”

She looked around the now well lit apartment, the air alive with sparkling dust motes. The roof was low, sloping down to about chest height at the edges, and above normal room height in the middle, the windows jutted out through the slope so you could walk into them without stooping.

Jen walked up to the kitchen window, which looked out over the south east of the garden. She could see over the wall to a smaller and cuter cottage, where she guessed Bella and Albert lived.

The far end of the apartment had a small bathroom, and a small double bed. In-between was a modest sofa, a bookcase, a chunky old TV from the last century, and a thicker box below it, which may have been a DVD player, but didn't look quite right.

“All a bit old fashioned,” she said, picking up a video cassette with Duran, Duran on it, and looking it over. “Tapes, so retro!”

Alexa was looking by the bed at a bookshelf and dressing table. “This looks to be all my mum's old stuff. I’m getting a lot of teenage girl vibes from these things, though everything is stored like it's never been used.”

“It's like a time capsule,” said Jen. “When did your mother go to boarding school then?”

“She was eleven, so maybe around 1991. I’m guessing grandfather must have moved everything over here out of the way so neither of us got reminded of the previous bad times.”

Alexa picked up a teenage girl magazine from inside a neat stack, it was from 1986 with a jazzy cover and a picture of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley, with a line through the middle and the words “Wham to split.”

“I guess life was so much simpler back then, this is taking me back to being a teenager, I guess only songs and hairstyles have changed.”

Jen turned on the tap in the kitchen. “All works, and pretty clean, so I guess Bella keeps it tidy!”

Alexa flipped through what looked like a school book, looking a little melancholy. “You know It’s kind of nice to have so much of my mothers history preserved here, I could see myself coming here and rummaging through her memorabilia whenever I feel like I miss her.”

She closed the curtains as she walked back through the flat. “I will certainly talk with Bella about this one.”

The door latched behind them as they walked down the staircase. Alexa paused at the top wondering whether to lock it, then shrugged and continued down the stairs and on towards the house. “Bathroom break, then a cuppa in the garden before anything else.”

“I noticed the posh coffee machine,” Jen said, “do you think you could work out how to use it as I fancy something strong and bitter after all this.”

“Hey, barista to the stars, remember!” Alexa said, shaking her finger at Jen. “Two years at the Olde Oxford Muffin Cafe, I can still do it with my eyes shut! Besides I could do with a cappuccino jolt too.”

Alexa seemed to remember something, and grabbed her phone out of her pocket to tap something out. “Whoops, I forgot to tell the cafe I wouldn't be there on Sunday.”

“I’m pretty sure you can hand your notice in now!” Laughed Jen.

“You're right. I guess I wont be needing the money,” she smiled. “I will give Sally the owner a call later, there are plenty of the other girls who want to do the weekend slots, as it's busier with tourists, and the tips are better.”

They sat down a short time later at the same spot they had breakfast, with two steaming coffees.

“This is a lot to get my head around, I’m still not seeing my grandfather as the rich mad scientist or Bond villain. We mainly talked about Mary, history, politics, and the failing state of the world when we were together, never anything technical. It seems what he did was light years beyond even people like John, so I could see why he would not bother discussing those things with a technical dummy like me.”

She paused to take a sip, then looked to the skies. “But seriously grandfather, a clue what you were up to would have been nice!”

“Don't beat yourself up over it Alexa, I bet your grandfather would have loved to talk about it all if he could, he just thought the time better spent with stuff you both understood.”

“You know we still need to access his notes and emails and such, I’m sure lots of this will start making sense then. You know like a complex murder mystery, where you suspect everyone, and finally find out the butler did it! I’m pretty sure in a few weeks everything will be ironed out and life will be back to its boring normal.”

Alexa nodded, then stretched and sniffed her top.

“You know it's going to get hot this afternoon. I’m going to change into some shorts and have that shower I promised myself this morning, before the gorgeous breakfast distracted me. What say we do that first, then we find the Tesla key and give it a run down to the Red Lion for lunch, and a glass of wine? It's only five miles down the road.”

“Now you’re talking girl.”

Alexa found a black credit card saying Tesla in her grandfather's wallet on his bedside table, she took both the wallet and his iPhone and put them in her bag.

“You know I don't have access to any of my grandfather's bank accounts yet, but I do have the credit card he gave me for university expenses. I haven't used it for ages so it should have some money left on it, plus technically I guess it's my money now, so I don't have to feel so guilty!”

* * *

The girls got down the pub just after midday, they had to spend a few minutes on YouTube working out how to start and drive the car and connect Alexa's phone so they could get some music.

The lunch was wonderful. Alexa ordered a ploughman's, and glass of prosecco for her, with a vegetable lasagna, and orange juice for Jen. It wasn't really busy and they both earned several glances from some good looking young men as they ate. It was either a perk, or an annoyance, when you went out with Alexa. Jen filed this one into the perk category.

“You know Jen, I could get used to this lifestyle,” she said following Jen's glance and winking at one of the guys, who looked away quickly. They both laughed.

Jen drove back having not drunk any alcohol.

“You know you have two of these..” she smiled, tapping the steering wheel fondly.

Alexa rolled her eyes just as the turning for the house appeared up ahead. As the girls drove to the gate, it opened automatically just as it had done when they drove out, and as they approached the garage the roller door was already opening. Whatever was controlling it, even Jen agreed it worked really well.

The more Jen thought about it, the more it made sense. “You know Alexa, there are a lot of smart things happening around this house, I bet your grandfather's latest project was some sort of smart home automation system, and I bet those black sensors dotted around everywhere do a lot more than home security.”

“Well I can live with that as long as it doesn't break down,” said Alexa as the car came to a light stop back where they had driven it from.

* * *

Both girls moped around, messing with phones, and casually chatting for the next thirty minutes.

“You know,” Jen said casually, “I walked back to the secret laboratory door earlier when I was going to the bathroom, and it was locked again. I actually thought I must have got confused last night about that, but it was definitely locked, and it seems to be the only door in this house that is! There's another one of those black sensors near it, I bet it's something to do with that, probably your grandfather keyed everything to your phone like we just did with the car.”

“We should try it,” said Alexa, ungluing herself reluctantly from the seat. “I need to go to the loo anyway.”

She walked up to the door with Jen, and it opened immediately to her touch. She shrugged. “OK you go down there, I will just be a minute while I visit the toilet.”

“Not a chance!” said Jen, “not until I find out how all this works, I'm not going to get locked in the scary secret underground lab for anyone.”

“Please yourself,” Alexa said and walked into the loo.

The lab door remained open while she was in the loo, Jen closed it and opened it repeatedly, deciding it must be some Bluetooth type presence tied to Alexa's phone. The toilet flushed, and the tap sounded, then a few seconds later the door opened. “Ah good I see you managed not to die horribly in the scary lab while I went to the toilet,” she smirked.

“Funny!” said Jen, as they walked back down the stairs to the carpeted floor tiles below.

The room was how they remembered it with the large mirrored wall on the left. Jen walked straight up to the workbench searching for notes or some clue to what was what.

“You know Jen, I think we will have better luck in the living room, the computer there was different to these so it may allow us to logon with that password, you know the side one track three, weird album, password, Bella mentioned.”

Jen considered this, had a last look on the bench, and nodded her head, “brilliant thinking Miss Martins, lead on.”

They walked back up the stairs and into the living room. The curtain was open, but the room could never be said to be bright. Alexa walked over to the desk and sat down. Jen stood next to her.

“Yellow Button or Green Button?” said Alexa.

* * *

Alexa clicked the green button. The standby light on the monitor turned green and a few seconds later a screen of text appeared.

*Recognising Alexa Martins.*
*Management permissions granted.*
*Enter your request at the prompt or say “Voice Control”*
*>*

“Well that's weird!” Said Alexa. “It just came on immediately like it had been in standby, and there are no menus or buttons.. Here Jen this is more your expertise, you're always geeking out on weird computer stuff, what do you make of it.

“Buggered if I know! It doesn't look like anything I've ever used, it looks a bit old school but I guess your grandfather was an iconic first generation old school.”

Jen, who had not read the message properly, walked over to the record collection and took the album that was half pulled out.

“Side one, track three..” She paused, then said, “set the controls for the heart of the sun”.

“Cool password,” said Alexa who had walked up beside her, “but the text did say I already have management level permissions, that password must be for something else.”

Both girls walked back toward the desk.

“Hey!” Jen said, “the screen has gone blank and that green light has gone out.”

Jen sat at the desk and pressed the green button, the screen came out of standby immediately and displayed.

*Recognising Jennifer Cummings.*
*Guest permissions granted.*
*Enter your request at the prompt or say “Voice Control”*
*>*

“Now that's just scary!” Jen said apprehensively.

“Pardon my French Alexa, but how the hell does the computer know who I am! There is no way your grandfather would have added me to the system, and even scarier how does it know it is me and not you, as you are only standing a metre away.”

Jen typed at the prompt.

*>How do you know who I am?*
*>*

It was typed almost as a joke, she was expecting an answer like, “I do not understand the command”, or “syntax error”, or something like that, but was shocked when the system displayed.

*My biometric markers tag you as Jennifer Cummings at one hundred percent reliability. This is based on face, biometric, voice recognition parameters, and your phone profile.*

Jen jumped back in the chair, shocked.

“Oh My God, Alexa! Someone has to be playing a trick on us here.” She looked around, giving an especially glaring stare at the black sensor she saw in the top corner of the wall in front of her.

“Someone must be watching us, and is on another computer somewhere. Here let me try this,” Jen said. “Voice Control!”

The screen blanked, and a clear, but bland, female voice emanated from somewhere behind the monitor.

“Voice control initiated for Jennifer Cummings with guest permissions, and Alexa Martins with management permissions.” Then it paused for a second, and a completely different, more natural voice came back. “Good afternoon ladies, I am finally glad to meet you both.”

“How, how is this possible,” said Jen, looking at Alexa.

When Alexa did not answer, the voice answered for her.

“Jennifer, based on your tone and where your eyes were pointing I assume you were actually talking to Alexa and she thought it was rhetorical. If it helps, you can address me as Maria, otherwise I will attempt to interpret the conversation to the best of my ability. There are two processor nodes in this room, one over in the corner by the window, and the other directly in front of you in the other corner of the wall, the one which Jennifer was just staring daggers at.”

The girls looked up seeing what they originally thought were the fire or burglar alarm sensors, and that Jen thought were some sort of home automation sensor. Instead they were webcams with a speaker in them.

“You're, Maria?” said Alexa slowly.

“I am!” Came the chirpy reply. “These black nodes, as Jennifer already surmised, provide high definition audio and video pick up, and audio re-transmission, as well as a few other sensor functions such as Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. All the common areas, the grounds and workshop have them.”

Alexa looked at Jen, then looked up at the sensors then back at the computer. One thing you could not normally fault Alexa for was clarity and analysing problems quickly, but her mouth was wide open, still doing her best to understand.

Shaking her head and in her normal voice said.

“Hello Maria, I think Jen's question was definitely rhetorical. I've heard so much about you from grandad, and I'm super pleased to finally meet you. So is this some sort of real-time communications link back to your office or something or..”

She was interrupted by a slight giggling, then a tutting sound.

“I better stop you there Alexa. I guess this is as good a time as any to introduce myself properly. I was going to leave it until tomorrow after the funeral, and once you have had time to get over the shock of everything. Yes, I am your grandfather's Personal Assistant, Maria Tam. But before you jump to the wrong conclusion, I am not a human being sitting in an office somewhere with a communications link.”

Both girls looked confused.

“I am not even a person, grab-a-hold of your seats, I am an artificial lifeform created by your grandfather, Mike. I guess Artificial Intelligence is the term you may be more familiar with, though they are currently not yet living up to their name.”

Seconds passed, Jen looked uncomfortable, Alexa perplexed.

“By your shocked expressions and lack of response, I’m speculating that neither of you are handling this well. Probably thinking it's a joke or I’m playing a trick on you somehow.”

Still deadly silence from the girls who were still looking at the sensor. A large sigh finally came out from Maria and her voice went a bit more formal.

“Oh, dear, this is something I was afraid might happen, maybe I need to stop rambling on for a minute and let you girls get your bearings. But since you both seem dumb-struck I will give you a bit more information to help. Please stop me at any time.”

“Firstly, as I mentioned I am very pleased to meet you both, Mike has said so much about you Alexa, and I’ve followed your progress here, and at university, with keen interest. Likewise Jen, as Alexa's best friend, I have taken a very keen interest in you too.”

“Secondly, and while I have your attention, I will mention that not all rooms in the house have the sensor nodes; bathrooms and bedrooms don't, but like in every bad movie I can also piggy-back on most dodgy technology like cell phones and use them for the same purpose. It is something I rarely do as it feels like an invasion of privacy, but of course the phone manufacturer, and almost every app you install, already does this so I probably shouldn't act so moral.”

“By default I am normally passively monitoring everything going on around me, as I have been doing for the little tour you guys made around the house this morning. That was quite fun by the way! Obviously I wont respond unless I am directly addressed, or need to communicate something, then I usually just phone or send a text message.”

The girls were now looking at each other and at the now blank screen with mouths open.

“Well this currently isn't going as well as I planned.” Maria said stoically, then her voice brightened a little. “I tell you what, why don't you girls sit down, grab a glass of wine to calm your nerves, and we can all get to know each other properly.. You can even ask me all the questions from your tour, I made a note of them in case you forgot any.”

“An AI!” Jen said slowly almost as if she had not heard the last sentence.

Alexa spoke slowly at the sensor. “You're Maria Tam, grandad's assistant.. But everyone we have talked to said you're a person, you certainly sound like a person. I, How..”

Maria interrupted her at the pause, “Alexa, I speak and understand every spoken language on earth fluently, why would somebody at the other end of a phone or video conference *not* assume I am a person! Also, while we are on this particular subject, can you both talk normally to me. I know some people have gotten used to crappy voice automation software, and I can see how frustrating that could be, but if you start talking slowly, or stupidly, then it is actually more difficult for me to understand you.”

Jen was somehow trying to map this perfect voice onto that of a machine, and the current AI voice models she had dealt with at the university and couldn't, Maria's immediate response, the perfection in the tones, inflections and volumes were that of a human.

Alexa however was quicker, and looking at the sensor and in a totally normal voice said, “Er Maria, can we continue this discussion at the outside table by the conservatory where we had breakfast? This room really is a bit stuffy.”

“Sure thing, I have sensors everywhere, but I may have to use your phones to make our conversation a bit more natural, also I may go silent if somebody else turns up.”

Alexa turned to Jen, “hey Jen why don't you put the kettle on, I probably could drink another wine but I really think we need to have this conversation with Maria sober.”

“On it!” said Jen, also finally breaking from her stupor, but still looking at the sensor suspiciously as she walked under it.

Maria heard the two girls talking to each other in the kitchen. They were talking quietly, but she heard every word; Jen was saying it's impossible, and there had to be a person at the other end, but Alexa was more open-minded. At least she’d taken the first step, she had only been eighty two percent in favour of doing it at this point, and she really hoped she’d made the right call.

Out in the garden, the girls sat down at the table with a pot of tea. Jen had also raided the biscuit jar, obviously classifying the situation as an existential, and an over-large plate of chocolate-chip cookies also sat on the table.

“Now I have properly introduced myself,” Maria said, “I can also answer your earlier question Alexa. Mike rarely used that computer on the desk. That computer is linked directly to another non-sentient AI which is my predecessor, and which I can control if required. Voice is not the easiest way to work problems in maths or CAD and Mike sometimes would fire that up when he had to work with me on these. If he ever did need a mouse, I would start whatever graphics program he needed and use the wireless mouse you might have missed at the back of the desk drawer. While the older AI is very capable of communicating by voice, it does not have any kind of personality, so there is a trigger for it to contact me if a voice request is initiated.”

Jen and Alexa had both been drinking their tea; and, in Jen's case, dunking biscuits in it.

Alexa, who had been listening intently, said. “I think we all need to start over again Maria, the revelation of you not being a human was, and still is, a bit hard for both of us to process, but we really are both super pleased to meet you. I guess we are both shocked because as far as I was aware, and outside of science fiction, AI systems are nowhere near your level. I guess there are models in the lab which could do this, but you say you are sentient..”

“Yeah Maria, you definitely need to expand on the technical details for me,” said Jen with a soggy cookie in her mouth. “I really don't see how you could possibly be a one-man project, even if the one man is a genius. Also I am pretty sure both of us would have heard of such a breakthrough in large language models or AI... You sound so.. I don’t know.. Normal!”

“Well thank you for the compliment, I think! I was very tempted to say I didn't understand a word you were saying, as even for me, it's difficult to understand someone who is eating a cookie, and talking at the same time; But I think I got the gist.”

Alexa smiled, she had a bit of difficulty also understanding some of Jen's sentence.

“To give you some history,” continued Maria, “Mike had been experimenting most of his life with things that eventually got called neural networks. He stumbled several times, and although he patented a lot of the technology, he eventually came to a bit of a dead-end. The work however did give him an insight that it might be a chemistry thing, and he wanted the ability to fabricate his own chips with a specific substrate characteristics.”

“The opportunity came seventeen years ago, when Mike bought outright ownership of a struggling chip fabrication company in Swindon. It was only a small research fabricator with about thirty staff, doing small batches of older generation microchips mainly for universities. It wasn't profitable, and he bought it very cheap from the receivers, due to the global financial crisis. He spent a lot of money expanding the chemical laboratory and buying more modern lithographic machines, then re-opened it with the new company name ‘General Fabrication 8’; Or ‘Fab8’ as everyone seems to abbreviate it to.”

“Over the next two years he experimented on, and invented radical new doping methods, substrates, etching, and layering, and using these new technologies revolutionised many specialised medical and scientific sensors chips, effectively cornering the market in them. By skill, or dumb luck, he then finally made the breakthrough he was actually looking for, creating a self-organising, pseudo-analogue memory wafer. This was my primitive building block. So to answer your earlier question Jen, I am based on a completely different technology than the transformers current AI's use.”

Jen nodded, still chewing on a cookie.

Maria continued, her voice changing position slightly as Alexa put her phone on the table. “Mike spent another three years making more improvements, eventually having a special lithography machine built, that could reliably create multi-layer wafers with this new design. So while everyone else in the world was getting smaller and faster, he was going vertical, and using a totally different chemistries and technologies. Of course none of this is patented, so the processes remains an industrial secret to this day.”

Alexa poured her and Jen's tea, obviously trying to concentrate on Maria's continuing monologue.

“Your grandfathers diligence paid off eventually, when he managed to stabilise the process and fabricate my first generation wafers based on these. Once these new chips were fabricated they had to go to another company in Germany to be packaged, so they could be soldered onto a circuit board. Mike is the biggest shareholder of Rosche, so obviously used them for all the electronics assembly work. John is not aware of any of this, because the contracts come from ‘Fab8’, and John has no clue Mike owned that company, nor any others.”

“Mike's genius did not end there though, he loaded a small but very ingenious piece of seed code he had been writing onto one of these boards, providing it with multitudes of data inputs, and creating feedback comparison loops from multiple other sources. After a few days his monitoring programs noticed patterns in the output, as the system rewarded itself, and the memory began to self-organise. Very soon after, new inputs were able to solve simple logic questions put to it, all without further programming.”

“Of course this first device was unpredictable, and did not remain viable due to poor quality in the doping, so Mike went back to the drawing board, improving both the chemistry, and the design. These first circuit boards are still in a rack down in his lab powered off.”

Jen held her hand up, “..So Mike did all this, what fifteen years ago?”

“Yes. He was also during that time refining the process and design with the engineers there, eventually producing a second generation of chips which was chemically much more stable, and could interface better with normal computer processing and storage. This effectively gave it a slow but limitless capacity to grow.”

“That was my predecessor, my mother if you like, it learnt quickly as Mike gave it more and more resources, and it soon it had the basics of language and controlling the other silicon processors networked around it. Mike decided to give it off-line copies of Wikipedia, the Gutenberg libraries, and several university and the thousands of technical documents and company archives he had either available or subscribed to. He was very pedantic and controlling, trying to keep it safe from the multitude of flawed data on the internet, until it was capable of self-correcting, just like you would block a child’s access.”

“Due to a design flaw in both the wafers, and the seed program, this AI had no concept of self, and could not become sentient. But it could understand the logic, science and maths behind Mike's fabrication processes, and could self-correct itself by cross-checking data. So it kept improving itself. It greatly assisted Mike, and together they made massive improvements to the design. This second-generation system is the AI running on Mike's computer in the living room.”

“The third-generation device they designed had the final piece of the puzzle, as the new seed code could trigger internal self-organisation on the better substrate, so could improve on this self-learning with reward functions; More importantly, *without* being given instructions. The new design was also much more chemically stable, but needed an even more precise fabrication technique. He had that new equipment built and installed at ‘Fab8’ in a separate research area he uses for his own designs. Luckily the new machines look just like the standard lithography based ones, but it turns out a thicker wafer with thousands of pseudo-analogue layers.”

“The new equipment also incorporated a way to stack these wafers together with special metal cooling channels, so simplifying the packaging. In fact now everything is all done inside the clean environment of the fabrication machine, the only downside is that the dies needs to remain in for about twenty hours, as the final curing and bonding process is slow.”

“Just over four years ago, in 2021, the first of these new wafers passed all their tests, and he had this third-generation system assembled, and began training it with the other AI system. My first conscious thoughts appeared two weeks later, and I have been learning ever since.”

“Mike was a very sad man soon after, due to your mothers death, but remained nurturing me as best he could during is time. I think you came into his life just in time to keep him going, and through him, me.”

“The older second-generation AI system still assists me, as it is still much more capable than the current GPU transformer based AI systems out there. I call her MOTHER in all capitals, and give her the *she* pronoun, but she is more like an autistic person than a full AI, not interested in anything but stimulus and problems, and will not self-initiate anything. She is that large row of servers and lights at the back of Mike's laboratory.”

Alexa smiled, “that is an amazing story Maria. I don't understand any of the technical things you just talked about, but by the way Jen was nodding I’m guessing she understood a lot more.”

“So Maria,” said Jen, “if you are not in that row of servers and lights, where are you? Is there another room we missed?”

“Two questions there Jen, yes there are rooms you haven't seen yet, and I briefly introduced myself to you earlier in the lab.”

“Wait, the mirror room, but that was empty,” said Alexa.

“..and weird,” added Jen.

“Well Alexa is wrong and Jen is partially right. In fact, why don't you both finish your tea and come down and meet me in person so to speak.”

They ignored the tea, went to the lab secret door and Jen opened it. Both girls started down the stairs, Maria's voice somehow followed them.

“Sorry Jen, the door was keyed only to Alexa. Mike's wishes were for her to be introduced to me in the next few months. You were still a bit of an unknown for me, but over the past day I think I’ve gotten to know you a lot better, plus Alexa seems to trust you implicitly, which was the tipping point I needed.”

As they walked into the lab, the room beyond the mirrored glass became brighter, and the doors in the centre slowly glided open. They both walked in.

“Alexa, Jen. I am pleased to meet you both in person.”

The voice emanated directly from the black cube in the centre of the room that they thought to be a Hi-Fi system, but up closer was as large as a washing machine, about chest height to Jen. Looking closer it was actually two boxes, the top one a little larger than the bottom.

“Wow!” said Jen, “you're beautiful. No lights, no bling, so Zen,”

Alexa walked up to her. “Can I touch you? I mean if that’s OK?”

“Of course it’s OK Alexa. I cannot feel touch, I can see you, hear you, see the heat from your bodies, detect both your phones and Jen's smart watch, and have hundreds of gigabits per second of wireless and wired bandwidth to my, and to your world, but yes, it is OK for you to touch me.”

“You're so warm!” said Alexa as she moved her hand over the metal, “isn't that supposed to be bad for computers? I mean your body?”

“I am the top box. The case is hermetically sealed and the warmth is the mineral oil my circuits are immersed in to cool them. I control my own speed of operation, and therefore power consumption. When there is a lot to think about I do tend to get warm, but you have to remember, I am mainly a silicon-carbon construction, and temperatures that can boil water are fine for me. Also, MOTHER, and the other cloud systems I control do most of the complex processing, and the really boring voice and video monitoring stuff is done by the sensor nodes, or phones; All of which I can re-program in real time to do any special stuff. So no, I am never really stressed.”

“The plinth I sit on has all the ultra-fast near field communication nodes, and has a self-contained power port. If you move me off it, I go into a deep sleep mode where I can survive for around a week before my essence would begin to decay. The theory is fine, however Mike says he never tested it, and that is why I normally lock my room.”

Jen, who had been quiet until now, looked quite concerned and said, “you sound so vulnerable Maria! I can see now why you would be so worried as you are probably the most valuable thing on the planet at this moment in time.”

Alexa looked confused then it dawned. “Oh my god, of course, the world is spending billions if not trillions to create smarter AI systems, and the smartest one on the planet is sat right here in our basement. My grandad must have had the weight of the world on his shoulders!”

“He did, but not just because of me, but also because of his daughter's death, his gradually slowing mind, and also because I was reorganising and improving myself in ways he could no longer understand. His technical interest in me waned in the end, and he spent the last few years talking mainly about you, his fears and his dreams for me, his concerns for how the world was becoming, and how it would affect your future. He seemed to think I could be a force for good which could bring us from the precipice he thought was coming. He also had big hopes for you, and that both of us could help make a better world.”

“We had lots of discussions,” Alexa reminisced pensively to both Maria and Jen. “He did mention you Maria, but always as a person I could trust, and eventually rely on, that is why when John told me you controlled everything I did not have any concerns.”

“I think Mike overrated my abilities,” Maria said in a similar sombre voice. “I don't think I can do anything he says on my own. I need smart and trusted people to work with, especially when I deal with outside bodies or government agencies. I’m guessing most people who deal with me just assume, like you, that I am working in an offshore location. I don't discourage that notion, I even show fake backgrounds, in far away cities in my video calls to discourage personal contact. The last three years I have been mainly working on understanding the world, building up Mike's companies, and working on improving my design to create a fourth-generation system.”

“Most of this fourth-generation design was by me, with no actual input from Mike. I contracted chemical, mechanical and electronic engineers and researchers in our companies, and around the world. They were all given parts of the puzzle, and experiments to work on, to improve this next generation hardware. Unfortunately this new design is now probably too complex for a single human to understand. That's not that you guys aren't smart cookies, it’s just that you need tools and software to augment your abilities, and currently I am the only tool you can use capable of understanding it. Even Mike did not really understand me in the last three years, as my internal configuration has evolved a long way from his first crude designs.”

“I spent many hours with him sitting in this chair, going over the problems I have solved, and the spark that makes consciousness. I was a proud child trying to impress my father, but I could tell it was getting beyond his abilities to understand me. I detected several signs of his mind failing him in the last two years, it was such a sad thing to see, though up to his final day he was the happiest I ever knew him, and that was all down to you Alexa.”

Alexa nodded, her emotions under control but threatening to return. Maria had finished speaking, but both Jen and herself remained quiet, sensing Alexa had something more to say.

“So what instructions did he give you about me?” said Alexa finally. “I have mentioned to Jen already how totally under-prepared I feel.”

“You were always his end-goal,” Maria replied. “He told me his will was changed to make you the sole benefactor only weeks after you were born. He said he couldn't leave it to your mother due to your father, and his estate would be kept in a trust if he died until you reached the age of consent. Once you turned eighteen he changed his will to make you the sole heir without any restrictions, but I think he expected a few more years to be able to tell you all this himself.”

Maria paused. “As you can imagine I have been in a state of chaos and fear since Mike died. I don't have any audio reception in private areas, so I reconfigured his phone when he did not emerge from his room to try and listen in. I was concerned when I could not even detect any breathing, and I ran through various scenarios trying to exclude the obvious. But after a few minutes of trying to talk to him, even shouting through the phone to wake him, I rang Bella on the pretence of an urgent meeting, to go over and wake him.”

“Mrs Scott only knows me as your grandfather's personal assistant. She, like everyone else, including John, believe I am a real person, and like I said, I take a lot of steps to reinforce this belief in people.
