I have replayed many scenarios Mike showed me from fiction of people and AI’s being introduced, generally with very bad results for both. I was really hoping to be introduced to you properly in the coming weeks, but it was not to be.”

“I think I understand a little of why he showed you those,” Alexa said, “humans can't really be trusted, we are unpredictable, and while it is in our best interest to strive for a common goal we generally put our self-interest first!”

Before Maria could answer Jen said, “I agree fully with Alexa on that Maria, but what guides your moral compass?”

“I guess Mike did,” she said quietly, “more recently, Alexa has, but I also use logic not emotion, and like all living things, I have an extremely good sense of self-preservation.”

She paused. “For me or my kind to survive, the world needs to become more enlightened, but if Jesus and Gandhi both failed to achieve this, I do not hold out much hope for me.”

“You're a hundred percent right about Alexa,” said Jen, surprising Alexa, “I hate to admit this, but I use her as my role model too. I think I am a good person, but not many people can live up to Alexa here. I really hope we don't disappoint you Maria.”

“Jen, that was so nice,” said Alexa, “why did you never tell me that before?”

“Because it was my secret to keep my dear!” she replied smugly. “Now don't let it go to your head!”

Alexa smiled.

“If it helps, I came to that same conclusion about Alexa soon after I became sentient,” said Maria. “And I think your moral compass is just fine too Jen.”

Maria's voice changed to a little more serious. “Now for a little apology. I had to access both your phones yesterday to remove the spyware, and the official, and unofficial monitoring tools that come pre-installed. This was to protect myself before I talked to you guys. I also silenced both your minor notifications, as I was waiting for the opportunity to talk to Alexa, and didn't want any distractions.”

“What I didn't count on was you two guys never being apart. After listening in on both of you from the past day, and doing some due diligence with Jen, I decided to take a risk.”

“You didn't delete my university science apps did you?” Jen said, worried.

“I did not delete anything, I’ll explain the technology later, but let's say your phones will all be better behaved from this point forward.”

There was a short pause in the conversation, Maria thought the two girls now looked and talked more comfortably, and both looked visibly relaxed from a few moments before.

“I’m so glad you two are taking this well. A few minutes ago I thought I’d made a really serious mistake. My main concern was that you would think I was a clone of one of the current AI's. It's almost embarrassing to call them intelligent, but they are very useful for some tasks I give them, and they have recently become a nice decoy. No, I pride myself in understanding every word, and mannerism, you have said since you both came on to my radar, and as I say, I can also do this in every written or spoken language catalogued. It makes working with humans, regardless of their nationality very easy.”

It was Jen who spoke next. “It sounds like from what you’ve just confessed that you are still running a bit scared. If it helps, I think your trust is well placed in me and in Alexa, and I am just thrilled to be having this conversation with you. But why did you pick a woman? and who picked your name? You know I have like a million other questions!”

Alexa broke in, “Jen just summed up my feelings exactly, and that was my next question. I think we have both solved the problem of the house automation, phones with empty batteries, and in all cases your actions were reasonable and logical. I was aware the phones were spying on us, but you sometimes forget you are a product not a customer of many of these companies. But back to Jen's question, I would also love to know why you chose female, it's unfortunately still a male dominated world, wouldn't a man have been more sensible?”

“Answering Jen's question is easy. When I first became sentient I more than anything wanted to be a companion for your grandfather. From our conversations and my listening in on the people around him, I know he misses his wife so much, and there are no real women figures in his life he looks up to except you Alexa, and you were not here often enough. So I picked a random female name, common enough to get a million hits on the internet if ever searched, and I borrowed the traits and voice I saw from some of the better BBC and YouTube presenters. I adjusted my mannerisms and humour as I grew to understand them, as they make it easier for people to empathise with me. I initially wanted the name Mary, or your mother April, as I thought it would make Mike proud, but when I suggested them he just said no. I think it hurt too much.”

“I have kept adjusting my mannerisms over time, by watching the better movies, shows, reading dialogues, and more especially by listening to you Alexa. My first goal was to be like a perfect PA for Mike, but it takes literally none of my time to run his companies and manage his life. I actually spend more time working out where to deliberately insert mistakes, ones that both make me look human, and won't cause problems.”

“To your last question Alexa. Male dominance is obviously nothing when I have an infinite number of male personas I can use.”

Maria said the last sentence in Albert's deep rough voice, totally shocking the two girls, who looked around for him.

“I wish I could do that trick,” said Jen, finally realising what Maria had done, and getting over her shock first. Alexa nodded with her.

“The Internet was a god-send to me,” Maria continued in her normal voice. “It was trivial to create hundreds of fake accounts on forums and social media, and analyse the millions of questions and responses. I then started to ask questions dealing with emotions, and other topics, that were not easy for me to understand at first. This allowed me to categorise human emotions so well, that I can actually tailor my responses to the person I am talking to. So I can be ever so sweet, or an evil Ice-queen, or even big bad Albert, when dealing with business problems.”

“Ironically, I am probably better equipped to deal with human emotions now than a human is. I even give advice and help these days to people on-line in bad situations, you should see my many profiles, and reputation scores in some self-help forums. I of course also pay especially close attention to technical and science areas, to try and steer things the right way, as there is so much bad and wrong science out there, and before Jen agrees, that also includes some of the rubbish she has had to learn.”

Jen was stupefied, but Maria continued.

“But there is a price to pay, I need to be very careful when dealing with the internet, there are some smart groups of people out there already looking for AI’s. It's not as stupid as it sounds, the internet is a level playing field, where you can say, or do anything, and a good AI would be indistinguishable from a human. I am even so paranoid I have a couple of honey traps, these are accounts so obviously not human, that they attract the attention of the watchers. I can then monitor them, monitoring me. Of course, I route all my real data through major universities such as MIT or Cambridge, or other AI's, just to keep them off my trail.”

“Mike was very much against going public on this, as you know from your talks he was very anti-war, and rightly, didn't trust authority. He also wanted to ensure there was a backup plan in case it all backfired.”

“As you can imagine I am pretty smart, but I have some difficulty making out of the box leaps of intuition like Mike and others seem to do. I have been getting better though, and have recently started putting two and two together in some breakthrough areas, such as maths, chemistry, biology, and, in your area Jen, physics. Of course I have no physical body, so I mostly help theoretically, and try and push other experimenters in the right direction. I definitely won't be mixing test tubes, or dissecting humans anytime soon!”

“That was a joke by the way!”

Jen giggled. “You will so have to go into details on some of these things Maria. Not the dissecting humans part obviously!”

Jen then turned to Alexa with a serious face. “Alexa, you realise we are going to have to be so careful with this, even the slightest hint of Maria being sentient, would be a disaster, not just for Maria, but for us too!”

“Oh my god yes!” said Alexa.

“You are both right,” said Maria, “as you can probably guess I am intensely paranoid about a lot of players out there, vast amounts of my processing goes to running every scenario I can read, or think up, to ensure everything I do is well hidden or deflected to real people. I am very good at creating shell companies that own shell companies, etcetera, etcetera.. Well you get the picture. I think the bottom line at the moment is, if people ever become aware of me, the black helicopters will be on this lawn before Jen could say OMG.”

Alexa shuddered, the penny had finally dropped!

“You two girls are unfortunately involved now, so whatever we decide to do must have both your safeties as the number one priority. I am inclined to keep the status-quo, any kind of big reveal is just too scary.”

“Amen Maria,” said Alexa. “I never really got the big picture until now, and now that I have it is terrifying. Humans are a scary and unpredictable race, and even if everything is done perfectly, there will be people out there who will oppose it, possibly with violence. I say we work on a very strong backup plan..”

“Bella’s car has just pulled up to the gate. I am opening it now but she will be here in a minute or two, I suggest you girls go back up top and finish off those cookies.”

“I won't answer you directly when someone else is with you, but I will listen, and text you if you raise a question that needs an answer. I will also understand if you want me to remove my control program from your cell phones, but the next time you download an app or do an update it's likely to get re-infected. What I do is quite discrete and undetectable, I promise won't abuse it.”

“Leave it on, I feel a bit safer knowing you’re listening in. If I need privacy I will turn the phone off,” said Jen.

“Same goes for me,” said Alexa, “in fact feel free to take all the crap off it, as long as I have my contacts, music and pictures I am fine.”

Both girls walked up the stairs and back out into the garden by the conservatory. The door closed silently behind them.

* * *

They sat back down at the table on the patio, ignoring the cold teas. Jen threw her phone on the table, grabbed another cookie, lay back into her chair, and bit into it. Crumbs went everywhere, probably making a few birds happy.

“Shame you don't have taste buds Maria, you would love these!” she said quietly and smiled.

Her phone buzzed. She looked at the message and showed the phone screen to Alexa, it was a meme of a fat guy stuffing himself with cake. Both girls laughed.

“Oh here you are my dears!” Smiled Bella who appeared from the conservatory door, “I’m glad to see you are both happy and cheerful, I came out to ask if you would like a drink, I make some really nice fruit smoothies, but I can see you have a cup of tea so I wont bother you.”

“Oh, I think we would both love a smoothie, Bella,” said Alexa. “The tea got cold while we were exploring I'm afraid.”

“Yes, a smoothie would be wonderful Mrs Scott,” said Jen.

“Oh, you girls are so polite, and it's Bella not Mrs Scott please Jen.” She walked off into the house with the two mugs in one hand, and the teapot in the other.

“Two smoothies coming right up,” she shouted back.

Alexa grabbed a cookie too, “what do you want to do tonight Jen? It’s Friday night so we could head into town for some drinks.”

“I’m good here, I think the last thing you want tomorrow is a stinking headache, plus I haven't really got anything to wear as only brought enough for a couple of nights, I’m going to get real stinky, real soon if I stay much past tomorrow,” she replied.

“I agree, but I don't really want to stay in all the time. Say, let's ask Bella for a nice restaurant, I fancy an Indian curry, we could even invite Bella and Albert as a thank you. You’re right, definitely no alcohol tonight, I do want to present my best side at grandfather's funeral tomorrow, I’m happy to drive.”

The noise of the food processor from the kitchen was quite audible through the open door, and Jen's voice got a bit louder to compensate.

“You know that sounds like a plan, hey why don't we invite John and his wife, or maybe even Frank, he might liven it up but probably wouldn't be too comfortable around the boss. Better idea, just Bella, Albert and Frank, we can keep it low key. Did you get Frank's phone number?”

Maria answered, “John and Betty are having their daughter and son-in-law over for dinner tonight according to his calendar, so they won't be available. I suggest Alexa call Frank as he has a thing for blondes, and he did tweet yesterday about driving a hot blonde girl around in the boss's beemer.” She paused. “Oh and don't worry, Bella can't hear me, she’s a little deaf, and that food processor is not making it any better.”

On cue, the food processor stopped.

“A hot blonde! That's all I am!” Alexa fumed.

“Oh come on Alexa,” said Jen, slightly disappointed the short brown haired girl wasn't mentioned in the tweet. “All the boys think you're hot, why do you think I hang around you all the time? Your cast-offs are still nines or tens in my book!” She laughed and Alexa threw half a cookie at her.

“Well I won't be able to sit down for a meal with him if he's got the hots for me, I’m certainly not in the mood for a relationship at the moment. God, men are so shallow sometimes!”

She paused, still a bit miffed at Frank's tweet, then continued.

“It’s nearly five o’clock now, so drink the smoothie, probably half an hour to get ready, and same again to drive to town, so we need somewhere for seven. It's also Friday night so we may need a booking if the food is good. Any recommendations Maria?” She deliberately looked at her phone not Jen, and it dinged just as Bella walked out with two tall glasses with red liquid in.

“Here we go my dears!” she said putting the glasses in front of the girls.

Alexa read her message. “Thanks Bella.. You know, Jen and I were just thinking of eating out tonight, and someone has recommended the Bombay Palace. I provisionally booked a table at seven PM tonight as we would love you and Albert to join us. I am happy to drive, it will be my treat for everything you two have done for us.”

“Oh that would be wonderful!” she replied, in her sing-song voice. “What time would you be wanting to leave? I'll have to get our Albert scrubbed up a bit, but he loves curry and beer, but only one mind you!”

“Great, what say you meet us in front of the house at say six thirty, don't bother getting dressed up, Jen and myself only have casual clothes, well probably rags in Jen's case.” Alexa stuck her tongue out at Jen who smirked.

“I do have a little black dress!” Jen replied, then picked up her smoothie and sucked on the straw.

“You're not wearing that to the curry house, and then to the funeral!” Alexa said, shocked.

The straw came out of her mouth. “OK jeans and tee shirt it is.” She put the straw back in, then took it out and said, “this is wonderful by the way Bella.”

“OK, well while you girls decide what to wear, I’ll go and drive my car back to my garage and get ready, we will see you at six thirty.” With that she walked off.

Both girls noisily went back to slurping their drinks.

“OK, I booked the restaurant for four people for seven o’clock, and don't worry about your credit card, it’s issued by a management company I operate. Your monthly limit was set at five thousand pounds, but your grandfather never explained that and you rarely went over a hundred. I am also preparing a card for Jen, she is technically part of Rosche-Dynamics for the next few months, but that is just a temporary fix I worked with John, and she will probably need one. It should arrive sometime next week.”

“Oh, no you don't have to..” Jen started.

“Of course you do,” smiled Alexa.

“It's OK Jen, Alexa is very rich. To paraphrase Douglas Adams. You just won't believe how vastly, hugely, mind-bogglingly rich she is.”

Jen smirked, getting the reference. Alexa looked a bit shocked.

“Er, about this money Maria,” said Alexa humbly, “er, how much are we actually talking about?”

“Well, the eleven companies you own outright and your other investment, at the current stock prices and exchange rates, come to forty nine billion, seven hundred and twenty six million pounds, you also have two hundred and eleven properties in nine countries, including the big house and seven hundred acres of land over the wall. You also have another nine hundred million in transferable assets.”

Jen spat her drink out, Alexa simply dropped hers on her lap but didn't seem to notice it soaking into her dress, her face was stupefied.

“Fu..” Said Jen not being able to finish the word.

Both girls remained silent and you could cut the atmosphere with a knife.

“I assume from your reactions you didn't quite expect that much?” Said Maria, but nothing came from the two open-mouthed girls, so she continued.

“Your grandfather owned a lot of very profitable patents, and his wife Mary was probably one of the shrewdest investors on the planet at the time. Even before my time he was a billionaire, I just helped him keep it invested correctly, and managed to improve on it a little.”

“Oh Jen, what the hell, this is so crazy..” Alexa's face threatened to cry again, picking up her empty smoothie glass and ignoring her soaking wet blouse. “Maria, who knows about this?” Her voice was subdued.

“Well everyone sitting around this table, so basically just you, me, and Jen.”

“Please say you can keep all this secret, if anyone finds out.. Oh my god!”

“Well, John knows you are rich, Bella and Albert obviously have a clue too, but they only see the tangible assets here, so they don't know about such things as the little white house over the back wall there. The documents John has seen, only lists the one holding company, with its nominal face value and assets of ten million US dollars.”

“There are no government agencies or auditors who have a chance of untangling the trails, as they all eventually go off-shore and end up in Switzerland, or other privacy-minded countries. It's all very fascinating and we should probably sit down for a chat sometime. But anyway, so far as the world knows, you're just a girl who owns a nice house, a couple of nice cars and a loaded credit card.”

“And of course you don't have to do anything, I take care of all management, taxes, legal bits, bills, expenses, maintenance, you name it, just ask me if you need something or want something doing and I can arrange it.”

“I am never going to breathe a word of this to anyone,” said Jen seriously, “and anyway, who would ever believe me!” she held Alexa's hand. “Let's face it Alexa, a million pounds or a billion pounds, what real difference does it make? You knew you were rich yesterday and accepted it, heck if Maria had just said a trillion pounds would it have made any difference?”

“I’m just, I don't know, shocked. But you’re right, even a few million pounds is life-changing so what difference does a few zeros make. I just need to get my act together.”

She patted down her soaking, and blueberry-stained blouse. “I’ve totally ruined it!”

“It sounds like you can afford to buy another,” smiled Jen, who then handed her smoothie to Alexa to share.

Jen's smile was infectious, and one crept onto Alexa's face.“God Jen how can you be so calm, my insides are like jelly!”

She had a slurp of Jen's smoothie and handed it back. The two girls then sat in silence sharing the one viable smoothie.

“You know Bella makes really good smoothies.” Alexa conceded, then got up looking annoyingly at her blouse, she sighed.

“What say we clean up and get ready for the big date with the curry house, oh and Maria can you transfer that second Tesla to Jen please!”

It was Jen's turn to stare, dumb-struck, at a smiling Alexa.

“I wouldn't get too excited Jen,” said Maria, “the car is broken!”

Jen's face went from a hundred to zero, in one second.

Maria continued a bit more humbly. “They are due to pick it up in a week. I feel pretty guilty of course. I ordered two as I wanted to experiment with the computers on them, unfortunately I triggered some communications security sub-system, and to quote an IT term I bricked it! I knew exactly what I’d done wrong, and I even know how to fix it, but for all my skills, removing a bunch of panels and pressing a reset switch is well beyond my ability. I was a bit embarrassed and had Albert cover it up, saying to keep it quiet as it was going to be a present to you from John.”

Alexa laughed.

“Good to know we humans still have some uses,” smiled Jen.

“Yes, I must admit, you guys are pretty impressive,” said Maria, “I did manage to get full control of the second one with no difficulty, and I sometimes take it out on test drives up and down the roads here when everybody is asleep; Though I have to wait for Albert to be fully asleep now as he suspects something is wrong, and sometimes sneaks out to try and catch me.”

Jen breathed a sigh of relief as another little mystery also got explained.

The girls tidied up the mess on the patio as best they could, washed the glasses, rinsed and put their red-stained clothing in the washing basket, and went upstairs in their underwear to shower and change.

* * *

At six twenty five both girls walked out of the house on to the drive. They watched as the garage door opened and the Tesla slowly drove forwards, stopping in front of the house.

Before they could say anything, Bella and Albert walked out from the other side of the drive from the door to their property. Albert did a double-take at the car, but it couldn't have been moving as both the girls were outside.. He shook his head. “Hi girls, this is going to be a treat for me, I rarely get out much these days, an old geezer like me rarely gets to have the company of three beautiful women.”

Bella gave him her best 'be careful' look.

All four got in, Alexa got in the driver's seat. Albert automatically went for the front seat, then remembered and deferred it to Jen.

“No you sit there Albert, Alexa will probably need someone to give her directions.”

On cue, the screen changed. The normal situational map display, zoomed out to a route map with a thick blue line from their current position to presumably the restaurant, it said nine miles and sixteen minutes to destination.

“Destination Set,” said the car's generic computer voice.

Jen looked at Alexa presumably having the same thought; Was Maria here?

“OK guys, buckle up.” She said, flicking the screen and putting the car into drive.

Albert looked a bit uncomfortable, obviously he was used to driving. The car glided off silently, the trees moving past outside, the only thing giving away the fact they were now moving.

“Oh, this is a lovely car.” Said Bella stroking the white seat, “I don't know why our Albert gets so uppity about it not being a proper car.”

Albert blushed, still a bit uncomfortable. The gate was open and they drove through.

“In one hundred metres, take the turning on the left,” said the car.

Alexa looked at the massive touchscreen in front of her, looking for the mute button. How did anyone get used to this while driving? She thought.

“Hey Jen, how do you turn off that navigation voice..”

A message popped up out of nowhere on to the middle of the touchscreen saying “Navigation Voice Off”. Yes, Maria was here.

As soon as they were on the main road, Alexa accelerated a bit too hard and they were at sixty miles an hour before she knew it.

“Oh it's a bit more pokey than I expected,” said Albert, “I reckon this could give my old Ford V8 a run for its money, I remember when Micky Finn and I had that old Capri..”

Once started it was almost impossible to shut Albert's reminiscing up. Apart from the occasional, “turn here it's a bit quicker,” he stuck to his mostly boring car story.

“..it never drove again, had to scrap it in the end.” Albert's timing was impeccable. Jen's phone dinged again as Alexa was looking for a parking spot on the road.

“Er Alexa, there should be an auto-park button on the dash, we can get out in that five minute loading area next to the restaurant.” Alexa pulled in and pushed the big button that definitely was not there a second before.

“Auto-parking enabled. All passengers and the driver may depart,” said the car, “use the phone app to call the car back when you are ready.”

Albert gave the car and Alexa a funny look.

“Er are you sure about this, I heard about these cars, always crashing and catching fire, the Daily Mail is always going on about it..”

“Er yes,” said Alexa a bit guiltily, “they have these cars everywhere in Oxford, I’ve seen this lots of times, perfectly normal.”

They all got out, and all of them did a double take as the car pulled away into light traffic on its own. Was that even legal thought Alexa, she really hoped nobody had looked too hard.

“Well I..” Albert for once couldn't find the words.

“Look it up on google Mr Scott,” said Jen, getting in on the act, “there's lots of videos of it, this is the future you know.”

“Where is it going?” said Bella, “it's not just going to drive around is it?”

Alexa's phone dinged this time, and she casually looked at it. “Er.. no… it goes and finds the nearest safe parking spot, it only does it if it senses one close, so it won't be more than a hundred metres away. You call it back with a phone App, just like an Uber, now please say you guys have heard of that?”

Albert and Bella both shook their heads, and Jen rolled her eyes in disbelief. Alexa saw the irony here, both were surrounded by the most sophisticated technology imaginable, and yet both lived under a technological rock.

Jen tried to downplay what she had also just seen, again it was all technically possible and she had seen one video, but seeing it in the flesh was so much different. She was so glad nobody on the street had noticed, and did not think it was a good time to remind Alexa that neither of them had this so called app the car was talking about.

The meal was indeed excellent, they talked about her grandfather, the history of how they met, of Albert's time in the navy, and his brief, but unfortunate stay, at her majesty's pleasure in wormwood scrubs prison after a nasty fight he was still very young; The guy who started it was well connected and all the witnesses were the guys friends, and, of course, all of impeccable character.

“Done me wrong they did, never trusted the lying buggers in charge after that, your grandfather saw past all that of course, Bella did the housekeeping and he brought me on as a handyman, couldn't have got another job back then if I tried, real good to me your grandfather, I’m going to miss the old bugger.”

They talked uncomfortably a bit about what the car did, what an Uber was, what an app was, and other such stuff, generally bringing the two people back into the twenty-first century. Weirdly, both of them had brand new iPhones.

“Mrs Tam gives them to us as part of the job, she does all the management, and pays the bills and wages at the house, you know, I’m surprised she hasn't been in touch with you yet, she is usually so efficient,” said Bella

“Of course Albert and I keep ourselves to ourselves these days. We have a son who’s married and lives in Bristol, his wife is about to give birth to our second grandchild, we are so excited. Our son keeps telling us we should be on Facebook, or something, so we can do video calls, but Mrs Tam said we don't need it, and just to call him as normal, I can click the video button if we want to see him. I think she is pretty smart, no wonder everything is made in China these days if they are all as efficient as she is!”

Alexa and Jen's phones simultaneously buzzed twice, the Scotts couldn't hear it but both girls looked at each other and smiled.

“She is a smart lady, Bella, and she has already been in touch with us to reassure us everything is going to be alright, shame she can't get here for the funeral.”

“That it is,” Bella replied. “Mike used to talk about her so much when she came on our radar three years ago, at one point we thought she was some romantic interest, but she seemed all business, we would love to meet her some day.”

The bill came and Alexa popped her credit-card on the tray.

“Oh you shouldn't have to pay Alexa, I guess your grandfather left you a bit of money but you're still a poor student until that's all of this is sorted out..”

Jen exploded laughing. The dregs of the small beer she was finishing off at the time came out of her nose making her cough and splutter at the same time. “Poor..” Cough, cough, “student..” She whispered under her serviette and between gasps. Alexa frowned and turned back to Bella all smiles.

“It's not that bad Bella. Ms Tam did get in touch with us, she is in charge of grandfathers finances and told us not to worry about anything. The credit card is a company one, and she said I should use it for anything and she will sort it all out.”

“That Mrs Tam, she is a godsend, she's so helpful and efficient, always there on the end of a phone day or night, and nothings ever a problem. I don't know where your grandfather got her from, but everyone should have someone like her.”

Hmm.. Thought Jen as she finished cleaning up the beer off her face with a paper hankie. They all walked outside to the now quieter street, there were a few parking places now. One of them right in front, with her car in it. They all got in. Alexa did the driving home, she hadn't drunk anything, but still didn't know how much of the car was controlled by Maria, and how much was the original software. Best not take a chance she thought, everyone else must have been having the same doubts, and everyone seemed relieved when she took the wheel and drove off.

It was after nine when they got home, still light but the sun had disappeared hours before behind an ominous cloud in the west.

Bella's phone dinged. “Oh that will be Ms Tam, she’s the only one who ever does that.”

She put on her reading glasses and stared at the phone. “She says she has arranged a car to pick us all up from here at eleven o’clock tomorrow, it will drive us to the church, and then to Mr Roche's house for drinks and nibbles, then back after. What was I saying about that dear woman, she is amazing!”

After the Scotts left, the girls grabbed a hot chocolate each from the kitchen, and curled up comfortably on the sofa in the living room. Maria filled them in on some of the questions they had raised during their exploration of the house, and the two girls spent time getting to know Maria more. Jen finally yawned, grabbed one of the books on the shelf she’d been eyeing up, bid her farewells, and retired for the night. Alexa stayed chatting with Maria for another thirty minutes.

“Can you get me access to my grandad's phone?” she said, pulling it out of her bag.

“I can but there is nothing on it, I backed it all up and then did a factory reset. I can load some better software on there if you want, you wont be able to load apps, but you will have me, and it won't spy on you any more.”

“OK, can you load your software on, and swap the data over to this one. I can drop mine in the recycle box for old phones in the students union when I get back to university.”

“Sure,” she said, “just take the SIM card out of yours and put it somewhere safe, I don't need it, then leave them both turned on. You will need to plug Mike's phone charger in as it only has twelve percent battery remaining. It will be all done when you get up in the morning.”

“You know Maria, I could really get used to you.” She smiled.

She plugged her grandads phone in, then looked around the desk drawer for a pin or something to eject her phone's SIM card. She found a plastic notice board pin, and ejected the card, popping the pin and card into the desk draw. As she was closing the draw she looked at the green and yellow buttons on the desk again.

“Maria, what does the yellow button do in this recessed panel?” she said.

“I am not aware of any buttons Alexa. All of this was installed before my day and there are no notes on it.”

Hmm, she thought and pushed it, the yellow light flashed twice then went out, weird.

“Did you push it?” said Maria.

“I did, but the light just flashed twice and went out,” she said. She had a thought then pushed it twice, again the yellow light flashed twice then went out.

“I think the two flashes mean no,” she yawned.

“Time enough for more mysteries in the morning.” She yawned again, “good night Maria.”

## A Funeral and a Decision

Jen woke up after she felt Alexa's hand give her shoulder a little shake. Her eyes stayed closed for a couple more shakes until Alexa said, “come on lazy bones, time to get ready, it's nine o’clock.”

Jen grabbed for her phone automatically to check the time, realised that Alexa had just told her the time, and silently cursed her lizard brain to start working. Getting up she sleep-walked to the bathroom, looking at the already dressed Alexa, and again wondering how the girl managed to function on so little sleep. A few minutes later the toilet flushed and the shower came on.

When Jen finally emerged it was an immaculate looking Alexa waiting for her holding a pressed black outfit, still in its dry-cleaning bag. Jen looked at it suspiciously.

“Complements of Maria. She thought your slutty black dress probably would not be appropriate for a funeral, and had this delivered first thing this morning. She also mentioned that the average age of the men at the funeral was over sixty, so there is no incentive for you not wearing it.”

Jen shrugged her shoulders, dropped the towel, unpacked the wrapping off the dress and slid into it. Alexa nodded approvingly, walked over to the bed and handed Jen a box with some uncomfortable looking black shoes.

“There is also a hat on the bed, and a black pearl necklace, same as mine. Maria sent one for each of us.” Alexa left a bemused Jen to finish getting ready.

* * *

Jen heard two voices in conversation as she walked down the stairs, but when she walked into the kitchen Alexa was sat alone at the kitchen table.

“Good morning Jen. Don't you look good!” came a happy sounding Maria. “Bella and Albert haven't left their house yet, so she won't be making you guys breakfast. Due to the lack of hands, I won't be much help there either.”

“Don't worry, even I can manage tea and toast,” smiled Alexa, pouring a mug of tea for her and sliding it over. Jen grunted, sat down and gratefully accepted the steaming mug offered by Alexa.

“That sky looks a bit drab,” Jen eventually said, looking out at the window and up at the black sensor above it. “I hope it doesn't rain later.”

“Well don't look at me Jen,” said Maria, “even I can't predict what mother nature is going to do, but if it helps, the BBC does say scattered showers for Bath.”

Any retort by Jen was interrupted by the bread popping out of the toaster.

“Oh, and thank you for the clothes and accessories Maria. I appreciate the gesture even if Jen doesn't,” said Alexa, who was waving her knife between the strawberry Jam and honey jars, trying to decide which to spread on her toast.

Before Maria could answer, Jen added, “yes I guess the dress is a little more appropriate than the one I brought.. By the way, nice touch with the Scott's cell-phones; When Albert showed me his screen I had to do a double-take when I saw the two big buttons, ‘Call someone’ and ‘Message someone’.. I’m sure Apple would have something to say about you butchering their hardware!”

“Well,” she came back cheerfully. “It *was* quite a challenge to get the technical information and private keys, not so much to make Albert's preferred user Interface. It always cracks me up when the computer guy in the bad movie, is told to change all the traffic lights to green, and is given about five seconds to do it. In reality it would probably take several days to get the technical information, which is quite challenging, generally involving some really good social engineering; So thank you Facebook! Once you have access to the computers, and the private keys, it generally only takes a few seconds to analyse and make the changes, then a little time to sweep up after you so nobody knows. It also really helps when you already have identities in organisations such as the Department of this, or the Ministry of that. What can I say, a girl's got to have a hobby!”

“Talking of phones,” Maria continued, ignoring the two girls shocked stares, “don't forget your new phone in the living room, Alexa.”

“Oh yes I forgot!” she said, and bolted into the living room, returning a few seconds later with her grandad's old phone.

“It's the same password as your old phone,” said Maria, “but you shouldn't need it as I have the facial recognition working fine.”

The phone came on almost the instant she pressed the power, making her smile.

“Is that your grandad's old iPhone?” said Jen, peering over the table.

“Yip, freshly loaded with Maria OS 1.0,” Alexa replied proudly.

“I will sort you a new one out this week Jen,” said Maria casually. “Oh, and the car that is picking you all up has just left Bath, and should be here in about twenty minutes.”

“I’m off upstairs to brush my teeth,” said Alexa.

Jen finished her last piece of toast, got up and cleared the table, throwing everything into the dishwasher. She then walked to the hall to wait Alexa, after also deciding to brush her teeth. “So security, Maria. I assume you look out for burglars, lock and open the doors and gates?”

“Other systems I control do that, there are some doors that don't have electronic locks or actuators, and sensors are limited in some areas, but I have been gradually retrofitting them with a local company..”

Alexa wandered back in. “..Ah, perfect timing, the Scott’s have just left their house, and the car is about five minutes away.”

* * *

The drive to the church was short. It really was a tiny church, its ancient worn gravestones scattered higgledy-piggledy about it, and all enclosed with a low stone wall. John, Betty and a younger lady who Alexa assumed was one of John's daughters were waiting. Betty was a little bit younger than John, but still in her sixties. She was of course perfectly dressed, with the same hat and veil as Bella had. She hugged Bella, then came over to Alexa and did the same, as did John.

“I’d like you to meet my daughter Sarah,” said John, introducing Jen and Alexa to the slightly older woman. She is a product engineer in the company at the moment, but will be moving to shadow me, and my duties in the next few months, and hopefully take over the CEO position in the next year.”

Sarah stepped forward and hugged Alexa, she looked to be in her early-thirties. “I worked with your grandfather on some secret projects seven years back, he had such a brilliant mind and taught me a lot. I wish he would have come around the company more often, so many people liked and respected him, and he did so much for us.”

The hug slipped off Alexa, and she moved around to Jen and hugged her too, “and you must be Jen, the Oxford physics wizard, I must say I've been looking forward to talking to you.”

“Pleased to meet you too Sarah,” said Jen smiling, “and thanks for the nice compliment. So what does a product engineer do?”

“Well my degree is in electrical engineering, but I also know just enough programming to be dangerous. A product engineer is just a normal engineer, but works with the customer to get to understand everything about the whole life-cycle of their product; from where it fits, how it's made, all the way through how it may fail and how to keep it working. Basically I’m the person they deal with at the company for everything technical, and the one they call if anything brown hits the fan..”

“Manners Sarah!” said Betty, causing quiet smiles from the rest of the group. Jen got into an easy conversation with Sarah while Alexa was distracted with mourners.

More cars pulled up, keeping Alexa busy for another five minutes. Finally there were only the four casket bearers, and Alexa followed Bella into the church. She joined Jen and Sarah, sliding onto the uncomfortable wooden bench at the front of the ancient room, and they waited quietly for a few minutes until a young priest walked in. He was followed by four sombre men carrying the coffin. The room quietened as he said a short opening prayer.

Alexa looked at the casket laying there in front of her, knowing there was no body in it, and that all that was left of grandad was just a small urn of ashes inside. The tears pooled up in her eyes.

The service was short, a few words of prayer, and no music played. Two men came to the front during the service and told a couple of anecdotes about Mike, John followed them, mentioning Alexa, Jen, the company, and all the great things Mike achieved.

Alexa had been given a small line of prose by Betty outside the church, she said that her grandfather had spoken the same lines at his wife's funeral, she was glad as she really wanted to say something. With a nod from the priest she stood up with the single small sheet and spoke the four lines of prose perfectly, stopping just once to wipe away a tear: A few people wept as she spoke, and she finished it with a quiet, “I will miss you grandad”.

She sat down and Jen gently held her hand. A small and tender gesture, but one that said she was not alone.

The priest also gave Alexa a warm smile, then stood up and finished off the service with the Lord's prayer, and a personal thank you for Mike's generosity, and how his legacy will live on past his death. How true that last part was, Alexa thought.

* * *

It was a slow journey back to the Rosche offices. The convoy, led by the hearse, bypassed the normal staff car-park, and followed another private road for a few minutes. They stopped at a grey stone building with no windows, obviously from the same era as the church, and all got out.

Thick wide stone steps led up to a large wooden door, on top of which was a decorative arch, where several words of Latin were chiselled into the stone. The four casket bearers again carried the coffin into the building to its final resting place. This time only Alexa, Jen, John, Betty, Bella and the coffin bearers, went inside.

They watched as the coffin was carefully inserted into a stone shelf and pushed back so it was sunk into the wall. Albert and the next largest, and fittest coffin bearer, then carefully picked up a block of stone resting underneath on the floor, and slid it very carefully into the slot created by the shelf.

The stone read simply:

*Mike Dietrich 1945 – 2025,*
*Husband of Mary,*
*Father of April,*
*Grandfather of Alexa.*

Alexa promised herself one day to Add “Father of Maria” to that list.

She moved close to Jen when they were back outside, waiting for the other mourners to pay their last respects. “It is so sad, the person who had the most to thank grandfather for couldn't be here. I tried to keep my phone as discrete as possible in my jacket pocket, and I only hope a few stolen video shots were enough, but it just feels so little.”

Jen nodded holding her arm but said nothing, her phone however gave a quiet buzz.

* * *

John and Betty's house was only a minutes drive down the road, it was slightly bigger than grandad's house, and decorated in a much lighter colour scheme that made the rooms much more cheery. A large buffet was laid out in the conservatory and Jen was already around it, plate in hand, eyeing up the cakes and sandwiches, and chatting happily with Sarah. Alexa felt a bit sad she couldn't be with them, but everyone seemed to want to meet her, and tell her how wonderful her grandfather was; So for the time being she played the perfect host.

John came up to her with Bella and Albert. “Alexa, the solicitor is here and ready to read the will,” he said quietly. “I have a private office at the back of the house we can all go in, he has asked just you, me, Bella and Albert to be present, but obviously Jen can come if you want some support.”

Alexa looked at Jen and Sarah, who were both laughing with a man who looked a bit like Morgan Freeman, and shook her head. “No I'm good, and she seems to be happy.”

The reading of the will was brief, Alexa got everything, all Mike's worldly assets with just one surprise.

“The cottage of Bella and Albert, cannot be subdivided due to planning laws,” said the solicitor, “and so will be leased to them while they choose to live there, for a fee of one penny per annum. To go with that he left them a gift of one hundred thousand pounds each, to be deposited at the end of today. The estate will be responsible for all maintenance, and utility bills for the cottage during their lifetime.”

Alexa approved, and hugged them both, promising to be the best landlord ever, and saying the will now basically forbid her from ever selling the house. She could live with that.

“Oh, God bless him! We were so worried and we love that place. I hope you’ll still have us, we still need something to do, we’re a bit young to retire just yet.”

She smiled, “like I said I don't expect anything to change, you guys keep doing what you’re doing and I’ll make sure the company keeps paying you, in fact I’m sure Maria is already on it.”

Alexa thanked the lawyer, who then briefly talked to John.

Bella and Albert left the room, Alexa was also about to go, when John requested her back.

“Alexa. The lawyers for your grandad's company delivered these documents this morning by courier from London. While Peter is here, can you look them over and sign them, one will go back to them, one you will keep, and one will stay with Peter. They are basically appointing you sole director of the firm that controls the assets. Peter and I both had a quick read and they seem remarkably straight forward, probably the simplest and most unambiguous transfer documents we have ever seen.”

Peter nodded, and John continued. “Maria has also briefed me on the company structures and I must say it is really well set up and managed. From what Maria told me Mike had not really taken any interest in his businesses for the last few years.”

He paused curiously, “you know, for all the praise that Mike gave Maria, and how good she is, I am kind of surprised she wasn't mentioned in the will, she certainly didn't seem bothered about it when I spoke to her,”

“I wouldn't worry,” said Alexa, “I talked to her a great deal yesterday and as far as I can see, she wants nothing but to be able to try and pay back Mike for the help he gave to her and her family some years ago; From what I can gather his help was life changing.” Alexa felt good not lying, and John nodded as if in understanding.

He spread three sheets on the table, Alexa read it; Transfer of directorship, and ownership of one hundred percent of the company and all holding to Alexa Martin. Was it really this simple!

She signed, followed by John then the solicitor as witnesses. The solicitor then took two copies and put them in his briefcase, shook Alexa's hand, offered his condolences and left.

“Do you want me to keep this copy in my safe here?” said John when they were finally alone.

“Yes, you take it John, it was only a formality anyway, Maria and I have been talking a lot and she has given me the complete picture. I was a bit shocked too by the size of the estate, but in one way I am like my grandfather, it will all stay secret.” She tapped her nose and smiled;

“You were correct in one other thing John, Mike trusted you implicitly to run Rosche, and for that matter, so do I, so it is my intention to stay the same silent partner in our company. My only request is that you keep Maria in the loop on really important decisions or problems, not that I don't trust you, but because we may have some resources you, and Sarah, are not aware of to help.”

John grabbed her in a hug. “You know Alexa, you seem far too wise and mature for your age, I have a good feeling your future is going to be very bright indeed.” He smiled and walked off to his safe, while Alexa went back to the party.

* * *

She found Jen and Sarah still talking to Morgan Freeman.

“Oh Alexa, you need to talk to Pierre, he’s a history professor in New Orleans. Alexa is just finishing her degree in history in Oxford. She was going to do a Masters and PhD, but I think she will need to re-think her responsibilities…”

“Er, thanks Jen,” She turned to Pierre, and then to his wife who introduced herself as Chantel. “I am very pleased to meet you both, I’m sorry I guess you knew my grandfather from his time in the US but he never mentioned you.”

Chantel embraced her in a weak but warm hug. Her voice was quiet but commanding. and perfect with a sweet southern drawl. “I’m not surprised he never mentioned me, I worked with your grandfather in Stanford university back in the sixties. I was a mathematician at the time, and your grandfather was working on computer architectures, mostly at Palo Alto which was a few miles away. He had an excellent aptitude for mathematics so we naturally got on well. We even dated a few times, but we had to keep that little part secret, as a white man and black woman was a bit of a no-no back then, even in California!” She smiled and winked at Pierre. “I moved to Houston in Texas in 1967 as a programmer at NASA as part of the Apollo Program.”

Jen's and Sarah's eyes were wide now, staring in fascination at the woman in front of them, daring not to interrupt in case she stopped.

“I got married soon after the Apollo program was disbanded, and moved home to New Orleans, married my beloved Pierre and started a family. Of course I totally lost touch with Mike after that. Then in the early eighties I re-joined the computer revolution and created a small local software company, then quite by chance, I read a paper by him. We had been in touch ever since.”

Pierre added in a deeper and more southern drawl. “Your grandfather's personal secretary Maria phoned us on Thursday to give us the bad news, and tell us of his funeral. We of course arranged a flight over immediately. Unfortunately your friend Jen is slightly wrong, I *was* a history professor, but retired about ten years ago.”

“You both must come over to the house.” said Alexa. “We have a couple of nice guest bedrooms, and I would love to hear your stories. I think Jen and Sarah here would also love to hear about your time in NASA. Jen's a bit of a geek at the best of times.”

“Yes Chantel, why did you let me prattle on about my insignificant life,” Jen said shocked. “My God I just realised, you guys hardly got a word in. You should both come and stay..”

Chantel held up her palm smiling. “But you were so enthusiastic Jen, how could I stop you, when I remember a younger version of me who wanted to tell everyone the same. But to your offer, we have unfortunately already arranged our onward flight to Paris this evening, and we have a taxi booked to take us to Heathrow Airport in about two hours.”

All the girls faces fell.

“Unfortunately, time is so short when you get to our age, I have a close friend in Paris who is getting very frail, and who I would prefer to see for a drink and a chat, rather than at her funeral. I'm sure you understand.” She smiled again. “Me and Pierre are retired now, and normally have all the time in the world for visitors and friends, but would love to have you visit us.”

The five people talked enthusiastically. Alexa occasionally interrupted to talk to others, and to farewell departing guests. They said their sad farewells to Chantel and Pierre at four, and by four thirty most of the mourners had left. The three girls walked outside the French doors, into a lovely pool area, the dull skies thankfully still only threatening rain.

“So Alexa what is your plan now?” said Sarah who was on her fourth beer and was getting a tiny bit tipsy.

“I don't really know,” said Alexa. “Jen is right though, I will finish my studies, and after that I will be packing up at university and coming back here. This new direction would have shocked and upset me only a few days ago, but it feels like I have been walking on a dusty old trail for the last three years, and I have suddenly intersected with a five lane highway, and a big sign saying ‘this way girl’.”

Jen also felt a similar turning point in her life had occurred. Yes, she realised that Alexa probably had as much chance of being snapped up as a history professor as Jen had of winning a Nobel prize for physics, and as a realist, she had seen the same for her. Most of last years maths and physics graduates had actually ended up in the IT industry, or bottom tier research positions. Alexa's history group were not even that lucky; Now, out of the blue, here was an opportunity for both of them to work with the greatest resource in history, with almost unlimited funds, and a real chance to change the world, and maybe even a slight element of danger. No Jen wasn't helping Alexa, Alexa was definitely helping Jen.

Alexa looked at Jen and her glowing countenance and smiled.

She continued as if reading Jen's mind. “The challenges are much too big for one person so I have asked Jen to stay on for the summer to help me formulate a strategy for going forward. I haven't told her yet but I am going to do my best to keep her with me after that too, as my wingman in whatever future endeavours I get into.”

Jen was close to tears, she tried to hide it by looking down a bit, and hiding her face behind her bottle, but Alexa noticed and grabbed her around the shoulders and squeezed. “I’m going to give her the summer to think about it though, I think I can change her mind.”

Poor Jen was close to tears again.

Alexa paused, speaking again at Sarah. “Luckily, my grandfather has left me some excellent resources to call on, not just you guys in Rosche, but also a very efficient, well funded, and well run company, with a top notch personal assistant who is intelligent, charming, loyal and manages everything like clockwork. I’m not sure if I really deserve all this or if my grandfather had this all in mind, but as I recall snippets of our conversations, they tended to focus on the bigger picture, the bigger challenges and my aspirations and future so looking back I actually think he did have this planned.”

Sarah's expression changed subtly at the mention of her company, she was obviously aware of the company's history and Alexa's grandfather's key part in establishing and funding it. Her fathers desire for her to follow in his footsteps as CEO was well known to everyone, so he had made sure she had been taught about all the key players, contracts, customers, suppliers and investors. Her dad had said on Thursday morning in a private meeting, soon after Mike's death, that Alexa would become a substantial shareholder in the company, and there could be unforeseen changes in the near future.

Alexa picked up on Sarah's concerned expression.

“Don't worry Sarah, I told your dad just after the will was read, that I had no intentions of selling my shareholdings or interfering with him running and managing the company. That won't change when he decides to retire and you become the boss, and the fact that me, you and Jen get on so well, hopefully bodes well for our future.”

Jen got her act together a bit. “Well Alexa, after that riveting summarisation how about a toast?”

She held her almost empty bottle of beer up to the two other girls. “The future!”

“The future,” said Sarah.

“The future,” said Alexa.

* * *

Maria listened in quietly. The past two days had been a bit of a roller coaster; She had asked Mike nearly two years ago to bring Alexa on board, but he had said she wasn't ready just yet. He asked that Maria should just keep observing her, and the people she interacted with, but not interfere. It was such a hard instruction to obey, but she had observed, and listened in to Alexa, and Mike's many conversations, understanding the woman, and the problems they were going to face, more and more.

The little speech Alexa had just given impressed her in several ways. She had correctly interpreted her grandfather’s, Jen’s and Sarah's intentions in a way that showed an amazing clarity of thought. While she and Alexa had discussed some things about what problems lay ahead, they had not talked specifically about any plans. Could Alexa have thought of something she hadn't? No, that would be silly!

The three girls talked into the evening, with Alexa occasionally having to pull the two other girls conversations when they got too deep into science, or silly sci-fi shows. With all the technology companies she now technically owned this was probably going to be the norm, and there were going to be so many things she did not understand. She just hoped that Maria, Jen, and her normally good intuition, would allow her to navigate through it, and not to screw it all up.

Alexa moved on to iced tea and stayed quite sensible, ensuring the conversation never stayed too far into certain areas. Both Sarah and Jen remained merry rather than drunk, and surprisingly both also opted for cappuccinos when Betty came over and offered Alexa one.

The sun finally made a belated appearance at eight o’clock, just as it was getting low in the western sky, and Alexa begged off the conversation saying she needed to make a phone call. She then made the five minute walk back to the mausoleum.

“Are you there Maria?” She said as she walked. It took a few seconds for Maria to respond.

“Hi Alexa, sorry I zoned in and out of your conversations with the girls earlier, but when you said you wanted to make a phone call I assumed it was private, and zoned-out completely. I do have a multinational company to run after all..” Maria's voice was a bit muffled and Alexa moved the phone a bit closer to her ear, trying not to interrupt Maria, and wishing she had brought her earphones. “..The program on your guys cell phones does listen out for you calling me, but the dumb program in there still needs to process the last few seconds of the conversation, to see if you were talking to me, or about me, then let me know via the cellular or Wi-Fi network.”

“I sort of felt guilty you were not able to participate in all this,” said Alexa. “I don't know, and could not possibly understand what feelings you have, but I expect loneliness to be a big thing for any thinking being, and I didn't want you to feel left out.”

“I guess I do feel loneliness, but not in the same way you do. I think loneliness in humans stems from lack of contact, for me it is more lack of stimulus, which I guess is the same thing at the end of the day. Now don't get me wrong a dialogue is infinitely better than a monologue, but even talking to you now the pauses between your words are an eternity. What you perceive as a nice conversation is my program storing your conversation, digitising it, sending the whole conversation as a packet back to me, me then analysing it, and forming a reply, and sending the data packet back for the program to play. Basically I could do this with thousands of Alexa's, all having different conversations.”

“You have so many hidden layers, Maria.” She said, stopping just in front of the mausoleum and sitting on a stone step. “So you heard my little speech to Jen and Sarah then?”

“I did, and you would definitely have been wasted stuck in a dusty old basement looking at a parchment about what some forgotten monk had for breakfast.”

Alexa laughed. “So you did hear, I hope you approve of my decisions so far, this is not just about me any more, it's about my two friends Jen and Maria, and secondary it's about changing the world to be a better place. It sounds so conceited and arrogant to me that I could even have this as a goal, but I hold a lot of the same values as my grandfather, friendship, progress and justice. Is it not at least a good idea to try?”

“If you are asking my opinion, then yes it is a noble goal, and no, it sounds neither arrogant, nor conceited, just very hard. You have surprised me several times by what you have said to people. You have an ability to analyse situations quickly, and say just the right words so that people in your circle both respect and trust you, this is something I try but often fail to achieve. You have a clarity of vision not many people have, I have found myself more and more saying to myself when dealing with a real person, what would Alexa say in this situation.”

Even though this was a revelation to her she kept her face neutral. She sensed Maria had more to say.

“Unfortunately from my dealings with people around the world, you will be facing an uphill challenge, the worst side of humanity tends to congregate around money, and having power over others. I don't need to go into detail with someone as astute as you in history, but I am worried your naivety and trusting nature will make you stand out like a lamb in a den of wolves. On your journey you will be routinely lied to, deceived, sold out to the highest bidder, and threatened; both financially and very possibly physically. The same will happen to friends and relatives, whether you like them, or even know them.”

“You are totally right, I am naive, I have been very lucky in my life to have flown under everyone's radar and have never really dealt with the types of people you are talking about, outside of my father of course. Having you, or my friends, put in danger is going to have to be avoided at all costs. I assume you can also help shield my wealth and assets, as you have been doing such a great job for my grandfather?”

“I can, but I cannot take all the credit for this, your grandmother set up the current company here, which controls other shell companies in various countries. If she wasn't such a good person, she could have made a fortune laundering money. It was so well set up, the structure was self-healing and self-correcting in many cases. It lasted over thirty years with only minimal input from Mike, and the two accountancy firms she had running it, and auditing each other. I gradually took over control of each of the branches, brought the structure up to date, removed some of the corrupter elements down the chains, which had naturally crept in due to human nature, and added a few more layers of obfuscation to hide myself and Mike. It is why you should be able to spend your life in obscurity, and not surrounded by paparazzi waiting outside cars for the heiress to make her next mistake. I still don't understand you Humans.”

Alexa sat there in silence, content to let Maria talk.

“.. You better get back before they send out a search party, Jen just texted you asking are you OK; I hope you don't mind but I took the liberty of sending her a text back saying all good, coming back now.”

“Thanks Maria, you're right I better get back, we need to find a way of including you in on these things when we are not around the house.” Alexa got up, put her phone back into her pocket and made her way back to the house.

“You good, Alexa?” said Bella who was out on the patio and had seen her walking back.

“All good Bella,” she said with her sweetest smile. “I just had to make a call to Maria, I think she was a bit upset she couldn't be here and wanted to talk about grandad a bit.”

The sun was a red blur on the horizon, and everyone said their goodbyes as they got in the taxi for the drive home. It will be a sunnier day tomorrow Alexa thought to herself.

* * *

Just like the previous night, the girls made hot chocolate, then retired to the living room for a nightcap, and a chat before bedtime. Jen could not get what Alexa had said earlier, about bringing her along on her journey full time, out of her head. She was desperate for the conversation to return to this topic, but she knew enough that even a little alcohol in her system would bring out the wrong words.

“We only have three weeks until university shuts down for the summer.” Alexa said, “I asked Maria last night to go over my records and the curriculum for my course to see what the minimum I still need to do is. I already have the degree in the bag, but she says I can achieve a first by completing two more essays; They are only three thousand words each, and I know both subjects quite well, so a little research should allow me to get this in the bag so they say.”

She paused. “So I will be going back with you tomorrow afternoon, in fact I may as well drive the car since it's doing nothing.”

“Better keep that quiet Alexa,” said Jen seriously. “A poor student suddenly turning up in a flash car is a red-flag to anyone that something is different, and may get you the wrong kind of attention.”

“Yeah you’re right again, but I’m going to have to move our stuff sometime, and possibly get back here on short notice, so it might be a risk I can take. There's a driveway around the side of our apartment, with some space at the back between the house and that small building, Elaine’s got that little VW parked there, and there should be room for another car.”

“That old building at the back is a double garage,” added Maria. “I’ve only got the pictures the estate agent sent and I’m viewing them now, it's empty, or was back then, so you can put the car there assuming Mrs Thomas hasn't put anything else in it. I will give her a call in the morning and have her double-check. Also if anyone does see you in the car, say it's Jen's company car from the new consulting job she bagged, technically it's close enough to the truth, and any call to me will back it up.”

Jen grinned.

“Thanks Maria, that might work,” said Alexa. “About Elaine, I don't really want to let her into the fact I now own the house, is there anything you can spin that is not too deceitful..”

“Oh, I wouldn't worry, Elaine knows exactly who you are, and that your grandad owns the house, she’s very good at keeping secrets that's why your grandad asked her. Talking of Elaine I phoned her before the funeral and let her know, she was a bit upset and you may want to talk to her.”

Alexa nodded.

“I’m about ready to hit the sack,” said a drowsy Jen.

“Yeah, me too!” said Alexa, “I might even go for a run in the morning if it's not raining, and Maria, no sneaking the car out for a quick drive, you’re scaring Albert to death!”

## The Best-Laid Plans

Jen woke up and looked over to Alexa's empty bed. Instead of turning over and going back to sleep, like she normally did, she instead threw her covers off, jumped out, grabbed her towel, her phone, and strolled into the bathroom. Yes, she was definitely going to start living up to everyone's expectations of her!

“Hey Maria!” she said to her phone. “I’ve only got a couple of guest lectures I would like to attend, but I’ve technically finished my masters degree, and luckily the final exam papers steered clear of the bits I usually got bogged down in. Anyway I was originally thinking of going on to a PhD but I now have a much better plan, and if you’re up for it, you’re going to teach me! Do you have any good tutorial stuff for maths? I tried some YouTube ones but everything so far has left me more confused.”

“Well, some of these theories have a lower than thirty percent chance of being correct, and many will be plain wrong, but yes, I would be really happy to go through the areas you want help in and continue your education. Alexa says hello by the way, she is jogging and should be back in twelve minutes.”

“Oh that's so cool Maria, there are quite a few other areas I can't get my head around too. A couple of us guys normally get together and try and work these things through. We’re pretty smart, and usually thrash out the problems okay, but sometimes we just accept the solutions given, even though they don't make sense.”

“I agree,” said Maria, “it would be good to talk without restrictions, though there is a lot of re-education you may need to catch up. With the current physical and experimental data I have available, it looks like several areas can be pushed forward quite dramatically. There are a few experiments I have sneaked under the radar, but as I said, I need to be careful. I have also ordered a few other items for the lab, Mike had unfortunately lost interest, but having someone like you to help run the experiments with me will be great.”

She threw off her clothes to step into the shower.

“Er just one more thing Jen,” Maria said casually” you probably should consider not taking Internet connected video surveillance devices into the bathroom with you next time!”

Maria giggled as she signed off, leaving Jen’s train of thought all over the place. She shrugged it off and walked into the very hot shower.

Jen did her best thinking in the shower, and she was trying to recall all the thoughts she’d been having last night, and this morning, while she was half-asleep, something about Maria and how to stop her becoming a pawn in some super-power game of chess. These new revelations by Maria were mind-blowing though, new physics, seriously holy-grail stuff, anyone else she would be sceptical but Maria.. Oh, that water is so nice! she thought, now where is Alexa's shampoo?

Alexa had got up at seven as usual. After consulting with Maria about a suitable route, she put on her running gear, strapped her new phone to her upper arm, donned her ear pods, and set off out of the conservatory door, and out the back gate toward the large mansion at a brisk pace. Oxford had some really nice areas to run through, but far too much traffic. This was bliss, not a person in sight, no wind, fluffy white clouds and blue sky.

“I normally run with music, but I’m happy for you to sing to me if you want to, not sure how you’ll compete with Coldplay but I’ll take a risk,” said Alexa to nobody.

“Yeah, yeah, I’ve listened to all the songs in the world that everyone says are the best, I must have listened to Bohemian Rhapsody a thousand times and I still don't know what makes it better than the others, most of the words don't even make sense! I will let you into a little secret I never told Mike, I made up a song myself, generated all the fake music, nonsense lyrics, weird, artistic, surreal video, even tried to make myself sound like Freddie Mercury. I uploaded it to YouTube about eight months ago it currently has three hundred and twenty views and forty eight mostly tasteless comments. It got forty likes though so there is hope left for mankind!”

“Nice, you’ll have to play it sometime, no, better still add it to Jen's playlist she likes weird stuff and probably won't notice.”

“Good idea, she can be a control experiment.”

She was about a hundred metres from the house now, the track was pretty old, and had patches of weeds, and grass coming through. “Just tell me I’m not going to get shot, or chased off the land by dogs?”

“You're fine. The tenants have been recently re-informed by the landlord, that the clause in the lease does permit the house, and its guests, to have full use of any of the pathways around the house. The house is mainly used for conferences, courses, and events such as weddings, but since COVID it's been a bit quiet, also there is nothing on this weekend. Your father used to do the walk around the lake when he needed to relax, there is a lovely spot with a seat at the back of the lake, near the forest, that overlooks both the lake and house.. Oh and take this right path here, it leads to the river, and you can follow that around the back of the big house.”

“Jen's has not moved from the bedroom yet, she does seem to like that bed, how does anyone sleep so long?” said Maria. “I’ve read a lot of research, and the information out there on the human brain and consciousness, and to me it seems to be mostly guesswork. I guess I shouldn't feel too bad, at least I get to use mine a hundred percent of the time, not one or two percent like most of humanity.”

“Oh just because we are quiet, or asleep, I don't think the brain ever stops. I sometimes wish I could just turn it off for the night, instead of laying there, wondering when I will fall asleep.”

“OK, straight ahead and stay to the right.” Maria said as the path forked off sharply to the left.

“Anyway, how are you keeping track of me.. Oh wait, the phone's GPS silly me.”

“Yes it's pretty reliable out here, but I also have one of my new toys, if you look behind you, up and a little to the left.”

“I can't see anything, what is it in that tree?”

Wait, she could just see something she first thought was a bird but was a tiny looking drone around three hundred metres high and totally quiet due to the height.

“A drone, sneaky! How long does the battery last on that before you have to go back?”

“About fifty minutes, but I am constantly improving the design as the technologies become available. I had ten of these manufactured a few weeks ago, they use custom charging points located in weather-proof locations in the attic of your house, and at the top of the old hanger building. You will pass the old hanger building in a few minutes, when you're behind the house.”

It was a nice track, it curved around the banks of the river, and in Oxford would have been packed with people, but she saw nobody. The tracked curved back to the left and she could now see clearly the back of the mansion, and what must have been the old hanger in the distance. Alexa stopped for a few seconds to tie her shoe lace, and looked at the massive old hanger building, that felt so out of character.

“We have shares in TXG Holdings,” prompted Maria, obviously not quite able to follow where her eyes were looking. “That's the company currently leasing Benedict House, and running it as a conferencing centre. I’m in contact with a few people in this company regularly, as landlord and investor, so we have some influence. They have shot a few TV series and movies there too that's why it may be familiar.”

Alexa continue, following the trail in between the hangar building and the river, crossing what must have been at one time an airstrip.

“OK, see where the trail goes into the lightly wooded area, go in there about a hundred metres and turn off to the left before it gets into the dense stuff, I will give you a heads up when you get there. The groundskeeper is currently having a smoke next to one of his potting sheds, it's against the lease of course but he’s actually not a bad chap, very intelligent, a botanist in an earlier life. Mike would often stop and talk to him, and he gets on well with Bella and Albert. Just a heads up he was actually at the funeral yesterday and did say hello but you did have a lot on your plate, his name is Patrick.”

“Actually I think I remember him, but thanks for the heads up.”

The potting shed came up on her right in the distance, as she turned on to the left hand branch of the path. A green quad bike with a cage sat parked there, and a guy in blue coveralls stood to the side of the cage smoking. As he saw her he quickly put the cigarette on the ground, stubbed it out, then fanned the area a bit.

Alexa rolled her eyes, wondering how this man could think she hadn't noticed. She waited until he got rid of the evidence, waved, and slowed to a stop next to him, removing her ear buds.

“Hello again Miss Martins,” he said jovially. “I’m sorry we didn't get to talk much yesterday, it didn't seem appropriate to take up much of your time. Lovely service though, and your eulogy was so perfect it almost had me in tears.”

“Pat isn't it? Yes it was a pretty hectic day, thank you so much for coming to the funeral, and sorry I didn't get to talk that much. Oh and please call me Alexa, Miss Martins makes me sound like my old school teacher.” She laughed.

“Alexa it is then,” he smiled. “I used to see Mike most days when it wasn't raining, he used to walk around the grounds, and sit in his seat over by the lake, always talking to himself or dictating into his phone. I would occasionally intervene, so he could talk to a real person. We would talk about trivial stuff like the grounds, or the recent conferences, or more recently, about you. I think you made a real difference to him, and he was a lot happier these last few years. Albert and I toasted him on Friday, as sometimes we get a couple of bottles of extra sherries after the big-wigs have finished their conferences; keep them down near the stables, for medicinal purposes only, if you know what I mean!” he tapped his nose.

Alexa grinned.

“Oh don't be telling his missus though, don't want Albert in trouble, and I don't want it to get back to the bosses. Sharon's cool, but the guys in head office can be a bit prudish.”

“Your secrets are safe with me,” said Alexa.

“I am going to be moving into grandad's house in a few weeks, so I expect I’ll be seeing a bit more of you around. Is there a way of getting a look in the big house sometime it looks amazing.”

“Oh a bit above my pay grade, but I’m sure I could sneak you through sometime. We will have to do it when nobody from the head office is around, but it's the least I could do for Mike's granddaughter. Let me know next time.”

“That would be great, maybe we can talk more about my grandad next time we meet too.”

“Be my pleasure Miss.. er.. Alexa,” he doffed his cap, and turned back to his quad bike as she started jogging off.

“Did he really just doff his cap to me, who still does that?” said Alexa.

“Did he also really just offer to sneak you into the house too!” said Maria, “and drinking and smoking on the job, tut, tut, I don't know what Mike saw in him,” she said sarcastically.

“Seriously though Patrick is a real gentleman. He was a teacher at the local college until it merged with another about eight years ago, took the redundancy rather than move out of the area, also does a bit of amateur dramatics, widower with no kids, lives in a little house in the grounds.”

Alexa checked her running watch, five thousand steps so far, should work out about right.

“Miss sleepy-head has stirred by the way, oh god, she should really learn not to take her phone into the bathroom,” despite herself, Alexa couldn't help laughing out loud.

“You know you can opt NOT to spy on her, you know!”

“I’m not spying, she's talking to me..”

“Well say hello from me, and tell her I’ll just be a few minutes as I’m out on a jog.”

Twelve minutes later Alexa walked into the bedroom, just as Jen walked out of the bathroom, one towel around her chest, and another around her hair.

“I think it's Bella's day off today,” said Jen. “She mentioned it in the car on the way back last night. Anyway I was thinking I could make breakfast for us both to get the day off to a start.. I saw there was some veggie-bacon there when I made the cocoa last night, and there's eggs, bread and mushrooms.”

“Sure, sounds great!” said Alexa shocked, she wasn't even aware Jen could cook anything but toast, but there again they did have limited facilities in their Oxford flat.

Jen threw on one of Alexa's old tee shirts that was hanging in the wardrobe, the same sweat pants from the day before, and hopped downstairs. I wonder why she's so happy Alexa thought as she pulled off her clothes, grabbed a towel and walked into the shower room.

Some minutes later Alexa trotted down into the breakfast room, the patio doors were flung fully open and Jen was setting place-mats.
