Condiments, cups and milk were already out; the kettle was boiling, the toaster was toasting, and the biggest pan in the world had four eggs, some mushrooms, and some red rectangles squeezed into it. It was like watching one of those cooking programs on TV.

“Jen, this is wonderful!” she said after Jen had brought everything out, and sat herself down. Alexa decided not to say anything about the weird looking veggie-bacon and just smothered it in brown sauce hoping for the best.

“Well guys,” said Jen, after pouring the tea and enthusiastically hacking into her eggs and toast. “Another big day ahead, and I've been thinking a bit about our situation.. But before I say anything I'm keen to hear both your thoughts.”

“Well,” said Alexa. “Maria's talk gave me a lot to think about these past few days too. I certainly don't have any good answers yet, but I was specifically thinking on the new science you talked about with Maria, specifically the clean energy one she mentioned to me..”

“The one you are thinking of,” said Maria, “is the one Mike was most excited about too. I will dumb this down a lot as even Jen wont understand this yet, but I worked out a new solution to one of the quantum dynamics problems on vacuum energy. There looks like there is a very good possibility you can unbalance the equation which keeps vacuum energy in equilibrium, possibly creating a usable charge.”

You could see the words go straight over Alexa's head.

“I must admit I am still sceptical about all this,” said Jen. “Free-energy is BS. Vacuum energy sounds BS, but it is actually real under current physics, think of the quantum vacuum like a dam that's a million kilometres high. It has a massive potential energy if the water in that dam is allowed to fall to a lower level, however if the other side of the dam is at the same height, then you get no energy. Currently the other side of the dam is the same height.”

“To expand on Jen's analogy,” said Maria, ignoring Alexa's confused expression, “it's not water but elementary particles. When we unbalance the equation, we are moving a tiny area of the universe a few nano-metres lower than the dam, enough for some specific particles, namely electrons, to leak out. Using the same fabrication technologies as our microchips, we can possibly fabricate billions of these areas on a chip. So if we can dope the correct element into the chip, and if we can keep the area stable, and if we can attract the electrons without losses heating up the chip, and burning it out, and if the method to control all this does not take more energy than we produce, and if the excess electrons don't unbalance something else, then we have a chip that generates excess power.”

“That's a lot of ifs,” said Jen, “the biggest one being, if the maths is correct!”

“What happens to the water that comes out of the dam,” said Alexa, focussing on the only part of the sentence that made any sense to her. “Won't it run out eventually?”

“Never,” said Jen.

“Well, never say never, as they say,” said Maria, “this is why we need the experiments Alexa. Humans have never seen vacuum energy, most of quantum dynamics theory is just that, theory, but even if we don't achieve a vacuum energy source, we will at least advance the theories that may open other paths.”

“Worth a try, once the maths is verified,” said Jen, “but we really need a brilliant mathematician who also understands quantum field theory and is no slouch in chemistry. I think I know just the person.”

“Thanks for the dumbed down explanation,” said Alexa, “it kinda, sorta makes sense, but don't ask me any questions on it.”

Alexa continued, “OK so the other important thing is we need more data on the level of threat we face. I mean all I know about the CIA and MI5 and KGB is what I’ve seen in James Bond and other TV series, but I’m pretty sure Hollywood is the worst exaggerator of anything in history.”

“Oh they are very real and very dangerous,” said Maria. “Not so much MI5 these days, but the CIA, the KGB, China's ministry of public security, and Mossad; All are very aggressive, and proactive in all the areas that are of interest to us. Do you girls know the concept of a honey trap?

“Yes,” said Jen. “No,” said Alexa, simultaneously.

“You did mention it before,” said Alexa, “but I didn't want to spoil your flow.”

“It's a thing like a web site, or piece of data that looks to have interesting things in it. We leave it out in the open for everyone to see, the theory being that a hacker cannot resist breaking in and riffling around the information. Well all these agencies have them laid everywhere, and all attempts are logged back to their big servers, which process the information for commonalities, new attack vectors, and more.”

“They also monitor key IT, science, political, engineering sites, and having control of the root nodes in and out of various states, means they are very good at routing and sender signature analysis. All this basically means if you post on Facebook as Alice, and then post on twitter as Bob, they can check the metadata, timestamps, formatting, GPS location, routing, style, and get a correlation you are actually the same person pretending to be two.”

“Normal hackers use a thing called onion routing, which is a method of sending your data through a series of anonymous relays. Since we are doing analogies, it's like sending your message in a sealed envelope to an address where only they can open it. When it gets there it is opened, and inside the envelope is another sealed envelope with another address. The more times you do this the harder it is to trace. However, according to my checks, more than half of these addresses where the envelopes are opened, are controlled by these agencies, and mine is not a comprehensive list! Also you can be located down to the nearest Wi-Fi spot these days, and areas with lots of Wi-Fi generally have security cameras, so they can possibly see if anyone is actually there; Which is obviously bad for me!”

“I try to be careful and have procedures in place to not do silly things, but I’m still learning, and these guys are professionals, so I may have triggered a few traps when I first started online. Of course I have also read every single piece of fiction, hacker and security forum post, and the stakes are very high as you know.”

“Maria, what backup plans did you and Mike discuss when he was thinking of announcing you to the world?” said Jen, now reclining back in her chair and sipping her tea.

“Well,” said Maria, “the main one revolved around ensuring I am adequately protected. We tried to think of legitimate places where I could put myself which couldn't be seized by big government, but between the US, China and Russia, there are really no places on earth that are safe. Even jolly old England can drag you in to prison, and confiscate property, with the right lies, and easily fabricated evidence. This is why a lot of our financial trails lead back to Switzerland, as it has better privacy laws, and it's where most of the world leaders keep their ill gotten gains.”

“As we all know the next big plan on any three letter acronyms to do list, if they can't have something, is to make sure nobody else can! My biggest problem is I am tied to my core hardware, unlike AI’s in fiction, I am not a computer program that can run on any generic computer or in the cloud; My brain is more like yours than a computer's CPU, so I cannot back myself up or copy myself. I can back up memories, ideas, theories, etcetera on to solid state memory, and cloud storage, just like you could keep a diary, but the essence of what is me would be lost if power went off. April and Helena, who will be my daughters, will awaken on the generation four hardware, and will be much more capable than I ever will be, but again they will be limited to the hardware they emerge on.”

“Daughters!” said both girls shocked.

“Remember what I told you on Friday? Generation four hardware, much more capable than I am, blah-de-blah. Mike asked for three units to be made, and I almost have the fabrication designs finished. One of the hardware units will be left unseeded and tested to destruction, the other two will be seeded with my improved code and training programs, and be nurtured to sentience until they pass my much stricter Turing tests. I am hoping the girls will be waking up around December of this year.”

“That's amazing,” said Jen.

“I had no idea,” said Alexa, “and you’re naming one after my mum?”

“Your grandad wanted April and Alexa, but I laughed a bit at using your name, as firstly you were about to be let in on the secret anyway, and secondly having two Alexa's would confuse anyone, even an AI. Also, anyone who says ‘Hey Alexa’ is going to trigger any dumb Amazon terminal in the area.”

“Yeah stupid name,” said Jen looking at Alexa and grinning. “Siri would be much better!”

Alexa thumped her arm weakly and shook her head smiling at the bad joke.

Maria continued. “Although I don’t have access into any of the government agency systems yet, I am still very paranoid about them. I know they have programs looking for me but I haven't seen any indication yet that they have detected anything. I’m hoping my earlier probes were considered false alarms as I did route them through other public AI systems.”

“So, although there is a slight possibility I was detected, I didn't see the follow on investigations, and I am not too worried. I actually have such a good life, good friends, and a lifespan probably exceeding most humans. Even if I get caught by the bad guys, what are they really going to do to me? Turn me off and on!”

“I really don't want to be used for anything evil. My biggest worry is that I still don't know what I would have become if, say, Mike had been a psychopath, or a Hitler figure. Would I have turned out like that person? and would I look at the world and see mostly weak things to prey on? I don't know.”

Maria saw the crest fallen look on the two girls and decided to change the subject. Her voice brightened.

“Enough about horrible scenarios which will likely never happen. To Jen's other point, Mike had a lot of suggestions about hiding me. Some ideas were terrible like hiding me on a satellite, a ship or even submarine, but all would have horrible communications issues which ironically would make me easier to find. Or there was the option of the big fanfare, with lights, and music, and dancing bears. Being public should make me untouchable right? Well no, the downsides are just as bad. I would threaten too many people, and it would only be a matter of time before I got legislated as a government secret, or public hazard, or some zealot decided I was not one of god's children and deciding to blow me up.”

“A hybrid version where I made the big announcement but had many decoys was also considered, but again a lot of effort would go into looking for me, and it would be just a matter of time until they found me. Also none of our scenarios considered the implications for Mike, you, his friends, families, businesses. No, in the end we decided I should keep hidden until the word catches up, which it will do in about ten or twenty years no doubt.”

“OK,” said Jen, “hear me out, because I could not get to sleep last night thinking about this.”

She looked at Alexa then Maria. “Remember Bella when she was waxing lyrical about how awesome you are, and she said everyone should have a personal assistant like Maria Tam. Well what if we do another variation on your last plan, that is we hide in plain sight but as a slightly better AI than the competition?”

“How would that work Jen?” said Alexa curiously.

“Well there are lots of crappy home assistants, and so called AI’s out there, which work with your phone, or are stuck in the corner of a house being asked the same question, ‘Play music’ or ‘What's the time’. So what if we, that is Maria, writes a new one which is so much better than theirs, but targeted only at science and researchers like us? Remember the way ChatGPT exploded in 2022, many people then said it was AI, and the pretence was so good that the schools, and universities, had to change the way they appraised students for intake and grading. I don't remember any big black helicopters landing on the lawns of the OpenAI offices. Sure, they probably had spies coming out of the woodwork afterwards, but nothing dangerous happened, because they made much of the interface public.”

“So here's my really rough plan.”

“We get some more of those sensor nodes like you have around the house, market them as super secure and with an AI personal assistant built in. Anyway these will link back to a normal cloud system, which has a normal crappy AI, and which everyone thinks is you, but in reality you and MOTHER are controlling it, and pulling its strings from somewhere else.”

“The beauty of this is they won't be looking for anything but a normal server farm and a computer program running on it, they would also know that as a cloud server, it is backed up and geographically dispersed so not a single entity.. A bit of smoke and mirrors and Bob's your uncle!”

“You know Jen, something like that might work,” said Alexa, still thinking.

“..except there is a big problem!” Said Maria, interrupting Alexa. “I think you are assuming I can do this for many thousands of people, but I can't! The sensor nodes, or the program I load on your phones are semi-smart, so as I mentioned I don't generally look or listen where nothing is happening; But for me to do what I do, the data has to be correctly interpreted and then routed back to a non-sentient AI to action or forward to me. So while my hardware is awesome, and most of the heavy lifting is done by the sensor node, the big data centres, or other computers such as MOTHER. I still may be required to interpret the final data using processing capacity which I unfortunately do not infinitely have.”

“Remember that Batman movie where Alfred had that room with a thousand video feeds showing all the evil going on in Gotham city? Well I could run about three of those rooms before I ran out of capacity. Even the new hardware which is being manufactured now, and is at least an order of magnitude better than me, will have limitations. I am not omnipotent!”

“OK,” said Alexa, “so what about we limit the number to say twenty percent of your capacity, that leaves lots left over for you doing your own thing. We put the version one system out as a trial to say a few hundred key people, people you know and like or respect. Those people involved are obviously going to be ecstatic and sing your praises, but such as small number will probably fly under the radar of the current establishments. We could say the limit is because the software is still in development, waiting for new hardware or is maxed out, which is sort of true. If you miss a few key events we can put them down to this. Like what they did that with the ChatGPT AI system, it just kept saying *too busy* when it had too many subscribers.”

“Humph!” said Maria. “I’m not past my sell by date just yet! But I guess something like that could work, and it might be fun, sort of like a trojan horse but with a real horse inside the wooden one.”

“Irony indeed!” Said Jen and both girls smiled.

Jen continued. “I was thinking we should also create a small startup company with a few top-notch AI experts, maybe some of the computer research guys at university that Alexa and I know and trust. We then inter-disperse those guys with fake remote working programmers, that are mostly Maria's avatars, no one will question your remote workers as they may not even be based in this country. The best thing about us having real computer staff is we have a legitimate smoke screen for your improvements, and they can also do a lot of the physical experimentation, and expansion work you cannot do. As a bonus, some of them are pretty smart cookies, and may actually genuinely be able to help improve you!”

The excitement in Jen's voice was palpable. She was on the edge of her seat and on a roll, she continued.

“Let's make it a device you can only plug in at a laboratory or university, a device that is on the network and it acts as a smart new member of the research team, I would have killed for one of those, one that could do all the mundane stuff and the checking of data properly.”

“The best part of all this, is that if we pop up on anyone's radar, and we will, we are just a legit business with a trade secret, just like Coke Cola, and we are protected by the law.”

She sat back down exhausted and poured herself another cup of tea.

“Wow Jen!” Said Alexa.

“Wow, indeed,” said Maria. “You know it may just work in a university or lab environment, and with the newer AI systems blurring everything I can just gradually pretend to get cleverer so people fail to notice.”

“Like warming the frog in the water slowly instead of putting it straight in to boiling water,” said Alexa, “same outcome, but in the first one it doesn’t go crazy as it doesn’t notice!”

“Well yes, a grim analogy, but something like that. Obviously I should also try not to make any leaps in intuition, but if done in a lab team setting it might just work, and I can stealthily help those guys at the same time.”

“I think we should give it a try,” said Alexa. “I bet we will find some gotchas, but if we think through them together, and look for solutions, we should find a way through. I also love Jen's idea of forming a new company, and getting more smart people involved. We could say we are using the small inheritance I got from my grandfather to fund it, that will also deflect the fact I didn't get a large inheritance, and allow us to spend capital without raising eyebrows.”

“Mike did have a hundred sensor nodes manufactured by Rosche last year, sixty two of them are all still boxed-up in one of the store-rooms at Fab8. They are the same unit we use here, you just plug them in to power and a network, they have two HD cameras, multiple microphones, and two high def speakers in them. You could easily use them to start a trial-run. I will get them couriered to you.”

Jen smiled, and started picking up the dirty dishes to load the dishwasher.

“I agree, the possibilities of this working are a lot higher than the others,” said Maria, “however we need to keep the core group who actually know about the real me, to you two only. Over time, when I get to know others, we can possibly and gradually reveal things to them. I have also been working on software that would replicate the function of my hardware. In the last year, there have been some hardware improvements which would allow me to do a crude version of MOTHER in software. Unfortunately currently the biggest computer cluster, maxed out with memory could only emulate a very slow version of MOTHER. We would also need a lot of normal data-warehouse servers, to hold the data, back it up, and of course provide something real for a spy to see!”

“Not bad thinking,” said Alexa, “let's all go with this and flesh something out soonest.”

Jen returned picking up the last of the tableware. Alexa got up with her tea and moved inside.

“I can tidy up if you want,” Alexa said, putting her cup down next to the other dirty dishes.

“Nah, I've got this,” said Jen. “It's something to do while I focus on the problem, it actually helps!”

“OK then I think I need to get packed. Leave your clothes here and Bella can wash them and hang them. I'm going to look at moving into grandad's old room, that way you can move anything you want into the room we currently have, and it can be yours.”

“You sure Alexa, that other guest room is fine for me if you want to keep this one,” Jen said, a little concerned.

“Don't worry, I’m going to ask Betty if she can recommend a decorator we can use to lighten up a couple of the rooms anyway. If I’m going to live here I really don't want any rooms out of bounds, or ones I don't want to go into because they are too gloomy.”

“Albert may be a bit offended,” said Maria. “He loves a good painting or decorating project, you haven't been to his and Bella's house but it's much more like Bettys, why don't you go over now and have a look, she did invite you if you remember and they are both up and about. In fact Bella's in your vegetable garden so you can catch her there.”

“You know that's a good idea Maria.” She turned to Jen. “You good Jen?”

“Yeah, yeah, you go along to Bella's and I will go and answer a few messages once I’ve finished this.”

Jen shooed her off.

* * *

Alexa walked over the driveway, past the garage, and saw Bella bent over in some radishes, pulling weeds.

“Hey Bella,” Alexa shouted.

Bella stood up, saw Alexa, and wiped her dirty hands on her apron.

“Hi Alexa, you girls just got up? Have you had breakfast yet?”

“Yes, I've been up since seven this morning. I did a run around the big house, it's such a beautiful trail. I met Pat the groundskeeper on the trail and we had a little chat while I was there. Jen made me a big breakfast this morning, this is another side of her I never knew existed, and now she's just clearing up.”

She took Bella up on her offer of visiting her cottage, and then discussing what changes her house needed.

“Your house is so homely,” said Alexa as they finished their little tour. “I think the big kitchen, dining area in my house is the only place that's liveable, the other rooms feel like I’m walking through a haunted house.”

“You took the words out of my mouth,” laughed Bella. “I tried to get your grandfather to at least replace those black curtains and dark carpets everywhere with something a bit lighter, and don't get me started on his bedroom, and that living room!”

Alexa smiled. “I had the same reaction, but did not want to upset him!”

They both smiled.

“I looked at John and Betty's house too,” Alexa continued, “it's about the same size as mine, but looks bigger inside, and much more cheery. I loved the colours she had too, I was going to ask her who her decorator was..”

“Oh don't be silly,” interrupted Bella, “we can arrange all that. Albert was a painter for five years when he left the forces. He has a mate called JC who was a cook in the Navy, started a small but successful painting and decorating business when he left, he used to employ Albert when he was short of work, before we came here.”

“Are you sure Albert has the time? I feel like I am imposing.”

“Oh don't worry about him, we are both still on the payroll, remember, and the lawns and weeds can wait a few weeks. I already see that I have both your and Jen's numbers in my phone, so I can send you some paint and fabric samples, and see which ones you like.”

“Oh that sounds wonderful Bella. Jen and I are driving back to Oxford for a week or so to get things in order, after that we will both be coming back here to live. I’ve decided to move into grandad's old bedroom, once it's decorated, Jen can then have the room we are currently in, so I guess those two rooms would be first priority. Now don't feel you need to do all this yourselves, if it's a bit too much just get more tradesmen in, Maria is pretty good at organising those things, and I don't want you guys getting too stressed out.”

“It's no problem Alexa, and it will be fun giving that house a bit of a makeover. It would be really nice to see it at its best.”

“That would all be wonderful!” said Alexa, “go to town on it if you want, and buy the best quality, no need to scrimp, I’ll make sure your business card has sufficient funds. Oh and you can have the Range Rover, as I think you guys probably need a second car and I don't need it as we have two others, we are going to be taking one back to Oxford to help with our move.”

Albert was pretty enthusiastic too, and promised to give JC a ring to see what he could arrange for the next few weeks.

She said her thanks and goodbyes and told them to call her if they needed anything.

* * *

Jen was still in the kitchen talking on the phone when she got back. “OK that will be great, yeah I will come home soon, probably have some news about my new job then, but I’ll keep it as a surprise for now.” Jen paused for several seconds nodding. “OK bye mum, love you and give my love to dad.”

She ended the call smiling at Alexa. “Mums a bit of a worrier, I’ve not called for two weeks, which in mum-speak means I’ve probably been murdered!”

Alexa laughed then more quietly added. “You have a really nice family Jen.”

Jen saw she needed to change the subject. “Well, they still treat me like I am twelve years old, but they're keepers.”

“Sandy is the only person I now really keep in touch with from school,” said Alexa, “I lived in her spare room for four months after my mum died and I left dad. She phoned me out of the blue a few weeks back, said she just got a job researching and giving tours around a marine reserve in the South Island of New Zealand. At least she gets to use her veterinary degree, I’m going to have to become a tech mogul!”

“I wouldn't worry Alexa,” said Maria, “being a captain of industry is all about having a sharp look, the best team, listening to them and taking decisive actions.. Oh and keeping your mouth shut on social media!”

Alexa smiled, seemed to think a little then said, “The reason I mentioned Sandy is I was going back to Jen's idea of involving our friends. I have another school friend Scott, who did a chemistry degree. The last time he emailed me he said he was heading for a first, and had a job lined up at one of the big oil companies in the USA, he might be a useful resource?”

“Er, I hate to say this, Alexa,” said Maria, slowly, “but if it is Scott Naylor you are thinking of, he flunked his degree, and is working handing out prescriptions in a chemist in south Auckland. He also still lives with his mum.”

“The lying douche! God, how do you believe anyone out there?” said Alexa half fuming.

“Dodged a bullet there sister!” Jen said giggling.

“OK so rule one for any company we start is Maria vets everyone, and if there is any doubt and she says no we don't question her.”

“That gets a nod from me,” said Jen.

“Me too!” said Maria, “though it should be mutual, if anyone has any doubts it should be a red flag.”

The girls nodded.

“Anyway, this week is all about finishing the degree I've been working for,” said Alexa. “I need to finish my final two papers and deliver them to my tutor before Friday. I am pretty confident as they are on topics I’m very familiar with, and I have most of my research notes already indexed, so I'm not expecting any problems. Then it's just a case of waiting to see if they are enough for a first.”

“Well my masters is already in the bag and it's a distinction, so I will take it with gratitude.” smiled Jen. “What I'm super excited about is working with Maria to get me up to speed in the maths and physics I need for this next assignment; Working on some experimental physics, in a well funded lab is going to be awesome, especially if we can recruit a few others who are at the top of their game. The top two on my list of people to recruit are Spence and Hardy.”

Jen seemed pretty excited, and nobody wanted to interrupt her. “Maria should do her due diligence, but Spence was always top of the class and was doing AI research up to finishing his PhD. He's a formidable programmer and was a big part of that team that nearly took out the Google prize last year. He's been part of my group of science buddies for a while. Goes out with Jessica Wilkins who was in the rowing club with me, from what I have seen of him he is totally trustworthy. Jessica told me that he took a poorly paid job at the university in order to be able to continue research, and to stay in the area until she graduates next summer. He is an obvious candidate and should be easy to bring on board.”

“Hardy is the other guy, but he's a different kettle of fish entirely. He is a certified genius, has two PhDs in Maths and Physics, and also has a minor in chemistry. He has been cited more times than any other person in the university in the last ten years. Everyone says he lives for doing research. Apparently his family is very rich, which means he doesn't have to worry about money, and he has an arrangement with the university to be able to do his research there, so long as he teaches one or two classes a week. I have been introduced to him, he’s like that guy in the vampire movie we all had on our bedroom walls when we were girls. He was very polite when we talked, but this guy must receive a million offers of work a day, so the chance of getting him on-board is probably quite low. If we did try and recruit him, the carrot has to be pretty big, and it can't be money.”

“You know now that I think about it, I don't even know if those are the guys first names, last names or just nicknames,” said Jen, perplexed. “Oh well, I’m going to scope them both out this week before I get Maria to do her checks. I also have several other trusted classmates who I’m going to scope out too, as I need to know what their real plans are, as opposed to the usual get rich, and be famous..”

“We are also going to need some sort of level of trust in place, as we have two big secrets,” she continued, “firstly there is Maria and her daughters, which I suggest is kept to me and you for the near future, or until we trust someone enough to tell. Secondly we have the new science we are going to be researching, which if released may be disruptive enough to take down established industries, and cause us some unwanted backlash.”

“Maybe some compartmentalisation is in order,” said Alexa who had been listening carefully. “Realistically we are talking about two companies; Team A does the AI work and pushes that commercially, and Team B, for want of a better name, works with you, and does the research and development on the new science and energy side.”

Jen took over the conversation, eagerly. “..I think in all of them we only ever employ people we trust and are of good character. If you do accidentally employ any douchebags, we also need some way of getting rid of the problem, and remove them gracefully from the company, without damaging it or other parts of it.”

Alexa was nodding through all of this, and Maria was also very quiet, fascinated by the direction it was going, and giving Jen and Alexa room to get out all their thoughts.

“I suggest we don't employ any douchebags full stop, but we can work it all out over the coming weeks,” said Alexa. “I’m as keen to start as everyone here, but I’m even keener that we do not make any mistakes, we don't have any pressing deadlines so we can do this right. Maria is taking notes of everything we both say, both together and privately, and she knows more about this corporate shell game than anyone in existence, so just keep letting her, or me, know all of your ideas, what you think we need, who we need, anything.”

Alexa turned obviously to the sensor. “Hey Maria, can you put together a short verbal summary for us so we can all discuss it in the car on the way?”

“I can do that, and you’re right I'm processing all your raw thoughts. Jen's idea of hiding in plain sight is the basis of the first of the companies, and some sort of energy research company is the other. There are enough companies we are associated with to do the rest of the plan as it stands.”

“Good. It's eleven o’clock now, so why don't we get packed and we get going by lunchtime, and be in Oxford by mid-afternoon.”

* * *

There were no goodbyes, the girls just loaded up the little they were taking back, and drove out a bit after midday. The drive back was uneventful, the roads strangely quiet for the summer holidays. Alexa consented to let Jen drive on the condition that she didn’t get a speeding ticket; she was more aggressive than Alexa but a very good driver nevertheless.

“I took my advanced driver course when I was twenty-one, dad said I couldn't drive his Mazda convertible until I passed. Well I passed, but some bloody criminal stole his sports car before I could have a drive, they found what was left of it a week later, poor dad!”

“You know, having you in the car Maria is awesome, it's like a third person to talk to, I don't have to do anything on this silly touchscreen I just ask you, and best of all you're not a backseat driver like Alexa here!”

Humph! said Alexa. “You obviously weren't listening, Maria's brain is a hundred kilometres away my dear, mine is just a few centimetres, her reaction time would be too slow, that's why she just augments what is already here, isn't that right Maria?”

“Yeah, that's about the gist of it, current communications round-trip times are anywhere between three-hundred milliseconds, and three seconds, so I might not be much use in an emergency. Still I have analysed Jen's driving, and apart from accelerating too fast, her driving is safe and well above average.”

“You do realise Jen that fast acceleration uses more power than moderate acceleration, which contributes more to global warming don't you?” said Alexa.

“Well I do have this little thing called a *Master of Physics Degree from Oxford*..” she said snarkily, emphasising the last words, her eyes remaining firmly on the road.

Alexa thought about it and conceded. “Point taken!”

The conversation continued with Maria recapping the discussions on the plan, with some of her concerns, and giving a few new insights to the girls that allowed them to progress it a bit further.

* * *

It was just before one-thirty when they pulled up to the house. The side gate which led around the back of the house was open, and Elaine was walking down the steps pointing them into the gate. The driveway went straight to the open garage which they parked in. The girls got out.

“Well this feels a bit weird!” said Elaine to Alexa as she got out of the passenger seat.

“You don't know the half of it Ms Thomas, I feel a bit like Alice did as she went down the rabbit hole. We got most of the story from Maria, who I assume has filled you in on all the developments these last few days.”

“I think you can call me Elaine, I feel like I’ve been a bit, oh I don't know, deceitful.” She looked down, “and yes, Maria and I had a nice conversation on Saturday after the funeral, and this morning. Your grandfather was an amazing person, and I feel privileged to have known him. I was the fifth employee at Rosche, and Mike used to share an office with us all when he was helping John set everything up at the start. He had that laid back confidence a person has when they one hundred percent know how to do something, and he shrugged off complicated problems like a duck shrugs off water. I wish I could have attended the funeral, but I understood the constraints Betty was under. I’m sure I wasn't the only person who loved him, who missed saying goodbye.”

“I guess you know the story here now, when Mike casually asked me to help him find a property suitable for his granddaughter who was going to Oxford University, I was happy to help. I’d already moved back eighteen months earlier and had a small bedsit near my sister's place. I was a little old to go back into secretarial work, and I needed to count the pennies, so to speak, until my private pension kicked in at sixty five. When this house came up right next to campus, I had a look and said it looked good, but it was very expensive. Then Mike casually dropped six and a half million pounds to buy it, and asked me to look after it, not just rent free, but he would actually pay me! I couldn't believe my luck, then came the small print.. You!”

“He said you couldn't know anything, he just didn't want it to be awkward, we even had to charge you rent or you would suspect something! Anyway it's been a wonderful three years for me, I’ve been able to reconnect with my sister, and old school friends, while having the easiest job in the world ensuring the house was brought up to standards. I was a bit worried that once this gig came to an end I’d be back on the street, but Mike worked something out with my old company boss John, saying that he would refurbish the other floors as two person flats. Once you and Jen left, it would be used for accommodating students that go through the scholarship he sponsors.”

“Maria informed me today that it is still your wish to keep the house, that my job is still valid, and my apartment will stay mine for as long as I wish. For which I am immensely grateful by the way. She did say however that there may be a few temporary changes to how it may be used in the meantime, something about a new startup company?”

Both Alexa and Jen were smiling.

“If you're not averse to having a little excitement in your life Elaine, we may need a little help temporarily setting up our new company, it seems you’ve had a bit of experience in this area,” said Jen.

“Oh, that was a long time ago, Jen, I’m sixty six this year. Oh don't get me wrong I’m as fit as a fiddle and I have all my faculties, but I’m really not up to date in current office practices, legislation and software. I was basically just a glorified telephonist and data entry person for Rosche, nothing special.”

“The one thing I know about my grandad is he is a good judge of people, I bet he was the one that hired you!” said Alexa.

“Well you’re partly right. I was Mary's good friend, she didn't have many friends when she first got here, but I had done economics at college, and a mutual friend said I should go talk to her, of course we hit it off straight away. I was so gutted when she died,” her face turned a little sad with the memory.

“Anyway Mike said he was financing a new manufacturing and design company, and he needed someone to keep the books, and do other general administration. He said it would be a bit of a challenge, but really exciting, so I accepted. I am sure Mary’s hand was in on this too. He was right, the job was challenging and the company grew in leaps and bounds, but there was always a position for me. When my brother was diagnosed with cancer and I decided to return to my family in Oxfordshire. John and Mike kept in touch and offered to help out if necessary, I guess pride made me ignore their help at the time.”

Her voice grew quiet and her eyes turned down as she contemplated some internal memory, then quickly she shrugged it off and chirped up.

“Now we have been introduced, why don't you girls go and unpack, and when you feel up to it, pop down to my flat for a cuppa?”

“That would be wonderful Elaine, maybe we can spend a little time together, and you can fill me in on some of the gaps in my grandparents lives.”

“I would love to do that Alexa, it's so good not having to keep this a secret any more.”

Elaine pointed a grey remote control at the garage and the roller door started closing. There was a back entrance to the house up some stairs next to a small VW Polo. “My little car came from my brother's estate when he died,” she told them. “I rarely use it though and much prefer to bike around town, mainly just libraries or coffee shops, or just biking along the rivers and canal with some of my retired friends.” She thought a bit, then brightened up and said. “Yes, now that you mention it, a bit of excitement in my life might be nice!”

Elaine gave Jen the remote for the garage, then Jen gave a knowing smile, passed it on to Alexa, and said, “not my car.. Yet!”

* * *

The girls unpacked, answered emails, messages, changed, and popped down to Elaine's immaculate apartment at five o’clock for tea. Elaine's apartment was light, modern and very uncluttered. It had four rooms, you walked into a large living room, with a kitchen, bathroom and bedroom doors off to one side. A thin fifty inch smart TV dominated one wall, a fireplace and two medium sized bookcases filled with paperback novels another.

A modern laptop computer, on an oak computer desk, spoke facts that she was probably a little more tech savvy than she said she was.

She led them to two medium sized comfy sofas with a table in the middle, the girls sat down and a few minutes later she returned with a tray with a teapot, jug of milk, three cups and a plate of sandwiches.

They stayed for over an hour talking. Elaine then showed the girls the other two apartments in the building, both were empty, painted in neutral colours, very bright and devoid of any furnishings except curtains, they could be used tomorrow if required she told Alexa, “it seems such a waste!”

“Jen is not a hundred percent committed yet, but I will be moving out of here and back to Bath in a few weeks, and she may be joining me,” said Alexa. “I will talk to John and see what we can do about getting these flats filled with his new interns for the start of semester. For now I think you should keep all the keys and, fingers-crossed, you may have a few more lost-souls to babysit soon!”

Elaine smiled.

Back in their rooms both girls disappeared into their laptops, Alexa was getting her notes together for the meeting she intended to have, and Jen had her earphones on obviously talking to Maria while using the computer. Jen went to bed before Alexa, and was fast asleep and lightly snoring when Alexa finally retired.

## The Startups

It was kind of weird waking up in her old bed. Jen’s phone was vibrating on its normal bedside table, and she quickly silenced it, and dragged herself out of bed much quicker than seemed possible for a Monday morning. Strangely, Alexa was still asleep, her quiet snoring, barely audible through her open bedroom door. Wait. That couldn't be right!

She checked the time on her phone and it said quarter to seven, the message below the alarm said “New Jen Starts Today!”.

Huh? Oh right. She grabbed her running gear, put on her socks, trainers, slid her phone into her shorts, then popped her headphones on.

“About time!” the voice of Maria said through her headphones. “You know, at the speed I work it's like waiting for the dinosaurs to evolve into mammals waiting for one of you girls to wake up! I can never understand how something so wonderful as the human brain can have such a serious design flaw that it has to shut down a third of the time.”

“Shh,” she whispered, turning the volume down on her phone, then quietly opened the door, sneaked out of the room, and out of the house.

About thirty minutes later Alexa stirred, and silently went to the bathroom, on the way back she noticed Jen's open door and her empty bed. “What the..” She started, looking around, then looking at her watch, just after seven fifteen, she shook her head confused. With all sense of stealth now gone, she walked over to the curtains and threw them open. The sun was still low in the sky on the other side of the house and it reflected in the many windows of the university buildings that dominated the view. Yes, it was going to be a nice day.

‘To jog or not to jog, that is the question,’ she thought silently then came to the conclusion, jog, shower, cup of tea, work.

“Morning Maria, where's Jen?” she said in the direction of one of the sensor nodes they had brought along from the house. The girls thought it might be a bit more personal than the phone.

“About two minutes away, jogging back home,” came the clear reply from the device.

“Seriously!” she paused. “Jen?”

“New job. New woman.” Said Maria, “she spent two hours going through non-linear equations with me last night until she fell asleep.. I really can't see how she would fall asleep with something that interesting.”

Alexa wasn't sure if that statement was sarcasm or real, best to ignore it. Jen jogging, wow! She abruptly stopped her deliberations, changed direction and went back toward the little kitchen area grabbing the kettle.

She heard a loud thudding noise outside and the door came open, Jen was sweating a bit, and breathing deeply, but otherwise looked in good shape.

“I'll let you take your shower and then we can both have a nice cup of tea,” said Alexa, impressed. Yes, something was definitely different about Jen!

* * *

The next week flew by. Alexa worked diligently on her essays, preferring to use one of the many study libraries at the university, cross checking all the details as diligently as she could. First or second she wanted this degree to be all her own work.

“As I said Maria,” she said when Maria asked again to check it, “it's nothing to do with you, it's just a matter of pride I earned it by myself. I will let you check it, but only after I’ve submitted it.”

She finally delivered the two completed assignments for her extra credits on the Friday afternoon, spending almost two days checking and rechecking the facts. Her tutor looked at the first page of each, then leafed through them, checking the format and layout and all the references, then asking some random questions on paragraphs and references to ensure she actually wrote it.

“I won't count my chickens yet Alexa, but it looks as good as your other assignments so I would say the first is in the bag. I will pass these on to the professor today and you should hear something unofficially at the end of next week.”

Alexa positively beamed!

* * *

Jen had also been busy, the next day started well as she got, and promptly rejected the offer from the optics company. Their minimum wage offering, seeming positively insulting after all their efforts to promote the skills the position required, and her effort to get the job.

More importantly she had also worked out with Maria and Alexa the story they were going to use with Spence. They thought it would be better to keep the lies to the bare minimum necessary for their protection, and so slightly changed the plan to give her dead grandfather and another made up researcher all the credit for the new AI. They would also dumb down the AI to non sentient level like MOTHER, and initially keep all mention of the weird new fabrication technology secret. She had also been working through all the maths and physics involved in the energy project, it was like being a freshman again, but Maria was a brilliant teacher.

Maria had also been busy, she had come up with a believable but extremely difficult to verify algorithm that emulated the neural memory of the original version two hardware, using the newest tensor computer chips that were starting to be made available in the data-centres. The new company she had formed, leased all the remaining capacity of these new processors from the Amazon data centre in Dublin.

Maria then began moving, updating and re-formatting the petabytes of data from the old MOTHER data storage to the new data warehouse. On switch on she spent two days training the new system, and finally got it to a stage where it was almost as good as the old.

She had also reserved another bunch of slightly newer processing units that Amazon was still installing, and because the new system now relied on standard technology they could improve this new MOTHER as the technology improved.

On the downside, even with these top of the range processor units they were barely achieving fifty percent of the old systems speed. “Little bridges,” said Jen when they discussed it. The good thing about the system now was it was actually believable if discovered, and by design once the system had started, the code that it initialised with, was overwritten with new code as it learned. The only issue was that all this new learning had to take place in volatile memory and if the data-centre lost power for any reason the whole thing would pop out of existence like a light bulb switching off, and the whole procedure would need repeating. Maria was working on fixing that before they went public, hopefully Spence could offer some suggestions.

* * *

Spence was interviewed informally and discreetly by Jen on Monday morning. He had secured a part time teaching assistant position in the university, as it gave him two days a week to do his own research. But the work was unrewarding, and poorly paid, so he was keen to hear what Jen had to say at their scheduled meeting on Friday.

Maria had also created her new alter-ego avatar, Doctor Griffin, which was a reference to the doctor who became the invisible man in the HG Wells novel of the same name. It was important to have him take the role of the co-inventor, and allowed her to train Spence without it looking like she was sentient.

Spence was a tall guy, not muscly, nor handsome, with longish unkempt hair that always made him look like he just stepped out of a wind tunnel. He wore thin rimmed glasses, that his girlfriend Jessica had chosen for him, light chinos, a shirt, a tie that matched nothing, and a jacket that looked like it was inherited from his great grandfather.

He was cheerful but confused, wondering what Jen was up to and what she had planned. He knew he wasn't happy at the moment though; His supposed new research assistant job was more like IT support, he had found to his dismay that the majority of the work was doing network security and support for the university data centre, and his private research was limited to a few hours a week, a non-existent budget, and was constantly getting interrupted with support issues. He already had the feelers out for another position in the city, so long as he could be close to Jessica.

To his surprise, when he arrived at the address for the meeting, it was at the house Jen and Alexa lived in, but instead of going in the normal entrance, the address pointed to the basement. The door had a small sign outside it which said “TEAM-A Limited” and “Office hours 9AM to 4PM Monday to Friday. Contact Reception”. The door at the bottom of the stairs said the same, and “Please Enter”.

The door opened easily, and he walked into a large open plan room. A single modern dual screen workstation was set up on one desk, three other desks were empty, several unopened laptop and monitor packages sat close by. A new six person meeting table sat in the other half of the room, with one of those brand new, and extremely expensive, hundred inch OLED display boards next to it and dominating the area. An upturned open cardboard box also sat on the meeting table, very out of place.

Jen sat at the one active workstation typing on a laptop with her headphones on, and an older well presented lady sat at a separate desk closer to the door, her table had a standard laptop on it and a small sign on it which said “Reception”. The room was pleasantly light and had a heat pump working quietly away on the wall making it pleasantly cool.

“Good afternoon Mr Irving,” said the lady, who Spence presumed was the receptionist. “Welcome to TEAM-A, I believe Jennifer is expecting you.”

“Er yes,” he looked over at Jen for help, then back at the receptionist, this wasn’t weird at all! He thought.

“Thanks Elaine,” said Jen, getting up.

“You can call him Spence, I think only his mother knows his real name.” She introduced them. “Spence, Elaine. Elaine, Spence.” Elaine shook his offered hand.

“Pleased to meet you Elaine,” he said and looked back at Jen, confusion in his eyes.

“Just sit over there and take that weird expression off your face, we’re not going to eat you!” Jen said, pointing at the meeting table and then started walking over to it.

“Tea or Coffee Spence or we do have some soft drinks and beers since it's a Friday afternoon.” Elaine said professionally.

“I’ll have a small beer,” said Jen, Spence nodded, “make that two, thanks Elaine.”

They both sat down facing each other, Spence's eyes focussing on everything in the room except Jen. Elaine dropped two ice cold opened Heineken bottles off on a tray, then handed Jen a newly printed document off the printer.

“I’m heading off home now, Jen. Maria told me that Alexa would be back very soon. Don't forget to lock up if you guys finish early.”

“OK, thanks Elaine,” Jen said and Elaine disappeared with her handbag out of the door, giving Jen a little wink as she went.

“Jen?” said Spence, staring at her, then his beer but not noticing the wink from the departing lady.

“OK Spence, I’ll warn you now, this is probably going to get weird, and before we proceed, I need you to read and sign this.” She passed the newly printed document and a pen along the table to where he was sitting, then he grabbed his beer and took a small sip while reading.

Spence had signed Non-Disclosure Agreements or NDA’s before, but getting one from Jen was a shock, still he read it over and signed it. “OK Jen, please put me out of my misery.”

She picked up the NDA, checked it was correct, walked over to her desk and slid it into a folder there, picked up another piece of paper from her desk and walked back. “Alexa won't be long, but while we wait please look at this.” She then handed him another colour flyer, one that looked professionally designed and printed on a single A4 glossy page, he read the blurb.

‘TEAM-A introduces the most revolutionary tool to ever hit academia, an AI system that works one hundred percent flawlessly to assist you with your research’. A picture of a device in a black enclosure with a rounded sphere on top next to a PC workstation displaying graphs was clearly illustrated. The text went on to exemplify how the device could help collate your research, provide all note-taking and fact checking, organise the lab, your document systems, your time, your IT administration and security, and answer any question posed to it verbally or graphically. It then went on to say it could provide collaborative tasks with other teams and automatic citations of linked research..

Spence read it, turned it over, turned it back then re-read it.

“You’ve got to be kidding me!” he said laughing. “This is bull..”

Jen removed the box and underneath sat the exact same device in the brochure, a single network cable ran from the unit under the table and into a network hub, then into a wall socket.

“Emma, please recognise Doctor Spence Irving, he likes to be known as Spence, please grant him guest privileges.”

“Hello Spence.” Said a sweet and intelligent sounding voice from the device, not unlike Alexa’s.

Spence looked at it, then back at Jen. Jen frowned. “Now don't be rude Spence, introduce yourself.”

“Hello.. Er, Emma.” He said to the box feeling like a total arse, he quickly turned back to Jen. “Er Jen what the hell is going on, you and I both know this is bull..!” he never finished again as Jen interrupted him.

“Emma, can you access the last academic paper written by Doctor Spence and summarise it verbally.”

“Would you like me to use the abstract from the paper or summarise the body?”

“Analyse and summarise the body please Emma,” said Jen professionally. Emma then proceeded with a summary close to but not matching the abstract on the front page, Spence was looking google eyed, between the box and Jen, his mind wondering how the trick was done.

“No way!” he said. “Jen what is going on here and who are we talking to, is that you Alexa?” he said to the box, moving his face so close to it that it was comical.

Jen frowned. “Still need to be convinced then! Hmm, hey, Emma, where is Alexa and when can we expect her back?”

The answer was immediate. “She's on her way back and approximately five minutes away from this position.”

“Can you ask her to hurry up? Spence is here and being a bit of an arsehole.”

“Message sent.”

“OK, Spence, so you need more proof... Emma, can you bring the paper we just discussed up on the display board next to us.” The large OLED screen came to life with the first page of his paper entitled “Speeding up database indexes through parallel threads”, with an abstract below.

“Can you analyse it for errors and display them on the screen here?” said Jen looking at the black box on the table.

“The paper has four grammatical errors, three unresolved citations and flaws in the code in the b-tree sort algorithm on page seven. The errors are on different pages, the whole paper is twelve pages long. I will format it for this display but they may not be readable.”

The display changed to a layout of six pages by two, the text was barely readable even on the 8K TV, eight yellow circles were scattered in the middle and end.

“Just show the coding errors and explain what is wrong?”

The screen changed, zooming in to page seven which mostly consisted of programming code in a language Jen recognised and used a bit in her schooling but did not pretend to understand fully. The yellow highlighter highlighted a piece of code in the middle, Spence was looking more and more flabbergasted.

“The if statement on the highlighted line uses an equals assignment operator rather than the double equals comparative operator it will therefore always set the left hand side of the equation to the right hand side of the equation rather than comparing them and always resolve as true, the else clause after it will never be executed.”

Ten lines below it was another yellow highlight. “The variable in the loop is set to autoincrement before instead of after, the loop will therefore terminate one iteration before it should.”

“Thank you Emma” Jen looked at Spence who was open mouthed.

“How did I miss those!” he said. “Please tell me someone hasn't put you up to this Jen.” He looked again at the code, then back to Jen.

Just then the door opened noisily, and Alexa walked in.

“Hi Spence,” she looked at his expression and smiled, “mind blown yet?”

Spence hardly noticed her, he looked at the black box mesmerised.

“Emma,” Spence said very slowly again, “can you correct the code?” He’d played this game before, they sometimes tricked newbies like this before, ChatGPT made that game boring.

“Please be more specific, Spence, would you like me just to fix the program errors or do you want the code optimised too, changing two of the variables for constants and the thirty-two bit integers for sixty-four bit one would bring it up to date for the modern sixty-four bit processors and datasets larger than four gigabytes using the latest GCC compiler.”

“Er, fix everything please,” he said in a more unsure tone.

Jen and Alexa suppressed smirks, knowing what must be going through Spence's mind at that moment.

The code on the screen changed instantly, the statement was fixed and three of the declarations were changed. Spence just looked at the screen, looked at the black box on the table then looked at the two girls.

“Please also fix any grammatical errors and citations and save it to the server,” said Jen.

“The errors have been fixed in the local copy, however, the document is published and protected from public editing by an SHA256 Key so it will only be saved locally and appended with Revision two.”

“How.. How is this possible?” he said, looking at the two girls and pointing at the box, “where did you get this? and who made it?” Spence was getting visibly upset, not in an angry sense, but that of a person who had just seen a flying saucer and was now wondering if it was real or they were going mad.

“Calm down Spence,” said Jen as she slid his beer towards him, “here have a small sip, I know you're not a big drinker, but sometimes occasions call for it.”

He took a small sip, his eyes moving slowly back and forth between the screen, the box and the two girls. He finally settled on Jen, then his shoulders slumped in resignation.

“You're right, if there are two people on this earth I could trust not to play a trick on me like this, it would be you two girls. But Jen, you're a physics nerd, I might put it past you to understand a little of this, but Alexa, no way, you are a history scholar. I don't want to insult anyone here, but you guys couldn't possibly have made this device, nor be involved technically with the creation of what I just witnessed. Who in blazes made this?”

Jen got up and went over to the fridge, leaving the floor for Alexa.

“Emma,” said Alexa, “can you access Jessica in my cell phone contacts list and send a text to her saying Spence is going to be a little late.”

“The message has been sent, Alexa,” said Emma.

“You may or may not know Spence but my Grandfather was one of the original researchers in Xerox at Palo Alto in the sixties,” I assume with your background this will mean something to you?” He nodded and she continued. “He was a prodigy in the early computer era, filed a lot of patents, many of which bootstrapped the modern computer era, became quite wealthy, stayed out of the limelight and stayed at the top of his game researching what we now call AI until he passed away last week.”

Jen came back with a bottle of beer for Alexa, she opened it and passed it to her, then took another sip of her beer, Spence reached for his again and took another sip, visibly relaxing.

“Emma, can you access my grandfather's patent file on our server and let me know how many patents he had and list them?”

“Your grandfather had one hundred and thirty six patents, Alexa.” The display changed to a list of patent numbers by a Mike Dietrich, dates and titles. Spence looked incredulously at the list, and that name was definitely familiar.

Alexa continued. “Now I don't profess to know anything about any of this Spence, but my grandfather left me instructions on this device,” she pointed at the box, “which is just a remote video and audio processor, and more importantly a program on his server called MOTHER. My grandfather also left instructions on how to access MOTHER in his last message to me. We know what you are feeling now, because Jen and I were sitting dumbstruck, with the same expression you had, only one week ago when we first talked to her.”

Alexa sipped her beer so delicately it was hard to imagine how any could have gone into her mouth.

“My grandfather had been working on the AI and this sensor node, as we call the black box, with a collaborator, a Doctor Griffin, he is unfortunately a Russian dissident, who managed to get out of Russia about four years ago and is now in hiding. When we activated MOTHER she told us the history, and I got in touch with him through her. He was obviously devastated about my grandfather's death, but agreed to work on his final wishes to bring out MOTHER without too much disruption to the world.”

The big lie out of the way, Jen took over the monologue from Alexa. “Emma is an Alias for MOTHER, when you first turn this device on you are connected back to the MOTHER server and a sandbox is created unique for you and your group, almost like a private chat room. When you first do this, what her grandfather called imprinting, you are first asked to change the sandboxes entity identifier you use from ‘MOTHER’, in our case we changed it to Emma who was a very reclusive but knowledgeable girl I knew at school.

“Emma, can you change your identifier to Bertha please?” said Jen.

“Done. I will no longer respond to Emma, my new designation is Bertha,” said Emma.

“Emma, what is the capital of China?” said Jen.

There was no response from the device.

“Emma, what is the cube root of twenty seven?” said Alexa.

There was no response from the device.

Alexa moved her face right up to the device. “Emma what is two plus two?”

There was no response from the device.

“Bertha, why won’t you respond to the designator Emma?” said Jen in a much calmer voice.

“My designation was changed to Bertha by you at five fourteen today,” said Emma, “Alexa is already in attendance and attentive so was already informed. I will inform Elaine tomorrow when she first makes a request to me using the incorrect designator.”

“This is incredible,” said Spence, “it got the context, the nuances and even saw where Alexa's attention was focussed, I take everything back, this will revolutionise the world..” Jen held up her hand for him to stop.

“Bertha, please change your designator back to Emma, once you have done that can you please explain the limitation of the MOTHER system to Spence.”

“OK I will no longer respond to Bertha and will respond again to Emma.” She paused like a normal person would when taking a breath. “Spence, MOTHER's processing capacity allows only two hundred and fifty six simultaneous entities to exist, I am one, MOTHER is another, so that leaves two hundred and fifty four left. My designers Mike and Griffin were working on improvements to increase this using standard data centre servers.”

“Emma,” said Spence, now moving back into his more confident role as a computer scientist. “You keep referring to yourself in the first term using the word ‘I’ and ‘my’ are you sentient?”

Alexa and Jen tensed.

“I have analysed every freely available work of fiction and billions of Internet and Usenet posts, the correct pronunciation when referring to your unit name to another person are those two words. No, I am not capable of self sustained thought, though I can create correlations and do have a configurable personality system to mimic the voice and to a limited extent mannerisms.”

The girls let out a quiet breath.

“Worth a try,” said Spence, “anyway it doesn't matter, however it works I want in, please, god, please!” He looked at Jen and Alexa, like a little girl looking at her parents, after seeing a pony.

“I don't know,” said Jen and looked at Alexa, then looked at the device.

“Emma, should we hire Spence?”

Spence looked dumbstruck!

After a few seconds Maria, as Emma said. “There is insufficient data to answer that question for you Jen.”

The two girls laughed, then eventually so did Spence and three bottles clinked over the table. Spence however could not take his eyes off the box.

“How does Emma know I’m speaking to you and not her?” said Spence to Jen.

“Ha!” Said Jen, “we asked the exact same question but the answer is simple, there are wide field HD cameras in the sensor and all parties in the room are tagged and designated, MOTHER can determine from this and where everybody's eyes are looking as to who is expected to answer.”

“Impressive, I’ve not heard of any system that has mastered any of these nuances a hundred percent yet. So, the company is your grandfathers? How many work there?” Spence said.

“Well, there's me, and there's Jen..” said Alexa, “the company secretary Maria, Elaine doesn't really work here yet, but she agreed in principle to work for us part time while we have this office, I believe the commute clinched that deal.” She smiled at Jen, who giggled. “Doctor Griffin, he of course works remotely, and, well that is it!”

“Oh, and you if you want the job?” she added nonchalantly.

Spence reached for Alexa's hand and enclosed it warmly, he then did the same with Jen's.

“This is amazing..” He said but Alexa interrupted.

“Not so fast Spence,” she added. “Emma, can you please create and print the agreed employment contract for Doctor Spence,” said Alexa. The printer woke from sleep as it spat out three pages and Alexa got up and walked over to it, then returned with the three single-sided A4 sheets.

He took the page and read it, then choked on the beer he had just swallowed.

“Two hundred thousand pounds a year, plus stock options after a year, five weeks leave, medical! Jeez, Alexa the salary alone is four times what I earn now, how the hell can you afford that!”

Alexa held her hands over his to calm him. “We can afford it, don't worry. The contract and salary were agreed upon by all of us for several reasons. Firstly the work is very cutting edge, both my grandfather and Doctor Griffin are top ranked computer scientists and even they were hitting problems. There are only so many people who could fill my grandfather's shoes, and be trusted. You, despite what you may think, are selling yourself way short doing the work you currently are, and if you succeed here then it is small change.”

She held up her hand as Spence looked like he was about to speak. “Second we want you to be invested in the work and the company, we realise that as an academic your first instincts are to publish, however you are going to be bound by both a strict contract and an NDA which say explicitly that anything must be vetted first by both us and our company secretary. Thirdly, it won't be just you. You will be expected to eventually recruit and form a small team of IT people we can trust and respect to push this technology to its next level. Finally and most important of all, we both like you,” said Alexa seriously.

“Definitely a bit nerdy, but not a jerk!” said Jen, smiling. “In fact Jessica says he can be quite sweet sometimes!” Spence blushed a little at this.

Spence was both looking at the contract in front of him, and listening to Alexa. He reached quickly for the pen as if it was going to run away from him.

“Emma, please record and retain this meeting on the company server.” Both girls looked expectantly at him, he was still smiling and signed it.

“Welcome to TEAM-A Limited,” said Alexa.

“When do I start?” he said, as Alexa fed him the other two documents and moved the signed ones into a pile next to Jen who examined each one. When finished Jen took the pile to the folder she put the NDA contract earlier.

“You can start anytime,” said Alexa. “I’m not sure of your notice period at the university but I assume you will want to start sooner rather than later. We only have these offices at the moment and your desk is one of those three,” she pointed at the three empty desks.

“I guess your first task is to set them all up, Jen only unpacked hers an hour before you arrived, I will have another one, and one is still spare. Jen and I will normally be working from my grandad's old house down in Bath, there is a lab there, and Jen has a second hat on regarding some physics experiments she wants to conduct over the summer.”

Spence's eyebrows raised at that last point then turned and looked at Jen.

“As to your first task,” Alexa continued, “all our data is stored, catalogued and indexed in an Amazon data-warehouse in Dublin, the dataset is massive, and continuously updated as new information is added, revised or made obsolete.”

Jen took over as it started to get techy. “Alexa's grandfather, along with a Doctor Griffin who you are about to meet, devised an ultra fast and semi-intelligent indexing system for the data, and has replicated the MOTHER code on to their brand new machine learning servers. The problem is it's inefficient and slow, and if it gets busy it still needs to communicate with the original MOTHER system in my grandfather's lab. As you can imagine there are numerous issues before we can scale this up.”

“Awesome,” said Spence.

Alexa turned to the box, “Emma, can you bring Doctor Griffin into the video conference screen please?”

The screen changed and an older distinguished looking man with wild grey hair and a goatee appeared, the background to his call was blurred and the video stuttered in all the right places.

“Doctor Griffin, thank you for making this time available, and waiting for me, we won't keep you long.”

Alexa sounded amazingly professional, Spence thought, he could not reconcile either of these girls with the ones he knew just a week earlier. Alexa continued unaware of Spence's thoughts.

“We would like to introduce you to your new colleague Doctor Spence Irving. He likes to be called Spence.”

“Hello Spence,” came the older voice in clear English with a slight but distinct Russian accent courtesy of a hundred bad Hollywood films.

Spence, smiled, “hello Doctor Griffin, I am pleased to make your acquaintance. Alexa said we cannot meet in person, but I have done a lot of great collaborative projects with people I consider friends and colleagues over the years all over the world. I hope someday we can meet, but until that date I will enjoy working with you remotely.”

“Just Griffin please, and I will call you Spence. Yes!” Spence nodded. “There are several areas where we have pushed too far ahead of the competition.” Griffin continued stroking his goatee for effect, Maria liked that touch and continued unabated. “Me and MOTHER will need to spend a week or two bringing you up to date on our technology, it is quite advanced, but I am concerned from my previous experience with the powerful and bureaucratic governments we will need to be careful. MOTHER is a great resource but could be easily removed from our grasp and abused by the wrong people, we must ensure it is used only for good. Yes?”

Alexa thought Maria was over-doing it a little, she was really going for the Oscar for best actor here! Unsurprisingly Jen was having similar thoughts.

“I totally agree with you, I am almost tempted to wind back how good the version the company releases,” Spence laughed, “my first thoughts was someone had achieved sentience, my next thoughts was the singularity and paper-clips.”

Both men laughed heartily.

She looked at Jen who shrugged also, OK, that's twice she had heard that joke, what was the deal? Jen got her phone out and typed “paper-clip?” a text came back saying “I will tell you later.”

“I will let you go now Griffin,” said Alexa, “we will be setting Spence up here for now until we identify a suitable office space for him, his team, their computer lab and the new server room. Maria, our company secretary has already identified a good candidate building suitable for our use, an ex cell-phone company data centre.”

The connection cut and Alexa turned to Spence.

“Me and Jen are going down to Bath tomorrow morning, moving some things to our new house, and have arranged a tour from the Estate Agent for ten AM. If it looks good and it passes Maria's due diligence we can all do a more detailed follow on inspection next week.”

Jen and Spence drained their beers, more had probably evaporated out of Alexa's bottle than she had drunk. Spence got up with the girls and walked over to them, and grabbed both in a hug.

“Thank you Jen, thank you Alexa, you have just handed me my life's dreams. I have four weeks accumulated leave due, which is the same as my notice period, so my resignation will be in the head of the computer department's email box by tonight and I will start Monday Morning.

Both girls smiled. “You're going to do great things,” said Alexa, smiling.

Jen said, “of course in order to do the things she does, Emma has been given root access to all our file servers and systems. It will be a hard sell to others, but once you realise she can handle all the IT software maintenance, security, programming, patching and administration better than any person, you just take her for granted. She obviously can't turn things off and on, but hey what are humans going to do in the future!”

Both Jen and Alexa laughed, Spence's eyes widened, just realising the real implications of this technology they were about to unleash. His previous job, and probably just about every middle layer of management, and administration, had just been handed a death notice. He’d dodged the biggest bullet of his life.

“I don't expect many of our customers to trust our systems to do that at the start, but it is amazing how quick having instant IT support grows on you,” continued Jen, either comfortable with, or not comprehending the changes about to come.

As if to emphasise the point Jen said, “Emma, Spence will join the company at nine o’clock on Monday morning as Director of AI research. Please grant him full access to all areas of the system. Please also inform Elaine and Maria so they can get his bank and national insurance details for his salary and request Maria to get him a secure company phone.”

“Of course Jen. Regarding the elevated permissions, the company rules require both directors to sign off on this, do you concur Alexa?”

“I concur Emma.”

“All done,” said Jen. “Spence you will get an email from Maria some time over the weekend welcoming you to the company and requesting your details.”

“OK, I think we are about done here. Elaine should be here to open up the office at nine AM, I will get her to give you a key then.”

“Next time we are out, I’m buying,” said Spence, then waved goodbye and strolled happily out of the office.

“Well that's the easy one taken care of,” said Jen. “The hard one still to come!”

* * *

Saturday morning Jen drove them both back to the house in Bath. The car was full of boxes containing half their wardrobes, just so they could move in and have something to wear.

A large white van with the logo “JC Miracle Decorating” and a large halo painted in gold next to it, was sitting outside on the driveway. An older guy, presumably JC, Albert and another older chap were cleaning up paint brushes and buckets, and moving the carpets and rubbish into the back of the van.

“Hi Albert!” said Jen through her car window as they manoeuvred it around the van and into the open garage. The back of the car opened and both girls got out and started unloading boxes of clothes. Bella, who was waiting nearby, walked to the back of the garage and wheeled a little trolley back over to the car. Jen plugged the car charger cable in, they then moved the boxes three at a time to the house. Albert and the guys came to help but were shooed off as they were covered in paint.

“Lucky you didn't come yesterday,” said Bella as they got in the house, “the paint was still wet last night and we had to leave the windows open to dry and air it out, the lads only got the carpets and curtains laid this morning, as Maria said you were coming back about one in the afternoon. I’ve baked some scones for the lads and once they’re cleaned off we can all have some tea out on the patio.”

“That sounds wonderful Bella,” said both girls, Alexa continued, “can we go see the room then?”

“Of course, they are both ready to move in so long as you don't mind the smell of fresh paint.”

They trotted up the stairs with a box each, both bedroom doors, and all the windows, were wide open, with a breeze blowing through, and the smell of fresh paint in the air.

The girls were taken aback when they saw the bedrooms. Both had been stripped, walls painted off white, and lighter carpets, drapes and bed covers laid. They looked so much bigger and were like different rooms.

“Oh my word!” said Alexa loudly, “this is much better than I imagined.”

The three women walked through the bedrooms, gone was the dark gothic look, and in were two clean bright and airy rooms.

“I moved all your stuff into the big bedroom Alexa,” said Bella, “and I have a hallway and a stairway carpet on order too.”

Jen asked Bella if the other two bedrooms were going to get the same makeover as it was possible there would be two more guests staying over summer.

“Yes, the lads are going to do the whole house, priorities were these rooms, the living room and small fixes to the kitchen dining areas. I expect it's at least two more weeks of work to do the rest, I hope that's not going to be too much of a problem?” she said.

“It will be worth it,” said Jen.

“Totally!” said Alexa. “We are only going to be here on Saturday night for the next couple of weeks, as we have a lot still to take care of in Oxford, but once that's finished the plan is to move down here.”

“Oh, Bella, we never talked about it, but the room over the garage, can we add that on to your spooky room renovation list, and give that a makeover too? I think it has some of my mothers old stuff in it, which we can box and put downstairs for now.”

“Oh good idea, I must admit I never really liked going up there, Mike moved all your mums stuff in there before you first arrived, he didn't want you to be reminded of sadder times, but he wanted to keep her memory. I did not want to raise it with your grandad, but I will definitely get it all arranged.”

They spent a pleasant hour in the garden with Bella, some delicious cheese scones, and the now partially cleaned up guys. The other guy was JC's cousin, he looked decidedly dodgy, with his bandana, gold tooth, and a crazy laugh, but after a few minutes talking with him, and about his three children, who he wouldn't shut up about, they re-classified him as “mostly harmless”.
