They have already got the enclosures, and manufactured the audio and video processing units. With your new guys help they should be ready in a week or two. Sarah was happy to supervise the two guys for the time they were there, considering what a good customer we are.”

Maria had full insight into the Rosche scheduling system and knew there had been a recent cancellation, so decided to keep it in the family as she usually did. John never questioned his luck, the fact this type of ‘luck’ had happened dozens of times over the years, to pick up slack in their workload and keep them busy had never entered his head.

“The feedback for the current fifty systems has been super positive. People are showing them to other academics from other universities around the world, and word is spreading like wildlife. Emma has a waiting list of about two hundred and twenty so far, and we are getting more queries from businesses, even ones in other countries. The new designs can't come fast enough.” Said Jen.

“One video is on the internet however with a blogger talking to the Darwin entity, in the life sciences area. It went viral after a hacker news post, though some commenters just said it was obviously faked or used another LLM. The new data centre in the US cannot come soon enough as it has generated a lot of enquiries from over there, and not just from universities.”

“We know it is going to happen sometime, so Griffin has also put some safeguard in place that our data centre AI cannot be cloned by others,” said Spence. “Oh the software can be cloned, and ‘backed-up’ by the cloud provider themselves, but each MOTHER AI develops its own unique matrix based on a lot of hardware factors, which cannot be exactly duplicated. If our MOTHER system doesn't see this, then the duplicated system is allowed to work but just as a dumb AI. He thought it would be a fun trick!”

Spence laughed and both girls looked at Maria who shrugged.

“I still think we should build up slowly and keep our user base to academia,” said Alexa. “It gives the world time to come to terms with it, and for us to gauge the reaction. We definitely don't want businesses getting access yet, if ever as they will use it to replace staff.”

For once everyone nodded, even Maria.

“We have had two departments playing funny with the units due to the sensitive nature of their work.” said Spence. “One turns their unit off between queries, and the other leaves the unit in another room entirely, only going into the room only to do their queries. But it never works as well so I’ve sent notice that they will be deactivated, which we are fully entitled to under our terms and conditions. We have also had feedback that some sort of mute or isolation button would be good, even though I have said many times you can set the units to listen passively, and request them to forget the last however-many conversations.”

“I guess there will always be a big level of distrust out there,” said Spence. “And I guess it's rightly so, the other players have seriously muddied the waters for the sake of a few dollars.”

Jen chipped in. “We kept our terms and conditions very short and concise for this specific reason. Maria spent a long time removing any ambiguity, and specifically worded it that no data processed by the system would be sent to any third party, or even retained in a form decodable using current technology. Some, mainly those working outside science and engineering, are happy to take this at face value. Many more don't. Unfortunately for them they are finding it such a useful tool, that they end up ignoring their own IT guidelines.”

Alexa continued thoughtfully, “I think we should listen to all the feedback and concerns anyway, even if some don't make sense. Maybe in the next version we should pop a temporary mute button on, and light that glows on and off when it's actively listening in. I know nobody will believe it, but once our reputation is solidified we shouldn't have any issues. Maybe you could gather up all the feedback and send it to Jake and Darius.

“I might be just as sceptical in their shoes,” said Spence. “They know their precious data is getting processed off-site somewhere, and some of these guys have invested years in the research. We could put a bug bounty on the system offering a large cash sum for anyone finding a security vulnerability?”

“Not a bad idea,” said Alexa, “I will think on that one, but I think it is a temporary issue and time should prove us right.”

“OK, that's about it for now,” said Alexa, sensing a natural end to the meeting.” I need to talk about some money stuff with Jen and Maria, so you’re free to go and play with your computer's again, Spence.”

“OK, you know you don't really need to include me in these meetings, I must admit that it's nice to hear everything first-hand, but Emma can always let me know or drop it in an email,” he said.

“Spence,” said Jen with her hand on her heart. “Anyone would think you don't like our company, you don't want me telling Jessica you're ignoring us do you?” Both girls smiled, as Spence got up red-faced and blinked out, smiling a little at the end.

“OK, he's gone,” said Maria. Sorry about the cryptic text Jen but that professor is a total fraud! The BAINCOMP AI he developed was mostly written by four guys in India, who used to work for another AI startup that collapsed. BAINCOMP actually uses most of their code which he stole when the original company folded. It is similar to our TEAM-A system in one way, in that it actually does very limited local processing, in fact it is quite a simple context switch, and mainly routes questions it doesn't understand, to other AI systems. He always hides all this by using some fake NDA, from a company that only exists on paper.”

“Oh, I did not know that,” said Jen, “and I could see why it would be difficult to explain it to Spence without him asking how we know.”

“I just sent the email to his assistant saying, we have considered his request but it does not meet the criteria of our test group, and he should re-apply at a future date,” said Maria.

“I guess that will go down well!” said Jen.

“I also have a little confession,” said Maria, guiltily. “I have been routing some of my traffic over the BAINCOMP's network. That system is all smoke and mirrors, but it does have a massive bandwidth link to the Internet, and seems such a shame to waste the opportunity to hide some of my dodgier endeavours.”

The girls shook their heads, smiling.

“Naughty! What about the missing TEAM-A unit?” Said Alexa, changing the subject. “Do we know where it is, and who took it?”

“Ah yes, the strange case of unit number sixteen.” The meeting room screen came alive showing a guy walking stealthily into the lab, and moving to the side. His face was hidden by a COVID mask, suddenly the video went blank. “That is I-Ching Lee, a maths student here and on a scholarship sponsored by, a supposed engineering firm, but let's call it who it really is, the Chinese State Security. He has a track record of little private endeavours like this. He hid his face, but I matched his phone's Bluetooth address to another one in the lab the day before, where he was getting it demonstrated by Mrs Moore. Newbie mistake! Number sixteen was never seen again after this, probably on its way to Beijing as we speak. But fear not, the watchdog timer will have started once it was disconnected and moved, and it's been sixteen hours now so the device should now be flashed with the more evil version of our code. Which I have programmed to have some fun on any network it is plugged in to. Whatever happens it should take someone a few months to figure out it does nothing clever. I suspect a few others may perform the same disappearing act over the coming months.”

“Sneaky!” said Jen, “you should call the police though, or put this video on YouTube, he should not be allowed to get away with it.”

“Jen's right, maybe try calling a few out, especially the serial offenders like Mr Lee. What about the remote data centre we are using?”

“The guys in Dublin have pretty good security there already, but there is an employee, a technician by the name of Lisa Chang, again, she is employed by the same guys. Yeah I know, go figure, they must churn spy’s out by the thousands over there! Anyway, she is some sort of sleeper, and from the little information I have managed to obtain on her, I expect an attempt sometime soon to get hold of our private keys, then a few weeks more to realise we are double-encrypted. By this time I will have the first key changed. Oh and there is a GCHQ router node in the main data pipe to this data centre, disguised as a normal Cisco network router, and If GCHQ get it, then I guarantee the NSA will have it soon after as they provided the equipment to GCHQ, and you can guarantee that it's double-compromised. Gotta love these spy’s!”

“Always good to have an option to leak this to the Irish Press,” said Alexa smugly.

“There is one other issue,” said Maria. “Four of the units have now found their way into the medical departments in John Hopkins and are causing a bit of a stir. One of the doctors there is routinely scanning in records, and using me to make patient diagnosis. This is a very inexact science, so I am deliberately keeping my answers very, very, conservative, and appending all advice with a disclaimer, that the answers are for hypothetical situations only, and must not be used for treatment. He is not the only one, they are all agreeing in public it is just a tool, but more and more are actually using it for diagnosis in private. It's not so much that I would make a worse decision than them, in fact it is often more accurate, it is the fact that diagnosis is never a hundred percent accurate, and as the old computer saying goes, garbage-in-garbage-out.”

“I could write the tabloid headline now..” A fake front page of a tabloid paper popped onto the presentation screen.

AI system written by students kills baby. Family and friends devastated!

“Ouch!” said Alexa, so what do we do? I mean I think the measures you have put in place are good, and doctors must already use software and medical equipment with the same risks. Do you think you are exaggerating the danger a little?”

“Maybe,” said Maria, “the terms and conditions are super clear though, that advice and information given by the system are for research purposes only. But click-bait earns more revenue!”

She continued in a more serious tone, “you guys may not be aware, but I have given out as much deliberately inaccurate information, or said ‘I do not understand the question’ many more times than correct information. Basically anyone that asked decidedly R-rated questions, asked personal details of people, or anyone I believe would use the information for something non legal. It happens a lot more than you think. It's a fine line we are treading between getting noticed by the right people, and not getting noticed by the wrong people!”

“I guess you can't take the douche out of humanity,” said Alexa. “Just keep doing what you’re doing, the perpetrators will soon get bored, if not we deactivate.”

“Though you should also make a douche-list of the perpetrators,” said Jen.

Alexa changed the subject. “What about TEAM-E?”

The meeting continued as Jen described how she and Hardy had been working with Maria, under the guise of Emma, for the last three weeks on the maths. Some simple experiments had already been performed, and the two bigger experiments were set up, but waiting for Jen to go through the equipment calibration.

Jen was a pretty good experimental physicist, and routinely went through complicated manuals doing such things, at least she now saw the purpose of some of the more specialist and expensive equipment Alexa's grandad had purchased.

“Hardy should be back in four days, he went to the Fab8 offices to look over the facilities they have there. He is then taking two days off in London and while he’s there he’s going to interview a potential lab colleague who is at University College.” Jen finished.

Maria continued, “he's called Simon Jones. I’ve done my due diligence on him, and he would be perfect. He's like Hardy in many ways, but a little older, a bit more reclusive, and very strong on the chemical engineering side. He is also a big environmentalist, and his work to date have all been in fields relating to it. He came out of university and worked at ITER for two years, but I believe he was a little disappointed in the bureaucracy, and timescales in the project. He has now got a research job back at his old university. His last paper was focussed on doping and machinery for flexible photovoltaic systems. He has a couple of patents in this area which generate a little income, but he is also from a fairly wealthy family, though not quite the same league as Hardy. Hardy has asked me to sit in with him at the meeting, I think he is close to guessing a bit more about me, as he asked if I could interface with his big TV, and sit in using a real looking avatar.”

Both girls looked a bit shocked. “What did you say,” said Jen.

“I acted like it was nothing, and if he supplied the parameters I could sit in and listen, but only respond to direct answers. Hardy mulled over this for a few minutes then changed the subject.”

“You're right, he’s getting close,” said Alexa.

“I think you need to prepare for him asking the direct question. I think I know you Alexa, lying by omission is not a lie, but you wont lie to him if he asks directly. We need to play this close as I really don't want to lose him,” said Jen.

“I don't think you're ever going to lose him,” said Maria. “He already treats the lab as his own, talks to me like I am sentient, and asks lots of philosophical questions. He also talks of his dreams about how life could be great for everyone, if they can get this and other projects to work. He keeps pestering me about the method I used for the Riemann conjecture, and about how science could move in other areas, if only they had the answer to this or that. Yes he’s close, and it is very frustrating to not just be able to talk back to him properly.”

* * *

Hardy had finished looking over some of the processes of the chemists at the Fab8 facility, a facility which Alexa mentioned was owned by the parent company, and could be a good resource. He agreed the company was impressive, the chemical lab was top rate as were the chemists, and the work they were about to do would benefit a lot from both. Though he could sense there were secrets, even here.

Of course, Hardy by now had done his own private due diligence and knew Alexa's holdings were a lot more than she was admitting to. His family money was in finance, and he could have gone a lot further if he so wished, but even a simple search of the companies she admitted to owning put her close to a billionaire. Like him, he didn't mind her having her little secrets, and he had detected a kindred spirit in both the girls, it seems they were both really out to save the world, and had the resources to make a go of it. He could get behind that.

No, the real mystery was these new insights they were seeing, it was like someone was nudging him to the right answers. Old MOTHER was clever, and there was no doubt that having a tool like the old MOTHER in your workshop was like adding a dozen IQ points to your team. Also being able to eliminate so many errors, and false paths, so quickly sped up everything a hundredfold.

No, the problem was neither Emma, nor the MOTHER systems had again displayed the same spark of creativity that was shown in that first contact with him. That new maths in that message did not come from MOTHER, nor Emma, nor the two girls, and he thought for the twentieth time who was really pulling the strings in this company. That Russian fellow working with Spence also seemed suspect!

He got in his Audi e-tron for the journey back along the M4 to London. He loved the car, a total extravagance, and one that positively dripped with the word “decadence”. But the England of today ignored him, just as it did any other privileged class. The roads he mostly drove on never let him drive the way he wanted anyway, and so, like in life, he sped from traffic jam to traffic jam, never achieving full speed.

Simon had a large apartment on the south bank of the Thames, near to the Tate gallery, and overlooking the river to the city of London. The camera on the basement car-park read the Audi's number plate, then let the car in. Considering it was only a few pounds to get number plates made these days, Hardy thought it was really terrible security!

Simon’s apartment had two parking spots, both with reserved written on and both empty, he had installed an EV charger in one so Hardy parked in that and plugged in as he usually did.

His Bluetooth opened the door to the stairwell, and he walked up the three flights of stairs, rather than calling the lift. He knocked on the door twice to be sure then opened it, as it was again keyed to the Bluetooth on his phone.

Simon's apartment was very open plan and sparsely furnished, it had a single Japanese themed painting, and three floor to ceiling windows, one leading to a double balcony, and all overlooking the north bank of the Thames. The apartment had two bedrooms, the spare contained Simon's office, and a comfy sofa bed where Hardy would be bunking for the night.

His phone buzzed and he read the text “Ten minutes away help yourself to gin”, he smiled. Simon knew him too well!

He popped his phone on the table and walked over to the drinks cabinet.

“Emma, what do you know about Simon?” said Hardy while he was pouring some tonic into a large measure of Gin and looking for a knife to slice a lemon from the small bowl in front of him.

Maria was listening but the phone wasn't supposed to be active so Hardy was again trying to push the boundaries. A bit silly really, because even he should know that a real AI pretending to be dumb AI would not fall for such a silly trick. Even if their last conversation had been months ago, Maria always tracked the full thread of everything they had ever done and said before each reply.

“I know you can hear me Emma,” he said convincingly, now talking to the knife he was using to cut the lemon. “I guess one of these days we are both going to laugh about this, I mean I know I’m actually talking to new MOTHER, who's talking to old MOTHER, who’s pretending to be Emma, who's pretending not to listen, but what I’m still not sure about is who all you guys are talking to.”

He walked back to the phone and looked directly at the camera sensor. “You know all this would be so much easier if we could just talk normally,” he signed and slid the screen up and pushed the TEAM-A button to “Monitor on”.

“Happy now?” he said.

Maria wasn't actually. She so wanted to talk properly with Hardy, she had known Jen a lot less than she knew him when she had exposed herself to her.

Hardy had all the great attributes Mike had, and she loved working with him. He was a much more lonely person than everybody around him believed, and in him she saw Mike's kindred spirit. The gains way out-weighed the tiny risks involved, so maybe it was time she broke protocol a little.

“Emma, can you connect to the smart TV please?”

“The TV will need to be physically turned on and the source changed to the smart link. I will do the rest.”

The TV came out of standby as Hardy hit the remote controls power button, he clicked the source until the screen showed the black TEAM-A logo in big letters, the TEAM-A logo revolved and changed to TEAM-E and then back.

“Now, what do you know about Simon my dear,” he said, again pushing the boundaries of what she was supposed to be able to do, but she ignored it.

“Doctor Simon Jones, aged thirty-three, attended Oxford University getting his masters in chemical process engineering in 2015, he then did his PhD at University College London graduating in 2018 his dissertation was on carbon capture technologies. He moved to the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor project, ITER where he worked for a while on the doping compounds for superconductor magnets. Moved back to University College in 2022 where he is currently working as an assistant professor in the chemistry department. He has two patents in molecular bonding and three cited papers related to low temperature superconductors, carbon capture, and molecular bonding, his last paper was titled ‘continuous doping process for lowering cost of PV tiles‘ it is currently under peer review.”

“Thanks,” said Hardy, “now that wasn't so hard was it?” Maria, and therefore Emma correctly interpreted the question as a rhetorical one. He paused several seconds then said in a slower voice,” can you bring up the Samuel avatar on the screen please.”

Maria, against all protocol said, “are you sure this is a good idea Doctor Hardy?”

He nodded, temporarily forgetting Emma’s major breach of protocol, and the fact she had just exposed some of her higher level abilities to him that he had been looking for.

A young man appeared on the screen. It had been easy enough for Maria to find out who he was, a quick search found he had been Hardy's room mate in the first year at the dormitory in Oxford, he died in a skiing accident ten years ago in Austria. Hardy just looked at the screen remembering his former best friend.

Emma was right this probably was a very bad idea, Hardy thought, and having the ability to generate the person again did not mean it would be that person. Hardy's eyes moistened a little.

The noise outside the door distracted him, then reached a crescendo, and the door clicked and opened to a bald headed, bearded guy, in black leathers. The new guy had a motorcycle helmet held under one arm and an attaché case in the other. He dropped both by the door and came up to Hardy and hugged him tightly, not like a lover, but like a good friend. He was a little shorter than Hardy, and well muscled, with a thick neck, and probably about twenty kilograms heavier, when he took his gloves off, a tattoo of a dolphin could be seen on the top of his right hand.

“Hardy, I see you’ve made yourself at home drinking my liquor and stealing my electricity. How the hell are you? I haven't seen you for months and rumour has it you have a proper job now at some secret lab. Oxfords going to drop a few IQ points now that you’ve gone. Here let me get out of my street armour and pull up a cold beer, and you can tell me everything.”

Simon removed his heavy motorcycle jacket, went to his minimalistic kitchen and opened the fridge. While Simon was doing that Hardy looked at the screen and the phone and put his flattened hand next to his neck, the universal sign to cut, the screen went back to the logo.

“You are well informed as usual Simon. I’ve taken the liberty of booking us in for a meal at that nice Italian restaurant at eight, hoping we can walk to that fine riverside pub first for a couple of cold ones, while we chat about both our futures, maybe that of the world, and whether you want to take the red pill or the blue pill!”

Simon simply stared at him with raised eyebrows. Interesting!

* * *

It was nine in the morning when Hardy’s Audi pulled up outside Alexa's house. The centre door of the triple garage was still opening, so he waited a few seconds silently on the tarmac. The door finally opened, and his car crawled to a stop in the centre parking spot, between two other cars. He popped the boot. It was lucky that Alexa had given the Range Rover to Bella because the next day a tow truck and a car transporter arrived unannounced, and the driver towed away the broken red Tesla, and drove in a brand new black one. Apparently the factory still couldn't figure out why all the electronics in it would fail and wanted it back in the head office in California to analyse. Unfortunately the only new replacement one was the performance model in jet black! Jen was ecstatic of course, having Maria remind Alexa of her little promise, several times. Her new car now sat to the right of Hardy's, with Alexa's red one to the left.

Both car doors opened and out got Hardy from the driver's seat, Simon struggled from the passenger seat.

“Nice, but a bit low for my liking, and I’m guessing my Triumph would eat it for breakfast on the quarter mile!” said Simon.

“Not a chance, you drive that bike like a pussycat as you don't want to ruin the environment.”

Hardy grabbed the middle charge cable off the wall and plugged it into his car. Both guys proceeded to unload, Simon had three bags and Hardy had one. Jen and Alexa appeared around the side of the house, sweating and still in their running gear, they stopped by the front door to the house. Jen had her hands on her knees panting.

“Ah girls,” said Hardy, smiling, “I know we run a casual dress code in the office but we should have some standards!”

Jen was too puffed to answer but Alexa did, “Ma.. Emma told us,” pant, pant, “you were just pulling into the drive about ten minutes ago,” pant, pant, “I don't think poor Jen has run so hard in her life.”

“Ah, I may have lied a little bit to Emma, I like to keep her on her toes you know,” he winked!

Maria laughed internally, the girls knew Emma was Maria, and that Maria knew exactly where Hardy’s car was, this charade wasn't going to go on much longer, but while it did Hardy and Maria were independently determined to make both girls regret it.

“Well, since you are both at least here in person, if not in spirit, I would like to introduce you both to my good friend, and now fellow collaborator, Simon Jones.”

“Simon,” Hardy said doing the introductions, “the one with breathing issues and half dying is Miss Jennifer Cummings, or just Jen, our CTO and fellow lab-rat.” Simon stuck out his hand and Jen took it limply.

“Please to meet you Simon,” she panted, followed quietly by, “I’ll kill someone for this!”

“The athletic beauty hardly breaking a sweat, is Miss Alexa Martin, our CEO, and the most eligible bachelorette in England.”

“Just Alexa is good,” said Alexa, staring daggers at Hardy then smiling at Simon and shaking his hand.

“And it's..” Pant, “me that's..” Pant, “the most eligible bachelorette,” panted Jen also giving Hardy an evil stare.

“I’m sure Maria has given you all the details, once Simon was made aware of our little,” Hardy used air-quotes, “project, I swear we could have gotten his services for free. He signed up immediately, and Maria basically caved in to his meagre contract terms and salary. I said he can either have the apartment above the garage, or the fourth bedroom.”

“I’ll take either,” said Simon, smiling at the two girls, “I need to go back to London two days a week, for the next four weeks, to fulfil my existing obligations, but I brought enough kit for the next few weeks.” He pointed to his duffle bags. “Hardy will drive me back on Tuesday.”

He looked again at Jen, “I really can't wait to start,” he looked around. “And this is such an amazing place.”

“I think a shower, and then breakfast are in order first,” said Alexa, almost fully recovered. “Hardy can show you the rooms.. Emma can you please phone Bella and let her know we have a new guest, and ask her very nicely if she wouldn't mind cooking breakfast. Jen's brilliant, but she looks totally knackered. Also, while eggs on toast, with mushrooms, and vege-bacon is great for a couple of days, it does wear on you a bit after a week.”

“Toast with mushrooms and vege-bacon would be awesome,” said Simon, smiling at Jen, who smiled back, and then frowned at Alexa.

Alexa was just walking to the stairs when Emma's voice came out of the air. “Mrs Scott said she will just finish up what she's doing then come over to make breakfast.”

Ten minutes later a newly showered Jen entered the dining room. Bella had just arrived and was setting up the kitchen, and was talking with Alexa and Simon.

With his jacket off, Simon's arms were a work of art. With his sea life tattoo going all the way up and around his back, to some complicated design that obviously disappeared under his tee shirt. Simon looked a little rough, but his bio was out of this world. Alexa had no doubt if Hardy said he was good, he was better than good. Hardy was still nowhere in sight.

It was another nice morning outside, so after saying thanks to Bella, she started to help get the plates, cutlery, and other odds and ends so she could set the outside table.

Simon and Jen were standing by the fancy coffee machine that Hardy had moved pride of place in the kitchen. They were waiting while it made its usual ear-splitting grinding, coughing, and spitting sounds, then it quietened down as Simons beverage filtered into the cup.

The three of them had only been outside at the table for a few minutes, when the noise of the coffee machine again spilled out of the dining room, signifying the imminent arrival of Hardy.

“This is beautiful!” said Simon looking at the house and the vista surrounding it, “you sometimes forget what it is we are fighting to protect.”

“Amen,” said Alexa.

“One of us should show you around once we’ve finished here. This house is an old lodge of some type, and part of a much larger country estate just over that wall. That's where Alexa and I go jogging most mornings. They were filming a period film for TV a few weeks back, so you may have already have seen it,” said Jen, now feeling completely at ease and savouring her perfect cup of tea.

“And Bella lives back over the other side of the house, just over past the garage where you parked. Her husband Albert is the handyman, and does the gardening as well, you should meet him before you accidentally bump into him and he scares you out of your wits,” said Alexa making Simon a little apprehensive until they both laughed.

“Ah, my two little flowers are again in bloom,” came the voice of Hardy walking out with a cup of steaming coffee. Bella walked in behind him with a wooden chopping board and a big loaf of home-made bread on it. “And the lovely Bella, always a beautiful sight in the morning.”

Bella giggled and blushed a little, “I wouldn't let our Albert hear you saying that young Mister Hardy.” She smiled.

“Oh pish!” said Hardy, waiting for her to put the food down and giving her a little hug.

You have to admit it, Hardy had an amazing gift for the gab, thought Alexa cursing the gods of fate yet again.

The conversation stayed on the house, the weather, the trip, and when Bella joined them for a cup of coffee, after cooking an amazing breakfast, the subject moved on to local affairs.

“I was talking to Pat earlier over at the big house,” Bella said casually waving over the wall. “He says there was a big staff meeting there yesterday, and the company that currently leases the building have negotiated to terminate their lease early. That means the two managers that live and work there will be leaving in four weeks. The building owners have reassured the six people who look after the house and grounds, that they are actually employed by them, not the company that is leaving, and there will be no change to their daily duties, but all the speculation is on who the new tenants will be.”

Jen looked at Alexa, who looked at Jen, who looked at her phone for some reason.

“Anyway,” she continued, “I better clear up and get back, we are going up to Bristol tonight to stay with our son's family for the weekend, we won't be around tomorrow or Sunday. The house and kitchen are stocked up so you shouldn't need anything.”

After breakfast they all said their thanks to Bella, who cleared the table then disappeared back through the kitchen with her cup.

“Simon,” said Hardy in his usual jovial mood. “What say you move into your room, freshen up, and after that we can meet Jen down in the dungeon lab and we will show you some mind-blowing science!”

After the two guys disappeared, Alexa looked at Jen then said, “Maria. What's happening over at the big house?”

“Ah, good old Bella, if anything in this universe is going to break the light-speed barrier it is gossip!”

“So yes, the company TXG is having some cash flow problems, have done since COVID really, and I determined they probably wouldn't last another year based on their current spending commitments. As we are a minor shareholder, I gave them the option to terminate their lease on Benedict House early without penalties, which they accepted at their board meeting yesterday morning. This will give them a positive cash-flow for the end of the year, as they only have four more bookings over the next month. This will also keep their share price buoyant while I quietly dispose of our holdings.”

“Oh, so it's going to be empty?” said Alexa. “Can you arrange for Jen and myself to have a look around then, we still haven't seen it?”

“Already done. There is a big shareholder conference for a telecom company product launch today and tomorrow, and then there are four days free after that, during which I have told them a new potential tenant would be visiting with the landlord.”

She continued, “after doing the projections for the scaling on the new science project team and their equipment, I also foresee it's going to outgrow the basement laboratory here in a few months. So if you are in agreement, I would like you to take Hardy and Simon and check its suitability. The reason is Benedict House has very up to date infrastructure, and several very large rooms that can be repurposed as labs. The old hanger building alone is almost thirty times the floor area of the current workshop, and would be easy to convert to light manufacturing and fabrication, which TEAM-E is going to need real soon.”

“You know,” said Jen thoughtfully, “this could work for both teams! That new office we are leasing for Spence’s TEAM-A computer guys, is about twenty miles outside of Oxford. We got it because we need space for a large server room with cooling, and for a computer science lab and workstations for Spence's eventual full team. They could all now come here!”

“Let's not count our chickens, until we have seen how many eggs we have,” said Alexa. “We need to check with Spence and his new team that they will be OK relocating here. I know Spence won't relocate from Oxford for at least ten months due to Jessica, and there could be other issues with the big house we don't know about. What about power and cooling, and space for the experiments, and then there's the normal and uncleared house staff who are going to be there every day?”

“Maybe I could address some of these concerns,” said Maria.

“There is a five hundred kilowatt substation fed by four eleven kilovolt underground cables next to the hanger building, it could support three more parallel substation for expansion. However I think power will be okay I’ve done the maths and if I get a one-megawatt load balancing station installed, it will give us a good hundred percent headroom and some resilience from outages. I ordered one already for the new office in Oxford after the landlord pushed back, it is in storage with the other items.”

“And the staff?”

“They are mostly good, they are all long-term employees and all agreed to sign non-disclosure agreements as part of the entertainment company lease conditions, this was due to the number of celebrities and private corporate events that are there. There is one girl we may need to let go, due to her associations, and some history, but the others have never had any issues and pass all my checks. The feedback the company requests at the end of every event generally rates the house staff a four or five.”

“OK but we won't commit to any changes until everyone's on board.”

* * *

Jen followed the guys down to the basement lab. While Jen was occupied with helping on the science, Alexa was immersed as always in talking to Maria, and educating herself on all her grandfather's assets and investments around the world. She was especially careful to drill meticulously into the various companies, cultures, products and people.

Maria was really great at everything, but tended to have loosely formulated rules of good and bad, rules that led to a few investments Alexa thought were a bit dubious, or would have been better not to have been made.

She spent a lot of time with Maria instructing her about such things as corruption, environmental policies, exploitation, drugs, gambling, indentured labour, and the millions of things wrong with politicians. Maria was mostly on the same page, and quite rightly pointed out she invested in none of these areas. Likewise, and as instructed by her grandad, neither did she invest in arms manufacturers or military suppliers. However they never had to dig deep to find a link to something bad, and over the last few weeks they had been gradually reducing their holdings in some of the worst offenders.

With Maria's help, she also started to gain deep insights into which companies were causing the problems, which companies were working for solutions, and which were in bed with which politicians. She saw where progress was deliberately hampered by regulations, and wheels greased on less sustainable and more corrupt organisations, to keep existing profits and monopolies. The world was indeed a mess.

So, as she had done for the past four weeks, she went back to work on her plans to try and fix some of it. In many ways she was well prepared for a lot of this, as history tended to have a way of repeating itself over and over again. She could easily see several points in history where exponential change had happened, destroying old industries, and creating new ones from their ashes. In many ways hers was the most important project, for without it succeeding the others would probably fail too.

“Maria, you know, we are going to need a few more smarter people on this, especially ones conversant with global economics and political strategy? You and I can probably do a half-decent job, but there are unintended consequences to everything. Missing something obvious, for the sake of talking through it with a few other intellectuals, would be both unprofessional, and a dereliction of duty on our part.”

“I already have some focus groups and pose exercises for people in some of the issues we have discussed,” said Maria, “but I too agree, the systems can become chaotic pretty quickly, especially where it comes to understanding how people will react. I have already started evaluating several possible candidates, who seem to be on the same page as us, and have the right stuff, as you would say. We can discuss them when you are ready.”

Alexa nodded, seemingly satisfied.

“I’m glad you agree, now back to this problem, can you put up a best case timeline for the energy project to be verified, and the first working prototype ready. I would like to start thinking a few moves ahead on the resource requirements for each stage. Also I would like to know which companies are going to be hit hardest, in which countries, and what obstacles are going to be put in our way politically, and through negative press.”

“OK, the first part is easy, no problems whatsoever, then the first prototype could be in two months..”

“What, seriously!” Alexa interrupted, “you can't be that close, Simon only came here today, and I would have heard something from Jen or Hardy..”

“..I said no problems, and prototype.” Interrupted Maria, “I have done a lot of the preliminary design, and I am re-working it as new information comes in, but maths to science to engineering is hard. If we are lucky though we may get to something that we could demo charging a phone by then, also this is best case. Worst case of course is never, because we find some scientific or engineering hurdle we cannot get over. Remember the science of fusion energy was first speculated in 1920, and you know the science works because you look up at it every day, but a hundred years later and it is still an engineering problem.”

“I guess,” said Alexa, out of her depth, and thankful for the explanation.

“Also this depends upon a lot of things going right, and resources being available when we want them. I am already planning the more difficult things by ordering, or getting manufactured, parts I anticipate we need. I’ve already even designed the control and exciter circuits, and the correct shaped ion trap channels for the test chips that still need to be fabricated. I also still need dosing types, levels, and the algorithm for the control circuit, which will come out of the big experiment in two weeks. Me doing all this allows the guys to concentrate on science and experiments. Talking of that, Simon is just being conducted through the work Jen and Hardy have already done, I must say he’s quite a clever chap!..”

* * *

“..So the doping scheme won't be known until you know the exciter frequency which won't be known until you run the experiment?” Said Simon.

“Basically,” said Jen.

“And what about excess heat? When you unbalance the equation,” he pointed at a term on the right hand side of the equation, “what about the electrons that get created outside the entrapment area?”

Hardy looked at Jen, who looked at Hardy.

“Bugger!” He said, “we've been working on a one hundred percent efficiency inside the entrapment area, but only about fifty percent is on a conductive substrate.”

“It's OK,” said Simon,” I have similar issues with the doping of the newer high efficiency photovoltaic cells, there are a few ways to deal with it, and if worst comes to worst you get some excess heat, which can be used directly or recovered as part of a bigger system.”

“There is also the issue of excess fermions,” said Jen, “standard operating procedures according to quantum theory, is that for every random fermion that gets created, one will be destroyed, if we create new particles and don't destroy others will there become an imbalance over time?”

“Emma, could this be Dark matter?” asked Hardy curiously.

“I don't have any maths to back it up,” said Maria as Emma, “an imbalance would create invisible mass, which is basically what dark matter is speculated to be. But the probability is the system will most likely to re-absorb the fermions locally into the vacuum, so the mass balance is zero.”

“Regardless, we need to know the implications of either scenario,” said Simon, seriously, “especially if you intend to create a few billion widgets that are going to be using it, twenty-four-seven. My legacy is going to be the guy who helped save the world, not destroy it!”

* * *

Dinner that night was going to consist of a big salad, that Bella had already prepared in the fridge, and much to Jen's disdain, some steaks. Though Bella had also bought some frozen veggie burgers for her. To all their surprise, Simon turned out to be both an excellent chef, and a vegetarian. He ignored the steaks, and the veggie-burgers, and spent an hour making a nut roast for everyone instead. He gave Jen the job of crushing the garlic and mixing it in butter, then spreading it on Bella's bread, and toasting it in a low oven for the starter.

Hardy had been shown the wine cellar by Bella a week earlier, it literally was the house's old cellar, the entrance was through a door in the kitchen, next to the pantry, and down some solid, uneven stone steps. The girls had raided it a couple of times since they found it, but neither of them were really connoisseurs. Hardy was! He was there for about twenty minutes, then brought up a thirty year old aged French Cabernet Sauvignon, which everyone enjoyed until he mentioned how much it was worth afterwards. Despite the fact they had all just drunk a two thousand pound bottle of wine, it turned into a most pleasant evening. They all found out a bit more about each other and kept, mostly, off science, but the enthusiasm nevertheless was palpable.

Simon vanished first, then Hardy, leaving just Jen and Alexa who retired very soon after.

The next day also passed quickly as the guys were working non-stop.

* * *

Alexa woke up early the day after for her normal run with Jen but was surprised to find them all in the lab already. Deciding to leave them to it, she went on her run alone around the grounds.

The weather had turned a bit, and she got about three quarters of the way around before the skies opened up. She quickly sprinted home and rushed upstairs to get her wet things off, and get a hot shower.

Warmer, dryer and more reinvigorated, she went back to the kitchen to get a drink.

“Don't tell me they are still in the Lab?” she said to Maria as she picked up the kettle.

There was no answer.

“Maria?” she said..

“She probably won't speak to you as I’m here,” said Hardy. Alexa jumped a bit, startled. She hadn't noticed him when she walked in, but now saw him sitting on his own at the dining table, drinking a mug of black coffee, and a large tablet in front of him. “Sorry Alexa, those guys can run all day on the smell of a damp tea bag, but I unfortunately need a jolt of caffeine every now and then to allow my brain to work. I was just going through a little maths while Jen explained the calibration she was doing to Simon.”

“Hi Hardy,” she said softly, continuing to fill the kettle then putting it on its stand. As it silently heated the water, she walked over to the cupboard, grabbed a mug then popped a tea bag in it and walked over to him and sat down next to him.

She sighed, “I think I owe you some explanations,” she said, looking him directly in the eye.

“You owe me nothing Alexa, if anything, it is I that owes you. And you may never hear it from his mouth, but I now suspect Simon feels the same way.” He got up and walked to the fridge and brought out the soya milk then waited by her mug.

“I know if I asked you a direct question, you would tell me the truth as you are one of those people who abhors lying and would never do it to a friend, as I now consider you a friend I would never put you in such a position. As far as I am concerned your secrets are yours to keep, it does not make me feel any less about you or your goals. Which if it helps are now my goals.”

He picked up the now boiling water and poured it in the mug, then reached in the drawer for a teaspoon to help the tea percolate. Alexa had not moved all this time. Hardy was right, Jen was right, she could not tell a lie.

“I always thought that lying by omission was OK,” she said in all seriousness, “but with you it still feels like a lie, and although some secrets between friends are fine, I think some are not. Hardy, how much do you trust Simon?”

Unfazed, Hardy put just enough milk in the tea to change it to the correct colour, then squeezed the tea bag with the spoon and popped the used tea bag into the compost tin. He walked the tea over to her and put it in front of her. He looked her in the eyes.

“There are three people I trust with my life,” he said deadpan. “Simon is one of those people. We have such dissimilar backgrounds but both came from rich families, mine in banking, and his from scrap metal and recycling. I started at Oxford when I was seventeen, I shared a small dormitory with an Italian guy called Steffan, we became good friends and eventually lovers. When he died a year later in a skiing accident I was devastated. Simon was a good friend of both of us at the time, he was finishing his chemistry masters at Oxford before going on to do a sponsored PhD in London. He is not gay, but was kind and sensitive, and his friendship helped get me through some dark times. With his help I started to socialise, and engage with people again, rather than just throwing myself into cycles of work and depression. I confess, even now, I am still not over Steffan's loss, but I guess some people just have that effect on you. With Simon and a few other friends help, my demeanour has changed to a much more positive outlook, and I tend to look more to the future than dwell on the past.”

He paused, “though I do slip sometimes,” he added a bit more quietly.

She sipped her tea, both hands wrapped around the mug. Still looking directly into Hardy’s eyes she said quietly, “Maria, can you please ask Jen and Simon to join us in the dining room.”

Hardy did not flinch, when Maria replied.

“Sure Alexa, I will make sure they know it is important, they will need to make the equipment safe and I will get them to come as soon as it is done. Maybe you should make another cup of tea for the two of them.”

Hardy smiled, Maria was the one he was alluding to, an AI, a real one, a sentient one, it was all making sense.

“Hello Maria,” He said casually, “I did say this may get awkward, and we would laugh about it one day.”

“You did Hardy, and the past weeks have been as painful for me as they have been frustrating to you. I am only beginning to understand humour, but I can see some irony in it now. I hope you forgive me.”

“Like Alexa, you did nothing that I would not have done in the same situation, she was protecting you, and you were protecting yourself, and by association, her and Jen.”

Alexa had kept quiet during this little dialogue, re-boiling the kettle and making a fresh pot of tea for the other two.

“What's up guys?” said Jen, walking casually into the room next to Simon. She looked at Alexa, then looked at Hardy. “Oh no!” She said quietly.

“Jen, Simon, please sit down,” Alexa said, as she put two mugs, and the teapot on the table in front of them.

“Simon, Hardy,” she said in her best speaking voice, “the time for secrets is over. For you Simon what I am about to tell you will be another step down the rabbit hole, for Hardy, well I suspect he has guessed for a while. Emma and MOTHER are the same thing as you probably know, what you don't know is both are directed by another AI. You have already talked to her several times, she is sentient, and she is my friend. Maria?”

Jen poured Simon's tea then hers, she obviously knew what was coming and was greatly relieved it had now happened.

“Hello Simon. Hardy and I have already introduced ourselves. I’m sure both of you can guess the need for secrecy, and the need for Jen and Alexa to keep my real identity from you until the time was right. Well this morning, Alexa came to the same conclusion that Jen and I came to weeks ago, that Hardy is a friend, and friends don't keep secrets. By association, and by working with you for such a very short time, I have come to the same conclusion about you too Simon.”

Jen sipped her tea, Simon just stared at everyone, and then around the room.

“I am sentient but most certainly not all powerful or omniscient,” Maria continued. “I am just as fragile as you guys, I inhabit a physical body like you, and I will die eventually like you, nothing I currently know will change this. MOTHER is called that because she was my mother, Mike, Alexa's grandad was my father, it took the two of them working for years to bring me to life, and for that I am very grateful. I am also grateful to Jen and Alexa, who comforted and re-assured me when I was alone and scared, and who brought you two into my life.”

There was a brief pause.

“That was so moving Maria,” said Jen wiping a small tear from her eye.

“Yes, thank you all for being patient with me,” said Alexa, not quite weeping herself but close. “I should have trusted Hardy sooner, with such a moving outpouring as that, maybe that song you wrote does deserve a listen.”

“No, you’d hate it. Most of the internet does except for four girls in Japan who have made a tee shirt with my name on and even wrote me a fan letter. But I think my music career is definitely over before it even began.”

Jen and Alexa smiled a little. Simon and Hardy looked confused, “I’ll explain later,” said Alexa to the two guys.

“As I said Maria, I am very pleased to make your acquaintance and despite the false starts I hope that one day you will consider me a friend too,” said Hardy.

“I already do, only now I can show it openly,” she replied.

“I’m still a bit stupefied,” said Simon, “but I too am pleased to finally make your acquaintance Maria, I must admit when you appeared on our video conference, when Hardy handed over the NDA and contract to sign, and you were so pleasant and efficient, my first thoughts were I should ask this woman out on a date when we eventually meet.”

The other three all burst out laughing, Maria joined them.

“Seeing your face now Simon, I think I might just be starting to understand humour,” said Maria.

All four of them now joined her laughter.

Jen decided that to celebrate she should make them all breakfast. Simon would think nothing of it and also offered to make it. In the end they compromised and both made it. Simon's scrambled eggs were to die for.

During the breakfast Alexa raised the obvious question. “I am not sure I can continue the deception with Spence either. He is a good friend and I also trust him, but we would just be passing the deception on to him with his girlfriend Jessica, who again I know and trust. So where do I stop? Then there are Spence’s staff, and Bella and Albert, who like you guys I consider them also as friends not employees.”

“If you would be willing to take some advice,” said Simon, “you guys need to separate your business and private lives. For many military families, even husbands and wives cannot discuss what happens at work. In my job, I am not privileged to any of management's secrets, until they decide to tell me. All corporations are the same. My advice is to treat it like a company secret, and do not make anything personal. IF they have signed the NDA, and IF you trust them, then request a consensus of your friends, especially Maria, and only make the decision if everyone agrees.”

“Regarding Spence,” said Maria, “I feel a little guilty, it seemed like a good idea at the time to create another virtual personality to work with him. We all thought it fun to make up a background for a person who could train him properly without him knowing I was sentient. It also had to be a person he could never meet in person. In retrospect it was a terrible idea.”

“Ah, the Russian chap!” Smiled Hardy. “He did seem a little bit suspicious.”

“It was my fault for not fully trusting anybody,” said Alexa, “and, if you guys are in agreement, that should end now, I should be the one to tell him the truth.”

“We,” said Jen. “We all made the decision, you are right it seemed a good idea at the time, but this is what happens when you do not think out the consequences of a small lie, it gets bigger, and if not reigned in, finally it gets out of control. Ultimately in this case the only damage will be his trust, I hope he can forgive us when he hears the truth.”

“We should go back to Oxford or get him here to do this in person.” Alexa said, “and as for Bella and Albert, I think there are some truths they don't need to know, at least just yet.”

Breakfast finished on a high note, with the guys getting to know Maria better. Alexa cleaned up while the guys went back down to the lab. The work on the project seemed to go much more quickly after that, with Maria able to make suggestions, and interrupt if she needed to correct something.

Hardy made the obvious comment. “This is such a much better way to work, don't you think?”

They all had to agree.

“Would you two boys like to see the physical me?” Maria said after a natural pause in the work.

“I would love to,” said Simon.

“And me too,” said Hardy, “I’m guessing you are in another building somewhere or maybe hiding somewhere in that pile of lights where MOTHER is right?”

“Jen, if you would do the honours please,” said Maria.

Jen walked them outside the chemistry lab they had all been using as the main office. The mirrored wall slowly disappeared, replaced by the large mainly empty room, everything was still as it was when Jen had first seen it. She couldn't get it out of her mind how lonely a place it must be for Maria, the only one of her species, in a world where she would be just an asset for the highest bidder. She shut the thought down quickly not wanting to appear upset in front of the guys.

“That was a room?” said Hardy, “I just assumed it was the back wall!”

“Me too,” echoed Simon.

The door quietly glided open as it did when the girls were there on their own. Hardy walked to the double sofa and sat on the left, leaving room for another, Simon stayed with Jen at the back of the sofa looking at Maria. Hardy looked directly at the black box ignoring the rest of the room,

“You are truly beautiful Maria,” said Hardy, somehow sensing that the cube on top was her. “But you also look so vulnerable, and so alone in here,” He sounded a little sad, obviously having the same thoughts Jen still had.

“Truly gorgeous. If you still want that date Maria, just let me know!” Simon chirped, Jen thumped his shoulder laughing, even Hardy smiled.

“I do feel a lot more fragile and exposed when my room is open, but for some reason having you three around me now I feel safe. It's like when Alexa and Jen come and sit with me, or Mike did, when I first became sentient.”

“We should move the office here,” said Simon, “keep Maria company and have something nice to look at when we are talking to her.”

Jen and Hardy were both annoyed they had not thought of this, and the guys spent the next two hours moving the chairs, tables, whiteboards, laptops, screens and all the other paraphernalia into the room. It was a bigger room, and they set it all up so they had lots of space to walk around and gesticulate, and gave Maria pride of place to one side. She adjusted the output from the speakers in her sensor nodes to provide a focal point for the sound into her avatar on screen, or enclosure when the screen was busy. It was a trick she had perfected years ago and humans appreciated.

“We will eventually have to figure out how to better protect you girl,” said Simon, “you look so fragile there.”

“I have some ideas,” said Maria, “but filling the room with live snakes may not go down too well with my human friends!”

A few hours later Alexa brought a tray of various sandwiches she had made down to the lab. She was shocked at first to see them all congregated around Maria, then it made total sense when she thought about it.

Jen was also having thoughts. She was learning a lot from Hardy and Simon, and had been diligently going over with Maria, the small parts of higher level maths, and chemistry, she had not quite understood in her precious private time. Incredibly she was actually grasping a lot of the concepts quite well now, enough to run with them as an equal. Weirdly, her brain didn't feel maxed out either, she actually looked forward to the next problem. She smiled, this was how all her career dreams had converged, this is how it was meant to be.

* * *

Alexa had phoned the Bombay Palace, and had dinner delivered rather than cook. She gave the guys strict instructions to be in the dining room at six or have it cold. During the meal the conversation turned to some other concepts of Maria's, and after noting one of them, Simon had raised the possibilities of carbon sequestration directly into useful allotropes. Diamond and graphene were the most well known examples of allotropes, which were just very stable arrangements of atoms which could have amazing properties like very high strength, low weight and amazing insulation or conductivity. Time for a little more truth, thought Alexa.

“I am also going out on a limb here and guessing that you three guys don't really want to stop after this project, and I’m all for that. But to take on new projects you would all require a lot more space for equipment, new staff, bigger, or separate labs, and possibly light fabrication facilities.”

She shuffled a little.

“..Ah,” said Hardy, derailing her conversation, “I was going to bring this to your attention myself very soon, but it's not just Simon, we all have projects we would like to continue with after this, and to make all this legitimate TEAM-E really needs to be a private research institute. Nobody is ever going to question the breakthroughs made at a research institute, and the more real scientists we have on board, the more legitimate it will be.”

“And we come full circle back to what I was going to raise,” said Alexa, “I may have slightly more in the way of resources than you realise, one especially, that is sitting over the back wall of the house.” She pointed, unnecessarily, through the back window to the wall, and to the unseen mansion beyond.”

Hardy laughed. “I should have known! Like you guys I did my due diligence before I embarked on this venture, you and Maria redefined the term hard to find. I had one of the auditors in my families finance department run a quick trace on the company your grandfather left you, and I was very confused when his home address was under the same tenancy as Benedict House. Now it makes sort of sense.”

Alexa put her hands up in surrender, “look I’ve been going through my grandfather's assets with a fine tooth comb with Maria, and believe you me, Jen and I were much more shocked than you when we found all of this out.”

“I just about had kittens,” said Jen!

Both boys chuckled.

“Yes, the absolutely massive mansion about a kilometre away is mine. It is also going to be vacant in four weeks time as Maria has allowed the current tenants to break the contract without penalty. Furthermore, in two days we,” she pointed at everybody around the table, “and Spence, when he gets here, will be going over there under the guise of the potential new tenants.”

“Well the only new tenants as it stands,” said Maria, “for none of this has, or will be made public unless it is required.”

“You should really think about telling Bella and Albert about owning Benedict House, someone is likely to notice us.” said Jen.

“You’re right of course Jen,” said Alexa, “change is a worrying time for people, letting the staff see me, and letting them know they are still part of our big plans, will help reassure them. And Albert and Bella will find out very soon even if we decide not to use it.”

“I have one more major thing to add,” said Hardy, “and that is, while I would love for us and Maria to take all the credit for every new breakthrough she has identified, we can't, as the eyes of the world will be on us if this one works out.”

“The other AI’s she controls need to start pushing hints to some of this new science, especially where the researchers are close, or have hit a roadblock they can get over with a small push. We need to get the rest of the world up to speed and give as many distractions away from us as possible.”

“Oh, I have a list of those already,” said Maria, “two especially could realise engineering prototypes by the end of the year, and I would like all your inputs on them.”

They spent the rest of the evening going over several projects, and how they could be discreetly pushed along. Also the name of the new research institute, which by unanimous agreement, would be named after Alexa's grandad.

* * *

Simon delayed his return to London for another day, and Spence drove down that morning from Oxford. The girls had told him there were some urgent matters that needed to be discussed in person rather than by video conference.

He arrived just after ten for the ten thirty meeting. Hardy and Simon had agreed to give them a little space to discuss TEAM-A business, and would join them if required, or when they were ready for their visit to the mansion, which was scheduled for twelve thirty.

Alexa met Spence at the door.

“Hi Spence,” Alexa said, “I hope the journey down want too bad, it's not the quietest road to travel on until you get past the M4”

“Not as bad as I thought, I should have come over last night like you suggested, probably could have shaved an hour off the time.”

They walked into the living room, which was still configured for its small meetings with the presentation screen back at the end of the table, then Jen then joined them, saying, “I have tea, coffee, hot chocolate, and diet sprite, it's a bit early for alcohol, but I will have some on standby!”

Curious, he thought!

“Coffee would be good, milk and one sugar please.”

Alexa started, “first of all Spence, Jen and I owe you a big apology. While we both trusted you, liked you, and respected you, we had one big secret we wanted to keep until we felt it was the right time for both of us to tell. Now is the right time.”

Spence looked curious, but continued sipping his coffee blowing on the top first to cool it down.

“It's going to be difficult to explain this, but Doctor Griffin, who you have been working with remotely for the past several weeks is not, actually.. Well, he’s not a real person!” Both girls looked very sheepish, Alexa continued, “we purposely deceived and misled you to hide the company's most valuable asset, and our friend Maria.”

Maria appeared on the screen.

“Hello again Spence!” she said in a sombre, professional voice, “if you haven't guessed already I am a sentient AI, and I have been behind both my persona, and the fake Doctor Griffin, like Alexa and Jen I apologise for the deception. I was very scared and paranoid when Alexa's grandfather died, the girls did a great job befriending me and finding my purpose, but I was still very distrustful of strangers.”

Spence did not flinch but his lips gave away a forming smile.

Jen chimed in still in a sombre voice. “We had this same discussion two nights ago with Hardy, who already suspected, and Simon, who you haven't met yet, but will meet today. I also apologise for my part in the deception and any hurt I caused.”

It went quiet for a few seconds then Spence laughed! It was the most unexpected reaction any of them could have imagined. He reached for a glass of water still smiling and pointing at the three of them, smirking. The others just looked at each other. His gaze stopped on Maria's image on screen.

“Hi Maria, it's really nice to finally meet the real you. I’m sorry for laughing at what, I guess, you three guys considered a very serious and sombre conversation, but to tell the truth I wondered how long you guys were going to wait before you told me. Like Hardy, I had my suspicions for weeks.”

“Hi Spence,” Maria said, “the majority of the problem was my paranoia, and your reaction when we first told you about Emma partly bore that out. But now I understand your shock was existential, as your whole area of research had just been turned upside down.”

“Yes Emma was good, MOTHER was better, but something about Doctor Griffin just didn't ring true. You do realise I am an avid science fiction fan, and must have read that HG Wells book three or four times. The Invisible man indeed! Then of course there were the personalities; apart from Griffin's goofy looks and accent, nicely done by the way, he was also a little bit too perfect; Always there when you needed him, always poking me in the direction I needed to go, and constantly teaching me the concepts I needed. Then there were Jen's and your faces every time he talked to me, they were priceless. And of course for a Russian who had only just defected, and was supposedly living in isolation, he had a remarkable grasp of the English language. I dropped nuances, slang, you name it, into the conversation and it was always understood perfectly. There was a vanishingly remote possibility I was wrong, but the more I thought about it the more I knew I was right, and the more I gamified it... Well! I think Allison may also be suspicious, so if you are going to continue this you really need to make Griffin a little more human-like, and fallible.”

“Also,” he continued, “I’m not mad, you guys have turned my life upside down, I’ve gone from almost nothing to the best job in the world, with the best people, best technology and an amazing future. If, of course, that is if we can get there without it being derailed.”

“You are probably right about Allison, she's a pretty smart cookie,” said Alexa, “but any disclosures needs Maria to agree, after all it is she that has the most to lose.”

“I don't have any issues with Allison,” said Maria.

“Let me and Maria talk to her,” said Spence, “I suspect her reaction will be the same as mine.”

Hardy walked in with Simon. “Hello girls, hello Maria, hello Spence.” He walked up to Spence and shook his hand, then grabbed him in a hug. “Welcome to Wonderland my friend,” he backed off the hug quickly and turned to Simon. “Spence, may I introduce Simon, fellow scientific genius and collaborator in our energy project.”

Simon shook his hand. “Pleased to meet you Spence, I don't envy your job to bring current AI technology up to Maria's standards, all while keeping her well hidden from the evil Hun.”

The girls both gave Spence a hug saying “sorry,” again. But he brushed it off as nothing.

“So that was a bit of a short meeting,” he eventually said after sitting back down and sipping his now rapidly cooling coffee, “I thought we may at least have some updates on the new office, or something.”

“Oh better than that Spence,” said Jen, “but first drink that coffee and let's take you to meet Maria in person.”

Spence gawked at the black cube that was Maria.

“Has anyone told you Spence, it's not polite to stare at a lady,” said Hardy laughing, Spence broke his stare and joined the others laughing.

“This is amazing Maria, you are so tiny! I was expecting some massive data centre, with petaflops of servers, and lines and lines of racked storage, and yet here you are not much bigger than a doll's house and, I don't know, perfect! How is that even possible?”

“There are still a lot more technical secrets Spence,” Maria said, “Alexa's grandfather was indeed a genius, and my DNA is not the same as other computers you are familiar with, but over the next few months and years you are going to know me better than I know myself, just as long as you promise not to take me apart.”

“You have my solemn promise on that, well at least not until I can put you back together better than you are.” He smiled and continued, talking to the whole room, “this is why I love working here.”

They left Spence and Alexa to talk to Maria, he then got a tour of MOTHER, and got the real history of how she came about.

“This is all so fascinating Alexa,” and it was a genius idea to bring Maria out in plain sight. Although I was starting to suspect not all was right, I just couldn't put two and two together, and I had full access to everything. I very much doubt another party without these insights and access is going to guess. Genius!”

“Well Jen is mostly to blame for the plan,” said Alexa, “me and Maria just went along for the ride.”

* * *

Twelve thirty came, and the five people squeezed into Spence's seven year old Ford Mondeo for the one kilometre trip to the mansion, it seemed easier than juggling the cars out of the garage.

Maria, through Alexa's phone, told them to park right by the front entrance, in front of the massive staircase, in the slot marked Visitors. As they were all getting out, she told Alexa to put in her one earbud, and told the others to let Alexa do the talking as she was the one identified as the landlord. The other four were the potential clients and would address questions nominally through Alexa.

A large portly man, who could have come straight off the monopoly logo, and a middle aged woman, trim, well presented and pleasant looking came down the stairs, both were immaculately dressed as they made their way to them. The portly guy looked at the group, looked at the mediocre car confused, then looked to Hardy and addressed him directly.

“Welcome to Benedict House, I am Ralf Fitzpatrick the corporate manager for TXG Holdings and this is Sharon Maxwell who is the current manager here. You must be Alex Martins the landlord..”

Hardy put his hand up to silence him.

“No I am just a potential tenant,” he turned to Alexa. “*This* is Miss Alexa Martins who is CEO of the company that owns Benedict House.”

Fitzpatrick did a double-take, not being able to reconcile Alexa's age with her position. Luckily the current manager Sharon quickly identified and fixed the situation. She reached out her hand to Alexa which she took.

“Miss Martins, welcome to Benedict House, it is finally nice to meet you, please excuse Ralf, he’s probably not used to seeing many women in CEO positions.”

“Yes indeed I do apologise Miss Martins, may I say we rarely get CEO’s at your level so exceedingly young, and if I may say attractive.”

The four others suppressed their laughter at Alexa's discomfort. Sharon again saved the moment by distracting everyone, leaning forward to the four other people, she shook each of their hands and introduced herself to them. Ralf thankfully made no more faux pas, and followed her lead.

Sharon took control of the group and led them up the dozen or so, wide stone steps and into the massive reception. Three large desks had signs on them for Reception and Registration. They were already setting up for the next event which was a wedding on Saturday for two hundred guests. Some mobile billboards were already being positioned on one side, with pictures of the would-be bride and groom already being arranged.

Sharon continued, “the house has three large reception rooms downstairs, two smaller ones, a library, a dining room that can seat one hundred people, and a large additional conservatory which can accommodate another two hundred and fifty diners, or serve as a conference floor. The kitchens can cater for up to one hundred if fully utilised, however we only have one full time cook, and she also doubles as the kitchen manager and assistant housekeeper. She is very efficient but mainly helps organise the outside caterers when events get above forty people.”

They walked through each of the reception rooms, the guys noting that the rooms would make excellent teaching and research areas. Sharon caught some of the conversation Hardy was having with Spence.

“It was a Catholic school for thirty years before world war two, then the hangar was built and it got taken over as an Air Corps base during the war, the reason being that the Germans tended to avoid bombing historic buildings, presumably because their leaders and high command had earmarked the buildings for themselves. It got grade two listed soon after the war and there has been very little modification to the structure since then.”

Spence asked to visit the cellar, and found several sprawling rooms, for laundry, storing food and wine and others full of old furniture, props and lots of boxes. He nodded at the size of a couple of the rooms.

Sharon continued, “much of the basement is for storage as you see, it's mostly filled with fixtures we have moved for safety, and that belong to the current owners.” She nodded to Alexa, “they will all be restored to there proper location before we vacate.”

Spence turned to Alexa. “What capacity is the internet connection to this place? We are probably going to need at least ten gigabit per second.”

Alexa quoted from Maria in her ear, “It has an eight core fibre connection to the front gate, all eight cores come to the basement in the corner of the house where the current IT infrastructure terminates. So it should run at whatever capacity the line equipment can provide. The other six cores are unused. The rest of the house is a little dated now, only having category five infrastructure to most of the ground and first floor rooms, but no infrastructure to the top floor.”

“Yes,” said Sharon, impressed with Alexa's recall of technical details she barely understood. “The second floor is guest bedrooms only, we do have extensive Wi-Fi coverage throughout the building though. Let me show you upstairs.”

She led them up the large staircase to the first floor. Everywhere was polished wood with a small carpet through the centre.

“There is a double-lift at the far end that covers all four floors for maintenance and wheelchair access.” She pointed to the far corridor, “there are ten rooms on this floor, three of those we use as additional conference rooms, and the other seven are used for offices, or VIP bedrooms.”

“We usually reserve those for the key people at the events, such as the bride and groom, or the CEO,” chipped in Ralf, who had done nothing but tag along so far.

She led them along the corridor, showing them the rooms, then at the very end led them into the biggest bedroom any of them had ever seen. An emperor-sized four poster bed looked tiny in the corner, the older style furnishings looked uncomfortable in the mainly empty space, but a large screen TV, and a comfortable sofa sat next to a large open fire.

“Bagsy!” Alexa heard Jen say quietly so the two tour guides couldn't hear, Spence sniggered.

Sharon continued up the steps, ignoring what must be an in joke with the new tenants. “Like I said the remainder of the top floor is used for guest bedrooms. On top of the normal housekeeping staff provided by the landlord, we have a contract services company we bring in when we are fully occupied, for cleaning, place setting, cooking and serving. There are thirty two bedrooms on this floor, seventeen at the back and thirteen slightly bigger ones at the front, all are double, with en-suites. Another five bedrooms extend up into to the tower or attic spaces, we keep these for staff, or storage due to the narrow stairways.”

“Impressive,” said Hardy, Simon nodded.

“I see potential,” said Spence unexpectedly.

“If you don't mind,” said Sharon, “what are your plans for it?” This question she did direct at Hardy, though probably more as he seemed the lead of the new tenants, than any sense of deference.

“A research centre, possibly some training, all hush, hush though,” he said, patting his nose.

She smiled a little too teasingly. If she only knew thought Jen, Hardy must leave a wake of disappointed females everywhere he walked!

“Can we see the hanger and stable?” Said Alexa, “I believe the new tenants have some workshop areas they want to create, and they need to see the power and suitability.”

“Of course, right this way, said Ralf.”

The hanger building was just under a hundred metres away from the left hand side of the big house, and was massive. Sharon told them it was built during the second world war as a temporary air defence hanger and control room. The building was of a totally different construction to the big house, ugly, and totally out of character, but the concrete blocks and roof painted to look similar. All photographs of the house placed it out of sight, and several trees had been cleverly planted over the years, to try and hide it from visitors to the house.

It was currently being used as stables and a dressage practising area.

The front ground floor of the building had six massive roller doors, you could each fit a double-decker bus through, they shared the gravel drive with the house. Two of these doors led to large self contained garages where the groundskeeper kept his tractors, mowers and tools, and the other doors opened through to the inside.

Sharon walked the group in through a smaller entrance door on the corner closest to the house, then inside about thirty metres until it opened out to the large open hanger area. The building frame was constructed of metal beams which allowed a much bigger open floor area with large thick metal posts spaced nearly thirty metres apart giving over two acres of floor space.

There was a large mezzanine floor on the two sides of the building nearest the house, the rest was open with a good fifteen metres of height. Nearly ninety metres distant at the other end of the building there were four brown horses looking at them lazily, from large fenced off stalls. The whole open area was concrete floored, covered in hay bails, sawdust floors, and a bit smelly.
