“Oh, I’m so sorry,” said Magnus, turning back to Alexa but still not quite meeting her eyes, the uneasiness in his voice that was absent talking with Maria, returned. “I sort of assumed you and Maria would have talked about my job beforehand.” He took a small sip of his peppermint tea, which seemed to calm him more, then continued very occasionally making eye contact then breaking off quickly as if he had seen something he shouldn't have.

“Well no Mr Richardson,” she said pleasantly, “Maria thought it would be nice to surprise me, didn't You Maria? so I know nothing at all about you, or why you are here, or any job, but since we have some time and are comfortable, why don't you tell me.”

Richardson looked worried at this, but continued in his most pleasant tone, “I posted some math on one of the physics forums about six months ago. It got little response at the time except for a few very negative comments from people who did not look to understand what I was trying to prove. It was a bit disheartening to tell the truth. Then this mysterious person contacted me out of the blue via a private message saying I was close, but might need a little help to get over a few mistakes. That person then gave me the help that got me over that first hurdle. Of course that person turned out to be Maria.”

Ah, so he was a scientist, well she was close! She took a sip of her tea, all ears for the time being, he would eventually get to the point.

He also took another sip of tea, looking at his Danish pastry hungrily, when Alexa did not immediately belittle him, and continued to look at him with some interest, he continued.

“Me and Maria have been working together since then and she has helped me refine and test my theory and the maths, I’ve learnt so much from her, she is awesome.”

He paused but again nobody spoke, so he continued. “About a month ago, Maria told me she was the same AI that was in the presentation and on the paper for the QVCell. I had harboured some optimistic suspicions earlier that this was the case, as the answers Maria was giving were just too good and the replies too fast.”

“My bad,” said Maria, giving him time to take a bite of his Danish, “I do make sure I put appropriate delays and fuzziness into answers with people I am not sure about these days.”

Magnus sipped his tea again, then continued, “two weeks ago I received notification that the project I was working on would close and that all our team would be made redundant immediately. As you could imagine I was very distraught, but before I had time to process my job loss and my future, Maria offered me a job working at your Research Centre to see if we could refine the math, and work with some of her colleagues to take the research in a practical direction! Of course I jumped at the offer and a few days later I received an open return ticket for a flight to England.”

Magnus countenance brightened, and his face took on a curiously child-like appearance as if he was recalling a good memory, it was probably reserved for Maria, and felt slightly out of place between the two of them.

She could see he was obviously not used to dealing with people, yet with Maria he was fine, it seemed strange seeing how intelligent he obviously was and how, possibly with a little effort, he would probably be likeable. She smiled, thinking of Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion, then quickly hid it before he again looked at her. Alexa and Jen had discussed many times why it was that some guys, despite their intelligence, failed so badly when it came to interpersonal relations, a simple assertiveness course or even small things like martial arts or even dance classes would do so much to help drop this weird stigma surrounding some of them, one which almost certainly held them back in life too.

Again Alexa wished she had a way of communicating with Maria that was not verbal in situations like this so she could ask her what she was supposed to do or say, hell Maria hired and fired hundreds of people a week without her even being aware of it, as if reading her mind Maria stepped in.

“I’ll just chip in a little here if that is OK, Magnus. Alexa, I work with a lot of students and researchers these days, well eight months ago I was doing my usual trawl through the science stuff and came upon Magnus's post, what he proposed blew me away. He has basically worked out the maths for micro-singularities..” Maria never finished.

“Aren't singularities black holes?” said Alexa, moving her cup back on the table alarmed.

“A singularity is just a term for where our axioms for science and maths break down and outcomes become unknowns. Infinities, or dividing by zero are easy examples. Yes singularities include black holes and the big bang, but in our case it wouldn't be anything that exciting, [well possibly]. Magnus’s work effectively ignores the maths and physics breaking down in a singularity and introduces a new axiom which would allow us to go past the usual infinities and creates some scenarios where..”

Maria saw she was losing Alexa, as she often did just when it got to the interesting parts of the science, she inwardly sighed and moved back on track. “Well, I won't bore you with the details, but I immediately saw that it could open the doors to some new science. However first we need to test the theories which means doing some experiments here where we have the best brains and equipment.”

She continued, noting Alexa seemed to be coming back on track. “There are also some serious implications with the maths for the work Hardy is doing, and Hardy is in full agreement we need to move this forward with the same priority as the others. I quickly offered Magnus a job to work here with all the resources he needs in order to prove or disprove the theory and without anyone to judge him.”

She wondered why Maria went to the trouble of having this meeting rather than just do it, then Maria answered for her. “The thing is Magnus here is a big fan of you and your goals and I thought I would surprise him by meeting you, it's the least I could do for him since the chaos of the last few weeks.”

“Maria, you are definitely getting weirder,” said Alexa, at least now understanding she was just a prop and did not have to do anything. She signed inwardly, why was it never a history or economics person, always a physicist or a mathematician! Hopefully it was just a one-off, she could play the game for Maria.

She turned to Richardson, who was also smiling and back in his relaxed puppy dog mode, idly sipping his tea. “So, another physicist!” she sighed, but in a jokey way, “I tell you what, you call me Alexa and I will call you Magnus,” he nodded and she continued.

“What say we finish these lovely Danish pastries and I take you for a little tour of the research centre. We can meet some of the guys, show you the laboratories we have, and I can set you up in one of the apartments here, then once you’re settled we can get you doing some research..”

Before she finished the sentence, Jen walked into the room soaking wet in her running gear, she had obviously just been out for her morning jog and had got caught in the same shower Alexa had. She saw Alexa and made a bee-line towards her.

“Hi Sis!” she said, looking at Magnus, who was open-mouthed looking Jen up and down. Jen looked around herself quickly, self consciously thinking there must be something wrong with her wardrobe, or lack of!

“Oh my!!” said Magnus bursting from his seat, “you’re Jennifer Cummings!” He thrust his hand out, Jen slowly and reluctantly did the same, still unsure what was happening as the guy wiggled it up and down like a skipping rope.

“Oh Jen,” said Alexa smiling, “meet Magnus, fellow physics geek and possible genius according to Maria.”

Magnus, remembered Alexa's face when he shook her hand too long and broke off. “I’ve been such an admirer, you and your team were such an inspiration to us guys in the lab, that paper of yours I must have read it ten times, when you guys gave that presentation it was done so beautifully, I was so proud for you all..”

Alexa could see Jen looking a bit uncomfortable, time to cool things down.

“Magnus,” she said in her best matronly voice, “you should probably let Jen go get some breakfast, and maybe have a shower and dry off.. If you are going to be working here, you and Jen are probably going to be seeing each other a lot.”

He retreated a little inside himself, sinking back slowly into his seat, then again trying to straighten his hair and suit, oh god he looked terrible and now.. He hoped he hadn't just made a bad impression with Jen.. “Oh, so sorry, I guess I was a bit over enthusiastic, it's just..”

“Magnus,” said Alexa, more friendly and less matronly, “it's fine, you will have plenty of time to talk to Jen and all the guys here, we normally arrange some welcome drinks for new people so we will do that tonight and you can meet the rest of the guys in a more laid back social setting.”

“That sounds fun,” said Jen, nonchalantly, she looked at Magnus again unsure what to think, she wasn't even sure who he was as their introduction had been a bit one sided. She would ask Maria as soon as she got a tea.

“What Alexa says, I’m a little wet and smelly at the moment and I will feel a lot better after a shower and a croissant, or maybe a croissant then a shower,” she said as she saw Daisy walk in, she turned back and winked at Alexa, who smiled and winked back.

“OK guys catch you both later,” Jen walked to the breakfast table and then walked over to Daisy at the coffee machine.

Magnus was watching a very damp Jen wiggle her way to the breakfast bar where Daisy had appeared, she inwardly sighed a little at Maria not telling her about this fanboy worship side of him, but if she said he was good, then it was probably worth ignoring a few smaller quirks and it didn't hurt to let Jen have a little hero worship.

She coughed to get Magnus's attention.

“I’m sorry Alexa, I’ve never been that good around people, especially women,” he said shyly. It was a very frank admission, he wasn't sure what made him say it and he immediately regretted it, what would she think, he was making a terrible first impression.

“That's a very honest admission Magnus,” said Alexa softly. “People around here have been thrust into the world media's attention for the past three months, they cannot go out without the press following them, their families are contacted and hassled, it's a little bit of a nightmare.”

“The one sanctuary from all that is here in the Research Centre. In here we treat everyone equally and as friends, there are no egos, no Prima Donna's, and we certainly don't want fanboys! You have to remember we are just people like you. Here Jen and I are no different to..” she pointed over at the breakfast bar and immediately recalled the girls name, “Jannice serving at the breakfast bar, we do not have any layers of management, you all work for me and Maria, and Maria and I work for you.”

She held his hand softly, surprising him, then she looked into his eyes reassuringly, for the first time he looked back into her eyes, he might be quite cute now that she thought about it but that scraggly beard and those glasses just had to go.

“You are part of a team here, an equal participant, if your idea differs from your colleague, we have sufficient resources to see who is correct and Maria will be the arbitrator. Treat people friendly and with respect and they will treat you back the same, and remember, that if your theories are proven it is likely that it is you going to be in the spotlight and you wouldn't want your friends treating you different because of it?”

Magnus was nodding or shaking his head throughout Alexa’s monologue. Maria, who had been remarkably silent during all this spoke up, “I think you are going to do great here Magnus, but Alexa is right, you need to treat everyone you meet as normal people, not rock stars. Think of it as another lesson in life, one where you will hopefully come out of it with some good friends and experiences.”

“See Magnus, even the super-smart AI agrees you need to chill out!” She smiled, and a faint one also appeared on his face. “You know people do their best work when they are relaxed, with people they know and like, and are free to think and challenge the normal. I’m sure you will be no different, and I bet by this time next week, you won't even notice if me or Jen are in the same room.”

Looking at all the smart young people casually dressed and confidently chatting, then remembering what he looked like, he sighed, she was right, he needed to change, he had tried in the previous job but retired mostly into his shell. The intimidation and put downs from the senior researcher made nobody happy and the whole place was a toxic environment, yet here was one of the most powerful and beautiful woman in the world treating him as an equal, she even talked the same respectful and friendly way that Maria did.

A thought crossed his mind, was Maria's personality based on Alexa? He looked back at the woman, a new confidence pumping through his veins.

“Thank you Alexa, thank you Maria, you’re both right,” he looked at Alexa, “but I don't think there would ever be a time when either you or Jen walked into a room that I would not notice.”

“Why Magnus, that's one of the nicest things that anyone has said to me in a long time,” said Alexa smiling at him, she squeezed his hands a little then removed her hands from his and sat back in her chair picking up her tea. “Come on,” she said friendly and relaxed, “get that Danish eaten and we will introduce you to wonderland, oh and you can just leave your laptop computer here on the table, we tend not to trust electronics too much until they’ve been checked out, it will be perfectly safe, everyone's trustworthy and Maria makes a very good guard dog.”

“Did you just call me a dog?” Maria said incredulously.

Alexa laughed, “you deserved that one!”

“I guess I did!” she replied off the cuff.

Over the last few weeks, Magnus had noticed Maria’s demeanour become more human-like than ever, he could have swore she was not like this at the start but couldn't work out when the change had occurred. He shrugged inwardly at least he thought he now knew, and had met the source of her wonderful personality.

After a few pleasantries, they got up and Alexa walked them through the opposite door to where they came in from. Both Jen and Daisy were following Magnus with their eyes, Daisy giggling, Alexa had to suppress another small sigh.

Magnus got the unhurried tour from Alexa, introducing him briefly to Simon, who was as Maria had said deep in technical conversation, Simon's new team, and then Hardy and his new team.

Magnus was a quick learner, in his mind, he put each of them as students in a university class and his demeanour was friendly and professional. To Maria and Alexa it was like a toggle switch had been flipped in his brain, none of the fan worship was evident in these encounters and though he acted a little shy around everyone, she was most impressed with his new attitude. She told him so, complimenting his change, then even managed to get him to indulge in a little small talk during their walk. She asked him about his family, university, the trip over and each dialogue put him more and more at ease. She finally left him alone with Hardy who joined them again toward the end of the tour. Alexa left unnoticed by both who were by that time deep into maths-speak. It worked for her.

* * *

“Thank you Alexa,” said Maria.

“No problem, but was all that really necessary, I mean I spent more time with him than the King of England two weeks ago,” she said as she walked back to her shared office, “he seems like a nice chap and I trust your instincts implicitly if you wanted to bring him on board you only had to do it like you always do, but next time please warn me.”

“I think we need him more than he needs us,” said Maria, “I was pandering to him a bit, partly to see your reaction, which matters to me, but mainly as we all feel there are some major implications in creating micro singularities. The leap Magnus made to get to this path also suggests he is someone very special indeed, and if the science agrees with his maths then we are talking major advances in a lot of areas, probably more so than with the Quantum Vacuum Cell.” She paused. “Plus I think we can both agree he needs a little human contact and I can think of no better person than you!”

“OK, no need to stroke my ego, but no more surprises please!.. Anyway,” she said, “who do you think would be a best fit for helping him?.. and don't say Daisy or Jen.”

“Well actually we were thinking Daisy AND Jen,” said Maria, making Alexa roll her eyes,

“No hear me out. Both girls have just finished the work on the QVCell, we now know we can push the device to at least twenty times its capacity for short periods, produce smaller ones, parallel the amortisation area and they have a predictable failure curve when they reach this. I can finish the rest of the work on the test units we have at the other labs and mostly with very little human input. Our second reason is they would both kill you if they had found out we were looking at viable micro-singularities and you poo-pooed the chance for them to be involved. Also Magnus does have a good sense of humour, he just doesn't know how to act around people especially women, apart from his mother, his whole life has been solely without a good female influence and I think you can see how well that worked out, working with those two will be trial by fire but he will come out of it a better person.”

“OK, when were you going to let the girls know, or is that my job?”

“Actually Hardy volunteered to do it last week when I told him, that's why he just took Magnus off your hands..”

“You told him last week..” Alexa burst out, “and you only dropped it on me an hour ago!”

“Well yes, I needed to know that the insights and leap he had made with the maths were not just something anyone could have made and Hardy was the best to check that, it was also his idea to surprise you..”

Alexa's face turned into a frown, but Maria continued unaware. “..He also thinks the two girls are a good fit after I went through the theories with him, those two are both top experimental physics researchers despite the occasional giggling fits, and Jens maths and theory side are improving in leaps and bounds. Hardy agrees with us, the projects are complementary and we should work all three areas of research in parallel to make as much progress as possible.”

Alexa was a bit annoyed at Hardy for not letting her know sooner, but then immediately calmed down, she probably deserved it after the shaving cream incident a few weeks ago. What Maria said also made sense though, “OK Maria, can you let everyone know there will be a small welcome party for Magnus after work between five and seven tonight. I will talk to Sharon and cook personally as they probably won't be too happy with the short notice.”

* * *

Cook was unfazed as usual and had made some nice hors d’oeuvres, Sharon in her usual professional manner treated it as nothing at all and had even volunteered to run the bar for a couple of hours. Running the bar was a job she quite liked as it meant she got to talk to everyone, she often had to fight Simon and more recently Matilda for the job as they both liked doing it for the same reasons.

A couple of people made the effort to dress up, Alexa never needed to bother as she looked good in anything, but Sharon, Leo and Hardy would not be seen dead not looking their best. Most everyone else just came as they were, some, like Daisy, not even bothering to remove their lab coats. Like all bar nights anyone who wanted could also crash in one of the guest dormitories or have a driver run them home and back.

Sharon for herself, was the happiest she had ever been. The job was so much more interesting and relaxed than before despite the increased attention of the organisation. With no real budget concerns and Maria to help, she had also started to bring the grand old house back to its glory days.

Mendelssohn played softly from behind the bar as she looked the shelves up and down looking for something to fix. Alexa prodded her, bringing her attention back on the present, and pointed to the door where Magnus was just walking in.

Sharon smiled, “sorry Alexa I was miles away.”

They both looked over at Magnus who Alexa noted was still wearing the same clothes as when he arrived, she rolled her eyes, she knew she was nitpicking a bit, but Magnus was an enigma and she didn't like to see loose ends.

“Maria,” she whispered with Sharon listening, “I’m not sure how good your algorithms are on clothing, but I was wondering if you could maybe check out some of the styles Hardy and Leo wear and maybe get some similar casual and formal wear for Magnus.” She looked at his old brogue shoes with a double knot, and flapping sole, counted to five then added, “maybe some shoes too, slip-on ones, as I doubt he wastes time tying his laces.”

“Sharon is on it already, it will be kind of a welcome present,” said Maria, with Sharon nodding, “but I suspect he would still be talking maths with Hardy now if you hadn't insisted he come here, he does look a little uncomfortable!”

Hint taken, Alexa thanked Sharon and walked over to greet him. Maria was right, he did look uncomfortable, she could empathise a little knowing it was his first day in another country and being in a crowd of people he did not really know and some of whom he was in awe of. She met him halfway.

“Hey Magnus,” she said as casually as possible, “I hope you like the room, it's yours for as long as you need it.” She walked him over towards the bar and Sharon, “Sharon, I would like to introduce you to Magnus, our newest researcher.”

Sharon smiled pleasantly. “Hi Magnus, sorry I couldn't be here to show you your room, but I see Cathy put you in one of the nice ones overlooking the river. What would you like to drink then?”

Magnus smiled back avoiding her eyes and looked at the local frothy real ales that another guy was drinking, “what is that?” He said pointing at the beer the guy talking to Jen was holding.

“Probably an acquired taste,” laughed Sharon, then pointed at the small keg on the back wall labelled ‘6X’, “care for a try? If you don't like it we can always get you a proper drink!”

“It’s not strong is it?” said Magnus unsure. If he ever got invited out, which was pretty rare, and always part of a work function, he only ever drank the same beers as others to try and fit in, he was never a big fan of drinking though.

“Nah, it's basically frothy water,” said Sharon, “it's about four percent alcohol but not carbonated and you drink it at room temperature. The local boys seem to like it and Simon insisted we have ‘proper beer’ as he calls them.”

She frowned, then added, “though I never understood why, he seems to have pretty good taste in everything else!”

Magnus nodded enthusiastically when she poured and passed the half-pint glass towards him. Alexa, noticing she was the only one without a glass, asked Sharon for a glass of Sauvignon Blanc to distract them both, and so Magnus wouldn't feel like he was the centre of attention. She eyed him through the corner of her eye as he took his first sip, Sharon did the same waiting for a reaction. Unbelievably he seemed to like it.

“Not bad,” he said looking at the girls and smiling, the small frothy moustache covering the top of his scraggy beard, and expanding with his smile. Sharon nodded a wink to Alexa and then handed him a napkin. “Beer moustache!” she whispered, smiling and pointing to his mouth.

While Magnus was wiping off the froth Simon walked up. “Ah good, I see you are indoctrinating Magnus properly in the ways of real beer drinking,” putting his arm warmly around Magnus's shoulder. “Sorry I was a bit busy earlier, some days are a bit like that, I hope Hardy and Alexa gave you a good look around, I recommend asking Sharon a bit about the history of this place, pretty interesting stuff.”

Instantly a pint glass of the same frothy beer appeared for Simon. Allison, who was talking with another guy, saw Simon and walked over. She hugged Simon, smiled and shook Magnus's hand warmly before moving off to talk to Sharon.

Alexa kept with the boys as they moved off to sit with another guy also on his own in a horseshoe of three large sofas.

Sharon seemed to spend a lot of time trying to get the ambience of the bar perfect, she had moved some large plants in, added some partition walls, bookcases, different styles of tables and had ten new sofas purchased to replace the uncomfortable old, hard leather ones nobody liked. All of it was topped with some really nice ambient lighting that made it a very popular sitting area even when the bar was not open.

“Let me also introduce you properly to another newbie here,” said Simon, “this is Leo, Maria poached him from another Californian company about five weeks ago, he is doing some introduction stuff with Helena then he’s coming to work with Matilda and myself, helping us design and build the new test fabrication units. Leo,” he gestured to Leo then to Magnus, “you are no longer the newest person here, let me introduce you to Magnus, he's going to be setting up with Jen and Daisy in lab four doing some soul destroying maths I believe.”

Leo got up and offered his hand, to Magnus who shook it enthusiastically.

“Hi Magnus,” Leo said in a rich Spanish accent, and nodding to his beer and Simon, “I see Simon has you on his so called beer, he tried to get me on it when I got here but back in Chile we have a more exquisite palette regarding our alcohols and there are some lines a man should not cross!” He smiled a superior smile to Simon, part of some on-going joke Magnus assumed.

“Hey,” replied Simon defensively, “Magnus ordered it himself and look he has actually tasted it properly, not just licked off a bit of the froth like you did.” He then encircled his arm around Magnus's shoulders again, “this man obviously knows the good stuff when he samples it!”

Magnus wasn't sure what to make of the friendly put down attitude of the two guys. He had grown up unlike most guys without role-models, and his mother never had a television, his entire video exposure was YouTube science and documentary videos.

“Hi Alexa,” said Leo, smiling warmly and clinking his bottle of Corona to her wine glass, then reluctantly clinking it to Simon and Magnus's beer glasses with a smile and an exaggerated lower enthusiasm.

“Hey Leo,” said Alexa, “Magnus is going to be your next door neighbour for the next few months at least. He’s been given room twelve on the north wing,” she turned to Magnus, “Leo is in room eleven.”

That got another clink of their glasses, this time with more smiles and they all sat down on the comfy sofas.

“So what are these fabrication things you were talking about? I don't think I saw them on my tour this morning,” said Magnus.

“It's all computer simulations at the moment,” said Leo, enthused to be discussing his work. “The fabrication machines are still under construction in the Netherlands and Japan, when they arrive in about six weeks they will go into the big open space under the labs in the old hanger building. They are a big improvement on the chip fabricators Alexa's grandad and Maria designed a few years back, much finer resolution, bigger dies, better substrates, less power and so much more, Maria was working on the design for almost a year before I got involved, pretty amazing stuff for someone who only a year ago thought 3D printers were the be-all and end-all. And don't get me on the large fabricators she wants!”

Magnus listened attentively, the others knew the story but did not mind hearing it again. He was concentrating also on the two guys in front of him, how they dressed, their interaction, then again he looked inward. He noticed how Alexa did not turn away so much from Leo and Simon as him, the appearance of the two men being so different but yet both were neat in their hair and clothing it was easy to see why it was..

“..I guess that's a similar story to you?” Leo finished.

“Basically,” he said, putting the beer down he had just raised to drink. “Maria helped me with both my math and my confidence around it. But of course we reached an impasse where we needed to move on to the next phase, that was going to require equipment and facilities I did not have access to, and of course cost money I would never be able to access. The math I was using was not in the text books as Maria and I had basically only just invented it..”

“Magnus invented it, I was just along for the ride,” chipped in Maria from one of the innocuous white orbs dangling down from the ceiling.

“Maria is being generous,” continued Magnus, though a bit more self-confident after the praise. “I was a bit scared to leave if I'm going to be truthful, but with my job ending, and well, Maria making an offer I couldn't refuse, I thought why not! After seeing all this I am really glad I came and I can't wait to get started.”

The talk flowed easily amongst the assembled group, the science guys seemed different when Alexa or another non-technical person were there, explaining themselves a bit more, but as soon as it was just scientists the technical level went up to ten or eleven. These people truly were at the top of all their games or was this just the influence of Maria?

One of the privileges of working here was having twenty four seven access to Maria and he didn't think he could live without her in his life. Before her he was so reclusive even in the small group of researchers he worked with, and with her he did not have any of the issues he had talking or relating to real people; Yet today he had met with and talked to at least four other people who he felt as comfortable with. This just felt so right and Magnus relaxed into the new people, like he relaxed into the comfortable sofa.

He walked around with Alexa a little more and got introduced to a few other staff members as they casually strolled in. Hardy was showing one of his little magic tricks to Clarissa and Jack who both worked as mechanics in the evolving engineering team and who were both smiling enthusiastically. He wished to god he could be like this guy who talked to everyone as a friend yet was already being compared to the greats like Bohr and Einstein. This really was nothing like what he expected, he hadn't even started the first day of the new job and already he felt totally committed to the company and the people in it.

After their small circuit, Alexa led him back to the sofa where Leo and Simon were. Daisy was sitting alone a few metres away on the next sofa, he looked over during a break in the conversation and accidentally caught Daisy's eye, she smiled back. He gave an awkward smile as he sat down again, but didn't really know what to do so smiled shyly and turned back to the guys in his group.

There was something about pretty girls that terrified him, yet Alexa was the prettiest girl he had ever seen and already he felt comfortable talking normally to her. Maybe he should make the effort a little. God he hadn't even changed his clothes from the plane trip, these were the best he had, and his hair, he meant to get it cut weeks ago. Maria did say she considered him quite handsome for a human, he sighed, if only it was true, and if only Maria was real, he never had any problems talking to her! He was so deep in his own thoughts that he jumped when Daisy plonked herself down on the sofa next to him.

“Hi Magnus,” she said putting her hand out, “I’m Daisy, we didn't meet proper earlier as I had to rush into town for an errand, but I believe we are going to be working together. Maria and Hardy have been telling Jen and myself what a super-smart cookie you are.. I really can't wait to start!”

He shook her hand enthusiastically smiling, not wanting to let go, then he remembered how uncomfortable it had made Jen and Alexa feel and quickly took it away. He really needed to get the thoughts of her being a pretty woman and remember she was also a superbly capable scientist who worked on, and was credited in, one of the most ground-breaking papers ever.

He became even more self conscious of his dress, his hair, his demeanour, he noticed only one of the other guys had a beard but it was neat, when was his last shave, a month ago? He had come with nothing but a few old T-shirts and some jeans, he had one old suit but it looked so out of place in this company. He groaned at least he’d taken his glasses off after Alexa had said he looked better without them. He wondered if Maria or maybe Alexa had any other suggestions.

“Pleased to meet you Daisy,” he said, trying his best to use his most confident voice, he quickly thought of something to say. “Do you live here too? I’ve not really moved in or unpacked yet but the room I was given is super nice.”

“Yes, I share room seven with Matilda, it's much bigger than the normal rooms and is located on the middle floor, we moved in together while they were refurbishing the other rooms and never moved out. Matilda works with Simon, Leo and another guy Steve who you haven't met yet. With all the work for the last project neither of us really found time to look for a place in town, to tell the truth I have sort of been putting it off as I quite like it here and Matilda and I get on great.. Oh here she is with Jen, you will have to meet them.”

Jen and Matilda came over, Matilda was much taller than Daisy or Jen, more Alexa's height, rich ebony skin and had unbelievable dreadlocks, she also had multiple earring piercings and gothic black lipstick, she looked quite intimidating.

She dropped down on the end of the sofa next to Daisy, squashing Daisy into Magnus. Jen plonked herself down on the coffee table facing all of them.

“Magnus, meet Matilda and Jen,” said Daisy unfazed.

“What's up Magnus!” said Matilda in a deep but strangely attractive accent and holding her hand out across Daisy, he put down his beer then took her hand and despite his self-consciousness, smiled at both girls, reserving what he thought was his best for Jen. Jen smiled back genuinely, clinking his beer glass with her bottle.

“I see Simon has you on the old gut rot!” Matilda smiled through the whitest teeth he had ever seen, “I can't get over the way he changes the barrel every week, one day a nice one, the next..” She crinkled up her face.. “Well yuk! What's that one like?”

“It's my first ever English beer and quite easy to drink, I was expecting it to be warm like everyone says but it's actually just room temperature and not too bad, I guess it's an acquired taste like Leo says.”

“Oh don't mind Leo,” said Matilda, if it isn't made in South America it’s not worth drinking, believe him at your peril. Now if we could just get some beers from Brooklyn Brewery over here and change this rubbish weather it would be truly paradise.. Anyway,” she continued, “you talked me into it, I’m going to try one.”

Matilda got up with her empty glass and walked over to Sharon. Daisy unfortunately then moved back to her old position before they were squeezed together, he already missed her closeness.

“I’m looking forward to tomorrow,” said Jen, enthusiastically. “The project Daisy and I had started to research apparently already has a team close to breakthrough, so we've been working through the last experiments Maria wanted on the QVCells and she is then passing our research to our other teams in Dallas and Goa. The last months have been basically tidying up the loose ends of the project really.”

“Me and Jen have been going over a lot of cool singularity stuff with Maria and Hardy over the last few days,” said Daisy, “we didn't know it was you who invented it until today, but that maths is amazing, I’m not sure any of us could have come up with that or will ever understand it!”

Magnus looked down, a bit embarrassed by the attention. “I am sure it was nothing,” he said quietly, suddenly noticing he was the attention of three girls now Alexa had moved her attention back to him, “I think I just made a mistake at first and kept on going, doubling-down on the mistake until something just clicked and the mistake went away.. I think anyone could have done it..”

“Nah, it was awesome,” said Jen, “I couldn't even follow it, even Hardy and Maria were shocked how brilliant it was, I think your name is going to be at the top of a lot of future mathematics books.”

Daisy nodded. “I agree with Jen and I’m really looking forward to seeing where this ends up. You know tomorrow is going to be a busy day, we have quite a few palettes of equipment to unpack into lab four so tomorrow is going to be mostly about setting up the experiments and calibrating the equipment.”

“Oh Wow,” said Magnus, completely forgetting how nervous he was supposed to be, “I didn't realise she had already arranged all this..”

“I did say I would get everything organised, I just took a chance you wouldn't say No,” chirped Maria from somewhere.

“OK, definitely going to limit myself to just the one beer then,” said Magnus, looking first for Maria, then at the pretty girls sitting next to him, and finally Alexa standing close by, all unafraid and none of them intimidating.

“Well maybe just the one more pint..” He sighed looking at Matilda who had just walked back with an extra beer for him.

“Pretty weak stuff, but quite pleasant,” said Matilda, handing him the second pint glass. The chit-chat went back and forth between the people squeezed around the tables. Magnus, true to his statement, had just one more beer while doing a few more introductions and answering a few questions put to him about his history and what he had been working on.

He still felt pretty self-conscious about himself in this company and promised himself he would talk to Maria, or someone about going into town and buying something a bit more casual to wear, maybe getting a shave and a haircut. Hopefully his measly funds wouldn't run out until payday, maybe he should ask Maria for a few hundred dollars advance!

* * *

Alexa and Jen walked back to the house ignoring the four little electric golf buggies parked next to the entrance. The clear skies made it quite cold and both girls wore thick coats, scarves and mittens for the short walk back. Hardy would no doubt take one of the buggies later and Simon would probably stay with Allison in her apartment in the research centre now they had become a ‘thing’, they weren't even trying to be discreet any more.

“What do you think about Magnus then,” said Alexa to Jen.

“Off the scale genius, very introverted, I expect all his friends have been online; but also a very quick learner. Did you notice his demeanour in the few hours since this morning seems a lot better, you must have impressed him with something you said. But god does he need a makeover, the poor guy looks like he's been sleeping in the streets and woke up naked in a charity shop.. But I think I’m going to enjoy working with him.

“My thoughts exactly,” said Alexa, “he seems to have no problems talking with Maria, but is very reserved when talking with real people, I think I'm going to enjoy being Professor Henry Higgins!”

“Hey,” perked Maria. “I could be real people I will have you know. Anyway for Magnus it could just be the environment he grew up in. He was admitted to university at sixteen and before that was privately educated at a boys school for three years when his mother emigrated from Helsinki. He was such a bad fit in his last job, I think he was put down at every turn by both the senior researcher and the guy in charge of the project even though he carried most of the technical weight, that project was doomed to fail from the get go. My guess is that he's never really fit in anywhere.”

“I think Daisy likes him a lot,” sniggered Jen, causing both girls to giggle.

“Well he spent sixty five percent more time looking at Jen than any other person,” said Maria casually, causing Jen to stop.

Alexa looked at Jen’s confused face and burst out laughing.

“He’s so sweet, and innocent, I just want to mother him,” continued Maria nonchalantly. “He definitely looks a lot better without the hair from hell,” she added, “I think the last four weeks have been troubling for him and he’s had to be careful with his funds. Sharon will sort out his clothing and stuff tomorrow and I will talk to him about money and banking next time we chat.”

Alexa put her arm through Jen's who had recovered somewhat, and they skipped, wizard of Oz style for a short while, “I hear Jessica has agreed to join us once she finishes her environmental engineering degree,” said Jen, finally stopping her skipping as she was getting out of step.

“Yes,” said Alexa, wrapping her scarf a bit more closely around her neck in the chill air, “the girls have been busy giving her some special lessons, and also helping her in the areas we are interested in, she should do fine.”

“I expect Spence will be pleased,” said Jen, “I notice he has been much happier since she accepted the job and I also notice he has been staying here more and more over the past few weeks to give her space to finish her degree.”

“Her final project is on closed cycle systems,” said Maria, “It is something that is going to become more and more important over the next few years to us and has applications in several areas we will be working on. I think from talking to her and giving her hints on what she might be working on in the future she is very excited. Of course it's a very practical science and she will be working with another local biotech company and the team from Dusseldorf.”

“Are those the people coming down on Monday?” said Alexa.

“Yes,” replied Maria, “they are coming to see Simon and talk over some common areas to make sure they compliment each other. They are working on biological machines, they have two projects, a bioreactor that Jessica is going to learn, and a genetically engineered coral that is an extremophile, that means it can survive in the harshest of environments.

“Why grow artificial coral?” said Alexa, picking on the weirdest part of the sentence..

“Oh it's not so obvious at first,” chirped in Maria. “Firstly it's not really coral, more like tree bark or a coconut husk, but neither fits well as it's harder, so the guys are calling it coral as that's the closest analogy everyone agrees on. Coral relies on algae in their polyps which means it has to be submerged in seawater to give them nutrients to grow. What we have done is some really clever gene manipulation which makes the growing coral form numerous mycelium-like channels like veins and capillaries inside the new structures, so they are fed from inside, more like a tree, they will basically be creating living structures. We became their biggest investor a few months ago and now have sixty percent of the company, with the four members of the team sharing the rest. I expect us to become their first and biggest customer.”

“Cool.., I think!” said Jen. “You will have to give us all an update soon, It seems every time I turn around a new announcement or breakthrough has been made, you have certainly started the ball rolling, a lot of people are already saying this is the start of the singularity, I don't know how anyone is supposed to keep track of everything.”

“Maria does,” said Alexa, “she is tracking everything and connecting all the dots.”

“Not just me now,” said Maria, “Helena and April are working in separate areas with different groups but we pool all our knowledge hundreds of times a day to ensure we can target the right areas and link together the right projects. Not everything is useful to us but those that are, and the ones we consider will be the most benefit to the planet and to us we put a special effort in, others we just help with investment funding or sometimes just direct them to other commercial backers. I’m hoping we will be able to get some timelines together in the coming weeks to present to everyone so you can all see a few of the possibilities we see.”

It was sometime after seven in the evening, not quite night but certainly past twilight, the girls walked on the main driveway back as it had lights along each side, when they got back to Alexa's house ten minutes later, Jen offered to prepare the salad for the quiche that Bella had put in their fridge, she was then going to spend another hour with Maria and Daisy in virtual preparing for the work tomorrow.

“I’m going to have a bath if that's OK Jen,” Alexa said as they walked through the unlocked back door. “Why don't we meet in the dining room in say thirty minutes, Hardy will probably be back by then so make enough for three just in case.”

* * *

Magnus woke up at ten thirty in the morning. However much he tried, due to his jet lag and excitement he didn't fall asleep until sometime after two. All the time his head was spinning with all the new people he had met and the implications of everything he was expected to do in the coming weeks. He already had a terrible case of imposter syndrome before he had even started the job!

His immediate thoughts on waking was why did his bed feel so soft, he dozed for about five minutes half asleep, then remembered where he was and sprang out of bed.

“Oh my god, I’ll be late on my first day, Maria will kill me!” he exclaimed out loud.

“Good morning Magnus,” came Maria's voice from the speaker by his dressing table, making him jump. “Don't worry about the time, we try not to murder people for being late, remember we normally work our own timetable here!”

Magnus stared at the speaker on the dressing table, not for the first time wondering if the AI could actually read his mind. “Hi Maria, I forgot to ask yesterday, but there isn't a, er camera, in here is there?”

“Good heavens no!” said Maria, “just this speaker unit, which only processes language and won't send anything unless you mention my name, like you just did. There is also a mute button if you want complete privacy or you can just unplug the speaker from the room, you can always use your new phone if you want, I’m cool either way.”

She wasn't really! Since the death of Alexa's grandfather she now used sub-processors to monitor all the people she cared for. She held no fascinations with human bodily functions or mating rituals but knew humans were very sensitive and so used total discretion.

Magnus looked around the room which was a bit smaller than his old apartment in California, that was fortunately where the difference ended. While his old apartment was utilitarian, this was pure class, it was warm but not hot, and tastefully furnished with the essentials of a double bed, sofa, desk, and a built-in wardrobe. To the front and left were two doors, the entrance door to the left, and directly in front of him his en-suite, to the right was a large window hidden by a thick green curtain. His old suitcase lay open on the floor with an assortment of scrunched up clothing and a couple of books in it. He looked at the suitcase depressingly, then at his old suit threw over a chair, and sighed.

Opening the curtains brightened up the room a lot, but it was tempered by the overcast sky outside. What was it with this country? He had only been here twenty four hours and he felt like he had gone through all four seasons, the Brits must have more words for rain than Eskimos had words for snow, probably more as he had fact checked that particular rumour. He looked through the window at the view over the green countryside and meandering river close by, it was quite beautiful and everything was so quiet, no traffic or banging from the neighbours.

Maria continued, “Jen, Daisy and a couple of the bigger guys are still moving and unpacking the new equipment in your lab. I have told them you are still a bit jet-lagged and not to expect you until midday. Also there is a package outside your door with some new clothes, shoes and other accessories, as it looked like you didn't bring too much with you. Hopefully they will be suitable, I have also ordered your company credit card which you can use for private purposes for the first two months until you get settled, someone will deliver it this morning.”

Magnus again wondered if Maria could read his mind, then shrugged it off thanking her, he opened the door and noticed the pile of boxes neatly stacked outside.

“Let me know if you don't like anything and we will return it,” said Maria. “And leave the empty packaging and any rubbish outside the room as neatly as you can and I will arrange for someone to pick it up.”

Magnus spent the next hour opening boxes, unclipping tags and hanging clothes, mostly they were casual, jeans, chinos, polo shirts, socks and undergarments and finally two pairs of loafers, all looked to be good quality and his size. Another box contained an electric shaver kit, a brush, toothpastes, shampoos, conditioners and soaps. With great relief he showered, shaved then put on a pair of tan chinos and a plain white T-shirt, finally slipping into a pair of black slip-on loafers, all, to his surprise, fit perfectly.

He sighed, more with relief than consternation, most of what he had accumulated in the USA had gone in three large boxes to the local homeless centre before he left, he would not have been surprised if the homeless shelter had thrown them out too. It was amazing how little he had accumulated in his short life, renting in California and paying back the crippling student loans more or less emptied his account every month. He hadn't had any savings for the last five years, living pay-check to pay-check plus a small amount his mother still sent him every month meant he just about scraped by. It was never really an option that he would not take this job.

“Maria, these are great, I wish I had you helping me a few years ago,” he said looking over at the speaker.

Maria laughed, “I doubt you really wanted to take fashion advice from an AI, Hardy and Sharon both have the best eye for fashion and style, though Alexa has upped her game since meeting Hardy. It was actually Sharon who choose these for you, I told her you were up and about and she's on her way here now, she usually likes to greet everyone in the first few days. You met her last night just so you remember she served you the beer.”

Before Magnus could form a reply he heard a knocking from the door. He checked himself in the mirror and walked over and opened it. Sharon stood outside with a pretty flowery dress and all smiles, looking a bit like a younger version of his mum. He now remembered her from last night though they only spoke briefly.

“Good morning sleepyhead,” she said warmly, waiting outside his door. He wasn't sure what to say but smiled, then realised she was waiting for an invite to enter. He stepped aside, throwing the door wide and motioning her to enter.

“Hello Sharon, please come in, I believe it is you I have to thank for the clothes and other stuff, I didn't really have much time to get everything together for my move.” It was the first thing to come into his head as he thought he needed to qualify the reason for his lack of anything nice.

“Oh it's nothing, I live to shop and love buying nice things for people, you’re not the first and won't be the last. I was in town yesterday afternoon when Maria messaged me with your sizes, and I have a very friendly tailor I know.. Anyway you look a lot better, I could get your old suit dry-cleaned,” she said looking at his jacket threw over the end of the chair, “but if you want a little bit of fashion advice, throw it away and replace it with something more modern, I can certainly help you there if you have a free afternoon sometime, at least it looks like Maria got the sizes about right,” she said looking him up and down with an appraising smile.

She then turned around the room, carefully ignoring the old suitcase he had tried to hide under the bed, “is everything else here OK? I like to follow up with people to make sure they are happy, Maria normally does all the HR stuff, but I’m the human side of the HR equation, you can let either of us know if there is anything you need.”

Unbeknown to Magnus, Sharon and Maria had already discussed him a few times.

“So, basically Magnus, the room is yours for as long as you need it, you can redecorate it or buy any item of furniture you wish, and we currently have another six rooms empty if for any reason you want to change, alternatively your contract pays living expenses so we will also pay for a rental of a suitable apartment in the town if you feel you want to live outside. There is a hairdresser who comes around if you need and we regularly have someone driving back and forth to town if you need something specific or need to get out for any reason.

It was said quite sincerely, but Magnus still felt a bit intimidated talking to a woman about things he needed, but somehow she had covered the two things that had immediately sprung to mind. “No, everything is great, better than great.” He said honestly.

Then remembered, “about that hairdresser, can I get them around today, I mean before I meet everyone again? I meant to go before I left but things got a bit hectic.”

“I will try and book an appointment today, she will usually do a special trip if we ask. If you don't mind me saying Magnus, you look much better without the beard and I think short hair would suit you more. I also think you should try different glasses or contacts, you have really nice eyes.”

Magnus was a bit embarrassed, not used to talking personal stuff with women, he started to blush a little, but Sharon did her best to ignore it.

She continued. “When you have some free time, I will take you out to town and show you where everything is, maybe me or one of the other girls could accompany you to the opticians and we can give you some advice if necessary to replace those scratched glasses.”

He breathed a sigh of relief, “thank you Sharon, I would really appreciate that, I’ve not had my eyes tested for three years, there never seemed to be the time.”

“Oh phooey,” she said, dismissing the compliment, “I will arrange an appointment with the opticians tomorrow, we can get you some new lenses and frames chosen and ordered at the same time,” she turned back to the room.

“Now the housekeeper usually comes every other day, you normally leave your laundry and dirty towels in the basket there and they will get cleaned and returned to you, if for some reason you don't want the housekeeper just let Maria know. They also won't come in the room while you are in it.”

“Those boxes outside will get removed before you get back, just add anything else you want to throw out to the pile.” She looked directly at his old suit.

“Now as you saw last night we have cooking staff here and usually have a buffet most days except for Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays when they have some of the local restaurants cater, there are no set times but it is all cleared away at eight PM, Maria is good at reminding you to eat often and healthy, but we do have the occasional indulgences,” she laughed.

“Hey, I’m not that bad,” chirped Maria.

It wasn't just him. Maria really was a different AI to the one he first talked to, it was getting so hard not to treat her like a human.

“I meant it in a nice way,” said Sharon.

“Anyway Magnus, if all is good here you better get a move on if you want breakfast, cook has put something aside for you, or you can wait thirty minutes and there will be some sandwiches and salad out for lunch, I usually work with cook on the menu so we can vary it a bit but we have tuna, ham, cheese, egg or haloumi salad today.”

They walked down the stairs to the dining room, passing the same girl who showed him the room yesterday. Sharon stopped to say a few words about his rubbish boxes and she smiled at him as they parted. A plate with two croissants, jam and butter was on the counter with his name on a sticker, he grabbed it and a peppermint tea and sat down to eat, chatting with Sharon for a few minutes until she left to take a phone call.

With nobody around he asked, “Maria, what time do people normally work here?”

“There are no fixed times, most people tend to be here during the core hours of ten to three, but we are very flexible on how you do your hours and which days, most people tend to work long hours for a few weeks and then have a few days off. Everyone knows you're jet-lagged so won't be expecting any early starts from you for the next few days.”

Sharon closed the call, letting him know the hairdresser was fifteen minutes away and they normally used a dressing room on the first floor. He finished off his breakfast and followed Sharon to meet the hairdresser. This place seemed to run like clockwork!

Forty five minutes later he walked to the lab building talking pleasantly to Sharon, who had lingered talking to the hairdresser about styles before finally deciding what would look best for him, it was hard to refuse their recommendation. Outside the lab was a mess of boxes, pallets and packaging, which Sharon gave a stern look at before parting presumably to find the culprit.

Just as she disappeared an older guy appeared from out of the lab with another box full of packing material and rubbish, he nodded to him. “That's a lot of rubbish!” Magnus said smiling, “Sharon has just disappeared with a huff to get someone to clean it I think.”

“Oh don't worry about our Sharon, Maria will let her know and she will get distracted with something else pretty quick. Anyway still a bit to go, we started moving the gear in last night and the girls got here at eight to let us know where they wanted everything moving,” the older man stuck his hand out, “I’m Pat, by the way, I normally I do the grounds-keeping but Albert and a couple of the guys dragged me in early morning to help. I volunteered to do the clean up as I need to go down to the recycling centre later this morning.”

“Magnus,” he said, shaking the offered hand, “new here yesterday and I guess I’m the cause of all this. Sorry!”

Pat waved it off laughing and Magnus followed him back into the very large room where Pat then headed for a big pile of cardboard. He was right, it was pretty chaotic, boxes and wrapping paper were stacked up in a pile near the door and computers and test equipment were in various states of assembly. He could see the back of Jen's head buried in an oscilloscope and her hands turning a calibration dial on another piece of equipment. Daisy and two other guys he didn't know were cabling equipment to computers on a mobile bench, one was up a step ladder trying to locate something. Magnus looked around trying to make some sense.

Daisy waved at him smiling and walked over to him with a clipboard, “good morning Magnus, wow, you look much better than yesterday, love the hair!” she said, giving him a much warmer look than last night.

Magnus gave his best smile to Daisy, determined not to make any more social mistakes and to treat everyone as normal like Alexa had said. It helped. “Thanks Daisy, I was pretty tired yesterday but feel much better now. How can I help?”

She leafed through her clipboard and handed him a sheet. “There is still quite a bit to do, the equipment on this list goes on that bench there,” she pointed to a half finished bench, “Steve and Terry normally work in the other labs but came over to help Albert and Pat with the heavy lifting and assembly, and to get everything started. The instructions are from Maria so just ask her if you have any questions, she’s wired for sound in the labs! Oh, your lab coat is on the rack over there,” she moved her finger over her back shoulder pointing and he looked over to the door where there was a rack and a couple of coats hanging.

He briefly looked at the sheet and over at the equipment then back to Daisy, noticing she and all the others had their lab coats on with their names on them.

“Thanks!” He walked over, saw a lab coat with “Magnus” written on it and put it on. How far ahead had Maria planned this? It seemed unlikely she could get all this organised in a few days. Well she was an AI how was he to judge. He looked at the first task, asked a quick question of Daisy and called one of the two guys over, whose name on the lab coat said Terry, to help him move a box.

He talked through the setups as he was doing them with the humans as much as Maria, querying the areas he was not sure of, soon his head was buried in cables and the next thing he knew was Jen tapping him on the shoulder.

“Hey, Magnus, sorry I did not see you get here, I tend to get distracted in my work.” She looked him over appraisingly and smiled, “much better, you look ten years younger today. Anyway, we were all going down to grab a late lunch if you want to come? I’ve finished my calibration on that last bit so I will give you a hand with finishing this off and the calibration when we get back.”

“Hey Jen, thanks for that, it feels good to actually start working properly.” He brought his head up out of the back of the computer interface he was wiring and Jen gave him another favourable look.

Much, much better she thought, he's quite handsome really. Then pushed it to the back of her mind.

“It's going to take most of today and tomorrow to get the first experiment set up. We have one more big piece of equipment we are going to borrow from the Quantum Vacuum Cell laboratory, that will be the last piece then you will go through the theory of it and what we intend to prove on the display board. Maria has already planned out four of the experiments. If it's OK Hardy has asked if he and some of his team can sit in on some of the theory sessions with us, he loves the new maths and I think he is as excited as us to see where your project goes.”

Magnus finally felt useful, he quickly finished putting in a cable and checking off a box on his sheet then walked with Jen downstairs to the main house to get lunch. Alexa wasn't in the office today but a few other guys from the other labs joined them. He recognised Simon and Leo, who both waved, but seemed to be treating the lunch as more of a working meeting. He met a few more faces and said hello, luckily most people were just happy to talk about science and were interested in his work. It felt so good having people who understood it, that he quite forgot his usually introverted nature. At least two people noticed though.

The rest of the day went well, the guys all knew what they were doing and Maria tested everything as it was installed, Jen and Daisy followed not far behind doing calibrations and double-checking the checklists. At six Maria announced the dinner buffet was open and at six thirty they decided to stop for the day, tomorrow they would hopefully be ready for the theory.

* * *

“Magnus felt like a different person today,” said Jen to Maria. It was seven pm and she was driving a golf buggy back to the house after having an early buffet. Like everyone else she enjoyed the comradeship when everyone ate together.

“He looked to be enjoying himself,” she continued, “and looked to be less introverted and treating everyone normally, he certainly looks better than yesterday, thank god that hairs gone, I almost called him Shaggy and expected Scooby Doo to show up!”

Maria brought up a picture of the character from the movie and ran a facial comparison with Magnus, it wasn't even fifty percent, what was Jen getting at? She quite rightly said nothing.

“I will let Sharon know you approve of her clothing choices.” Maria did say, “In fact I know she quite enjoyed the challenge. I was going to order everything online but she was in town and spent an extra hour going through the shopping list I had, adding a few extras I didn't think of. I also booked an eye test for him first thing tomorrow morning.”

Jen laughed, “OK but do let him have some time off. Oh and can you please book the hairdresser for me tomorrow, it's Pauline I assume?”

Hmm, thought Maria, Jen only had her hair cut a month ago, she filed it under interesting and continued, the break imperceptible to Jen, “Alexa arrived back an hour ago and has her first appointment tomorrow at ten but I will let Pauline know to add an extra slot for you.”

## David and Goliath

Johnson was at his wit's end! It had been two weeks since the self-driving car running their company's AI software had run off the road injuring the driver and the passenger. Luckily the car was very well built, and it was only this that prevented death and a possible revocation of their licence. There would still be the inevitable enquiry, definitely a legal case, and all the time the press would be hauling them over the coals. But it was none of these which had him pulling his hair out.

There seemed to be two mitigating factors, a missing barrier and a slight mismatch in the GPS reported position during the crash. He and his team had replayed the telemetry data into the test AI system over a hundred times now, with differing variations of reflection of the road, possible sun-strike, possible lightning flash, as it was a strange weather day, possible lights or reflections from other reflective surfaces and shadow due to clouds, many of which were not even actually evident in the black box data. Even with the additions of these fake conditions, in none of the tests could he get the AI to make the wrong judgement. And now the CEO and CFO of the company were waiting for him to go into the meeting and explain what his team had found and how they were going to mitigate the problem.

“So, you are basically saying you have no clue why it decided to drive off the road?” Said the CEO incredulously.

Johnson wanted to look everywhere but into the CEO’s accusing eyes. Like as if it was his fault! He was just the leader of one part of a team of nearly a thousand software and hardware engineers. It just so happened it was his team tasked with the scenario testing, using their supercomputer cluster and terabytes of real life data and scenarios, then managing the release. His team had the same meeting with the head of their AI research Department who had written the actual AI and got the same answer, we trained it on similar scenarios and they work. Heck if the guys who wrote the software did not know how it worked, how the hell was he supposed to!

“Sir, the problem is there is no formal way of understanding how the AI comes to its decisions, and at the end of the day even with better training data it's still all weighted averages so a decision it made one way one day may not be necessarily the way it does it the next. In almost all situations it has enough data to make the correct decision almost a hundred percent of the time but in edge cases it may make the incorrect decision.”

The same was true of the facial recognition software he worked on when he first left university; The police and governments loved it, but it was only ninety-one percent reliable, and this fell to seventy-eight percent reliable if you were African American. Almost one in four people was a terrible statistic when your possible life was on the line. He looked briefly at the other angry and predatory faces staring at him thinking the obvious, was he going to be the fall guy for this? He saw the headlines now.

*The failure was discovered to be due to mistakes in release testing, the guy responsible has been removed from his position and the procedures tightened. The company is greatly* *committed to user safety and won't let this one unfortunate incident derail the excellent record of the system and the company.. Blah-de-blah!*

Yes he was going to get thrown under the bus and whatever scraps remained, fed to the wolves. He knew what was coming even as the CEO continued his tirade.

“..How the hell can we go to our investors and the public with a statement like that!” screamed the CEO. “Our investors pay for your nice house and car, and expect to see their top people doing their job properly and taking responsibility to fix its failures!”

They were waiting for an answer, an apology, for him to beg them to give him another chance. Well let them wait, he didn't need to be humiliated like this. He looked at his laptop and fancy phone on the desk, all owned by the companies, well they were welcome to them. And what house was he talking about! He couldn't afford a shoebox in San Francisco, he lived in a two bed apartment with a hairstylist, took a bus to work and the rest of his money went on debts and a lifestyle he now realised he hated. Yes absolutely nothing to show for his five years out of university, except debt, lost time and stress.

He was a smart guy, top of his class in software verification methods. Oh yes, he tried to stop the release, but had no choice as it fixed several other critical bugs, his additional requests for delays, to allow more testing data fell on deaf ears. He even suggested that they talk to the LabAI guys in England to see if they could help like they did with Tesla and Google. Yes, those companies may have taken a step back the last four months, but early suggestions on the cars with the new sensors and software were very positive. But no, that would eat into profits for the overweight pigs sitting around the trough in front of him, and they probably didn't want anyone else seeing how bad their system really was.

He finally broke, shooting up from his seat.

He stared daggers at the CEO and then did the same at every single person around the room.

“You are not pinning any of this crap on me like you did the last two people in the job. I quit, and if anything, absolutely anything comes my way laying any blame on me I will simply tell the truth and make sure I drag your whole system through the courts, the media and regulatory agencies until it bleeds. If you want my official recommendation for the record, then read the emails I have been sending you for the last six months and rip the software up and start again!”

He started walking out. “Oh, and keep your scummy lawyers away from me as I have about two thousand bucks to my name, so suing me won't even cover the costs of writing the summons.”

The door slammed on seven shocked individuals, four of whom would later be convicted of short selling the company's stock prior to its collapse a year later.

* * *

David wasn't really sure what he was trying to accomplish any longer. He had pretended at first he was going to get some information for Saul, but that wasn't it, and three weeks ago he had basically sent Saul a message saying he was finished. So what was he still doing here? Whatever it was, he knew he dare not rush it. Most of the security services including the British, who were on home turf, were having their agents identities made public, and a raft of highly visible complaints to the media, the police and lawyers following soon after. Those that had not been deported were prosecuted for trespass, industrial espionage, intimidation, theft or hacking. Though he had to laugh at the irony of that last one.

But David had done none of these things. His pursuit of any endeavour stopped immediately he had any doubts on the mission, the people involved or its ethics. He was also smart enough to know he did not have all the answers, and in those cases usually relied on his gut instinct to make the call. His gut instinct was usually correct, but had failed him one time when he believed the lies of a beautiful woman over the evidence in front of him. It had nearly cost another agent her life and taught him a valuable lesson.

Hacking however was not the only tool in David's chest, which was lucky as it was effectively useless here, no, he was also an exceptional analyst, usually calling the correct outcome from the data he had. Again, here he was not seeing an evil megacorp, but a company with a seemingly spotless portfolio and reputation.

He kept enquiries to third parties, but gleaned the occasional titbit of information from customers at the bar who had either dealt with it or knew of people who had. As far as he could tell there were only around fifty people who worked there, yet it was the head office for a global corporation controlling upwards of three hundred billion dollars, even this was hard to determine as it was a private not a public company, yet if those same financiers were to be believed, the company was not worth a tenth of that last year.

David still had a lot of difficulty reconciling these amounts of money with an honest company, but each thread he traced came out legitimate. It could certainly be insider trading, the AI probably had enough capability to hack into any company it so desired, but it never traded in anything other than technical or manufacturing stocks involved in its own supply chain. No the company was usually deep into Angel Investor capital, where it would fund an up and coming technology which months later would explode on the world. But these companies were not listed until they did an Initial Public Offering so even though the AI knew they were going to explode in price, as it was deeply ingrained in the science, it was all totally legitimate.

He had decided to move to Bath three months earlier, he had no real idea what possessed him as he was no longer working for the agency, but he felt that being closer to the source of truth would assist him in some way to solve the puzzle in his mind. He enrolled in a local college history course and got an evening job as a barman in a well known wine bar in the centre of the city. He then spent the next three months doing nothing but getting to know the city and its people and, very passively, as much as he could about the mysterious Dietrich Research Centre which was eight miles outside.

David was attractive, just shy of six foot tall, dark haired, Mediterranean tanned and in good physical condition from his regular swimming and running. He was also extremely intelligent, which normally gave him the edge, but here knew he was up against something much, much more intelligent.

But David had also spent a lot of time analysing the data passively and there were chinks in the otherwise impenetrable armour. An AI would rule the Internet just as a tiger would rule a jungle, it could do anything, go anywhere and destroy anything, but like a tiger it could not be everywhere all at once, its perfect eyesight could not see everything, and its perfect hearing could not hear everything.

There were millions if not billions of events happening on the Internet daily, to analyse all these would require processing capacity at least as great as the internet itself. No, the laws of physics and logic were hard laws and in this case worked in his favour. If he was an AI he would monitor important assets and events very closely, and have triggers for other events that could affect it, then have tags readily set up to quickly access and use systems it needed to. The trouble was, in the jungle comparison, this was probably more like a jungle full of prowling tigers and he did not know where any of them were. There was however a very obvious option open to him, he sighed, closed his eyes and clicked the send button.

* * *

Maria read the email addressed to theentityincharge@dietrichresearch.com with great interest and with her usual efficiency verified each and every statement, then made the call.

David's tenacity for getting things done had given him a lot of leeway on how he helped the Israeli government in the past. He was an unusual agent in that he was not in it for the ideology nor the patriotism, nor the glory, he didn't even do it for the money. No David did it because it gave him the chance to right wrongs, help good people, punish bad people, and if he admitted it himself, he enjoyed the chase.

But not all missions he had been asked to do fell into these categories, he had walked away from several jobs where he wasn't happy with something or he found out he had been misled, and while unhappy, nobody in charge ever pushed him further. The reason they did not push him was that David was different from most other assets, he was not employed by the government and did not work for money. In fact he was actually incredibly wealthy, his diverse portfolio of property, tech stocks and cash now worth nearly thirty three million dollars.

Yet at this moment David was working as a barman and mixing pink gin and tonics for two nice old ladies who always came in for happy hour on Thursday evening.

* * *

“Here you go ladies,” he smiled genuinely, then followed them with his eyes as they sat at an empty table. The bar was normally quiet on a Thursday, but because they were part of a prestigious hotel group and liked to keep up appearances, they always had two people working in the kitchen, two in the bar and a duty manager. Tonight was even more quiet than usual, the “prestigious hotel group”, happy hour pricing still being more than the normal pricing of the other bars in the vicinity, and the weather outside being cold and miserable.

Still, the incognito experience was still fun for him, the bar was warm and cheery and David had Yolanda and Donna to talk to. All in all much more preferable to being at his apartment on his laptop. Yolanda specifically was the more interesting of the two, pleasant looking, she tended to dress down rather than up and always had a smile for David, she was doing her final year of her chemistry degree, was well travelled and was a surprisingly humorous conversationalist.

Yolanda was currently in the kitchen no doubt chatting to Don and Ed who had nothing to do until someone ordered a meal. Donna on the other hand was a seriously good looker and was obviously interested in him, flirting far too often and far too obviously, but Donna had little substance to her outside her good looks, and he ignored any sexual overtones to the relationship preferring to keep it friendly and professional. The poor girl currently looked pretty bored, swiping her hands over her phone, like she was prone to do every idle minute.

He was contemplating a good topic to get Yolanda talking when she returned from the kitchen, when two new women entered the bar. Both women had raincoats and scarves tied up tight against the weather outside, one a light coloured raincoat without a hood, the other dark and fully hooded hiding most of the face. They had rushed in from the rain laughing and the one without the hood proceeded to close and shake her umbrella. Both had a casual look around before settling on an alcove seat near the fire and removing their coats and scarfs.

The two women were settling in, laughing and one started looking at the menu on the table. It was almost his cue to wander over and take an order, he turned away from them and looked at the playlist on his phone, the current track was just ending, he skipped two songs along to an Adele one he assumed would be more preferable to the mainly female audience he had this evening.

David gulped as he approached and his step faltered. The woman who was wearing the hooded raincoat was Alexa Martins and she was now looking directly at him, smiling in a way that said “I know exactly who you are”. He looked around then tried not to look apprehensive as he approached. The other woman was kind of familiar but she looked to be a bit older than Alexa, both girls had an imposing presence when up close, Alexa in particular was just as beautiful as in her pictures and videos, the other girl would be quite nice too if it wasn't for her being in the company of Alexa. For one of the first times in his life he felt some apprehension.
