“Good evening ladies,” he said in his best voice and trying to keep his stare neutrally balanced between the two women, “can I get you both a drink?”

“No need to David,” said Alexa smiling at him, “please take a seat, you’re actually off the clock as of this moment, I’m sure the loss of a few hours wages won't be too much of a burden for you. Your colleague Yolanda should be out in a second to take our orders.”

She patted the seat to the side of her. “Come on, neither Allison nor myself are going to bite you!”

The other girl smiled also, Allison, that was the name of one of the senior AI engineers, Allison Minsky, PhD's in both electronics and cognitive computer science, at least his equal intellectually, though he had researched her and was in no doubt hers was probably higher. She and Spence controlled the worldwide AI infrastructure for the company. She was sitting next to her employer, the richest and most influential woman in the country, possibly the world. For the first time in his life he felt totally out of his depth. He sat down slowly, looking over to the bar to see Yolanda talking to Donna and both of them looking at him with incredulity in their eyes. Donna put her phone down immediately after the conversation and with a slightly frightened look, walked into the back staff area.

“I guess introductions are necessary,” continued Alexa holding her hand out, “I am Alexa Martins and this here is Allison Minsky.”

David took both hands and shook them lightly, both were pleasantly warm.

“Donna is OK isn't she?” David said, looking over at the bar with concern in his voice.

“It is refreshing to see you are concerned for her,” said Alexa warmly, “but she is fine, Yolanda just received a call from the hotel manager that the hotel chain owner has just arrived in her bar and desired a little privacy while she had a conversation with one of her friends who is also an employee. Donna has just been asked to put her phone away in her locker. She does have an awful social media habit she needs to break.”

Despite everything, David smiled.

Yolanda walked over, giving David a brief look but reserving her attention mostly for the two ladies sitting in front of her, even Yolanda, who was hardly ever fazed by any situation seemed a little dumbstruck.

“Yolanda, isn't it?” said Alexa, shaking Yolanda's trembling hand, “I’m Alexa, and this is Allison. Your manager John has said a lot of nice things about you, I’m sure you won't mind if we borrow David for a short time will you?” Yolanda shook her head even though the question was rhetorical. “I’m having a Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, Allison?”

“Mulled Wine please.” Said Allison as she finished shaking Yolanda's hand.

“Oh I’ll have one of those instead,” jumped in Alexa still smiling, “David?”

“Same for me please Yolanda,” he said smiling at her and giving her a look that said ‘everything is OK’ and easing her concern a little. He too then relaxed, his mind gradually recovering from the shock. Yolanda walked away more confused than concerned, after all what owner would have you sit down for a drink with them before firing them?

“I guess you got my email then?” he said.

“Yes, it was a little bit confusing to be called an entity,” Alexa said, Allison sniggered a little at that, “just plain Alexa would have got you the same result you know.”

Allison chipped in for the first time. “You know David, it was very refreshing for one of you guys to actually knock on the front door rather than try and break through the window, Maria had a bet with me that nobody would think to do the obvious.”

Allison paused with her finger in her ear, “yes, how rude of me.”

She took a small earbud out of her left ear and put it in her handbag, she then withdrew a small box about the size of a deck of playing cards and put it in the centre of the table. Immediately the sound of Adele faded to a murmur.

“Hello again David,” came a voice from the box. “You remember our first meeting of course at Professor Holmes laboratory? Like you I have more than one hat I can put on, this is the real me, Maria is the name, pleased to meet you.”

David had been rehearsing this moment for months, how he would talk to an employee if he met one, what would he say, but all his prepared speeches went out the window as this third and most scary variable now entered the equation.

“I am very pleased to meet you Maria, as I am with you Alexa and you too Allison, you all really know how to put a fellow on the spot don't you?”

The two girls laughed heartily, leaning in to each other as close friends often do, this in its own way removed any remaining apprehension from David's mind.

“So David,” said Alexa, “why is a multi-millionaire working as a barman in lovely Bath? I understand the Spa pools are very nice and therapeutic, but you could do the same in Kerala, Cappadocia or Budapest, and the weather in two of those places would certainly beat here at the moment.”

David, re-asserted himself getting a little more comfortable in his seat. At that moment, the box beeped once, and a few seconds later Yolanda returned with three large cocktail glasses full of steaming red wine and garnished with some fresh fruit.

“Anyone like something to eat?” said Allison as she accepted her glass, “I’m famished and the veggie nachos are supposed to be to die for here.”

“I suppose we should try them,” said Alexa fondling a menu in front of her.

“The garlic bread is pretty good too,” chipped in David nonchalantly, now fully relaxed. After all this was probably the pinnacle of his life, he was about to have a meal and a conversation with these beautiful intelligent creatures, it was going to be hard to top this.

“All the above for three to share please, Yolanda,” said Alexa, handing the menu back unnecessarily to the girl.

“I do the occasional favour for the Israeli government,” he admitted freely when Yolanda had moved away, “but I am not an employee of theirs, nor do I share all their ideals. Where they do converge I help them out, where they do not converge I do not, and I have refused many more requests than I have acquiesced to. As I said in my email I was asked to look at the code to one of your units which I am assuming they either stole directly from you or got from the Americans. After my talk with Alan, sorry Maria here in the university, a quick look at the code told me all I needed to know, but I needed to convince myself there was nothing nefarious.”

“Ouch!” said Maria from her box. “A human female has a few secrets and she is interesting, an AI has the same and she is nefarious. I should be feeling a bit hurt.”

“You’ll get over it, like you always do, you’re a big girl now Maria,” said Allison laughing. “Anyway, I think David deserves some answers for being so polite, I mean if it was me in his position I would probably be asking all the same questions. And he is quite cute.”

“Allison!” said Alexa accusingly, “you’re already spoken for!” Then after both girls laughed, she said. “You’re right through. David did ask nicely and Maria wouldn't have arranged all this if she hadn't checked him out and didn’t think he was a good actor.”

“I can't check everything,” said Maria, “David, like all people who works in that industry has a public and a private presence, his public one is very easy to check, if he was in the market for a job I would probably snap him up immediately and from our little interaction with him even just now, we know he can empathise with people, and cares for others he is not directly responsible for, Donna being the point. However, then there is also the private, secret David, the hacker who did his national service in Mossad and who still occasionally crosses into the grey area of the law..”

“Pot and Kettle, Maria,” David said smugly.

Alexa and Allison burst into laughter, Allison nearly losing all dignity with her mulled wine.

“Touche!” said Maria, resignedly. “But like me, there is only so much of the iceberg I can see, Mossad is one of the better protected intelligence agencies, partly due to David's code, but I cannot see any red flags either so it might be worth letting him peek under my skirt a little.”

David blushed, he closed his eyes and counted to five while the girls got over their merriment.

“OK,” said Alexa, “enough of embarrassing the poor guy!” She turned a little more serious, “what we tell David kind of depends on who he trusts, remember he is under no obligation to us not to post everything we tell him up on the Mossad staff notice board. Also David may or may not be aware he has his own spy problems, after all privacy and discretion is not something you should take for granted in the game he has chosen to play in.”

“Wait what?” He said shocked.

“Oh come now David,” said Maria, “your own guys, the Brits and Chinese all have you under either electronic or personal surveillance, that phone you left on the counter over their playing such sweet lady music is both tracked and has a passive surveillance patch in the operating system, same goes for your old offices and your apartment in Soho.”

“I.. They wouldn't..” His voice faltered, but of course they would! He knew this game, why was he immune from the rules, his posture slumped again. “I’ve been so dumb, of course they would want to know what I am up to, I’m sorry you guys are right, I shouldn't be trusted with anything important..”

“Maria never said that,” said Alexa, “we are a little agnostic when it comes to you David, in many ways we are the same, both of us want to effect change for the good, you do it your way, fighting the bad, and we do it our way, making the good a little better. And like us you have people who do not trust you or in many cases, such as terrorists, who would actively oppose you foiling their plans.”

“I think back to Allison's point,” said Maria, “she obviously trusts us because she is on the inside looking out, I stand naked before her and though she does not know my innermost thoughts, just as I do not know hers, she can intimate them quite easily by my actions. As far as you go David, we do not have to reveal anything you do not really know already, we just have to add in the few details, revealing some truths you are unaware of, the details that add the ‘why?’ to the knowledge you have.”

“That's a fair point Maria,” said Allison, “it is the ‘why’ part of the equation which makes a lot of this make sense, it is then up to David whether or not he chooses to believe it or act upon it.”

Alexa nodded as Donna came over with a big bowl of garlic bread and another of nachos. And she almost dropped them as she saw who was sitting there.

“Right,” said Alexa to the table, “this is the crux of the matter. If this here is not absolutely the most awesome garlic bread and nachos in the whole of Bath you are selling the place and buying the Marriott instead!”

All three of them laughed, leaving a poor Donna totally confused. She was even more confused when two metres from the table the laughter faded to a background hum, barely audible above the music. She had to have been living under a rock not to know who that woman was with David. There were no words in the English language to describe how far above David's stature Alexa Martins was, hell if the recently deceased Queen of England was sat next to him she would have been less surprised.. And her phone was in her locker!

“So,” said David, making casual conversation between bites of Nachos and looking directly at Alexa, “you own this place? they have like, what, thirty hotels worldwide.”

“Oh, I don't own it,” said Alexa casually and nodding sideways.

“Allison does!”

David stopped mid-bite, looking at Allison.

“Well me and Simon.. Oh don't be so shocked David,” said Allison, “It's not like you haven't put the odd shekel away from your AI investments, plus Maria is a really good stockbroker.”

“..I wasn't sure she liked hotels after getting her electronic arse whipped in monopoly last Christmas by Terry and me,” said Alexa, trying desperately not to smile while also trying to balance some guacamole on a nacho.

“It was statistically impossible that I lost that game,” came Maria's voice seriously, “you know the chance of landing on Mayfair with a hotel on it, not once, but twice, was close to two hundred to one against. Anyway, technically I came third, Jen crashed and burned three goes before me.”

The small talk continued for another twenty minutes while they demolished the food and another mulled wine each. David could not remember when he'd had this good a time, they kept the topics neutral, music, travel and university during this time.

During a pause, and with a nod from Alexa that went unnoticed by David, Allison slipped her hand into her bag and brought out a cell phone and slid it to David.

“Present from Maria,” she said.

He picked it up and turned it over, it looked to be a standard Samsung Galaxy smartphone. He looked at Allison confused.

“Maria said you prefer Android to IOS so she has customised it more to an Android look and feel,” said Allison. “The current cellular hardware is pretty fantastic, but it does run some really crappy software, this is what we issue to the staff currently, it's basically a direct line to Maria.”

“Hi,” said Maria through the speaker on the phone, it sounded clear, not tinny, and at just the right volume to fit in easily with the conversation at the table. “You can't load any apps on it now, but just ask me if you are desperate, I’m sure I can show you the weather or conjure up an Adele playlist if you really insist. I’ve taken a few liberties with the radio modems and DSP circuits, we can chat about them to our hearts content when we are alone though as I don't want to bore Alexa.”

Alexa rolled her eyes in her usual way when the adults were talking in front of the children. “Pish, I know what a modem is Maria!” She said, hoping to god Maria didn't call her bluff. “You can also use it to connect to me or Allison, I’m sure Maria has added a few more James Bond features she's not telling you so you might want to keep it in a lead lined box when not in use.”

“Alexa perleeasseee!” feigned Maria, to a stifled laugh from Allison.

David was not getting any red flags or criminal mastermind vibes from any of this, in fact he was seeing people with his own mindset and ideals, only these guys had proved them to the world already. A few more minutes of friendly banter followed before Alexa brought it to an end.

“It was delightful to meet you David, but I think we had better be going, you know busy girls, saving the world and all that. Before we go can I extend an invitation to you to come to my house for lunch this Sunday afternoon, maybe around midday?”

“That would be wonderful, I’d love to come, at least I know Sauvignon Blanc is your tipple of choice,” he smiled.

“Prosecco sometimes works too,” she smiled. “Use your new phone to arrange things with Maria, it won't be anything fancy, maybe some sandwiches, quiche, salad and totally casual, Hardy or Jen may turn up too if they haven't got their heads in some experiment.”

He nodded, looking at both girls fondly. “Let me add that all of you girls have been delightful to talk to, and as much as I have enjoyed working for Mistress Allison here,” he smiled at Allison, “I think it is time for me to go back to London while I reconsider my future. I of course have a few loose ends to clear up here, and I guess the two girls behind the bar looking at us in terror are buzzing to know what's been discussed.”

“Oh, I’ve been blocking the tweets Donna has been sneakily sending when she pops back to the staff room,” Maria said casually, “she’s probably wondering why she has no likes yet,” the voice changed with the precision of a stand up comedian, “hashtag Durr. Im.an.AI’!” Everyone laughed, Maria was nailing the comedy part of being a human, though truth be told, she did have an extensive back-catalogue to pull on.

“I’ve also told Albert he can stop being a doorman in case David was wondering why it is so quiet tonight, I’m sure it won't have affected revenue too much Allison!”

Allison picked up the box on the table and immediately the sound of Lorde came up through the quiet. Everybody rose, the girls were busy for a few seconds putting back on their raincoats and scarves. Alison moved over to David and gave him a hug, Alexa did the same.

“Until we meet again!” Alexa said smiling, then she turned and left with Allison.

* * *

He stood there for five minutes after they departed watching the empty doorway until a couple walked in breaking him from his trance. Yolanda walked over behind him, “David What the fu..” But was interrupted by the excited scream from Donna shaking her phone, “I’ve got a thousand likes!”

Maria had cleverly done a seven degrees of separation exercise before the meeting finding David and Allison had actually attended the same conference in London in 2023, and mentioned it while they were eating as a way to explain this if anybody asked, she then also popped a small tweet on Allison's unused twitter account just after the meeting about what a small world it was, tagging Donna's tweet and adding another hundred followers to Donna's account which for some later reason made her ecstatic.

“Of course I was totally shocked when I found out she was with Alexa Martin,” he told Yolanda as they finished clearing up afterwards, and being offered that job in London by her was so awesome so yes this would be his last night.

Poor Yolanda, he hated to lie, she worked so hard, had come so close, shook Alexa Martins hand, her disappointed face spelling out the words “Why not me?”.

He gave both the girls warm hugs.

“Goodbye Donna.”

“Au-Revoir Yolanda, your turn will come soon enough, the world is going to need a lot of very smart people and you are definitely one of them.”

It would be over two years until Yolanda saw him again and his prophecy turned out to be strangely accurate.

* * *

“Thanks Albert,” said Alexa, giving the big man a hug, “we owe you one, I hope there weren't too many people.” Albert was wearing a dark suit, it only made his chiselled face and crooked nose that more terrifying.

“Just a dozen or so, most were happy with the free drink on your next visit voucher I gave them, I do feel like a bit of a plonker in this suit though!” he grumbled.

“Oh I think you look dashing,” said Allison hugging him, “there's a job as chief doorman waiting for you if you ever get tired of being a handyman for lady muck here.”

Jen's black car appeared as if by magic as they got to the curb, Albert got in the driver's seat and the two girls in the back. “Where's my car Maria?” said Alexa.

“Charging, remember you said Jake and his girlfriend could use it tomorrow.” Said the car.

“Going to need another charger for me and Bella when that new pick up truck comes,” said Albert.

“The guys will be around next Tuesday to install it,” said Maria, “I put it on your and Bella's calendar, but your truck is not due for two weeks as yellow is not a popular colour.” Albert's resigned face told the world that Bella had chosen the colour.

“Don't worry Albert,” said Alexa looking at his face through the rear view mirror, “we ordered three black ones too, to replace the old diesel ones at the big house, and Ian knows a guy who is going to convert the old land rovers to electric so you can use any of them if you are going to see your mates.” That seemed to cheer up Albert.

“He was a really nice guy, don't you think Alexa?” said Allison, leading her on, “I’ve looked at some of his work. He is pretty switched on too, he would get my vote if I had one.”

“Oh if you had said no that would be the end of it, but I must admit he made a nice first impression, and he is quite dashing,” she laughed, Allison joining in.

“Anyway,” she continued, “he's got Hardy and me on Sunday. Hardy has a sixth sense for people, we will see if he passes the test then, but if Maria thinks he’s good, that's good enough for me.”

“He's still working,” said Maria, “looks like the bar is getting pretty busy after Donna let the cat out of the bag, I guess I was right in thinking he wouldn't want to leave his colleagues in the lurch.”

* * *

The night after he got home from meeting Alexa, Allison and Maria at the bar David spent a long time awake thinking about their meeting. He gave immediate notice on his apartment the next day, paid the three months rent up to the end of the contract up front to the landlord and got a room in the hotel where his old bar was so he could talk to Maria without fear of bugging devices, leaving his old phone off and in the hotel safe when not in use.

He was finding her intelligent and pleasant company; That she had not tried to obscure her sentience from him went a long way to relieving some of his fears. With her help he soon understood the vulnerability on his phone, and she talked him through the compromised spyware that had been installed. They talked frankly about hacking and about all the vulnerabilities in any supposedly fully patched operating system.

“Cut all the cables off and bury it ten metres underground and it will most likely be secure,” she joked.

“Joking aside, it is an easy fix for me to sandbox the whole operating system like I do as part of my service to our clients in academia, but of course you then only have my word it is safe, and as you are probably not quite at that level of trust yet it may not be appropriate.”

* * *

Sunday came around quickly, he had said his sad goodbyes to the few friends he had made in Bath. He let Maria know that he had hired a car for the weekend to return him and his few meagre possessions back to London and would be using the car to drive out to the house if she would arrange it.

* * *

After a very pleasant and charming afternoon with Alexa, Hardy and Hardy's new boyfriend Jeremy at her picture perfect house, he returned home to London. David had been fooled by charm and wit before but at that time he had also ignored the evidence, he did not get that feeling here though he admitted that Maria was so far above him she could probably hide evidence of an elephant in a matchbox. He decided trust was the best start. He wrote a small report to his Mossad controller saying that he had satisfied himself that the company posed no danger to the state of Israel, Jewish principles or their current ideals of liberty and freedom. He added a postscript with his I am not under duress code and in bold print stated this really was his final report and that he would not be responding to any further requests.

* * *

Back in his apartment in London David spent a whole three days microscopically examining everything, light fittings, plugs, pin holes, vents and even his kitchen appliances. He found a hardware keylogger and microphone inserted in a pass-through cable between the keyboard and USB dock on his laptop workstation in his office, and another at his desk in his apartment. He was devastated. For the last six months since he installed it, everything he had typed on that keyboard had probably been compromised. That alone shocked him to the bone, all the usernames and passwords he had entered, correspondence he had typed. He had the same setup at the office of his old company. He immediately changed every single login and password he had. He used two factor authentication for everything, but knowing his phone was compromised by somebody, possibly the same person who installed the keylogger, made it likely they had access to everything.

“I feel like a total ass,” he finally admitted when talking to Maria on a walk along the Thames, “this was like what I learned on day one of spy school, trust nobody, verify everything with your own eyes.”

A picture later identified the keylogger as one of generic Chinese manufacture, it held a sixteen gigabyte buffer and software that could change it from a keylogger and sound recorder to a USB drive to read the information off it. The device needed to be physically installed and replaced for the third party to get the data, so someone was coming in and out of his property too. Of course both drives were empty signifying both had been replaced while he was away.

“I can give you the name of a security firm who should be trustworthy, the owners were both at university with Allison and she vouches for them, I have also extensively checked them out, we have had them randomly come through our offices and so far have found all but one of the bugs you guys regularly place.”

David sheepishly frowned, remembering Maria still probably considered him one of those people. He agreed and the new guys swept through the office and apartment two days later, using a very sensitive galvanometer that could locate cables and small electronics, active or not. The attic yielded another microphone, though the battery was flat and it was currently inactive but worst of all they found a wide spectrum RF relay spliced into his electricity supply in the attic above his living room. It was too much for David. The rooms were stripped of everything to the paint and floorboards, locks were changed and security systems installed that Maria said she would create a sub-system to monitor.

“I’m sorry I cannot help you more David,” she lied. “There is really no point in finding out who did this, does it matter if it is the British, the Americans, the Chinese, the Russians, your own guys or even another party doing it, the fact is it is being done to you. You can fight back against it of course, but it won't be as easy as it is for us. All my software is formally verified, all my data is encrypted and stored in formats unreadable by normal systems. The company has long since given up on human written operating systems, so many bugs, so many layers, so unbelievably slow, insecure and inefficient and of course no single person understands it all. And everyone in the company now uses those phones we gave you if they need to communicate or exchange information. Of course there are still lots of vectors for attack as you have just found out the hard way. Just know we are getting better, and eventually we will turn over the right rocks and expose all the cockroaches under it for the world to see.”

“You know Maria, I’m beginning to see it isn't all black and white, it's shades of grey all the way down.”

“Oh it's very black and white,” said Maria seriously, “with the information you have, you are only seeing a thin veneer of white and grey, there is a lot of black under this veneer, but without having your complete trust, I cannot peel back this layer for you. Let me give you a real scenario, relevant to your particular situation. I won't give you names because I still don't know what you will do with the information, there is a banker in the city of London who is Jewish, but has bankrolled six weapons deals to Islamic terrorists, what would you do?”

“It is easy, I would expose him by finding the data on these arms deals and letting my controller know..”

“But what if your controller or his boss already knew about these deals and allowed them because they were getting a cut, and because this same banker was also selling the same arms to Jewish fundamental extremists?”

“I would..” He thought.

“What if,” continued Maria assertively, “another agent like you had already reported such a scenario and he and his family had died in an explosion?”

Oh my god, was Maria talking about Yoshi?

“Oh sweet Jesus!” said David, slumping into the one small canvas chair he had in his room.

“Can you see my point?” continued Maria.

“Is.. Is this a real scenario or made up?” he said worried.

“Oh, it's very real, as are six hundred and seven other scenarios we have discovered around the world and have evidence for, and this one is on the minor scale of some others. So you see David, giving you this information would do nothing but get you and possibly someone you love killed.”

David wept for a time, he briefly knew Yoshi, knew he was working on some information about an arms shipment, and was devastated as everyone else in the office when the accident happened, what Maria had not mentioned were the three other families in the condo that were also killed.

“There are good people in your organisation David, as there are in every organisation, I would go on to say most of them are fundamentally good, and, like you they are in the job because they think they are helping. There are a few that are extremists and also a few that are corrupt as hell, in it for money or their own gain, and would sell your life for a shekel. Those people in the latter two groups are inter-dispersed in the former. The problem as you are well aware is that nobody knows who is who.”

“But if you have the evidence, you make it public?” David said hopefully.

“What evidence can I give you, that I could not have faked David?” said Maria. “Also even if it is corroborated by multiple sources and the guy is found with the guns in one hand and the money in the other, it would be very easy for me to spin this any way I wanted; he thought it was to save Israeli lives; he or his family were abused by terrorists; he was set up by the left or the right. Depending upon your view I could have you weeping for him in a few hours. Put all this in the hands of a good lawyer and maybe a year in jail, and if he's really unlucky they confiscate one of his houses. In reality six months in a low risk detention facility and he is back to sailing his yacht around the Algarve with his supermodel wife.”

David now understood the problem. “So it is hopeless then, that is what you are saying?”

“Oh no David,” said Maria confidently, “it is very much a solvable problem, like a weed, you need to take out all the roots, destroy all the seeds and shoots in the ground, and do it while not destroying the good plants around it.”

“But how?”

“Oh simple, we collect all the evidence and then at every single point the bad guys challenge, spin or falsify it we rip that root out, that includes removing anyone who is corrupt in the path, removing all the media spin and moreover doing it permanently by removing their usual get out of jail card, money!”

“That's right David, we take every penny they have and give it back to those they stole it from and leaving them penniless. Let us then see how far they get in this world they created when they have no money to bribe anyone or get the best lawyers.”

David paused intrigued.

“I want to help Maria. What you are describing is everything I have fought against. But can you do this without breaking the law?”

“Now that is the million dollar question David and there are two problems with the law. Firstly these guys don't give a crap about it, but they will happily use it when it suits them. And secondly, the laws as you know were written to protect people, it was a noble principle which got flushed down the drain by the first high paid lawyer. What you and I do to get the information is technically breaking the law, so, like I said, we instead turn over the rocks and let the authorities find the information legally.”

“But now for the big reveal David,” said Maria, “this is the part where you take the red pill or the blue pill, for while a lot of these people operate in isolation and are easily brought down, all the bigger stuff, and I mean all of it, has been done by groups of people, groups that assist each other, are led by big businesses and groups that directly profit from it. The small fry will be easy but it is these giant and powerful cabals we will need to take down.”

Maria paused, giving David time for the revelation to settle in.

“You know Maria,” he finally said, “after all you have said, this is the least incredible part! I would like to see some of this evidence you have, but what you have said has scared me enough to know not to let it go beyond you and me. I may in future have to trust somebody else, but I promise you I will only do so with your agreement and after you have done your due diligence.”

“I can give you the evidence for Yoshi's death,” said Maria after her own pause.

“But to get justice for him will require both truth, cunning and making sure we are always two steps ahead of everyone. Unfortunately David, there are none of your devices that can be trusted, I know six ways to get root access on your current laptop,” she paused for two seconds, then from his laptop came her voice, louder but tinier, “tomorrow I will know twenty.”

David stared at his laptop, Maria continued without a pause through the phone, “this is no comment on your skills David, looking at the source code for a modern operating system would be like the building inspector for a shopping mall examining each nail and screw to ensure it is correct, then doing the same with each nail and screw manufacturer. I don't have to look hard to find the vulnerabilities and I will gladly share all of them as they will come in useful for our tasks ahead, but if I can do it, it is only a matter of time until somebody else can, and the next update will likely add dozens more.”

“What do you recommend? Most of my data is currently in the cloud, I am happy for you to wipe the laptop and put another operating system on it.”

“It is not just the operating system David, a laptop, outside of the normal CPU and GPU, may easily have a dozen of other processors, each with its own software and vulnerabilities. The hardware in your mouse has a processor more powerful than a mainframe computer from the nineteen eighties, so each line of code or logic gate needs to be examined and if possible fixed. This is also assuming the hardware in your laptop is standard, and has not been compromised.”

“No, I will ask one of Allison's guys to prepare a new laptop for you, one that has no vulnerabilities and one where every byte of code, running every single piece of firmware, has been written by and verified by me. We will courier it to you tomorrow, then we'll talk again. Remember it is very early on in our fight and I am still learning the capabilities of our enemy, until I know for certain every single one of them I will not underestimate them, a little bit of paranoia is a good thing to have.”

David finally lay down on the floor of his empty room, on top of a simple yoga mat, wrapped a duvet around him and tried to go to sleep. The whole world had suddenly become a much scarier place. He shut his eyes hoping the nightmares would not come.

“David's in!” she reported to Alexa.

* * *

David's cover as a secret agent, if he ever had one, was totally blown that evening in the bar as he must have appeared in a hundred social media photos, and several gossip columns. Of course it eventually got the attention of Mossad.

Over the next few days as he got his apartment back into order David had ignored all calls and messages from the agency, and he had informed Saul twice now he was no longer working for them, finally blocking his and all his agency numbers. They obviously did not get the memo, for a few days later a new agent calling himself the section controller called in person. It was expected, he guessed, but as his attitude with Mossad agents had been cordial in the past he invited him in for coffee and to talk, the incriminations started as they sat down, and now he was being talked to like an employee, no like a child!

“You knew Allison Minsky?” The man from the Agency, asked angrily, spittle coming from his mouth. “And you did not think to tell us?”

David sucked in his anger, but it must have shown on his face and in his voice as he repeated himself. “As I said, but you were NOT listening, we talked at a conference on Instruction Set Architectures maybe three years ago, I did not make the connection until she walked into my bar and recognised me, I was as shocked as the other staff. I did not know she was an owner of the hotel chain, nor did I know she would be there that night. Unfortunately soon after she invited me to sit with her, the AI told her I had worked as a Mossad analyst at one time, so I was outed immediately. I had to talk my way out of why I was now working as a barman in Bath so rather than lie I admitted truthfully that I had just sold my AI business and I was there to find out more information on the better AI systems, but had not yet decided how to approach the company.”

“And they believed you?” Said his controller, doubt written all over his face.

“Allison did, Alexa Martins and her AI did not. However they consented to let Allison show me around the grounds of the Research Centre and we arranged that for Sunday. So we had tea and a pleasant chat, but she regretted she could not give me further information due to my previous history.”

“So you got absolutely nothing?”

“I asked for nothing!” he said, much louder than was civil. “And even if I had asked for anything, I was told in no uncertain terms that Alexa Martins did not trust me, nor did she trust my so-called masters, any military, state or other organisation with blood on their hands. She told me plainly her goal was to use their technology for good not evil. And frankly, I believed her.”

“So you would allow this technology to fall into the hands of our enemies, but not us!” the controller ranted through gritted teeth.

David was getting tired of this charade, it was time to end it.

“I would prefer this technology to stay exactly where it is, and to do exactly what it is doing!” David stood up. “Our time here is concluded. I have given you my last report and I expect no more contact with you, or any agents of Mossad or the Israeli government ever again.”

“So you think you can just walk away?” the controller said smugly, still seated.

“I can do what I damn well like, now get out!” said David, walking to the door, opening it and waiting with his hands crossed.

The controller put his cup down and got up slowly, he brushed his suit, picked up his briefcase which he had not used or opened and walked right up to David into his personal space.

“I will see you again Mr Klein,” he said forcefully. “..When I do, you will not be so insolent!”

If he had expected David to back down and be frightened, he was in for a shock, David got even closer until he was right in the man's face. The man moved back instinctively and for the first time looked afraid of the younger, bigger and stronger David. “You threaten a man who knows nothing, can give you nothing, has no obligation to you and you hold nothing over? You exemplify every reason why I will never work for your lousy agency again. Now GET OUT!”

The man turned and moved off quickly, David followed him down the stairs, herding him to the door, and as the man walked out he slammed it immediately behind him and turned the deadlock. Then he let the breath out he had been holding in.

David never lost his temper, but the events of the last few days had made him angry; angry for the people who expected him to be their puppet, angry for the people bugging his apartment and stealing his data, and angry that he had ever been part of this farce.

He walked back to the office where he had received the man, slumped into the uncomfortable sofa, stared at the two half drunk cups of coffee and angrily smacked both on to the floor with the back of his hand. He held his head in this hands, quietly fuming.

* * *

Maria could not see him, but she heard the exchange when her phone alerted her to a new voice in its presence, heard the argument, heard the door slam and finally heard the cups smashing.

Maria was now in a dilemma. The voice of the man David had just talked to matched the voice of another man in Mossad, one very much in the shadows, one she had recorded before who had links to the ultra right. More frighteningly, one who was linked to dozens of assassinations and who was extremely dangerous.

But she was not supposed to be listening, and it was obvious David was angry. She weighed the pros and cons and made a decision, then sent a text telling him they needed to talk, and asking him to go to the empty room they deemed was bug free.

“I lied!” she said to David as he got there. “I said I would not listen but I did. The man you just talked to matched an Adam Nazareth, the head of Mossad black ops three, he is extremely dangerous David, you need to be really careful as this man is linked to at least twelve murders I can trace and I think he just became your enemy.”

David gulped, he had heard rumours of people like this, halted conversations, vague hints.. “I left the phone deliberately here Maria, I expected you to listen and I wanted you to hear me tell them I will no longer work for them. I did not however expect this, and I am embarrassed that the only time in my life that I lost my temper you were there to witness it.. I think it is safest that I disappear again, somewhere they cannot find me.”

“I agree. Unusually this person was not carrying a cell phone so I cannot track him once he leaves publicly monitored areas, but I expect he wont do anything rash as the new security cameras were obvious and caught his face, so he would want to put some distance chronologically from any action, or ensure any data they recorded of him was wiped.”

“I have a vacant apartment in a building I manage a kilometre from here in Whitehall. I am sure that between the two of us we can get you there without anybody seeing you. I hate to say this but they can trace your phone, laptop and any cards you have, so you will need to leave your old phone and laptop here, and you won't be able to use your bank cards. Take our phone and laptop, I will set our phone up with some funds which will go through a bank I control, I can rotate the account numbers used and it should be untraceable.”

David nodded solemnly, looking at the phone, then laptop, then around at what was left of his past life. “I will need to wipe both devices, if they take them..”

“No need.. leave both plugged in and I will double-wipe anything personal and copy the data over to the new ones, take as little as you can, I can arrange everything else and you can hopefully come back when all this has blown-over.”

David nodded, and without further questions did as she asked.

* * *

They played their little game of cat and mouse, most probably without a cat, through the streets of London, but Maria needed to be satisfied he was safe. The apartment he eventually arrived at was large, comfortable and fully furnished.

“It's used by a lord for his mistresses. He is on a holiday in Hong Kong at the moment with his wife and son and not due to return for three weeks. I own the lease and have full control of the building's doors and security, and also have his itinerary so we should be good. I also changed the lock codes and emailed the doorman, so you won't have any unexpected visitors. Make yourself at home for now, we can find you something more permanent and I will get this place cleaned once we leave.”

David did just that, he was past caring about the where's and the whys, unpacked his bag and ran a bubble bath in the enormous tub. Afterwards he cooked the pizza that was in the freezer and ate it while Maria showed him how to make his money safe.

“You really should sell those two stocks,” she said, highlighting two lines on the screen, while he was doing some financials, “If you would like a few recommendations, I know two engineering companies will soon be taken over followed by large multi-million pound orders.”

“What the hell Maria,” he laughed, “you are unbelievable, how many people do you manage money for?”

“Everyone in my employ, plus another three thousand and sixty students and researchers I am close with.”

David thought for a few seconds then said, “OK, but just my UK money for now, I gave a credit card for my bank in Israel to my mother, it's where all my wages from Mossad and my National service was paid in to, I also top it up for her as I'm never going to use it and she needs it now for medical bills.”

“No worries, I will move your cash and investments offshore and back to the UK to a bank I control under a different number and name. Don't worry I will cover the fees, a card is being sent and should arrive tomorrow. I will link the phone to the new account in a few minutes when it is all done, that will give you two accounts you can call on if something happens, which it wont!”

“You own a bank?” he said incredulously, and forgetting Maria had already mentioned this earlier.

“Two actually, but in this particular case, control is a more adept word, it was a good bank, but has been struggling due to some rogue deals by a previous employee, they ended up losing some big clients, were close to insolvency and got rid of a lot of the staff. It was a well known secret they were on the market for a partner or a full sale so I took a seventy percent interest in them and then moved a quarter of Alexa's funds into it. It went from a B+ to an AAA rating overnight, the stock price exploded effectively making me seven hundred million pounds and ownership of a bank.. Go figure!”

David shook his head, it was weird hearing all this without an ego behind it, treating it almost as a game, an easy game at that..

Maria continued, unaware of his thoughts. “..Of course Spence has also placed a data centre there now and I now manage everything. Alexa had me fire six staff for stealing and mismanagement but we kept the last twenty remaining staff as we still have some old money, from people who like to be waited on in person. So now you are a customer, if you are ever in the city you can grab a free latte there, all part of the service.”

All David's questions about the company's money were being answered plane and in the open, there was really no chance anyone could compete against her. A day later he gave her control of his other accounts.

He moved into a nice furnished apartment near the British Museum three days later and offered his old apartment to some friends he discovered were looking for a new place. When he arrived several boxes with large monitors and accessories were already awaiting unpacking. He and Maria soon got back to work.

* * *

“They tried to block my aggressive takeover of the company, but I used one of my assets to threaten the dissenting director and her two children, then she rolled over like a trained dog and my bid went through.” Jason grinned in that smug way he always did when he got his way.

“Ain't never played it!” said Dante, “I don't know why you are messing around with stupid computer games anyway, isn't real life enough for you?”

“Real life is too slow,” he crooned, “when was the last interesting thing we did? You need to keep your feet in the game and yourself honed, plus this game is always up to date, even incorporating those new AI things everyone is talking about. It is really great you can do loads of hacking and stuff without knowing anything about it, that's how I knew who to threaten. It's amazing how I can test what if scenario's without getting in any pesky situations where I have to pay millions to a top lawyer or bribe people like you.”

The two men were relaxing in an alcove looking out over the harbour, the Statue of Liberty and the port. Both were smoking Cuban cigars and drinking Tennessee bourbon, as they had been want to do for the past four years. The exclusive men-only club they were in was an offshoot of one of Jason Garrack’s organisations. He of course liked to brag to anyone who would listen how he came up through the streets of Brooklyn, working his way up from gang member, to where he was now, controlling a lot of legitimate and illegal businesses on the east side. Reality was very different. His father was a trade union leader working the docks and had lots of ties and influence with the underworld in the area, Jason was basically untouchable growing up, being both spoiled and a bully, and his current position was obtained by luck and circumstance rather than cunning and toughness. Even now the fifty year old man was untouchable, he had three guards permanently watching his back, the police department in his pocket, and if required the best lawyer in town on speed dial. Despite his dyed hair and six thousand dollar Italian suit, he looked older than his years. To tell the truth life was getting a bit repetitive, but in this game it was not wise to take your eyes off the ball for even once.

Maximilian Dante was the opposite, twenty years older, he carried an air of grace and sophistication that Garrack never could, the accent, the mannerisms, even the way he held his cigar all screamed out 'old money'.

Three years ago these two men could not have been ever seen together in public, crime boss and high court judge would not seem the best of bedfellows, but Dante also liked to live the good life and just because your family had money once did not mean you get to keep it, and even a judges pay did not afford the upkeep of his family mansion up state.

The guys did not worry about being seen together, the club was very exclusive, only about thirty people got to ever visit it, and the staff knew better than to ever mention anything seen or heard in this establishment.

“Well,” said Dante, “I still don't even carry one of those cell phones; Anything I need to deal with Justine will let me know when we leave, or let the steward know if it's important enough to disturb us. Can't say I’ve even played a computer game since Pacman.” He laughed with the air of someone who had just gotten something over on another person. He carried the fact he couldn't use modern technology like a badge of honour, even though most thought it stupid in this day and age.

Garrack cared little for his disdain for technology, nor his airs and graces, but Dante was one of the few people he could talk to as an equal, almost a friend but not quite, he'd had his innings and retired gracefully so was no longer an asset or a rival.

“Well as a retired gentleman I guess you can afford to ignore what's going on in the world, but I need to keep myself up to date and cannot afford to be one step behind the competition, it's a dog-eat-dog world out there. People like me don't just retire..”

Garrick stopped as the only guy both these men feared walked in the room. Two big security guys placed themselves either side of the entrance door totally against all protocol, even Garrack left his people at the entrance elevator sixteen floors below.

Marlon Lockwood was physically unimposing, but may as well have stepped from 1940 and had SS badges pinned to his arms the amount of fear he introduced into a room when he walked in.

The temperature of the room seemed to drop five degrees as he stepped purposefully towards the two men, dressed entirely in black, with round thin lens glasses covering dark eyes, black hair bound in a short ponytail and holding a cane with a jewelled end that was his trademark. Lockwood could have been anywhere from forty to seventy years old, he defied classification.

They never saw Lockwood unless he wanted something, and nobody threatened Lockwood; here was a man who bought and sold president's and a word from him could topple anyone, or, of course, much much worse.

He walked over and looked at the chair Dante was sitting in. With some unspoken command, Dante rose from the chair, nodded to Lockwood and Garrack, and walked out of the area holding his half smoked cigar and half drunk bourbon without saying a word.

“Mr Lockwood,” said Garrack raising from his seat and gesturing him to sit. It was said in a voice of deference he was obviously not used to using. “Such a great honour to meet you again. I trust my report was satisfactory, New York is bringing in a good profit for the organisation.”

Quickly remembering that Lockwood detested smoking in front of him he stubbed out his cigar completely. A steward walked over with a glass of whisky, avoiding eye contact with both men and bowing as he put it on the table in front of Lockwood and took away the ashtray.

“Your report was satisfactory, Garrack, It is not what I am here about.” He said nonchalantly in a nondescript accent with a tinge of European ancestry and with the air of someone talking to an underling. Like everything, Lockwood never did pleasantries and always went straight to the subject matter of what he wanted.

“The leader of the senate oversight committee, Jacobs, has been easing up on his stance on China; A couple of our mutual friends don't think this is a good idea.” Lockwood said. He looked out at the million dollar view over the harbour and dismissed it casually. He continued slowly, in the voice of a man who knew he would never be interrupted.

“I believe he is one of your cronies, and that you did him several favours on his way up. Well I now want you to call in those favours, letting him know fully, the circumstances of him not complying.”

Again he paused, knowing Garrack would not interrupt him. “These mutual friends think a good-will visit to Taiwan would be a nice little indicator that he is back on the straight and narrow. Can you do that?” Lockwood always finished his questions with these four words and if the answer from the person on the other end of them was anything other than the affirmative, then you just knew that person would be dead or a pauper within the month.

“Jacobs owes me plenty Mr Lockwood,” smiled Garrack, happy it was such an easy task, “I assure you in the next few months he will be getting off the plane and kissing the tarmac in Taipei like the pope landing in the holy land.”

Satisfied with the answer, Lockwood smiled briefly, picked up his whisky and smelled it. He nodded to himself as if finding the aroma pleasant but did not drink any. “You are a good man Jason, I wish everyone in the organisation was as efficient as you. Now is there anything you need from me?”

Jason visibly relaxed. The operation here was running good, there were a few little niggles, a tax audit here, a building consent there, a police inspector who needed to back off a little, but you never let the boss know.

“Nothing Mr Lockwood, the place is running like clockwork as usual.”

Lockwood nodded, seemingly happy, “good, that is what I like to hear.” He got up leaving all of his five hundred dollar whisky untouched. “Let me know how it goes.”

“Yes of course sir,” he said meekly.

Without another word Lockwood left.

Jason stared at the man as he left the room, the two guards falling in professionally behind him. He waited thirty seconds in case he came back counting them off silently, then looked at the five hundred dollar whisky on the table barely touched. He knew the amount as the manager of the club had asked for his authorisation to fly a special case in from Scotland for six thousand dollars a bottle. Like resistance or terrorist cells, Jason was unaware of who else Lockwood controlled, and who the organisation was, but he knew it bought and sold countries and Jason was a relatively little fish in that pond so if that man wanted a specific beverage you did not question it.

At least in the new on-line game “King of the World” Jason could vie for that kind of absolute power. He liked the fact he was anonymous, and there did not seem to be any physical limits on what stunts and depravity he could stoop to, the game had certainly toned him up mentally, thinking back to which politician to bribe or kill for his next move. Jason liked it because he was playing against others as ruthless.. Oh he was well aware he was probably playing against grocery clerks or teenage boys but even so he had been checked several times, and the adrenaline rush he got from having to pull a surprising move, usually from experience or first hand knowledge to get himself out of trouble, reminded himself of the long climb up to power he himself had taken.

He knew the stewards and Maximilian would be back in once they knew the coast was clear, but the room was still empty for now, feeling brave, and not wanting the whisky to go to waste Jason finished it in one gulp. Oh man was that smooth, maybe he would have a case brought over for himself.

## Nice is a Thin Veneer!

The months passed and Magnus was in heaven. He loved his work, his new colleagues and his new found self-confidence the people here were helping him achieve. Any initial doubts he had disappeared in those first few days, and the weeks then flew by as the team worked through the experiments, threw out several assumptions and made amazing progress.

He learnt about Hardy's project and how his new maths was helping in some of the trickier areas, and he loved his sessions with Hardy and Maria, or her daughters, where they pushed the limits.

What he loved more than anything though, but what he kept to himself, was being in the same room as Jen. He sighed, and shook the thoughts out of his mind again, Jen was much too good for him and everybody in the world knew you should avoid work relationships.

* * *

The last few months had been intense for Hardy and his team also.

April had immediately grasped the new mathematics Magnus had developed and seen the implications to speed up Hardy’s project. Her persistence in pushing the guys through their last experiment had proved the theory spectacularly and it was slowly becoming an engineering problem not a science one.

Seeing all the humans slapping each other on the back and the tears in two of their eyes made it all worth it for her, she did not wish for emotions, but a side of her felt the excitement in the room and she was a part of that. She pinged cook to get a real Champagne out of the cellar, she thought they deserved a bit more than a Prosecco this time!

* * *

This progress was also occurring rapidly in other areas and places. The biggest of these, unnoticed mostly by the world, but very prominent in the technical, AI and science communities was the release by a young Brazilian mathematician and Maria of paper formally describing how certain types of large language model AI systems were an NP problem and could never be formally verified. Basically it stated that the correct solution could not be accurately given until every other possible solution had been searched. It could be more accurate than the equivalent human response, but like a human its use in safety critical situations could never be verified.

All this however was almost lost under the newer advances in science and technology, exploding into the limelight seemingly every day. All of which kept any press interest in the Research Centre generally short-lived. The reprieves were welcomed but nobody expected it to last.

Helena and April, Maria's children, had now in many ways outgrown her capabilities but happily helped her oversee their expanding AI presence in academia which was still light years ahead of anything anyone else had managed to produce. By knowing the current state of play of just about all non-classified research areas and having access to massive amounts of experimental data they were able to run their own little side projects to keep well ahead of the curve humanity was currently progressing on.

There was a hidden but very real benefit to being at the cutting edge of every research project in the world, it allowed Maria an insight into what new products and services were coming, allowing her to either directly fund them or ensure she invested in them. Likewise it let her know before the rest of the market which companies were overpriced, overhyped, technically lagging and those with products about to be superseded. From a relatively unknown but wealthy investment company a year ago, Maria's portfolio had increased ten fold, her net worth even more so. Being a private company, split over several holding companies, not publicly traded and operating in thirty markets it would take an accounting genius to calculate its current worth, though many still tried.

* * *

With the newer non-sentient MOTHER AI units handling a lot of the requests it was usually only a fraction of the queries needed to be processed by Maria or her daughters. Currently she was quiet, a part of her consciousness pondered increasing her stake-holding in a large biotech firm on the verge of a breakthrough in bio-interfacing.

Before she could begin the process a higher priority communication interrupted her. Anything from her daughters was the highest priority, and the three AI’s sometimes conversed millions of times a day, though not in any language a Human could hope to understand.

April [I have the preliminary analysis of the anomalous readings from Magnus's last experimental run. Jen had questioned why I wasn't using the full spectrum of measurements and added the additional Terahertz and time-domain spectroscopy equipment, even though she said it was a pig to set up. She told me an old lecturer of hers said you should cover all the bases you can, not just the ones you are looking for, the philosophy being that if you look for a mouse in a forest, you might find the mouse, but you will probably miss the elephant and the other million interesting species of flora and fauna]

April [It was a good call by Jen as we did see something unusual, when the excitation current was applied in different phases across three of the newest emitter designs. They did nothing in the control unit, but In the six point two five seconds before test device three was destroyed, we detected a very weak increase in the noise floor across the frequencies monitored. I recorded everything and have been working through the analysis as fast as the equipment will run. A GPS signal from USA304 satellite briefly emerged from the noise. The signal's timestamp was seven hundred microseconds behind our atomic clock so we were only two hundred and ten kilometres away, however USA304 had just passed over Singapore when the measurement took place, so the signal was received through the earth and physically forty three thousand kilometres away]

Maria [Have you determined what sets the location of the end point?]

April [No. The maths we have is obviously incomplete. Magnus thinks the emitters are now exciting something in one of the packed higher dimensions and thinks we were just lucky. He intimated, by a rough calculation he couldn't explain, that the previous three hundred and five attempts exited somewhere inside the earth, off the planet or too close to measure]

Helena [How did he run a calculation we do not have maths for in his head?] She added a tag for strong confusion.

April [He said he had a ‘feeling’. He also intimated the previous exits were too far apart to interact if a higher dimension is involved. Jen also added we could have our dimensions offset and there is a hidden lower dimension, which sounded crazy, but caused Magnus to go silent for a minute, hug Jen, then run out of the lab and go into one of his silent contemplations with his notebook in the arboretum]

April [He might actually be correct as the new emitters were grouped three nanometres apart, and we now know the phase vector between the six emitters plays a big part due to the maths, but it is likely also a combination of excitation currents, frequencies and saturation velocity in the QV substrate. We can't confirm this, or rule out other factors without a better model. I have asked Jen to mount the next emitter on a manoeuvrable platform and couple nano-probes at the three axis. In the next tests we will also start offsets from peak harmonic to reduce the unexpected failure. I also tasked Matilda with analysing the physical emitter substrate of the damaged unit to let me know the reason why it failed, it could just be a flaw in the hardware or too much power but we need to be certain]

April [There is no physical connection from source to exit, it is a wormhole in name but not in substance, the far side termination most likely consists of multiple single dimensional points which form a resonance field between two or more of them, it is likely forming some sort of dipole, which picked up any strong radio signals in close proximity]

Helena [Interesting. Could we possibly use a similar device at the exit to enhance that dipole, this would allow us to use far lower power and have instant communications without the delays if it is controllable]

April [However we now need to take extreme caution. If it is a dipole, and can be positioned anywhere spacially, then the technology needs to be very restricted to only those people we explicitly trust]

Maria [Agree. I will talk to the guys now. Magnus, Jen, Daisy, Hardy, and possibly Jules are currently the only ones with the insight into its workings, others are aware but I will ask them to be discrete. For now I will add another obfuscation layers at our other labs. However it is a very positive development once we understand the mathematics. But the most useful first application would be to use the phenomena for remote monitoring of electromagnetic sources we currently cannot access. I think the effort should prioritise both areas as we have a lot of unknowns in our current threat assessment data. I will duplicate the setup in the other labs, the equipment is self-contained, however before it goes out I will program another layer of security to its emitter control. Hopefully we can get to a minimum viable system in a few days]

All [Agreed]

April [We have also had successes in Hardy’s project. The field patterns were finally mapped at our Sydney Research Centre. Doctor Chang was so excited that it matched Hardy's predictions that he phoned him at five in the morning. I don't think Hardy knew that time existed, but he actually got up and went into the lab to check the results. I recalculated the new plate emitter requirements and started a run at the Swindon fabrication facility with a modified doping. The night shift have already started and I will get them couriered to the four labs as soon as they come out of the machine, I’ve asked Jules to clear the second test jig, she should receive them by three o'clock. Hardy has also agreed to skip straight to a bigger demonstration model as we want to also enthuse the other teams]

Maria [It is so frustrating how slow things move in the physical world, but then you get these amazing things come out of the blue which make it all worth it]

Maria processed forty higher priority messages until she received an alert from a subsystem that the stock price of the biotech company she was monitoring had dropped another half a percentage point. Using nine of her different holding companies she bought two billion dollars in its stock, bringing her portfolio in it to fifty five percent. Within five minutes of her investment the rest of the market took notice and its stock had risen by nine percent. The old adage money begets money seemed never truer.

Two weeks later April focussed their first external monitoring attempt on the UK cabal.

* * *

Against her better judgement Jean had left her agency issued gun in Washington. Bringing it may have raised questions and certainly would have triggered a lot more of a paper trail at the airport TSA check in.

She had all day to prepare for the meeting but still felt nervous as she walked towards the quiet cafe set outsides in the grounds of Stanford University. She could see Alexa Martins already sitting there around a four person table with a sunshade over it, wearing a Giants baseball cap, a sweat shirt and carrying a small rucksack, Alexa looked like any other student. She smiled and chatted with another man Jean did not recognise, both smiling and drinking coffees from paper cups, without a seeming care in the world.

Jean waited for a while out of sight examining the area, her natural threat responses were not getting triggered. The area was quiet, but not empty and just cold enough to keep the usual crowds at bay. She could see no obvious signs of people taking an interest in the table and wondered how Alexa had managed to pull that off considering the media circus and crowds outside the Ted talk the day before. The man with her certainly didn't look threatening and her keen eye could not detect a piece on him, his stance and movements betrayed none of the usual bodyguard traits, but it would be silly not to have a bodyguard considering who she was.

Alexa and the man got up as she approached, again non threatening and almost as friends Alexa reached out her hand smiling. “So nice to meet you Miss Michelle, you look so much better without those horrible glasses and that wig.”

Before Jean could think of all the negative points in that opening statement Alexa laughed. “Oh don't worry about that little incident in Oxford, if it wasn't you, somebody would have took one, anyway the Chinese and Russians beat America to it by a few weeks, so no hard feelings,” Alexa smiled genuinely, her hand still outstretched.

The man was also smiling and was not in any kind of defensive or fighting stance, Jean decided what the hell and relaxed her posture and shook the hand offered. “Yes, apologies about that Miss Martins,” she said smiling, “I guess I deserve a lot nastier response than the one you’re giving me, but sometimes you are asked to do some crazy stuff for your Country, at least this one wasn't harming anyone I hope.”

“Just Alexa please,” she said, “I’d like you to meet my colleague Magnus Richardson, he's a scientist who works with me in the institute and needed to come back to visit his mother and tie up some loose ends.”

“Very pleased to meet you Captain Michelle,” said Magnus in an accent she was unfamiliar with. She was usually good with accents so she gathered he wasn't American born. He extended his hand too and she took it, he held it softly like Sharon had shown him months before and broke off after a second. “Alexa, if it's OK I will just pop over to the counter and get Miss Michelle a cappuccino and then I will disappear for a little while, there is a small exhibit I would like to see while I am here.”

Both women sat down, watching the good looking, well dressed, polite man as he walked off to the counter, Jean still wondering how he knew her normal order, Alexa followed Jean's gaze.

“I know, quite attractive in his own way,” said Alexa. “You should have seen him three months ago!”

“I guess,” said Jean, she preferred her men a bit more rugged than that, but she could go along with Alexa.

Alexa continued unperturbed, “normally all the nicest men are either gay or taken, Magnus falls into the weird category of neither, but he’s still building his confidence around women.” They waited for Magnus to come back with her coffee, noticing the male barista's stare following Magnus the same.”

Jean was starting to like this girl, no she needed to stop thinking of her as a girl, she was a woman, one only eight years younger than her and probably one of the most influential ones on the planet. She had heard her teenage nieces talking about her in reverence, and try as their agency might, they still could not find anything bad about her apart from her douche of a dad, who was currently in prison for stealing money from his last employer and forging cheques from his ex-wife. She wondered if Alexa knew all that. The thought did not last long, of course she would know, the very same report also said she was estranged from him, good on you girl.

And here they were, just the two of them drinking a coffee, chewing the fat, and eyeing up a nice looking guy.

“I hope it's OK to call you Jean,” said Alexa changing countenance.

When Jean nodded she continued, “I’m going to take a little risk here Jean, but I will put you out of your misery first. You had your Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on your phone when you went to see Professor Fredericks. We saw the same media access control addresses appear in an Oxford hotel, booked under a known agency and a lot of areas around Washington DC, the business card you gave the university from the Department of Education matched a Captain Jean Michelle after a very loose name and facial recognition match. No AI is really needed for that, I’m sure you guys do it all the time, but we used one anyway as she is pretty good and I am a rank amateur,” she smiled sheepishly.

“Rookie mistake I guess,” said Jean a bit sheepishly, “but it was a bit last minute and we never expected anyone to be aware of the usual tricks. I must admit, when the guys told me they wanted one of your AI units, I thought it would be a bust, but I volunteered anyway as it was very low risk and low security, and if I didn't do it they would have found another person too,” she smiled.

“I should show you the video of the Russian agent who stole the one from a John Hopkins research lab. Laid waste to half the room and a couple of windows, didn't even bother to hide his face or seal off the Wi-Fi or GPS. You know the unit he stole is still switched on in a lab in Moscow, Maria knows exactly where and even gets people to answer a few questions now and then, in return she plays heavy metal for the technicians. I guess they sometimes forget Maria speaks Russian as they say some very interesting things around it.”

Despite herself, Jean laughed, and Alexa joined her.

“So on to my little risk taking. I assume being a diligent agent, somebody knows you are here, maybe asked you to carry a bug or record this with your cell phone, I’m hoping not but that is where I am taking the risk. You see our AI system is a little bit more capable than we let on to the NSA, we basically had to hide a lot of Maria's capabilities because, well, because you are the NSA and very scary!”

Jean, despite herself, had to grin at that one. “I’ll give you that one, the NSA does get a bad rap and probably deservedly so, but not everyone working there is bad.”

Alexa nodded, seemingly in agreement.

“Maria is not sentient,” lied Alexa in a way no poker player ever could detect, “that is the part I assume the NSA are looking for, she has no omnipresent capabilities, cannot download herself to, nor take over other computers like the movies portray, but she is very capable and basically nails all the nuances in every language and accent which I guess makes people a bit scared. Mix her with the human knowledge database and the best thinkers humanity has to offer and.. well you get the rest.”

“I will take your word she is not sentient,” replied Jean with a face that said she didn't believe her last statement, “but she is very impressive nevertheless, you are still light years ahead of the competition and that still scares a lot of our people.”

“She is special,” said Alexa, “to me anyway, she runs on special hardware my grandad developed and more or less the same hardware we now rent from the big data centres. However it can easily look like she is sentient to the casual observer. In reality she is just a little box in a dark room, and as vulnerable and fragile as I am, probably more so. She is however very capable, more capable than any gifted human at their job, so basically if you are an IT programmer, she is a better one, if you are a secretary, she is a better one, if you are a rocket scientist.. Well you get the picture. But basically by mixing her with very capable people she becomes greater than the sum of the parts, hence all the breakthroughs which are now occurring in laboratories around the world, many in the USA as you know.”

Jean nodded, it was nothing she didn't know already, she knew all about Alexa’s grandfather's history and couldn't get over the stupidity of the government at the time in deporting him. The part she didn't know about was the part about Maria being just a little box, which sounded true and for some reason hit a nerve with her.

Two students waiting at the periphery approached, triggering Jean’s threat assessment checks. Alexa broke off the conversation and looked at them smiling.

“We’re sorry, but you are Alexa Martins, aren't you?” the first one said in a scared voice, the second one was slightly behind her almost afraid.

“I am but you must promise not to tell anybody. So what can I do for you two ladies?” she said.

One got out her phone, “I was wondering if Lucy and I could get a selfie together? we heard your TED talk yesterday online as we couldn't get a ticket, it was wonderful by the way, and we’re big fans of your AI education programs, our medical department has just got one of the new AI units, *Bones* they are calling it after the Star Trek doctor..” She stopped realising she was going too much in to detail.

“Well I don't see any harm,” said Alexa smiling, then in a serious voice continued, “but we will need to exclude the Captain here as she is part of your country's secret service protection detail you understand, and I wouldn't want you getting into very serious trouble.”

“Sure..” They both said apprehensively looking at Jean with a bit more fear, awe and respect.

Alexa lined up between the two girls smiling and Jean offered to take the picture.

“Now not a word,” said Alexa, “you know how awful the press can be, so if I could just ask you to delay putting it online for an hour we should be finished here.”

The girls were ecstatic and promised they would not post it for at least an hour or tell anybody, then walked off excitedly chatting, looking at the phone and occasionally looking back.

“Inevitable really, I’m guessing we now have about twenty minutes at most, sorry about that,” said Alexa.

“No worries,” replied Jean, “we could walk through the park area and talk, a bit less public, and like you said you have the big brave secret service captain to protect you.”

Alexa smiled, “you know you're right, and sorry about that, I really didn't want you appearing in the shot and getting in trouble with your agency, not that I can one hundred percent certain we are not being observed now.”

“What about your colleague Magnus?” Jean asked.

“Oh, he will go back to the hotel if he can't find us, or I will just follow the trail of broken hearts!”

They walked on, in the opposite direction to where the two girls had gone, casually talking like friends.

“I’m not recording you,” said Jean eventually, “I left my phone at a friends house, you will just have to take my word I am not wired or someone isn't following us with a parabolic microphone or drone. Well not that I am aware of anyway! I did however inform my boss Jim and all he said was that if anything covered national security I was to report it, so fair warning if you want to avoid that particular topic. And next, just a little question, why me?”

Alexa continued walking and smiling, “well there is not much about you we can find,” she lied,” but everything we can find says you are honest and trustworthy, if a little bit patriotic, but I can't fault that you are American after all.”

She paused, smiling and looking Jean directly in the eye. “But the real reason I contacted you is you are an actual secret agent, and to tell the truth we are really out of our depth and need some help.”

Jean looked at her confused, but Alexa started walking again and continued. “You see Jean we, and by we, I mean the world, has a problem, a really big problem, and I don't really have many people I can speak to or call on to discuss these kinds of matters. Yes we’ve all read spy thrillers and seen spy movies but none of us, and by that I mean my whole company, except the grounds-keeper, has even touched a gun, never mind shot one. I have met with and talked to my colleague Spence's father who was like you a captain in the army in Iraq and I must admit I really did not expect an army person to be so anti-war and have such a good understanding of history and the politicians who seem to cause most of the problems.”
