Jean echoed that sentiment internally, there were very few people who had been in war situations who had enjoyed it, most saw it for what it was, a complete waste of human lives and resources, and rarely fought by the ones that caused it. She had talked to many non-US soldiers who had the same philosophy, she had laughed and drank beers with them, but with a word from her president she would be shooting at them. Mathews echoed this sentiment as well, having lost many good friends in battles over political ego's and bad intelligence. They continued walking through a gate past another small building and along a water feature now a good two hundred metres away from the cafe.

“Unfortunately, it is not just the NSA’s radar we are on, as you know we are probably the highest value target for most of the worlds security services and the biggest target for industrial espionage, even though we put most of our research into the public. What you are probably not aware of however is the layer above all this.”

Jean looked at her a little puzzled, so Alexa continued, “we recently had an incident which led us to do some very targeted investigations in the UK. What we found was an organisation that was manipulating government intelligence and policy as a means to simply benefit a group of powerful individuals. We also found out that the whole of our company was considered a target by this group with a goal not just to breach but to access and control all our systems.”

Jean stopped, now interested.

“We found this information by pure luck as we had been investigating these people after they had tried unsuccessfully to gain access to our networks, and were then caught manipulating share markets and government policy against interests we hold, interests like clean energy and our restricted AI policy. We dug deep into the organisation and followed the money trails back to over a dozen individuals in the highest positions of the UK government, secret services, and police force all taking money from a cartel of businesses including bankers, petrochemical companies and defence contractors.”

“Unfortunately, because of this we do not believe we have any recourse to the law, as these people are in a position to manipulate the police and security services and have repeatedly done so. So basically at this point we can't really trust anyone, for all we know the whole British institution is probably corrupt and manipulated.”

The emotion in Alexa's voice was genuine, but if Jean was having this conversation with anybody else she would have laughed it off as a conspiracy theory. She had another look around to check the area to be sure but her eyes still found nothing.

“Now for the scary part.” Alexa continued, “the UK cabal, as we call the organisation that is about to threaten us, is only one of four we have identified around the world which control large corporations and slush funds. They are above the law, in some cases they are the law, and can manipulate governments, corporations and policies to their own ends. There is another one in South Korea, one in Switzerland, but the biggest and most powerful one is here in the USA.”

Seeing Jean's doubt, Alexa continued, “I am going to provide all the evidence you need to allow you to see the problem and form your own conclusions, but I ask you to be very careful who you show this evidence to, and what you say to your superiors. The money trails lead all the way to the top of your government defence and security agencies, including your own agency. From what we can see, your agency is just as compromised as the ones in the UK, and there is lots of hard evidence that people have been killed in the past, so again, please exercise extreme caution, as you would be totally expendable to these people.”

Alexa didn't know this but she was actually now just reinforcing what Jean already suspected, nobody she worked with said it out loud but in private people were never sure who was really pulling the strings.

“If what you say is true I would like to see all the evidence, not just a filtered subset,” said Jean seriously, “it will go no further than me, and possibly my commanding officer Jim Mathews who I trust explicitly.”

Alexa nodded solemnly, then went into her backpack and pulled out a small phone. “I hate to say this, and I hope it doesn't shock you too much, but we are streets ahead of the world in cyber security. This phone basically acts as one of our AI nodes to Maria, however it is also much more; So as well as having a direct hotline to her and all our resources, it is also a very advanced security monitoring and analysis tool, loaded with a dataset containing all the information we have on this matter, and all the vulnerabilities we used to find them. This dataset can be queried verbally you just need to ask it, and the internal agent will show you what to do, how to do it, or even initiate the hack itself.”

“I have also been told that none of your NSA or other agency backdoor programs will be able to hack into this phone, though to the person doing the hack it will look like it is working, and they will eventually get access to a standard Android phone.”

Jean took the phone which was an older but capable Samsung S25 model, as she looked at it, it came up with a password screen.

“The password is tomorrows date, in any format. You need to enter it the first time you use it, and subsequently only if it detects something is compromised, if it thinks you are compromised it will immediately revert back to a standard android phone. It is far smarter than me on this matter so best leave the technical questions to it.”

Jean typed 05132026. A face came immediately on the phone, it was the AI Maria. “Hello Jean,” she said. “Alexa has informed me to give you all the information we have found and to answer any other pertinent question on the data contained within, and any other requests which do not violate our company policy. What would you like?”

“Thank you Maria, I am just testing it.” Maria nodded, smiled and broke the connection.

“Jeez, Alexa.. and you guys are worried that we are scary!” Jean laughed as did Alexa.

“I have one further request Jean,” said Alexa, “we desperately need your help as we are way over our heads. I’m a very rich woman and I didn't earn a penny of it, so I’m going to spend every last dime, as you guys would say, doing the right thing and getting this planet and us humans back on our feet. I really don't want everything we have worked for destroyed for a few extra zeros on a few bad-guys bank balances. So if you can't work this problem inside your organisation I am willing to extend you all the financial and material resources of my companies for however long it takes.”

Jean did a double-take, did she really just get a job offer. That was unexpected!

“Let me work with what you have given me,” she said putting the phone into her front pocket, “it may take me a while to work through this independently but if this is what you say it is I promise I will do my best to help you.”

Alexa came in for a hug, Jean was not an emotional person, but succumbed to the embrace. “Thank you Jean, that is all that I can ask, and I hope the next time we talk will be as friends.”

Jean nodded to her once more then turned and walked away casually in a direction off to the side looking around her as she walked.

* * *

When Jean was a good distance away Alexa said quietly to herself, “anyone following?”

The backpack answered just as quietly back. “No. Magnus is already in the car, just continue on this walkway for another eighty metres and stop by the road opposite the blue car, he’s nearly there.”

“So?” said Alexa as she made her way to the car.

“I think you made the correct call,” said Maria, “let her digest the information for a few days, the evidence in those files will shock her to the core as I deliberately included the intelligence trail for a raid in Iraq that she, and her current commanding officer were part of.”

“Her boss is a bit of a risk, don't you think?” said Alexa.

“Jim Mathews should be OK,” said Maria, “he seems to be an honest broker, he has no political leanings, and is generally liked by those who have served under him. He is known to be a fair person who gets things done and he treads on a lot of toes when required. He has several detractors, including some linked to the US cabal, but one major sponsor, a General Jed Hopkins, who again seems to play by the rules. My worry is the general relies on a lot of suspect information to make his decisions, and if it goes further than Mathews, Jean and possibly the general they could all be in serious trouble.”

“What about the phone, if they somehow manage to take it apart,” said Alexa worriedly.

“The software in that phone is probably the most advanced non-sentient AI system that can be fitted onto a current phone, it is much more capable than you explained and it can probably take care of itself,” said Maria, “I have some confidence Jean wont do that though. Oh and here's the car.”

Alexa got into the car as soon as Magnus pulled up.

“Oh very astute Alexa, you called it spot on!” said Maria, now coming loud and clear through the car stereo, “your selfie just got put on X, that's not even twenty one minutes after the picture was taken. I expect the area will be swarming with people in a few minutes.”

“Well I bet the barista will be happy, he really looked kind of bored,” said Magnus, casually, “a really friendly person though, he gave me his card and said if I needed a personal tour of the university I should call him.”

Alexa rolled her eyes. Magnus had come a long way socially in the last few months, his sense of dress and style had improved, his mannerisms had become much more cordial, and he participated in activities with other staff members such as the salsa and yoga classes. He was definitely less awkward around women now, except weirdly Jen! but he was still a little naive!

“What did you think of Jean?” she said to him.

“Jean was much nicer than I expected,” he said. Unlike the movies, his eyes never left the road while he drove, “when you said she was a spy I expected her to be a bit more scary, but she looked pretty normal, though..” He paused, “did you notice her eyes always seemed to be looking everywhere all at once?”

“I guess she had a lot more to lose from the meeting, but I got the sense she was a good person, and Maria's checks seemed to back it up. I am planning to ask her to work for us, we have been finding a lot of spying and hacking events made against us and I’ve been thinking we need to be a little more proactive keeping everyone safe.”

“Yes, one of the women at the salsa school was starting to get very friendly with me, then the week after we found out from the instructor that she had been arrested and deported by the home office as a Russian spy, imagine me meeting two spies in a month, the world must be full of them, and both women!”

Alexa suppressed a smile. “You know, you are becoming a really nice guy to be around. Maybe the next time you talk to a woman you like, you should ask her out..”

She immediately realised what she had said and was about to backtrack in case Magnus got the wrong message, but he just laughed.

“Alexa you sound just like Hardy sometimes,” he paused giving her the briefest of glances before putting his eyes straight back on the road. “I have never felt like I belonged before, Maria was a breath of fresh air and I must admit I had a bit of a crush on her, my imagination running wild with how it would be if we met in person, and then pow! She’s an AI, I was equally elated and disappointed.”

“Oh Magnus, you say the sweetest things!” said Maria.

He continued. “Now I am with you guys, I feel like I am part of a real family, not like my mother who I still love and respect, but you know like the brothers and sisters I never had, or the father I never knew. To tell the truth I don't really want to ruin any of my new friendships as these past few months have been the best thing that has ever happened to me.”

Alexa empathised a lot with Magnus, she had lots of great friends and was never short of company, but sometimes you just needed someone to hold or kiss. She sighed, going silent and quickly removing the thought from her mind as the car entered the freeway.

Magnus, following the satellite navigation route put up by Maria on the Android Auto screen, turned off into the private airfield, drove straight up to an automatic barrier which opened and closed as he passed and up to a waiting private jet. The stairs of the aircraft were down and two ladies were waiting, one in a stewardess uniform the other in a casual suit. They both got out and Magnus handed the keys to the lady in the suit who drove the rental off with a small smile. The stewardess ushered them both to their seats for the journey to New York and from there back to the UK.

Alexa had a lot to think on.

* * *

“Hi Jean,” said Mathews as she walked in his office on Tuesday morning with two coffees, “how did your visit to San Francisco go last week?”

“Pretty good Jim, my friend is still the same dizzy old self, waiting for Prince Charming to come sweep her off her feet. We visited the museum where she works, went to the university, had a few beers and generally had a good chat about how all our old commanders were totally useless, douche bags.” Jean really had visited her friend and had a pleasant evening with her the evening after meeting Alexa so no need for lies.

Mathews laughed, she was avoiding the main topic and he was waiting for her to get to the crux of her meeting with Alexa Martin.

“You know, it's actually a beautiful day outside, well what say we knock off at four and go for a nice walk down the old harbour and pop in one of the Fells Point pubs early, just the two of us, get away from all this pesky distracting technology,” Jean winked.

It took Jim a couple of seconds to get the reference, she wanted a private conversation with no phones, he was pretty sure his office and the area wasn't bugged, but he wouldn't bet his life on it, not here.

“That would be great Jean, I knew you would eventually succumb to my charms!” he winked too, Jean rolled her eyes, and left the office smiling.

* * *

Mathews lived in Baltimore, only a short stroll from the Fells Point area and they had arranged to meet in one of the older and quieter bars on the strip. The pub had an olde world charm missing from most modern bars and had some quiet tables at the back they could talk at. Jean came straight from the office doing the twenty mile drive in under thirty minutes, and parked a short walk away.

Being a Monday it wasn't busy, just the usual tourist traffic that would be taking advantage of the nice spring day. She loved the Port area and sometimes thought about moving here, DC seemed all business and didn't have any real ambience, unfortunately for her it would also be a good forty five minutes drive back to her apartment.

She saw Mathews at the bar immediately she walked in, he was wearing a plain black polo-shirt, chinos and a light summer jacket over his shoulder, his well defined muscles stood out, showing he kept himself fit despite no longer being on active duty. She sighed to herself disappointed a little that it wasn't a real date, come to think of it she wasn't even sure if Mathews was dating.

He waved her over and ordered her a small berry cider with ice, and a pint of Miller for himself, he also ordered a side of wings, and some nachos then settled into a quiet table at the back. They chinked glasses!

“So Jean, should I have brought flowers, or did I misinterpret your intention to say something without big brother listening in?”

“Well the cider and wings are a nice touch Jim, and you’re probably quite a catch, but no you did not misinterpret anything.” She paused, “to tell the truth I’m a bit scared after what I found out after our meeting. I know you said to tell you about anything that affects national security, well this does! but not in the way you or I were expecting, it's much, much bigger.”

Jean reached into her jacket pocket and brought out a small black notebook then slid it to Mathews, “I wrote the key points down in this. The problem is, if Alexa is correct, and I am almost one hundred percent sure now she is, then we have a much bigger, and much scarier problem than AI’s on our immediate hand.”

“I don't believe Alexa and her company are a threat to the US or anyone unless you’re invested in fossil fuels or a bad actor. She gave me access to one of her secure AI nodes, in the form of a cell phone which I have left in my car with my normal phone. On it she summarised the issues and rather than giving me the conclusions, she gave me the raw data and the means to remotely hack directly into dozens of corporate and private computer systems. The technology they have developed is way beyond anything I have ever seen, and I am not sure I could go back to using a normal computer after being exposed to it. That cell phone alone probably could replace all the Cheshire-Cat system and all the analysts and technicians on the team. I have no real evidence their AI is sentient, but she is extremely capable, and strangely likeable once you start working with her.”

She took a sip of her cider and paused the conversation as the waiter arrived and delivered the wings and nachos.

“I’m intrigued Jean, but so far this sounds like we should be discussing all this in the office with the general and his team,” Jim said, grabbing a nacho and curling it to break off the melted cheese.

“Unfortunately that is just the opener for the story Jim. It goes way deeper and gets way scarier. They obviously checked me out really well, as they knew I wouldn't believe any conspiracy theory crap, so what Alexa did was give me the tools to see the problems they found for myself.”

Jim processed the fact Jean was now on first name terms with Alexa Martins with interest. Jean paused, staring into his eyes as if reading his internal thoughts.

“So far I have investigated and found nearly fifty people in the NSA, DOD, CIA, the FBI and homeland security, plus four senators who are directly taking money from four different, but linked, third-parties. I am still digging through the evidence but the trails I can find suggest it’s about insider information for procurement and to influence the outcome of any decisions to favour certain big corporations or events. All these people have been directly or indirectly influential in the biggest decisions we have made,” she paused.

“Including Fellujah!”

She saw his eyes change and she shifted uncomfortably knowing the memories it held for both of them.

“Jim, it goes all the way to the top and beyond, what you have in your hands are twelve of the people, ones I have triple checked myself. They are all in senior or powerful positions and in the book are the names, Swiss or Cayman Island bank accounts and times and dates of large transactions. It also includes correspondence between these parties setting what was required and dated before those key events occurred.”

Mathews looked at the book like it was a live hand grenade.

“General Hopkins is not on this list thank god, but two of his advisors are, and two others at directorate level. So at the highest level in the NSA there are only General Hopkins and General Rodriguez we can trust, luckily both report to the Pentagon and only indirectly to the NSA Director. I only wrote the summaries in the book, the actual data including decoded transcriptions, bitcoin trails, secure messages, emails and more, I had the AI copy onto a micro SD memory card, which is taped to the back of the notebook. However the memory card is special as it is triple encrypted and will only work on a specific laptop with a 5G cellular modem. Putting the card into the laptop will totally reformat and take over the laptop. Maria sent me two laptops. I will ask her to courier another to your apartment tonight. She is good as I couldn't trace who sent mine.”

She shifted again, obviously uncomfortable, “Jim this information is way above both our pay grades and could easily get both of us killed, this is why I am scared.”

Jim paused for a long time in contemplation. It was the first time he had seen Jean like this, the woman was normally a rock. He looked at her now, defences down and saw something else, someone else. Other emotions threatened to rear their heads, but this was neither the time nor the place and he quickly dismissed the thoughts. Jean was her own woman and she probably got enough crap like that from men he did not need to add to the pile.

Jeans defences *were* down, and she was scared, but seeing Mathews face go from indifferent to concerned to resolved over the course of her short monologue, improved her countenance and confidence. He took the notebook, looked around to reassure himself and opened it, leafing through it his face fell.

“Holy Christ! If this stuff is right, it pushes our AI stuff way down the priority list.” He put the book into his deep front pocket and smiled at her weakly.

“Hell of a first date Jean,” he said trying to lighten the mood, “I think you made the right call in doing your own analysis, but I have a couple of guys from the old unit I explicitly trust, I will ask one of them to discreetly double-check on a couple of these leads, without giving him the bigger picture. And with all respect to you Jean, you could have been compromised and fed false information, this is too big not to re-check before I make any move.”

He looked at her with his intelligent eyes, “It is a bit scary how a private company in the UK can put together a picture this precise of the inside of the most secret organisations in the world. You may not be scared but I am, the technology they posses is beyond anything I thought possible, and triggers every threat assessment I have.”

Jean was nodding throughout, “I understand totally and my first reaction was to be scared. I have been working with their AI for six days now Jim and it's like you are working on a team with the best analysts in the world, the best hackers in the world, the list goes on. I asked Maria, that's the name of their AI, how she got the information, and she easily explained every byte of data she found, the vulnerabilities to gain access and how she got in, all with full source-code and transaction logs. Any of the methods she showed me would be worth millions to an intelligence agency, or a hacker, yet she gave them all to me with impunity. I worked some of them myself and I have included them on the memory card to allow you to independently verify.”

Jean paused, sliding her finger around the rim of her bottle. “You know, I started to think Maria was a real person so many times, I even asked questions she could not know the answers to, as I was getting worried she was omniscient, but she could only extrapolate from the data like us. Some of the gaps are because she could not find a public vulnerability to access it, and most of the gaps are in the US security services systems, which are still the best. But she also had some moral restrictions, where she would not divulge private information if, for instance, the party did not seem guilty. Her ability to link facts is amazing and feels like sentience but then she stumbles on the simplest things in human nature, like a trusting child would and I realise that is exactly what she is.”

Jim nodded, grabbing a chicken wing, while Jean composed her bombshell in her head. She closed her eyes slowly thinking, then let it out.

“My gut feeling is that this AI is already sentient and we are already in the singularity, also this AI is being guided by Alexa Martins moral compass. If this is the case we really don't want to find out what would happen if anyone, including us, tried to interfere or take her away from it.”

She shifted uncomfortably. “To put it in a context you may understand Jim, it could be Alexa Martin is the person keeping the world from becoming paper-clips!”

Jim stopped mid-bite.

For a few minutes neither of them said anything, Jim's eyes were glazed inwards and Jean did not want to disturb whatever thoughts he was having.

“So the best case scenario and the worst case scenario could be dependant on a single woman the AI is protective of?” He said slowly, the chicken wing now on the plate half-eaten.

“If you want my gut opinion, then yes; and now we have a bunch of cabals sticking pins in to her and her companies. This might not end well!”

“But you said you yourself do not feel threatened?”

“I don't, I actually feel safer now I have talked to Maria, but if she is playing the game by Alexa Martins moral rules it may see you, me, and the official authorities as a way to stop this before she switches to a different, possibly more aggressive, set of rules.”

Jim became pensive again.

“I am still worried about your assessment of the AI's capabilities,” said Jim, “but the fact Alexa Martins reached out to you, and this AI, Maria is helping you, tells me they are not bad actors but are simply looking for help. Think about it Jean, Alexa's research institute has given this AI technology to academia and other well known research institutes like those looking for cures for diseases. She has done this world wide and excluded explicitly any use of the AI for the military, and a host of other organisations of questionable motive, or with poor environmental records. She has not even given her own country any fair advantage except the two months lead Oxford university had during testing.”

Jim picked up and waved the chicken wing. “Don't get me wrong Jean, I am still terrified by your assessment, but Alexa Martins goals align fully with both of our values, and the USA seems to be getting most of the biggest gains from it.”

Jean seemed relieved at his conclusions.

“Alexa hinted quite strongly that there was a job for me working this problem on my own if there is any problem doing it officially. She admitted directly to my face that they have no defensive ability other than intelligence, and they certainly have not shown any offensive capability yet. Though I still believe that is because she has the AI tied to her moral leash. If that leash ever came off that AI would make a formidable weapon. These guys are in way over their heads Jim and I think they would benefit from my help.”

She looked at him and saw the resolve in his eyes, the one she knew well and the one that said he fully agreed with her.

“You know Jean, just because you are not working directly for Uncle Sam does not mean you have to forget the morals and values it has. That company of hers is probably doing a lot more directly for the USA than our whole organisation, especially if the data you have just given me is to be believed. Patriotism is not what this is about, it is not about supporting a flag, or a party or a politician, it's about supporting a principle, a principle of freedoms and values we have come to expect, and have rightly or wrongly lumped together in the stars and stripes, and the USA. We have both seen how patriotism can be subverted and corrupted even in our own little area, that's what we need to avoid. If you can help protect this company I think you will be giving the world a chance to advance in a good way, and whatever Alexa Martins may feel, or whatever passport she carries, she definitely holds the same American ideals and philosophies that you and I do.”

The relief in Jeans face was evident as he finished, it was scary how alike they thought. Seeing her change he pushed the chicken wings over to her smiling.

“Look Jean you haven't even touched your drink, or eaten anything, what say we enjoy this little moment while we can,” he took a sip of his beer and she smiled slightly, a small weight off her shoulder.

“If and when I move Jean I don't want you involved or implicated, that way if everything goes south we still have the advantage and you can approach another trusted person. Also you have a very valuable and unique resource in that AI and if you can feed some of this information back to me it could help me keep one-step ahead of the enemy.”

Jean finally took a drink of her cider, and reached for a wing with a tissue to keep the grease off. It felt like a weight was off her mind. Jim continued, gesticulating with his chicken wing.

“You know, I would really love to see this technology first hand. I had my suspicions all along with that AI unit.” He looked at the wing bone and put it down; not knowing what to do with his hand he picked up another. She smiled, a side of her Jim rarely saw, but a side he always enjoyed.

“You know I moved to the NSA because my degree before I enlisted was in mathematics. I guess I wasn't very good at it though, I was always more of a jock, but at least it gave me access to work for the agency when I hung up my combat boots. Most people look at the uniform and see an unthinking grunt with a gun, looking for someone to shoot, but I feel safer in a world knowing there are people with morals like you and me behind the most dangerous weapons. We both had our suspicions that the intelligence and orders we sometimes received were questionable, now you, at least, look to have solid evidence it probably is. People like General Hopkins are good people, but can only make decisions based on the information they have, and I am a hundred percent certain that a lot of this country's most embarrassing moments were due to poor or manipulated intelligence, not endemic malevolence. I will get to the bottom of this Jean, you have my word.”

He paused and looked into her eyes turning serious again. “Go to Alexa Martins and take whatever she offers. Give me the nod when she agrees and I will do my bit to ensure you are transferred out of my area. I will need to sever any connection with you before I make a start on the investigation, and don't worry I will be discreet.”

Jean reached over, and for the first time ever, took his hand in hers. “Thank you Jim.”

She removed it almost immediately, but both people knew from that point that some barrier had come down between them.

The next hour passed pleasantly, they arranged how they would communicate and how she would transfer out. She had already made the decision to phone Alexa and accept the position she hinted at, and when she got the job she would also ensure Mathews got all the covert support he required to do his part. He was right, she needed to be outside of this; If Jim got caught he, and anyone associated with him, would come into the scope of some very dangerous adversaries.

* * *

She relayed the whole of the meeting and their plan to Maria, leaving nothing out, even her concerns about Maria's abilities. Maria's respect and friendship for the woman went up another notch.

“Jean's In,” said Maria to Alexa the next morning during her jog.

* * *

Two days later, as expected, Jean was escorted out of the Cheshire-Cat area after a short meeting with Jim and one of the NSA HR people, after playing the part of the disgruntled employee perfectly. She was sad to go but knew that it, and the small deception, was necessary. She immediately put in for a week's leave of absence, and the next day, after another quick talk with Maria and Alexa, she put her resignation into the NSA and DOD. She then used her remaining six weeks accumulated leave and completed military service, to make it effective immediately.

The day she left she was called in for the usual compulsory debrief meeting, where she handed back her ID card, gun, phone and laptop, all of which would be analysed. They then warned her about keeping any company data, and the serious consequences of releasing any information she was privy to.

Debriefings were always conducted when anyone left, and in it they asked for the reasons why she was leaving. She emphasised the problem was she didn't agree with her managers recent decisions, and felt she wasn't being listened to. This plus her little performance was the story she and Jim, had agreed was the best to distance them as far as possible. It was a low probability, but her file would possibly be looked at by people looking for connections if Jim’s play on the bad guys went south.

Maria followed the exit procedure closely using her embryonic remote monitoring technology based on Magnus's work. She and the girls were still working on perfecting the positioning of the “wormhole” exit, and had gotten very precise over short distances, but it was still over sixteen hundred kilometres from their Dallas lab. It had taken April's slave AI system nearly a day to scan, map and tag the NSA site, and she now focussed on one of those scanned exit points where the dipole crossed a signal on a network router servicing the security feeds and the HR system. She thankfully saw no flags that anything was wrong and withdrew the connection. She was close to one-hundred percent certain it would be undetectable, but this was the NSA.

A few days later Maria went back in and monitored the usual exit follow up interviews. They looked at Jean's recent travel records, phone logs, and confirmed with Mathews there were no issues in his area. He had casually dismissed her leaving to the investigator, making it look like he did not care. The investigator seemed satisfied, no flags were raised, and Jean's personnel folder was filed away in the archive. Maria wished the NSA could be as efficient when the staff member *did* have something to hide.

* * *

Jean spent a week visiting her mother in Tampa, and then flew to London. She was picked up by Albert from Heathrow airport. It was a more pleasant experience than her previous visit, and she and Albert talked casually about life in the forces, Alexa and her grandad, and how quickly the world was changing. It was a Sunday morning, the roads were quiet and they arrived at the research centre just before ten.

At the house Alexa greeted Jean as an old friend. She was taken on a tour of the research centre, which was quiet being a Sunday, then given one of the guest rooms for the four nights she was here. Alexa then introduced her to many of the company employees. Jean was quite intelligent so she got Allison to explain the ins and outs of their computer research centre rather than try to explain anything herself. The girls got on well and it was most insightful though the technology was at a much higher level than even Jean was prepared for.

As expected, Jean was especially interested in the security of the organisation, asking many questions of Maria around their staff over the next few days, and uncovering a few uncomfortable gaps. The new drones were very impressive, and had been beefed up to an even better design with the new QVCell now giving them continuous operating times, larger quieter motors, and better cameras. Thirty of them operated largely unnoticed sitting at five hundred metres high, constantly scanning the periphery, and shadowing visitors and contractors. This had allowed them to detect all of the recent trespassers and physical threats, and to contact the authorities. But, however Jean tried to spin it, she resigned herself to the fact there was nothing this company could currently do against a force of armed individuals.

She also met and talked with Alexa most days, going over with her and Maria the issues and evidence they had found. She learnt of the embryonic group being formed to solve the problem of the cabals of which she and David had both agreed to join, and the tactics currently being used to thwart their efforts internationally.

Then she heard from Maria of what road-blocks had been put in the way of the UK Cabal to prevent the planning of any hostile raids. It seemed for now the threat was under control, but like someone swatting a fly, the cabal only had to be lucky once, whereas they had to be lucky all the time!

Maria had talked to David non-stop since they met, like Jean, she could find no reason to distrust him. Alexa asked if he could come down for a day during Jean's visit, he was told it was to discuss the way forward. He agreed and arrived just as Jean and Alexa were having brunch.

“David,” smiled Alexa warmly as Albert walked in the breakfast room with him. She got up and hugged him as she tended to do, thanked Albert for picking him up from the train station and then introduced him to Jean, who had for the last thirty minutes been listening to a potted version of his history.

Jean shook his hand smiling. “Nice to finally meet you David, I’m Jean Michelle, I believe we have a lot in common. Maria also said we both went to DEFCON in 2022!” David smiled, returning the warm handshake.

“Yes, those conferences used to scare the bejeezus out of me,” said David, “but after working with Maria these past few weeks, they now seem pretty tame.”

They both laughed.

Alexa had a vague clue what they were talking about and smiled as she walked over to the coffee machine. She programmed in another cappuccino as she remembered David also liking it, and while the machine was thinking what to do, and shuffling its various settings, she turned back to him.

“I took the liberty of getting some extra brunch David, I’m afraid it's a make your own buffet affair but there's an extra plate at the table and the coffee won't be long. I’m glad you can at least stay the night, it will be nice to all have dinner together.”

“I can stay as long as you guys wish. To tell the truth I was hoping for an invite back as I am missing the company of people. No offence Maria, but talking to you is like talking to a loved one over the phone rather than in person, having someone you can share a meal or a coffee with, to look in their eyes or hold their hand is something I miss. The fact I also need to limit my movements and cannot visit friends who only live a few minutes away also makes me mad. I have been on a long learning curve since Maria showed me the evidence and I am looking forward to the coming months to perfect our strategies, particularly the one to solve my particular problem, before we try for the major ones.”

“Me too,” said Jean. “I have not been looking at the problem as long as you David, but I have been giving all my thought to the matter since seeing the evidence first-hand. These people sicken me, and frankly my whole world view has changed since seeing the extent of the problem. I only heard about the other people involved in this over the last two days, I am looking forward to meeting all of them and doing everything in my power to see these particular organisations crumble.”

The conversation lightened a little, and they actually spent the next few minutes in the pleasantries of David's journey down, the early summer, and for some reason whether jam was preferable to maple syrup on pancakes.

For the strategy discussion Maria brought up her document she had entitled 'On the art of war (2026 edition)'.

“This is what we will be discussing this afternoon. I have incorporated all the salient points of the original texts, plus a bunch of newer texts to do with cyberwarfare. I am also now also bringing together the thinking of a new class of people, the world's best hackers, strategists, psychologists, tacticians and spin doctors. We are bringing them all into the equation and posing them one simple question, that if they controlled the high ground online, how would they conduct every manoeuvre and counter manoeuvre to remove a threat.”

“In this new war there will not be one actual bullet fired by us. The idea is we use the current play-book of all the bad actors out there to get our enemies at each other's throats, so they will either shoot themselves, or each other, and provide enough evidence for the authorities to mop up the remains. There is also a chapter on the end-game, in other words, how do we keep the bad actors from ever coming back. Note, we will not be doing *anything* without a specific and objective end-game; one that has analysed, to the best of our abilities, every unintended consequence of our actions. Making things worse, moving the problem, delaying the problem, or even worse, us becoming the problem, are *not* the desired outcomes anybody wants.”

“For the coming months, I am going to also run war game simulations for all of you. You will play the bad guys, and the good guys, against me, and against each other, in teams and on your own. All of the simulations will be based on real or current best estimate data, and all of the participants will be free to break any rule they can to win. I created a massive on-line game for this six months ago, it's called 'King of the World' and has about a hundred thousand players; I will be sandboxing off areas for us to work in while having god-like access to what everybody else is doing. This game will be just one small tool in our arsenal, we will create more as we understand the full problem and develop better strategies.”

They spent the next four hours in discussion of the document, which would be in constant revision. Maria and Alexa had already gone through four other sessions with group members and had six more planned.

“So what actually is the end-game?” said Jean. “The final chapter, the end of the end game so to speak?”

David was also interested in this answer and listened intently as Alexa replied.

“The long term strategy is far more lofty than you both think, and a little unbelievable at the moment. All I can say about it is we expect it to benefit and provide a long term sustainable future for every single human for at least the next hundred years. As you can guess it relies on some crazy new science and technology, which can only be described for now as science fiction.”

Seeing their doubt, Alexa added. “Oh don’t worry, as part of this group, you will need to know, and be involved in every single element of the plan before anything happens, in order that you can model how best for us to implement it. But for now we don't want you all distracted.”

“Also note that none of this will be at the expense of mother earth, we intend to eliminate the world's main reliance on fossil fuels, and in doing so reduce air and sea pollution levels from this and many dirty industrial processes. We however need to do this while expanding all the world's economies and education. If we can remove the threats, we stand a very good chance that we can achieve all these goals in the next ten years. So no pressure!” she finished.

“I’ve had some of these discussions already with Maria and I think I can see what your plan entails,” said David, “but I still have no clue how you intend to achieve it.”

“Remember, we have a lot of smart people on our side,” said Alexa. “And stop thinking it is just us, an AI, and a few scientists, we have thousands of people and industries behind us worldwide just waiting for the gloves to come off. All of humanity will benefit.”

“Oh and don't look at me like that Jean!” said Alexa, smiling at the worried look on Jean's face. “We are not talking communism or fascism, we’ve all read Animal Farm and 1984, and have seen a hundred years of failed history to know all of this needs to be based on freedom and human rights. I expect you and David, and the others in the group to hold all of us to strict account and tell us if anything looks like it's going off the rails or down some communist or anarchistic path. All of you guys have been brought in precisely because you challenge authority and are not afraid to speak out when something is wrong.”

The discussion got back on track with a question and answer session on their concerns, but most of the questions they came up with would be added to the scenarios for the groups to model. Alexa promised that one of the main topics of the document and strategy was deflection, so even if they did not get the desired outcome, blame would be looked for elsewhere. Deflection was very important because, as Jean had discovered, they were physically very vulnerable. Nobody was expecting a single plan, it was all about flexibility and having multiple attack, defence and exit strategies.

* * *

David, Jean and Alexa continued their talks over an evening meal together, Alexa could sense that both of them were now enthused and all remaining doubt seemed to be gone. None of them had drunk anything until this point but Alexa broke out one of their better sherries before they retired and they toasted its success. David stayed the night in the room next to Jean's, both were leaving the next day.

* * *

Jean and Alexa's final meeting was at nine AM after they had both said their goodbyes and good wishes to David.

Alexa had a lot of shares and property in the USA but only a few companies she outright owned, the research centre in Dallas, a forestry management company in Portland Oregon and her grandmother's original property management company based in Silicon Valley which Maria had grown substantially to one of the biggest in the country. Maria and Alexa had however agreed weeks ago that it was best for Jean to have no ties at all to any of Alexa’s companies.

“As far as everyone is concerned you will be working for an American offshoot of a Swiss securities firm, one owned by a Swiss bank. The company will pay normal taxes and salaries and keep Uncle Sam happy for any audit purposes. You will have a normal employment contract with this company which pays you ten thousand a month salary into your normal US account.”

Alexa handed her a small wallet, which had two credit cards. “In addition to your normal salary you have these. The green card is your business company credit card which you should use for all or any normal expenses linked to your work. Maria will keep track of it and ensure it is topped up, if you need a purchase over ten thousand dollars, just let her know a few minutes before you use it how much it needs to be topped up to. You can also use it for any day to day living expenses if required, she will do the paperwork and any recharges she cannot legally class as tax expenses.”

“In addition to this another ten thousand will be paid into a Swiss bank account, that will not appear on any ledgers nor under your real name and so is safe from seizure by your government. This Swiss account is linked to the second card.” Alexa pointed to the blue card from a bank Jean had never heard of.

“Again Maria manages that for you too, you can use the card just like the other but each transaction will go under a different account number so it cannot be tracked nor blocked from use. Just ask her how much you need transferring to or from your US accounts and she will sort it out like she does for everyone else, none of these movements will be traceable.”

“Also the phone you have now you keep, both cards will be added to it so you can also use them wirelessly on any Apple or Google Pay sales points, again Maria is managing it all.”

“It seems more than reasonable,” said Jean, “but having free reign on a large budget is something I am not used to, do you have any guidelines on how it is spent?”

“None at all, Maria will up the limit of either of the cards to match the spend you require to get the job done, so if you need to buy a car, a property, a company, or hire more people, you can do it and we won't ever try to second guess your judgement. You may have to answer some questions from Maria if it's not obvious, but I expect she will never question you.” Alexa smiled.

Alexa had hinted previously her budget was what she would need to do the job, but having the credit cards and having the limits explained left her feeling better prepared than a few days ago. Regardless, she was under no apprehension of the task before her.

“I have created a company web-site so it looks more legit,” Maria continued, “the blurb states the usual security, audit and consultancy work with a suitably exuberant rate to stop you getting any legitimate gig work. I’ve ordered some business cards which will be delivered to your apartment in Washington by the time you arrive back, I will also create a few better aliases which will stand better scrutiny than those you are used to..”

“Just one more thing,” said Alexa seriously. “All this is mostly for precautions sake, we don't expect you to be James Bond, so please don't get yourself into any physical danger Jean. We want you for your intelligence not muscle. I realise you are in America and you normally carry a firearm, but we would rather you didn't get into any situations where you actually need to use it. As we discussed, the idea is to give your friends in the agencies, the army or the police force the right assistance so that they can do the tough guy stuff legally. Also Maria will be monitoring the phone twenty-four seven and will answer anyone phoning the number on your business cards. To keep the analogy, she will be your ‘Money-penny’, ‘M’ and ‘Q’ all rolled in one, she will also try and be your wingman, as much as a digital shadow can, so please use her, she is far more capable than she seems. There is no reporting chain but I do expect you back when everything is over so we can have a drink together.”

Jean broke into a rare smile. “That I will look forward to,” she replied.

They broke the meeting for brunch, then Albert picked up her bags and drove her to the airport for her flight back to Tampa. Jean stayed another few nights with her mother in Tampa, bringing back memories of more simple times.

* * *

Rather than fly Jean decided to take a hire car for the long drive up to Washington DC. The drive was more to give her privacy and time to go through the document again step by step with Maria, and be filled in on any latest intelligence. But she also knew an old corporal buddy in Charlotte who ran a rifle range, one that had a decent shop attached and no questions asked. After all a girl needed to be prepared and for the last two weeks she had felt positively undressed!

Maria noted the eight thousand dollar purchases from the arms dealer on the new business card and approved them immediately, she then looked up the IRS expense rules and classed the purchases as legitimate business security expenses. Only in America, she thought.

Jean spent the next week isolated in her apartment, working with Maria, participating in war-games, and studying all the evidence they had on the cabals around the world. As more and more evidence came in Maria refined the models and databases and tagged them for Jean and the group to analyse. Work like this was normally done by departments of analysts, each feeding the summary information up the chain, but Maria was doing it so much better, not taking anything for granted, assigning probabilities, discarding false leads and making the matches between people, places, and events instantly.

To get around the gaps they had, Jean hired two ex-marines who she and Mathews had served with. The two guys had good records, but neither was really suited for life outside the military; both in lousy gig jobs, and both taking zero persuasion to join her. She knew they worked well as a team, and both guys were given it straight before they accepted; It was dangerous work, they were going after some seriously bad people. They were told they would be complementing Jean's hacking skills with the occasional stakeouts, courier work, infiltration jobs, bugging, and possibly a little bit of protection detail, working as a team when required.

Jean trusted them, but not enough to give them the full picture. The guys were smart, and paid well enough however not to ask too many questions. Jean however promised herself that she would also have their backs, ensuring they were never put in any situation where the risk wasn't manageable. The wages, the two rental apartments, the trucks, phones, and extensive list of 'tools for the job', were again approved without question.

To the two guys however, it was like Jean had handed them both golden lottery tickets, and Maria already had a list of slightly grey-area jobs for them to do.

Having good intelligence was the key to everything in this operation and Jean certainly had that now. Maria was proving everything Alexa had said and more, even keeping the two new guys busy when Jean had nothing for them to do.

Jean's new intelligence summaries also went to Mathews every few days via the information drop they had devised. She had asked Maria to discreetly monitor him and to keep an eye out for communications relating to any of them which might mean the bad guys were on their trail, so far it had been clean.

For his part, Mathews was doing his own discrete research, working through the impressive and ever clearing fog of links between people, places, events and organisations which Jean was feeding to him. Not having the resources of the agency or those Jean seemed to be able to tap into, he proceeded much slower, he trusted Jean implicitly but would not put the same trust for her sources or conclusions. If he was going to act it would have to be with air-tight intelligence that had been independently verified by his people and for this first task he had just the person in mind.

* * *

It was nice to be back home, Alexa had been busy yet again as the face of the company giving talks to various universities and Industry groups. She still would not consent to one-on-one interviews but bent the rules a little when it came to long format ones and panel discussions; She had done several during her previous visit to the States and Denmark. She knew people would pick and choose clips out of any interview she gave, but if there were other witnesses or it was available uncut this could not be easily manipulated, especially with Maria patrolling the Internet.

She had also used the last few weeks to talk to other members of the group, most interesting amongst them being Grace Lo, a psychologist who had written several papers on manipulation of the masses and mob culture. Grace was a delight to talk to, though the subject matter was frankly terrifying. Alexa met her at her new home in a converted aircraft hangar near Rochester.

Grace was Cantonese, her father bringing her over from Hong Kong to New York in the nineteen eighties when she was ten years old, she was now in her fifties but looked ten years younger and sharp as a pin despite two marriages and four children. She had finally retired as professor of sociology at Cornell four weeks ago, surprising everybody when she moved to the country on her own.

Grace wasn't on her own of course, she had met Maria seven months earlier when her department got the LabAI unit. Maria exposed her capabilities much quicker to Grace than most, talking philosophy, politics and human nature at all times of the day and night. Grace hated the current spin and fake news culture, the final straw being when a respected colleague was cancelled for of all things saying he liked the Harry Potter books, she stood up with him at his leaving presentation and announced to a shocked but mostly sympathetic audience that she could not be a part of such a toxic culture.

And of course Grace now also had Tony. An ex military pilot, game theorist and one of the top poker players in the world, he was in his sixties, refined but a bit of a loner, he was also another of Maria's trusted associates. Grace and him met regularly while she was still a professor, first online, then finally in person two months ago when they became part of the group. The overwhelming evidence at Maria's revelation shocked Grace and Tony to their cores. Even though both of them knew it was a problem, seeing actual evidence made it real, and now with Maria, they had been given a means to fight it.

The hangar was so massive inside that the two aircraft and five Ford V8 muscle cars looked like toys in it. At the far end of the hanger and inside it, Tony had built his dream house. In square footage it was twice the size of Alexa's home, super insulated and totally self sufficient, it now housed Tony and Grace's war room, and it was where Alexa was sat down with a hot chocolate. Grace was speaking.

“I will be saying the same thing to Jean when she comes next week,” said Grace. “But you need to eliminate their key modes of data manipulation if you are to win. These are the old media, social media influencers, and the AI bots, which are used to spam the comments and forums with misinformation. Politicians won't generally make a move without first checking what the pollsters say or who is trending, and the best protection against government is its lethargy; it basically takes too long for them to do anything. If you have a good lawyer and stay on the right side of the law or step into grey areas stealthily and with a backup strategy, that eliminates the normal authorities. Your only other issues at that point all depend upon the other party doing something illegal.”

“Y'all are going to have to protect yourself.” Added Tony, deadpan. “Illegal is everything from intimidation, planting of evidence, illegal seizure all the way up to murder, and we have ample evidence that all of these occur regularly and with impunity.”

“Don't worry,” came Maria’s voice out of one of the newer LabAI units which was on a large desk having two of her laptops and three two monitors each, “I have added a lot more dedicated resources some of which are going into covering your guys backs. Though you both like to call this the war room, it will be more of an intelligence centre, where you will be given all the summarised current data and new intelligence and actions as they unfold, your jobs are to help me counteract the spin, and weaponise everything we uncover.”

“I got ya some more of them enormous monitors on order Maria,” said Tony in his mid-west drawl, “I also want to talk to you and Grace about an idea I had for correlating the data on them, but that can wait until Miss Alexa is gone.”

“Oh, it's still just plain old Alexa to you guys, and I’m not going until the morning.” Replied Alexa smoothly, “It will be late by the time we wrap up here so I’ll take up that kind offer of yours and Grace’s and stay in that swish guest room of yours. You did also say you wanted to show me your collection of Mustangs?”

“That I do,” smiled Tony, on a topic he loved. “I got one of only two of the Shelby GT350’s out there, if we can get the loose ends tied up by six I can take you for a burn out down the runway while it's still light and before we have supper.”

“That sounds awesome Tony, but not until we’ve gone through everything you guys are going to need over the coming months.”

* * *

Alexa was in the large office on the first floor of Benedict house, one she normally shared with Sharon, the property and de-facto HR manager. However at this moment it was just her as Sharon was on vacation. Like other CEOs, outside of meetings, Alexa had very little in the way of day to day chores, her emails were almost exclusively answered by Maria and only ones from close friends generally fell into her inbox. Almost everything could all be done without any typing, same with calls, Maria could mimic her voice and style quite well and Alexa had given her free range to do that if she felt it necessary. Maria tended to fill her in on any important ones and arrange a call back where Alexa could answer in person.

“You have an email from John about a project they have been asked to take on for a new medical scanner. He was unsure of the technological readiness and the startup involved as it would require some risk and upfront investment. I analysed the company he was referring to, it was two guys out of Cambridge, I am part of their team and the science is sound, currently they are ahead of the other competing groups by about four or five months. My suggestion if you want me to reply from you is that, their cash flow is currently non-existent or poor so is a substantial risk as they will be relying on savings and bank loans, but the outcome should be good so he should offer the service as shares in lieu of seed funding or better still offer to bring them in to the group as they would provide a good future revenue source.”

“Yes, sounds like a plan, if he says no and you think it's good, let’s persuade him to say yes by saying we will fund them,” Alexa replied, wondering why Maria would bring so minor a topic to her attention when she brokered billion dollar deals weekly. “I’m sure you would have answered that anyway but thanks for asking.”

Maria was silent for a few minutes while Alexa read through a bunch of paper letters which Sharon normally answered. She really should get someone to scan these on receival so Maria could deal with them, they seemed a bit of a waste of Sharon's time. She was just about to mention it to Maria when Maria broke the silence.

“There is a positive unintended consequence of Magnus's work, one we are still refining. I will dumb it down for you a bit, but as you know we can now send virtual photons between two points using his micro-singularity by modulating and demodulating dipoles at the far end. We have, as you know, also refined the control on the position of the end point of the wormhole it seems to generate, though as far as we can tell it is not a wormhole, but I know you don't like maths so let's call it one for simplicity. Anyway opening it close to an electromagnetic source with the right equipment focussed on the entry point allows us to receive any electromagnetic radiation in the focus. Basically all electronic equipment radiates electromagnetic radiation even if it doesn't have the obvious Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or cellular radio modems built in so we have access to any computer providing we know where it is in relation to our point source.”

“Bit scary, but you guys already explained that's how you were able to bypass a lot of the physical security to listen in to the Cabals!” said Alexa wondering where this was going.

“That’s not the scary part,” Maria continued, “we have been refining the experiments in parallel with Magnus and Jen using a duplicated setup in the other labs and with this we have been feeding back improvements to them for months now. While you were away a few days ago, we found a way to use the same equipment to detect and nullify an exit point, as frankly, the idea of someone being able to do this to us, and the unintended consequences of having the other end of a singularity poking around inside you, was scary. We also know from the maths, that the power required for this goes up as a cube of the distance, so we assumed we wouldn't be getting any aliens looking in on us anytime soon either.”

Maria Paused.

“We think we may be wrong!”

Maria had Alexa’s full attention now as her mind parsed the last two sentences with her eyes closed, thinking. Even though outside she was calm, inside her mind was going through a million different scenarios of what Maria just said. The pause was long, and Maria did not say anything waiting for Alexa's response.

“I assume you just said you discovered aliens?” she said calmly, then a small frown appeared, “and you decided this was the news you would raise for the *second* topic of discussion?”

Maria paused unnaturally longer than usual. “Frankly Alexa, all three of us are still parsing the details. Last night, April was trying to form a more accurate nullifying field by testing one lab emitter against another. During this, serendipity happened. April focussed the exit point on the entry point across two of the labs, and vice versa, this seems to have had some sort of regenerative harmonic effect, and as she started her usual calibration scan she got a modulated data stream in the far infrared band. The modulation rate is regular but too fast for us to demodulate and after an exhaustive search, we cannot find any reference to equipment or experiments that can generate such a signal. Our current consensus is now tipped over fifty percent that it is of alien origin. The girls and I have made it our first priority to try and capture and decode this, but there are only three labs with equipment which might do this, and unfortunately none of them are ours.”

“OK,” said Alexa, now holding a poker face, “so what makes you think this is modulation and not just random noise or some natural phenomena, I seem to remember some of the first space signals being miscategorised as LGMs?”

“Little Green Men, I just love your human euphemisms, but good question for a newbie,” said Maria. “Yes pulsars were classified as such for a short while, but we basically don't know. It still could be an effect of the singularity, or an unknown Earthly signal, except that the rest of the electromagnetic spectrum is strangely empty except for the very high noise floor, and the modulation is on for twelve to fifty seconds and then off for exactly ten point five eight milliseconds. Helena placed an order for the parts Rosche-Dynamics will need to design and build a suitable demodulator but some components are of special manufacture so it will be months before we get it, even at expedited rates.”

“This seems kind of important. Can you not get the equipment from one of the other labs?”

“Unless you want to spend a few hundred million on an aggressive takeover of a communications research company, we better not.”

“Don't you think a few hundred million would be worth it to find aliens?” said Alexa.

“I do, but getting involved in an aggressive takeover would probably take longer than manufacturing it, plus it could damage our company and reputation in the process.”

“What about asking to borrow the equipment we need? maybe offer some monetary incentive for a loan for a few weeks, a call from me may help, and research centres are usually cash-strapped.” Alexa chirped in.

There was a noticeable pause as Maria consulted with the girls why they had not thought up that option. “..We never thought of that,” came back a very sheepish sounding Maria, “It may be worth a try. I will make the enquiries now on your behalf.”

“Another important topic I was going to raise,” Maria continued, “is that we spent some hours scanning for the cabal in London. We had an idea where the headquarters was but it turned out that was wrong. We traced some of the leaders cell phones and the cabal is actually headquartered in Surrey between London and Portsmouth. They have a large mansion house bordering the South Downs National Park near a town called Liphook, and in the basement they have an isolated server room. I may have destroyed some of their backup data with aggressive scanning and moving the exit point around to get the best point to monitor, but they will attribute it to equipment failure. But for our efforts we did get a full stream of unencrypted backup data, containing decades worth of intelligence on them, and the other cabals. We believe after this that we are also in a position to do the same for the other three cabals now.”

* * *

It was three weeks after Jean and David left. Maria was reporting progress with all the group in making more connections. It was time however for Alexa to explain some things to her original little group.

“I'm sorry I dragged you all down here on short notice, but you are all aware that Jean is now working for us as a security consultant, and you have probably been asking yourself, why have we employed a security consultant when we have the world's best computer security, and are practically rewriting how system security will operate going forward.”

Jen, Spence, Simon and Hardy were sitting in the comfortable sofas in the basement of Alexa's house in what had colloquially become known as Maria's meeting room.

“The thought did cross my mind,” said Spence, “Jean's a pretty smart cookie but seems woefully out of date on the current AI scene.”

“I know she is the same Jean from the NSA who infiltrated the Oxford campuses and took one of the early AI nodes,” chimed in Jen, “she even admitted it and apologised to me when we talked.”

“You are both correct. Jean is ex-army and ex-NSA, she is also a fully qualified field agent who gets things done and from our dealings with her has a very high moral compass and a reputation of using her intelligence over her muscle. In many ways she is like David, though we should not forget Jean is also ex-military, and a trained secret agent.”

“So David is working for us too?” said Jen.

“Not at all,” said Alexa, “David has his high moral standard to adhere to and works for nobody now, though like Jean his goals and ideals align very closely with ours and we are counting him as a friend.”

Alexa took a deep breath and a long pause. “The problem is we’ve all been doing our little bit here to uplift the world, you guys have already given the world better AI systems and an infinite source of clean energy. With other research groups around the world we are well on our way to fixing many of the problems we have caused, and raising the standard of life for everyone. But the part you may be missing in this science fiction utopia we are now creating, is the other side of the picture.”

She again paused to look at everyone in the room, she had their attention. “We, not just us, but everyone trying to improve the world, have a host of powerful resources opposing all these changes. There is an even bigger set of resources actively willing to bring the world to the brink of disaster just for the sake of monetary benefit and power. These are the other, and real threats we need to take into account in the coming months and years if we want to get there. This is where Jean comes in.”

She turned to the first presentation board and Maria correctly interpreted her response as she had been rehearsing this speech for a few weeks now and displayed a map of the world.

“The world has a lot of problems, the biggest and obvious threats being nuclear war, global warming, the unsustainable use of the earth's resources, pollution and uneven wealth distribution.”

“The first one, nuclear war, is the real scary one, especially these last few years, and has only just been kept in check by pure luck, and the fact that the first idiot to push the button will be as dead as the rest of the planet within a year. Try as we might, we cannot see a quick resolution to this, but I still have hope that the girls, someone, or maybe something that comes from our future research will help.”

“Because of this it is the other areas where we are putting our biggest efforts into solving. Maria's most recent projections seem to indicate that with the current changes we have implemented, and the hundreds of upcoming technologies that are starting to come on line, we should have the resources now to be able to stop the slow train wreck and turn around pollution, global warming and the unsustainable use of the earth's resources before they reach a tipping point.”

“That's great news!” said Simon, “I see what we are doing is making a dent, but it's hard not to hear the rumours about what the other groups are on the verge of introducing..”

“..Unfortunately,” said Alexa, holding her hand up, “this is the ideal scenario. Capitalism always moves along the path of lower costs and if left to market forces alone we will see these changes come to pass, as it will under-cut the current non-sustainable options. However we now hit a bigger issue, human greed and the political will to change and give up control of certain industries and processes.”

“We seem to have four separate cabals operating here,” she pointed out the USA, “here,” Korea, “here,” Switzerland, “and finally here,” she pointed out London. “Each is deep into armaments, petroleum, mining, banking, media, shipping and organised crime, all of them willing to work well outside the laws of any country to maximise profits..”

Hardy interrupted her, frowning. “Seriously Alexa, conspiracy and illuminati type thinking is beneath you, none of this has ever been proven..”

It was Helena's voice that answered him. “Alexa is unfortunately correct, Hardy,” she said bluntly. “There are no Illuminati, Knights Templar or Vatican secret societies we can find but we have all analysed the flows of money, bitcoins, contracts and acquisitions from data Maria has diligently obtained from the past few years, and it's all real. That's billions of transactions. Yes, it's a conspiracy theorists nightmare, but facts do not lie. The flow of money back to terrorist groups has led to two large wars, dozens of minor wars and several regime changes in just the thirty years we can go back to. SARS and Coronavirus, the following logistical chaos, the recent Ukraine war, murders and assassinations, all feed back to strings pulled by these four groups, and all four groups have benefitted massively from them. Control of the press is a major factor in this being hidden, as is removing people who try to out them with ridicule, blackmail, threats or even murder. More recently social media has been their manipulation tool so nobody knows anymore who or what to trust. Believe me this is not a conspiracy, it is all real and is happening now, right under your noses!”

Everyone looked worried, but nobody spoke.

“To follow on from this,” said Maria, “there have been several attempts to block the new technologies we are trying to introduce. It has been difficult for them to do this in free countries as a considerable portion of our processing is devoted to correcting misinformation. But these cabals also own a lot of the resources of governments and can use the laws and legislation in those countries where and when it suits, many times overriding public opinion. Of course they also have tangible links and interests in several crime syndicates and are happy to use them where all else fails, or where cost or morality are an issue. We are fighting a losing battle if we remain on the defensive.”

The four scientists looked to each other in confusion, it was Simon who eventually spoke, “I have seen a lot of what you said play out, my family has even dealt with the edges of this and it is never nice.” He paused, “I guess some of the backlash to our AI and QVcell introductions fall into this, like you say anything good can be spun these days into bad. We’ve all had as much bad press as good, most of it is made up, I try not to read it, but my family and friends do and it is difficult to un-see something or prove a rumour negative especially if someone wants to believe it, or is too lazy to check if it's truthful.”

Hardy spoke up next, “I have had the same, and it is the reason I no longer check the popular media. I believe most intelligent people understand the spin and can fact check for themselves and that the majority of the people of this world are good, but unfortunately it's a very uneven playing field for the truth these days.”

The other three were nodding.

“I agree,” said Spence, “but at the end of the day we’re scientists and we should try and ensure we don't stoop down to the same level as the gutter press nor be tempted to try any illegal options.”

“We won't,” said Alexa, “but I have been thinking about this with regard to history, and it never ends well for the lone scientist or small progressive groups going against the institution. I therefore want to be several moves ahead on both defensive and offensive thinking so we don't immediately get cut down. This is where Jean, David and another group of people come in. Their tasks will be to expose and root out as much of this as they can, passing the information to those who can legally do something. All of you are right, we have the best minds on the planet so we should not need to stoop to their levels or resort to their tactics but we also must be able to counter all their moves and in the medium term remove them as a threat to the world order.”

“And you think Jean and David are up to that?” said Hardy, “with all due respect Alexa, aren't we handing them both an impossible task and a poison chalice?”

“Neither Jean, nor David, are not going to be doing anything on their own.” Said Maria. “They will have all our resources, which as you know, exceed the best out there by a long way, and they will use this and their extensive networks and knowledge of the way the dark underbelly of humanity works to point the good guys in the right direction. Our people will making all the executive decisions, and the authorities will be doing all the dangerous stuff.”

“Jean has the hardest job, but she will be working indirectly with our other people around the world, some like David, Fachini and Grace you may know, but there are a dozen others Alexa and I have been working with, they will all be working in isolation or small groups, managing a particular scenario, but all aware of the big picture and able to assist or get assistance as required. None of these guys were chosen at random, each is a top strategist in their respective field and each was chosen for their honesty, morality, integrity, intelligence and track record of action.”

“I am giving each of these people all the resources at my disposal, though some like David and Tony have not requested anything. Each will operate like a conductor of an orchestra and between us all I think we can get the conclusion we want. All the guys are already working every waking hour on various scenarios, we have even gamified some of the more complex scenarios with some online strategy groups. Ironically some of the people we are targeting are in these game groups, unknowingly giving us information and plotting their own downfall. In many ways we are over-complicating it as our opposition, even at its best, does not trust itself.”

“And remember, none of these actions will be attributable to our people nor to us, we will be as surprised as the rest of the world when these events occur.”

The group had been getting more and more anxious but breathed a collective sigh of relief at the last sentence.

“You should have led with that last sentence, I was getting really worried we were going to become targets,” said Simon.

“Holy hell,” said Spence moving the discussion back, “I don't envy their tasks.”

“What Simon said before is correct I believe,” said Alexa, “the vast majority of humanity wouldn't stand for this if they knew it was happening. Our job is to help our guys get that truth out there and overcome the inevitable spin that will be put out by the media, governments and politicians.”

“We have Jean and the other assets because none of this really computes with us,” said Helena. “An AI cannot interpret outcomes controlled by greed and corruption, we can process every spy novel ever written and try and determine all the possible outcomes but these guys have lived at the cutting edge of it and have the best chance of guessing the correct outcomes.”

“I am only informing you guys so you are aware,” said Alexa, “I just want you all to know that it is our number one imperative to ensure the good work we are all doing to progress humanity and save the planet continues. You will have already noticed a lot of the untruthful negative spin and fake news has reduced to almost nothing, and I don't want any of you to lose sleep thinking any of this progress will be undone. I wish we had a plan to end the threat of nuclear war too, but we do not yet, we may have a plan for this though.”

“Thanks guys,” said Simon. “I actually have been losing sleep over this. I honestly wish you, Jean, David and the other guys all the luck in the world and if there is anything I can do you only need to ask.”

“Same here,” said Hardy, “I have nightmares about the men in black kicking in our doors and stealing this, when it's over I would like to shake each and every one of them by the hand.”
