“I second both of you,” said Spence, “I am from an army family, and I still have many contacts if you need me to say anything just ask.”

Jen simply nodded in agreement with the guys.

“All of you are right.” Said Alexa. “I’ve only known some of this a little longer than you guys and I’m still working out the implications. However I’ve been looking into the political end of the problem since day one with Maria so I needed you guys to understand what we are doing. There is a famous saying that no plan survives contact with the enemy. We are going to need backup plans to our backup plans and keep refining the plans to ensure any cockroach that scurries away and finds a temporary refuge is caught.”

Maria continued, “Magnus, Jen and Daisy's singularity work has unexpectedly handed us a royal flush when it comes to intelligence gathering as we can now connect to air gapped systems or bypass firewalls. The information on the board now was obtained through real time links to their off-line systems, and real time transcription of key cell phone traffic. We now know every head of the snake and where the money trails lead. Because of that, Jean and our guys will go in with all that knowledge, knowing every asset they control, and more importantly their next moves. One of the reasons we needed to act so swiftly was because the London cabal was actually talking about moving against the research centre here and seizing its assets under the guise of national security.”

Everyone except Alexa reacted with shock to this.

“They were what!” said Jen.

“Sorry,” said Alexa, “we should have added first that we are in no actual danger. We know their next moves before they do, and the group has already analysed the situational data and found there is no credible way they can achieve it.”

“..But,” said Alexa with a poker face and serious voice, “in doing this they have crossed a line in the sand and now have three pissed off AI’s and a dozen of the smartest and most devious humans on the planet who will make the next few months hell on earth for all of them.”

“Why is it I almost feel sorry for them for what you are about to unleash,” smiled Hardy relaxing a little. “Like the rest of the guys I have been kept up at night thinking of some of the implications, it's no good building sandcastles if someone is going to just jump on them.”

He got up off his seat stretching. “You know all of us have the rest of the evening free, we can go through any other worries or questions on this and maybe we can spend an hour on your master plan for the bits we four can actually help with.”

There were nods from the other three, and, after a small toilet break, a journey to liberate one of her grandad’s finer clarets. Alexa went through her findings with Maria on the rest of their so-called belt and braces plan.

* * *

“This is something I am very passionate about,” said Hardy. “Up until Maria showed me the implications of the maths and science I really didn't care much at all for all this giant step macho nonsense, it was like someone telling me about this land called America which is just across this ocean oh and by the way here is your rowing boat to do it, oh and your rowing boat will cost you a hundred million dollars a trip!”

Alexa laughed. “I think you nailed my thoughts up to about a few weeks ago.”

“Anyway,” continued Hardy pensively, “I know many of you also have re-looked at the same problems, in its new light, and now support it, and if we can pull it off correctly it will kill multiple birds with one stone. The good news as you already know, is that three weeks ago my team managed to generate a few milli-newtons of thrust using just electricity and without any propellant. We have also reproduced the experiment over a dozen times.”

“This alone is a Nobel prize, but it is also just a useless science curiosity unless we can scale it up, and we obviously believe we can. If we can get to three point one percent efficiency, and with the latest power cells, it could lift its own weight. Every gain from that point on will give us the potential to decarbonise much of the world's aircraft. More importantly for this discussion though is we will open up unlimited access to space. We are improving with each iteration, however we are still two orders of magnitude off this figure,”

“As Hardy said, I was not a fan of this at the start,” continued Alexa. “However the more it was explained to me by Hardy, the girls and various economics experts the more convinced I became. The world is fighting over limited space and resources, and nations are pulling up their drawbridges so people don't have the option to move. We need to provide a safety valve to expand, just like the Europeans had a hundred years ago with the new world, only this time there will be no native populations to decimate. The economic advantages alone are enormous, it will provide jobs in creating the infrastructure, jobs in space, and a lot more jobs in supporting all these new industries, which will be needed as the populations expand. The moving of mining, refining and manufacturing, off-earth will eventually relieve the pressure on the earth's environment, and the near infinite expansion space for people to live in should relieve any pressures of war. Finally, we will not be subject to any country's untenable regulations and security which will give Maria, Helena, April, and any more children they decide to produce the freedom to safely come out into the open.”

“Don't get me wrong,” continued Alexa, “I don't want any of this to come at any expense to the earth, saving the earth is and must always be our primary goal and this is where Simon's project comes in. We are going to build this new economy mostly from captured carbon and other recycled materials, and basically give humanity the stars as a fringe benefit!”

“Nicely put,” said Hardy, “I intend to pull out all the stops over the coming months with our teams to make my end of this a reality, however it's not just Simon's recycling and material technology we need, we need improvements in hundreds of other areas to come to fruition if we are going to live and work in space. Lucky for us the girls are already on the case and many of those are already being worked on from multiple angles as we speak in laboratories around the world.”

“Wow,” said Spence

“I just love the synergy,” said Simon, “so when do we let the world know?”

“Forget the world, when do we let our staff know,” said Jen, “our guys will be so up for this, I know for a fact everyone would work twice as hard if they knew what the end goal was.”

“We can't just yet,” replied Maria, “It's going to be soon but we need to eliminate the threats first, I really just wish I could give you a date.”

“I think giving our staff some inkling of the goal as Jen says would actually be low risk,” replied Alexa, “I think we can trust them with a subset of the goals at least, maybe we could time it for Hardy's first practical demo..”

“Which is a month or two away,” said Hardy, “but I agree we should do it, after all if we cannot trust our own people, who can we trust?”

The meeting dissolved into upbeat planning and renewed enthusiasm, by the end they had all agreed the strategies and roles they would play, and hoped for the best that they hadn't missed anything.

## Unintended Consequences

Working in his new temporary apartment, away from the hot June temperatures, David had gone through hundreds of permutations and refinements of their strategy document with the group. In the back of his mind all that time, was what was the best method to bring those responsible for the murder of Yoshi and his family to justice.

They used one of their simpler tactics to expose both the banker and the Mossad agents in the chain responsible for the arms sales, and the explosion which killed Yoshi and his family. It was a tactic that would become the cornerstone of their later successes.

There was always an ongoing operation by the Israeli secret services monitoring the Iranian embassy, the two countries permanently existed in a state of cold war, and vast resources were put in to collect any form of intelligence. It was therefore trivial for Maria to insert a message encoded in a recently broken cipher from Tehran to the Iranian embassy in London at the same time the embassy experienced an internal network failure. The outcome was the Israelis had a message they believed was from Iran but the Iranian embassy did not receive the message and so did not query it.

The message gave the instructions for an Iranian agent to make contact with Johan Zimmerman, a wealthy London banker and known arms dealer. The message commanded them to coerce Zimmerman into supplying twelve German made RG4 surface to air missiles through a specific shipping line to an address in Egypt. The message also added if the price was greater than three million dollars they paid last time or he should refuse then they were free to resort to blackmail. They then gave details of the previous shipment and the bombing of the Mossad agent's family to cover it all up which they could use to do this.

The original documents, logs, phone records and transcripts that Maria had copied had been pieced together from multiple sources, something David was unsure the analysts there could do as well as they did, so they made it easy.

David knew the message would be picked up and go to the section where he used to work to decode and analyse. Maria therefore ensured the documents and the names and numbers of the three rogue Mossad agents, they had evidence against, and who were involved in the arms deal and subsequent murder of Yoshi, were placed in the bankers PC in the trash can and encrypted using the bankers last name.

For the first four days, nothing appeared to happen, then the sparks started to fly.

Unbeknownst to David, Maria monitored the progress of Mossad as they decoded the message, tried to hack the bankers computers but failed and sent someone around to the offices during a staged fire evacuation to clone the bankers laptop disk.

The problem was that the computer used by the section three guys was off the net, when it was finally picked up and the data retrieved for analysis, Maria saw that it showed a fabricated report on the visit made by the Mossad agent to David and details of what had been done to find him since, in this were photos taken in the last three days through telegraphic lenses of David outside the British museum and walking into his supposedly secret apartment. Worst of all it also contained details of two bitcoins sent to a known hitman on the dark web, and targeting David.

That was the reason David was now at Alexa's front door.

* * *

“It is good to see you again David,” said Alexa, hugging him warmly.

David dropped his two bags and returned the hug and held on to it a few seconds longer than necessary as he was genuinely happy to be here and to see her again.

“I wish it was under nicer circumstances Alexa,” he sighed.

“We’re just glad you’re safe,” she said.

Alexa popped out of the front door to her house. “Thanks Albert,” she said waving to Albert who was waiting by the charger with a cable waiting for Maria to reverse her car into the garage. He waved back.

“Here,” she said grabbing one of his bags and leading him up the stairs, “Simon, spends all his time with Allison these days in the big house, most of his stuff is up there already and he hasn't used this room in months so you can have it for as long as you need it. She led him to an open door which led into a big room tastefully decorated, with two large bay windows, an en-suite, some built-in wardrobes, draws, big mirror, desk and a large double bed.

“Make yourself at home and when you're ready come downstairs for dinner.” She smiled and disappeared down the corridor and down the large staircase.

He dumped his two brown leather holdalls on the floor, unzipped one and took his toiletries and a towel into the en-suite. It already had two towels hung up so he draped his over the bathtub and walked back out. He spent a few more minutes unpacking and hanging his clothes, then spent a minute looking around the room and out the window, then finally at himself in the mirror.

The last three months had been a roller coaster, he remembered a simpler fun time as a playboy in London, and a not so secret agent bartender a few months earlier, the latter culminating in the visit by Alexa and Allison. He smiled, knowing these guys as he knew them now, he wouldn't have been surprised if the chaos at the end of the night had been some sort of a test, it was totally calculable that Donna would send that tweet, would he abandon his friends?

In many ways he was happy to be here, they still had a lot of work to do to take down the cabals but here he would be closer to friends. Unfortunately the fact he was now also a man marked by an unknown assassin to be murdered, had shattered his easy going demeanour.

The meal that evening was just the two of them, Jen and Hardy both still working, and probably sleeping up in the main house if it got too late. Maria had messaged David that food was nearly ready if he wanted to go down to the kitchen. After unpacking his bags, he showered and Maria then directed him where to find an ironing board and iron so he could get out of the thrown on clothes he had travelled here in. Finally when he felt presentable he wandered down to the kitchen.

The kitchen was sparkling clean and devoid of clutter as it always seemed to be, except for the diner table which was set for three. In the middle of the setting was a whole grain sourdough loaf, a bread knife and tray of condiments all on a large wooden chopping board. Something that smelled really nice was still cooking in the oven. He looked around wondering whether to call Alexa, when a door opened loudly at the back of the kitchen and she walked in carrying a bottle of wine.

“Oh, you're here, good. I made us some vegetarian lasagne. Jen was going to come down but seems to have been caught up in something, so I will put hers to the side and it's probably just you and me.”

“You cook?”

“Not very well,” Alexa said with a little laugh, and putting the bottle down on the table. “But there are a couple of dishes I can make that seem to be appreciated by the guys here, vegetarian lasagne is one, Simon and Jen being of the vegetarian persuasion.”

“I wasn't sure which wine to choose, Hardy is the expert and keeps trying to let me in on how to choose wine, but to tell the truth I just look at how posh the label is, and mostly I get lucky. Anyway, I didn't have to look far today as Bella did some wine shopping and the merchant had put three boxes of Californian Pinot Noir aside for Hardy, so I am appropriating one. I blame him for saying how good they were.. Oh, better not forget..”

She rushed around the counter, her white knee length dress swishing as she navigated the corner, then clicked a button on the oven and opened it with her pink oven mitts. A large cloud of steam gushed out, and from the depths of the oven she extracted a small casserole dish, which she walked slowly over to the table and put on an empty place mat in the centre.

It was impossible to stay in a bad mood with this beautiful and exceptional girl in front of him, cooking him dinner no less. It was surprising how an existential threat like getting murdered put things in perspective, and if these were to be his last days of his life he certainly was not going out being a grumpy sour-puss.

“This looks and smells wonderful,” he said genuinely, his resolve to be happier taking over. “And you look great too, whoops, I mean attractive, er I mean the dress is nice.” God I hope that didn't come out the wrong way he thought blushing a little.

“Why thank you, David, always good to know I still have that je-ne-sais-quoi! You're looking pretty dapper yourself,” she replied, either ignoring or accepting whatever gaff he thought he had made.

She popped over to the counter then looked up, before unhooking a medium sized serving spoon from the rack. “I don't need to save any for Hardy, but Jen might still come home if she sorts her problem out.” She cut the small dish in four and scooped a quarter out and onto a plate, handing it to him, she did the same for herself and sat down.

“The bread is fresh this morning, Bella makes a dozen every other day, she’s been doing it since discovering this thing called YouTube during the COVID lockdowns, and she has been perfecting it ever since.” She pointed to the condiments, “this one's butter, the other is olive spread and that yellow one is hummus, but you would know that growing up in that part of the world.”

She cut three slices of bread putting one on his side plate and one on hers, “we can toss a coin for the crust if you like?” she smiled.

He looked at her and smiled cheekily, then put his hand in his pocket and brought out a coin. “How did you know I liked the crusts? Heads it's mine, tails it's yours.”

She laughed, “OK.”

He tossed the coin and uncovered it. “Damn!” He said with a fake frown.

“Double or quits for the other end?” she said just as wickedly.

He tossed the coin and uncovered it again. “Double-Damn!”

She gave him the crust, “I think you deserve it.”

“You're a pretty amazing person, you know that?” he said as he picked up and buttered the crust, “You know they have T-shirts for sale in the stalls outside the underground with your face on it and the caption, 'Old white men used to rule the world'.”

She frowned, “don't I know it! Daisy only wore one two weeks ago at the pub, how embarrassing was that. I feel especially bad as this is not about putting down white men, old or otherwise, my grandad ticked all three boxes and he was the nicest man I knew, likewise most of my best friends are white and male. All this is about lifting everyone to the same level and making sure the bad guys whatever gender, race or colour they may be are taken down.”

She went to the other side of the bread and cut off the other crust, then used it to eat a small portion of lasagne.

“Sorry about the cheese, I tend to get carried away, thank god I go jogging every morning!”

“I jog and swim most days, though it's been difficult these past few months to do anything.”

“Come with me tomorrow. I usually go out about seven, sometimes with Jen if she's here, otherwise I usually see her somewhere along the track with a couple of the other guys. We have an outside swimming pool in the grounds too, it's unheated but it's summer now and when it gets hot we sometimes change pub night to a pool party. Maybe I should get some heating installed, all that heat that comes out of Spence's area could be put to some good use.”

They talked history and university for the remainder of the meal, both finishing their plate and David taking the other quarter, happy to listen to her chatter.

“Thanks Alexa,” he said as he finished his meal and took a sip of wine, “that was really nice.” He relaxed his posture a little, “you know I really look forward to seeing you, you’re such a beautiful orator and so well informed, not many beautiful women have that other side to them, I really wish I had met you years ago.”

“Careful David, I’m only twenty three,” she teased.

“Oh you know what I mean.. To talk to!”

They both laughed, enjoying the moment and the wine.

Getting more serious, David said. “I don't think I’ve ever said it to you, but I really owe you guys so much for giving my life meaning again.”

“Oh pish David,” she smiled, “you sound like someone who has been given the last rights! You owe us nothing, you are a free agent who we were lucky to have the same goals as us, you know I am pretty sure Maria is putting every resource she can into finding this threat and eliminating it.”

“Well..” Chipped in Maria who had remained purposefully quiet letting the two humans enjoy the moment as they called it.

“I wasn't going to disturb your supper as you both looked to be having a good time, but David's problem should be history in a few hours.”

“See,” said Alexa, not changing her dreamy countenance one iota. “Maria’s a treasure more precious than diamonds.”

David was still parsing the, “should be history in a few hours”, statement.

“What?.. How?..”

“Oh David, you know how we work now,” said Maria, “you’re family and I’m not going to let any bad guys get you! The contract went to a shady character called Leon Perrez. He thinks he is clever using bitcoin but they are real easy to trace the audit trails as you know, so it's only secret if you never spend any. Perrez cashed his in the same day. Perrez is wanted for murder in four countries, and by at least three crime organisations. He is currently at Milan airport wondering why his phone is not dead, his passport and ticket have been revoked, and why all his credit cards are not working. His details have also been passed to the Italian police, Interpol, airport security and two mafia gangs all are on the way to say Hello. All mention of you from any system he has access to has also been wiped. It wasn't worth spoiling a good meal though.”

David slumped into his chair, relief showing all over his face. His next thoughts were totally selfish. Did it mean he had to leave?

As if reading his mind, Alexa said

“You know David's part of the family now, let's ask him if he wants to stay here a while?”

She directed her look at David who was now doubly relieved, unless he heard wrong, Alexa had just asked him to stay.

“I’d love to stay, if it's OK with everyone else.”

“Well,” said Alexa, “Hardy likes you full stop, whatever you guys talked about that time it certainly made a good impression. As for Jen, she may have let on that you were quite dishy for a spy, when she said hello last time you were down. That was before she found out you also had a Masters in Computer Science, so I wouldn't be surprised if she hasn't already got a poster of you on her wall next to the one of Brian Cox. I may have to tell her to stop walking around the house half naked though!”

David blushed.

“Hmm,” said Maria, “if Jen was to find out that you said that, you are going to be in such BIG trouble. But, if say you were to do me a little favour, I might be persuaded to delete that little snippet from my history.”

“Blackmail!” screeched Alexa playfully, “Maria, that's a new low,” then more cheerfully said, “OK what do you want?”

“Well, I think it is time you introduced David to your other occupant,” said Maria, “you know the one you keep locked in the basement.”

David looked around the room trying to find the source of Maria's presence to give it a weird look, however his stare fell on Alexa.

“So, you want to know our secrets Mr Bond?” she said in the deepest male voice she could muster, with her little finger held to her mouth. Then she looked at him with a silly smile, “why is there never a fluffy white cat to put on your lap and stroke when you need one!”

“That was possibly the worst Doctor Evil impression I have ever heard in my life,” laughed David. “But I’m going to put it on my next T-shirt.”

“You dare!” she screamed!

Jen, with her usual poor timing, ran in on the scream.

“Alexa! Oh I heard you scream.. David?”, she looked between the two of them laughing, shook her head and walked out. “I hope you saved me some food,” she shouted as she departed.

They spent a few minutes tidying up and loading the dishwasher, leaving one place setting for Jen, they then refilled their glasses and she led him out into the corridor and to the door at the end. She twisted the handle and opened it fully exposing the carpeted staircase going down. David looked a bit worried, I mean it looked comfortable, but she didn't really have someone living down here did she? He kept quiet and followed her down.

Most of the rooms had been cleared, the old computer at the end running the first MOTHER system was still there, still switched on, and still helping Maria with tasks. Its pretty lights, now that they were not obscured by cables, boxes and tables, looked quite impressive. The two right hand labs had been tidied up also, and now also had racks worth of newer singularity modems and an earlier device from back when they called it a wormhole thingy.

David peeked into the two rooms on the right with their humming equipment and laboratories which still would not look out of place in any multi-million dollar corporation, then he noticed the large window wall to the left changing and looked over to it.

Alexa was walking into the double doors that had slid silently open. It was a large room, growing brighter every second, it looked a bit weird, mostly empty space with two big sofas, three workstations, a small black box on a pedestal in the centre, two extremely big presentation monitors and some lights on stands, wait not lights, speakers, no those pod things so probably high definition cameras too.

Alexa led him to a sofa and sat down patting the seat next to him.

“Hi David,” came Maria's voice, the clearest he had ever heard it and directly from the black box. Then it dawned on him, that black box was Maria.

“Maria! Is that really you?” he said, looking directly at the black box.

“In the flesh, so to speak.” Her avatar came on the monitor, or it would have been her avatar if it wasn't in black and white and she was clothed in rags.

“What the..” Alexa started, but Maria continued, the voice moving to the screen.

“It's kind of my office too, the guys have their super secret meetings in here and someone occasionally comes down here to work, but most of the time it's just me.. On my own.. In the dark.. And.. And.. They don't feed me..” Her avatar sobbed.
