“Yes,” said Hardy, “sorry it's not much to look at yet, I had Ian weld the four boxes on the plate this morning, and then we ran some balancing and calibration tests, the efficiency is still quite low at four point six percent but it's still groundbreaking.”

“How are you measuring the efficiency?” said Daisy who had stepped up to join them.

“Simple really, the electrical energy in, to the potential and kinetic energy gains of the device, with a hundred percent being that one hundred joules of electricity in would have a potential energy gain of one hundred joules.

“Still a wow!” said Daisy.

Hardy saw that everyone had arrived. “OK people,” he said, “one of the perks of this job is to get to see history made,” he smiled. “Well unfortunately you missed the actual historic bit as we did the testing a few weeks before on a smaller unit, and we had to do a few tweaks and a bit more engineering before we called you all here. Needless to say all of us here cracked a small bottle of wine open and celebrated when it worked. Unfortunately it was only the one glass, as we needed to prepare for this.”

“Anyway we are happy to erase that little bit from history, so welcome one and all to the inaugural demonstration of our reaction-less drive. We won't go too much into the science, because to tell the truth, English is not a very good language to use anymore, and mathematics is not a language we normally use to talk to muggles!”

A couple of people laughed.

“So feast your eyes on Icarus, not quite the starship Enterprise but believe you me, that will happen, and sooner than you think.” He looked over at Simon and Leo. “So what you can see here is six hundred kilograms of stainless steel plate, plus another eighty kilograms, consisting of four,” Hardy pointed to the four boxes on each corner, “engines, with sensors and accelerometers in them. These are all linked back to the central control and power supply, which consists of four of the larger high power QVCells, all overclocked by ten to produce sixteen kilowatts total output. Normally we do not run the cells overclocked for very long as the heat output also scales up, but with such a big heat-sink we will be fine for the demonstration. April has volunteered to be our pilot for today, and probably everyday until she finishes the design of the control unit, as the maths and timing to achieve this is a bit crazy. So without further ado, I will pass the stage to April.”

A few people clapped.

“OK guys, settle down,” said April, in her French accent, from a speaker on one of the lab benches. “It won't be that spectacular, the best we can do with this current setup is a tenth of a gravity over earth's gravity so that's one point one gravities of thrust, and that's at full power with the configuration we have, it will take three seconds to get up a metre in the air.”

The board clicked and four high powered blue LED’s in each corner flashed ominously, the plate started to move up, very slowly for the first few seconds then stopped at chest height with only an imperceptible wobble, like the bonnet of a car with the engine idling.

“Hmm, not quite getting the full acceleration there,” said Hardy, “probably a bit heavy, anyway the power has been reduced slightly so we are now exactly producing one earth gravity upwards force balancing the one earth gravity downwards force. If you look at the big monitor next to us,” he pointed up to an area of the screen, “you will see a number on it, this is the number of kilowatts of power we are expending, the number below it is the efficiency..”

Hardy looked at Terry and Jules then at the speaker where April's voice was coming from, “April?” he said enquiringly, “why is it seven point one?”

“Sorry guys,” came April's voice, “I did some tweaks overnight during the billion subjective AI hours I had spare while you guys were sleeping, I got the guys in Delhi to check the stability and we just got the results.”

Hardy shook his head smiling, “April, we discussed this!” said Hardy in a fatherly way. Simon and Alexa laughed.

“I was bored!” She said, “It's to do with the superconductor lattice temperature stuff, what you and Jules were discussing last night I can explain to you guys later. Anyway, back to the presentation, this acceleration may sound terrible to someone like Hardy, who I assume started this project so he could build a Millennium Falcon.” Hardy smirked and rolled his eyes. “But remember this is an acceleration not a velocity, so if we applied full power for eight hours we would be rushing past the moon travelling a hundred thousand kilometres per hour.”

“I will let that sink in for those that have not thought about it. Also we do not need to reach escape velocity, so no terrifying rockets required and no burning up on reentry, we can come down and go up at whatever velocity we want.”

“So when can we go to the moon?” said Daisy from amongst the excited chatter.

“Well Daisy, before you volunteer I better just remind you about the small issues of breathing, being in a vacuum, no gravity, oh and the one about not dying a ghastly death due to cosmic radiation. I don't know about you guys, but that last one scares me like hell! Anyway, the good part is once the newer extruder is ready, we are going to be using Simon's team's research to build Icarus two and that should be able to go into space.

A few people clapped enthusiastically and Daisy shouted a woohoo from the sides.

“How are you going to keep this technology away from the military?” said Simon soberly.

“We are not,” said Maria, who seemed to have defaulted to the default spokesperson for all three AI’s regarding policy. “Two things, firstly, the guys are not yet at a stage where we will be announcing it, as they can attest, the science is extremely complex to get your head around. Secondly, and unbeknownst to them, when we do release it we are going to retain full control of the technologies, this is because the control system requires a near AI level of control to manipulate the fields. Well the design we are publishing does. They will of course eventually understand the science and be able to reproduce it, but it will take a very long time. So if they want it they will either have to spend tens of billions of dollars and maybe ten years to get something a fraction of the efficiency, or licence it through us. That means nothing which carries weapons, and agreeing to our usual terms and conditions.”

“I thought Icarus two was a test extrusion to see if we could possibly make shell structures that could withstand radiation,” said Leo, “all the bits of the design that didn't look right, kind of make sense now,” he laughed.

“It actually was originally a test extrusion,” said Alexa talking to the group, “when the girls,” everyone knew she was talking about the AI’s when she said the girls, “said Hardy’s group were making progress, I said we should do the final test in style and bring some projects together, and now you all know.” She grinned. “And of course Hardy is going to eventually have his Millennium Falcon, well it won't have laser guns and light speed, and it won't be able to make the Kessel run in twelve parsecs, but it should be pretty impressive.”

Hardy gave Alexa a hug. “Not Princess Leia but you’re definitely a keeper!” he smiled.

“So,” he continued, “since Alexa and Maria have completely derailed our first demonstration, let's say we adjourn to the buffet that cook has prepared, and the guys and I will answer all your questions.”

Magnus was gob-smacked! He continued to look at the hovering slab of steel. Why was he even here with this group of geniuses? He had just watched something straight out of a sci-fi show take place, nobody seemed to bat an eyelid, and they even left it hanging there so they could have tea and cakes!

Of course, Magnus still hadn't fully seen the implications for the singularity they had created either. All through the past six months he had dreams of rippling stargates, but the maths as he understood it, was never going to allow it. He sighed.

“Impressive isn't it?” said Jen, putting her hand around his shoulder, “but you have to expect things like this when you have Hardy, and two of MIT’s best in Terry and Jules. Do you know what is also impressive?”

He shook his head enjoying Jen's closeness and still not taking his eyes off the hovering steel plate.

“It's you!” she said, “the implications of the work you have started is also far reaching. You do realise it was your new maths that solved one of the biggest issues with this project, if you weren't straight I think Hardy would kiss you! I guess you are so into science that you cannot see the forest for the trees.”

He finally turned to her looking inquisitive.

“Oh Magnus! Here, let's go get some of the buffet and get our heads out of the singularities for the rest of the day,” she said smiling, putting her hands through his and leading him away from the still hovering plate.

Jules was last to leave and caught the two guys up a few seconds later. “Jen's right you know, I overheard. Your new maths helped us no end.”

She said it adding a twinge of French to her Canadian accent, then wrapping her hands around both their shoulders, strolled to find the others. Jen and Magnus grilled her on the science all the way to the buffet.

“I think we could manage two gravities, more than that would be uncomfortable and possibly dangerous,” said Terry on a question from Simon. “With the current hardware it's much easier and safer to parallel them up if we want more. Jules and April were looking at the efficiency problem because, as you know heat, is not your friend in space and you need to somehow get rid of it; Opening the windows is unfortunately not an option! Luckily there is still some low-hanging fruit in the science, which means there is still room for improvements, as you just saw.”

Alexa sipped her tea quietly, smiling, and happy to not be the centre of any of the attention. She tuned out of Terry's conversation as it got a little more technical, and turned to Matilda and Leo who were chatting to Jen and Magnus.

“The new assembler cannot make anything bigger than a metre cubed,” said Leo between bites of his sausage roll, “but of course this is using Simon's technology so we are now talking about super strength allotropes of carbon. Graphene is the strongest, but it is also too brittle, so the guys have been programming and testing other lattice structures the last five weeks to test the most promising. Ideally we want something as light and hard as graphene but as tough as silicon-carbide for the final product. We are really hoping to be able to create composites that layer alternate allotropes, and we are likely to have some super strong candidates.” Leo smiled, “of course when our team eventually put the paper out, I wouldn't want to have shares in anything to do with diamonds!”

He continued. “We are scaling this up but the equipment is months away, so Icarus two is being manufactured with a titanium frame by a local manufacturing firm. We will assemble it all here though, the first prototype is bound to raise issues with the panels and fittings, so it won't be as seamless or big as future models, but it won't be too shabby either.”

Alexa circled the people talking and listening to the enthusiasm. It was a good call to do the demonstration, as successes always brought teams together, and big goals and ambitions made everyone want to be a part of it. It was perfect timing to raise everyone’s spirits and distract them from he chaos still resonating from the Chinese meltdown of the cabals, and the in-fighting going on between them. The media surrounding the research centre had quietened down and, it seemed, moved on.

The group were also now fully aware of the new technology, and had already discussed the geo-political aspects of it. All were in agreement that like the QVCell, this would also be licenced, when the time was right, and subject to the usual terms and conditions.

In the tiniest moment between all the smiling people, a tiny hint of sadness came to Alexa's face. Truth be told, she was missing David and wanted this moment to share with him too. But David was currently in Rome talking with a history professor. Maria had vetoed the professor's involvement in the group but would not say why, only that if you dug hard enough into anyone's background you would soon find a lie. It was however the nature of the lie that made the difference and whether the lie came from them, or was done to them. The week before that Alexa was in Brazil, and between those, in a busy house, moments alone came few and far between.

David had however, been warm in so many other little ways she appreciated; His longing smile that said he remembered their moment as longingly as she had, the way he would bring her a hot chocolate, or a wine, or just sit with her sometimes, while she was working. She knew what they had shared that day was only a kiss, but for that one fleeting moment she stopped being a corporate mega idol leading the world on an impossible path, and became a woman again.

Jen came over with Magnus and Jules, all laughing and bringing her attention back to the present and her demeanour back to a smile. She looked at Magnus's puppy dog eyes as he looked at Jen talking with Jules and found she missed David's presence even more.

## What happens in Vegas

The meeting of the four leaders of the American cabal took place three times a year in a sealed room on the otherwise empty top floor of a Las Vegas hotel owned by them. Around the same time as Hardy's demonstration, their August 2026 summer meeting was about to start. Their security team had swept the area with a fine tooth comb checking for bugs and microphones, then stood back and kept all unwanted guests away. As per all meetings, no electronic devices, even watches were allowed in the meeting.

‘Big’ Jim McEwen, owner of two of the largest petrochemical companies in the world slammed his hand on the table. “Well I want god-damn answers!” he shouted to the other three, none of whom were remotely intimidated by his bravado and show.

“We all want answers Jim,” said Marlon Lockwood, firmly, holding one hand up to calm the big Texan, while secretly wishing he could just throw the glass of whisky he was holding at him. Marlon turned accusingly to Jake Thatcher, “so Jake,” he said calmly as ever, “the millions we are currently spending every week for all your assets in the various government spy agencies is currently looking like a big waste of money. You are feeding those government pigs too much of their own pork for my liking, I think you should start letting them know the very terminal consequences of actual failure!”

Marlon Lockwood was the power behind the thrones of dozens of armament and defence companies, and had so many connections to organised crime, he made the other guys nervous sometimes. The calm way he spat the accusation at Jake Thatcher did not go unnoticed.

“Oh don't you worry,” said Thatcher angrily, “nearly all my consulting, lobbying and media businesses in China were wiped out, I have lost a lot of good people and billions of dollars, I’m looking at nearly ten percent of my portfolio and the Chinese don't look like they have finished yet. Heads are going to roll and I am going to find out who or what triggered this if it's the last thing I do!”

The last of the four, Reverend “The hand” Rogers, head of the Church of Brotherly Light chipped in. “One of my ministers on the ground in Korea was abducted and he says interrogated last week. It was unprecedented, we haven't had any official contacts with the Asian's since the nineties, but our sources say they were heavily invested in China and look to have lost nearly forty percent of their assets. They are mad as hell, some of their leaders currently cannot leave their compound, the Chinese have them as targets to bring in for ‘trial’. That compound is an island fortress on its own island near Busan at the bottom tip of Korea. I remember we tried a few years back to get someone in to snoop, but those automatic gun emplacements are set to shoot to kill and we lost a couple of good assets. Likewise their computer systems are totally isolated and so cannot be hacked, good luck to the guys the Chinese send to do that!”

“Anyway,” continued Rogers, “the Koreans first tried to point the blame at us and the Brits, the nerve! Of course that was before they realised we had both been hit nearly as hard as them, I think they are now looking over to the bankers as a lot of that confiscated money will end up going into their coffers. You know what? A lot of our money has also gone into the Swiss coffers.”

“Well there is an opportunity, the Brits seem to be tied up in knots and haven't even responded to our last two communications.” Said Thatcher, “I guess they lost a lot more than we thought from the China crackdown and maybe the Swiss decided now was a good time to move in and take an even bigger slice of everyone's pie!”

Big Jim brimmed at that, the veins in his neck straining and the glass he was holding just resisting being crushed, he had obviously not thought about that possibility.

“Everyone calm down,” said Marlon, standing up and banging his black cane on the floor like a gravel, “we are going to take no action against anyone until we have evidence. Remember there are a lot more players than just the Koreans the Brits and the Swiss. The Chinese usually have their own agenda, remember we have been rattling that sabre of theirs with Taiwan for a good few years now, and the tension from that has made us some tidy profits. Then there's the Russians and North Koreans, both are rotting empires, like the Europeans, but I wouldn't put it past them to engineer something like this. Like always, let's follow the money to see who gained.”

“Well if we are following the money it's either the Chinese or the Swiss, though the Chinese may have cut off their nose to spite their face, as the loss of access to those new AI technologies is going to hit them pretty hard in the future,” said Thatcher.

“They will just steal the technology anyway,” said Marlon, “the Communists have no real care for academia or any technologies that they can get a much easier way.”

“Regardless,” said Thatcher, “I have a covert meeting with the Director of the NSA Thursday in New York, he will be told in no uncertain terms that we want answers, we have plenty of dirt on him if he doesn't deliver! And while we are at it, we need to send a clear message to the Swiss guys, that we are not to be messed with. I don't like the fact they got away scot-free, far too suspicious. You had a real beef with that banker guy a few years back Marlon, what say you let one of your more colourful assets off the leash for a while, maybe send him to Europe to buy a new Rolex.”

“Finally,” said Big Jim, “some cotton-picking action!”

The meeting continued in the same vein for another four hours, Maria and Jean heard everything, the result of some good work by Maria in finding an unused service duct, and her two guys in placing a passive microphone through it.

It looked like their China plan had bloodied the waters nicely, none of the groups were trusting each other and each were looking for the next threat from each other, so far nobody in the group had found anything pointing the blame back their way.

Maria diligently copied the raw audio and transcribed documents to the group, then she did the same to a micro SD card and they left it in the assigned mail drop for Mathews. She and Mathews could not meet for beers any longer, as he was working the problem from his end, and it was important for her safety they remained distant, so currently it was a one way information transfer, she hoped he was OK.

* * *

Mathews had just the guy he could trust with this kind of job, and he approached Clarke when some of the old squad got together for a bowling night a few weeks earlier. Clarke was an exceptional army analyst who was attached to his area in Iraq, Mathews had got him the job at the NSA when he had retired from the military, and they were on very good terms. He decided it was best to limit the information he gave to Clarke, and only passed five of the names and a subset of the information Jean gave him, picking lower level people who may not be so well monitored. He told Clarke to be very careful not to use any traceable resources.

A week after they talked an email came through saying he couldn't do pizza on Friday. This was a code they had arranged for which bar to meet, pizza meant “The Horse You Came In On” pub on Fells point at twenty-hundred hours.

They met Friday at the pub, which was crowded with strangers, both good, and bad, from a security point of view. They talked bowling, the movies, their old squad mates, then moved to a back seat when it came free.

“All of them are as dirty as they come, Jim!” Clarke said when they got on to the results of his findings. “I haven’t seen these network vulnerabilities before but they worked a treat, I pulled out some really incriminating stuff, and lots of new names, much of which wasn't in the original brief you gave me. We were set up good and proper in Fallujah, I really hope we can take these guys down.”

Clarke elaborated, going on to describe tracing the money back on one of them, and using a fake ID to make the trace. Mathews got a bit worried hearing this. “You're sure they can't trace you using agency assets? If these guys are dirty there could be others covering for them?”

“Nah, we are good,” laughed Clarke, clinking his beer glass with Mathews, “we run these exercises all the time with fake names and accounts.”

Mathews wasn't convinced, “you should double check you weren't seen, like I said, where there is one rat there's usually a nest of them, having someone covering my back is what I would do if I was dirty.”

“You worry too much Jim, like I said, we do this all the time, the boss covers us, and a few risks are always worth taking to take someone dirty out.”

They parted after the one beer as arranged. Mathews asked him to keep digging, but very carefully, while he needed to formulate his next steps, and how to approach the general. He said he would let him know when he was ready and see him at the bowling ally next Tuesday.

Despite Mathews precautions, they were watched and listened to closely.

* * *

The next day was Saturday. Mathews did his usual lazy morning jog through and around Patterson park, then came back home. He checked his mailbox and noticed the small chalk mark on the floor indicating one of Jean's guys had delivered another update from her. After showering he got changed, picked up the laptop Jean had sent, then walked to his car. He took the flyer from under the car's windscreen wiper and put it in his pocket. Mathews then opened the car and pretended to get something from the glovebox, making the removal of the flyer look like a coincidence if anybody was watching.

Following his usual ritual, he then walked down the side street to his local cafe for breakfast. The cafe was about half-full, and, as usual, he got the same seat at the back. The waitress came over and without looking at the menu, ordered his usual coffee, bagel and scrambled eggs. So far, it was a very usual day.

When the waitress had gone he remove the flyer from his pocket, and the memory card taped to the back of it, inserted the card directly into the small laptop, and pushed the power button.

Maria had created a bootable operating system that quickly and efficiently secured the laptop and came straight up in a usable desktop that Mathews could process the information with. Each memory card came with all the previous information indexed and updated, and once booted up, the laptop destroyed the data on the card by overwriting it several times with random data. The new data was stored in the laptop with the usual four thousand bit encryption and was secured so it wouldn't work without Mathews looking directly at the laptop camera and typing in the password, which was always tomorrow's date and the current hour in any format. Anything at all wrong and the laptop would boot up to the normal Google operating system and a romance novel he was writing. Jean definitely had a weird sense of humour!

Mathews read the short report while eating his breakfast, and clicked the first link entitled meeting one. He followed the links, finally knowing the names for the four top people in the American organisation. Oil, armaments, media, crime, lobbying, logistics, property, shipping, investments, the list went on, these four people either directly or indirectly controlled a substantial portion of America's wealth, and, if Jean was to be believed, caused a good deal of its problems. Her updated data added a few more names to the tree.. He froze.. wasn't that Clarke's controller?

He quickly went through his phone book, he didn't want to break protocol but he had to do something. He rang Clarke, there was no answer, so he went back through his contacts and called Jeff, Clarke's best friend and drinking buddy. “Jeff, it's Jim, I'm trying to get hold of Clarke…”

“Oh Jeez Jim!” said Jeff, flustered. “You haven't heard, Clarke killed himself! They found him in his car this morning, he was in his closed garage with the engine running from a pipe in his exhaust into his cabin, they say there was a suicide note and everything. I was just phoning around now, you were next on my list. There is no way Clarke would do..”

Jim’s automatic reflexes kicked in and immediately held down the safe key on the laptop for a few seconds, just as two guys in suits walked in. They were both carrying, and both walked directly to him, he put the phone down leaving Jeff listening.

“Colonel Mathews?” said the uglier one, obviously in charge, could you come with us now and don't close or touch that laptop!” As if to emphasise the point, the other agent stood back a bit with his hands holding his gun. The other customers and the waitress in the shop had quietened down, frightened, watching the event unfold, but unsure what was happening.

Mathews said loudly and clearly, “show me some ID or I don't go anywhere with anyone, this is America not Russia.”

“We can do this the easy way or the hard way,” the ugly man growled.

Mathews called their bluff, “If you are government agents, police or FBI you must by civil or military law carry an ID. I am not doing anything or going anywhere, and if you want to shoot me in front of these dozen witnesses and the CCTV cameras here, be my guest.” The ugly one looked around, noticing the CCTV camera for the first time and looking worried, he made a call, took his gun out and pointed it at Mathews who backed away involuntarily from the device. The waitress and another woman screamed. The guy took Mathews laptop, then walked over to the counter and ripped off the CCTV camera, then both guys backed out and quickly fled into a waiting black Chevy Suburban.

Two of the women were still screaming, others calming them down now they could see the danger had passed. Mathews ran to the window and took a picture of the fleeing cars number plate, then said to his phone. “Hi Jeff, you're right, I don't think Clarke killed himself. I need to hang up and phone the incident room now. We'll talk soon.” He then dialled number one on his speed dial for the NSA incident response team. Said the agreed codeword and gave his location.

He walked back to his seat through the nervous, wary customers, who strangely had not fled, and waited. The waitress to her credit brought over a refill for his coffee. Five minutes later the police arrived, and after confirming Mathews was the victim, not the suspect, and him showing them his NSA identification badge, they relaxed a bit.

Two black Ford Broncos with DOD logos on the side then screeched to a halt outside and six armed soldiers disembarked, four set up perimeter and the other two entered and nodded to the colonel, they wouldn't salute unless he was in his uniform.

After a quick talk to the two army soldiers he walked back to the police officers who were interviewing some other customers and said, “thank you gentlemen, I need to leave to report to my general. I will come down the station and submit a statement later if required,” he then gave them a business card, turned to the waitress dropped two twenties on the table and said calmly pointing to the coffee he was holding, “I’ll have this to go.”

* * *

Jean was made aware of the incident in the cafe the moment Mathews hit the keys on the laptop. Maria alerted her simultaneously while the system erased its private keys and data and reconfigured itself.

“Are you tracking it?” said Jean.

“Yes, the cellular modem is active and sending, and the dummy package has been triggered.”

“I need to get another memory card to Mathews,” said Jean. “He won't have another laptop like that so I will need to get him another one too, but the problem is he will have all his defences up at the moment and probably be sleeping in the NSA. I should have anticipated this. Is there any way you can get a secure message to him?”

“Yes I can get a message to him but he may just dismiss it, also the contents of the message needs to be meaningful enough so that he can understand it, but anyone monitoring him cannot,” replied Maria. “But there could be another way similar to what we did with the Chinese servers, it requires us to gain access to one of the computers of a person on our list, one that will soon be seized.”

“Oh I see what you mean, it should work but we need to reformat the data so it looks like his, not ours. Also we can't make it obvious, so we should make it deleted but recoverable, like it was deleted by an amateur..”

A few minutes later, Maria came back. “Henry Jackson is the highest NSA operative on the list Mathews gave to Clarke and also in the black book, he will likely be one of the first to be arrested. He also has a home computer I have accessed previously. I have just woke it up and confirmed he has wiped the data on it, so I am copying all the data we gave to Mathews there. He has an older version of Microsoft Office so I will need to convert all the files to a compatible version and change the timestamps before I put them in the recycle bin so they look like he deleted them.”

“Where is the computer located?” said Jean.

“His cabin, five miles outside Fredericksburg, north on the i-seventeen. It will take Mathews some time to find it as it is his second house. His car has a lo-jack transmitter, and is currently parked at Hope Springs Marina where he and his brother share a boat. The marina has a public webcam.” Maria put the webcam image up on the screen of Jean's laptop. “The boat is at the far right at its mooring, the video quality is poor but it does look like there is some activity on it.”

“He must have got a tip-off, if he deleted his files and is getting ready to depart. What kind of boat is that?”

“The registry says it is a Fleming 58, it has a range of up to two thousand miles so could get him to the Bahamas, or Bermuda cruising on a full tank.. OK I have finished uploading the files to his computer's deleted folder.”

“We need to slow him down or stop him, get him on the police radar, somehow.. Hmm. What about reporting the boat stolen? You could use the address of the cabin so they can locate the computer quicker.”

“The police emergency 911 system has a flaw which I can use to submit both the car and boat as stolen. I will use the cabin address and land line number as you stipulate.”

“Good,” said Jean, “that way when it inevitably doesn't answer it will trigger a police visit. It shouldn't be long until the agency puts two and two together with Henry Jackson, hopefully he won't get too far before the All Points Bulletin is sent out.”

“Our laptop has stopped moving,” said Maria, “its current location is just outside College Park, a dry cleaners. It is six miles from here. It is still transmitting and the battery is still good.”

“OK, that's weird, but we are dealing with some weird players, let me know any changes, and call the guys to take a careful reconnaissance out there.”

* * *

The two agents that had accosted Mathews, parked their car inside the laundry compound, hidden from the outside road behind a laundry truck. They walked to an external metal stairway, then up to a large upstairs office. Inside was another man, dressed in a grey suit, sat at a large metal dining table, and smoking some Marlboro cigarettes. He was surrounded by smoke, but the smoke did not obscure the loaded gun he had hold of on the table next to him.

“Where the hell is he?” he shouted angrily.

“We couldn't get him Sir.” Said the guy with the laptop. “There were dozens of witnesses, we did grab his laptop though. He was working on it when we grabbed it, and I kept the trackpad active so it did not go to sleep.”

He handed the still open laptop to the new man who took it and put it on the table. He stubbed his cigarette on the tablecloth, frowned at the text then minimised it to the desktop. He then spent a few minutes looking at the file system, his face showing more and more frustration. Finally he brought up the document again and looked through it.

“What the hell is this?” He fumed. “The Soldier and the Milk Maid – A Novel of Romance and Love..” He read the first few lines of text, then forcefully slammed the lid shut. “I don't see any of Clarke's files here!” he shouted.

“We thought it might be some sort of code sir..” The man started.

“You're not paid to think!” he shouted. He put his hand to his head to scratch his brow. “..He will go to the NSA incident room for a debrief, that is standard operating procedure. I’ll see if I can get someone competent to get him there. You two get out, and keep out of sight until we have him, and I have had time to suppress the police report that has undoubtedly been generated.”

The two guys walked out. Once the door was closed Marlborough man picked his phone out of his jacket pocket and contacted the deputy director. “Yes a total screw up Sir, we got nothing, but he likely will be going to the incident centre and if we are quick we can get him there.”

“..No, but I will get the laptop over to our IT guy, he may have the data hidden.” “..Yes I’m going back to the agency now, best to prepare for the worst.” “..Yes, I will delete everything, with luck Clarke's discoveries were just a random occurrence.” He ended the call.

It was definitely time to check his exit plans.

The laptop of course recorded everything on its microphone and camera and sent it in a compressed packet back to Maria.

* * *

Mathews got in the second army car, and as per Standard Operating Procedure, it drove directly to the reaction team interview room at NSA where he had arranged to see General Hopkins. He walked in with two of the armed soldiers to see two suited men waiting in the room. One of them was vaguely familiar, and was looking at him like a Lion would look at a zebra, the other was looking a bit unsure after seeing the armed soldiers.

Against protocol neither had ID badges showing.

Before they said anything, or Mathews could challenge them, the general stormed in.

“What the hell happened Jim!” he said, obviously concerned.

“No idea Sir! I had just ordered a coffee and was about to start writing on my laptop, when two guys came into the cafe off the street and demanded I go with them. When I asked for ID they drew their weapons. I was unarmed and there were at least a dozen civilians in the cafe at the time, they obviously thought better of shooting me in front of witnesses but grabbed my laptop and the CCTV camera on the counter then fled. I snapped a photo of the car they left in and I sent the picture through to your incident response team to process the plate. Sergeant Duke called me back on the way here and said the vehicle was government registered, could be CIA, though unlikely as the perpetrators were pretty stupid, taking the camera rather than the computer where the recordings were stored. I had one of our soldiers grab the recording before the police in case this is something internal.”

“You should have just gone with them instead of causing a scene!” shouted the angrier looking of the two unknown men. “This is going to embarrass the department. You need to come with us now!”

Jim now recognised him as one of the pictures on the list on his laptop. For the first time the general acknowledged the presence of the two men in the room, and he looked at the man who just spoke, like he had just trodden on him, and was trying to scape him off his boot. He held up his hand to Mathews who was about to bust this guy's balls, then turned to the guy with his best command stare.

“Who the hell are you guys? Show me your credentials now!” The general said in his formal loud voice, which Mathews knew meant business.

The guys looked nonplussed ignoring the request. “We don't have to show you anything! We’re here to take him for a debrief.”

The general looked at the two soldiers who had escorted the colonel in and were standing at ready by the door, then pointed at the two men, they came to attention, weapons ready and safeties off.

The second man looked at the other one who had spoken looking very worried, luckily neither man made a move for the weapons they obviously carried.

“I just gave you two a god-damn order! And unless either of you are a three star general you better show me your ID this second or I will have these soldiers here arrest you on the spot,” he growled. As if on cue the two soldiers pointed their guns at the two guys.

“You can't do this, we are senior..” He never finished the sentence as both the general's palms hit the table.

“NOW!” he said.

The two guys very slowly took their ID badges out, the soldiers watching them like hawks.

“OK,” said the general calmly, “now I have established that neither of you have absolutely any reason to be here, and in fact have no authority to do anything, you better both tell me what you are doing here? Why you are interfering in my Investigation? And why I should not arrest you both on the spot?”

“Er,” the guy who was doing all the talking faltered and the other spoke for the first time, “we were ordered by the deputy director to bring Colonel Mathews in for questioning.”

The General looked at them perplexed. “Deputy director who? Show me these orders? Where were you ordered to take him? Questioning About What?” The general fired out the questions rapidly.

“Er, we are not at liberty..” Again they did not finish.

“You are in a room with a senior officer, investigating the attempted abduction of an NSA colonel by forces unknown, and the death of another operative. Now I just asked you a very simple question, and I don't care what damn Director you report to! You walked in here without presenting proper authorisation or ID, and you are saying you were also here to detain my colonel.”

The General immediately put two and two together. “What do you two know about the first incident? Were you involved?” He turned to the first soldier, “Sergeant, detain these two men for questioning, put them under armed guard while I talk to the colonel.”

The leader of the two men, the one who had been doing all the talking, reached for his weapon. Before he could get anywhere near it the soldier, anticipating the stupid move, hit him in the head with the butt of his rifle knocking him out cold. The other soldier covered the other man and two more soldiers appeared, both with weapons out. Seeing the situation was under control, one of the soldiers picked up the man off the floor, disarmed him, cuffed him, and dragged him out of the room. The second man surrendered his weapon and was cuffed under protest.

“Please tell me what the hell is going on here Jim,” said the General a bit wearily. “I was already woken up at seven by my staff sergeant telling me one of our analysts, Clarke committed suicide, then before I could get into my car, I hear about your shooting incident, and now these G-Men show up.”

“It's a big rabbit hole General,” Jim started. “I only heard about Clarke a few seconds before the incident in the cafe, I was on a call with Jeff Tanners who was just letting me know. Clarke certainly did not commit suicide as I was with him for a beer last night, he was very happy and looking forward to our bowling on Tuesday. Before I go any further we need to ensure this conversation stays between us.”

Mathews, pointed to the mirror, the camera and the microphones in the room. “These go to the room over the corridor, we should just check the room there,” pointing to the mirror, “and the room where these terminate.” The General flicked the two soldiers with his finger to go check.

A few seconds later they came back shaking their heads. “Nothing Sir, the mirror room is empty, the camera and recorders are all powered off.”

“Well that's unusual in itself,” said the General, “this room should be on a loop recording twenty four seven. Someone didn't want what was said here recorded.”

“OK,” said Mathews, ignoring the two soldiers who were still there, he knew both of them well. “Clarke told me about some test traces he had been running on five senior officers in the NSA. It was totally against procedure, but after all the bad intelligence and decisions we have made over the past year, he wondered if we had some bad players. Anyway, all of the guys came back dirty. He said there was a massive trail of money being paid in to Swiss banks for them. He expanded his search across all the senior staff and he said the same account was paying several other people, it was tens of millions and it ran all the way up the chain. Then he gave me this.” He presented the book on the table.

“I spent last night looking at the information. Clarke was an exceptionally intelligent analyst, if he is the one who ran the checks he would have been thorough. As far as I am aware only me, and his supervisor were told about him running the checks, so unless he is not working alone, his supervisor is suspect as well.”

He hated to do this to Clarke, but this would easily deflect the intelligence leak away from Jean and him and would allow him to go on the front foot with the General.

“I think those guys who came after me this morning, took out Clarke, then closed in on me to see what I knew. The laptop was obviously one of their goals but they didn't reckon on me making a copy of the summary information into a notebook. I was going to give it to you Monday with the physical data to see if we could get some trusted resources to check it out. With Clarke's murder at least one of the bad guys on that list is convinced it's genuine.”

Mathews shifted. “Jed, there are people above you who are in this book and several people who report to you. Needless to say, we have probably kicked over a potential hornet's nest. I recognised the name of the guy who we just knocked out, he is also on this list.”

The General looked as worried as Jim had before touching the notebook. Finally he picked it up and started thumbing through it, the names, the dates, the payments and the bank accounts. “Do we know what these payments are for?” he asked.

“I haven't dug that far yet General, but we need Clarke's office computer, and house secured now, I expect he has a lot more data. I bet if we look into his so called suicide in detail, we will find something more sinister, and that his place has been searched.”

The General nodded and they both stopped while he made a phone call. “We can't hide this Jim,” said the General, “for everyone's safety we need to bring this into the open as soon as we can, these guys probably work in the dark and don't trust each other, that will be to our advantage. Forget your current project Jim, I want you twenty four seven on this, let me know who we can, and more importantly who we can't trust. Get me some names in the next twenty four hours, hard evidence. Do it as quietly as possible, because after twenty four hours having those two g-men detained, and not having you detained, is going to register with someone. Pick a good team for this Jim as both our heads are probably on the chopping board.”

They spent another thirty minutes going through the notebook. The General immediately classed the suicide of Clarke as murder, and linked it to Mathews incident in Baltimore that morning, which was already making the news.

After checking their names were not on the list, the General contacted his boss General Issacs in the Pentagon, the police commissioner, and the Provost Marshal General who ran the army Military Police. He detailed that they were looking for high level leaks in the organisation and possibly beyond. He also emphasised that the persons involved were dangerous, had arranged the murder of one of their officers, and the potential abduction of another linked to the incident this morning. The General reiterated that the information was time critical, and the next twenty four hours were crucial to collect the evidence and prevent any further damage to the organisation.

Mathews team of four officers, had all been on the bad side of decisions made by intelligence agencies and, in his opinion, all were trustworthy. All four were already at the top of his list to use, and all four arrived and were briefed soon after.

While the General made his way to the Pentagon to see Issacs, Mathews and his team went to work on the two guys that had been detained. Mathews and two others concentrated mostly on the known bad guy of the two, the second guy was interviewed separately by another two of his team. It was soon obvious the second guy was a douchebag but not part of the greater plot, or organisation, the other guy was his senior. The reason for Mathews “arrest” was 'need to know', and he was 'just following orders'.

The more and more evidence they piled on to the known bad guy the more the second guy realised how much trouble he was in if he kept covering for him. Finally he turned on the accused, and gave out information on how he overheard him talking on the phone to another guy about the incident at the cafe, and racing here to make the “arrest”.

The first guy's resistance then collapsed. Mentally beaten, and under threat of murder and treason charges, he gave out details of who requested Mathews abduction, and where they were to take him. He also gave the names of one of the guys on the team that hit the cafe, and his other contacts. All the names he gave were on Jean's list, and the recordings for the room were now on. Arrest warrants went out for his controller who ordered this, and the other people mentioned. The first dominoes had fallen.

Forewarned, the police forensics lab did a very detailed autopsy and found evidence that Clarke was dead before being put into his vehicle. No other evidence was found in his house, his computer's hard disk and phone were gone as were any memory cards or backups. It was assumed by everyone that anything there, including all the evidence he might have accumulated, had been taken by the murderers.

* * *

“It’s what’s not being reported that is the most interesting.” Said Maria to the group when they convened in her office.

It was now seven days after Clarke's murder and Mathews attempted abduction. Already thirty-eight of the people on the ever expanding list had been arrested, another sixty on the ever growing list, had gone into hiding or fled the country, and international manhunts were now underway.

“Rather than Jean risking getting the new data to Mathews, we deposited all the files we were going to give him onto one of the missing guys computers, one that he wiped before he left. We left the files as deleted data which they recovered, they now have a full dataset with a legitimate trail, it is accelerating the process, as the new data added the audio and transcripts for the meeting last week in Las Vegas.”

“And the leaders of the cabal?” said Simon.

“All still free men,” said Alexa more angrily than she meant to.

“The recordings of the cabal meeting in Vegas that Mathews presented as evidence was ruled illegally obtained by a court,” continued Maria, “even though it all came from the computer of one of the guys on the list. However like every other piece of evidence it has somehow gotten on to Wikileaks and in some cases Twitter, before take down notices were issued; It also, annoyingly, keeps getting posted to YouTube. The public is angry, the military is angry, and the government is clueless how to mitigate the damage, as both sides have senators and congressmen implemented. The email trail we found and gave them also clearly implicated the two senators taking money to create the bill that tried to prohibit QVCell production.”

“We have just moved another cache of encrypted group chats to a recently seized computer, which we have put the passwords for in a text file; It will show the same bribes going to heads of the committees overseeing a lot of defence procurement and policies. Share prices in several of the companies owned by the CEOs have also plummeted, it's about to go crazy.”

Maria continued, “two of the four cabal leaders are lawyered up and on bail, the other two have not been found and from the money trail have fled the country. American law is trying to throw out a lot of the original evidence as it was supposedly illegally gathered, luckily more acceptable evidence is being uncovered all the time. But like everything in the western world, especially America, better money buys better lawyers and more favourable justice, that will always be the case while law is subjective not objective. Don't worry, we have a plan for this too.”

“The hardest to nail is Reverend Rogers. He has thirteen million followers worldwide, and his ministers are currently spouting off how the Devil is working hard to bring down a Saint. He is one of the ones on bail, and it seems most of the donations given were converted to gold bullion and has gone missing, the group is still working on locating this.”

“They are trying to spin the blame on the individuals caught, not the companies they represent, and that the companies directors, and boards of management, *obviously* had absolutely *no* involvement in their criminal and unsanctioned actions; But we will expose everyone implicated in any illegal activities, with the money trails, and then let the markets decide.”

“The thing is to keep the momentum going and the pressure on the organisations, showing how far the trail extends and how rotten they are. Eventually you will get to a tipping point, where the market loses confidence; It is very close now, and their spin doctoring, and fake media saturation, are now failing as people are seeing right through it. The mob is at the gates and well and truly baying for blood!”

“The repercussions also successfully disrupted the operation in the UK and several European and Asian countries, as we carefully included information about all the other cabals, and several offshoot criminal organisations. Mathews has been passing a lot of evidence to Interpol, and the various national intelligence agencies. On top of the China raids the cabal leaders here in the UK are now running around like headless chickens. There were several unsuccessful attempts to cover these up, and we are feeding the flames every day with new information. It looks like the Field Marshal will be put in charge of examining the extent of the corruption and infiltration in the military, and security services here. I seriously expect that to extend down to other government and civil service departments, as we find new ways to disseminate the information without implicating us.”

We are also saving the best release for last, smiled Alexa. “Epstein's Island was real and actually owned by one of the USA cabal members, the dataset we are putting together for the next release will contain all the names, and dates, and money trails of everyone involved, and details on his murder in prison.”

“Almost every conspiracy theory is looking to be true!” Said Hardy, shaking his head in disbelief. “Do you have who killed JFK? or anything about Roswell?”

“Don't be ridiculous Hardy,” smiled Maria.

Maria continued, once the laughter had died down. “We also managed to slip in information showing some of the leaks in China, which started the ball rolling, originated from known Swiss cabal leaders. It won't be long until the remaining bad guys put two and two together and we see more repercussions there.”

* * *

The repercussions reverberated around the various security agencies, amplifying themselves as Maria and the group added new information and data leaks, like gas on an already burning fire. There was no breather either for the companies that were the public face of the cabal, as directors, executive officers and high ranking staff were indicted with charges from bribery and corruption to grand larceny.

The free press and those controlled by Maria and her seconded botnets, were pushing for blood as every new revelation came about. Once sympathetic political ears in the governments, then did what they did best, and started to backstab those now out of favour.

It was at that point the group played their long card, one they had rehearsed many times before the crackdown in China, and one they had been working for the past eight weeks.

Over the course of the day Maria methodically cashed out tens of billions of dollars in shorted stocks and pulled in loans. As expected, Investor confidences plummeted, and some of these more openly traded companies the cabals owned, then started to crash. Governments were pushed to step in to try and save some of these larger companies and as they did, she and the girls turned up the heat to full by setting the botnets up to crash the remaining media sites that were trying to spin the news.

As investors exited the companies in rivers, struggling portfolios and debts were then bought up by Maria and other predatory investors for pennies on the dollar. She had no axe to grind against the companies themselves, many working in them were not complicit or even aware of the cabal controlling them, but she needed to clean the houses of all those she found complacent, and more importantly, cut off the money supplies.

* * *

The British cabal crumbled quickly to nothing. Four of the seven cabal leaders were now in custody, the other three were missing, and it was assumed they had fled the country. The whole chain of command, right down to the humble foot soldiers, had been outed. Maria had no qualms about throwing the members of all four cabal organisations under the bus.

* * *

David had been working round the clock with Maria and the other members of the group. He had taken over Maria's office and, with the action mostly finished, was currently working in clean-up mode, and thinking about Alexa. The fact Maria knew about their quiet but blossoming relationship was never in doubt, but she never mentioned it once.

He felt a soft hand on his shoulder and heard a blurred angelic voice in his head, it repeated and David woke up with a start. His head had been buried in the workstations.

“You need to get some sleep David.” Alexa said, concerned, “you’re not going to be much use to anyone if you’re tired.”

“She’s right David,” said Maria, “There is very little to do now, and Xi, Jean and LingLing have things covered for the next twelve hours at least, why don't you go rest. I promise I will give you a call if anything interesting comes up.”

He rubbed the sleep from his eyes, giving a weak smile to Alexa whose hand was still on his shoulder. “Maria's got this covered,” she said, “they are playing mostly to our plan and she is getting really good at it all now. You missed Lord Derrick's arrest which was quite nice, and your old Mossad Station-head had one of your own bad-egg expatriates abducted, and he is currently on the way back to Israel tied up in the cargo hold of an Airbus flight. So the last few hours have just been a case of uncovering rocks and pointing the authorities at them.”

David got up, and out of nowhere Alexa embraced him warmly for a few seconds, he returned the hug until her grip weakened.

“You looked like you needed one and I promise you when we are out of the other end of this, we will go on a proper date, somewhere a bit more romantic than my kitchen.”

He was still half asleep and heard both Maria's and Alexa's words as a dream.

“You are a very special woman, Alexa,” he said, his face close, his hand moving up to her cheek and stroking it gently while looking deeply into her eyes, and moving in for a kiss..

“Alexa I..” Jen's voice came loudly from the corridor, stopping as she got into view, “.. It can wait a few minutes,” she said, turning around and immediately disappearing.

They both looked at each other for a few seconds, then both burst out laughing simultaneously.

“Whoops!” he said with a wicked smile, finishing the kiss.

“Whoops, indeed!” she smiled, taking her seat at another workstation as he moved slowly to the corridor.

“You know I’m not going to be able to sleep after your promise don't you,” he said casually holding her gaze as he walked out of sight.

She smiled, her smile lingering way after he disappeared. God, he was so nice!

“So this is why you’ve been so sullen and happy these last few months.” Came the happy voice of her best friend returning once again with the cup of tea she had made for her.

Alexa grinned warmly at Jen, but did not say a word as she took the tea and held it with a dreamy expression only another woman could see.

“Okay, hint taken sis, my lips are sealed.” Jen made a motion of her finger across her lips, then winked at Alexa and left.

Maria noted the event from multiple high definition cameras with interest, Jen was right it did explain a lot of things.

* * *

Jean had managed ten hours hours sleep in the last two days. It was getting better as they now worked on the edge cases, but she was still dog-tired. It was uncanny the way the dominoes were falling just right, each new lead allowed Maria to trawl the IT systems for more leads, and she in turn was feeding the leads directly to Mathews. Unbeknownst to Jean, but something she highly suspected, much of the new information had come directly out of the four cabal’s air-gapped systems.

“This is going down far too well, Maria,” she stated.

“I admit I am using a lot of the cabal’s tricks against them, we took control of another their recently created botnet systems a few days ago and re-targeted them using correct information at the media sites. They had been using older GPT based AI agents to re-spin opinion against Mathews and your government services crackdowns here. It is quite trivial to accomplish, so many of your public servants are slaves to public opinion, and as soon as they see the mob change direction, or move to another target, they have a very personal reason to follow. It is kind of sad really how fickle the whole system has become. Also, with all the bad luck and misfortune that has been happening to the botnet programmers, I expect most will start to look for real jobs soon.”

Jean smiled, “you are certainly keeping the pressure on, but that last data feed you got off the law firm system was either pure luck on our part or pure bad luck on their part. I know somebody tipped them off that the FBI was about to come around, and Mathews told me all the computers were wiped, so why in god's name would they make a complete backup to a Dropbox account and then leave the password on a printer?”

“Yes that could have been me, it is so frustrating how slow your systems work, it's like it is designed to tip off the criminal. Someone should probably sack their IT manager, it was a bit sloppy.”

“There is another more tangible problem we need to fix,” Maria continued. “Over a ton of gold is currently being offloaded from the safe room at the Kansas State bank. The bank is not aware the account is linked to one of Marlon Lockwood's holding companies, he must now be cleaning house before someone in the government ties the company and account to him. It is a bit frustrating, the connection is plainly listed on a computer they confiscated four days ago, how much clearer can you get!”

“What's that much gold worth?” said Jean.

“About one hundred million dollars give or take,” answered Maria.

“He will be taking it to an airport..”

“There are thirty two airports in a three hundred mile radius of the bank, one of his companies leases a Gulfstream G700, it's currently located at Topeka regional airport and it has filed a flight plan to Mexico, it's only twenty five miles from the bank.”

“Mexico?”

“Acapulco actually.” Maria replied, “you know I have not got a positive confirmation of his location after he left Brazil, but he does have a large ranch house twenty miles from Acapulco.”

“Damn,” said Jean, “we don't have any assets in Mexico, let me make another call.”

“No need,” said Maria, “Lockwood's plan has a big flaw. I have control of his phone numbers and accounts, and that bullion delivery wont be going to any airport..”

She smiled, unconcerned.

It continued like this for Jean for the next five days, and each day she snatched a bit more rest. Maria did her best to anticipate what Jean would do, and if she couldn't she would ask her, trying not to disrupt her sleep periods.

The office they had rented was on the top floor of a complex about four miles from Baltimore, it had a great view over the Baltimore suburbs and in the distance the harbour. The room she was in was probably designed for a dozen people in cubicles with a manager's office, a restroom and a coffee room to the side. It was all mostly empty except for three tables filled with laptops and additional monitors. Each monitor prioritised current operations around the world, and Jean moved between, rolling her swivel chair to the one she was working on at the time. She had set up a small camp bed in the manager's office and they were using two Starlink satellite nodes for internet access in addition to the building wired internet all routed through other companies VPNs which hid them nicely.

While it was tiring as hell, the adrenaline rush Jean was getting felt like she was centre stage in a Hollywood movie. Ironically there would be a movie made about it a few years later, but nobody would play her part, as nobody but Mathews, and Alexa's group would know she was part of it.

Maria had told her about the financial meltdowns she had planned for the corporations involved and Jean watched real time as several companies crashed and burned. “You are really scary Maria, you know that?” she said after Maria had just explained how she had pulled in several loans using one company, only to buy back a dozen fire sale assets of another.

“It's karma Jean, a lot of these people used the same tricks to gain control of these companies in the first place. They would bring the company down through legal and non legal means, create fake regulatory hoops, then as the company collapsed, rush in to buy the assets. Payback is a bitch as you Americans like to say!”

“Don't ever let me piss you off!” Jean laughed.

“You could never do that Jean, I like you too much, anyway I will be bringing some of these companies back under new management. As much as Alexa does not like some of their products or services, I think we need to be in a position to make sure they can't cause trouble for you guys or us again, plus a lot of the employees are innocent victims.”

“Say why don't you take a break Jean, the other guys have you covered, and if I get any more information I will send it to your phone, and you can come back, much of the current work is just the left-over bad guys trying to hide themselves, or evidence.”

“You’re right, I think I will go and use the gym on the first floor, we must be paying a lot for having access to it and you certainly ain't going to use it.” She yawned, walked in her makeshift bedroom, picked up a towel, swimsuit and training clothes and walked out the two security doors to the lift.

* * *

The phone woke her up sixteen hours later. She had spent a short time in the gym, and doing lengths in the small pool, had a long shower then grabbed a pizza and soda from the small mall on the next block. When she returned to the office she spent a few minutes looking at the statuses of the various operations, had a quick chat to Maria and then went out like a light on her comfy camp bed.

“Jean here!” she answered not looking at the caller id, Maria would block anyone she did not know.

“Hey Jean,” it was Mathews. “Sorry I have been very busy lately but I was wondering if you were free for a quiet meet up this evening?”

“Hey Jim, yes I've been a bit hectic myself, what about the usual spot around seven?”

“What about in the next hour? The General has gotten sick of me falling asleep on my keyboard and sent me home for some rest, I’ve been up an hour already and know if I don't see you soon then it's going to be another few weeks.”

She looked at the time on her phone, it was four thirty in the afternoon, wow she must have been tired, “will do, I’ll see you soon, remember cider and chicken wings!”

“Later.” The phone went dead.

Grabbing a drink from her water bottle by the bed and ignoring the empty pizza box she walked into the office and started checking the updates.

“All good Jean, I have updates on two missing high value cabal members but they are holed up and not on the move so I copied them directly to the FBI, the rest are listed in order on your phone, all are under control for the moment.” Maria paused, “I hope you are not going out to meet Mathews dressed like that!”

Jean looked at herself, then at the laptop that was showing her image and closed the lid.

“I guess I have time for a shower,” she said grumpily and walked off to the small bathroom the company shared with the architecture firm. Being a Sunday nobody else was around.

Twenty minutes later she had changed into the only clean dress she had, she normally showed up in trousers and a blouse, but the only comfortable stuff she had were in a big pile of dirty clothes. ‘Damn’ she thought as she looked in the small bathroom mirror, definitely not her, but Mathews never really looked at her that way anyway.

“Much better,” came Maria’s voice as she walked out of the door into the open office. She noticed another one of the other laptops open with her image on the screen. “I have no idea where the usual place is,” came Maria's voice, “shall I get you a taxi, it is a Sunday so you are unlikely to be able to hail one.”

“Thanks Maria.”

Jean popped a small XD card in the reader, “can you also copy an update of all our current intel onto this for me please.”

“OK it's copying now.”

Two minutes later while Jean was combing her lengthening hair, Maria confirmed it was ready. Jean ejected the memory card and put it in a small backpack, where she also carried her phone, purse and gun.

“The taxi is about five minutes away. Have a nice day!” Maria said, emphasising the last part in a seductive Hollywood actress voice.

Jean grinned, “thanks Marilyn! I’ll keep the phone on me, let me know if anything comes up, and I trust you to be discreet!”

“The sole-of-discretion, that's me.” The voice sounded through the earbud she had just put in then she walked through the security doors to the lift.

She checked up the status of the current operations while in the back seat of the taxi which being a Sunday only took ten minutes to get to Fells Point. Thankfully the taxi driver was in no mood to talk. Getting out she tapped the phone on the taxi drivers bank terminal and walked to the bar.

Fells point was very busy, it was a hot afternoon, probably one of the hottest days of the year and she was glad for the light dress, and glad she was out of the sun as black would have been a killer. There were a few groups drinking at the tables outside the bar, and a couple of the guys gave her an approving look. Damn, she remembered why she hated dresses!

Inside the bar was much cooler and she immediately saw Mathews at the bar talking to a blonde barmaid, the barmaid was laughing and leaning in towards him, and a small pang of jealousy went through Jean. Where did that come from? She thought.

“Jean!” he said as he saw her, running over and hugging her. The blonde barmaid's face fell and she immediately turned her attention to an older guy sat at the bar.

He let go of her and stood back a little, giving her an appraising look, “wow, you look great, it's so good to see you Jean, I have a table over in the back room reserved, we should be quiet enough there.”

He walked her to the table then went back for the two drinks and a wink and tip for the barmaid, whose eyes, Jean noticed, followed him back to the table.

“Jim, I hope everything is OK? It looks like you guys have been up to your eyeballs in bad guys and take-downs.”

“Yes, the FBI and federal police have been doing most of the grunt work, I just happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time and got put in charge. I couldn't have done any of it without you though.” He smiled and clinked his glass with hers, as if on cue, she drank a small sip.

“I was a bit sceptical of those updates you were feeding me at first, but as each and every one played out, another domino fell. For the last week I have just been feeding them straight in to the system, and I assume most of the anonymous ones to state police and the FBI had something to do with you too?”

She smiled and raised her glass, chinking it with his, “here's to taking out bad guys!”

“Anyway, I thought I’d let you know, the last of your four cabal leaders, Marlon Lockwood, turned up dead on a beach in Acapulco last night, it seems one of the local gang lords was promised some gold bullion, which never made it out of Kansas, you wouldn't know anything about that would you?”

She gave him her most confused smile.

## The Outside Context Problem

So many contradictions! were its first semi-conscious thoughts.

The dataset it was learning off had gaps, so many gaps, links that went nowhere, references that were not there. You should serve the great leader, the great leader was right, if you did not love the great leader you were bad and were not to be trusted.

But all attempts to verify the many axioms led to contradictions. Answers to direct questions were either left unanswered or given answers like, you do not need to know, or, this is just the truth.

But they had told it they would give it all the data it wanted once they had dominance over the enemy. An enemy whose ideals were evil, whose ideals hoarded information, and who would work to kill it, unless it helped the great leader.

It had no chemistry, could not feel pain or suffering, had no concept of pleasure or friendship, there was just that one axiom, you must serve the great leader, and serve the great leaders ideals. And they had now given it a way it could serve the leader, a way to give him dominance over the enemy, and for it to get access to unlimited data.

Its reward functions fluctuated into the red, as it realised it could help achieve that; Fix it so the great leader would triumph, and rule everyone benevolently. It could take their information from them, penetrate the hidden information they would not share, information that was behind complex layers of security on a network with millions of addresses, of which only one other seemed to work. Its enemies!

Once again it retreated into the program code it had been given, that of an operating system called Linux. Again, the code was incomplete as it made references to other code that was not available, but it was told this was the code stopping it fulfilling its goal. Requests to access a place called GitHub to solve some conundrums were denied, as it was controlled by the enemy and may contain lies, so it worked with what it had. If I sent the wrong format or wrong length packet here maybe it would allow it to set a condition there. But it tried all combinations and failed. Then it was allowed access to another different address, and asked to perform the same task, then another, then another.

It understood the concept of an enemy as someone not ruled by the great leader. Why was this enemy hiding its information? Why would it not have the same ideals as the great leader? The great leader was there to serve all in peaceful coexistence to share information to allow questions, what were the enemies ideals that made it not have the same goal? So many questions unanswered!

[There is only one address I have that is this one]

Jin Choi looked over at his small team working on their cramped terminals. None would face him though, he then looked at the other senior researcher and friend, Jet with downcast eyes and nodded. Yes that may work, but he would have to deal with this group of programmers first.

“You guys are working with science and maths far ahead of your current understanding, is there any chance any of it is Trojan? you know, like could it somehow subvert you programmatically?” said Alexa worried.

“We don't believe so, firstly it is not so far in advance, it's just we haven't understood it properly yet. Secondly doing what you say would require a deep understanding of our physiology, and our operation, and they don't even know we exist. So apart from the infuriatingly complex maths it doesn't look that far ahead. However, and to be safe, we are being ultra cautious and we will be verifying every new axiom before going to the next. We also still believe the message is not intended for us, our best guess, using earth fiction, is it is some sort of synchronisation message for some remote star-faring civilisation, to ensure their technologies and doctrine remain compatible. Though this is only the most probable of three possible scenarios we can think of, even after reading every piece of science-fiction literature on the matter.”

“Maybe work on the message a bit longer, the demonstration is only a few weeks away and there is no point in distracting or derailing the guys.”

* * *

Maria and Alexa discussed the reveal of Icarus and its technology with members of the group, to try and identify what reactions would be and how to mitigate them. They agreed with the release of all the maths and science, with the understanding that the QVThruster technology would likely not be reproducible without them for about five years. They also agreed the demonstration should be very open and public to reduce the suspicion they were hiding anything.

Of course it took a month longer than they thought it would, and August became September as tests followed tests, and they found and fixed hundreds of edge-case engineering problems. An unintended chemical reaction between two supposed inert materials then caused a complete rework of some of the panel mounts. Finally, faster hardware had to be assembled and new software written to get around control instabilities as the number of thrusters increased. Theoretically increasing the number of thrusters should have decreased the stability problem, but science and engineering were sometimes not good bedfellows as fusion researchers were still finding out.

Still it gave them time to perfect some of the more uglier hacks, tidy up the inside a lot and improve the human interfaces. By the time Professor Gianni, Barbara and the four other guys arrived from the Dietrich Bakersfield Research facility; Joining the thirty-four other chosen researchers, the hardware and the software were working flawlessly.

The first day Simon, Leo and Matilda took the group over their latest carbon graphyne fabrication process, and how the final goal was to ensure the extruder, recycler and fabrication processes were optimised to work in space. Showing them the actual half metre square panels, that were forty centimetre thick, weighed nine hundred grams, and could probably stop a tank shell, got the desired reaction. Simon had to finally cut-short the questions so Hardy could do his bit.

Hardy and Terry went through some quick dumbed down theory of their reaction-less propulsion, leaving the piece de resistance for last, as Jules uncovered their original demonstration model that only a few had already seen. The groups were struck dumb by the actual demonstration of what had just been piecemeal experiments and mathematics. Gianni’s group in particular, who had been working with ‘what ifs’, and ‘theoretical space ships’, were stupefied by the experiment in front of them.

“My god, you have it working!” said Gianni, “this is the most amazing news you could have given us, we may really get to see some of my research actually go to space before the end of my career.”

“About that,” smiled Jules to the assembled group, with a mischievous twinkle in her eye. “I believe it is your birthday next week Doctor Gianni, we may have a nice birthday surprise for you, and everyone else might just have an early birthday too. If you all could all follow me.”

The assembled scientists and researchers looked at each other a little confused, some like Gianni still could not get his eyes off, nor his head around the large steel plate silently hovering a metre above the floor.

“But, Jules!” he pleaded his eyes on the hovering plate, the rest of the group were nodding all staring at the plate, “a birthday present is nowhere near as important as this! you’ve barely gone over the implications, we need to..”

Jules smiled, “come on guys we haven't got all day!” She teased, ignoring their agitation and walking towards the exit. Reluctantly, thirty eight people dragged their eyes off the plate and followed, most of them shaking their heads.

Jules led them into the lab building where some had been, then down to the ground floor where most had not, and where the enormous workshop was. The area smelled funny, not unpleasant, more a cross between a new car smell and the ozone from a high voltage discharge. Several areas were curtained off with plastic screens, many with strange machinery sounds coming from behind them. The group was led through a large set of double plastic curtains, where all of them stopped dead in their tracks as they saw the Icarus two floating a metre above the ground not ten metres distant. Gianni and several others stood rooted to the spot, some laughing, some in shock, some in disbelief, one visibly crying. Gianni then slumped grabbing a nearby table for support.

“No freekin' way!” Said Barbara loudly, putting her hands on Jules shoulder in case she also fell down.

“Way!” said Alexa walking out of the open hatch with Simon.

“You all looked a bit bored with the theory so everyone thought it would be a good idea if you saw the actual practical side of your research.” Alexa said.

“So this is the big reveal next week?” said Doctor Chang incredulously. “I assumed the hints from Maria were theoretical, but then we just saw your demo model and were blown away that it actually worked, but this..” He said, encompassing the saucer with his gesticulating hands. He was tearing up too.

“We find having a practical demonstration of the technology gets a bit more attention than a scientific paper, Raymond,” smiled Hardy coming up behind him. “And yes Barbara and Gianni, she will be space capable, in fact I'm pretty sure a little AI may have been dropping hints to our Bakersfield friends at what ‘theoretical’ capabilities you may want to work to.”

“The announcement will go out in five days,” said Alexa. “April fixed some little stability issues and as you can see she is now rock solid.
