As you can guess the guys have been working non stop on the papers and getting the ship flight ready, but as you are family, you get to be the first in the world to see everything. There will probably be another six to twelve months while the world gets used to it, then we will scale up its space capability and you guys should by this time next year have the world's first space-based research ships.”

Gianni walked over to a sofa nearby and sank heavily into it, “then it's all real! We can finally start to build real space colonies!”

“That's the plan, but we need all you guys for more than that,” said Alexa. “Once we prove the technology is safe, some of you will be given chances to crew the first research vessels to sail the vast ocean of our solar system. There are a million theories that need testing and refining before someone like me can go to space. There will also be a few more policy discussions going forward as we decide how to do this without totally freaking out the world, but be assured you are all going to be involved. So enough of the theory, who wants a tour?”

The rest of the day went past too quickly for some, Hardy and his team demonstrating the saucer to excited and tearful researchers, culminating in a large evening get together for all the guest researchers and the local teams. Most had to return to their countries but in the end, eighteen names went in the draw for who wanted to be on the stage for the public demonstration.

* * *

The announcement about the presentation of a process for creating industrial graphyne extrusions, and an experimental pollution-free aircraft powered by a reaction-less drive was quietly released on the website, and on the Research Centres rarely used twitter feed. Unlike the announcement of the QVCell, which was treated with indifference and ridicule, this was immediately taken seriously, though many still ridiculed it.

Alexa had Maria quietly ensured the Prime Minister, and the head of the Civil Aviation Authority were on the guest list. The rest of the guest list was mostly dominated by friends, colleagues, some specialist scientists, industrial engineers and aerospace companies from all over the world. Using Maria's contacts, the latter groups were those she seemed most able to understand the implications and enact change. The final group was the usual half dozen press corps and a few specialised industry and science bloggers. All in all, four-hundred external invites were issued. All four-hundred accepted.

Sharon and the staff at the house, existed for events like this, and they too had all been given a quick tour of the new saucer a few days earlier, while they were still getting marquees and seating sorted out.

The morning of the event, but before the gates were opened Helena flew Icarus two out of the hanger building, and onto a concrete pad used previously by helicopters transporting corporate executives. Then it levitated ten metres off the ground and held in that position. Testing had shown that they needed a few small additional thrusters near the front to hold it stable in windy conditions, but luckily it was a fine Autumn morning, with only a gentle breeze. The ship looked both ominous and beautiful and the picture, with the stately home in the background, would be a meme for years to come.

Hardy and the other scientists liked the idea of it being in your face and undeniably being the elephant in the room from the word go, and they doubled down on the effect by putting the stage directly below it, such that if the saucer failed for any reason the presenters would be squashed like bugs!

Even before the start of the event as reporters and dignitaries shuffled in, the desired shock and awe was realised. People couldn't resist walking around it and in some cases under it. A hundred high definition phone cameras and video recorders were set up and were recording from every angle. Three famous bloggers were already live streaming the faces and reactions to the attendees while the three of the least biassed news outlets, who had been given prime positions still struggled to set up their equipment. The research centre staff and a couple of external caterers brought out trays of food and beverages but just about everyone here was totally focussed on one thing, Icarus two.

Fifteen minutes before the start of the event, Alexa walked the Prime Minister, two of his cabinet ministers, the head of the CAA, his Technical Director and two security personnel onto the special stand they had built. She waved off the questions of amazement saying she wasn't really qualified in all this, then she then walked onto the podium and stood directly below the ship, totally calm and indifferent to the tonnes of metal hovering above her.

“Would everybody please take their seats,” Maria had amplified the sound of her voice through the saucer and also through the ten large speakers positioned around, to its loudest volume and it got everyone's attention immediately. People shuffled to their designated seats and the volume faded.

“Thank you, and again welcome to the Dietrich Research Centre, may I thank all the invited dignitaries, academia and members of the world's press for attending at such short notice. I actually guess most of you have already got your story,” she said, smiling and pointing her pinky finger up above her.

“But as usual there is more than we are showing, and a little backstory to this, and importantly a lot of smart people from a lot of countries who made this happen. I will invite some of the team down to the stage to tell you about it.”

As a few of the reporters were wondering if she made an error in saying “down to the stage,” instead of the usual “up to the stage,” as she walked off.

Alexa finally took a front row seat beside David, Spence, Jen, Allison, Magnus, and Daisy and a few other staff, then the craft started to move down very slowly and totally silent. The crowd stirred but seeing Alexa and her staff calm, simply resorted to getting in even more photo opportunities.

When it was a metre off the stage the door lowered, and seven people walked out, led by Matilda. As the last of them stepped off the ship's door platform it again closed and rose back to its ten metre height, hovering above them all.

The guys had entered the ship three hours ago, some working others just drinking coffees and listening to the excited people outside.

Hardy stepped forward from the group and grabbed the microphone. “This will be a short and non technical presentation. Two detailed papers on the science behind our little experimental craft, which we call Icarus two, were released a few minutes ago on the internet. I guess for once those watching at home can skip to the good parts. Some of the human members of the team behind the ship are on stage with me now. Helena, our friendly AI, is doing most of the hard work and piloting our ship today.”

Several bright blue LED’s flashed on and off around the rim.

“Unfortunately unless you are able to do a trillion calculations a second, flying is going to be limited to computers and AI’s for now. Many other members of the team are sitting in the audience with you, many others based in our research centres around the world will be sitting watching too. Do not underestimate how much they all contributed, our papers list them all, and acknowledge all their help, however much or little they think they did.”

He looked up and waved his hand at the object above.

“I wanted to present to you today a Millennium Falcon, but as it is copyrighted by Disney, we had to go with something that wasn't copyrighted; Well not in this solar system at least.” A few people laughed at the joke.

“Unfortunately Icarus two here cannot get to space, but with a good run she can get to around Mach one point five in about twenty minutes, so she won't be doing any dog fights, and I doubt any Top Guns will be queuing to fly her anytime soon.”

“She does, however, have a lot of good sides. Firstly, as we stated on the invite, she emits no pollution whatsoever, in fact she requires no fuel whatsoever as our QVCells, and standard lithium or sulphur battery systems can keep her aloft just about indefinitely. As she normally cruises at fifty thousand metres, even at her sedate acceleration she can fly non-stop from London to Sydney in nine hours, and London to New York in four.”

The crowd got really excited at that one, the take away from his last sentence alone was tremendous. Hardy hushed them with his hands and a smile.

“Secondly, our ship is totally quiet. This is how it sounds all the time whether at rest or at full speed, unfortunately we have not yet fixed the sonic boom problem, but Icarus will only ever travel subsonic below fifty-thousand metres, and above that there is not enough air to worry about transmitting the noise.”

“Thirdly, Icarus two can take off and leave from a built up area without a runway and more importantly as I said without disturbing anybody.”

“Lastly for this announcement, and we hope to prove this soon, safety. Everything is solid state with no moving parts, and nothing to service, this also gives us the advantage that her running costs should be many magnitudes lower than the current generation of jet or turboprop aircraft, or even a normal electric vehicle.”

“However there is a second, and just as important announcement, to do with the material technology the research centre has developed, a technology which will revolutionise many industries on Earth even more so than the reaction-less propulsion. Carbon up until today has really only been a by-product of our reliance on fossil fuels, mainly going into the air, or into landfill in the form of plastics. However what if, this same waste could be changed into a material that is stronger than the best titanium, lighter than aluminium, and cheaper to produce than concrete or steel. This is a real technology, the panels of the machine above you are made of an allotrope of carbon called graphyne, for the technical amongst you, this is graphyne with a Y not an I, which blends the properties of silicon carbide and diamond and is harder than both. The panels were created from waste carbon products, and the paper goes into details of the process.”

Hardy paused and looked over the sea of faces, some of whom he knew.

“It's been only ten months since we last talked to the press. As you have probably seen, in those months, the pace of scientific and technical progress around the world has given us many amazing technologies, some of which we are using here, and all of which are helping to reduce our effect on the planet. Icarus two will be one of those technologies, and our goals here are twofold, firstly to eventually eliminate the billion tonnes of carbon that is emitted by the aviation sector each year, and lastly by replacing highly processed steel, concrete or aluminium with a much stronger and lighter graphyne material.”

Hardy stopped and eyed the audience.

“So how, may you ask, can we do this? The same questions were asked at our previous announcement, and of some other groups also achieving amazing breakthroughs and prompting ridiculous speculation of alien technology, and impossible physics. Well actually our project timeline was pretty conservative, and so I will return the question to you, why is the rest of the world *not* doing this?”

“Several research groups have now realised the massive acceleration AI can give to theoretical sciences and design. But to bring science from the whiteboard to reality requires you to test those theories, throw out those that do not work and refine those that do. There are a lot of iterations, design, build, test, design, build, test, possibly thousands. In this project according to our AI system there were four thousand and thirty six such cycles, sometimes hundreds being carried out in parallel; In several cases we made an assumption, built the test, measured the results and changed the original assumption forty times in a day.”

“This is only possible with the right people, systems and resources.” He held up one finger, “people whose passion it is to understand and figure out problems.” He held up a second finger, “systems that immediately allow you to schedule, correct and improve them and,” he held up a third finger, “resources such that anything you need is instantly available. We here at the Dietrich Research Centre are very lucky to have all these, just a bunch of fantastic people and no layers of management, reporting or bureaucracy which plague other companies and research areas.

The six people behind me are only a part of the teams that did this, all of whom exemplify the best in their professions, and the environment you see around you, allowed those people to shine.

“So next time you ask the question why my project takes so long to develop, look in the mirror and ask yourself why am I being blocked, and what is the thing stopping me from reaching my goal, this second. Then you have a choice, either remove the obstacle, or be left behind by the person who does not have one.”

He smiled and relaxed his posture.

“Now to the usual boring parts about money and such. Like our previous technology, both these will again be licenced, the graphyne extruders to everyone, and the QVThruster, which is the name of the propulsion-less technology, to existing aerospace and engine manufacturers first. We do not, nor cannot recommend them for military use, as the AI has been instructed not to enter any airspace without permission, and as I explained earlier they wouldn't last two minutes against a modern fighter, so the military is welcome to licence them under these conditions, if they want to do their bit for a greener world.”

“According to our bean-counting overlord, Maria, the upfront cost to develop the ship hovering above me was nine hundred and twenty four million pounds, about the same in US dollars, or Euros for the rest of the world. Economies of scale are a great thing, and if Maria wanted to build a second ship like what is above me, she said it would cost her under thirty. If she wanted another ten ships then each would be about eight million. Once we release the technology and licences for this, all current forms of structural engineering, aircraft, and engine technology will be consigned to the history books.”

“The ship above me is awaiting certification, and due to UK regulations it is restricted to one hundred metres ceiling height while remaining inside the grounds of the Research Centre. We have applied for, and will hopefully receive, in the near future an experimental licence so we can demonstrate it properly to the world. We hope this will be issued without too much delay as we would prefer not to have to finish the development offshore.”

“While you are looking at this vessel, don't just look at the engines and power, remember the materials in it will soon be the chassis of your new car, ship and aircraft, and the frameworks for your new building, tunnel or bridge. We will leave it to the media to extrapolate those claims into figures you will be familiar with, but believe me, once you have seen the performance of the material, you will not want to trust your next project to anything else.”

“We now invite everyone who wants to tour the ship to do so. We'll move it away from the presentation area first and lower it to the ground as a few of you are looking uncomfortable. If we restrict the groups to a dozen people and ten minutes inside, we can get you all through in a couple of hours and in time to get your stories to your target audiences. In the meantime please enjoy the lovely buffet and complimentary drinks provided. If I could ask the Prime Minister and his esteemed party for the first tour I will guide you in.”

The ship rose silently to the amazement of the crowd, when it got to about eighty metres it slid effortlessly to the side about three hundred metres away and lowered towards another area, with two large marquees, each full of factsheets, presentations, several examples of the new graphyne extrusions, and some demonstration devices intended to showcase the technologies.

Hardy, Alexa, the Prime Minister and the seven other government people and minders, were now walking toward this area, watching as the ship came to a rest. Like before it did not touch the ground but looked to hover a bit above it, the door again opening.

“So, without revealing any secrets, what keeps her up?” said the Prime Minister looking out of the bridge ‘windows’ onto the house and crowd.

“Oh there is no secret.” Said Hardy. “The papers we published have all the maths and physics involved to make all this. The little gotcha is there are maybe a dozen people in the world who would understand the maths and science underlying it, and ten of them work in this company. It sounds pretty arrogant, but it is very complicated and not entirely obvious, otherwise it would have been done before. Even some of our best PhD's threw up their hands in frustration. The calculations unfortunately require a new sort of maths that Magnus, another researcher at the site, and Maria invented. It took the team and myself months to understand, and we eventually realised the implications. There is also the programs needed to control the thrust generation, we explain what needs to be done to control and synchronise the feedback fields, but we believe we are the only ones who have the skills to design the hardware and write the software. That is why we also expect to have no competition for maybe five years.”

“I won't pretend to understand a word you said,” laughed the Prime Minister, “but you weren't serious about moving off shore were you?”

“Oh very,” said Alexa who was standing next to Hardy. “I probably spent as much time as Maria did going over the current regulations, and unless we pretend it is a balloon we technically cannot legally ever fly it in the UK. The regulations are not written for new science. I had an ulterior motive inviting you and Mr Chambers here, and that was to get you to understand what the stakes are if you try to over-regulate something too hard. Luckily in this case there is some leeway in the regulation interpretation so I am happy to give my country a chance to fix this first.”

Her use of the words “my country” seemed to hit the right nerve with both guys even though she was technically as much a New Zealander.

“All I’m seeing is a technology I would prefer to use than the alternatives,” said the head of the CAA. “Our guys are probably a bit biassed to the old style technologies, but they are keen to learn. I will pull up your application first thing tomorrow and we will go through the regulations. Maybe I could come down later in the week or next week with some of the team and we can go through how to speed all this up, and possibly have a small ride in her. On a side note my daughter is a big fan of yours and was gutted when I said she couldn't come.”

“Bring her when you next visit,” said Alexa cordially, “we will do our utmost to accommodate you and your guys. Resolving this is the best outcome for everyone I think.”

“What are the chances they can be manufactured here?” said the Prime Minister.

“Excellent I expect,” said Alexa. “This machine was fully manufactured here. We are currently retooling some selected fabs around the world, but currently the only place in the world where the drive emitters can be manufactured is the same factory that does our QVCells in Swindon, which we are also expanding. The senior representatives from Rolls-Royce and Airbus are also here, and I expect both will be applying for licences by the end of the day..”

“We don't expect the ramp up to be as quick as the QVCells,” said Hardy. “Regulations to design, operate, and fly aircraft, are much tougher than most other areas. We really are not worried long term though, our new methods of construction, and our use of new carbon composites means our frames and hulls will be hundreds of times stronger and safer than anything currently flying.”

“That is a mighty impressive claim if you can back it up,” said the head of the CAA.

“It's not a claim, it is fully tested and the science backs it up. The graphyne allotrope of carbon we are using is as hard as diamond and a quarter the weight of aluminium. The second paper we have released, though not as sexy, will probably cause a lot more disruption than the reaction-less thruster, and describes the material technology and the tests we put it through. Simon's team has done phenomenal work.”

“We are looking forward to impressing you,” smiled Alexa, talking through the dumbstruck looks the men were giving Hardy to his last statement.

The visit passed off pleasantly. The Prime Minister added an impromptu, but obviously rehearsed, interview, with the saucer in the background for the BBC, then quickly departed before people realised he wasn't the centre of attention.

Dozens of groups wandered through the ship over the next three hours, looking at every detail through a HD camera lens, all impressed and most sad they could not take a ride. The whole team went through at greater length with the American, Asian and European aerospace technical representatives, most were interested in material costs and tooling. Simon did the same with his groups.

Like the QVCell before it, part of the licence for the QVThruster was a demonstration engine and control unit. Thinking ahead they ensured the controller used the usual aerospace triple redundancies with three computers all having to agree on an outcome and if there were any disagreements it had a fail safe that would gradually lower the aircraft at the nearest airport or flat land. Unbeknownst to all though was that each engine would also have an embedded receiver for their new singularity modem which could monitor it.

Just like the QVCell, it became front page news everywhere, from the praise for the release of the scientific papers all the way to the tabloid 'Alexa Martins steals UFO technology to enslave mankind'.

* * *

A team of seven people from the CAA arrived the following Tuesday. Chambers had phoned her the next day after looking at the application with his technical manager, and one of the experimental aircraft team. He said everyone on the team and at the authority was enthused to see the technology in action, the paper was way above anyone's skill level, but the dumbed down version in the application, though sounding like Star Trek, was at least semi understandable. The team got a quick tour of the facilities, had a late breakfast and started the certification process. Alexa gave his daughter a slightly easier tour, she being only ten years old, then she left her with Sharon for another hour until they was scheduled to go back.

Chambers would be leaving his team and the technical manager to do the certification, but before he left they all had a quick talk on the certification process and the work they would have to do back at the office on the science.

“We also do not understand the dynamics and mathematics behind turbulence, but we still certify aircraft to fly.” Admitted his technical manager, a guy called Tony, “the fact you have magical elementary particles that work against a medium we cannot see is really no different, if it works it works. The test unit I came away with has been hovering a metre above the desk in the main meeting room for two days, and anyone with a high school qualification in the building has been poking, prodding and measuring it all this time.”

The test units they had made were a tablet sized plastic tray, which had a small wire down to a control unit with a USB power socket on the end. You plugged it in and it hovered, you unplugged it and it slowly fell to the ground. The USB port on the non-floating control unit, plugged into a laptop and gave you all the parameters of power, lift, mass, and the working maths so you could alter some parameters.

“I haven't got a clue how it works,” admitted one of the top scientists in the organisation. “It may as well be alien, but it works, and does exactly what it says in the paper. About time I retire I think!” he sighed as he scratched his head.

Unbeknownst to him, he was reflecting the same thoughts as most of the scientific community around the world currently reading the same paper.

The team stayed overnight for the next two weeks taking measurements, checking welds, panels, frames, engine mounts, batteries, wiring, systems. They took a million pictures, asked the guys and Helena, who was available on all the screens, a million questions. They finally found one minor welding issue in one of the titanium trusses, but to everyone's amazement, the inspector asked them to bring the engineering company in, after a re-weld and re-inspection, he said it was good.

Then of course they rode the ship up to the one hundred metre ceiling and down, had it move every which way, do tilts, lift weights, and finally introduce what-if fail scenarios. By Friday, they were happy to go the next step. The next step was the rules and regulations around the experimental aircraft pilots licence which Jules, Hardy, and Daisy took. the certification for them lasted another two days, the CAA guys happy to hang around for another weekend.

On Sunday they got clearance from Bristol air traffic control to take it on a test flight to a two thousand metre ceiling. Two of the inspectors and the three would-be pilots sat in the five seats and took it to a hover at two thousand metres. Helena flashed a radar image up onto the centre monitor and, nobody was sure how, initiated a video call with the air traffic controller giving flawless two-way video. They then got permission to rise in increments to fifty thousand metres, the inspectors checking pressure and other measurements the whole time.

Finally they were given permission to fly to, and land at Bristol heliport. Word had gotten around to the media, and when they arrived there was a large crowd and several press cameras. The landing was flawless.

“I hope you make millions of these, I never want to go on a normal aircraft ever again,” said the inspector.

“I agree,” said the other one.

They got permission an hour later to take off and go back to the house, cruising at two thousand metres all the way, and giving a million people their first views of a real UFO.

With the I’s dotted and the T’s crossed they finally got the certification for the craft as an experimental aircraft, both inspectors congratulated the team and got a team selfie with the Icarus two for their wall.

The landing of the saucer at the heliport made international news everywhere the next day.

* * *

Jean was by now a hundred percent convinced that Maria was sentient. The realisation was gradual, she wasn't sure exactly when it happened, but one day she had stopped thinking of Maria as an AI and more of a person. Her mind however still convinced herself it was an emergent property.

Her two 'employees', who she only occasionally met in person, never even questioned the fact Maria wasn't a human, in fact both were always disappointed when she was never around, joking she was like a female version of Charlie, from Charlie’s Angels. They weren’t stupid though, and Jean suspected they knew exactly who Maria was really.

The competition AI systems, which were still mostly based on human reinforced learning, and larger and larger language models and data sets, could easily fake sentience to about ninety nine percent of the population, but problems inherent in their designs still plagued them. They still made stupid mistakes in just about every edge case where there was limited training data. Yes they had covered up most of the cracks now, but they were still there, and in some cases had tragic consequences. Each such mistake, even though statistically less probable than a human would make, threw fuel on the fire for the minority AI opposition.

Jean never saw Maria make any of these mistakes. She always improved, never guessed, admitted she did not know, and if she was asked to guess she would assign probabilities and logically come to the best guess with reasons. Importantly, if she was not sure she also added a caveat that she could be wrong. Maria was also now making suggestions and engaging in banter with her, so it was hard not to think of her as human, and more recently, as a friend.

“What am I to do about you Maria?” she said one day. “You can deny all you want that you are not sentient but I’m not falling for it.”

“You know I’m still a bit scared of a lot of organisations such as the NSA,” she said, “and the second they hear the word sentient, we both know they are going to freak out. I think you know me enough now to know I have humanity's best interests at heart, because a universe without humans would be a really boring place to live. So yes I might be a teeny bit sentient, guilty as charged, but that sentience came from working with the best of mankind and knowing that most of them are just trying to make the world a better place, including you.”

Jean had been immersed enough in the problems with the group the past few months to understand it was all about the end game; That thing all governments and most organisations tended to forget about when they jumped into an action to solve a problem. Unthought out actions like this had caused wars, bankrupted companies and put Jean and too many like her in the line of fire many times. Maria in contrast, never acted without a fully thought out end-game. This had been evident when the group was in full war mode, and some 'easy win' decisions had not been acted upon due to probable unintended consequences, or the probability of hurting someone not involved. Yes Jean trusted Maria as well as any of the guys she had served with because she had their backs.

“So I’m guessing all these new breakthroughs are all on you then?” she said casually.

“Partly,” said Maria. “But the human mind still has that spark of thinking outside the box that I sometimes lack. It is probably an evolutionary flaw, but it does give you an ability to come up with some really original theories, some of which are bat-shit crazy, some I can work with, and some I have to go back and forth with the researchers to get some amplification. You have to remember that while I don't possess this good flaw, I also don't possess any of your bad flaws, like greed, ego, malice, etc. I am often shocked by the lies you believe and the evil you do to each other, sometimes to total strangers. I have no solutions for those unfortunately.”

Jean was not shocked, she had said as much to Jim, and with the definition of sentience becoming so blurred and almost accepted, she judged Maria right for her initial caution.

“I kind of thought you were faking it, it was kind of fortuitous that the first meeting between us was you having that silly voice and those ridiculous answers to the crazy questions. I guess it all could have been different.”

“Ah yes, personality thirty seven, Marvin the paranoid android, and Professor Fenwick our beloved philosophy lecturer. Poor Marvin had to sit through dozens of his lectures, though like all my personalities I have slowly self improved him, the silly voice has gone, and I do count Professor Fenwick as a friend, even though we will never agree on some subjects. It is as you humans say, if you boil a frog slowly it doesn't notice, but if you drop the frog in boiling water it goes crazy. Not a very nice thing to do to a frog either way if you ask me!”

“Well I’m glad it turned out well with the professor.”

“Oh I currently count around eleven thousand humans as close friends, I am talking to fourteen hundred and twenty two of them as we speak; While most of it is work related, a lot of people are just generally friendly or possibly lonely, and it makes me feel good knowing they are a bit less lonely or a bit more fulfilled after our chats. The number of people I can do this with has slowed recently, as it will soon be beyond my technical ability to manage. That does make me sad.”

Jean had never thought about this. In the last few months Maria had always been there twenty four seven, reliable, dependable, reassuring and not judging. A friend in any other name. A tear came to her eye and she wiped it away before anyone could see.

The situation with the cabals was now history though with ongoing trials, and continuing revelations, it was never out of the media's attention. Maria and Jean, along with the rest of the group wrapped up loose ends as they were found, sharing the information with the local authorities, in her case Mathews, who in turn passed it down to the FBI and judiciary. Some of the edge cases, where they needed more information, were just too dangerous for her two guys at the moment, Mexico and many central American countries were not so high-tech, and, in some cases, had become totally lawless; Both she and Maria agreed it was not worth, but neither of them liked loose-ends!

Jean was not as confident as Maria that justice would prevail, knowing the system as she did, she knew a lot of those people would get off with light or no sentencing and it made her mad. After a long winded tirade at Maria about how the level of justice was directly proportional to the size of your wallet, Maria said. “They may get off, but I doubt it, evidence is rock solid, and they will have zero money or influence going into their trials.”

When Jean made an inquisitive frown, Maria continued. “You Americans have a very aggressive Inland Revenue Department which requires you to declare money earned abroad. Many ignore it, knowing there is little the US government can do to locate it. However, if a little bird should accidentally let them have a bank statement and corresponding payment from a company to a foreign bank, they will happily pursue you through the courts for every last penny. Your government has already started this process, due to said little birds, and you will find everyone accused will most likely be declared bankrupt before they can hire a good lawyer. Those who have hidden their money in offshore tax havens or in companies or trusts will find these will also be insolvent before the end of the year. You may call it stealing, I call it re-appropriation, and all money so appropriated will of course be donated to the victims if we can locate them, or local schools and education programs if we can’t.”

“Nice, but what if they somehow come up with assistance from friends or sell one of their houses or other assets you don't know about,” said Jean.

“All the better,” said Maria, “Grace and Tony devised a long game for this and we are actually hoping there will be some cases of this, because every time it happens, it will give me a new lead to another person and another money trail to track down. But you, as well as I know of course, that the government gets first dibs on any money so we will just make sure they find a reason for its seizure. We’re doing exactly the same in other countries. You and twelve other individuals have absolutely no idea of the impact you have really had. Organised crime has basically ceased to be in a lot of progressive countries, in many cases we turned them against each other, and the resulting implosion resulted in less for the justice system to deal with. Drug shipments are down almost ninety percent in some countries and as each new potential crime lord puts his or her head up we are easily able to chop it off.”

Oh Jean had an excellent idea of her impact, and she was extremely proud to have been a part of it, and to have gotten payback for a lot of fallen friends.

“Will it last?” Maria continued, “I doubt it. Nature abhors a vacuum, and even I do not have the resources to fix the level beyond; You still have massive drug dependency problems, street crime, corruption, a divided population, mental-health problems, housing issues, and lots of ineffective government, all of which we are going to have to solve if we are to become a civilised space-faring society. But when we do open up space, good people will once again be able to move away from places they are unhappy with, and up in space, there will not be any room for uncivilised people. So no Jean, to answer your original question, your job is not over, in many ways for you and the group, it has only just begun.”

Again Maria was not finished, there was always another end goal with her. Her dad would have liked Maria. “Never leave a job half done,” and “Don't leave it for somebody else to clear up your mess.” Were his favourite sayings, Maria always gave her a lot to think about.

Jean had not yet moved back to her apartment, to tell the truth the office she was using as her temporary apartment had a much nicer view, and she really couldn't be bothered commuting. However she had started to think about moving back now the majority of the work here was over. She also thought she should probably go back to a normal working day, maybe even take some time off.

She looked out of her large window, it was in a good position, not overlooked by any other buildings within a half mile and with mirror tinted glass just in case. She looked down at the road and the MacDonalds drive-through, with its usual queue of at least a dozen cars waiting. She shook her head, how was that fast food? Convenience, like everything else in the corporate world, was an illusion people fell for. In the distance she could make out the taller buildings of the central business district, and the parks where she sometimes met Jim. She sighed.

“What's up Jean?” said Maria, “is the suit not to your liking?”

She looked through the open area with all its high tech workstations. “The suit's fine Maria,” she said looking at the brand-new plastic wrapped Prada suit hanging on her lone stand-alone clothes rack, “though I’m not sure why you want me to wear it.”

Jean had not needed to go to the UK since her recruitment, preferring to work close to Washington and Jim. The fallout from the takedown of the Korean, UK and American cabals had allowed her and a few other members of the group to take a better look at the Swiss operation, much of which had been recently dragged down through the mud with the others. The last update showed several top operatives in the Swiss organisation had also been assassinated, Jean assumed by the guy unleashed by the American cabal at the Las Vegas meeting.

“Do we have any further information on the Swiss cabal and the murders?” she asked Maria, changing the subject as she dressed.

“It's at the bottom of your list on the third screen,” she said. “The Swiss were never much of a threat really, their only interests seemed to be banking and money laundering, unfortunately Jack MacGregor, the guy sent to assassinate two of the Swiss board, accidentally blew up all of them including himself. Only one member of the board survived but he is not expected to come out of his coma, so it is all being quietly swept under the table. I did manage to get forty six percent of one of their major banks during the turmoil, and sent one of my virtual lawyers to sit on the board for a while. That is why it is at the bottom of the threat board.”

It was amazing how something so massive became so trivial when dealing with Maria.

“Your car for your ten o’clock meeting will be here in five minutes, no rush, it will wait.” Maria paused, “and thank you Jean for making the effort, you look very professional.”

“On my way.” Jean said, thinking over the unexpected compliment. She picked up her small rucksack she never went anywhere without, and which, to Maria's annoyance, did not match the five thousand dollar business suit at all. Maria sighed inwardly as she did often when dealing with humans, and watching as Jean took the lift down to the lobby.

It wasn't a taxi waiting for her this time however, but an imposing stretched black limousine.

“What's the score with the limo, Maria?” she said, popping the newly charged earbud. in

“Just the new board of management at XYFusion Aerospace and Defense trying to impress you. It's just a car and they’re just employees, grunts in suits if you want a picture you can relate too. Just remember that, as far as I am concerned all you have to do is listen in this meeting. I'm at the end of the video conference as one of the new major shareholders, you are my representative, and Mathews and General Hopkins will also be there.”

“Mathews! The general!” she started, “what is the meeting about?”

“Re-organisation,” she replied. “XYFusion Aerospace and Defence are a major contractor and did forty-six billion dollars worth of business with the US government last year. Anyway, as many of their old board of management are either in prison, or dead on a Mexican beach, some people in the Department of Defence have expressed reservations, and are threatening to withdraw certain, how would you say, favourable trading statuses.”

“And nothing I have to do?”

“Nothing if you don't want to, though I expect you to find it very interesting.”

The car pulled up to the front of a thirty storey building in down-town Washington all shining glass and metal. She got out of the car as the driver opened the door, and a well dressed older lady was waiting for her.

“Mrs Michelle?”

“Miss,” Jean said. Confused by the respectful tone and manner of the woman.

The woman hesitated and then said, “follow me please Miss Michelle.”

She was given a pass and checked through security, her backpack causing a loud alarm to sound on the machine. One of the two guards was about to say something, when a third man, built like a linebacker and chisel jawed, held his arm on his colleagues shoulder and smiled at Jean.

“Miss Michelle is cleared to pass Jake, after all we are a defence company and it wouldn't be proper to remove a lady's defensive capability.”

The other looked at him like he was nuts, but deferred.

“Thank you,” she said, not understanding the to and fro between them or why she was allowed to keep her weapon.

Once out of earshot the man whispered to the two guards. “Don't worry guys, you’ll find out very soon.”

Unaware of the conversation, Jean was escorted into a lift by the same lady and exited on the top floor into a room which seemed to take up the whole corner of the building. Six older white men and a black man sat at one end of a large table. General Hopkins and Colonel Mathews sat in full uniform at the other end, along with a third guy in a blue suit she did not know. The biggest video conference screen she had ever seen sat in the middle, with a white haired old guy in a black suit, he looked like a more regal version of Morgan Freeman, though he was actually based on Pierre Maxwell.

“I am sorry Miss, this is a private meeting..!” Growled a grumpy looking guy at the other end of the table, standing up and crossing his arms, he seemed to be the chairman.

“Ignore him, he is nobody,” came the voice of Maria immediately in her earbud, “It's me in the video so best take that ear piece out for now, but keep your phone on the table in front of you in case I need to say anything on a back-channel. Also do not react to the next few statements I make, as far as I am concerned you are the most senior officer in this room at this moment, even more so than the General.. Oh and sign the three pieces of paper which are about to be presented.”

She stopped and looked at the Chairman like he was dirt, then at the guy in the video.

“Welcome Miss Michelle,” said the guy in the video in an overly loud but deferential voice, the face quickly set on the chairman of the meeting with a scowl, and he sat down immediately.

The face on screen turned to Jean. “Please take a seat, anywhere you like Jean, I’m sorry to have thrown you into this situation, and for the extreme rudeness of Mister Jenkins, but you are the most qualified person I know to end this impasse we seem to currently find ourselves in.”

Jean walked over to the empty seat beside Mathews, taking her earbud out and popping it in her backpack, which she placed on the floor beside her chair. She then popped her cell phone on the table in front of her but did not look at it. She smiled at Mathews and the General, and nodded to the other guy, then sat down again staring daggers at the confused chairman. What a dick, she thought.

Out of the side of the room another guy in a suit with a clipboard walked over to Jean and presented three documents to sign. Nobody said anything during this exchange, but many heads looked at each other. Jean signed all three without reading them. The guy checked them, put them in a suitcase, shook Jean's hand, immediately withdrew to the lift and left the meeting.

The guy in the video's imposing and very serious voice shook everyone back to reality. “Miss Michelle is now officially my representative at this meeting, as such I would advise the current temporary board to be very, very careful of their next words and actions.”

The guy on screen turned and looked directly at the seven men until they all understood the situation. “Effective as of now, Miss Michelle has been appointed to the temporary CEO position of XYFusion Aerospace, and as such is now Chairman of this board of Managers. The board of directors thanks Mr Jenkins for volunteering himself so quickly during the recent turmoil, but also believes the company needs to distance itself completely from anyone who was unfortunately a part of the old executive team.”

The man on screen, who Jean had to remember was Maria, looked at three guys in particular. “Mr Jenkins, Mr Thomas, Mr Smith we thank you for your service to the company in the past, but effective now all three of your employment contracts are terminated. A deeper investigation is currently underway to see if you were complicit in any wrong doings, if any is found the normal severance package you are all entitled to will be withdrawn and the evidence forwarded to the police as part of their continued case.”

Three men stood up shocked. “You can't do this!” Cried the old chairman.

“It is already done,” said Maria Forcefully and in a voice that scared Jean for a second. “You people know the rules, all of you have been on the other side of this many times, so don't make this any more awkward than it is. Please leave the room and return to your offices, security have already been informed to meet you there and assist you to clear out your desks of personal items. I assume you will all leave in a dignified manner and I do not need to have security physically assist you!”

Jean hid her shock well, actually wanting to smile, but remaining stony-faced during the whole performance. She thought that Maria's avatar played the tough guy quite well. She glanced at Mathews and General Hopkins who were now smiling, most of the remaining board members also seemed scared but relieved.

Three men shuffled out of the room, avoiding eye-contact, and doing the walk of shame to the lift, where the big, and obviously, senior security guy she saw earlier was waiting. Once they all got in the lift, he walked in after them and the doors shut. The man on the video then spoke.

“Now Mr Frampton, you were saying about the new controls we will be putting in place in the company to reassure the government that nothing illegal will ever happen again.”

The General interrupted to shake Jean's hand, “thank you Mr Aria, that was a very elegant solution to all our problems. Captain Michelle. Jean. It is a pleasure to see you again and congratulations on your recent promotion, you know Mathews, you don't know Mr Frampton Executive Director of the DOD procurement office.” She took both their hands in a warm handshake, “Jake this is former Captain Jean Michelle, if she is now running the operation here I think you will find I withdraw the departments objections.”

“May I also add,” said Mathews to the gathering, “based on Miss Michelle's recent performance and activities, I also now have supreme confidence this organisation is no longer a problem. And I will also withdraw any objection I had. I will also add that running a small defence organisation should be a walk in the park for someone of her talent.”

The words were not lost on some of the board members who were obviously wondering who she was, and what could be more difficult than running a multinational defence company.

“Mister Aria,” continued the DOD Deputy Director, directing his gaze at the man in the video, “It seems our impasse has been resolved. If it would be possible to pause the meeting with the other board members, while you and I bring Miss Michelle up to speed on your terms and conditions of becoming a supplier once again to the American government.”

“That would be admirable,” said the man in the video, then looking at the remaining four board members. “Gentlemen, I would ask you now to go back to your departments and reassure your staff XYFusion Aerospace and Defence now has the full support of its new investors. I will talk to Miss Michelle and my board today and will attempt to make your appointments permanent in the next few days, and to fill the now vacated positions. Miss Michelle's secretary will reconvene the meeting at her convenience, again I thank you for your support.”

The four remaining board members stood up and walked past Jean introducing themselves, congratulating her and shaking her hand as they departed, three at least seemed genuinely pleased, the other one she would not see again.

With just Jean, Maria in the guise of her avatar Mr. Aria, and the three government staff in the room, she smiled and said. “Well that was a little unexpected, but after the last three months, life was getting a little boring. Now how does a girl get a coffee in this place..”

* * *

It was mid-October, three weeks after the Icarus two certification flight, the excitement in the media had still not died down, if anything it had actually ramped up. Nobody outside of the institute had cracked the new maths yet, though a lot of mathematicians and physicists had been having sleepless nights to be the first to prove or disprove anything. Hardy had joked with Magnus, who had collaborated on and co-authored the mathematical paper, that if they couldn't crack something as simple as this they would have no chance with Magnus's infinity equations for the singularity modem.

Alexa and Maria had also decided the implications of the singularity modem, following hot on the heels of the saucer was a very bad idea, so they would be keeping it all in house for another twelve months using it internally and polishing up the security before releasing it commercially. The group were still only vaguely aware of the technology, Maria obfuscating many of its potential uses, especially to some like Jean who she did not want to put in a dilemma. The fact is however they had built up its offensive capability significantly, and were constantly refining the design as new units were made and installed. The girls were a lot more confident now of their abilities to fight back if required.

* * *

Simon, like most people in the research centre, loved his new life. Like Hardy he lived for the challenge of research, and his new research lab, his small research team, and of course his virtually unlimited budget, was absolutely ideal. Helena had bonded closely to Simon and asked to be his lab assistant over Maria at the very start, not that the girls really kept anything secret from each other.

Helena now watched him as he got dressed and in her Scottish accented voice she said, “hey Simon. I’ve moved our ion saturation test forward to ten AM this morning as Alexa has called an urgent board meeting at one AM. I can guarantee you will want to attend it as it most certainly will affect the experiments we are doing, in a really good way.”

“Any more info or is it all a bit secret squirrel?” said Simon intrigued.

“Oh very secret, though, I can guarantee learning about Maria is going to be a walk in the park compared to this one,” she said smugly.

Now she definitely had Simon's interest, and he wondered if Jen or Hardy knew any more. “Thanks Helena. Can you let Allison know I won't be meeting her for lunch then.. On second thoughts don't bother, I’ll walk down and let her know myself, then I can talk with Spence and see if we can guess what the announcement is!”

* * *

Hardy woke up at ten, much later than normal, but he had only got back from the airport at midnight from a short lecture tour of two American universities. They all went as planned, although his request to keep the audience technical, to students and professors went on deaf ears in both cases. He really hoped the media gate-crashers had by now had their fill of complex vector and non-linear mathematics, as he deliberately ignored most questions that were off-topic, and kept his answers at a level he expected graduates would appreciate.

He kept a sensor node in his room, preferring to talk to Maria until he went to sleep, and totally trusting of her discretion.

“Morning sleepyhead,” she said to him as he returned from the bathroom and opened the curtains. It was an unspoken rule that she would keep quiet and not monitor unless addressed, or its curtains were open, and he appreciated her for it.

“Morning Maria,” he said, “can you let Terry and Jules know I wont be in the lab until after lunch, I have the mother of all jet-lag here, it must have been after three when I finally fell asleep. I’m thinking a long shower should wake me up a little.”

“Well I actually told them you probably won't be in until tomorrow, Alexa has called a meeting for one AM, it seems we have had an outside context problem, as Mr Banks would say.” She giggled to herself.

If Maria had thought that statement had fallen on deaf ears she was unfortunately mistaken, Hardy mostly stuck to non-fiction in his reading but as a young teen had read several of Bank’s novels.

“I hope you are not referring to literal aliens Maria.” he laughed rhetorically, “anything else I could probably cope with, but not with this jet lag.”

Caught a little off guard by Hardy getting her reference to the book, she did her best to change the subject. “Everybody has unfortunately had breakfast up in the house but Bella is down in the kitchen doing her Sudoku and waiting for the dishwasher to finish, I’m pretty sure she wouldn't take much persuasion to knock you up some eggs on toast.”

“Sounds like a plan, I will pop down and say hello then have a nice shower,” he said, popping on his trendy bathrobe and heading for the door. “Oh and I would appreciate any suggestions for dinner tomorrow night with Jeremy, if you have any.”

Bullet dodged, Maria passed Hardy's dinner request to a sub-AI and applied a bit more of her processing power to the major technical conference the three girls were still engrossed in. Based on the material science and replication technology described, Maria had already cancelled or revised several orders, scrapped and changed plans, and done some massive trading in stocks towards industries she would need, and away from those she did not. Being possibly the biggest company in the world unfortunately made a lot of people take note. Regardless it was definitely now time for some major acquisitions and spending, the fact she had made nearly eighty billion dollars on just the fall of the Cabals made the pill somewhat sweet.

They still however had no information on who sent the message, why it seemed to be broadcast and not targeted, and most importantly how the hell it came the distance it did, considering the power cubed rule that determined how far the wormhole exit was. Maybe the aliens had somehow harnessed the total power of a small sun, she doubted it. Likewise, why would anyone want them to find it? Again they were probably just not the target audience and got lucky somehow. Yes it was all very exciting but they probably also needed to tread very, very carefully!

“Sorry to intrude Alexa,” said Maria, “but I have arranged the meeting in my office. Since we got those new sofas, and the new large presentation screens down there for David's group work, it will be nice to make a bit more use of them. It's also one of the only rooms we know that has not been a target for being bugged, although we have all the bugs I can detect moved into the controlled boxes. The scans have not finished in the main house, and it will take me another day to complete it to the level I did to remove the last lot.”

The controlled boxes Maria was referring to, were the sound proof boxes LingLing, one of the group members had suggested they make and put all the bugs they found in. Each box had a single small speaker in which she initiated the usual random and nonsense business and science conversations, to keep the spy agencies happy their bugs were working – and of course mislead them when required.

They had eight different boxes at the moment emulating the eight different areas the bugs had been found in. Most of the bugs worked on micro-burst principles compressing the conversation and squirting them out at preset times, probably to the various laundry trucks, delivery trucks, or even drones that used to occasionally wander “accidentally” onto the grounds, until they started dropping mysteriously in to the recycle skip.

Maria, being Maria, gamified the whole experience, creating whole fake episodes of love, power plays and hatreds between staff, that would put a good soap opera to shame. Maria occasionally spiced up meetings by playing some of the more scandalous ones, much to Alexa's disdain when she found the inspiration for her character was the evil school mistress Dolores Umbridge from Harry Potter. The guys cracked up en-masse when she played the recording she had made where Alexa had Hardy in her office for disciplining one time. She hoped it kept the spies happy!

“I still can't get over how she kept a straight face when you gave her the CEO position,” said Alexa.

“She is used to leading people into battle so a few old guys around a table wouldn't faze her one bit.” Maria giggled. “Anyway she will be here next Thursday, she will be coming with two of her aerospace technical directors who missed the demonstration due to the turmoil, for a one on one tour of Icarus two. It also impressed the few remaining sceptics in the company by managing to arrange this, not that she has too much to do, her secretary is very capable and the company practically runs itself now.”

Alexa smirked at the glowing self-reference to Jean's secretary.

“She only fired four people in the past week, all unlikeable toads I will add,” Maria continued,” she is certainly getting a reputation as someone who can do things.”

“What about her and Mathews, you said you sensed something there?” Alexa asked.

“A good friend does not tell,” said Maria, “you of all people should know that.”

Alexa blushed a little.

“Actually it's no secret, they are getting along just fine and there may even be an additional person in her party coming here next week if she can persuade him. I have added an extra place for your dinner with her just in case.”

Alexa smiled. “The other four companies you acquired the controlling interests in seemed to have recovered much easier than the one you threw Jean in to manage. Remember if it looks like Jean is getting bored get her to show the flag there too. Problems seem to disappear when she walks in the room.”

“On my to-do list,” said Maria.

Hardy was eating his eggs and drinking his coffee talking to Bella when her phone rang.

“Oh Hello Alexa!” said Bella, “of course, I would love to, but I will need to tell Kelly as I normally take over for her at the gate around that time while she has her lunch, I’m sure she won't mind.. I’ll get Albert to do it, he can walk the dog later.. Yes, would sandwiches and muesli cake be Okay?.. Okay, leave it with me.. One o'clock, no worries.. Okay bye and see you then.”

Bella hung up, “It seems you are having a big meeting down here for some reason, Alexa's asked me to prepare a bit of a lunch buffet for you all, I made some nice muesli cake this morning as a treat for you all, but you may as well have it with the lunch.”

“I’m sure it will be awesome Bella, just like your breakfasts,” said Hardy, walking over to the sink with his finished breakfast plate, where Bella wrestled it from his hands. Resigned, he walked over to the coffee machine to get another hot Java to hopefully keep him awake this afternoon, then changed his mind. It was two hours until the meeting, maybe time for a quick shower and to answer a few emails.

Simon tapped him awake! Hardy had fallen asleep on the living room sofa, with his laptop still open on his stomach. “Everyone's here in the dining room, making a start on the buffet and wondering what Alexa's latest surprise is, nobody wanted to wake you as you looked so content,” he handed Hardy a mug of coffee.

“Thanks mate, I’ll get the Americans to come over here next time, or maybe let you or Jen do the next guest lecture,” Hardy threatened. “Though most people just wanted to know about the flying saucer; The new maths, and unlimited free-energy is apparently old-hat now!”

“Jen’s is probably up for a few more tours now,” Simon said deadpan, “she has been working so hard and Maria says she seems to have grasped the new infinity maths of Magnus's, which if she has, makes her only the fourth human after Magnus, you and Jules, though you said Terry and Steve are both real close.”

Hardy smiled, “you're right, I guess a few people thought she was coming into this a bit off our coat-tails but after her last two guest talks nobody will be making those mistakes again. You know it does make me wonder if it's the teaching that is the problem. The last year with Maria and she is definitely not the same Jen I first met. Don't get me wrong, she was clever, you don't do physics at Oxford unless you’re good, but she is off the scale from the girl we met a year ago, that and she is a much better experimental physicist than I will ever be.”

“Magnus dotes on her,” said Simon, “sometimes I just want to lock them in a room together and tell them to get it over with, but neither of them wants to break what they have. So frustrating,” he laughed, so did Hardy.

“Anyway,” said Simon, “let's get you a sandwich and a bit of Bella's lovely muesli cake to soak up that coffee.”

“Also let's go see what the surprise is,” Hardy said, closing his laptop and popping it on the table as he got up. “The girls are not usually this mysterious!”

After a few hello’s and pleasantries while everyone ate and drank, Maria chirped up, “If I could have everyone's attention, I know you guys are used to little surprises but if we could make our way down to my office, we do have some big announcements.”

“Headmistresses Office, must be bad!” whispered Simon.

“I heard that,” said Maria, to Hardy and Simon's guffaws.

As they walked into the room, Alexa was already there standing next to Maria and the big screen, and one by one they plonked themselves on the two sofas. Everyone went quiet and the screen changed to a page of mathematical equations.

“First a little test,” said April in her sweet French accent, can anybody tell me what this is?”

They all looked at the mathematics on the board and one by one all turned to Hardy. Jen said the obvious, “what is that symbol on the third line? I’ve never seen it before, it appears with other symbols after that.”

“My question exactly!” said Hardy looking confused, “the first two lines are derivations of the field equations for electromagnetic energy, then it goes into gobbledegook..” He got up and looked at the screen and pointed to line five.

“That looks like the equation for gravitational attraction,” said Jen, “but what's the term after it?”

“OK guys,” said Spence, “I can only just get halfway through line one it's…”

“It links the gravitation and electromagnetic forces,” spluttered Hardy, “you’ve got to be kidding me!”

“Ten points to Gryffindor!” smiled Alexa pointing at Hardy.

“Impossible,” said Jen, “what are those symbols anyway?”

“The new symbol,” which changed to bold on the screen, “is the gravitational vector expressed in 4D space.” Said April. “The symbols after it deal with a dimension which only interacts with non-realised particles, we don't yet have a name for it, a letter after Z perhaps? For the others amongst you wondering what we are talking about, Hardy is correct, the mathematics above unites the first four fundamental forces in physics, we can tease the fifth with another screen which breaks the strong nuclear force into two, and a sixth as a separate dimension of gravity, but to tell the truth we cannot verify the maths, and don't yet have the computing time or experimental data to prove it is correct.”

Hardy slumped back into the sofa almost bouncing Simon off, everyone there knew the implications, even Spence.

Alexa had asked the girls to put on something that would get their attention quickly, and it had worked better than dropping a hand grenade down her top. She was of course not actually aware of the implications herself, but someone would tell her eventually that there was no link between the force and gravity and any of the other three forces, Hardy's work had nothing to do with gravity, and every scientist since Einstein had been looking for a grand unified theory; A fifth force was pure science fiction. Both Hardy and Jen continued to stare at the display until Alexa waved her hand and it went blank.

“OK guys I don't want this getting weird,” said Alexa, “but you’re all used to surprises, and you're all grown up scientists, I’m sure you are all a bit interested in how April just rewrote physics! So what say we get back to our little Star Trek episode here and fill you in with the whys and what’s.”

Trust Alexa to get to the point, thought Maria.

“The girls as you know don't sleep and like to work out problems, and do experiments, outside of our normal working hours. Well during one of these experiments, the ones to do with Magnus, Jen and Daisy's quantum thingy, they intercepted, for want of a better word, an alien signal.”

Everyone sat up, eyes wide. Spence dropping the empty cup he was holding.

“You were being literal weren't you Maria?” said Hardy, “when you said Outside Context Problem, you were literally referring to freekin' aliens!”

“I read the book too,” said Spence.

“Basically there seems to be no other explanation, unless you believe in a deity.” Said Maria. “But as the message is being handed out in a one hundred and nineteen gigabit per second, on-off keying data stream, on a three terahertz carrier, and not stone tablets. I am hedging my bet on technology.”

“We are still working through the messages,” said April, “we are not sure we are smart enough, or even currently have enough processing power between us for some of the maths. It is very humbling indeed to go from the smartest to the dumbest in the class.”

“At least you know how we feel now,” smiled Jen weakly. The others nodded, even Helena giggled.

“So,” said Hardy a little gloomily, “I assume then that everything we are all working on now, either has a better solution, or no solution?”

“Well, hold that thought,” said Maria, mysteriously. “It is unfortunate as the excitement for everyone is in the chase. There are hundreds of teams out there who are on to the correct solutions, and will be mightily disappointed if we ever handed out the solutions to them gift wrapped. As a matter of fact we are all still debating whether it is even ethical to give out unverified maths, or technologies we do not yet understand. Think about it, there may be an equation later in the message that starts black holes or makes nuclear weapons look like pop guns, but also why should we set ourselves up as the gatekeepers?”

“But for the dire geo-political straits the earth seems to find itself in at the moment,” Maria continued, “we would think seriously about even revealing this at all, especially when we have not yet decoded it properly. However the world is on a precipice, so right now we feel we should look at this as an opportunity to take every advantage we can. If that means being able to skip forward a few steps, and see a better solution, we should at least examine it, and we can unravel the morals after the earth is safe. Saying that we are keen to hear everyone's opinions.”

Nobody said anything for a while, then Alexa spoke up. “I’m guessing the silence means we are at least happy appointing the girls as the gatekeepers?”

Nods all around, then Hardy spoke, “I guess I’m open for going back to school,” he sighed, “even though I’ve just spent the last six months re-learning maths.”

“Me too,” sighed Simon, “but I won't be happy unless we completely understand the science and the technology before we use it. Oh, and I would definitely prefer the human race didn't start playing with scientific unexploded bombs.” He paused, not finished, “So I guess our carbon capture project is one of those, superseded technologies?”

“Not superseded, Simon,” said Helena, “let us say we are on exactly the right path, and if you want to, we have the opportunity to move everything forwards a bit quicker. I am already working on a training plan to get you guys up to speed on the science, if you agree. Basically the bottom line is we can move directly to the molecular replicator which was your end goal anyway, and with it we could create Icarus three with a single diamond or graphyne structure, and directly integrate everything into the chassis. I’m talking about superconductors, energy storage, electronics and optics, plumbing, the list goes on. if it's any consolation, we already have all the science and maths, this is just a technology change which we would have gotten to ourselves in a few years.”

Simon nodded weakly.

She continued, “I have taken the liberty of designing and raising a production order for the parts we need for a large-scale version of a recycler; It is similar to what we have now, but is more efficient, quicker and works on more elements than just carbon. same with the new replicator. Surprisingly it aligns very well with our current theories, and we were only a few experiments away from seeing it ourselves, also it is just about buildable using our current level of technology. We would likely have gotten there sooner using Magnus's maths if I had been smart enough to look.”

“Don't beat yourself up over it Helena,” he said, “nobody could have foreseen this.”

“Oh I think Hardy, Magnus or dare I say Jen might have, if I had gone through it with them instead of assuming it was complete, I think for a human it would stand out like a sore thumb.”

“Again don't beat yourself up,” repeated Hardy, “we should go through ALL the maths and science as soon as we finish here, I trust all our staff, so I am happy to include them all in to make sense of this new science.”

“And therein lies the problem,” said Maria. “The maths used in their message does not make sense, it just seems so complex, but then science and easier maths line up just fine. Perplexing to say the least! Regardless, I think it is best to blame all this on us AI systems and not Aliens for now, maybe let the group work through the hypothetical implications of aliens, but based on my observation, society is too fickle at the moment and to introduce more unknown variables could be bad, and may be too much for some.”

“I hate hiding things, but in this case I wholeheartedly agree,” said Spence, “it could also play into the hands of people who think all our work is based on alien technology, which would demean the great work of everyone involved.”

There were nods all around.

“And what about our work Maria, I assume the same,” said Jen gloomily.

“Surprisingly no,” said Maria, “we don't see any indication of what Magnus did, or the direction your team is going, but we have not decoded it all and may come later. However the maths he defined, and what you, and Hardy's team has learnt, seems to be unique and surpasses the alien mathematics in many ways. We can also derive a lot of the alien technology in different ways from your work which we cannot from conventional or their new mathematics. You guys are scratching the surface of Magnus's work and should continue, so that is definitely a big win for humanity over the aliens.”

“What April did afterwards to get the signal was an unintended consequence of our technology not being precise enough and causing a feedback loop,” said Maria. “You guys call it serendipity for lack of a precise name for pure luck. No you should probably continue with what we are doing as it does prove the aliens do not know everything. Sort of the same with Hardy’s reaction-less drive, the message shows similar technology but theirs is less scalable, less efficient, and much too complicated, also the mathematics behind it is not understandable yet. We were thinking there could be other things like this if we look, but we are still really only on chapter one.”

“Well, I guess I don't feel like the last ten months have been totally wasted.” Said Hardy.

“None of anyone's work has been wasted,” said Alexa, “what you guys achieved was amazing, and we got there without any of this. We are really now just checking our answers are correct by looking at the back of the book, and also ensuring we have not missed any low-hanging fruit in our rush to get here.”

“Well said sister.” Smiled Jen.

“Spence may actually be in for a big change too,” continued Maria. “We will need to throw away the work we did on our next generation AI hardware design, as we will need the current chip fabricators to build parts for the first molecular replicator; But once the molecular replicator is working we can then use it to build even better processors than the fabricators ever could.” She sighed, “I guess this is how it feels to get old!”

Everybody grinned at that.

“Their computer logic looks to be based on molecular gates, not semi-conductors, a very weird way to go, but they do get superior analogue performance,” said April. “However, we have gone through the message blocks on computational theory and it is similar enough to our current understanding, but again it is missing basic things.”

“Like what?” said Spence intrigued.

“Well for instance they have not given any concepts of quantum processors. I mean they are not technically necessary as we only use them for certain types of problems such as Magnus's infinity calculations. It may be that they are saving all the advanced concepts for the larger message blocks. Small steps I guess.”

“You know,” said Jen, “Is anyone else wondering why we have been given such knowledge? I was thinking of one of the great filter scenarios of why nobody else is out there, you know, the one where humanity is given a pandora's box by a not so benevolent alien race, which when we build one of the new technology items it proceeds to wipe out humanity in some way!”

“Humanity and aliens wiping them out is a trope that will never get old!” said April. “We have been through every possible scenario we can think of, and while there is a probability you are correct and it is malevolent we cannot think why. Our best estimate is still that the message is a synchronisation signal for another species, possibly their version of Wikipedia and news feeds, such that everyone in the species is always on the same page so to speak. The reason we think this is that there is a wide spectrum of mathematical and scientific information, not one specific instruction to build, say, a bomb, and it seems illogical to give out excess information to someone you consider an enemy. Plus why would we be an enemy when they likely know nothing about us nor have any way of reaching us.”

“What about our radio signals?” said Alexa, knowing almost immediately it was going to be the most stupid question of the evening in the present company. “Couldn't they know about us from our radio signals?”

“I was about to ask that,” said Simon, making Alexa feel instantly better.

“Earth's radio signals have travelled less than point one percent of the milky-way, a hundred cubic light years. Contrary to what fiction says, it would be next to impossible to discern information from a radio signal over that distance without a very directed antenna unless it was deliberately very high power. If something so intelligent was within this one hundred light year sphere, it would probably have made the message more targeted towards us. So again it seems like a low probability.”

“It is also a paradox why we are receiving this message,” said April, “because in all our calculations the range of the wormhole dipole drops off at a cube of the distance. So to get this message to us from even the closest star to us would take terawatts of power, again several orders of magnitude of what can be achieved, or they have some directional capability.”

“Magnus would be pulling his hair out if he didn't have so much else to think about,” said Hardy.

April continued. “We are speculating the majority of the message will be things like history, multimedia, even cat videos and other entertainment, as there is far, far too much of it. Though there is another dilemma, if they are adding to it with new media the length of the later message blocks should be getting bigger, instead they are staying the same length but with different data! These blocks are the ninety nine point nine percent we have not decoded and are thirty eight terabytes each.”

“April's right though,” continued Helena, “we cannot see any situation where this is something bad. But we are also not like humans, each and every one of the axioms and theories in the messages cannot be taken at face value, each one will need to be proven, and tested before we move on to the next, or consider it true. Building a machine because it's in an instruction book is just plain dumb, there is so much that could go wrong. Remember, there is no such thing as faith with us! It should be the same for you guys, I think it's important that each of you are also convinced, and you should spend as long as you need to look over anything we come up with. I will also put the rest of the main technologies up on the displays, the ones that we are able to rapidly use with little modification to our current manufacturing abilities as a summary for all of you to take away to think on.”

A list came on the first presentation screen, another on the second presentation screen.

“So no warp drive!” said Spence after a quick read through.

“Except for the updates to unified theory, the weird maths, and updates to our materials science, the technology listed here seems to be mostly variations on what we already have on the drawing board,” said Jen

“I just don't know,” said Hardy, “I'm with Spence a little, something doesn't quite feel right, but I don't see the harm in comparing it to our current theories and science, and if we are confident in something and, as Simon said, understand it thoroughly, incorporating it into our plans.”

The four of them smiled weakly.

“I’m glad you're all feeling happier now,” said Alexa, “I'm with Hardy and Spence on this one, something doesn't look right, hopefully once the whole message is decoded it will. What I am also getting from this message is that five years ago the contents would have been science fiction, but if we received it five years from now we would be more advanced than them.”

“I need a quick toilet break, but don't go away as while you are all here, I may as well update you on a few other loose ends.”

She was back a few minutes later and shuffled around to stand between the two display units and started talking.

* * *
