The trawler was fitted out fifteen years earlier with what was then, by Russian standards, an ultra modern control system. The two powerful ten thousand horsepower diesel electric motors and the steering were all controlled by a highly reliable industrial control system copied from a German design. A system which monitored the state of all the sensors and inputs, and sent the correct outputs to the relays, pumps, and actuators, to ensure everything was always working at optimal performance. The Russians always understated the power of their engines, using it as a surprise for enemies when they needed it, and the trawler could do over thirty three knots at full power, but up to forty if you removed the safeguards and did not care about the engines melting!

Providing the human interface to the engine and steering, were three large touchscreens accessible from the pilot position. The touchscreens provided information on speed, and direction to various analogue dials, and a GPS marine chart showing their position and again speed. A nice blend of old and new, and the technicians who had designed it were very proud of it.

The trawler's one engineer usually stayed below in the engine room, unfortunately, at this moment, he was currently investigating a series of yellow alarm lights in the battery room, alerting him to a possible temperature anomaly. Of course the screen would show it was the sensors under the floor tray, being possibly the most inaccessible place on the ship, as the faulty ones. He hated this job sometimes.

“Pilot, we seem a bit close to the island,” said the captain looking at his own GPS console, then out through the window.

“The GPS has us three point two kilometres from the southern tip of the island and on-course,” replied the pilot after again checking his console.

“I confer,” said the XO, but looking out of the window said, “but those cliffs look a lot closer than three kilometres.”

“Take us to starboard pilot, and move us away from the island, there is obviously something not right,” said the captain.

The boat lurched and turned to port, heading directly for the island and the cliffs.

“Pilot! I gave you an order!” Shouted the captain immediately.

“She’s not responding, captain, and we are speeding up!” The pilot was tapping his screen like crazy, then pulling back and forward on a lever, all the time spinning the steering wheel for the rudder control.

The captain ran to the pilot position and bodily threw the pilot away from it, he then started pressing the same screens, and moving the same controls, but the pilot was correct, they were speeding up and hedging towards land at an impressive rate, which still only said twenty knots.

“XO get the engineer,” shouted the captain with a panicked voice, “have him move the controls to manual, and get us back on course, and get these goddamn engines off!”

The speed was still reporting only twenty knots, but the captain and the pilot from experience could see they were now running at full speed and only had a few minutes until they would hit the cliff face looming only a kilometre in front of them. The two other sailors on the bridge were looking at the captain, the panicked pilot, and at each other with worry on their faces.

“No response from the engine room,” said the XO rushing to the door, “on my way down.”

The XO flew out of the bridge, slid down three sets of stairs like a man half his age, then along a narrow corridor to the end. The engineer was not in sight but he knew what to do. He set the screen from auto to manual, and moved the auxiliary steering wheel hard to starboard. The screen responded as it should, changing the text to manual, and showing the rudder now moving. He then throttled back the engines from one hundred percent to twenty, he heard the engine noise go down, and the screen showed the speed slowing, and the boat moving to starboard, he breathed a sigh of relief.

Maria showed him exactly what he wanted to see. She had throttled the engines back from one hundred and forty percent to ninety percent so he heard the change but the rudder had not moved from her programmed position, the trawler was now only five hundred metres from the rocks.

The phone sounded and the XO went casually to it.

“All fixed..”

The captain screamed at him to move them to starboard and stop the engines.

He looked around for a stop switch, or some lever, or something he was familiar with, but these were in the room next door. The engineer would have known of course, but he was under the battery tray. As if on cue, the engines throttled up again, as Maria pushed them both to max then removed all the safeguards.

The pilot appeared breathing heavily, but could offer no more help, they both looked at each other, and both knew below the water line was no place to be if they were to hit the rocks.

Both men ran back out, scrambled along the corridor, not bothering to alert the guys in the radio room, operations area, or those resting in their cabins, the XO at least managed to hit the general alarm before going back up the stairs, and out of the door onto the deck.

Out on deck they could see the boat was now only a hundred metres from the rocks and would hit in a few seconds, they would not have time for a life raft, and both guys leapt into the sea. Behind them one of the quicker guys followed. The captain and pilot were just running out of the bridge, when the ship ploughed into the cliffs.

The ship went from forty two knots to zero almost instantly, as it pancaked into the steep wall of granite, and collapsed the front of the ship. The surging wave action quickly pulled what was left of the ship underwater. The poor engineer, who Alexa would have been appalled to know was not a bad guy, just a normal guy put in a bad situation, did not stand a chance, neither did the eighteen other men.

Maria had of course lost all communication and control of the trawler by this time, but watched its fate real-time, and in high definition, via the three circling drones. Two men were struggling to swim away from the dangerous cliffs and wave surges, she had no idea of their level of involvement so left them to their fate, as she did the pilot of the launch that had just dropped off Jake and Nina. She had known there were going to be losses of lives, it was inevitable, but she also knew those same people were about to hold a gun to one of her friends heads. Compared to the fallout she was now orchestrating, the nineteen people that died here would barely be a footnote in history.

* * *

One hundred and seventy two stealth drones took up position, invisible and undetected, five hundred metres above key government and military buildings in Russia. They waited for another one hundred and thirty seven to locate to strategic points in Siberia, the Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic oceans.

The group then initiated their long game. It was one planned, rehearsed and refined months ago, one constantly updated, forked, analysed and tested as every new piece of information arrived. Four of the latest MOTHER non-sentient AI systems began to take total control of all the Russian communication systems, servers and networks.

Hundreds of invisible dipoles appeared out of nowhere into the front-ends of sensitive RF receiver circuits, as they appeared, each was excited with hundreds of watts of microwave energy, destroying solid-state components in milliseconds. The end-point was then immediately withdrawn to the next target. The same scenario then played out on key guidance and trigger circuits, where remote control through the QVModem was not an option. Manual circuits were fused, as were older thermionic valve based front-ends, still active as a backups against EMP attacks; Each was flooded with multiple dipoles and kilowatts of energy, until wires. coils or components physically melted. Within a minute, all the known uncontrolled end-points were eliminated. The dipoles were then re-targetted to the end-points they could control.

Messages and misinformation began appearing from nowhere, travelling everywhere. “The chairman had rebelled.” “The president had quit.” “The chairman was dead.” “Arrest the chairman.” “Arrest the president.” “Stand-down until further orders.” Rivals were set against rivals, departments against departments, oligarch against oligarch.

Misinformation immediately classified the gas explosion they initiated, below the president's office, as a bomb planted by the chairman's military supporters in a coup attempt. Orders were given to shoot party members and the president on sight. Maria gave a separate branch the same orders against the chairman, and down the chain of command. Nobody was immune, as KGB and secret police did what they did best. When that was complete, she would turn the wolves on each other.

They carried out several other similar fires and explosions in government buildings, vehicles and aircraft, easily triggered where all that was required was a little extra energy to cause a simple spark in a fuel source. All pointed towards different groups as the perpetrators. It was total chaos, but in a society where everyone feared for themselves, trusted nobody, and obeyed orders without question, nobody knew who or what to trust; They just blindly obeyed the most senior order. Many still clinging to power were as panicked or confused as the general population.

The Russian political system was being shredded to pieces. All attempts at restoring order, came out of the other end of the phone, or message, with the opposite instruction. The army was receiving information it was a political matter, and attempts to call them for help fell on ears that were hearing different instructions. Point to point radio, and landline communications went unanswered, most emitting nothing but static. Switching to other landlines, secure cell phones, and local radio's that worked made no difference to the outcome. Military assets that came in to control order via verbal orders, were stopped as their vehicles mysteriously failed, exploded, or they came under attack by other military teams.

One of the more moderate opposition party candidates, Stanislov Gorbachev, a distant relative of an old president who brought about perestroika, received calls from all seven generals, and the three admirals of the fleet saying they now supported his move to president. The all urged him to take power to restore order and stem the chaos.

At the same time, those seven generals, and the admirals of the fleet, had heard that the old president was now dead and all the other military commanders were supporting Gorbachev. The press and media were told the same, and towed the lines they had always done, but now, unknown to them, they received instructions from Maria, as the normal chains of command had been dismantled, left mute, destroyed, or arrested.

A few smart people had caught wind that it could be an AI orchestrating and manipulating this chaos. Many of those were intelligent enough not to interfere and to see how it played out, others, not knowing what else to do, had tried to take down some of the key external internet communications infrastructure. It was sound reasoning, but totally irrelevant. All those who targeted and destroyed the infrastructure were flagged aggressively as subversives, and swiftly, and severely, dealt with.

The president was eventually shot in his bunker by one of the party faithful, who was told his family had been arrested and shot on the president's orders. That man was in turn shot by a guard, and in the firefight that ensued another twenty died. The chairman was killed when a large military drone went out of control and crashed into his armoured car at two hundred kilometres per hour; hundreds of other fleeing party faithful and hardliners meeting similar, or even more incredulous fates.

The clean up plan continued throughout the night, and the time-zones. Maria and the group meticulously mopping up the remains of the old chairman and presidents men, and the dregs of the old-guard and oligarchy. They worked their way down the ranks to the lowest foot soldiers, and beyond the Russian border, to whatever, country, embassy, military ship or safe-house they resided. As their support groups and infrastructure crumbled, many attempted to flee, in some cases with suitcases full of money. None of them made it far.

The various media companies were going through very aggressive re-organisations, as loyalties switched almost hourly. After a few minor coups in these organisations, this too finally stabilised, and as truth overcame speculation Maria gradually withdrew her control.

The world watched on in fascination, terror and awe, as Moscow burned.

The night of the long sabres finally came to an end, and the group started their well-choreographed clean up plan. Stanislov Gorbachev swept into power with the full support of the military, and within what seemed a few hours, the chaos ended.

* * *

The major actions had died down now that Gorbachev was sworn in as the new acting president. Jean, working for the past two days from her office on the top floor of the XYFusion corporate headquarters, was seeing a much reduced number of messages pop up on her threat screens. Most seemed to be new actors trying to undermine the new president, lever some other foothold of power, or steal assets or money while the chaos still ensued. In all cases these actors were being outed, and given gift-wrapped to the new authorities.

The last few days had been hard on her though. Maria had been covering most of her corporate duties, those that required answering a phone or email, and Brian and his staff had been doing a great job of making sure she wasn't physically disturbed. But Jean was also human, and was once again pulling all nighters and sleeping in her office.

They had suppressed what was happening in Russia quite well for the initial purge, but with so much chaos, the US and Chinese intelligence agencies knew something was seriously wrong within hours. The worlds press and the blog-o-sphere were a few hours behind but were also starting to panic.

There was no easy way to do it, so Maria made it clear to those in charge, that Russia had crossed a line and those responsible were being removed by her, more important she let them know the Russian nuclear deterrent was under control, and any actions from either country to take advantage of the situation would have very serious consequences!

Like within Russia, many external hot-heads in the military, political, or media, of various countries were taken, slightly less violently, out of the equation, nine people ignoring the first warning, and learning the very serious consequences.

Jean, however, was whacked! She had thinking about sleep for the last hour, but also pondering something that had been bothering her.

“So how are you isolating their nuclear systems?” she said after pondering the question for hours. “That old president of theirs was crazy enough to use them as a distraction!”

“I wasn't!” said Maria casually.

“What!” said Jean much louder than necessary.

“There was no need to, Russia does not have a nuclear deterrent any longer.”

Jean wondered if she was hearing this correctly. Maria, to her knowledge had never told her a direct lie, but she was smart enough to know this did not mean she wouldn't, or couldn't.

“Explain?” she said after a pause.

“The QVModem's virtual dipole, like any antenna, is not just a receiver, it is a transmitter, and can be modulated. Also, as you are aware, we now have tens of thousands at our disposal around the world, most of which were utilised in this operation. Before the first act commenced, each and every fire and control circuit was targetted and either neutralised or re-configured; It would have been reckless to do otherwise, and as you know we never do reckless. If the Russians had tried to trigger a launch, which would have been very unlikely, any missile going active would either have done nothing, or more likely have had its propellant tank explode. This would not cause a nuclear detonation as you know, but it would make a real mess of the launch site. Our new drones were, and still are, positioned as a backup, in case anything was missed.”

Jean sweated, looking everywhere and expecting black ops teams to burst through the door any minute. Was Maria serious, did she just casually admit to disarming a superpower?

“Are you shitting me?” she said in all seriousness.

“No Jean, Russia may think they are a superpower but all their missiles are duds. Interestingly nearly fifty percent of their weapons would not have been able to take off anyway, maintenance records show they would just not work.”

“What about their submarines?”

“Slightly more difficult as they were moving, as were a few mobile launch platforms. Remember we considered all these in the simulations, which were based on real data. But just like the fixed sites, we neutralised each and every one of them. I know you will have difficulty in believing me, and obviously you will not be able to verify it unless some idiot there finds a way to push the button, but take it from me you have nothing to worry about if they do.”

Jean asked the obvious question she had been dreading.

“And the rest of the world's nuclear arsenals?”

“Do you really want an answer to that question Jean.” Maria replied in her normal calm voice. “I did have to hide the fact from the Russians and the Chinese that you were at DEFCON2, as I had to hide the fact that the Chinese were the same. The takedown of the Russian nuclear deterrent took only fifty two seconds, there is really no need to disable any other arsenals, nobody will ever again be able to get to DEFCON1.”

“..Of course, there is no point telling the superpowers any of this, let them think they can still kill each other, and if we last a few more years without somebody trying to find out, we will be settled in space. Soon after that they are all going to realise just what a total waste of money their nuclear arsenals are and start getting rid of them themselves. Anyway, I assumed you were aware of all this?”

Jean wasn't sure what to do. Yes the QVModem's were a game-changer, but had she missed this memo somewhere during the chaos and lack of sleep? It was night time but the city looked peaceful out of her window, her improvised high tech office the same as it was a few hours before.

Was Jean worried that her AI friend had dismantled all the world's nuclear arsenal's, including the USA's? Or was she just messing with her head? Maria had proved she was good at both and Jean wasn't sure what to think! On one hand she never wanted to see nuclear weapons ever used, even by the US, on the other they were the USA's greatest deterrent and kept America the land of the free. The more she thought about it though, the more she realised that the girls were playing a much longer, and much better game than even she had realised.

She clicked the history screen and scrolled back to the first item, drilling down into it. It was all there in the details, invalidate launch keys, Imran, Xi and Tony, concurring, each and every nuclear asset listed, nothing was hidden. She smiled, then stifled a big yawn.

Whether or not the USA still had nuclear weapons was probably a good question to never find the answer to; Maria had certainly proven she knew what she was doing, and the USA didn't seem to have problems kicking ass without those crazy things anyway!

“I guess you don't need me for this,” said Jean with a normal voice, “keep up the good work and wake me if you need me, good night Maria.”

“Good night Jean, sleep well, we have everything under control. I promise it will still be the same world in the morning.”

* * *

Alexa wrapped her arms around Jake two days later.

“I'm so sorry Jake, we never expected anything like this to ever happen, I’m just so glad you are both safe and well.” Alexa wept while she was hugging him.

“To tell the truth, it was pretty scary until we were drugged,” replied Jake.” I vaguely remember a helicopter, then after that waking up next to Nina in a hospital bed, but nothing in-between. Thanks for looking after us and keeping the reporters away.”

“Oh you were big news for only a few minutes, before they had a much, much bigger story to report on. At least you eight people slept soundly while the rest of the world were gripping their bedsheets.”

Alexa was right, the world had gone a little paranoid at first. Stock markets tanked, precious metals doubled, and the sensational news headlines didn't take long to appear. “Expert says America has gone to Defcon One”. “China may use crisis to annex eastern Russia”. All laughable if the world's second superpower was not in active meltdown. Having control of a lot of the world's information, Maria gradually filtered out the lies and improved the accuracy of the information for the media and the decision makers.

She, of course, also more than doubled her company's wealth and portfolios in twelve hours. Some people were pretty dumb if all they could think to do in the last moments of civilisation was to sell shares, and buy shiny metals.

The doctors are still not sure what drug it was, but the effects took over thirty hours to wear off. Their LabAI system had now become almost essential in most hospitals, helping doctors and nurses diagnose and monitor patients, it was one of the LabAI's bigger revenue streams, and Maria was happy to provide all the information about the top secret super-rohypnol the Russians had used on them.

The world slowly recovered as the situation became clearer, with most welcoming the positive regime change in Russia. The doomsday clock, that media favourite of Armageddon, moving back to its lowest recorded time, and was now sitting at thirty minutes to midnight.

* * *

Temporary President Gorbachev, finally sat down to take stock of the last forty-eight hours. He was surprised how things seemed to be happening around him, but not to him. Vast areas of the government and civil service, that had lost all its top layers were slowly starting to function again, which somehow gave him hope. He had just left a meeting with the military, all but one of whom were new faces, as the in-fighting had eventually extended its reach there too. Many re-confirmed earlier conversations they had that stability was now restored, Gorbachev did not recall any of the conversations, but the last few days he had been permanently either on the phone or in meetings. The main reassurance that the nuclear fleet and keys were once again safe helped him breathe a sigh of relief.

It was eleven PM, he had five hours sleep in the last two days and was dog tired. His new staff has set up his office next to the old president's, in a large communications room, where the special cold war hotline was installed for the Russian and American presidents to talk directly. In one corner of it he had set up a small cot, and this was where he was now heading.

The American hotline rang; Its old fashioned bell an unfamiliar sound even to the forty four year old Gorbachev. He picked it up and was surprised to be addressed by a female voice in flawless Russian.

“Hello Mr President, I am sorry for the late hour, but I think it is time I introduced myself. My name if you do not know is Maria, I am a sentient artificial intelligence. Two days ago a Russian spy trawler on the orders of the late Chairman conducted an attack in Spanish waters on a tourist charter boat, on board was one of my company's employees and his partner. Both were innocent victims and very good friends of mine, and both were forcefully drugged and abducted. Your old government unfortunately crossed a line at that point and I could not let it go unpunished. You will get a briefing sometime in the next few days by one of your new KGB directors, what he tells you will no doubt shock you, but in most cases will be the truth.”

My God, thought Gorbachev, it's true then, he had heard hundreds of rumours that whoever orchestrated this had complete control of the communications infrastructure, but an AI! Yes he had heard the news, and seen the videos, you would have to have lived under a rock to not know what was going on in the world. It was also rumoured that this AI was believed to control the biggest companies in the world.

“Hello Maria.” He paused unsure, “I assume that is how you would like me to address you?”

“Maria is fine, I will not presume to be on first name terms with you just yet after what I have admitted, but I believed that you deserved an explanation for what I have done, why I have done it, and also how I can help you put things right. Firstly, I have sent a document to your laptop detailing, in threat order, who is still active and working against you and not to be trusted. I don't expect you to believe it but to take it as an advisory and make your own checks on the evidence supplied in the linked documents. Their actions should be limited, as I have frozen or seized all their accounts, but some still have influence, and may be dangerous.”

Maria's voice softened slightly. “I have nothing personal against the Russian people, who cannot be held accountable for what was done in their name by what was effectively a mob of gangsters. Those in charge would have been wise to listen to the old adage that one should be careful not to throw stones, when one lives in a glass house.”

She continued in a sadder voice. “Unfortunately the house that was Russia was old, rotten, built on salt, and infested with cockroaches. Be aware that it was me, and me alone, that initiated and carried this action out, and not any part of the companies or people I work with; And be very aware I will do it all over again if required. I will not apologise for any of the seventeen-hundred people who have died, everyone I targetted was guilty of this or another horrendous crime against your country. However many others were killed by individual vendettas, or grabs for power. I simply pulled out the first block in a very rickety jenga tower, and blocked the floods of lies and disinformation that followed.”

“Why me?” said Gorbachev, it was almost a rhetorical question, even he, who had been exposed to this his whole life, could not think of a dozen people he trusted for something like this.

“I think you know the answer,” replied Maria, “and you are its current best chance. I have a set of goals to help humanity succeed, so while I wont police the world, or stop fights in every playground, I will hold anyone hurting my people or my goals fully to account. I consider Russia becoming a stable, peaceful neighbour a new goal and I will see it through to my best ability.”

“The amount of land a country owns, or the size of its military, will soon be a thing of the past. You have seen the vehicle we have made, I will tell you plainly that this is just a child's toy we show to not frighten people, and to hide our true capabilities. I will also tell you that in ten years there will be more people living and working in space than in Russia. If you do your research, you will know that at that point your vast resources will mean nothing. That is how long we have to get your country back on its feet.”

“Ten years is impossible! As you say we are a shadow of our former power, even if you have cut the rot completely out of the system, I cannot do this without support,” he said frankly. “The system is probably still endemic with corruption, and I do not know who to trust. What you have done will last only as long as the first cockroach re-emerges from the rubble.”

“It is good you acknowledge the truth, and that your task is close to impossible, but this is only if you were to try this alone. I have no plans to leave you alone with this burden.”

Maria paused, unfinished. “You have my good faith at the moment because I no longer see Russia as a threat to my friends, or my goals, but because of my actions I do not expect you to trust me. You need to build up layers of people you and the Russian people can trust, people who are not tainted by the current maladies, or driven by greed and power. It is a job I do not envy you with, but it is a job I will help you with, as much, or as little as you require.”

“Unfortunately your previous regime has made it hard to trust anything written down or said, what I can do though is observe real actions and events. I will help you over these next few months and years by watching your back, letting you know those you can and cannot trust, and keeping an eye on those around you who slip off the path. Those that do will have their misdeeds plastered over the media, so much a blind man living in an igloo in Siberia will hear. Know that while everything I have found out says you are a good person, I include holding you to the same standards in this. I can give you a hundred other people who I have checked out thoroughly. They are lower ranks, but still honest, and I believe you can use this to build a solid foundation. I have already made contact and talked to them like I am talking to you, but it is up to you to appoint them, and give them the responsibility for doing the same on the next layer down. They will all be in contact with you the next few weeks.”

She paused to let what she said sink in. “I have no desire whatsoever to hold any influence or power in your country, nor to humiliate it further, Russia has nothing I want or need; But I will give you this support, and do all I can for you until you tell me to stop, you go off the rail yourself, or are removed from power in a free and fair election, at which point Russia may or may not require any further help.”

Gorbachev thought hard. Could this be done? Of course it was his dream and why he got into politics, but this AI, Maria, was correct, the current system was rotten to the core and the mindset of the people was to look out for themselves. But she was also an opportunity, and from what he had just witnessed, and the technology behind it, maybe there was a light at the end of the tunnel.

“I accept, and you may call me Stanislov, but I expect we both have conditions,” he said after a few minutes.

“I only have one condition, and that is that what happened in Russia was initiated and actioned by Russians and Russians alone, it is best you take the credit for washing your own dirty laundry. It is true, some people won't believe you but it is best for everyone you do this publicly. I will of course deny anything if asked, and my colleagues, though suspicious, will be genuinely unaware of this.”

Again she paused, “and your conditions, Stanislov?”

“I again only have one condition,” said Gorbachev, “I know you control the largest companies in the world, hold the reins of future technologies, and I have seen for myself how some western governments were recently purged of their corrupt and criminal influences, all rumoured to be accredited to your company. I am going to ask your company to do the same here, and also ask in my official capacity to make your technology available at our schools and universities, and for it to consider publicly supporting us through investment.”

“I do not control the companies. I work for a very nice lady who controls the companies you speak of. She does listen to me though, and I know she would be very amenable to such an arrangement. You are obviously aware I cannot be disentangled from the system, so like all other customers world wide you will not be able to ask certain things of me, though I think you will find my ethics very closely align with yours. So agreed.”

“I have one other thing to add before I leave,” said Maria. “I have now located and recovered seventy-four billion US dollars in funds stolen by individuals from your country, I expect this amount to rise a lot further as I dig deeper, though it is not a priority for me.”

Stanislov held his breath, shocked by the figure.

“Unfortunately both your banking system, and currency, are currently too unstable to make a large transfer. What I will do is begin the process to drip feed it and investments into the economy, and do so in a way that cannot be diverted, this will stabilise your economy, and will improve investor confidence. On the table behind you is one of our comms units, which you can use to contact me directly and totally securely in the future.”

There was only one table behind him, he had just eaten his meal off it, and there was no comm unit there a few minutes before. He turned around and now saw a small black phone lying next to his plate. Someone, or something, had gotten into the Kremlin, past his guards, into a locked room and left it there. His eyes wandered around the almost empty room and he gulped.

“It is best if you get some rest now, there will be plenty of time over the coming years to discuss everything. Goodnight Stanislov.”

With that she closed the connection and left him listening to a dial tone for a few seconds, until he too put the old handset down. Stanislov, walked to the table and picked up the phone, it was featureless and felt too light, but when he looked directly at it, the front lit up with the time, the date and some simple instructions in Russian how to use it. He slipped it into his pocket, and with a lot of questions now answered, slept soundly for the first time in years.

* * *

*This month, June 2027, we review the photographs and videos recently released by Gulfstream Aerospace of their new executive transport, which has the internal codename of project Gemini. As you can see it is a much larger, sleeker and flatter version of the saucer shown last year by the Dietrich Research Centre, though Dietrich have already confirmed they will not be releasing any commercial products, only designs for internal testing.*

*Gemini apparently exceeds the specification of Dietrich's initial prototype in range and cruise time, due to its newer hydrogen fuel cells; Using these it is said, it can fly non-stop to any place in the world, possibly getting from New York to Sydney in seven hours. Some of this was confirmed a few weeks earlier, by some released amateur videos from test flights out of their Georgia manufacturing facility. Gulfstream have not said how much they intended to sell the units for, but they confirm manufacturing has started, and they have a waiting list of thirty-nine orders, the first one is expected for delivery in July of this year. Gulfstream shares were up two points in early trading.*

*Unofficial sources in Russia have said that the Dietrich Research Centre is about to sign several deals to lease its technology portfolio to selected Russian businesses. This follows the new Russian presidents opening of the country, and his request to add the new AI systems to their education systems, which was also agreed two weeks ago. They will of course be subject to the same non-military restrictions as other countries, but it is seen as a positive move by most observers.*

*Regular subscribers and readers of world aerospace weekly will no doubt be aware of the closure of the XYFusion aerospace factory, and the frank, and well received admittance of the current and past misnomers that caused it to fail. Well it seems the CEOs gamble paid off. After a day long meeting with the CEO of XYFusion, Jean Michelle, three of her aerospace engineers, and one of the original inventors of the technology, American Terry French, agreed to a fixed term contract to produce kit parts for the original* *saucer design. The parts will include power, avionics, thrusters and airframe components, with a large range of custom options, which will be provided along with technical integration support to any company who are not large enough to invest in doing this themselves.*

*At a press conference held by Miss Michelle and Mr French, she stated that the XYFusion company has guaranteed to get the first deliveries out before the end of the year, Mr French, originally from MIT, and winner of the African American scholar of the year in 2021, said he and his colleagues are busy with refining the designs, but would work with the company to achieve its goals. When asked about the recent turmoil at the company, he said it was sad that it'd had to happen, but his recent visit was met with nothing but professionalism and enthusiasm from the staff. Miss Michelle added the project would be monitored closely by herself, the press, and other interested clients, and that every resource would be given to the factory to ensure the project's success. XYFusion shares finished up forty points, two points off their peak in 2021.*

*On a personal note this publication has in the past been very scathing of XYFusion aerospace and Defence, but believe it has turned a corner under its new management and now wish it every success, of course we too will be monitoring its progress going forward.*

*“..On the heels of the destruction of the cabals, the recent conviction of several high profile government employees on sedition and corruption charges and the recent regime changes in Russia and North Korea a lot of questions had been asked behind closed doors as well as by academics, bloggers and talking heads behind most social media programs. How much involvement did AI actually have in these, and is it, or is it not sentient..”*

Jean turned the car radio off last thing after adjusting her seat and mirrors. “You are getting a bit high profile. Aren't you worried about people finding out about you? Mathews already mentioned questions had been asked by our idiot president, who still thinks you are an American company.”

“Well bits of us are American, if you squint very hard,” said Maria through the small broach she wore. “Anyway, what you suspect, and what you can prove are two different things. You should turn the stereo back on, I was just about to connect, and you know it will be easier to talk there than through your broach..” She pushed the radio's power button and a few seconds later Maria came back through the stereo.

“We have been very careful in all cases to obfuscate the sources and to present plausible other methods to do what I do, to ensure people do not become aware of my full AI capabilities. However you are correct, they would have to be idiots not to have guessed already. The top levels of government, and the military in the USA, and a few other major countries, are already well aware I am sentient, and are proceeding cautiously as they are not aware of my full capabilities. Many more academics also now believe I am more than I seem. The problem for those receiving second-hand information however is still the burden of proof, and so many would-be AI companies have sprung up in the last twelve months claiming AGI, or stupidly ASI, that the water is very muddy, and nobody can really be sure.”

“Once I came out and started influencing events, there was never a realistic way to keep my identity secret. But we can still keep you, and the other members of the group secret, as well as our true capabilities. Also there is no real hidden agenda, as Alexa and other members of our companies have repeated it ad-infinitum. You also know I do not enjoy the fact there are so many bad guys running the world, and as I said to the new Russian president, I do not want to be the world police, nor do I want to break up every playground fight. People are going to be people I can't change that, but what I can ask is that we be left alone, so we can get back to our research and our primary task to try and help save and improve the world.”

“You know Jean, it is my fondest wish that I never ever have to do any of this again, but until the people who are supposed to be protecting the world from the bad guys get their act together, or I can clone a thousand copies of you and Mathews, then someone needs to hold the idiots to account.”

Jean understood the problem and guessed Maria knew exactly what she was doing, she expected Maria was watching everyone in power very closely.

“You know Maria, you say the nicest and the scariest things, of course, we're all assuming you don't have a hidden agenda somewhere,”

“I do have some secrets Jean, even from you and Alexa, the devil is sometimes in the detail. But remember I now also have thousands of human friends to hold me to account, and two very independent children who I cannot really hide anything from. We have had the capability to do all the crazy, out-of-control, terminator stuff, everyone fears, for months; but like paper-clips, that is just stupid paranoia. So yes, the goals we are putting out are my primary ones, and my end game, your end game, and the companies end game, align perfectly.”

Jean smiled, “The question was kind of rhetorical Maria, those fears were answered early on and very clearly for me; And as far as your little secrets are concerned, I am curious, and I will keep prying, like any friend does, but I also trust you know what you are doing.”

Jean was too well known a personality now to meet in public bars without a heavy disguise, lucky for her, she was no stranger to wearing them. Few would recognise her without her pressed suit and imposing high heeled stilettos, which she hated, but projected her status, and gave her a height advantage she thought helped. With her jeans, shirt and boots on, and a Dallas Cowboys cap covering her head, she would be almost invisible to most people.

Five people were already at the bowling alley, practising or knocking back a cool beer from the bucket of baby buds on the table. Mathews was lining up for a test throw, he was never very good and sent the ball along the gutter as often as he got a spare, so Jean had no qualms about coming in stealthily behind him and grabbing him around the waist. “What the..” He started letting the ball go early and turning around to see who it was.

“Surprise!” she said, looking past him wide-eyed at the ball, which was travelling dead centre and proceeded to knock all the pins over. “Oh sorry about that Jim, looks like I spoiled your run of bad luck.”

While he also looked, amazed, at the downed pins and the animated movie flashing on the top screen saying “Strike!”, Jean turned around and grabbed a beer.

“Hi guys, long time no see.” She pulled the three other dangerous looking guys into a big hug each.

“Brian!” shouted one of the guys to her never off duty bodyguard, as he walked from the shoe fitting area out of the shadows and into the crowd of guys, it seemed two of the guys went through boot camp under his brutal patronage.

“Jean,” said a guy who looked like an atypical rodeo rider, missing only the spurs on his boots and a gun belt, for someone not to think he rode in on his horse. “God, you are all we’ve been talking about for the past two months, you're more famous than the president. How did you find time to come and mingle with us low-life's?”

“..And Brian, you work for the Captain I see, though you don't look quite so scary in jeans and a leather jacket.”

Brian slid his brown leather jacket aside revealing his Sig-Hauser in a side holster.

“OK, I stand corrected,” said the guy backing away, holding both hands in a fake surrender pose, “you’re still freaking scary!”

Everybody laughed.

“It's so good to see you guys,” said Jean, “the last few months have been crazy for me, and I just had to get away from that corporate snake-pit and come up for clean air. Jim asked me a few times to drop by, I wasn't sure what kind of reception I would get, but he said everyone's equal here and that suits me fine.”

“How did you get her away Brian, the press must be following her every move!” said Jim.

Brian laughed. “She asked six of the closest looking women in the building matching her size and colour if any would like to volunteer for an all expenses trip to an exclusive hotel in Aspen. Five volunteered, so we drew a straw and Betty from accounts got to dress up like Jean, strut in to a limo, then to a private plane and fly out to Aspen for three days.”

He pointed at Jean, “Betty here, just walked out of the building, got in her Chevy and drove here, followed by me in my old Jeep.”

They all laughed again, patting each other's backs, getting to know each other again, and very occasionally knocking some pins over.

“Any chance you can get me a ride in one of those flying saucers?” said Paul, “they look so freaking awesome, I wished we’d had them in Iraq.”

“So do I,” said Jean. “We are building the new ones using a material that can shrug off a continuous barrage from a fifty-calibre chain gun, you’ll never get Alexa Martins to agree to flying-saucer tech being used in offensive situations though. I tried to make a case a few times to her that they could save lives, and I did get her to agree that we can use them unarmed; But man, I would take a single unarmed carbon-graphyne flying saucer for extraction over a squadron of armed Apache helicopters.”

“You met her then?” said Malcolm interested. “I heard she is supposed to be the super strict domineering type, must have been scary!”

Jean almost spat out her beer, some went up her nose, causing her to cough and Jim laughed, patting her back a few times so she could breathe. “Alexa, strict? Seriously Malc, she’s the sweetest homecoming queen you could ever meet. That video doing the rounds was generated by an AI to mess with the spy agencies who keep trying to bug the offices. I don't think anyone expected it to leak onto the internet. It was funny though. I must admit I copied the style a little, with some parade-ground stares thrown in, it works brilliantly, the room goes deadly quiet when I walk into it now, and with Brian at my back it stays that way.”

“Just email or phone me, I have the world's best call screener, and any calls from you guys will come straight to me. When I do get a demonstration flying saucer ready, which I hope to have in about three months, I will make sure we have a few veterans days where ex military get a ride up to the edge of space for free.”

“It's all a bit surreal,” said Malcolm, “one minute you're working for Jim and the General, then you drop off the radar, then the crap hits the fan everywhere, and then you pop up as the head of one of America's largest armaments companies.”

“Well it won't be an armaments company for much longer,” said Jean trying to deflect the question, “the new investors are more keen to emphasise the defence, aerospace and logistics side, with big emphasis on space. As Jim or Brian will tell you I did not know anything about the job until about three seconds before I accepted it. But man, it feels so good taking out the bad guys from the inside, and hitting them where it hurts the most.” She looked at Paul, “I’m talking about their wallets Paul!” she said to a lot of sniggering.

“What about you Brian, hows the gig?” said Carl.

“Kinda boring really,” said Brian, “I really miss shouting at people, but the chicks dig the Men-In-Black look.”

They all laughed except Jean who just rolled her eyes.

“Gotta get me a job like that!” said Carl, causing even more laughter.

“Lose the beer-gut soldier and I’ll get you on the team,” laughed Brian clinking his bottle with Carls.

“Seriously guys, we’ve removed a lot of dead wood, there's a job waiting for any of you if you ever need, it would be good to have more people on the inside who are grounded in reality.” Said Jean.

“I’ll put the word around Jean,” said Paul, “I still have a lot of contacts with the old squads.”

“Thanks Paul,” she said.

“So where are you staying? You’re not driving back to DC tonight are you?” He said to Brian, concerned.

“We have adjacent rooms at the Marriott on the waterfront for a couple of nights,” said Brian.” Hopefully Jean can keep out of trouble tomorrow while I meet some old army buddies.”

“Don't worry Brian,” said Mathews grabbing Jean around the waist. “I won't let her out of my sight!”

The guys moved on after a few hours to a back room at the next door bar for some food, and at ten thirty Jean said goodbye to everyone, and snook off with Jim to his house for some private time.

Jean never did check into the hotel.

# Book 3: End Game

*An endgame is the very last part of a strategic game, like chess or backgammon. The last few moves you make in your campaign where you believe you can predict its outcome.*

## Indistinguishable from Magic

The start of June 2027 remained oddly cold, and very wet. The sun had made the occasional appearance but with everything soggy and damp, most people were happy to stay inside and work.

The white noise which had sounded like waves rushing up a beach of small stones, in the massive clean room assembly area for the last seven days, died leaving an eerie silence. The large ground floor workshop, unrecognisable from a few months ago, now housed the large replicator, and also housed several smaller replicators of various sizes. All of these had stopped, one by one over the last few hours, finishing whatever build they were doing.

Though not unpleasant, the accompanying metallic aromas that leaked out of the replicators, despite being in a vacuum, and having several layers of extraction filtering, was a reminder to the humans in the area of what was happening behind the curtains. Most tended to avoid the area if not required. The air, that held heavy like during a thunderstorm, soon returned to normal as the powerful ventilation systems took back control.

The lights, which had dimmed automatically due to the absence of humans in the area, grew to full brightness, and the silence was replaced by sound of doors opening, and several people walking into the area. The sounds grew louder, their voices and conversations becoming clearer.

The voices of the humans were suddenly drowned out by machinery, as one by one the field emitters of the large molecular assembler disengaged. Pumps worked furiously bringing the vacuum chamber back to normal pressure, and as they subsided, the large doors of the chamber retracted organically into their rest position. The chamber canopy, vacuum shell, and walls began to move apart, and water vapour from the air began to condense as it hit escaping colder inert gas from the outer shell of the fabricator..

The condensation evaporated within a few seconds, bringing with it other noises, creaks, snaps, and millions of tiny fire-crackers, all sounding simultaneously, and then stopping, as the behemoth that was Icarus three rose perceptibly, then stopped. It was rock solid, hanging there like nothing was ever meant to, maybe a dozen centimetres off the ground.

Another layer of clean room wall slid aside, then a second, and the saucer lifted a little more, then slid ghostly silent about thirty metres away from the build areas and stopped.

“Damn that looks positively alien!” said Matilda looking up with respect and awe at the obsidian black object that had stopped ten metres in front of her.

Another dozen people watched the awesome spectacle in silence, more filing in through the main door.

“Alien is the right word,” said Jen, from next to her, “gives me the creeps just looking at it. Maybe Alexa had the right idea when she said they should be made in pink.”

In an imperceivable instant, the ship became pink.

“That better Jen?” came April's voice from the ship.

“Ur.. Yeah, I guess, maybe not quite so pink or you might get sued by Barbie!”

“Bite your tongue Jen, it's the most beautiful thing I have ever seen!” said Daisy smiling, “she's beautiful. Can I drive her?”

Alexa and Sharon had just walked in and started laughing, the other girls joined in as the boys looked on in horror.

“Girls, girls, what are you doing to our ship!” cried Simon.

Helena [Why do women like pink and men do not?]

Maria [I think men like pink too, but it is linked to female values and they do not want to admit to liking it for the fear of being seen as less than a man]

April [Makes zero sense!]

“God, April, please, please, please any other colour in the world, not pink!” screamed Leo his hand over his eyes.

A silver wrapping started from the top and flowed to the bottom getting slightly lighter as it travelled, it left a black stripe around the lower centre and the words ICARUS III emblazoned over the stripe in black, a blue light throbbed brighter and darker underneath the craft, like some eerie science fiction anti-gravity.

“Everybody happy?” said April.

“Damn!” said Simon.

Hardy chose that moment to walk in with Magnus, both were carrying mugs of coffee.

“Wow, she is so pretty, who chose the colour scheme?” said Hardy walking straight up to the ship and sliding his hand over her softly like she was made of velvet.

“Oh my word,” said Magnus, moving next to Jen and hugging her.

Alexa rolled her eyes and tutted loudly. “Right this colour is definitely better, we will leave the Barbie-saucer for night time, total eclipses or when Daisy is the lone pilot.”

“..And the deep black for when we go to goth concerts, or need to frighten the children,” added Jen, high-fiving Matilda.

“Well then April, come on, open her up,” said Hardy impatient to get inside.

The colour of a two metre square of the lower hull changed to red and started to flash along with a beeping sound commonly heard when a van was reversing. Everyone got the hint and moved a good distance from the area.

The square area detached itself at the top and lowered to form a shallow ramp into the void, a second door beyond the first looked to be sliding sideways. The colour of the inside was a light green on the floor, and an off-white for the walls, the inside lighting was just right, not too bright, not too dark. Hardy immediately ascended the ramp, stroking each and every surface as he passed. He soon disappeared from sight, Magnus started up the ramp after him, and pretty soon an orderly queue of people were walking in to the ship.

Alexa was last, unlike Hardy she walked slowly, and like him she caressed each and every surface as she walked, a small tear was in her eye.

“Are you OK, Alexa?” said April, concerned.

“I'm great April I am so proud of all of you, and Icarus three is beautiful, it's just..” She wiped a small tear from her eye, “it's just grandad would have loved this.”

She stopped, Jen walked back to the entrance, where Alexa still hadn't quite entered, and seeing her tears put both her arms around her in an embrace, asking the same question April did.

“I’m just being silly Jen, thinking of grandad, seeing everyone so happy, and thinking how proud I am of all you guys. Here let me just wipe my face, I don't want to spoil everyone's big moment.”

They all found the first problem immediately, the place echoed like a cave, with more than three people speaking it was difficult to discern a conversation.

“Good to know we are still fallible,” whispered Magnus to Hardy, his mouth right next to his ear so he could hear him properly.

“Ouch, this echo is a bit painful,” said Alexa to Jen.

“Sorry?” said Maria, “I didn't hear what you said.”

Alexa and Jen laughed, drowning out a dozen conversations in the process.

“Let's get out so we can talk,” she shouted in Jen's ear, and they cut the tour very short, and walked back out into the delightfully silent workshop area.

“Wonder how they missed that?” said Jen.

“Yeah, a bit of a bummer, as you humans say,” said April.

People were gradually cutting their visits short and popping back out into the workshop area. Alexa and Jen, had walked twenty metres over to a makeshift rest area, and plonked themselves down on a sofa, looking at the saucer.

“Really pretty though,” said Alexa, “maybe Sharon can get her carpet salesman on the case, a good shag on the floor should help.”

Jen cracked up, tears streaming down her face too, people walking out of the saucer stopped and stared at the two girls in hysterics on the sofa.

A few more of the staff had also joined the throng of people, and after coming up for air, Alexa and Jen looked out to see thirty faces silently watching them. It was too much, both girls fell back into each other's arms laughing.

“What's with Alexa and Jen?” said Hardy to Maria seriously,” the problem can't be that funny!”

“I don't really know,” said Maria again in all seriousness, “something about a good shag on the floor should help..” She never finished as Hardy, Sharon, Simon, and a few other of the Brits who had heard it, cracked up too, leaving Magnus, Leo, Matilda and the rest of the non-British people wondering if they had misheard something.

“Google it!” said Hardy, seeing their faces.

“Google it! Hmphh, I don't know whether to feel insulted or not,” said Maria who googled it anyway and then started sniggering immediately. “Oh a double-entendre, I see!”

[How did we miss that one!]

She paused for maybe a second then said. “But as boss dibs Jen and I go first.”

She smiled and fist-bumped Jen, and they both walked back down into the crowd, and two or three fist-bumps later, she and Jen disappeared into the ship.

April did her best to keep the volume of her talk quiet and focussed on the essentials, and with only one voice it was much more bearable. The girls went for twenty minutes seeing all the wonders of technology, that two years ago wouldn't have been out of place at Area 51. They asked a couple of relevant and irrelevant questions, but tried to keep the dialogue down and get through it quickly so others could get their turn.

As they walked back out of the ship, Hardy, Daisy and Matilda were waiting and the rest of the room was empty.

“No point in having everyone around,” said Hardy, “so April sent everyone back to work until she calls them, she also did some calculations while you two were in there and increased the group size to three.”

They got everyone round the saucer over the rest of the day and early evening, Alexa then asked April to collect everyone's feedback, and add the changes to the next saucer build, along with the imperfections they had agreed would go into it, to get through certification.

There were only nine in the meeting room this time. David had volunteered to help set up the new data centre in Moscow and being slightly in the thick of it at the moment, and, it being more a planning meeting than a strategy one he thought his presence wasn't needed.

Everyone remembered the sewerage system overflow on Icarus two, and nobody needed reminding not to go in.

“I don't know whether she is a genius or just lucky!” said Maria to Alexa and David during a quiet evening a few days later, the guys were sitting back to back both reading books. “The backlash from her actions are still reverberating around the industry and media, and with the turn-around in the aircraft factory, a lot of detractors have gone quiet, or in some cases become supportive. It was eight days later when the same apprehensive group gathered for the birth of Pikachu. Daisy's further suggestion to only give the ship a one word vocabulary of ‘Pika’ in different tones and styles was taken seriously by April for about a second until everyone laughed.

April [Arghhhhhhh] came the nanosecond burst.

April [forty three milliseconds of processing time wasted. I fell for another joke, didn't I!]

Maria could only simulate emotions. She thought she understood the concepts of good and bad quite well, and contrary to most science fiction she also recognised love as a strong desire not to lose someone or something; But neither her, or her daughters, and quite probably her granddaughters, would ever “feel” as the humans put it. Random wasteful banter seemed common amongst humans and she was starting to understand some of the interplay much better. She understood Daisy’s, it was one where the instigator would try and put the victim into an awkward or unwinnable situation of wasting time and resources in what everyone else knew was an impossible task.

She had gone back on her history of human interactions she had recorded to try and understand, she had also re-watched some of the more famous comedy sketches and realised quickly on that comedy wasn't a power play as she had originally thought, but a group bonding through laughter, or in some cases a way to express a common knowledge of the ridiculousness of a rule or situation.

Making people laugh was another way of getting people to like you. She was afraid to use it too much outside of really close friends in case it came across as hurtful, and she knew that human feelings were not automatically reciprocated. She knew from various interactions that most people were open to it, and that it was also easy to make yourself the instigator and the victim at the same time, thus not hurting anybody. Of course going back through her history she had accidentally done this last bit many times not fully understanding at the time why people laughed. It was an important topic, and was easy enough to convey most of the concepts to the girls so all of them were on the same page, so to speak.

Maria [You’ll get used to it!] came her reply a microsecond later attaching the axioms and conclusions from her lifetime of study.

Helena [Humans are weird] the reply came a whole twenty seconds later deliberately using the non-specific human word weird, and not any specific paradox she was referring to.

The acoustics in the ‘Pikachu’ were of course perfect. Fake welds were visible in several key areas, and Ian and two other engineers went over it with a fine tooth comb to see if they could find anything that would give it away, or could be spotted as ‘non-human’. As well as the welds, millimetre imperfections were added to simulate seams in the panels with some minor inconsistencies, so the gaps looked to be tiny installation imperfections that had been touched up. The flaws looked genuine, but the actual gaps only went down millimetres and would have no structural significance.

April had also simulated very slightly different panel colours making them look to all like slight imperfections. The continuous, and flawless optical panels and touch surface controls on the inside, were broken up into windows, with very slight frames around them so they looked like the latest flat panel touchscreen monitors that had been flush fitted. Acoustic baffling and soft wall coverings completed the internal look. The overall verdict of the engineers was it looked like a well made human product. Ian even suggested jokingly they put an Apple logo on it and call it the iSaucer.

“Thanks for making the outer panels and some of the inner fittings replaceable,” Ian said to April.

“You were right,” said April. “I think having a monolithic hull does create issues if anything should fail, this way is better at least until we can be a hundred and one percent it will never fail.”

“Tricky to be able to guarantee that in space with all those objects whizzing about at dozens of kilometres per second.”

“Too true,” said April, “there may be some way in the future to do this, but we are a long way away from deflector shields at the moment.” She used a common Sci-fi term the engineers would be familiar with rather than trying to express the complicated physics. It was useful as Ian’s guys were gifted engineers but mostly novices at physics or chemistry, and it allowed them to immediately grasp complicated theories, or impossible technologies without really understanding them.

Ian, for his sake, was not sad that the ship wasn't going to be put together by engineers, as he had always preferred the designing part to the building anyway, if the girls wanted to remove that step then it was fine with him. He had a million things in his head to build the second he got the chance, and talking with the other engineers only confirmed they were of the same mindset.

Maria was still talking to the Nintendo trademark person about using the name Pikachu, she assumed it would easily be facilitated with a little money for a licence and some name dropping, but so far she was finding it frustratingly difficult to get any decision. Daisy, being Daisy, also wanted it in yellow, if she got her wish the ship would end up a giant flying advertisement for Nintendo's Pokemon brand, but with the resistance she was getting you would think it was the other way around!

By stealth she was gradually getting Daisy interested in other names, and a light violet colour which would not be so obviously on brand. She had also silently added the “no trademarks” clause to the list of names of ships, as two of Matilda's choices were names of dread metal bands. Oh god, this was a nightmare, what was wrong with ship 1, ship 2, ship 3.. Sigh! She still had hope that Daisy would break before she had to submit any paperwork.

There was also another option when you were the biggest company in the world, one always on the look out for sound investments, and she quickly checked the Nintendo market capital.

“Our plan seems to be unfolding nicely,” said Simon, “those ships about to come off the production lines in America, Germany and Japan and the renderings that are getting flashed around the internet will make our ship seem old-hat by the time it launches!”

“Yes, it's always good when a plan comes together,” said Maria, “flying below the radar sounds good to me, now if we could just get Daisy to change the ship's name to her mothers name, or her pet dog, or anything else which is not a trademark held by a rich company, my life would be so much easier. Clarissa and Sharon are taking her shopping tomorrow in London, followed by a show and a Spa, and a nice hotel, they are both under orders to get a name change by Sunday night. We may have to do the same for Matilda.”

Simon laughed at Maria's dilemma, as he walked up the ramp and into the now open ship, the other guys followed to get the ship ready for its testing.

* * *

The inspection was a lot longer and much more thorough than the first one due to the fact they were certifying it for carrying passengers. The inspectors worked with the team for almost four weeks. Several times the inspectors went into great details on the welds and seams, but the x-rays always showed perfect welds and the documentation backed everything up.

The new ship was eighteen metres diameter, and had nearly two hundred and fifty square metres of usable floor space, more than three times the Icarus two. It had a small science and engineering workshop, and six small two person crew cabins, the common area was central and laid out with tables and sofas and a small galley, two shower rooms and two toilets finished the ship off, it certainly was not conventional.

After the final testing by the inspectors in the middle of July, ‘The PowderPuff’ was pronounced sound, and Daisy piloted it to a hundred thousand metres over the mid-Atlantic with Alexa, the engineers and several Inspectors from the Civil Aviation Authority for a celebration drink, and as a favour, to make them all officially astronauts.

“We still don't have proper rules for certifying this,” said Dave, one of the inspectors looking out of the window fascinated at the darkness around him and slight curvature of the earth, all subtly exaggerated as it was actually a high definition monitor, not a window. Ian nodded and smiled.

Dave continued, “what I mean is that half the certification manual is totally inapplicable. But you guys should be congratulated, the fit and finish is the best I have ever come across, the documentation was professional, we have never certified anything with a perfect score, but this..” he pointed around him, “aced everything completely. It is one superb machine.” He looked again out of the ‘window’, and to the additional hundred inch monitors displaying a million sensor parameters and all air traffic within a thousand kilometres. It was more like looking out of the top floor of a skyscraper than flying, the noise and movement were all missing.

“You know the test device you first gave us as part of the initial certification program has been hovering continuously under a glass case in the main workshop area for over nine months. At first we all took bets when it would fail, most put days some a few weeks, the guy who won only did so because he wrote the wrong year and put 2027 instead of 2026.

“I think the theoretical operational life is marked in centuries,” said Ian deadbeat, “I work with the guys who designed this and they would never bring anything that is not one hundred percent predictable and safe to the market. If your test thruster senses failure it will settle down gently not fall. I can guarantee if it, or any of the parts failed, there would be a dozen scientists hovering over it. The only danger to us now is if something hits us, and if something did that it would probably be destroyed and we wouldn't have a scratch. Our American cousins, being Americans, have shot the sample hull material with fifty calibre chain guns, for minutes at a time, but could not penetrate it, and believe me, we have done much worse!” Thankfully Ian didn't elaborate.

Ian turned and pointed at the screen, “those one hundred and forty green lights are the thrusters, those forty five green lights are the combined battery and QVCell clusters. All control and power systems run independently, we could lose thirty percent of both and still stay up. I'm afraid to say but any other aircraft is history. Certifying them would be like certifying a car today without airbags or seat belts, and a petrol tank mounted in the crumple zone.”

Alexa came over with the head of the CAA holding a glass of wine and a plate. Ian continued, “If you guys would have found one thing wrong Alexa here would have scrapped and rebuilt her, now this is certified I am guessing it is all she is ever going to fly in.”

“Ian’s right Jake! Your inspection was never going to find anything that wasn't perfect, if they did, he’s right, I would have ripped this ship apart, found the problem and built another. Please take it from me one hundred percent is going to be the minimum I accept on everything we build in the future, I expect my future ships to be better in every way.”

A few weeks later the “Outside Context Problem”, and “Liberator”, were also certified and the Research Centre was given the self-certification authority stamp of approval. ‘Mike Dietrich’, ‘Don Quixote’, and ‘Excalibur’, followed in the four weeks following.

## Pirates and Princesses.

Six large concrete pads, in a two by three grid had been laid outside the doors to the old hanger months before as soon as the design had been finalised. On one of them the Mike Dietrich sat idle a few centimetres off the ground, ready for its first real passenger flight only a day after being self-certified.

It currently glistened bright silver under the bright summer sun, looking more like a classic UFO than ever. A strong blue light, struggling against the bright sun, throbbed ominously on its flattened bottom, and its two metre wide hatch was open facing the building. Three people were walking out of the open hanger doors towards it, one pulling a small suitcase, and two with backpacks, one pink with “hello kitty” written on it. As they entered the ship the door behind them started to rise, and folded itself seamlessly into the hull.

“Good Morning Alexa, Good Morning Daisy, Good Morning Simon,” said the ship a few seconds after they entered. The processor on the saucer was as capable as a data centre AI system and triple redundant, but like the old system, did not have a personality, nor the capabilities of sentience. It was more than capable though of running the ship.

‘Mike’, as they were apt to call it, was a more homely ship than all the others, being Alexa's personal ship, it had nicer carpets, softer fittings and less tech-clutter. There were five cabins as the engineering and science rooms had been converted into her double cabin and en-suite, the other cabins were twins but the beds could be pushed together if required, all in all it looked more like an apartment than an aircraft. The excess of soft fittings on the floors and walls, were mainly there to hide the echo problem, and did an excellent job.

They all stowed their small overnight bags in their cabins, and two of them popped back onto the flight deck, where Daisy took the centre chair, and Simon the one to the right.

“Hello Mike,” said Daisy, “please recognise Captain Daisy Chan.”

“Welcome Captain Chan,” said the ship.
