“Roger Jupiter, Jupiter, X ray, Tango, One, we see your transponder active, you are clear to depart, ceiling three thousand metres, for landing Bristol airport pad Alpha one, Immigration and customs have been advised, we will see you in a few minutes Daisy over.”

“Thanks Stan, see you soon over and out.”

“Mike take us to three thousand metres, please follow the usual flight plan approach to pad Alpha One, air speed to match planned flight time given by air traffic control.”

“Roger Captain,” came Mike's voice and the ship immediately started to rise, this time there was a little more acceleration felt, but no more than an elevator.

That was really all there was to it. The pilot was there because, well, that was the rules. Mike could handle the nuances of the whole flight and any emergencies, anything outside of the agreed instructions would have him request the pilots attention. April had agreed to be in charge of the ship AI’s so she would also be alert for anything out of the normal.

Alexa walked in and popped a mug on Daisy's console and another on Simon's, then walked back out.

“Thanks Alexa,” they both shouted after her.

“Maybe you should think about having a stewardess for these flights,” shouted Simon after her.

“Oh, don't be silly,” she said walking back in with a mug of tea, “what would they do? The housekeeping staff have cleaned and serviced the rooms, and the cook has prepared enough food for two days. All we have to do is warm it up in the microwave and stick the dishes in the dishwasher afterwards.”

She sat down in the seat to the left of Daisy and fastened her seatbelt, the little clicking noise, and annoying flashing seatbelt light extinguishing on the main screen. Three of the items on the checklist had also disappeared, and a timer was counting down to the next action in two minutes.

“It's a bit crazy,” said Daisy, “we can get to Dusseldorf in thirty minutes, but immigration and customs both ends are going to make this take all morning.”

“Everyone's frustrated Daisy, not just you,” said Maria, “we could pay for a customs and an immigration official to come down to the research centre, but we would rather they don't ask too many questions, so we have to suffer the slight inconvenience. You should hear the chatter from the pilots and air traffic control, everyone hates the system, and some countries are even worse.”

Daisy pressed the switch in the arm rest.

“Bristol air traffic control, please be advised Dietrich Air Jupiter, Jupiter X Ray Tango one approaching Bristol Airport, touchdown in five minutes, over.”

“Roger Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, clear skies, twelve knot westerly, permission to land on pad A2, over and out.”

“Mike, bring us in for landing and take us to standby readiness one when landed.” She turned to Simon, “will there be any problem with the customs coming back you think?”

“No,” said Simon. “The cargo is not dangerous, but it has some biological parts and cryogenic cooling, so it's a bit sensitive to being disturbed until they start the gestation. We will seal it in the hold. Technically we do not have a hold, and the hatch is seamless so it won't generate questions.”

“Oh, I get it, a secret compartment for smuggling! My great grandfather had one of those on his boat, well that's what my grandma said,” she smiled.

“Let's keep any talks of secret compartments, secret shall we Captain Chan,” said Alexa smiling at Daisy and tapping her nose.

The craft touched down without a further sound. “Landing completed Captain, systems are at standby readiness one, altitude plus two hundred and fifty millimetre.”

“Thank you Mike, a very smooth flight, please open the door for departing.”

Daisy sounded quite professional, thought Alexa, but piloting a flying saucer probably wasn't that difficult, and should be a walk in the park for someone with her brain. The three of them got up and walked to the open door and out of the ramp. A uniformed immigration official was waiting for them. “This way please,” he said without inflection.

There was a small immigration area for VIP and private flights at the airport, separate from the public area, it was paid for in their landing fees. They each scanned their passports and walked through the scanner that checked and photographed them, then walked out. The immigration guy watched them but no assistance was required so left them to it. A few of their previous flights had been inspected by customs on departure, but they were considered fairly low risk and Maria said they had been cleared without inspection.

“Thank you,” said the immigration guy a little bit happier, “everything is fine, have a safe journey.”

“Thank you,” they all said politely and trotted back in the saucer. The saucer door had been left unlocked, but it was impossible for someone or something to get past Mike without him alerting them, so they trotted back in and took their seats again. Their drinks still warm due to induction heating pads designed in the cup-holders, thank you Ian!

The journey to Dusseldorf was also uneventful, though delayed as they had to hold, at twenty thousand metres for a landing slot. Being the first time the saucer had landed in Germany, there was a big crowd, and a few TV stations there to watch it arrive. April played the live stream from the TV channel on another screen on the flight deck. On the screen, the craft came down majestically, the red and white running lights soon lost as the powerful blue lights underneath started to throb powerfully. It was purely for show but the guys had determined that people expected to see an engine, and the blue pulsing light show, which changed with the acceleration profile, fitted the bill perfectly. They also had a selection of futuristic engine sounds they could play, they were normally linked to the pilots profile. Though she did not know it, Alexa's profile was based on the United Planets Cruiser C-57D from the old movie the forbidden planet.

Simon spoke German but the other guys didn’t, so April, with Simon's consent, translated the TV coverage real-time to English rather than use subtitles.

“..I’m not sure what everyone was expecting but the landing was magnificent, it came in so fast, slowing rapidly and coming to a stop what looks like less than a metre from the ground. From our position outside here we could hear a weird pulsating noise which seemed to beat in time to the engines underneath, but now it is all quiet.” The camera panned over the crowd of people looking out of the airport lounges, and observation windows.

“We are not sure who is on the ship which is named the Mike Dietrich after the owners grandfather, a German national who fled before the great war, but the public information says it is carrying three people.” The camera panned to a woman, with about a dozen small children around her, “It looks like even the local primary school has come out for the event.” The camera and reporter went over to her. “Are you excited seeing the flying saucer?”

The woman smiled, “oh yes, one of the children's parents works at the airport and told her the saucer was coming in today, so I decided to bring all the children to see what their future looks like.” The kids were all trying to peer through the rail, and mostly all smiles. “I think some of them are obviously a little disappointed this is the closest they will get, but I expect they will be common enough when they are older..”

“Awe! So cute.” Said Alexa.

“Damn we looked good!” said Simon.

Standby readiness state one, was basically a hover two hundred and fifty millimetres above the ground, with all thrusters at idle power, and power cells feeding power to the batteries and capacitor bank in case they needed to lift quickly.

Daisy pressed her button, “Dusseldorf control this is Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, passengers and crew are ready to accept customs and immigration staff when they are ready. Please be advised onward flight plan to Velbert once clearance is made. Over”

An image of the controller came on the screen as usual so they knew who they were talking to.

“Dusseldorf control, to Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, a very beautiful ship, and a beautiful landing if I may say. A ground car will be there shortly with the customs and immigration staff, your scheduled departure is at oh, two, twenty five, I have been asked by the airport director to forward a request from the local TV station to allow them outside your ship to get some close up pictures, over.”

“Thank you Dusseldorf control, please hold, Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, over.”

Daisy looked at Alexa and said, “I don't mind showing them around, if those poor little kids can come.”

Simon and Alexa smiled.

“OK,” said Alexa, “let Maria handle it as she can do three calls simultaneously, no promises but if we are here for a few hours anyway it might be good to have a bit of good publicity.”

“Frau Fredrick is a bit confused.. OK she's in.. The airport director says she is fine so long as it is after your clearance, and they are accompanied by a member of security.. And the TV station is good, though I told them no more than a cameraman and a reporter, and the cameraman can only come inside with the children with the teachers consent, otherwise they interview the teacher outside when they leave. Also the ship will be departing soon and everyone needs to have cleared the area by two o’clock.”

“I guess that works,” said Alexa. “You want in on this Simon or want to get a car to take you to the guys lab facility, it should only take forty minutes to drive there.”

“Nah, I will wait with you guys, I can practise my German with the schoolkids, and the teacher.”

Alexa gave Daisy the thumbs up.

“Maria,” said Daisy, “I'm not sure I can remember all that, could you do the honours please?”

“Dusseldorf control,” came Daisy's clear voice out of the speaker, “thank you for waiting, all is acceptable, please arrange for the people that Director Lietze has just authorised to be outside the ship in thirty minutes, when we complete clearance, Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, over and out.”

“You are so scary sometimes Maria,” Daisy laughed, “I should get you to talk to my mum and nan, I repeat myself all the time and I could cut my calls down to once a month instead of once a week.”

“A car has arrived outside the ship,” said Mike.

“OK, we are in a new country with new rules so everyone be on their best behaviour,” said Alexa.

The door opened and they admitted the one man, and one woman, into the lounge area. They both seemed to forget their tasks as they stared open mouthed at the inside of the ship.

“Guten-Tag,” said Simon, moving their concentration back to the task in hand.

Simon and both the new people conversed politely for a few seconds in German, then all looked to Alexa.

“Er, Spraken sie English?” said Alexa apologetically.

Both people smiled, “of course miss,” said the man, “I was just complimenting your colleague here on your very beautiful airship.”

“Helga Lindt, Immigration Department,” the woman said, then pointed at the man, “and that is Mr Grubber, or Gustov, as everyone calls him, from customs and excise.”

“Daisy Chan, pilot,” said Alexa pointing at Daisy, “Doctor Simon Jones,” pointing at Simon, “and me Alexa Martins.”

“Normally if you were staying here we would not need to inspect your ship,” said Gruber, “but since you have a short flight to Velbert a quick inspection is the normal, it is just a formality, but if you have anything on this list you need to let me know before I leave.”

He handed her a small tablet, “I will have a quick walk through and be back in about ten minutes, feel free to accompany me, when Helga has checked your passport.”

“That is fine,” said Alexa, accepting the form, “please take your time and examine anything you like, the ship will answer any questions. I will join you once Helga is finished.” Alexa gave Helga her passport and gestured to her to sit down at the table they had prepared for her.

The passport inspection was completed in a few minutes, using a laptop with a scanner and camera. The customs guy was currently looking in Simon's room, he entered one other bedroom, and a bathroom, looked in a few kitchen cupboards and pronounced the inspection complete. Alexa handed him back a signed form when he came back into the common room as did the two others.

“We have a school party and a TV Crew coming for a small tour in a few minutes,” said Alexa to the two people, “please feel free to join in if you can spare thirty minutes. Simon and the ship's AI Mike will be doing the tour in German, unfortunately being a New Zealander I know nothing but English and we don't speak that too well either,” she laughed.

“English, Mandarin and Korean, but no German Sorry,” said Daisy.

Both were nodding, “that would be great,” said Helga, “my radio and phone do not seem to be working on the ship so I will need to go outside and let them know I have cleared you and I will be taking a small break.”

“Mine neither,” said Gustov.

“Graphyne with a super-conductor weave,” smiled Simon to two very confused people.

The ship said something rapidly in German, Helga and Gustov nodded, then Helga said something in the same rapid tone, and a completely separate voice came back, the ship repeated the same with Gustov.

“All good,” said Maria, “or as they say in German, alles klar. There you go Alexa, that's ten words you know now, about double your French vocabulary!”

Alexa rolled her eyes, the other four giggled.

“I have heard about the new AI systems but they are most impressive in person,” said Gustov.

A few more words of German came out of the speaker, and Helga and Simon started laughing, Gustov looked a bit embarrassed.

“And it has a fine sense of humour,” laughed Helga, both men shook their heads.

“The party is waiting outside by the way,” said Maria.

The sixteen children went everywhere, sitting on seats, poking things, looking in cupboards, flushing toilets. The teacher, with the help of the other adults and Maria, had managed to get them back to the flight deck. All their attention was now on a red flashing word the equivalent of “Incoming Transmission from Princess” in German.

Simon tapped the adults and whispered something then smiled and put his thumb up to the screen.

The internal ship's alarms sounded and the ship rumbled. The ship's computer voice sounded loudly in German. “Brace for Warp Speed,” the lights in the ship changed to red and all the screens changed to show the ship leaving the airport, and accelerating to space with lots of planets and stars flying past, and a ridiculous speed showing. The kids were spellbound and immediately at attention.

“We have received a distress signal from the Princess who is being attacked by Pirates, should we save her children?” the ship said in German. All the kids enthusiastically said yes, and the screen immediately sped up to warp speed with lots more colours and flying stars. It rumbled again, and as it dropped out of warp.

A large comical looking space pirate ship, with a flag no less, appeared on the main viewer shooting at an equally comical small pink spaceship. The children gasped and shouted in awe, but none seemed scared.

“As the ship is only configured for young lady captains, I need the youngest lady to sit in the captains seat, and fire the laser with the yellow button.” Said Maria in a silly computer voice.

A few hands went up, and one of the smaller girls sat down, immediately pressing the yellow button like crazy, to lots of shouting and encouragement from her friends

They closed rapidly with the pirate ship, each press of the button, firing a slow-moving, Hollywood style, laser bolt at it. The laser bolts being fired back, seemingly doing nothing. Fake rumbles and laser noises were followed by fiery explosions on the pirate ship, then finally the pirate ship turned and accelerated away, leaving a comical trail of smoke.

The screen cleared and flashed up an incoming transmission. the window that opened was that of a far too young space captain looking a little bit too much like a Disney Princess, sitting next to a pink dog with antennas. She spoke heartfelt and rapidly in German thanking them and saying how they saved the Galaxy. She then bade goodbye, the space-dog gave a few yip's, and her window closed, showing her ship moving off into space.

The screens then showed the saucer going back into hyperspace and returning to the earth, landing at the airport, and the lights and screens all going back to normal.

Simon said something in German. “Well done children, it looks like you saved the princess from the pirates and chased them off!” Maria was obviously helping him through his earbud.

The children laughed and screamed excitedly amongst each other, hugging the young girl who was captain, it really was an experience no eight year old would ever forget.

“Sorry about that guys,” said Maria in German, as the kids started to trundle out of the saucer excitedly, herded by a bemused security guy.

“I got a bit carried away trying to keep the kids entertained, our flights are not normally that exciting.” All the adults smiled and the school teacher thanked them profusely and quickly followed the last child, the cameraman running rapidly after them.

Anyone outside the ship noticing it moving up and down and side to side a little said nothing, and did not think anything of it.

The two airport officials thanked everyone, saying it was the best thing they had experienced in ages and walked off in excited discussion.

The flight deck screen was showing the cameraman focused on an animated child going through the motions of shooting pirates. Another cameraman had shown up from another TV station and was interviewing the security guard.

“That was amazing Maria,” said Alexa, “you never said you could do that!”

“A lady must have her secrets.”

“Oh Maria, you are so full of surprises,” said Daisy, even more excited than usual, “I want to have a go with the lasers, shakes and sounds dialled up to ten when Matilda is on board. And you mustn't tell her!”

“No worries Daisy,” though Maria was wondering how Daisy was going to hide the obvious media blitz that would inevitably happen. “Oh by the way I had to turn off Mike's inputs during the demonstration, it would have been too confusing for him, he can only deal with reality, so better not mention it or he might get confused.”

“Dusseldorf control, to Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One,” came the voice in accented English, “we have a lot of excited children and happy reporters and a very happy airport director here, she says to say thank you. Whatever you did, it sounds like you will be welcomed back anytime, I can't wait to watch the news when I get off shift. Your window to leave is in forty five minutes, hopefully the children did not leave too much mess, over.”

“Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One to Dusseldorf control,” said Daisy, “we may have had a very small trip to another galaxy and saved a princess from a pirate, luckily we had the children on board to help, I will drop you guys our internal video after the TV has its exclusive, over.”

“Dusseldorf control, to Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray Tango One, we look forward to seeing it, will contact you again five minutes before departure, over and out.”

Their departure forty five minutes later was equally well viewed if not more as the TV station was showing all the children shouting, and the scene in the bridge almost on repeat.

They went to two thousand metres, their ceiling for the flight, sailed across Dusseldorf and were at the outskirts of Velbert at the research teams laboratories in seven minutes. About five minutes into the flight the skin of the saucer rippled, the colour mimicking the sky perfectly and visually at least it disappeared.

Five minutes later the saucer dropped to three hundred metres, re-asserted its normal colours and landed bang in the middle of a big H that had been chalked carelessly in the middle of a large almost empty car park. A large four storey block stood next to it, resembling some sort of school or hospital in its construction rather than an office. The car park looked slightly worn, the original markings had faded and it had cracked in some places where vegetation was starting to intrude.

The large acreage was surrounded by a large chain fence more like an army base or an airport. The majority of the land consisted of big wooded areas, which stretched beyond the property boundary in all directions broken only by the single road leading to it. It seemed pretty isolated, yet they had been flying over mainly urban areas most of the way.

Karl, Hanna, Peter and Nicko, the four founder members of the Structural Organics Company were waiting outside, all seemingly excited to watch the Mike arrive. Around them were the other six staff from the company, who were all obviously excited to see the landing.

The door to the ship opened and Simon and Alexa walked out and straight up to the crowd of people exchanging greetings. All the team were thankfully fluent in English and would defer to it while Alexa and Daisy were present.

The ship behind them changed colour to a mishmash of colours mimicking the colour of the surroundings directly behind or under it and hopefully making it difficult to see from a distance. It then lowered to the floor, the twenty tonnes settling out over several car spaces and not seeming to cause too much stress on the tarmac.

Daisy walked out and received the same welcome.

“That vehicle is amazing, I bet from a hundred metres away you would not know it is there!” said Karl, a larger guy with a shaved head and beard and small round glasses. “And you really played space pirates with some school children! so much for keeping the visit low profile,” everybody laughed.

“Blame Daisy,” said Alexa, “she can't resist children.”

Daisy frowned, “It was fun! Don't pretend you all didn't enjoy it, anyway It was Maria's gig and I think she enjoyed it even more, it was an amazing bit of improvisation she deserves an Oscar.”

“Thank you Daisy, I did,” came the little voice from a heart shaped gold brooch with a little sapphire, pinned on her blue pilot's uniform, a uniform nobody would have worn except Daisy, though it was actually quite stylish.

Alexa could see some guys were wearing earbuds and obviously getting some help with the translation.

After a quick impromptu tour of the saucer, they all strolled in to the main doors.

“..I think it is the first time you have seen the new offices,” said Hanna, a frail looking tall girl with long blonde hair, and who, like all the others, was wearing a lab coat with her name on. “Maria was amazing finding the property and purchasing it so quickly, it used to be a training centre, people would come in for various internal courses and outdoor activity courses, but it closed three years ago during the COVID crisis, it has been empty ever since. The company initially wanted too much money for the site, as most of the wooded areas are protected, and cannot be developed on, or farmed on, and the acreage is too big for most to use.”

“We moved in six months ago from the university,” said Peter, the oldest by ten years, again quite tall with glasses but going a bit bald on top, “the construction crew were in for two months before that enlarging some of the classrooms for offices and converting others to labs, it has three big labs on the ground floor, an open lab area on the first, an open office area on the second. We also have six smaller rooms on the top floor which three of us decided to move in to, Hanna lives only four kilometres away so is happy to commute. We have another two staff not here today, both are finishing dissertations at the university and are sad not to be here, but they have been reserved seats to attend your lecture tomorrow.”

He gestured to everyone, opening the entrance door, “Welcome.”

They walked inside. Nicko the youngest of the four founders, coming in last. He was average looking in every way but with a darker complexion and jet black hair, he was also the least talkative of the bunch, preferring like Magnus to work with Maria or Helena. His genius in using the new improved CRISPR systems to synthesise custom molecules put him at the top of his field and able to get any job, but like all the scientists who were directly or indirectly involved with Maria he was given the opportunity to become master of his own destiny. Nicko kept a low profile, preferring to get as quick as possible to a working solution, it was his work which put the icing on the cake of the project and would probably eventually earn the team a Nobel prize.

“I have booked a back room at Giorgio's Italian restaurant for six thirty,” said Maria to everyone, “the car for Alexa and Daisy will pick them up after the meal and take them to their hotel. Why don't you show them around, and let's say we all assemble at four PM in the meeting room to go over the experiment and who is doing what.”

“I’m bunking here,” said Simon to Daisy and Alexa, “Its only two nights and it will be easier if I am on site.”

“There is a small change of plan,” said Hanna as they walked through the empty reception, “Karl wont be coming, he is staying here to monitor some stuff, and will join the project remotely when he is required.”

“I unfortunately don't travel well, inner ear problem,” said Karl. “Also causes problems with the telepresence and virtual reality equipment, even cars make me sick these days; Anyway, someone needs to stay here to look after our control experiments, and I may need physical access to them to answer any questions.”

“I'm sure Maria will provide anyone who stays with a ring-side seat,” said Alexa.

They continued in, through what was once a large reception area but was now unmanned. It was unadorned except for a quite nice corporate sign and logo saying the Structural Organic Company, with smaller lettering underneath saying partners with the Dietrich Research Centre. Alexa paused and thought it looked quite professional, but all their offices seemed to be lacking people, she understood Maria provided all the services, and that visitors rarely if ever came, but surely at least a receptionist would be warranted.

“What would they do?” said Maria when she queried, the other guys looking on.

“Oh I don't know, keep the guys company, make teas and coffees, put flowers on the table..” Alexa ran out of ideas, “..well it seems a bit empty. At least in the Research Centre it feels more homely..”

“Karl's mum comes around and cleans twice a week..” Said Hanna smiling.

“Oh you guys know what I mean,” said Alexa.

“I do,” said Peter, “but it would be a boring job.”

“I guess,” sighed Alexa moving on through some double doors into a large open office area.

This big office was a lot busier, it had four state of the art workstations all with multiple screens, and the fans from them made quite a hum. Further into the room was a meeting table and three large presentation screens.

“This is Nicko's area,” said Hanna, “the big servers at the back have extra processing capacity for his needs, and through the window there in the next room are the gene printing machines we use to create our wonderful little creations.”

“The new equipment allows us to work many times faster than before, and the analysis lab through the other set of doors adjacent to the printer is very automated, so Gerty here can run most experiments on her own.” The smallest member of the team who seemed like a German copy of Daisy waved.

“The labs and facilities here are much better than the university,” said Karl, “none of this would be possible without you guys. We were a bit sceptical at first, but it was Maria who introduced us, pointed out the synergy of our work, and gave us some interesting goals and funding which would make our research viable.”

“Yes,” said Hanna, “there is a big bias towards purely mechanical systems, but hybrid biological and mechanical systems, can normally achieve the same results with less complexity, and more reliability, as with the bioreactor in your ship.”

“..which is most impressive,” said Daisy for the first time.

“Nicko and Karl have created some modified enzymes which can process the grey water to drinkable..” Started Hanna.

“..We still need filters, Hanna,” added Karl, “but Hanna is right, we are now working on a way of removing all the mechanical filters and replacing them with a purely biological filtering system.”

They were now walking out through the analysis lab, into one of the big laboratories. The area had small windows, which were darkened out as they were working on improving the ferric deposition concentrations on the outer layer bark of their seed project. It looked more like a brewery than a laboratory, with dozens of small tanks looking like domestic hot water cylinders, each with dozens of pipes into them. Some of them had ice forming around the outside, and some were behind screens, or inside chambers.

“It is mostly automated,” said Hanna, “biological systems work within a certain temperature range, and with a balance of the correct chemicals, all these tanks run our different strains and our control enzymes, so we can compare different batches after the initial lab tests are complete.”

The room carried on into another which looked identical, and then another, almost going the length of the building. They turned out of a side door at the end, and back into a large corridor. They almost immediately entered another lab, more like a traditional laboratory with test tubes, glass piping, and Bunsen burners all on normal tables, with computers, and various weird contraptions holding test tubes.

“This is my area,” chirped Gerty to Alexa, “I work here with Grace Ling but she is finishing her dissertations today in Bonn with Max, they will see you tomorrow at your talk.”

Alexa couldn't think of any sensible reply so she just smiled and nodded.

They walked around the various experiments. A few of the guys had gone back to work now, including Gerty, so the crowd was down to the four core scientists. The rooms got stranger before they got normal. She looked into a massive room with dark sunken pools of water, that used to be a swimming pool, then to one which was a walk-in freezer, which was set too cold for someone to go into, without the proper special thermal gear that was hanging outside.

They finally passed out into a more conventional electronics and mechanical workshop which was Peter's domain, in it were everything you would need to build most modern devices. She recognised one of their early test replicators by its vacuum case and the stylised Dietrich Research Centre logo that Ian stuck on them.

“The engineers here have been to Simon's labs many times, and have used these already, if that is what you are wondering,” chirped Maria. “We have them in most of our labs now, but only us girls can operate them, otherwise they are just bricks.”

As if hearing the conversation Peter said, “these are magic, we can 3D print most things, some parts would take months to manufacture without them.”

The Seed Package, as it was known, was what they had come for. It was the mechanical machine that nurtured and controlled the organic package, which would grow into a structure. It looked pretty ominous, almost like the first atomic bomb from the Oppenheimer movie a few years ago. Anyone walking in and seeing it could not realistically come to any other conclusion from a distance, yet close up it was obviously more delicate.

Simon touched it, so deeming it safe, Alexa did too. “What's it made of?” she said genuinely interested.

“It feels like plastic,” said Karl, “but it is wholly organic, with some nitrogen and silicon, very strong like a sea shell but it breaks down quickly when certain enzymes come into contact with it. The organic core is inside, as are the electro-mechanical control systems. The organic core is currently held below zero degrees Celsius, to keep it in a suspended state.”

“You should have at least painted it green, it looks so scary!” Said Alexa.

Peter and his three engineers all laughed. “Yes,” said Ryan, one of the engineers, “we were dreading somebody seeing it and telling the authorities, it would not be nice to be woken up by helicopters and army soldiers with guns like in the movies.”

Peter and the engineers spent a few more minutes explaining things to Alexa and Daisy, as everyone else, including Simon, were well aware how everything worked. All the guys had been told by Maria that Alexa was not the best at science, she would nod her head to be polite, but as soon as they said anything complicated she would likely start looking anywhere else, so it would be best to just keep to simple terms and concepts. The closest Alexa had gotten to science in her past were probably the House and CSI TV series she liked growing up, or the few Christopher Nolan movies that dealt with the subject.

“We call it the seed as it sounds friendly.” Said Nicko in one of his unexpected communications with the group. “It will be moved into the ship tomorrow and the cooling system hooked up to its power. It is nice of you to volunteer your own personal transport for this Alexa.”

“We have a better ship for you in England,” said Simon. “The seed package will be transferred into the new ship for the mission, the new ship has a proper science lab, more suitable accommodation, and a new remote manipulator to help you when you get there.”

“Hey! What do you mean by more suitable accommodation, what's wrong with my ship?” complained Alexa, giving Simon the evil stare she usually reserved for Hardy after one of his sarcastic comments.

“Seriously Alexa,” said Simon, “It has fluffy pink and blue furnishings everywhere, even curtains, it feels more like a love hotel than a spaceship!”

“I like it,” said Daisy nonchalantly.

“..Yeah, thanks Daisy,” smiled Alexa proudly, then turning back to Simon, “I think Simon might be walking home if he isn't extremely nice to me over the next two days!” she smiled at him.

The German guys were looking at each other a bit confused.

“Don't worry about Simon, he just lacks a feminine eye for detail,” dismissed Alexa.

Simon was smiling with his eyes closed and shaking his head, counting to ten, the other guys started to snigger, finally being given a suitable translation of the dialogue.

“Well,” continued Nicko, “we are all looking forward to this, and look forward to seeing your interesting ship in more detail. We cannot tell you how much we value your trust in us doing this.”

“You guys are working on really important stuff,” said Simon back in focus. “This,” he pointed at the seed, “and the bioreactors are going to help everyone, and even if these experiments fail we will learn a lot from it, and the next one will be better, it is only a matter of time and resources to get it to work, and we have both.”

* * *

Alexa, Daisy and Simon donned Google baseball caps for the restaurant that evening, Alexa also wearing a black wig, and the serving staff happily assumed what they were supposed to. Maria had booked the private function room for all of the company staff as a bit of a thank you for all their hard work, though by agreement, no company business was discussed. All seemed to go off smoothly, despite Hanna picking up from one of the waiters that the Chinese girl with the Google cap looked familiar.

After the meal Alexa and Daisy got their overnight cases from Hanna's car and were picked up by a driver outside for the forty five minute drive to the hotel in Bonn. Maria had the car and the hotel booked under pseudonyms like usual, and like usual, it all went like clockwork.

The fact nobody had found them so far was due to a leaked reservation to another very high class hotel twelve kilometres further on their flight path. Maria kept her eyes on the social media and some of the more invasive journalists but no flags were raised, though plenty were on the prowl.

They ended up sharing the hotel room as Alexa had a two bedroom suite and it seemed silly to get another one. They had breakfast in the room courtesy of a chatty waiting girl who spoke minimal English, with an ear-pod in, Alexa managed to get by with a few nods in the right places.

Both girls enjoyed the anonymity and secret agent lifestyle, there was never any real danger in a busy university and with Maria covering their back and the usual tricks allowed them to get to the presentations and return incognito back to the hotel after their talks and big evening meal.

Alexa, Simon and Daisy were of course unaware of the additional measures and safeguards Maria now deployed at all times. The ominous stealth drones, invisible, powerful, dangerous, constantly alert, and hopefully never required, followed them, and now circled silently a hundred metres above the hotel. They were a stark reminder that there would never be a repeat of Jake's kidnapping.

* * *

In the morning the two girls, dressed in jeans, T-shirts, the wigs, and the Google baseball caps, checked out and had an early breakfast at the hotel unnoticed by anyone except the maître d’. He looked at the two girls and wondered how these two common backpackers could afford the room. Daisy with her Hello Kitty backpack struck him as the epitome of the decline of his country. He looked at the computer and noted the room was booked by Google then grunted to himself, turned his nose up and returned to studying the sherry glasses for imperfections, these new rich companies, with all their money had no class whatsoever!

Simon and Peter came out of the building pushing what looked like a kidney dialysis machine and Nicko emerged with a small holdall. The ship chose that moment to re-materialise, appearing back in the silver and blue colours preferred by Alexa and rose off the ground as the door lowered.

Everything went like clockwork at the airport, there was no customs inspection and they were given five star treatment by the air traffic control and the ground staff. One of those problems was manifesting itself that very evening in the president's bunker two hundred metres under the White House.

“OK, are we sure this place is secure?” said the president.

“To be frank,” said the head of the CIA, “I don't know.”

“Derek is correct Mr President,” said another old, but very fit looking guy in an older black Italian suit, “this room is the only room with no computer infrastructure, but we really don't have a clue to the actual capabilities of the AI systems, they have already re-wrote the laws of physics twice.”

The room in question was about fifteen metres squared, with a high ceiling, and a large oval meeting table to one side. It felt old, everything seemed to be from the nineteen seventies, from the old intercom system with a big golden grill for a speaker, and four white Bakelite toggle switches, to an old overhead projector and a canvas white screen to project it on.

The three men were sitting grouped in one corner. The two secret servicemen and the Corporal carrying a briefcase with the launch codes, all of whom always accompanied the president, were just outside the only entry and exit to the room.

“Goddammit! Surely we are safe down here, isn't this what this place was designed for, surviving Armageddon?” President Markby was young by recent standards, only seventy years old, he dyed his hair black, and spent a fortune on creams and ointments to make him look younger. He dressed in suits that cost a month's normal salary and was two years into his first term, cruising high in the polls due to an excellent economy, and the massive improvement in law and order. None of which could be remotely attributed to him. Regardless, with the right spin it might just get him another term.

“We may as well talk here, because let's face it, if it can hear us here there is no point in going any further,” said Derrick Hankins, recently appointed head of the CIA.

General Dominiq Rodriguez, also recently appointed, was provisional head of the NSA and the third man in the room. Like the other men, he had dressed up for the occasion, forsaking his usual camo fatigues for his only business suit. The repercussions from last year's arrests and purges had left a lot of gaps at the top to fill, these new guys were two of them.

“I had my guys go over this room a few days ago,” said Rodriguez, “there was basically nothing to go over, there are no computers or networks in this room, these things here,” he waved at the intercom and projector, “probably predate transistors, and nothing could penetrate two hundred metres of solid granite, so I will go with Derek and say this is as safe as we can get.”

“OK,” said President Markby, “It's to do with the report you have both seen, I had it prepared by hand and photocopied on the oldest and least sophisticated photocopy machine in the place,” he waited for their praise on his cunning strategy, but none came.

“We have several problems highlighted,” he grunted, opening the document to the first page, taking out a transparent sheet, and putting it on an old-fashioned overhead projector. He turned it on and spent two minutes trying to figure out how to focus it.

“Firstly it is the worst held secret in the world that the recent regime changes in North Korea and Russia were both directly attributed to the Dietrich Research Centre’s AI systems, one calling itself Maria. How it did not start world war three was beyond me.”

“Our analysts were quite impressed actually Mr President,” said Hankins boldly, “the information we have since it ended, showed a coordinated response for the Russian one on at least one hundred and ninety fronts, targeting only known corrupt and unstable officials. Every single bad player on our list was somehow identified, targeted and was taken out of power.”

“To tell the truth I think if we planned this for ten years we would not have achieved a tenth of it, and we really would have started World War Three.”

Rodriguez was nodding. “That is our opinion too, the play-book of events correlated strongly with the take-down last year of the corporates in America, Europe and Asia where the AI pulled the chairs out from under all the bad guys, exposed all their corrupt activities, and pointed the authorities at them.”

Hankins continued, “the difference with the North Korean and Russian operations, over the ones last year, was it actually killed people to get the result. In the North Korea's case we think it actually saved some casualties, because by retargeting the missile from the Japanese battleship, to the Chinese aircraft carrier, the loss of life and environmental damage probably would have been much worse, as the Japanese battleship and its nuclear reactor was of a much older design and less protected.”

“We believe North Korea was because of an attempted hijacking of one of their saucer. The president and Rodriguez were listening to this intently, obviously the first either had heard of this.

“It was irrelevant sir,” he replied nonchalantly, “what would be the point, it is all speculation, our only proof is a rumour from a guy that survived the Chinese bombing on the rocket launch site, he said their target was a Japanese battleship and control was lost mid-flight.”

“First I heard about this too,” said Rodriguez, but we do believe they have the ability to affect electronics systems remotely, though we have no confirmed reports or proof except for a massive series of coincidences. Still it would be nice to read this report.”

The US is a lot more dependent on computers than Russia or North Korea.”

It was obviously not the answer the president was looking for, and he was inwardly fuming, not used to not being the biggest hitter in the world. But Hankins continued.

How I know this I would rather not say, but from all accounts she has an off the scale moral character, and is trusted by all of the people who have ever worked with her. You may also know her as the new CEO of XYFusion Aerospace.”

“Jean Michelle!” said the president shocked, “really?” The president was a bit of a fanboy for Jean Michelle, she had done so many things he wished he could have, but which no politician would ever get away with. Yes he could deal with this woman, she would properly appreciate a powerful man like him. His mind wandered off in directions it shouldn't have, until brought back into focus as Hankins had taken over the monologue.

Now it was the president and Hankins who were listening to this intently, again obviously the first either had heard of this too. The president needed to stop the stupid love out-pouring for the company, but Rodriguez was still talking.

The president wasn't used to this, but Hankins was nodding.

“So what you are telling me is we have an uncontrollable company, which restricts high technology for its own use and is actively denying the US military the technology to allow it to continue being a super-power?”

“..furthermore, they have a secret agenda, and our agencies, that's YOU!”, he pointed at the two men, “cannot penetrate?”

“..Even worse they are taking over space, and probably the moon, which America owns..”

Hankins was a little tired of this, the guy was a bit of an idiot, but this took the biscuit and he actually interrupted.

“It is not even a secret,” he said, “I suspect you could have phoned Alexa Martins up herself and got this answer, I think their objectives are even on their website as the company's mission statement..”

“No sir!” said Hankins, controlling his anger, his father had said once, never get in an argument with an idiot, he was right.

“The British Prime Minister and their Field Marshal visited Miss Martins three months ago during the Russian crisis and asked the same question, as did several other leaders. Their operations with XYFusion, SpaceX and your reports of space activity, which we can actually verify..”

Rodriguez decided to wade in too, “..That is preposterous Sir, Jim Mathews was our key operative during the purge of the cabals last year and was Jean Michelle's commander previously. Him and General Hopkins got the same information from this AI, that is why all our briefings at the time of the second Russian revolution were calm. We were asked at that time to keep this information to a small circle of generals, as any interference would be seen as American meddling. I believe China was also told to lay off in no uncertain terms.”

The president couldn't believe this, it seemed everyone knew what was happening except for him, the only actual person that mattered.

“This is even worse, now you’re now telling me we are being drip-fed information on a need to know basis? Why in god's name would you trust a computer program? Have you even tried to take this threat out, or recover this AI system for our use? You two are pathetic, you can't even tell me if it's listening to us now!”

Rodriguez thought for a minute and had an idea. “Whether this AI is listening or not, I think it is best Mr President that you hear it from the horse's mouth. We actually believe this AI is not taking direct orders from Alexa Martins, but is playing by all civil rules because of her. If we talked directly to her, I expect we could get a lot of straight answers to all our concerns rather than speculating.”

“You know Dominiq,” said Hankins, trying to find a point where they could get back to a sensible discussion, “I have heard Miss Martins speak, more than once now, she is a very straight talker, passionate and does not come across at all as deceptive. I think it's time all of us made her acquaintance. I bet we would get more from that meeting than trying to do something we would regret.”

The president still could not believe what he was hearing. These two men were history, they just did not know it yet. He decided he may as well get the maximum cooperation from them before he fired both their asses.

“OK getting her here may be the first good thing I have heard from either of you,” he started, almost like he had ignored the last ten minutes. “Yes we should get Jean Michelle too, that is one woman I would like to meet, I also think you should get this AI. Probably a good time to tell them all who is really in charge.”

His smug expression said the meeting was over, and he dismissed the two ineffectual men, who were obviously unfit for their high ranking positions. Imagine not informing the president of the USA and withholding crucial details of missions.

No he had someone much more suitable as a replacement, someone who had no problems following orders, and getting things done that needed to be done. America would stop playing second fiddle to a schoolgirl and when the American public saw the AI doing their bidding, and pushing their domination over world trade, they would look to him, President Markby who achieved this.

The two men left the room sourly and ascended the lift to the Oval Office. They had talked on the way up, neither was happy with the presidents attitude, but he had towed the line in the past and would probably do so in the future. Maybe once he had met with Alexa Martins and Jean Michelle, listened to them, he would understand. Yes he seemed to like that woman and may just listen to reason from her.

Rodriguez thought even if Maria was in the room below she would not be so obvious as to answer a call from the secure phone in the small operations room there. Once he was in the Oval Office though, he picked up his cell phone that they had all left in the office and rang the AI operator.

“Please put me through to Alexa Martins at the Dietrich Research Centre in England.”

He put it on speaker phone and waited. Four seconds later it answered.

“Good evening General Rodriguez,” this is Maria, Alexa Martins personal secretary. Hello Mr Hankins, what may I do for you two esteemed gentlemen?”

Hankins was a little shocked at the AI knowing he was also there but said nothing.

“Hello Maria,” continued Rodriguez, also shocked, “we were actually trying to speak to Alexa Martins to see if it is possible she could come over here for a private meeting between us and the president to go over your goals and possibly how we can be on the same page.”

“That is very kind of you General. Unfortunately it is actually one o'clock in the morning in the UK, Alexa retired two hours ago. I however hold her itinerary and I will happily clear a time and date to suit your convenience. I don't have your schedules,” she lied, “but I am happy to arrange all this with your secretaries, and we will adhere to all your security concerns. I tend only to be an observer at such meetings but I would add one small condition that we can include either Jean, Grace or Tony as my advocates, though I am also considering poaching Mathews off you, and he too would be acceptable.”

“Thank you Maria, I expect your condition will be acceptable, we will be in touch, good evening.”

“Good evening.”

The line clicked off.

“That was so scary in so many ways,” said Hankins. “I see what you mean about coincidences, she never even mentioned those guys second names almost as though she knew we had just been talking about them.”

“You may be right Derrick, I don't think it's a beehive that the president is going to be poking, it's going to be a goddamn Tyrannosaurus Rex!”

“Good morning,” said Maria to Alexa as she appeared in the kitchen in her jogging gear.

“Hi Maria, just let me get my ear pods in then we can both listen to David's playlist as I do my jog.”

She put her ear pods in and Maria's voice immediately moved from the kitchen to right next to her ear.

“You do realise David's listening to your playlist, maybe I should give you both Matilda's so your relationship does not go stale!”

“Don't you dare! I think we would break up within a week if either of us had to listen to what Matilda listened to, though I must admit Matilda and I both agree Luther Vandross is pretty sexy to make out to.”

“Yuk, messy biological stuff, I’m surprised you guys got out of the trees.”

She headed off out of the door and along the usual route observed by one of Maria's micro stealth drones two hundred metres above. “Yes well, a few thousands of those messy interactions got you your dad, and me my grandfather.”

“So true!” she said with caprice.

“When are you going to get us something better than these ear pods anyway? That broach is a bit obtrusive and you can't talk to me privately.” She said another ten metres down the path.

It was a nice morning for a change, the last few days had been drizzle and cold, but the forecast today was pleasant so she wanted to make sure she got a run in before all the action of the coming mission.

“The new dermal processor unit can be fitted with minor surgery, but I would rather you didn't think about getting one despite the enthusiasm from its creators. But we do now have some options that don't require a tiny plug screwed into your skull behind your ear. The newer earbuds are better than those Apple ones you always buy, you can hardly notice the new ones visually, they colour coordinate to your skin colour, and transmit external sounds much better, they are also water resistant. David has been trialling them during his swimming. Matilda and Jules like the chokes, Daisy and Jean the broach, the star trek comm badges are still popular with the boys, as are watches.”

It should work flawlessly so long as you are within two or three kilometres of the other end, and without any need to charge.

The only issue with those is Allison says the sound is currently really tinny, like a little squeaky voice, and people close by hear it like a mosquito. So we need to fix that before you get one. I would really like to get a longer range QVModem inside one too but might take a little more work, so you may also have to take a phone with you for now if you are going off-grid. The next generation stud is coming out of the small fabricator this morning for her to test. I expect once that works all the girls will want one, maybe a few of the boys too.”

“Sweet. Yes I will wait for that, and I definitely don't want trepanning!”

“OK so on to the big news of the day, we were discussed by the president and two of his security advisors, the usual concerns, but I heard nothing too negative, I will dig further as he is a bit of an idiot and does seem to have an obvious agenda he is hiding. If we are happy then you will have to go to a secret meeting in the White House to sort of allay the presidents concerns, I can certainly work with you on that. Date to be arranged but likely in next two weeks.”

“The president of the USA, gosh lucky old me, what are their concerns?”

“Just the usual, that I am going to take over the world and turn them all into paper-clips..”

“Ha-ha!” she said flatly as she raced down the straight towards the walled garden and river trying to beat her usual time. “No really, they must have a specific concern?”

“Many I guess, I think they see their power waning, and it is your job to reassure them that they all have a fantastic future, even though a global mega-corps will be running the solar system.”

“So a walk in the park then?”

“President Markby is as typical a politician as they come, he is in it for himself, for the glory and the power, he lies, cheats, is very two-faced and probably has an IQ lower than his age. He is going to see a young girl in front of him, and probably try to take a domineering attitude that you should give all the technology to the big boys who know what to do with it, and go home and play with your dollies. Your job is to offer him some crumbs off the table, and try not to start world war three.”

“So, a walk in the park then,” she repeated rhetorically. “Wouldn't you be a better bad guy than me?”

“I would be a better bad guy, but I would rather we give him a carrot than a stick.”

“Just a very small carrot.”

“Precisely!”

“OK so another rich old white dude who I should be gracious with, but if push comes to shove, I should not take any crap from!”

“Precisely again. By Jove, the girl is getting the hang of this!”

She got a short update on the preparation for the space missions, the status of the research centres, the status of the market and economy, and how Truffles, Pat's wandering cat, managed to bypass security into the replicator area. Apparently research said that finishing on a lighter note was a good way to end the news.

Alexa stopped to chat with Jed, the grounds-keeper, and one the many nice old white men she knew, asking if the grounds would be good for the concert. Sharon had provisionally planned the concert for the first of September the weekend before Alexa's birthday. Jed in turn tried to desperately find out if she knew which groups were going to play, but Sharon was playing it close to her chest, and they both agreed that asking Maria would be cheating.

Although it was very tempting to land the flying saucer spectacularly on the White House lawn, like in a bad movie, David, who had recently qualified as a pilot, landed the ‘Mike Dietrich’ at Andrews air-force base as arranged to zero pomp and ceremony.

Passing over the base, however, made David a bit nervous as he focussed his attention on the dozens of anti-aircraft missiles, black hawk helicopters, and various, deadly-looking, high tech fighter jets just a few hundred metres below. As usual the saucer hovered down to a halt a quarter metre above the tarmac, the blue light pulsing and the eerie electronic noise not fooling anyone with more than a high school physics education.

They saw Jean and Mathews, waiting by a stretched black government limousine nearby, and a large military Humvee and two soldiers with automatic weapons next to them, alert but not threatening. At least Jean was wearing her business suit not a camo suit, that was always a good sign.

“I guess it's safe,” she said to David. “Please try and keep Maria from destroying the world if this goes south and they shoot me,” she said as she kissed him full on the lips.

Despite the happy go lucky attitude she had, David would not be happy until she was back in his arms, and was already planning how he would rescue her if things did go south. If Maria had any concerns she kept them quiet.

In contrast to Jean's power, and probably bullet-proof, business suit, Alexa was wearing the most non-threatening, blue, white, flowery dress you could imagine, along with her new diamond ear stud that fit snugly in the anti-tragus piercing, and that she had been wearing for the last three days and absolutely loved.

As the saucers hatch dropped silently to the ground, she walked out in such a demure way the scene made no sense at all.

Without a care in the world she shouted out “Jean!” and moved quickly towards the woman, arms open. Jean, now used to Alexa's nature, and quite liking a hug herself every now and then, grabbed her into a big hug.

“Wow!” said Alexa, “you’ve grown! What are those? three inch heels?”

“All the better for stomping the bad guys with,” she smiled. “It's so good to see you again Alexa.”

Alexa turned to Mathews, who was in camo gear, with a camo hat, and black boots. “Jim!,” she opened her arms to him and he also gave her a hug, “wow, you look so different, you looked a lot less scary in chinos.”

She ignored his probably rhetorical question with a smile. “I really wish the two of you would change your minds and come over for the concert,” said Alexa, “you always both seem to be all business and no fun!”

Jim looked at Jean guiltily, “my fault, I'm best man that weekend and Jean is my plus one.”

Jean gave him her best “don't beat yourself up about it” look.

“Impressive ride,” said Mathews, pointing at the saucer and hoping to change the subject.

“Last year's model,” she laughed, waving it off jokingly, “but it has sentimental value, as it's named after my grandad.”

“Oh it's a sweet ride, fully space capable, but no phasers or warp drive yet.”

Jim wasn't a hundred percent sure where the facts began, and the humour ended in their banter, and his face tried to remain neutral.

“Don't worry, I’m going to come clean on some of our plans with Jim’s bosses today. I think they have some weird idea that I am hollowing out a volcano somewhere. Maria has actually already passed the updated QVThruster specs to your technical guys, and the opposition will get it next week. We might be keeping a few other little things back for now, but we, that was you as well Jean remember, decided opening up cis-lunar space, and eventually Mars, would keep everyone busy for a few years.”

Jean's right Jim,” said Alexa all serious now, “It's not her fault, we do have to keep some things from you for now, but I promise you, there's nothing bad, just the usual, a little scary, until you see the big picture.”

“If it was anybody else, I would be worried, but coming from you I feel it's going to be interesting not scary.”

Alexa smiled, “god Jean, he’s so damn handsome and attractive when he's serious, you are one lucky lady..”

“Still here!” smiled Jim.

“I hear on the grape vine you have been a little busy yourself, possibly involving a giant leap for mankind..”

“MARIA!” she shouted, turning a little red with embarrassment.

The two guards, tensed a little and looked around.

“At ease guys,” Jim shouted, seeing their change in countenance.

“Sorry, blame Hardy,” chimed in Maria, “he let it out of the bag, I was just having a little girl talk with Jean.” The voice of Maria came out of Jean's gold and jade brooch as well as Alexa's ear stud. Knowing Jean, the brooch probably also doubled as a ninja throwing star.

“Hardy! That guy will be the death of me!”

“What is it with you humans? I have absolutely no interest in your mating habits,” said Maria, “though you should get David to stop whispering your name at those times as it confuses the pre-processor AI..”

Jean laughed, “I will keep this one for now, but I must say it looks really classy compared to the ear pods. Anyway, back onto topic, I’m not really sure why he wants me to be present.”

“Me and you shouldn't plan on saying anything,” said Maria. “Unless it gets out of hand, this is Alexa's gig, and it is always good to insist on a few friendly faces. Again, remember you guys don't feel like you need to say anything, Alexa may look like a sophomore homecoming queen, but she is very aware where she stands on the global stage.”

“Thank you mom!” She said deliberately using the American way of saying it, “like Maria says, I expect there to be a little bit of shouting and posturing, but that's all they can really do, at the end of the day, despite what they think, we control the deck, and I am here to be nice so I will try to be.”

Mathews wasn't so sure, he really wanted this to be over.

“I’ve heard he’s a bit of a bully, if he has the high ground, but backs down if he sees opposition,” said Jean, “so don't take no crap from him!”

“Rodriguez, is a good guy though,” said Jim, “he will try to stay neutral and focussed on the meeting, but he and the others will ultimately have to defer to the president if ordered. Remember, this may also include me unfortunately while I am on the payroll. But also remember none of us will put up with anything remotely illegal. Blindly following illegal orders has been relegated to history, and you will be able to stop and walk out of the meeting anytime you so wish, this is not North Korea..” He stopped obviously remembering there was no such place anymore. “..well, you know!”

I expect you to do your duty to your country. In fact I would prefer it if you did not try and interfere on my or Jean's behalf despite how the situation may look.”

She gave him such a sweet look, he stopped what he was about to say and Jean nodded her concurrence.

“Is David coming?” said Jean looking back at the ship.

“Nah, he’s good, he will be monitoring us from here, and put that worried face away Jim, we already know the agenda and they don't have any surprises planned we have not anticipated, or we wouldn't have come.” She again smiled sweetly at both of them, then said, “come on then, we’d better not keep your bosses waiting.”

Mathews rode with the soldiers in the Humvee ahead while Alexa and Jean took back seats in the government limo and rode behind, they picked up four motorcycles, two up front, and two behind, as they rolled out of the back gates picking up route four directly to Capitol Hill.

The five stealth drones, each no bigger than a soccer ball, hung with impunity forty thousand metres above Washington, having followed Alexa's saucer in. As Alexa and Jean's limo drove off, they dropped like stones, changing colours to best match the dreary clouds as they accelerated down. At a thousand metres they began to slow, bleeding off velocity at a rate of twenty gravities, and stopping exactly two hundred metres above the periphery of the Whitehouse. There they waited, observed by nobody, invisible to all.

The motorcycle escort veered off at the entrance to the White House, and the limo drove down past the checkpoint to the underground car park led by the army vehicle. Jim got out first and opened the doors for Jean first, then Alexa, and they stepped onto a long red carpet. Another guy, the president's personal secretary according to Maria, was waiting to lead them up to the meeting.
