As Jean stepped into the detector, there were several loud beeps and a red flashing light and she stopped.

“Whoops!” Jean said to the guard as she pulled out the largest gun Alexa had ever seen. The guard did not smile and tagged the gun, letting her know she could collect it on the way back. Mathews, handed his gun and phone carefully to the guard, before going through the machine, they examined both, then gave his phone back.

At the entrance to the East room they were appraised by two secret service agents, who must have had orders to let them pass. Despite everything looking normal so far, Mathews had a bad feeling that this was not being done by the book. He wished he could be anywhere else, but he had been ordered to attend, and that was another reason that rubbed him up the wrong way.

President Markby had forcefully argued the point several times, that the US should be the ones to lead any technologies to space, but all his advisors were totally against doing anything rash. There were definitely going to be some big changes once this was all over.

He now stood by the end of the large table, looking at the three men stood around the other end, none would sit until he did, all waited on his word. There was Hankins the head of the CIA, Rodriguez the Director of the NSA, and Luke Peron his vice president and running mate. To tell the truth Peron was appointed by the party, and Markby knew him just enough to detest him; The other two were just in the right place at the right time when the purge happened last year.

Markby's new status after this should allow him to fix all those little mistakes. All these men were weak in his opinion, and all were about to get a lesson in what strong leadership really looked like.

The door to the room opened and his private secretary Jacob walked in followed by two stunning women, both of whom were annoyingly more famous than he was. Behind them came an African-American man in a camo uniform, his hat in his hand, this must be the Mathews guy. His eyes feasted on the first woman in the blue summer dress, who walked up to him and looked him directly in the eye.

“Mr President, I am Alexa Martins, thank you for inviting me to your lovely country and house.”

Markby saw none of the usual deference that came from people first meeting him, she made up for it in her politeness, but it annoyed him nevertheless. Alexa was a little annoyed how tight he squeezed her hand, she had been warned, but it was uncomfortable anyway. Markby smiled seeing the change in her smug expression.

Alexa stood aside pulling her hand back, not smiling now, and the other beautiful woman stepped up. Now here was a real woman, not a schoolgirl. The two women could not have been so different, Alexa Martins demure yet confident, and Jean Michelle's, powerful, dangerous looking, but probably unsure of her standing in this company. So she should be, she of all people should appreciate who she was in front of.

“Mr President.” She said, also without any hint of deference, and strangely not elaborating any further. But it wasn't necessary, being the president of the USA was all it took to get this woman here, that was his power.

He shook Jean's hands too, but she was totally used to childish power tricks from idiots who thought it meant something, and she put twice as much pressure back without changing her expression once.

Jeez, that hurt, that woman had some grip on her he thought sourly, not used to being the one at the receiving end.

The other three men in the room were more civilised, shaking the ladies hands with a light pressure and giving genuine not fake smiles. Markby introduced them as his vice president, head of the CIA, and head of the NSA like he was showing them his prize turkeys.

Alexa knew, from Maria's briefing, of the two non-political appointees already, they both had skeletons in their cupboards, like most people in power did, but were generally respected, and of a good moral character. The vice president had been chosen as he had the least obvious vices, and was not seen as a threat to Markby's authority by the party; It was hard for her to see how a guy like him rose to such a powerful position, but there again she only had to look at herself in a mirror.

Mathews was warmly received by Rodriguez and Hankins, Ignored by Markby, and had an indifferent introduction to Peron, who usually just followed what his boss did in these situations.

Introductions done, they sat down, Markby at the head of the table as expected. He was surprised when the Martin's woman took the seat next to him, and Jean the seat the other side of him and between him and the vice president. Mathews sat next to Alexa, and Rodriguez and Hankins sat at the ends. Markby's secretary sat to his back well away from the table with a notepad and pen at the ready.

Markby had his great speech prepared but Martins started before he could stand up.

“Before we start, we should also acknowledge that Maria our company AI is also joining the meeting. I don't know why Jean is here, but we welcome her as a senior representative of our company..”

“And so we get directly to the crux of the matter, who is wearing the pants..” Interrupted Markby snidely.

[and so it begins] sighed Maria internally, as all cell and Wi-Fi coverage inside the Whitehouse cut out.

Her five stealth drones above the Whitehouse went fully active, as did two hundred others around the world.

The inside of the Whitehouse, already flooded with QVModem dipoles, was now flooded with the newer optical-range singularities. Maria now watched and listened in real-time as the act unfolded, waiting for Jeans trigger.

A second door opened into the east room, further away from the one they entered through and a new person walked in, dressed in similar fatigues as Mathews, but also with a sidearm attached. He was a large set man with a fierce expression, and both Jean and Mathews knew him well.

Mathews anger and protectiveness towards Jean made him look at her, and he made a motion for her not to do anything, but her expression was strangely relaxed and she shook her head as if trying to signal something to him.

Mathews stood up, “what the hell is this criminal doing here?”

Markby continued smugly, “Sit down Mathews, THAT IS AN ORDER!”

Mathews slowly sat down, never taking once his fierce expression from the man. The other men in the room looked agitated too, but Jean and Alexa's expressions still remained relaxed. Jean even winked at him.

“Now,” continued Markby in the confidence of somebody totally in charge of a situation, “let me introduce the recently pardoned General Lentz, a good man, wrongfully persecuted by his own people. By you Mathews, and by you Rodriguez, I am sure you will find some forgiveness in your hearts when you are reporting to him.”

Markby was in real political speech mode, and now turned his stare on Alexa and Jean.

“..I am not sure why the AI chose you two as its pets..” He started, wondering why neither woman seemed fearful, “..but I don't deal with lackeys.”

He looked directly at Alexa. “You must think I’m stupid if you think I am going to let any corporation control access to vital technologies and space access..”

“Sir..” Began Rodriguez worried.

“You will not speak while I am speaking!” Markby shouted, and clicked his fingers at the new man Lentz..

Lentz's sneered at Mathews, his eyes not moving even as two more armed soldiers walked out of the room and stood behind him, weapons levelled but not pointing at anyone. General Lentz grinned, not even bothering to look around, but knowing what the people in front of him were probably thinking. He was going to thoroughly enjoy this spectacle.

The president continued directing his gaze at a frustratingly indifferent Martins, and getting madder as neither woman reacted.

“You think you are so smart controlling access to a few computers and phones. We don't need technology to plan an operation without your AI knowing, and we don't need anything more than a few dozen men with M15 rifles to take you down. As I speak General Lentz's men are going through your little stately home in England, brick by brick, and wire by wire. By this time tomorrow, what's left of your AI will be under the microscope of our NSA scientists..”

Alexa stood up smiling at Jean. “Well that was interesting!” She said to Jean who also stood up, both totally ignoring Markby, “it seems you and Tony called it perfectly.”

Markby turned from Alexa to Jean, fuming and waving his hands, “SIT DOWN NOW, I HAVE NOT FINISH..” Jean punched him really hard in the mouth, knocking him back into his chair. Alexa shuddered a little as she heard the nose bone shatter, but otherwise remained indifferent.

“It is so satisfying when you are correct,” said Jean rubbing her knuckles.

The three other men at the table looked at Jean shocked, unable to comprehend what just happened, but turned to Lentz as he stepped towards them.

“Oh,” said Lentz calmly, motioning to the two soldiers behind him and starting slowly for his own pistol, “I believe that, Captain Michelle, counts as treason..”

He and the two soldiers eyes rolled into the back of their heads, and all three of them dropped to the floor, like puppets whose strings had been cut.

“What..” said Peron, totally out of his depth and slowly rising. He barely got the first word out, when the main doors burst open and two other soldiers rushed in and took up positions next to the fallen men. Six other men walked in more calmly, one was General Hopkins.

Hopkins looked at the dazed, and blubbering president with his nose gushing blood, “I really hope somebody got that on video,” he smiled.

[Uploading as you speak]

Rodriguez got up and said Incredulously, “can somebody tell me what the hell just happened?” He looked at Hopkins who seemed about to speak. But he deferred to the man next to him, who seemed to be somebody important.

“It seems the president of the USA just admitted in front of witnesses, and the world, to at least three very illegal, and impeachable actions.” He said soberly.

“Firstly authorising an armed military operation in the country of a friendly ally in order to forcibly steal the assets of its largest company. Secondly he has pardoned a man indicted for six counts of murder. Furthermore he authorised an armed assault on an unarmed aircraft belonging to the same corporation. I'm sure there are a few other things..”

Hopkins turned to the two soldiers, “Are they alive?”

One of the two solders dropped to the ground and checked each of the men. “Yes Sir!”

Without further prompting, he disarmed the three men and tie wrapped all their hands behind their backs. Unceremoniously, all three were then dragged out by three other soldiers who had appeared.

One of the suited men identified himself as the speaker of the house, he was visibly shocked with the vista in front of his eyes. He looked at the president who was still dazed and confused, unable to speak and using the sleeve of his expensive Italian suit to help halt the blood flow covering his face. The president spluttered out a few words which sounded a bit like, “broken my nose” and “treason”, but they were basically indecipherable and a few seconds later he thankfully fainted.

“Would someone please remove this man from here and get him to a nurse or something. Then have him guarded while congress decides what to do with him.”

He turned to Alexa, “Miss Martins, may I apologise profusely and sincerely from the people of America for this outrage done to you.”

“Thank you sir, I accept your apology, and I only hold this man and not his country responsible, no harm was really done to me or my colleague Miss Michelle here.. Though I am so happy she was able to defend me, and herself of course. I felt certain that mad-man was going to attack us both!” She feigned shock.

[Oh nicely done Alexa]

“Yes..” He said uncertainly as the medics rushed in and started to move him, “..It was a good thing she was able to, er, defend both of you. I am sure we can add attempted assault to his charges.”

“Since we have the vice president, and all you distinguished people here, I would still be happy to answer your questions and concerns, though I think Miss Michelle's may require a coffee to calm her poor nerves, and if you are making one I will have an English breakfast tea with milk, that's hot tea.” She smiled.

[Don't push it Alexa] Maria thought as she moved the four stealth drones back to passive. Glad they were not needed.

Amazingly after the situation was back under control eight new people sat down at another table in the Oval Office, those included the directors of NASA, education, and three other advisors keen to hear what she had to say. That meeting was cordial, Alexa saying they had now made the necessary improvements to the QVThrusters to allow full access to cis-lunar space, and they promised they were going to improve them further over the next two years to hopefully open up the whole solar system.

After the meeting, Alexa and Jean posed for some seriously needed good press.

The world, and especially the American people were outraged by what had happened. The vice president, recently sworn in, apologised again, saying it was only sanctioned by one man and using criminal elements of the military; the government speech writers working overtime, on the damage mitigation.

The military was of course as outraged by the incident as everyone else, especially releasing a man who was complicit in the murder of so many of their own. The new president emphasised it was always right for soldiers to refuse illegal actions, and those that did so would never be punished in a free society.

A crowd of two hundred freedom supporters, protested outside the White House for a week afterwards, to the shame of everyone including the old president who disavowed them and tried to spin the actions on his advisors. Of course Maria would not let any such spin happen. She was very, very good at this now.

The twenty American soldiers, part of a black ops unit operating illegally in the middle east had thought their planning perfect. They had done everything by word of mouth, courier mail, or in some cases coded on short wave radio. Each had got to England separately, at different times, and from different countries of origin and were supplied weapons by a local deep cover assets.

Yet, ten metres into a coordinated attack on the house each of them was found unconscious, as were four others in support vehicles. The British soldiers who had been dispatched to deal with them asked what happened, but the persons who had defended the Research Centre were never found.

The disgraced soldiers had been moved quietly back to the US under guard for trial. They were mostly wanted for other crimes too, and by agreement, they were kept well away from the media who were fighting each other like crazy to get any further information on the whole incident.

Jean apologised to everyone for the leaked video of the event, she had apparently just started a video blog and had accidentally left her brooch camera streaming. She of course stopped it as soon as she remembered, she then decided that making a video blog was probably a bad idea after all. If anyone wondered how it got out while all the radio frequencies were still jammed they never asked.

“I wasn't sure whether to laugh or be terrified,” said David, as they flew home. “Just after you went into the meeting room, six large military trucks screeched in and surrounded the saucer, then this helicopter rushed out of left field to hover above us. Several other helicopters then started hovering close by with big guns pointing at us. Next thing I'm watching thirty armed soldiers out by the entrance, one with a megaphone demanding we surrender, throw out our weapons and come out with our hands up.”

“It wasn't that dramatic,” said Maria, “you had them on your threat screen for at least two minutes before they arrived.”

“Well I was listening to that psycho trying to berate my beloved at the time, and remember I’m a man so I cannot multi-task!” he smiled for Alexa's benefit.

“Anyway, we ignored them, then they opened fire with automatic weapons on the door for a few minutes until one ricocheted and hit one of them with friendly fire then they called a halt. Then they stood back, talked and another soldier came forward with a big-ass rocket launcher or something on his shoulder, and they repeated the same warning to surrender.”

“The ship told me not to worry, then next thing I know there is this terrific bang outside, apparently the shell ricocheted off the door and hit one of the cars, injuring another two soldiers. Six of the men got them to ambulances, then this guy came up wheeling a plasma cutter and started work on the door. They stopped when they realised after ablating a layer of graphyne, nothing was happening, and not noticing there was a hundred kilowatt laser dissipating most of the heat through a big hole in the tarmac.”

“Then the helicopter moved off and hundreds of other soldiers came, surrounded the soldiers trying to get in.”

“After some discussion they all left and the place was once again empty, but with a burned out truck and a massive melted hole in the tarmac. The firefighters and a large tow truck came around a few minutes later quickly put the fire out and towed the burning truck off. A few hours later more soldiers turned up, this time facing outwards and your limo turned up with you and the General in it, then you both had a coffee here and now we are on our way.”

“Oh David, that was so exciting!” she swooned into his arms. “My Hero!”

He tutted, but decided now would be as good a time as any to comfort the poor distressed woman.

Jean's reception after Alexa left was not too dissimilar. Rather than face the press they put her up at one of the guest rooms at the White House. The temporary president, the generals, the chiefs of staff and two of the judges had another big meeting directly after the small photo opportunity of Alexa's departure where they went through the incident under oath.

It was obvious to Mathews that Jean was ten steps ahead of everyone both at the incident and the briefing after it, everyone getting their statements correct despite the now three hundred million views of the video, which may have been real-time altered to show Alexa little more fearful than she was, the president's hands balled into a fist, and Jean's knock out of the president a bit more self defence looking, and a little less forceful than it was.

If there was any way of naming her president at that moment every person involved, including the temporary president probably would have done so.

Mathews stayed with her until they got to the door of the apartment.

“Your secretary has dropped off your overnight bag Miss Michelle's,” said one of the White House secretaries with a gleam of admiration in his eyes before leaving them both in the room.

The second the door shut, Mathews pounced on her, kissing her passionately.

“You knew didn't you?” he said as they both pulled up for air.

“Of course we did silly,” she smiled, “didn't Alexa say it about three times not to worry, the only time I was worried was when Lentz actually came in armed and you got up to confront him, I almost had to go to plan B which would have been very messy,” she tapped her thin black bracelet to emphasise something.

“Alexa thought he would back down before the no going back point, but Tony and I read his countenance in the day leading up to it, and she deferred to our better judgement. The rest of the plan we were so far ahead of them I could have had a T-shirt printed with it on. Though knowing Lentz was out and free made me sick to my soul. I guess the only part not planned was me hitting him, but it just seemed the right thing to do at the time.”

Her fingers teased his face then moved down his chest, “I can't wait to let you in on a few more little secrets, but well,” she sighed, “you were potentially an enemy combatant.”

Her fingers stopped at his chest, her eyes burning into his. “But you were so brave..”

He grabbed her in for another kiss which she did not resist at all, carefully putting the brooch face down as she fell into his passionate embrace.

* * *

“It's kind of weird knowing you are not the top dog anymore,” Rodriguez said, as he sat in the comfortable seat in front of Hankins in his well appointed office. “How do you fight an enemy who knows your every move and can seemingly just knock somebody out at will?”

“You can't!” said Hankins. “The boffins still do not know how they did it, the soldiers all recovered, but all of them reported massive headaches for days after. One said it was like his whole world turned grey, and for a few hours he could not even remember his name. Hell you were there, Lentz stopped mid word. The AI must have been watching that whole area real-time, despite all radio coverage being down.”

“We put three of the soldiers under an MRI, there was nothing the doctors could find, our only theory was from one of our scientists, who said studies had shown a high magnetic field can disrupt the thinking process, and in other mammals a dozen focussed microwave beams converging at a point in the brain killed them in a minute.”

Rodriguez swirled his sherry around his glass, he would only have one, but after the lack of coordination between the departments in the past, the two men decided that the occasional get together in a less formal setting could only improve things.

“I had our analysts look back on some of the weirder reports we had this year, from ones similar where a bad guy has been found dead, or unconscious for no reason, even to reports of apparitions, ghosts, monsters, you name it. The common factor is that every single report was against illegal logging, fishing, mining and drug operations. Equipment, including weapons, are simply failing, much of this equipment is really old-tech, stuff we would expect to be exempt from the AI influence, but again it is the only logical conclusion our guys can come to. It is getting really bad out there for a lot of the cartels, criminal organisations and bad actors.”

“Yeah, we have dismissed a few of these weird reports ourselves, but now we are not so sure, of course there are no pictures even though people claim to have taken them. I really hope nobody else ever gets technology like this, even knowing it exists scares me more than any nuclear weapon. I would hate to think what would happen if somebody like us, Iran or China got it. there is no need for terminators robots, or war drones. My advice, to anyone who asks in the future, is to stick to cooperation with these guys, because for the AI to be doing this so openly it must have calculated the risk to be almost zero. I think our job is going to get a lot easier from this point forward.”

Hankins seemed happy to pour a second glass, then gestured his other hand around the office.

“You know she is watching us and listening to us now don't you? Yet if I get the best of the best of my guys in here, with every piece of tech at their disposal, we wont find anything. We literally are cavemen banging rocks.”

“I totally agree,” said Rodriguez, “and in a way I'm kind of glad we lost this war. I suspect nobodies going to be invading countries that they don't belong in, or pushing any launch buttons in the future. I still talk to Maria, in fact I think a lot of people do, I feel like a blasphemer, but she has almost replaced God in my life! Yet you say that to her and she laughs, saying she does not want to be anyone's god, and she certainly wont talk to anyone who sees her that way.”

Hankins was intrigued. “I've never been a believer, I don't think there are any true believers, because if your god is all present, why would you do the bad things you do. I think this is the reason I don't have faith, because I don’t ever want a god like that! But I am also glad Maria does not think she is a god, I do think of her as a person though..”

“Anyway, enough of this, we both have bad guys to find, and idiots in power to calm down. Let's make it a bit earlier next week, maybe we can do lunch too.”

“So, as you can all probably guess,” said Maria to a packed lecture theatre, “our first proper manned mission is going to be a science one. The goal of this is to test, and refine the design, for an organic structure which will be grown from a seed. We are going to do this test on a C type asteroid, that's an asteroid mostly made of carbon for those of you not in the know.” Everybody turned to Alexa.

“What!” she said, “I can't be the only person here who did not know that!”

Maria waited for the nods, and sniggering to die down and continued. “The guys have had a lot of success in the lab, and now it is time to go to the next stage and to see if it is possible to grow a space habitat. As we all know, this is being done in parallel with our other habitat design, and we don't see any conflict, in fact having two ways to achieve the same goals is always good.”

“Also, it is likely any artificial structure we build will incorporate organic components, such as the new bio-reactors, so we are hoping the technologies will have a great deal of synergy.”

“Anyway, the Structural Organics guys have been working amazingly hard toward this goal, the seed they designed has been undergoing lots of tests and improvements here for the past few weeks, and we believe the modifications now have everything it needs to begin a live trial. This new package will include an energy source to provide enough heat for the seed to start growing, all the essential elements required for this early stage, a small processing unit which will help search for and pre-process elements it requires, and the control unit which will provide the electrical, hormonal, chemical and timing signals to direct the growth.”

“In four days time, the ‘Don Quixote’, our latest Icarus three class saucer, will take off from here and begin the journey to the asteroid belt with the new probe. The target for the mission is an unnamed asteroid, similar to the 162173 Ryugu asteroid which the Japanese Hayabusa probe landed on and returned a sample from back in 2020. In case you have all been wondering where many of the saucers have been these last three weeks, all except the Mike were sent to various locations in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, firstly as a test of their systems but secondary they had a mission which was to catalogue all the asteroids we could find, do spectral, sample and mass analysis and determine the best target for this and future missions.”

“The data is being correlated and fed back to Barbara's small team in Bakersfield, she has set up an offshoot lab to work on the classifications. The asteroid chosen is one kilometre in diameter and seems to have a good balance of all the elements and hydrocarbons required for the seed to germinate. As well as that, it is in a quite low density area of the asteroid belt and on a safe predictable course. A special probe has been made to help position the seed inside the cavity, backfill the hole, monitor its progress and do any manual actions if required.”

“Hanna, Peter, Nicko, do any of you want to speak?”

“Yes,” said Peter, “we need the seed to be at least twenty metres underground to ensure it is not affected by cosmic or solar radiation, ideally the seed would be down in the centre of mass before it starts to gestate, but for the test, and with such a low mass asteroid with barely perceptible gravity, we see no issues. The asteroid will basically be a loose pile of rocks, and will try to get down as deep as we can.”

“The growth is quite slow,” said Nicko, waving at a small simplified diagram on the presentation screen, “the chamber will first be heated to twenty two degrees centigrade, how quickly it gets to that temperature, and how much power is needed to keep it there, will depend on the size and insulation properties of the cavity. Once at the desired temperature, the machine will activate the seed pod inside, which will begin absorbing the nutrients and minerals it requires.”

Nicko gestured to the air and a different diagram was put on the screen.

“The branches grow similar to a mycelium network, producing very dense strands that have a large surface area and finally combine to form a kind of bark or husk. Growth rate, direction and Biode type will depend upon the enzymes, nitrates and hormones we secrete. Some Biode’s will process water, some the silicon, iron, carbon, hydrogen and the other elements required to set up the neural control paths which will allow some integration with the computer processors. If all goes well it will sprout several chambers which will eventually thicken into a shell with a breathable atmosphere inside. Think big coconuts! A nice white inside and a husky tough outside.”

Why didn't he just start with big coconuts, thought Alexa, finally understanding what they were all talking about.

“Me and Nicko will be in the ship, Hanna will be here, and Karl, the little icon next to Helena, will remain in the Dusseldorf laboratory with all the other staff and the control experiments to provide assistance if required.” Peter said animatedly.

“What exactly have you configured the seed to grow into and how long can it survive?” said Naomi, one of the more recent lab technicians. Maria had recruited her from Copenhagen University where she had worked in the medical research department, she had also been a minor YouTube celebrity for a series of medical and nursing videos. Naomi was a little older than the rest of the scientists in her early forties, but looked a lot younger due to her fitness. Maria, as usual, had seen something more in her and she got on really well with everybody.

“The goal,” said Maria, “is to try and build human-liveable chambers, connected by tunnels, we won't be spinning this up so there will be no gravity inside. Part of the experiment is to also make human structures like tables and chairs, process waste, and test how it will be able to repair itself. The guys have added lots of experimental features for this first try, they don't expect all of them to work as we are juggling a lot of unknowns. They are also going to try and fabricate some biological sensors that our probe will monitor.

“As to its lifespan,” said Nicko, “these are basically trees, so we expect hundreds of years, as long as we maintain a steady flow of light, nutrients and water, most of which can be provided from the waste output of our bio-reactors. In this case however we will only have enough nutrients in the machine for two or three years, and that will limit the growth size and lifespan.”

“You said it was a manned mission?” said Ian.

“The ship is rated for twelve people,” said Maria, “well thirteen but someone decided they didn't like that number.” Maria's avatar again turned to Alexa who again shrugged.

“However, we are only taking five for this journey, everyone else can follow real time from mission control which will be set up here.”

“Who are they?” said Jen.

“Well Jules is the pilot, Matilda who will run some experiments for Simon's team, Nicko and Peter from the Dusseldorf team and finally Naomi who will be there as our roving reporter and medical specialist just in case.”

“What? no Hardy?” Jen said, looking at him.

“I'm staying with you, Magnus and Daisy in the lab, much more exciting there, and I would rather not be gone for two weeks. However Daisy, David and myself will be backup pilots in the PowderPuff if it is needed.”

“This will be the first long term human mission, the team and myself have already done a few test runs so we know the ships are good, also for safety another saucer is going to accompany them remotely. And don't worry, this is the first of many missions so everyone will get a turn in the future if they want,” he added.

“You know we probably need another one or two medical doctors on staff or at least on standby if we are going to be doing stuff in space,” said Simon.

“I think we are going to need a lot of people,” said Alexa, “but you are right, we have a big list of skills we are going to need and doctors and nurses are on the list. We just need to let these next few months play out and see what progress we make so we have a timetable to work to. There is a whole other project and group looking at this already.”

“I have thousands of medical researchers and doctors lined up for when the time is right,” added Maria.

“If we get into any trouble I cannot handle we will just get the ship to return directly to the accident and Emergency unit at the most suitable earth side hospital, there may be a few questions asked but it would be quicker and safer than flying someone up,” said Naomi.

“We already have most emergency situations and contingencies covered,” said April. “Humans have been in space for nearly seventy years, and science fiction writers have imagined most everything else that can go wrong, up to and including aliens bursting from your stomach.” Several people smiled. “We seriously don't expect anyone to get into any problems, but as everyone will tell you, space is very dangerous and we are going to take every precaution and cover as many bases as we can.”

“Naomi,” said Maria, “you are going to be working with Petra remotely to get medical data on our astronauts, and documenting as much as you can. It was one of your early training video series on early embryo development, that was cited in the Dusseldorf team's original paper, so we knew you have an interest, and they want you to help video document it for their final paper.”

“I shouldn't be surprised really, you dropped enough hints,” she said smiling.

“Oh, and now is perhaps a good time to introduce you to another member of the crew, she is new, and may be a bit shy, so without further ado I present you with crew member number six, Eve.”

Simon, who was at the back of the room, opened the door. A floating white robot about the size of two beach balls and emitting a slight hum, wobbled slowly inside and stopped in the centre of the lecture theatre. It was a tall ovoid in shape, had no feet but two wing like arms that folded flush to the shell and a big round head the same size as the body had two large green eyes, two elf like ears, a small antenna on top and a comical mouth shaped in gold gauze where the speaker obviously were.

“Hello humans, I am Eve one!” came a surprisingly sweet metallic voice from the speaker.

The crowd stood up and started clapping and cheering wildly.

“Excellent,” said Hardy, “you’ve outdone yourselves there.”

“Looks like a total rip-off of the one from the movie Wall-e,” said Alexa, “you sure we are not going to upset anyone?”

“It looks nothing like her!” Said Maria, “we are different in at least fifteen areas, as well as the blatantly obvious one, that ours is real, not a cartoon character.”

“Which one of you is driving it?” said Jen, fascinated.

“None of us,” said Maria, “though we can obviously take over her control if required. Eve is a product of Ian and Simon's devious minds as part of their wishes to have something that can help inside and outside the ship, she is a remote drone with a MOTHER level non-sentient AI core and a Daisy mark one personality module, so no being nasty to her!”

“woohoo!” said Daisy, rushing over to Ian and hugging him excitedly, then doing the same for Simon. Ian looked extremely happy.

“The lighthouse keeper remembers.” said the robot unexpectedly and causing the room to fall silent. Simon looked at Ian, who shrugged.

“Er.. Yes!” said Simon. “Probably a bit heavy on the randomiser, a few tweaks maybe!”

Alexa looked at both of them, then at Eve, then at Jen, and both girls laughed.

“Yes, definitely a few tweaks!” continued Maria soberly. “Anyway, getting back on track, Eve can obviously just about fly in an atmosphere, but it will be much more stable and manoeuvrable in zero and low gravity situations..”

Eve wobbled again.

“She has two small arms to manipulate things, they are not very strong, but can unfold and be quite dextrous so can open things, grab things and use special tools. We have also added a small compartment in her chest about half the size of a shoe box for storage and samples.”

Two small manipulators, which were tucked under the wing like appendages, extended with a whir, and a small compartment opened and closed. In an almost comical move Eve then toppled over onto the ground, clanged twice, recovered and slowly rose to a metre height it was at before.

“Whoopsie!” it said.

“Er, it only came out of the replicator an hour ago,” said Ian, apologetically, “still a few software and hardware tweaks to do, but she’ll be alright on the night.”

“She of course is made from Simon's favourite carbon allotrope, graphyne,” said Maria, unfazed, “so a few bumps and scrapes will be fine.”

Maria continued spouting out the specifications as Eve toured the room, occasionally warbling. “Eve has twin eight hundred watt QVCells which can be overclocked to five kilowatts each, they provide heat for the internal systems which don't like absolute zero, and charge her six kilowatt hour barium graphene battery for backup, and peak power requirements. Her six tiny QVThrusters provide three degrees of movement, and the two axis gyroscope provide stability and give her some rotational ability. Like Simon said, she needs a few tweaks..”

“..And of course she has a QVModem receiver so can work at a good distance from the ship or earth.”

“That is awesome!” said Alexa, “Simon, Ian you are geniuses, I think, let's make lots, each ship should have a couple at least and I would love a few around the research centre if you can get the stability problem sorted, I bet we can think of lots of use for them.”

“Can we tweak her design or colour a bit?” said Jen, maybe different colours and definitely write the number of the unit on the front and back so we don't get confused.”

“No worries guys,” said Ian, “like I said Eve here is the first, let me, Simon or one of the girls know and as long as it's not too silly or difficult we will see what we can do.”

Daisy gave Ian another knowing wink and he smiled back shyly.

Yes, definitely something there. Thought Maria.

*August 2027 America and the world is still reeling from the on-going impeachment of ex-president Markby last month for arranging unauthorised military operations against the United Kingdom, the attempted assault of one of its citizens, Alexa Martins and America's favourite CEO Jean Michelle. There has been little comment publicly by either woman, their companies, the Whitehouse, nor the British government, and details are still limited to the now deleted, but easily available, video and the press conferences by the parties concerned.*

*However it is well known that the raid was orchestrated to steal their AI system, which many believe is giving the company a massive competitive edge over the opposition, and is responsible for the company's exponential growth rate these last two years. Facts are extremely hard to obtain, but BFG Capital in London, recently estimated the company and its holdings at over five trillion US dollars, which if true would make it as big as the world's next two companies, and bigger than many countries.*

*At the conference at the White House after the incident, Miss Martins briefed several of the government agencies and outlined the company's plans to open up space to the world, by releasing a design of the engine that is fully space capable.*

*Speculation is running rife over the possible specifications of such an engine, but most commentators believe it will usher in the second-age of mankind as it gets full access to the stars. The stocks of most space based industries were up significantly on this positive news.*

## Missions To Nowhere

September 2027

Simon, in his usual paternal manner, had wanted each of the five crew members to have some sort of space-suit, 'Just in Case', as he said. As such, Maria had negotiated the purchase of ten of the newer Blue-Origin compression suits, one of which he was now proudly modelling for Jules.

“They are err.. nice, Simon, but I'm not sure they are actually necessary.” She said trying to keep a straight face. Her accent, however, betraying a tiny trace of her French Quebec origin, usually only evident when she got slightly annoyed or emotional. Jules of course was wearing a fashionable light pink top, with one of the latest diamond ear studs, close fitting black trousers and plimsolls.

“April did also say that if anything ever got through the ship's hull then it is most likely the ship, and everything in it, would be just so much floating debris, and it wouldn't matter if I was wearing a space suit or I was butt naked.”

“OK,” said Simon, knowing April probably did not say those exact words, and ignoring her little tease, “but if you all at least keep them handy in the emergency..”

“..Sure Simon, I don't see any problem with that,” she said, cutting him off. “I was going to add getting back to a room, as one of the emergency drills we intend to do, I can include putting the suit on during the drill.”

She knew that would be enough to please Simon, and he walked off seemingly happier, to find the next problem, and hopefully to change into something less embarrassing.

The emergency rooms as Simon put it were two of the cabins that could be sealed off airtight, and had self contained food, water, oxygen supply and CO2 scrubber; all of which could technically last them four days, hopefully enough time for someone to save them. However Jules was correct, April *had* said this, adding also that anything that could breach the graphyne hull of a ship, definitely meant the ship, and anything organic inside it would be instantly dead.

“Simon is never getting me into one of those suits!” said a very gothic looking Matilda once Simon had left.

“Me neither, but let's never say never, and let's not upset Simon as he does mean well,” Jules said, winking at her and getting a rare smile in return.

The 'Don Quixote' had been a bustle of activity for the past three days. Bags, equipment, food, toiletries, were being loaded for a twenty day, and a seven hundred million kilometre round trip. Their support ships, ‘The Excalibur’ and ‘Outside Context Problem’ were on the other two pads, and ready to follow.

One by one everyone reported ready and the 'Don' sealed the door. Jules took the centre chair, Matilda and Naomi, the ones on the right Peter and Nicko the ones on the left.

“Hello Don,” said Jules, “please recognise Captain Jules LeCaire.”

“Welcome Captain Le Claire,” said the ship.

“Hi Jules,” came April's voice from Eve-four who wobbled softly onto the flight deck. They had finally come up with a plan to incorporate a simple light emitting surface on the drones. When Eve was in control of herself, it would be white with its serial number in bold black letters on the front and back. When any of the girls had control they would change to another colour, and a name badge on the chest. Eve-four was currently a deep blue, with April written on the top left of her chest, its 'eyes' containing optical and infra-red sensors, sat in small depressions, and were currently tinted green, the mouth grill had gone, and the 'ears' and the 'nose' were just small sculptured holes, which contained various environmental sensors. The design pushed cute and harmless, and delivered on both.

“We’ve been given clearance to take off in forty six minutes for our test flight over the Atlantic,” said April, “I have updated ‘Dons’ checklist accordingly, but remember everyone, as far as the UK authorities, and everybody else are concerned, we are doing an extended low pressure and hover test, to calibrate the drives for space use. The plan we submitted says we will be hovering there for twelve days at one hundred to two hundred thousand metres.”

She paused as the checklist changed, then added, “OK I better return this Eve to her position for departure, hopefully its stability issues will also get sorted by the end of this flight.”

“Thanks April, the checklist looks simple enough,” said Jules from her command chair. “Why are we bothering with the deception anyway?”

“Blame the group,” said April, “it seems the world is OK with us testing low earth orbits, but not yet ready for us casually flying a civilian crew to the asteroid-belt, to converting a kilometre sized asteroid into an organic space station. Also the UK flight regulations would self-destruct if we actually went fully into space with a crew and tried to come back.”

The little droid changed back to white and wobbled off to the special wall attachments they had fabricated for them, a new ship was being printed with a much better way to incorporate them inside and out.

Jules looked down at her checklist, it was still counting down to the first event in twenty three minutes time.

“Remote flight data has been input,” said Don. “All flight and space systems are operational Captain.”

“Thank you Don,” said Jules unnecessarily.

The flight-deck of the Don was again a slightly different design as they continued to work on the ergonomics. It had been configured with a continuous screen two metres high and six wide taking the whole of the front wall of the bridge. In the middle they had spread out the five chairs a little, and given each chair its own small workstation, which allowed crew to work in the company of others as well as from the ones in their cabins. Except for the entrance to the bridge, all the other walls in the room had screens and workstations built in, in case people preferred working standing up. None of the workstations served a particular purpose, you did what you did from where you wanted to work.

The whole front wall currently showed the view outside, with the other saucers spaced about twenty metres away from each other in the grid. It would look like some Sci-fi movie scene if not for the rural setting, and a green and yellow tractor currently pulling a mowing attachment on the lawn further towards the river.

A window appeared on the left hand side of the main monitor, and displayed a map showing southern England, and eight hundred kilometres into the Atlantic. On it there was a blue line showing the fake flight plan which went south-west six hundred kilometres. Multiple green dots were also moving slowly, highlighting the other commercial and military flight traffic in the area, each with a number and altitude in text underneath. Red dots showed the same for shipping. Jules flicked her finger, and the checklist that was was currently on Jules workstation, slid into prominence at the right-hand of the main screen.

“OK, Don, bring us to full readiness, sound external warning, and when the area is clear take us to one hundred metres to await final flight clearance.”

‘The Excalibur’ and ‘Outside Context Problem’ rose off their pads with the ‘Don’. Just before they cleared the top of the lab building the OCP and the Don went into stealth mode, painting their hull colour with the view from the opposite side, unlike the movies this only worked from a distance and from a limited focal view, up close it just looked weird.

“OK guys, the Excalibur has gone active with the Don's transponder code and livery, you and the OCP are in stealth. For all intents and purpose there is just you going up there.” Said Maria.

“Don bring up full active windows.” Said Jules.

The walls, floor and ceilings except for a few areas with carpeting, air ducting or displaying flight information changed to the outside camera views. The Landing pad was a hundred metres directly below them.

“Eek!” said Peter, gripping his armrest.

“Whoops, sorry about that Peter, I was just wondering what the option on the summary command list was for. Don, please turn off the floor display, and disable that option when Peter is on the bridge.” As the AI acknowledged the command, Jules vaguely remembered Peter was afraid of heights, but was also thinking that she couldn't wait to try the full effect in space.

The floor went back to the normal grey colour, and Peter's fingers loosened their tight grip on the armrest. He looked visibly relieved. They waited, quietly chatting and watching the checklist countdown.

Looking at the checklist, Jules pressed the yellow switch on the armrest of the captain's chair, “Bristol air traffic control, please be advised Dietrich Air Jupiter, Jupiter, X Ray, Tango, five awaiting clearance for test flight Tango Golf four niner as authorised by CAA Charter. We will be leaving UK air-space vertically to our cruising altitude of one eighty thousand metres when authorised, then leaving vector two fifty degrees west south west to the test area, over.”

Another window changed to show their normal air traffic controller Stan, and a new guy behind him wearing the same air traffic controller uniform. The new guy was shaking his head in disbelief, this never got old for them.

“Roger Jupiter, Jupiter, X ray, Tango, five. Hi Jules, we see your transponder active, you are cleared for vertical ascent to your cruising altitude of one eighty thousand metres, you have clear skies, and above fifteen thousand metres, there is obviously nobody else and can execute your chosen vector from there. Wow, it says you're going to remain at the edge of space for two weeks. Keep in touch I guess, and good luck in space. Over.”

“Thank you Stan, we are ascending now. Follow us on radar if you can, we have plenty of coffee and crosswords, going to be pretty boring, feel free to talk to us if your radio will get that far out, but it's all in the name of science, see you soon, over and out.”

Jules had slipped slightly into her French accent once she knew it was Stan, he may have been older, and happily married, but he was a bit of a treasure, and always gave the pilots a warm courteous service whenever he talked.

“Don, please take us to one hundred and eighty kilometres and execute pre-prepared plan.”

“Roger Captain,” came the ship's AI’s voice and everyone was pressed down a little in their chairs as the ship immediately started to rise, the screens showing them rising vertically slowly at first, but gaining speed steadily. The display showing the altimeter gained more prominence on the wall, now showing they had already gone through a thousand metres. A few seconds later it was two thousand, then four thousand, then eight, sixteen, thirty two, sixty four, then their acceleration slowed, and they felt the extra weight removed, gravity eased the velocity change lower, until finally stopping at one hundred and eighty kilometres, the blue of the sky had disappeared and the horizon was black.

The altimeter had already re-calibrated itself for kilometres, additional parameters appeared, and a few like the barometric pressure, temperature and surface weather conditions were removed.

“Holding at one eighty kilometres, Captain,” came the Don, unnecessarily and always by the book.

“Wow,” said Peter, “so we are officially all astronauts now!”

“I guess,” said Jules.

“Not as limited a club as it used to be,” added Maria hovering back into the room in a green coloured Eve, “but you guys are in the top one thousand. In five hours however you will all hold the record for the furthest humans have ever travelled away from planet Earth. Unfortunately you will all have to keep that little record a secret for a couple of years.”

“And Alexa was the first woman on the moon. Unofficially of course,” smiled Jules.

“Seriously!” said Nicko.

“Jules, you're heading into dangerous territory,” warned Maria.

“Yes,” smiled Jules, and tapping her nose, “but as Maria says, best to wait for her biography to get any details. Asking her about it now may get you on toilet cleaning duty for the rest of your life.”

The two men laughed.

“Hi Maria,” said Naomi, finishing up something on a touchscreen and smiling, “you hijacked the DaisyBot again, April was only just in it.”

Annoyingly to the AI’s, the Eve robots they, Simon and Ian had so diligently named, had their names 'shortened' by Jen to “DaisyBot”. It made no sense to them why that stuck, considering the amount of time they had spent finding a name they *wouldn't* do that with. However “DaisyBot,” had stuck, and that is what all the humans, even Simon and Ian, had been calling them in the last few days.

“Looks like our poor DaisyBot AI won’t be getting much action this trip, you guys seem to like your new found mobility.”

“Yes, it's kind of an interesting sensation,” said Maria, executing a careful slow spin.

“Shame we only have Eve-four inside the ship, we probably did not have to put Eve-seven in the outside hold, since the air-lock has been tested several times now and seems stable.” Said Maria, continuing defiantly to use the old Eve moniker.

“Simon can be a bit parental,” said Matilda, “but here he insisted, correctly I think, that if the air lock failed there would be no way for a DaisyBot to get outside to help.”

Jules nodded in agreement.

“A very low probability but I conceded the point,” said Maria, sighing that even Matilda was now using the DaisyBot term.

They all watched as another item on the checklist changed colour, and the Excalibur, pretending to be the Don, broke off formation and headed off to the south west to their supposed test position.

“What if someone notices, there must be lots of telescopes and spy satellites focussed up and down on us.”

“Dream on Jules,” laughed Maria, “we are a hundred and eighty kilometres up, and the saucers are either invisible, or visually identical, they are going to see and hear what they expect to, a very bored bunch of scientists playing at being spacemen. We will simulate most of the ground radio and phone chit-chat and test stuff so you guys don't have to.”

All five of the humans laughed.

“Best to add a transcription of those contacts and messages, so we can all at least see what we are supposed to have said,” said Naomi.

“Good point,” said Maria, throwing an additional window up and squeezing the map off.

“What!” said Peter looking at the log, “I already have two missed calls from my mum, what does that in dark green say next to it, I can't read the font against the black background.”

“Sorry,” said Maria as the font colour changed, “it's just saying it played your voicemail. We are expected to be out of cell phone coverage so we need to play the part, but we will activate outgoing connections in your bedrooms so you can make private calls if you wish using the QVModem’s. All communications will be routed through the Excalibur to Starlink so it should all look normal. You can also all use emails from the workstations here, or the ones in the common room or your cabins. We will monitor for any faux pas, and give you the option to correct them if you need to. Can't go letting your mother know you’re in the asteroid belt or it may blow our cover!”

“Sounds like a plan,” said Naomi.

“Don, please begin acceleration phase one,” said Jules looking at the checklist and noticing the text now had a yellow background as she was fifteen seconds overdue. April had told her the captain must authorise everything, unless it endangered the ship, however the ship would become very insistent if she went too long before confirming a mission parameter, unless she put the list on hold. The item box checked, and the text greyed, highlighting the next item on the checklist. The screens showed them moving forward into space, there were no stars flying past, or anything that crass.

* * *

The ‘Outside Context Problem’ led the procession, and stayed ten seconds ahead, not visible on the monitor except by its icon. They all sat there, feeling heavier due to the increase in acceleration from one to one point three gravities all of them, once more, looking at the various instruments showing them reaching higher and higher altitude from the earth.

“How does this work again,” said Naomi, “I understand we are under acceleration and I feel heavier, but we are going forward.”

“No we are not going forward, we are going straight up, just with thirty percent more acceleration than gravity,” said Jules, “hence why we are heavier. The ship configures the screens, and view for the most comfortable. Humans are used to gravity being down, and moving forward, that is not really possible for us, so we just pop on a small visual illusion with no acceleration in the X axis, and one point three Gravities of acceleration in the Y axis. No point in confusing people for no reason.”

“We are also not in orbit,” said Nicko, “If we were in orbit you could turn the engines off and we would all be in free-fall but stay circling the earth, falling, but due to your speed and the curvature of the earth never hitting the ground. With our profile, if we stopped the engine anytime in the next hour or two, gravity would take over and we would go into free-fall, like someone cutting the cables in a lift, and we would plummet straight back to earth just like Mr. Newton's apple, but with a bigger splat!”

“Nicko is correct,” said Maria, glad for a bunch of scientists in the audience to explain, “gravity falls off as the square of the distance. The earth is a big mass, not a point, so it's a bit more complicated, but basically as we get further away it looks more like a point and as our distance doubles its effect falls off by four. In two hours our speed will be fast enough that gravity won't have a big enough effect to drag us back down before we escape, though we will still be subject to it, and that from all the other bodies in the solar system.”

“We will also be gradually reducing our acceleration from one point three gravities down to oh point eight, so you should all be a lot more comfortable, and our speed will pick up substantially as we have nothing pulling us back.”

“Why is the OCP so far ahead?” continued Naomi.

“Even I know that one,” said Matilda, “we are on the same trajectory, so the OCP will extend our sensor range, and hopefully detect, or bang in to anything in front before it becomes a problem for us.”

“Unfortunately space has things coming at you from every direction, so technically we can also be blind-sided, even from behind,” said Jules soberly.

Everyone looked at their rapidly increasing velocity, currently at twenty two thousand kilometres per hour, the “Altitude” label had changed to become “Distance From Earth” and in the ten minutes they had been accelerating that distance was now close to two thousand kilometres. Apart from that nothing really seemed to change, they seemed to be heading vaguely twenty or thirty degrees off the sun, with no other objects visible. Space was indeed both very exciting, very scary, and very boring all at the same time.

“Anyone want a coffee?” said Naomi.

* * *

Their temporary mission control room in the lecture theatre had been rearranged slightly to allow comfortable viewing of the three massive screens, and a more relaxed sitting atmosphere if people wanted to socialise. The first screen showed the same trajectory information as the Don; The middle screen a view from the back of the Don's flight deck, looking forward over everyone's head, and to the screens, so people could get a sense of being there. The final screen looked down into the meeting area in Simon's laboratory, which had been taken over by Hanna for her equipment, and where Leo and Hanna were talking and working on something. A fourth smaller screen had been added back to the meeting room in Dusseldorf, it was empty at the moment but was normally occupied by Karl or one of his other guys.

A couple of additional workstations had been added if anybody wanted to work here, but both were empty. A drinks fridge and a tea and coffee station were also there, with the biscuits being continuously refilled. It was late afternoon, four people and a pink robot sat around one of the U shaped sofas talking.

“Have you seen how big it is though?” said Magnus to Alexa, Jen, Daisy and one of the Eve robots, currently taken over by Maria and sporting a very pink skin.

“Not seen it yet,” said Alexa, “why don't you pop the picture up,” she waved at the big screens.

“Holly..” Started Alexa.

“I know,” said Magnus, “it's the first of four that they say will be used to go to the moon once we release the software tweak to the engines. That is why the press and the space nerds are following our fake final test mission so much.”

“Hey,” said the little pink robot, “I am trying to make it exciting. I took it up to one hundred and ninety thousand metres for four hours, then to free fall for thirty seconds, in a few cases using acceleration profiles to make it look like the ship had run out of steam. Added a bit of chatter and random encrypted telemetry from them to us and back, so they all think we are doing something.”

“Jules is still going to be so mad at you,” said Alexa, “you are definitely leading Jake on!”

“Oh it's not that bad,” said Daisy, “Jake is married with two grown up kids, all the girl pilots wind him up so it would be out of character if Jules didn't, and it’s all in public.”

“Jules is nonchalant, and anyway Jake is well aware that Jules ‘bats for the other team’.”

“Maria!” said Alexa sharply, “Jules does not ‘bat for the other team’ she is a proud lesbian!”

“Sorry, I am still perfecting my humour and only repeating what she said to Nicko, I will tone it down a tiny bit.”

“Oh poor Maria,” said Jen sympathetically, “you’ve gone and upset her.”

“I don't get upset Jen, it is correct that I know the limits so I can stay within them.”

“Anyway,” said Alexa, “I will come down and cuddle your chassis tonight until you feel better.”

“Alexa!” said Jen, “how is that any less appropriate, you’re giving poor Maria mixed signals. I still love you Maria if you need a proper bestie who won't tie your logic in knots!”

“Thanks Jen, at least someone is nice to me.”

Alexa shoved Jen playfully, “suck-up!”.

“Nicko and Peter also did a small live interview for their national TV,” continued Maria, changing the subject. “We passed it through with a three second delay, which we blamed on us not having a direct link, but we thought we should include in case they accidentality said something not in the plan. But they kept to the script, so all was good.”

“It's like the moon landings,” smiled Jen, “the inside of the ship looks so much like a star trek set, that a lot of conspiracy people are saying it is being streamed from a movie studio, and not from a hundred and eighty kilometres up over the Atlantic. Oh the irony!”

“They are going to have a field day when you eventually release the footage from the asteroid, that is, if you ever do,” said Magnus, one arm tenderly wrapped around Jen and playing with a twirl of hair now she was growing it longer.

“Unfortunately that won't be for a little while yet,” sighed Maria, “no need to tip our hand too soon as we have the other missions underway, and, let's face it, Jen's right, if they think the inside of the saucer is fake, who's going to believe the inside of an asteroid three million times further away.”

“Or an enormous space habitat!” Added Jen.

“True!” said Magnus, nodding.

They all laughed, and spent a bit of time looking at the big screen. The Don and its crew were past Mars still travelling hundreds of kilometres a second, the velocity display recalibrating from kilometres per hour, then kilometres per minute when each got past a hundred thousand.

It was still another eighteen hours from the asteroid, the ship had made its long lazy U turn to turn it around, it was inefficient but allowed them to keep the thrust constant, the gravity normal, and the manoeuvrer undetectable by the crew. The ship was still accelerating, but now facing the opposite direction and so slowing down, timing its exact stop for the target asteroid.

Jules took that moment to walk into the flight deck and sit down on the captain's chain, the actual DaisyBot, came in a minute later with a mug of some hot drink, curtsied, made some weird R2D2 sound, then left. Jules accepted the drink and thanked the sweet, but crazy machine.

The ships were working the same time as the guys at the research centre, because it was logical. So it was late afternoon there too. Don would start dimming the lights at eight, and go to low intensity red lights for the night, there was no need for a night shift, as the AI’s monitored everything.

“Hi Jules,” said Alexa, seeing her on the screen with her coffee in hand. “A few of us are here having a drink after work. You okay there? not getting too bored I hope?”

The screen changed to her upper body front view, at the same time on the ship the guys on earth appeared full screen on her large monitor, moving the space view window to the side.

“A bit,” she admitted honestly, “it doesn't feel like I am that far away. I know we’re travelling millions of kilometres an hour, there is a hard vacuum outside, and I am a week from getting back to earth and being able to walk out the door. But that is the only thing making people anxious.”

She put her feet up on the chair drawing them in with her arms, “Peter is putting on a brave face, but he certainly doesn't look comfortable. Naomi dropped a cup near him a day ago and he nearly had to change his underwear! So no, I don't think space is for everyone, no matter how safe you make it, but how you find those people and make a perfect crew is something way outside my experience or comfort zone,” she paused.

“There is one thing most people have brought up, since we have two ships, we should have a way to move between them.”

Alexa looked confused, “I thought we could?”

“The oversight will be corrected in the larger design,” said April. “But the bigger ones will have enough space that you wont want too. However, for the Icarus three ships it was assumed nobody would ever enter or leave them outside of a breathable atmosphere.”

Jules waved it away, “apart from that, hmm, maybe a few more people to talk to would be good, as would a gym or a swimming pool for exercise, and Naomi reckons a cat would be nice, though DaisyBot is much more awesome as I am not a cat person.”

She sipped a bit of her coffee glancing up to the right at Daisy, “Ian must have taken a lot of notice of all your little mannerisms Daisy, a man does not notice these things unless he has an ulterior motive I think,” she smiled.

“Jules,” exclaimed Daisy, “like everybody is here listening!” she fidgeted a bit. “He is cute though, gave me some flowers from the garden for my room, and I can't believe he likes the same things as me, we talked for ages on Japanese Anime the other day. Oh I’m sure Ian is just as sweet with everybody,” Daisy looked at the other girls who were all shaking their heads.

“Never got flowers,” said Jen confused.

“Me neither,” said Alexa.

“Anime? Ian? a first with me,” said Jules.

“He definitely fancies Daisy,” said Allison from the other sofa where she was sharing a pizza with Simon and half in attention. “He spent quite a bit of time with Maria programming in all her mannerisms.”

“They are pretty random,” said Magnus, “I saw a DaisyBot in the garden yesterday just spinning in circles around the flower bed with its wings out, it was so cute I took a video and sent it to Daisy and Jen.”

“One asked me if I wanted to look at the pictures in the dining room, it said I looked bored and needed cheering up,” said Jen, “It was surprisingly pleasant company.”

“Yeah, I think Ian is wasted as an engineer, he should definitely be transferred to the computer department,” said Allison, “he has a bit of a knack for writing things in the control and personality language the girls wrote.”

“Even I can use that,” said Daisy, hoping to change the subject, “I hated Java and C at university..”

“Don't change the subject, you little tease,” said Jen, unhooking herself from Magnus and slamming down on the sofa next to her, “let's hear all the dirt on Ian girl, cone of silence Maria!”

The other girls closed in for the kill, Jules making some muffled sounds and gestures then going quiet and obviously listening in.

“Er.. Time for me to go, I think I have somewhere to be!” said Magnus, lifting himself up from his solitary position on a sofa and walking away, to a shrug from Allison and Simon. He wasn't sure whether to think poor Ian, or lucky Ian!

* * *

April [It missed the Excalibur by two hundred milliseconds. Nothing on lidar, and only just detectable with four returns on the millimetre radar, too fast to get any accurate size, or density data. The velocity, however, was in the order of sixty one kilometres a second. The closest approach to the Don was twelve kilometres and we calculated no change was required. I have tagged, and added it to the scary object database]

April [Based on returns from similar objects, it would have close to one hundred megajoules of energy. Survivable, as there would have been minimal momentum transfer, but the energy transfer would probably have damaged the graphyne hull. To the humans on board it would have sounded like a nuclear explosion had gone off outside, and I know from the psychological reactions to other loud noises, and being in space, it would have caused a major panic. I doubt any sort of acoustic dampening we are testing would have helped in this case. The humans need to be made aware of possibilities like this in their training]

Helena [It is like everything. We need a lot more data]

Maria [We do need to up our game on the detection of these. We need dedicated ultrafast hardware for the detection grids, the current technology is not effective enough for objects moving potentially hundreds of kilometres a second]

Helena [The new stealth drone designs will also extend the detection range without changes to the saucer. One of Giannis team worked on a similar concept for his PhD. Its priority is now high enough that I will allocate some resources to get it done officially. There are also Samuals and Huang, they conceived of a similar concept for a solar system wide array of probes, mapping all known objects, but at the tech levels then this was unachievable. It could be possible now, but easier strategies we are planning to adopt, like travelling outside the plane of the elliptic would achieve the same]

Helena [Radiation is still the main issue we have to address. It is still causing issues for the all our drones, especially the smaller ones; Two of the thirty two we manufactured have suffered reset events in the last ten days. I have doubled the gate size on the latest replicator batch again, so we are now at twenty-five nanometres, we are also trying a new four-layer insulation layer, and a newer checksum algorithm covering smaller memory block sizes, as well as faster watchdog processors. Having the three cores on the latest batch has so far prevented any terminal problems, but I see no easy way yet to completely eliminate this without a thicker hydrogen-based protective layer]

April [The increased current to the active shielding superconductor, and the changes to its orientation fields, have reduced charged particles by a further seven percent, and I believe further improvements are unnecessary as we have reached a diminishing return. The risk inside the human habitation areas is also quite low, but not zero, and high energy non-charged particles may still get through. I think we should keep the guys home for a few months after this, for observation, and until the medical staff look them over]

Helena [All this corresponds with the data we have for the sixteen confirmed incidents of bit errors on both the Don and the Excalibur's processors. All were corrected, and all were on hull facing systems, none of the cabin facing systems reported any incidents.]

Maria [I wouldn't feel comfortable being in space, without more cosmic radiation shielding. In the last four years my debugging systems have recorded twelve such errors, so we need to remember we are not immune even down on earth]

Helena [We can improve on the conditions on earth with just ten metres of ice, so I think we can provide a much better environment for AI's in the future habitats, and the larger saucers]

April [I have looked at the efficiency calculations and prepared a recommended option for Gianni for the second mission to begin the habitat construction. I have also added another three saucers to the replication queue in anticipation of him agreeing. The preferred option is to build the first recycler and larger replicator on site and transport just the materials we cannot get locally. At the end of it we can begin making the extruders much faster. We however need to identify a reliable source of carbon, silicon and several other elements]

Helena [We currently have enough of the rarer elements at our earth facilities for a year's worth of production. This is just from the last two months at our e-waste test processing facility in Cardiff; Projections give us at least twenty years stock just from the UK landfills. The sixteen other planned processing centres around the world have been green-lighted, we were just waiting to see how well Cardiff worked out before we made a full commitment. With all these processing facilities fully active it should technically be able to supply all of humanity's needs, hopefully it will be possible to do a planned phase-out starting with the biggest polluters. Once we locate sources in the asteroid belt it will reduce our requirements from earth completely]

April [During the e-waste processing we are also identifying a lot of other elements we should start to stockpile such as metals, oils and plastics which we can convert to carbon for processing. We also have a team now working on the really nasty stuff like acids. It will never be profitable to clean these, but if we can return a waste site to productive land there is a long term benefit and a possible profit centre]

April [With us being down to only two saucers still mapping the belt, we are only seven percent complete; this is mostly at low resolution so we will be missing millions of objects under a hundred metres. The catalogue we currently have shows nine hundred and thirteen suitable asteroids for our purpose. The closest one is only seventy million kilometres spin-ward from the asteroid we are currently seeding, and is on a slowly retarding orbit so it will come within four million kilometres in sixteen years time. It has a diameter of twenty six kilometres on the major axis and twenty one on the minor; It is part of an asteroid grouping in the same orbital trajectory, so we could be lucky]

Maria [Let us exclude the luck part of the equation. Task the closest of the two saucers with a DaisyBot to do a full survey of it. Something more suitable may be found before the mission is ready but we should plan this as our principle objective until we do]

I will volunteer to do the first transfer and we can refine the design for you guys]

The massive AI cores we have designed for these looks so tempting to inhabit, I have been working with Spence, Allison, and now David on how my consciousness would be transferred, but we have so far failed to make an exact model. You two will have no issues as I designed you better, but the surgery for me would be too complicated until we have better tools. Even if I cannot transfer logically, I will at least transfer physically and have a big strong AI next to me as a nest-mate. Maybe this is how our human girls feel?] She added suitable humour tags.

The debris cloud was bigger than anticipated, which means the density of the asteroid is lower than our estimate, but it has cleared the area to work on. The OCP has increased its lead and should arrive in six minutes. Five hours before the Don]
