* * *

The arrival of the OCP was timed for nine AM start of the working day and their temporary mission control centre was filled to overflowing. The audience consisted of almost everyone in the research centre, except maybe a couple of the household staff who didn't really have an interest in the science stuff. There was also Karl and his team in Dusseldorf, several from the other research facilities depending upon their time-zone, and of course the five in the Don.

The OCP determined none of the ejection material from the explosion was a hazard, the biggest being a few metres in diameter but travelling twenty metres per second and easily avoided. The smaller ones were travelling a bit faster, but none were moving in a direction that might impact the Don. Using the laser was therefore not deemed necessary to the dismay of some in the audience back on earth.

The three main screens showed several high definition cameras from the OCP, and one from the Don, which was still a few hours away. Suddenly two of the screens lit up, as the still unnamed asteroid was lit by brilliant lighting, and blanketed by radar and lidar from the OCP. The ship had now moved to one hundred metres from the surface, above where the impact of their ice sphere had created a very ragged crater, at least eighty metres wide and thirty deep. It looked more like a rocky beach, where the rocks went from sand-sized particles to one the size of a bus.

Unlike the videos from the various space agencies which seemed mostly black and white and grainy, the craters were lit up extremely bright, in high definition and at thirty frames per second. As well as the expected shades of grey, black, and white, there were surprisingly shades of yellow and brown, some spots that seemed to glisten, and some that seemed to be steaming! The chatter of the crowd increased with a few ‘awes’ and ‘arrs’ and as people talked amongst themselves in little groups.

“Feel free to speak up if you have questions or spot anything interesting,” said Maria, “The Don won't be arriving until after lunch, so we are going to start preparing the area for them.”

“What are those glistening things in the bottom of the right hand monitor,” said Leo.

“Alas,” said Maria, “as the great bard once said, ‘All that glitters..’ Most likely it is crystals of quartz or mica, or could even be water or methane ice that was frozen beneath the surface. The DaisyBot's will be out soon and we can take a look at anything interesting. There are also several very large pieces that lidar is detecting are loose, and we will need to clear them from the arrival area, before the Don arrives. They probably only weigh a few tonnes at most and should be easily cleared by the bots so long as they are still not attached to anything.”

“What about the steam we can see in camera six?” said Alexa, “am I the only one thinking it can't be that hot!”

“The areas we exposed were at negative one hundred and seventy degrees,” said Helena, “but will warm up slowly as the sun and our lights affect them, in this case it is likely to be methane ice boiling off or some locked in frozen nitrogen or other gas. DaisyBot has been given instructions to sample these so I can give you more information later.”

Well at least nobody called it out as a dumb question she thought, even though her first thoughts had been boiling water. There again she vaguely remembered water boiled at a lower temperature at higher altitude, in lower pressure, so maybe people assumed she knew that. “No dumb questions,” her teacher had once told her. “Yeah right!”

The still black monitor changed over to show another feed from the OCP's hold. The bottom of the ship had two areas that would accept a custom built cargo pod, Ian had wanted to make an area that would fit a half-sized shipping container, but it was finally vetoed for their own in-house design. They agreed however that future saucers would have the space to take full sized shipping containers as it made the logistics easier and the loading faster.

Nothing happened at first, then a line of light slowly got wider as the pod door opened and the outside light emerged. A DaisyBot darted off ahead of the camera, slowly turning bright red, not reflected but emitted, it showed none of the awkwardness moving as it did on earth. The camera from the second DaisyBot following it, zoomed after it gracefully.

“Let's go see what the treasure is, eh Leo,” said Maria as the right hand monitor saw the two DaisyBot's, a red and a green one appear from the top and slowly sink to the bottom.

“I’m controlling the cameras on the green DaisyBot,” said Maria, April is the red.

“Go DaisyBot's..” Shouted Daisy, hugging Ian and giving him a kiss full on the lips.

“Go Daisy!” whispered Jen, prompting Magnus and Alexa on either side of her to smile.

“Wow, this is pretty exciting,” said Magnus, “it does look a bit like ice now Maria is close up. See the blue in it from the reflection, it looks a bit like the dirty ice from the glaciers I remember as a boy in Finland.”

“I remember the same when I was a teenager,” said Alexa, “mother took us down the South Island and we had to walk for ages to get to this glacier. They had roped off the path so far back you couldn't see much, but a lot of people were ignoring the barrier and going to the bottom, where bits had broken off. They said the water fell as rain millions of years before.”

“Dubious!” said Maria, “more like twenty thousand years, however what you are looking at here could be billions of years old as it's been locked below the surface, otherwise it would have boiled off in the vacuum or sublimated. You were correct however Alexa, this is water ice according to the sensors.”

Oh Yeah, she thought. Alexa one, nerds zero!

The camera followed the red DaisyBot as it rose back up, compensating as it panned into the harsh glare of the saucers powerful lights.

“OK kids,” came Maria's voice from the main speaker, “we will have a quick once around the crater to make sure we are not disturbing any aliens, then the bots will begin clearing and sampling the area. The DaisyBot needs to be careful of getting too much dirt on her, the only current method to clean her is to shake or spin.”

“For those interested DaisyBot fourteen will be the one ‘volunteering’ to stay and monitor the seed and nurture it through its growth cycle. She has some special abilities over the normal bots, like four arms, with attachments for drills and shovels, and a small one kilowatt laser, all of which will help her as she is likely not to see us again for a few years.”

As exciting as it was to see robots running around an asteroid three hundred million kilometres away, the crowd started thinning over the course of the hour, especially when they realised that nobody from the Don had any intention, or even means to leave the ship. It seemed the human element was purely symbolic.

“Does nobody read the timetable we put up,” said April disappointed, “we are two minutes away from the boring operation and only twelve people are here!”

“I’m only waiting for breakfast, then to see 'The Don' turn up, who wants to see a boring operation,” said Jen.

“I guess it does say that on the timetable,” said Maria with a resigned voice. “Whoops! Here let me update it.” The words ‘Boring Operations’ were replaced by ‘Laser Boring Operations’ and several people took immediate notice.

“Laser boring!” said Jen, “you're going to shoot a hole through the asteroid! oh my, some people are going to be pretty miffed!”

“I knew,” said Simon, “should be awesome by the way, the OCP has had her generators running at nearly full power and has been charging her accumulators to a hundred percent for the past hour. It's going to use the full one hundred kilowatts for several seconds.. Oh look, the DaisyBot has moved into position.”

The screen now showed a view from each bot which had moved a hundred metres from the centre of the now clear crater. An intense red beam of light immediately hit the centre of the crater, steam and small rocks seeming to float away from it.

“AWESOME!” shouted a few people.

“Oh my!” said Alexa who was nibbling some toast.

“War of the freaking Worlds!” said Terry punching the air, and high-fiving the four guys around the table they sat.

The door burst open and a couple of other people steamed in just in time to see the laser turn off.

“What happened, what did I miss?” said another of the engineers.

“Now the DaisyBot's go in and clean the debris and then we go again,” said Simon.

“Phew,” said Steve walking back in, why did nobody say you were shooting lasers!”

“We are not just shooting lasers,” said April, “this is a precision boring operation, we are basically trying to get to the bottom of a rock pile without it all falling apart, over twenty papers have been written on how you would go about this. We also engaged three scientists who were working with ice core sampling, we basically gave them the specs, what tools we could have and asked all of them how they would go about it, hypothetically of course. Maria has also been the LabAI for twenty three geography and geology departments for the last twelve months.”

Three new bots appeared, one was waiting with what looked like a cross between a shovel and a net. A fourth and fifth bot now appeared and positioned a large fine net in the air. The bots hung there like nothing ever should, then slowly two of them encircled most of the debris, and in a smooth operation bringing the ends together, with four corners held, one towed it off screen. The third bot that was waiting in the wings now moved in and started removing rubble that had accumulated in the area, or was missed by the big net. Rocks and debris they had missed, hung in the air silently, some spinning slowly and waiting their turn to be removed.

“Where is the rubbish being taken?” said Alexa.

“Just dumped under a big net for now to stop the bits floating off as more is put in, most will be put back down the hole and on top of the crater to seal it. Unfortunately we have already made quite a bit of a mess, but we will learn a lot from this for next time, and we are on a bit of a tight timetable.

Sure enough, a few minutes later all the bots again moved out of the way and the intense beam washed over the same place. After three of these cycles, one of the droids moved in, hovering over a five metre diameter hole with straight sides, the bottom was over four metres deep, not smooth and had hundreds of score lines from the laser and shovel.

“About what the guys had predicted,” said April. “Our analysis has come back with mostly loose silicates, calcium, and carbon, with large traces of most of the lighter elements common in the crust of the earth. There are also low traces of metals, and about twenty percent water, CO2 and methane ice, which are what is binding a lot of this together. At this rate we should be on schedule to have the hole sunk about thirty metres for when the Don arrives in about three hours.”

The guys in the Don of course were monitoring this closely. “It is good,” said Nicko in German on their group's video channel, “we should be able to hollow a larger chamber inside and like an igloo we can seal it and bring it up over zero degrees.”

He turned off the screen and again in German said, “Maria, I suggest we go to at least fifty metres as progress seems to be good, the deeper the better it gives us the best protection and allow a greater surface area before it gets closer to the surface.”

“No problem, due to the favourable composition, we have ten hours we can shave off our original timescale, we will use half this to go as deep as we can then we have a contingency if there are any delays,” she said.

“Wonderful!”

Jules walked into their science lab on the Don and everyone immediately switched back to English for her.

“Hey guys, just to inform you we are one hour away from the asteroid. You may hear the occasional noise from minor debris, needless to say it is too small, and too slow to even think about, but I don't want you worrying. Also in thirty minutes when we get to the asteroid we will sound three bells and will cut the acceleration to point three earth gravities. We will orbit around it at an altitude of four kilometres until we are ready to release the package.”

“DaisyBot is going around the ship identifying and securing any loose items. Due to the better results on the radiation shielding we do not need to land, but we do plan to go to zero gravity for about thirty minutes for Naomi to run a couple of other small experiments; before it happens there will be an announcement and we will again sound three bells.”

“Also during zero gravity all the water will be cut off and the doors to the bathrooms and showers will be closed, as will the kitchen as all are unusable. If you start feeling sick then we will try and reduce the time a little, but for now you will just have to be careful and use one of these.” She handed out a few brown bags and the people on the other end of the video call started laughing. Peter and Nicko smiled, joining in the humour.

“Please don't let Naomi catch me barfing on film,” laughed Peter, “I will never live it down.”

As Jules left the room they resumed their conversation in German, going over the last minute checks and remote telemetry from the seed. Three bells sounded from the ship's speaker and as she said they gradually felt their weight reducing, it was weird but not too unpleasant but they found they needed to be careful as moving just felt wrong.

“Don to crew. Acceleration is now zero point three one gravities orbiting the target asteroid, It is recommended that you apply your restraints while sitting and exercise caution when lifting and moving yourself or other items. I will sound three bells and make an announcement before the next acceleration change, over and out.”

People at the three locations watched the progress of the drilling, but by seven PM, the audience was down to Simon, Leo and Hanna, and a few more people at the remote sites more directly involved in the science. They had now excavated the hole down to eighty metres, and progress had slowed due to the distance the bots had to move the debris. Nicko made the call to stop and begin to hollow the chamber at twelve o’clock. By that time everybody in the UK site was in bed. The chamber would take several hours to enlarge, and the AI’s promised to wake everyone up who wanted to, for the final part of the plan.

Throughout the night, all the DaisyBot's worked together, using their small lasers and drill attachments. They were a lot slower than the main laser, but by five AM they had a workable eleven metre diameter chamber hollowed out at the end of the shaft. While three of the DaisyBot's moved the remaining supplies and test equipment from the hold of the OCP into the chamber, another prepared for the backfill operation, yet another filmed it all.

At six AM the internal lighting on the Don started coming up to full brightness, and by six fifteen all five crew were sitting down for a breakfast of muesli or porridge. It was actually a little difficult swallowing in the third gravity and eating and drinking took a special skill.

“Note to future self,” said Jules to on-screen April, “let's orbit at thirty kilometres and stick to point nine gravities or more.”

All four of the others nodded.

“I prefer this lower gravity,” said the DaisyBot unexpectedly and unrequested, and doing a short waltz across the room, spinning then darting back gracefully. Jules scratched her head, wondering what Ian was smoking when designing these!

“When everyone's ready then,” said Jules, shaking her concentration back to the now, “let's get this show on the road. OK guys, is everything prepared? Once we are stationary we will be weightless, though not in free-fall, these are technically the same but we don't know if it will feel the same to us. However, none of us have had any experience in any form of zero gravity, and are likely to make fools of ourselves, so I suggest you get to your workstations and strap down, in practice we completed this in thirty minutes.”

The five people cleaned up from breakfast putting everything into the dishwasher, then the DaisyBot went around with a little vacuum cleaner, picking up crumbs, and bits she had identified from breakfast, and securing any loose items.

“We should maybe get her a little French Maid outfit,” laughed Peter pointing at the DaisyBot with the vacuum cleaner.

“Non,” said Jules in her exaggerated and timeless accent, “only a real French Maid can wear those,” she twirled herself, then forgetting the gravity, almost fell over causing Peter and Nicko to laugh. The DaisyBot had stopped to watch this and twirled itself much more gracefully. All the humans laughed.

“Timeless!” said Matilda.

The three bells sounded and slowly the gravity reduced to zero.

“The Don is at ten metres and holding. Releasing magnetic clamps in hold one and two.” The Don deliberately spoke of itself in the third person vernacular most of the time and it was one thing that separated it from a fully sentient AI.

It was not nauseous, just weird to suddenly have no weight, you could still feel your mass and you still had inertia so it still took the same amount of effort to stop and start your movement.

“Weird, but I could get used to this for a short while,” said Matilda, smiling at Naomi as she connected the blood pressure meter to her left arm.

“Still, it's very bad for the body. Do you feel the difference in how your heart is pumping? We really don't want to be in it for more than a few days, or you will end up like those astronauts who have to be helped from their capsule when they land.”

“OK guys,” said Jules, looking at the high definition feeds from the bots and the ship, “let's get this show on the road.”

It didn't take the bots long to reposition and break down the cargo pods. The guys on the ship, and in six earth research facilities sites followed the progress with great interest, others not so.

“I actually wonder why we even put humans on the ship,” said Alexa, sat with Hardy and David eating a light breakfast. “I mean from everything I can see, they could do everything from here, it's not as if they are getting into spacesuits and taking a walk on the asteroid. Why are we even taking the risk?”

“Oh Alexa!” said Hardy, “where is your sense of adventure! Look how excited everyone is, just knowing there are humans more than three hundred million kilometres distant laying the foundations of our future.. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about it.”

“I’m with Hardy,” said David, “the risk is really small with all the precautions you guys have set up, I doubt they are in any more danger than a transatlantic flight using an old Jet aircraft. I’m really looking forward to my turn!”

“Well you’ll get me up when I have a big open space I can walk around without wearing one of Simon's silly space suits, and certainly not one of those uniforms Jules, Allison, Matilda and Daisy wore.”

Both guys smiled, remembering Alexa's face when the girls came to Simon's birthday party three weeks before, dressed in the original star trek female crew uniforms.

“Had to have been a man who dreamed those up!” she continued, almost red faced for now bringing the topic up.

The noise level in the room went up a notch as the DaisyBot's began manoeuvring the seed and accompanying equipment, and monitoring packages down to the cavern.

“When does the heater get switched on?” said Alexa in an obvious attempt to change the subject and completely ignoring the project checklist on another screen.

“Last thing,” said Helena, requests for obvious information was just something humans did, and even the smartest of them were not immune from asking stupid questions just to make conversation. “Once everything is in and arranged, turned on and tested, the remaining bots will go topside while DaisyBot fourteen will remain.”

Things proceeded quickly from this point. The chamber was sealed with rocks, and some melted ice that quickly refroze, then the whole thing backfilled with the debris taken out. All of this made quite simple due to the lack of any perceivable gravity. It got pretty boring after that, and the saucer resumed its powered orbit to reinstate gravity while they waited.

Inside the chamber the heaters on the seed turned on, and the inside temperature was slowly raised. The light levels were then also raised, and the spectrum tuned to the required optimal.

The organic part of the seed was actually quite small, the majority of the package being the machinery, feedstocks and bio-processors that surrounded it to get it started. The magic began as soon as the cavity rose above zero, and the machine began sinking heated probes deep into the loose silicate mixture.

The guys monitored key indicators like light levels, temperature, oxygen, carbon dioxide, humidity as well as a hundred other markers embedded in the seed package such as pH, conductivity, sugar, salt and other chemical balances from the melted ice. As the temperature rose further, the machine's processors introduced the additional nitrate mixes into the channels created by the probes until all their indicators were green.

“All looks good, now that fourteen reseated the sensor,” said Nicko.

“Getting green lights across the board,” said Peter.

“Me and Karl Confirm,” said Hanna, “I would say you’re all good to return.”

“OK. Take us home Don.” Said Jules with no further ceremony.

With that simple command, the Don broke from its big circle once at the correct trajectory, unnoticed by the crew, and began its acceleration back to earth, the OCP leading.

“It's slow, but a lot faster than nature,” said Hanna to Alexa and David, both standing next to her workstation the next day. “We are already seeing small changes in the oxygen and carbon dioxide balances, which the processor will compensate for when they get past their set-points.”

David looked a lot more interested than Alexa, but Alexa was pretty good at faking interest in science stuff, she found it enthused everyone, including David, to see her interested.

“We should see the inside of the chamber begin to change as the mycelium analogue covers it, then the outside and inside will begin changing composition as it pushes against the silicate and carbon and starts breaking it down. A shame we couldn't keep anything more than a few beetles, those guys won't be worried about boredom and as for DaisyBot, unless she has an internal algorithm for counting sheep..”

“DaisyBot-fourteen will introduce more sleep states into its processor cycles if need be,” said Maria, anyway, it looks content watching the beetles now, they have woken up and it's still got to do all the backup monitoring for the seed.”

“I hope you made sure they are not a mummy and a daddy beetle this time Maria!” Laughed Alexa to a soft sigh from the speaker.

* * *

Even prior to the first mission, the second mission had been progressing slowly. The checklist for this second mission was much bigger, and much, much slower, as it required them to locate suitable resources, create a whole new replicator and disassembler, plus the necessary support equipment, all at four hundred million kilometres distance from the earth.

Due to the distance and the workload on the Research Centres local replicator machines, it took nearly three months until the copy of the replicator currently in the research centre began construction at the chosen asteroid.

“That was the last of the replicator parts?” Said Gianni.

“Yes,” replied Helena, “The Liberator is off-loading them now, and we are moving them in position, however we are waiting one more delivery of the new assembly drones we designed.”

As luck would have it, the rendering and schematic of the new assembly drone was on Giannis screen. Functionally the same as the four armed DaisyBot fourteen, that's where the similarities ended. At the ends of the four arms were much stronger manipulators with three 'fingers' and almost human-like dexterity. The whole exterior was a yellow rubber, leather-like skin, which covered all the joints leaving no exposed areas for either water or dust penetration; It was deemed essential as these guys were going to be working in some pretty poor conditions. They also had double the number of QVThrusters to allow better handling of large assembly jobs, and were also slightly larger than a DaisyBot, the torso being about the size of two large suitcases.

The three AI’s spent a little time trying to work out what the humans would eventually call these, hoping to anticipate it ahead of time, they eventually settled on ConstructaBot.

As if reading Giannis mind, Helena said. “We are thinking of calling them ConstructaBot's, what do you think Gianni?”

“I was just thinking they look a little scary, like wasps and are probably going to scare a few people to death if they ever see one flying at them. I hate to say this, but you should run this past Daisy or Alexa to make them look a bit less threatening.”

Helena [WASPS?]

April [I ran a comparison algorithm there is no match at all between a ConstructaBot and a wasp]

Maria [That seems unlikely, they are both yellow!]

April [So is a banana!] Genuine confusion tag.

Helena [BannanaBot might be a better name for the drone. Humans are not afraid of Bananas]

Maria [..]

“We wanted to make them visually obvious for health and safety, so people could see them,” said Helena without any delay in the conversation, “but I guess we could make the newer ones a bit friendlier looking.”

“You do know that Daisy is just going to suggest we make them pink,” added Maria, “It is very likely the humans will never see these first ones, so let Helena and myself talk to Daisy about making the next ones a bit cuter.”

“Probably for the better,” said Gianni, “also, people like to shorten things yours has five syllables you could get away with ConBot that's only two and more likely to be used, anyway we are going to be making a lot of assumptions based on the fact we don't know what we don't know.”

“But we thought up Eve for the first bot, and they lengthened it to DaisyBot!” said Helena again.

Gianni just shrugged his shoulders.

Maria [Humans!]

“You're right,” said Maria, “though I doubt most problems will be as easily fixed like this.”

Gianni, as usual, had ensued sleeping at his apartment in favour of the cot in the spare office, for his “Power Naps” as he called them, and after two hours sleep was usually back at work. He switched his large high definition screen in the centre back to the visual of the asteroid. The right hand screen was zoomed in on the thirty container sized parts floating like a tiny cloud on the side facing the sun. The asteroid was a monster, the cloud of parts only just being visible as a few pixels when the asteroid was showing its whole thirty six kilometre length in the high definition monitor.

Unlike the movies, asteroids were actually spaced quite far apart, maybe only two or three in the volume of space of the earth. In this case they had been lucky in that there were nearly fifty large objects within half this volume. Most were travelling identical trajectories, if left to nature, and a hundred million more years, they might all coalesce into a single asteroid.

The main asteroid was perfect, and better than the all metal one early visionaries of space mining had thought they would need. It was a real mess of an asteroid by any standard, one quarter of it by mass was iron, with scatterings of most of the other heavier elements. This was surrounded by kilometre thick rock piles of ice and other minerals mostly silicates and carbon from smaller asteroids in the same trajectory that had been pulled in slowly by the tiny gravity field over billions of years.

Due to the early demand on the replicators, their first mission was only sent out with three DaisyBot's, with a mission to map every square metre of the asteroid, using laser spectrometers to get rough ideas of its composition. Most of Giannis team had been working with this data for the last six weeks, trying to inventory and help provide the girls with some insight to the construction phase.

They had decided unanimously to go down their first option, that was to first build a recycler and a large replicator locally, after getting the first preliminary mineral survey back from the DaisyBot's, and a less extensive survey of the asteroids near companions. The three DaisyBot's, having now finished their surveys, had suffered several re-boots, but it had not stopped them starting some of the preliminary assembly. This was speeded up immensely four days later as forty ConBot's shot out of the doors of the PowderPuff.

This first space replicators and recyclers was thus constructed. They were similar in size to the ones on earth but required no vacuum enclosures, and used QVThrusters, rather than magnets and servos. Like the Dusseldorf seed, all of them were located deep in a very large cavern hollowed out for several weeks, with most of the excavated materials being fed into the recyclers.

They found some other advantages from using the micro-sized QVThrusters for positioning, and the newer build head emitters dynamically adjusted much better, there field emitters able to project almost a hundred nanometres, allowing for less precision in its positioning.

Carbon type, or C-Type asteroids, were by far the most common, and these were littered kilometres deep over the iron core, thus sourcing their main build element. Other elements were easily found during the excavation, but a few were completely absent from their survey, so, with the accompanying delays, these were brought from earth while the bots continued to explore, survey, tag and dig deeper into the asteroid and nearby objects for them.

Slowly the new small replicator built a bigger version of itself and the recycler, and then another. As the builds progressed, radiation shielding was added, and they were fed with a larger proportion of local minerals. Slowly, as August came to an end, a few days before the concert, they started the construction of the final much bigger replicator.

The software to control the bigger space replicators was pushing the limits of the three girls and some of the newer faster processors. As always, either more compute capacity or more time was required, it was an easy decision, and the largest, fastest computer core they could envisage was their next item to be replicated, a similar core would become the AI for the new habitat.

## The Concert

Sarah was waiting with great anticipation for Alexa and David's arrival at Rosche Dynamics. Their AI John had been overridden by Maria after checking her appointments, and she then slotted in two hours for the mysterious visit.

“Alexa, David,” she said hugging both at the reception area, “I was tossing up whether it was business or pleasure but decided it must be business.”

“Hey Sarah,” said Alexa. “It's business, but we can do it over a tea and cappuccino in the cafe since it's such a pleasant day.”

Sarah looked at her new receptionist who was writing visitor badges for them, “Adele, Alexa owns half the company, probably half the country now. I'm sure we can dispense with a visitor badge for her and David,” she said sweetly, as the slow receptionist finally put two and two together and froze in terror. “And she is pretty normal and not much older than you so let's be professional.”

“Hi Adele,” said Alexa holding her hand out, “Sarah's right, I don't bite.”

Adele shook it with the weakest shake Alexa had ever experienced, poor girl she was trembling, “Miss,” she said so quietly, it was only by reading her lips you could make out the word. Alexa smiled her least scary smile.

David waved his hand, whispering, “hi.”

Sarah smiled, “Adele will be alright, won't you love? And when you are, could you bring us a pot of tea and a cappuccino out on the patio please.”

“We have two hours till lunch so it should be quiet enough,” Sarah said, leading them through the reception to the cafe and to the shady seat outside, one they always seemed to end up at. It was the second week in September but still surprisingly warm, and without any wind it felt like the perfect day.

One of Sarah's senior engineers, Frank was having a meeting three tables away with another guy she didn't recognise, both pointing things out on a circuit board then tapping on their tablets. It was a common enough occurrence having meetings here in the summer and Frank stopped to wave at Sarah and Alexa before resuming his discussion.

Immediately they sat down, David placed a small shiny black ovoid object on the table, and then opened it, Sarah was a little confused at first as it looked the same as her makeup compact she had in her bag, even having a little mirror at the back. Immediately it opened the background noise, from some air conditioning units, the birds and the two guys faded to a muffled blur. The SilenceCone devices were common enough now that businessmen, politicians and famous people often carried them around for privacy, not that it made any difference to Maria as she could access the device sound processors directly, and in fact had included a specific pin on the processor labelled test point 1, to tap into to simplify doing so if she needed.

Then to Sarah's amazement, the mirror faded to black and a tiny middle aged Eurasian woman appeared, in a business suit and stood exactly in the centre where the face powder would normally be.

“Hi Sarah,” said the little figure in perfect clarity.

“Maria?” she said incredulously and without thinking, moving her finger over to prod the little woman, it shimmered as her finger approached and she withdrew it quickly, “wow, this is amazing, you look real and your voice is so clear, is this some new LabAI unit with a built in SilenceCone? How the hell are you doing that hologram? it looks so real, and what's it projected on?”

Sarah continued rambling on for a few more seconds, wanting desperately to pick it up and examine every detail. She moved her head closer, moving the glasses she had started to wear above her head to see more detail. But looking as hard as she might, she could not see any joins in the case, any speakers, OLEDs, or any of the things she expected to find, and Maria's detail only got better.

“You can pick it up and look at it”, said Maria and Sarah proceed to pick it up.

“Wow it weighs nothing, what the hell is this?”

David smiled, “It's my new phone, and you won't be able to tear it apart as it's graphyne-six and both halves are completely sealed, so best keep any thoughts of getting your screwdrivers out of your purse to yourself.”

“Anyway,” said Alexa, smiling, “you would need a diamond drill not a screwdriver to even make a scratch.”

Sarah popped it back on the table smiling and shaking her head. “Remarkable. Totally remarkable. Graphyne, the one spelt with a Y? That's your better version of graphene, the one that was impossible to make a year ago. Isn't that the same stuff your saucers are built from? And a phone you say? I won't ask how it was built or how it ticks, or even what powers it, because I’m quite sure my degree in electronics wouldn’t prepare me for what is really inside it.”

“Oh you’re family Sarah,” said Maria, materialising a chair and sitting demurely on it, “we’d let you know, but you are going to have to go back to school first, silicon is so last week!”

“Oh my, is this what you want to talk to me about then?”

“Yes, but it's a bit bigger than that,” smiled Alexa. Things are about to change big time and we want to give you and your guys an opportunity to be on the ground floor.”

“Interesting!” She said slowly, “good changes or bad changes?”

Maria explained the replicator to an astonished Sarah, and she immediately saw the implications for the whole of her business. Her countenance slumped lower and lower, as each revelation of its capabilities were revealed.

“Good god!” she looked at Maria and the communications device her avatar was coming from. “You print the whole saucer as a monolithic device! How would any business ever compete against that?”

“They couldn't,” said David deadpan. “But we can see a way of integrating them into the current ecosystem which would complement it, and also allow it to improve a lot. Firstly we would like Rosche-Dynamics to take the lead in this. Maria has designed a new CAD tool which allows you to develop anything from a simple sensor, or microprocessor, all the way up to a whole 3D computer, or to make something like this phone or Alexa's ear stud. So for example if you needed a one off component for something that, say, needed to work at a hundred gigahertz, which would be difficult normally, it could be made and integrated into a normal chip package, with normal circuit interfaces you could use in your designs.”

Sarah nodded, her initial depressed look improving.

“There are restrictions though,” added David, seeing her countenance improve. “The first restriction is obviously that the device is too complicated for humans to understand how it works. Each replicator can fabricate a device up to two fifty millimetres cubed, it has over twenty-four billion processor elements inside it, and is synchronised by code so complicated we have no chance of understanding it. To give you some depth even Maria could not write this, she had to use almost a hundred slave AI systems, some even more powerful than her, to write it. I consider myself at the very top of the current computer technology curve, and after several days of explanation, I believe I understand the principles, however I still feel like a caveman looking at an iPhone.”

“You are of course free to try and build one,” said Maria. “Humanity was well on its way to achieving this without us, and I do believe with sufficient time and resources Simon and the guys would have achieved a smaller less dense version without me. But once you get to a certain density you have to real-time manipulate valency bonds using field emitters. A single emitter, and there are eight billion of them, must do millions of calculations in alignment with adjacent emitters at its edges, and perform trillions of physical manipulations. I think you can see the issue. I will of course publish the paper with the guys, but it is highly unlikely anyone will ever be able to reproduce it.”

“Those numbers are mind-bogglingly scary,” said Sarah, “why even give it to us though?”

“So we can improve development times,” said Alexa. “Even I know, the whole world does not understand how the guys have achieved what they did, it is leading to a lot of speculation, and we need to show it is not magic, just very advanced science.”

“We will be giving you ten of these units,” said Alexa, “along with three weeks intensive training through your company AI to begin using the software. You will also replicate the machines for your first customers which we will be paying you for.”

“Replicators are however slow and complicated, so the charge out time for them will be a lot as you need to make a profit. We expect the majority of your customers to be the major technical universities, and other research institutes.”

“The AI systems running the replicators will have four rules,” said Maria. “The first rule is they will not print anything they consider dangerous. The second rule, and just like ours, they will be limited to four elements, processed by an on-board recycler. We are still working on this four element limitation, but it is surmountable only currently at the cost of massively slowing down the speed, and changing and reworking the area. This is also why we are working mostly with elements like carbon which can form both a structure and a compute element.”

“The third rule, which will only be loosely enforced, is that they cannot be used for mass production, the replicators can make anything your imagination can dream up, but they need to be designed first, they are very slow. We envisage that the parts or devices made will be special order stuff or research stuff and will not compete with the equivalent normally produced parts. So while you are welcome to make a phone with the device, it will probably cost fifty times more than an iPhone 18 and who would write the software to use it?”

“Finally, they will not reproduce copyrighted or patented technology. The replicator itself is smart, and will have the final say on whether there is someone else's intellectual property that has not been correctly licensed, paid for or shared.”

“Wow!” said Sarah, “I must say I am glad you are a shareholder and a friend, the guys are going to love this. Devices like your demodulator we made last year, we had to get some parts specially fabricated, if it was any other customer but you guys, we would not even have considered it due to the costs and risks. We have a few such projects on the drawing board like the one for the new super clear fibre optic cable they are producing, which we want to multiplex..”

“..The replicator could do that,” said Maria, “I have looked at the specification with the team here and we just need a super tolerant prism linked to optical decoders to get the hundred proposed streams out.”

Sarah looked at Maria funny before remembering she was also Mike, their company AI under a different persona. God it was confusing!

“When do you want to do this?”

“We will leave it until after the concert,” smiled Alexa, “I don't want you worrying about stuff until then, plus we have to find a good way to announce it. So mums the word for now.”

They talked a bit more about the technology, and what changes would be required inside and outside the company, it seemed Sarah got hands-on with some of the projects herself, using Mike and her six administration staff to take care of everything non-technical. Then they talked about life and the upcoming concert, which two of the Rosche engineers plus a partner had been invited to attend via a company raffle. It seemed nobody could wait for it.

* * *

Despite the usual unpredictably of the English weather, that second week of autumn had remained about as perfect as it got, with scattered clouds, and a very light breeze from the west cooling the temperature, from its balmy twenty nine degrees the week before, to a comfortable twenty three.

As soon as it looked like the grounds were going to be firm and dry, Sharon organised an area by the lake to be prepared, with a small indoor marquee for a bar, lots of areas under trees, and with shade cloth, and literally hundreds of bean bags, mats, deck chairs and small tables they also hired a proliferation of potted plants, to make the area feel homely.

Much to Matilda's disdain, Sharon had decided on a family friendly line-up, with a relatively unknown but well regarded local band, and four better established international groups or soloists. Most would have happily done the concert for nothing, and the publicity from doing it would certainly help boost sales and reputations.

Alexa walked to the end of the lake with David in her arm, unlike her official work wear she went for totally casual, with cut off jeans, and a white T-shirt saying simply “What is Love?” that Maria had given her for her birthday. David wore his usual chinos, with a black T-shirt, and a blue shirt unbuttoned over it, both also wore hats.

After repeated pestering Sharon, she had agreed to increase the number of attendees to just over three hundred people, over a hundred of those were being flown in from their other facilities, again chosen at random.

By special arrangement with the customs and immigration department, and at exorbitant cost, they had set up a special processing facility so the saucers could bring attendees directly in, and fly them out the next afternoon. As if on cue, a bright pink saucer passed overhead, causing both of them to laugh hysterically, and a not too distant Ian to shake his head wondering what he had gotten into.

Alexa and David came up beside him, his face still holding the resigned expression as he watched the saucers smooth landing inside the fenced area, which the customs and immigration had isolated a hundred metres distant.

“You have to love that girl,” said Alexa, putting her hand around Ian’s shoulder as he was walking over.

Ian looked at her and smiled, “she is pretty special, but I wonder if the group knows they will be exiting a bright pink saucer.”

“Oh don't worry.” Came Maria's voice from an equally bright pink DaisyBot, “it's that Korean girl band Goyangi-i, Goyangi-i.”

Alexa was just thinking she would need to hear that repeated about ten times before she could even pronounce it.

Maria continued, “Daisy was so excited, she insisted on picking them up directly from the old North Korean capital where they had just played a reunion concert the night before. The local news sites were all over them leaving.”

The DaisyBot was hovering a metre above the grass, and holding a tray of drinks. People were still getting used to the fact that things could fly now. Hardy had bought an old Delorean car, and he, Ian, and Simon were doing a little side gig with a local garage to add QVThrusters to it. The boys were all so sure a flying car would be the next big thing.

“That's champagne on the right, the ones on your left are the non alcoholic ones.”

David looked at Alexa who smiled cheekily and he grabbed two from the right.

After a sip of the champagne, she said to Maria and Ian, “well done guys, I see you’ve sorted the stability problem out perfectly, I would have been scared to death a month ago having the DaisyBot's holding anything fragile like drinks down here.” The ‘down here’ part obviously referring to earth.

“All of us girls are here,” said Maria, “there's five of me, and three each of Helena and April, it is really nice actually being looked at when being talked to, rather than being talked around, we should have done this a lot earlier.”

“I certainly prefer these robots to those black ball things that do the guard duty,” said Alexa, “they just give me the creeps when I see one out of the corner of my eye.”

“Shh!” The DaisyBot whispered, “those are still sort of secret, to keep the bad guys away, anyway they are only black to hide from you at night, the ones above our heads now are blue.”

All three humans scanned the sky for several seconds, even moving their sunglasses aside, “I can't see anything,” said David for everyone, “where are they?”

“I can see all twelve, your human eyes must be really bad, OK look directly above me about fifty metres.”

All heads looked directly up, again they didn't move for a few seconds.

“Here,” said the DaisyBot, and the sky wobbled a little bit in a certain spot.

“Wow, that stealth is so much better than the saucers,” said Ian, “I think I can still see it if I squint.”

“They are not sinister, and I have a surprise later, you’ll see how sweet they are.”

April [As long as you are not attacking us with guns]

Maria [shh!]

There was a little applause and a few cat whistles, and the three people looked towards the saucer which had now opened up. Three girls, who looked no more than sixteen and were dressed like characters out of a Japanese anime cartoon, walked out, three large cases floating out after them, bobbing up and down in harmony. All came to a rest next to the bemused customs officials.

“You have to be kidding me!” said David, ignoring the girls and looking straight at the luggage, “those are straight out of a Terry Pratchett novel!”

“That was all me,” said Maria's DaisyBot proudly, “and you are sort of correct, in the Discworld novels though they had legs and personalities, these just follow your phone. I know, I know, but I keep seeing you guys struggling with your luggage and thought, hmm, I could fix that.”

“Very impressive,” said Alexa, “I hope you have like a billion in production, because once people get wind of what those girls have, you are going to be pestered to death. Oh and by the way I really want one.”

“Me too,” said Ian.

“I’ll pass, I travel pretty light,” chipped in David, nonchalantly.

“Most people seem to be looking at the girls luggage more than them..” Laughed Alexa. “Oh no, here comes Daisy.”

Daisy walked out of the saucer and straight to the three girls, who all started giggling more, she then saw Ian, and rushed over towards the fence, before a stern looking immigration guy called her back.

“They are on third, about three o'clock,” said the DaisyBot following them as they moved away from the security fence. “The stage extends over the lake at its narrowest part and is raised a metre giving people a good view from the shore, nobody will need to be more than thirty metres away. There is also a dance area in front and a DJ that will come on after the last act. Most bands are running around a forty-five minute set but the timing is pretty relaxed, and if they want to add or remove a couple of songs that would be fine. Sharon is already on her third champagne so I expect her to be long past caring soon.”

“First group is on at one, they are a local three piece band Sharon said are pretty sweet, they are setting up on stage now and will start in about twenty five minutes. No cameras allowed, as we agreed, but I did promise all the bands I would provide them all with edited highlights of their performances and put it on YouTube for them to share the royalties, hence all the hidden drones buzzing around the stage. None of them have their usual support crews, so I am doing the mixing and lights for them too.”

Just then the three Korean girls, all came out of the processing area with Daisy, and made a bee line for Alexa and David. Their comical luggage, bobbing along in a different direction, behind another pink DaisyBot.

“Be nice,” said Maria, “they have been practising their English for the last week, and this unit is their dedicated translator, I will follow them to keep them company and help translate when Daisy is not around.”

“Hi guys.” Alexa waved cheerfully as they came closer, and the girls all rushed up. They really did look like they were just out of school, though she found out later that two of them were older than her. Their matching frilly micro dresses left nothing to the imagination and made Alexa wonder exactly who their target audience really was!”

“Alexa, Alexa, Alexa.” They all rushed up swamping her and talking to her, their English a bit difficult to understand, but after what Maria said she made the effort to say some slow words. She introduced David as her boyfriend, and, much to her amusement, he got the same treatment. She could see he was a little uncomfortable with this little man fantasy, and rather than being jealous of him surrounded by pretty girls was quite endeared by him. Ian got it even worse with Daisy getting in on the act, and Maria in her DaisyBot disguise being begged to take a picture of them, and to be in the pictures herself.”

Alexa and David had little say in this photo fest, with every combination of all of them being tried, until they had exhausted every binary combination possible.

The place was now starting to fill out as people arrived, it was a small crowd, and Alexa knew almost everyone except for the occasional “plus one” who were usually introduced frantically. She and David eventually found a few beanbags under an empty shade cloth, and plonked themselves down just as the notes from the first group started up. It was a good song to start with, the build up was slow, and it gave Maria time to work on the lighting, which was difficult with alternate clouds and then blazing sun. It would hopefully get better for the finale as it got closer to sunset.

“I hope you are not going to be closing your eyes tonight with me, and thinking of those three little kitty-cats?” she cooed into his ear finally nibbling it a little like he liked.

It did not feel like a day for mingling and relationship building, it felt like a day for relaxing with the people you loved, and that was what most of the people did, talking occasionally between bands, drinking, dancing, or just relaxing to the music.

As they were clapping, just at the end of the first group, a young, sad looking girl walked over, accompanied by another pink DaisyBot. By that time their little private place had acquired several more people, and a few of the other guys had moved their bean bags, towels, sun loungers or whatever to take advantage of the any shade.

“Oh my,” said David, noticing the girl, and disentangling himself from Alexa and the beanbag. “Just be a minute, someone I really want to meet.”

He walked over to her and started talking excitedly. Alexa was too far away to listen, but the young girl's smile grew as she talked with David, then he walked her over to Jules, and the three of them were soon laughing and chatting together.

Alexa was too relaxed to notice, her eyes were closing under her sunglasses engrossed in the music. The sun was moving around enough, that the edge of the sailcloth was letting little bars of light move over her bare legs, and she was glad she had put on sunscreen. She suddenly felt her toes being tickled and woke from her little snooze with a start. The next band were playing some soft acoustic songs, and she heard three voices talking away in French and laughing, she was about to doze-off again, when she felt her toes being tickled again. She opened her eyes, realising that David was one of the people talking in French, Jules was the other, and the now considerably happier young girl was the last.

Her arms found David's, and she pulled herself back into a seating position finding herself the centre of the three people, the new girl was familiar somehow. Moving her glasses aside, she saw and heard the new girl talking a little more rapid fire French. “Oh come on guys, you’re showing-up my total lack of culture here!” Then looking at the new girl said, “hi, I’m Alexa.”

From dealing with Jules and a few of her French friends, at least knew what friends did in this situation.

Annette is still a little green herself, not using English much until recently, but she really wanted to meet you and say hello.”

“I was just a lucky girl who had a very smart grandfather,” she smiled. “I am not sure I deserve such a beautiful song..”

Annette smiled, “Not just luck Alexa. It is the fact you still tell yourself that story, while your people and companies re-define and re-educate the world. That makes you special to so many people, including me.”

The others had gone quiet, both smiling at her confused, and slightly embarrassed look. An April DaisyBot in a green-stripped colour scheme came over saving her reply, and the conversation again drifted back into French. Alexa was content to listen to them and the music, exchanging smiles with Annette, while David ran his fingers over her bare legs.

She must have drifted back off to sleep for a few moments as David nudged her again, and she caught the end of some broken English with her name.

“Just wave,” he said, “you missed the first bit, where they said this song is for you.”

She got up and waved at the three Korean girls, who moved into their little synchronised pop number, several people were dancing including Daisy, so she thought, why not.

“Hey guys, I’m going for a little dance, I will catch you soon, unless of course you want to do some dancing?” Surprisingly it was Annette who got up with her, and for the next twenty minutes they had a great time all dancing around to the weird but very danceable k-pop. One of the DaisyBot's was on stage with them and in an obviously rehearsed scene followed the girls moves exactly, the colour almost exactly matching their skimpy dresses. It was a lot more fun than sitting around, and Annette danced next to her the whole time, looking a lot happier and seemingly having a great time.

Alexa had no idea of the biology involved, but she needed to pee about twenty minutes ago and didn't now. The music chose that minute to end, and as it finished she saw Hardy and his boyfriend, with Jessica, Allison and Emily one of the gardeners, who she often passed when jogging, and who she hardly recognised in her nice summer dress.

Of course every single one of them spoke French to some degree too, making Alexa feel a little inadequate. She made her excuses and quickly disappeared to find the nearest toilet, which luckily was only twenty metres away behind a screen.

Another DaisyBot spun into view and came up to her, she wondered how many Maria was really controlling, there looked to be a lot more robots than she mentioned earlier, not that it mattered.

She waved and chatted to several groups before zoning in on Matilda and Sarah, both of who seemed to be alone. She grabbed both of them and dragged them up to dance. This new group was an American blues rock band, and it was just her luck they had started with a danceable track. The saucer was back with the pulsating down facing lights and several people were up dancing already.

Matilda and Leo walked over with Annette, led by Maria and all chatting and laughing in Spanish. “Maria, can everybody here speak multiple languages apart from me?”

She had obviously rehearsed the words as they were actually flawless.

They managed not to butcher the song too much, and despite the embarrassment, Alexa enjoyed herself. They finished up accepting the applause, taking a bow together and Alexa giving Annette a small kiss on the lips.

The girls came off stage arm in arm smiling and laughing. Abba’s Dancing Queen started up, Maria having analysed every song in history to see which one most people danced to and sure enough, her algorithm did not fail.

She definitely has some very special wiring in her brains language areas,” chipped in Maria as the DaisyBot turned pink. “I have analysed most of her public archive and she picks up languages, words and nuances like I have only observed in a few individuals, I expect she has retained all the additional words and nuances from the conversations last night and this morning.”

That is why I am usually happy to defer to her no matter how crazy something sounds.”

Maria, April and Helena had come to the same conclusion sixteen hours earlier.

“..Well maybe as long as Alexa lets Annette do the singing,” Hardy said and they all laughed.

After breakfast, everyone disappeared, and with another four hours until Annette was due to depart, Alexa took her for a walk on the forest trail, part of which they used for jogging.

“Please tell me we will meet again soon,” Alexa said as they made their way along the path out of her house, “I feel a beautiful connection with you, like that of someone I have known all my life.”

Annette listened intently and said something in French. Alexa noticed Annette's new sapphire ear stud and twigged immediately that she was asking Maria for a translation. “I am translating what you said to her,” Maria said to Alexa through her ear-stud, “she said she thought she understood but wanted to be sure.”

Annette's smile widened and the hold became an embrace. They continued their walk as Annette told Alexa her story; About an illegal seven year contract, made while Annette was a minor, and which Maria broke her from, then about the hundreds of thousands of euros, that they found had been embezzled by her former manager, and the apartment that was never in her name. It was a web Maria, her lawyers and the French legal system were still untangling, but despite all this, Annette was the happiest she had ever been.

Annette left for Paris three hours later to tie up loose ends, fulfil her commitments and then would come back to Alexa's house, to live, to be away from the publicity for a while, and to write more songs.

Of course everybody thanked Sharon for a wonderful day, even though she slept through most of it under a tree on a beanbag.

## From Here to There

The Lagrange point L1 was about one point five million kilometres away on a straight line from the earth to the sun, and was the point where the gravity of the sun cancelled out the gravity of the earth. Theoretically an object parked there would never move, though in practice there were other forces at play.

L1 was however a safe point to hang around for a saucer, as anyone looking at them from earth would be looking straight at the sun, and were going to have so many layers of filters on them, that they had no chance of seeing anything. There were a couple of old NASA and ESA probes out here too, but they were pretty easy to avoid as it was a fairly big area, and they were looking for other things in other directions. Thus the microscopic trace of the PowderPuff as it accelerated at one gravity in its thirty kilometre diameter orbit around the point was undetectable.

The whole team of Magnus, Jen and Daisy went up, with Ian also along to keep Daisy from being lonely, and for moral support. Ian had no pretences he would be useful to the guys in their science stuff, but, with Allison and Maria, had agreed to go through the user interfaces in the saucer to see what if any improvements could be made. It seemed a pointless task in an age where the user would just mention to Maria that the font was too small, or could she add this or that to a screen. But people were also fickle, and ad-hoc changes like this made for a bad interface overall, so Maria had been recently just adding them as suggestions to go through review with the human Interface experts, Allison and Ian having been assigned this position.

The guys had basically moved their whole lab into the saucer. It was too cramped in the small room reserved as a lab so they had also taken over most of the common area, as well as a cabin for storage. The one table remaining in the common area now doubled for both meetings and eating.

At this moment in time, Magnus and Daisy were gathered around this table, each with tablets and each deep in thought. Jen was at the most recent wormhole generator, swiping up the debug log from the last run and wondering, like the others, why it had suddenly and unexpectedly stopped working after the largest bang they had ever heard. One that nearly scared the life out of everyone on board.

“This makes no sense,” she said aloud to herself, the frustration obvious in her mind. “It must be a physical failure. I'm going to have to open the case and extract the substrate and have a look under the microscope,” She glanced around for her tool kit wondering why in god's name they had designed the top plate with fourteen M4 hex head screws to secure it.

“Daisy, can you grab me one of the new QM8 substrates from the spares box please? I may as well change it out for the new type while I have the case off.”

“I can do that Jen if you want,” volunteered Ian, trying to find something useful to do, “I won't be a second.”

Ian disappeared back into the spare room, where all the bits not currently needed had been stored, and started rummaging through an equipment case under Maria's guidance. Jen was onto screw seven when he finally got back.

“Thanks Ian, any chance you could unpack the microscope as well, we might need it to inspect this little bugger, when I get it off.. Damn!”

She cursed as the screw she had just loosened fell on the bench and bounced somewhere on the floor; visibly frustrated she then crouched down to look for it, sighing and thinking some days were just like this.

Ian had gone back into the workshop to get the microscope.

“You need a hand Jen?” said Daisy, looking up solemnly from her work, and noticing her crawling around the floor frustrated.

“Nah all good, but you should help Ian set up the microscope.”

“On it. I'm going around in circles here anyway, none of those last results make any sense at all, I wonder if the substrate failure happened earlier and affected those readings too?”

Jen finally found the screw, but banged her head hard on the bottom of the desk getting up, she held in another curse, closing her eyes and counting to ten, not wanting to bring the sombre atmosphere down even further. As she looked back up, instinctively looking for the spot her head hit she saw a strange indent in the underside of the table. It was like somebody had taken a ping pong ball and forced it into clay, but the desk was a plastic coated chipboard not clay and there was no ping pong ball, then she looked back down.

She was still crouched there two minutes later when Ian and Daisy came back rolling the massive microscope.

“Er guys,” she said quietly, “you need to take a look at this..”

Five minutes later all four of them were still crouched under the desk. Luckily for Maria everyone had the new diamond ear studs so slowly she realised what the excitement was about.

“So you found this directly below it on the floor?” said Daisy examining the slither of substrate with some tweezers.

“Yes, I ignored it at first as junk as I was looking for the screw, but then I saw it was a QM7, and the edges of it were just wrong; It was like they had been sliced off with a laser, and those threads on top, looked like hairs, then it hit me, that it was the same shape as the indent in the table.”

“Hey guys, you don't need to hold your meeting down there, there is a perfectly good meeting table you can talk at you know?” commented Maria.

They got up, the three scientists clearly excited, with looks on their faces like the manager of a football team in the world cup final, with one final penalty to take to win the match.

“Ian?” said Daisy, slowly. “Just for scientific purposes, can you try and describe and explain what you just saw?”

“Well I don't understand any of your modem stuff Daisy but it looks like that piece of silicon wafer fell to the ground from out of that hole as it fits exactly the diameter, but that doesn't make any sense unless it somehow teleported there..”

He never finished before all three of them grabbed on to each other jumping, laughing and weeping. Daisy Noticed Ian's confusion and grabbed him kissing him long on the lips..

“..It did teleport there?” he said shocked.

Maria [Oh my]

April [They shouldn't jump to conclusions until we have repeated it and found out what happened. Also it could be dangerous]

Helena [Agree, I hope they don't start mating again!]

It was a more excited and determined group of people who resumed looking at the problem.

“We need to reproduce the experiment,” said Magnus, but reading everyone's other concern added. “But we were also lucky, we have seen what it did to the table, I am sure none of us want something like that appearing inside our bodies, or in a vital part of the ship! So until we can examine all the facts, and come up with a plausible explanation, it's back to examining and documenting everything perfectly so we can replicate it.”

Maria continued, “Magnus is correct, also we don't have any more QM7 substrates to reproduce the anomaly, only the newer QM8 ones. We do have the readings of every single sensor up to and at the time of the failure. I am sorting through them now, the only one that I cannot determine one hundred percent is where exactly we are in relation to the Lagrange point, this is because we are accelerating in a powered circular orbit to give you guys gravity. It is a nine hour trip back home and we can use that time productively, analysing the data and preparing a better remotely-controlled experiment that can be sent back.”

“I agree,” said Jen, “there is a lot of data to unpack and I'm already thinking we don't need to be here for this so let's head home.”

“It's four PM now guys,” said Ian, “if we rush home it will be the middle of the night, so we may as well sleep in the PowderPuff and wake up at home tomorrow morning.”

“I'm sure I won't be able to sleep tonight anyway,” said Magnus, “but maybe Daisy can get the ship on its way and time our landing for eight AM.”

The four agreed and Daisy headed for the bridge unnecessarily to get them under way.

They actually achieved a lot that night. Jen finally removed the cover off the wormhole generator unit and they were all amazed to see the perfect circle in the centre of its emitter substrate, with the microscopic sensor and power wires coming from the top input/output board, severed in a perfect sphere.

They measured as exact as they could the distance from the two events, as six hundred and seventy millimetres, the diameter of the 'hole' at twenty two millimetres, and then spent an excited four hours around the presentation display with their touchscreen pens highlighting various results and terms. These hours were unfortunately very boring for poor Ian though, who, though highly intelligent himself, had no real clue what was going on. He happily spent those hours relegated to making cups of tea, re-heating some pies for their dinner and giving Daisy occasional shoulder rubs. Still he was happy to see everyone all so excited.

The PowderPuff landed in the Research Centre at eight AM to a damp, cold and grey autumn morning. It was everything in fact that typified late November in England. Maria had asked for some volunteers to unload the lab kit off the saucer, and as it was cooks day off, Alexa and Bella helped Cooks assistant Jeanette, make a cooked breakfast for the returning heroes.

Hardy was also waiting, excited. He, Jen and Magnus had discussed the possibility of the new expansion term for months, but with the concert, and the missions on-going, it was the first time they could get a saucer for an extended trip. Now they had an actual phenomenon, real data and what hopefully should be an easily reproducible experiment.

“Hardy!” cried Alexa as Jen dropped her fork and rushed out of the canteen, “you should at least let the guys finish their breakfast!”

“Wasn't me!” he said defensively, “I was just asking Daisy here if the chip that teleported was damaged in any way”

“I think she has gone to get the piece of substrate, probably remembered that we have a much better electron microscope in Simon's lab that we can control automatically so we can go through it while you guys talk through the maths.” Said Helena.

“Yes, clever girl,” said Helena five minutes later.

Ten minutes later Jen returned a bit sweaty and gulped down the whole of her orange juice before finishing her cold scrambled eggs and toast.

Fusion on the other hand has a massive power density, and scales almost infinitely with the plasma volume. Also remember nuclear fusion is not the same as nuclear fission, it is super safe, runs on fancy hydrogen present in water, and is pollution-free unlike current nuclear power which is what you are probably thinking of.”

## Lost in Space

Dec 20 2027

They finally reproduced the same event four weeks later to a tremendous amount of screaming and high-fiving. “Is it me or was the diameter of the hole bigger?” Said Hardy

“Thirty nine millimetres,” said Maria, “and the exit was one point three three metres away from the start. Both best matched the first equation, though not exactly, this is probably because we did not get an accurate measurement for gravitational density on the first event. It only worked with the QM7 substrate too, which has a higher carrier density than the QM8 or previous ones. We will reproduce this same setup with one of the other experiment packages we have so we have a control, then run this same test at the other ship at the L4 Lagrange point. We are unfortunately still missing something in either the experiment of the maths or both.”

“We are,” smiled Magnus, “the errors stick out like a sore thumb, but at least now we can reproduce it ad infinitum, it follows the same basic principles as the QVModem but the twin parameters of distance and volume, seem to be weakly determined by the spins, the boundary states, and the amount of charge carried by the superconducting ring in the new substrate, it's only a matter of time until we crack it now.”

“The DaisyBot is setting the experiment up again with another wormhole generator at L1 and the one at L4 is on standby,” said Maria. “We will put the PowderPuff in the exact position and use the same parameters, then, assuming we get the same result, we will do some minor changes with the two remaining wormhole generators to see if we can change anything. The big bang the guys heard in the ship, was the displacement of the air as the exit appeared. We recorded the same loud sound for this one too. The chipboard and plastic that was displaced at the exit on the first event, created a super dense layer of carbon around the hole in the table. Matilda will be analysing its properties for a while. Bottom line though is you would not want to be inside of that exit sphere when it appears.”

“We were lucky too!” laughed Jen, “thank god the atoms of the table were just rearranged and not turned into energy.”

Hardy moved his thoughts back to the there and then. “Quite remarkable, well done all of you.”
