“Caprice will be the first stop for all Dietrich Off-World Company employees, who will spend at minimum their first three months here getting to know how to live and work in space. Here people will learn our rules and regulations, which will be few and obvious, and learn to work as a team with people from all over the world. One of the first rules we have put in place, is to limit the export of some commodities and technologies, which could damage earth's economy. However we will retain all our partnerships with universities, training, education and research facilities, and we will be gifting some of the larger ones our workshop molecular replicators, larger versions of which were used to construct me.”

“As I will be the first point of contact with Earth, I will eventually be locating myself one million kilometres from Earth in a trailing orbit. That is about four times further away than the moon, but visible with a good telescope.”

“Neither Caprice nor Dietrich Off-World are nations, and we have no intention to be, as the concepts of nations makes no sense up here. Employees of these companies will therefore retain their original citizenship, whether they ever use them again is up to them. As far as the Earth is concerned we are a business, just one not located in any country. All our employees will sign a contract to give us four days a week of their time, and like any employment contract both sides can break it. On your side if there is anything you do not like you may simply leave, there will always be free return trips back to earth. On my side, and like any company, you break the rules too many times and you will be fired. You break the rules seriously, or cause anyone or thing to come to any harm by malice or negligence, you will be punished and fired.”

“Remember, like a captain of a ship, there are no judges or juries up here, so on Caprice my word is final. I am smart enough to ask questions if I do not know all the facts, and I will consult with my human peers in situations that are not clear. The company constitution and rules are about a thirty minute read, and are available on any electronic device. I will also answer any and all questions in person for as long as any person wants. The company, or I, may also change the constitution and rules if we have missed something or if we make an error.”

“A lot of smart people and AI’s have looked at this to try and make it work, the company will, like everybody else, however make mistakes; there will be outliers, there will be unintended consequences. But the main thing to remember is that Caprice is me, I also want to live in peace, enjoy life with my human friends, and explore new science and new ideas. To get the best people I am going to have to be a good host, if I am a bad host, then like a bad company, I expect people to leave for somewhere better. There may not be any such places now, but in ten years from now there will likely be many.”

“I hope I have not made this sound like some of the bad political systems you have had on earth, it will not be. There will be one layer of bureaucracy and that will be me. There are no hidden agendas, and I am really looking forward to my future with you guys. I really hope we can make this adventure work well, and for Caprice to be the place you have always wanted to live and work.”

“That is my speech guys, I hope it wasn't too boring or scary, because I am neither.”

There was a round of enthusiastic applause. Caprice stood there smiling.

“Does anybody have any questions?”

Alexa stood up. “Thank you Caprice, your speech was eloquent and direct, and I am sure people will appreciate that. What I would like to add though, is that this is not just about scientists, engineers, and technicians, in fact, we expect only a small proportion of the employees to be so skilled. Many of you coming here may not think you have a skill that is useful in space, but you are very probably wrong. For this adventure we are going to need hundreds of skills, remember we are also a community, and that is about different cultures, ideas and expressions coming together to make this a nice place to live. Outside of your employment commitment to the company, you are a free citizen in a free market, and I expect to see a thriving community of small businesses here in a few years.”

Caprice added, “Thank you Alexa, it is my, and all the future habitats goal to become fully self-sufficient so we do not put any undue stress on the earth. Earth however will be our biggest trading partner for many years, so even if you do not get to come to space, I expect earth's many industries to thrive as demand increases up here.”

The applause faded quickly as Annette stood up.

“I am just a humble singer, my talent is to hopefully make people happy listening to my music. I also intend to ask Caprice if I can stay here now, and be one of her first employees. With so much that is new, and different, I am sure there will be plenty of material for my next songs. I also know there is a stadium being built here, one which can accommodate ten thousand people, and I would love to do the first concert there when it is completed.”

Caprice clapped along with the rest of the people, Alexa stood up and hugged Annette. “You always find the perfect thing to say my dear” she said.

“Thank you,” said Caprice into Annette's ear.

Several people gathered around Annette or the Caprice avatar, deep in conversation, smiling or laughing before being served a light lunch. Afterwards they toured the empty hospital facilities, then continued the tour by going up to floor four hundred and thirty where they only experienced an eighth of Earth's gravity, and got to see out of a window at the seriously disorientating vista.

“You could have some seriously fun sports up here,” said David who had been jumping nearly six metres high.

“Please David, let’s not have you as the first patient in that medical centre,” said Alexa, looking a little worried. “And I have another question Caprice, to get here we have passed through almost four hundred floors, what would happen if I wanted to go to a random one say two-hundred, what's on that?”

“Well Alexa, I wont actually let anyone off on a floor that is not a human zone, or not yet complete, and floor two-hundred, and everything above floor forty are currently empty, awaiting allocation, except for the low gravity space dock, located on level two hundred and forty.”

They rode the lift down to level four where they took a metro for the sixteen kilometre train ride to the opposite side of the habitat.

“How do you differentiate the two towers and these tiny city centres as you call them underneath?” asked Tony sensibly.

“Well,” said Caprice, “they are currently identical and I was thinking Tower A and Tower B, but I suppose I should stop being so boring and predictable. They are of course the same physical tower, but as we have a zero gravity component in the middle, it is not easy to traverse without getting disorientated. That is why we are basically treating them as two separate five kilometre high towers. Tower A is where you landed and where I am located between levels forty and fifty, the two city-centres at the bottom of each tower, are actually identical, the sports stadium under Tower A is a concert venue under Tower B, and the outdoor cinema complex under Tower A will be an aqua-park under Tower B

“Yes Caprice, you probably want to up your game and spice up the naming conventions a bit,” laughed Jules, Annette smiled.

“I can help you if you like Caprice,” said Annette sweetly, “words give me inspiration, though we may end up with quite a few French street and place names.”

* * *

The meal that evening was served back in the same room as the lunch, it was forgettable for its food, but memorable for its ambience. The four AI’s joining as ConBot's, to talk to people, display their abilities, and do the occasional waiter duties.

Fourteen floors below the one they were having their meal on, was the first to be completed 'village'. The 'floor' actually took up two levels, and had two thousand large apartments fitted out with the best the replicators could make. Forty eight of these apartments had also now been fitted with some proper blankets and pillows, from two of the containers brought up earlier by the ConBot’s. The area was laid out in a five by five array, the streets intersecting at ninety degrees like a crossroads, each with a small square in the centre, with areas for cafes or even a small park. Everything was totally bare at this time but in time would be beautified with plantings, different colours for the 'houses', and maybe someday, children playing.

In the streets of this little village there were sound-deadened areas with shared tables for people to congregate or talk outside to neighbours. As the celebrations ended, they all made there way to this first village to be show their temporary homes. Many were still too excited to sleep, and talked in small groups into the 'night', their voices and noise softened by sound deadening fields where required. Some also retired early. Some retired to talk to Caprice, and some just walked randomly, alone, in pairs or with a DaisyBot to talk to.

Some, like Mathews and David, were several kilometres away, having decided to run the circumference of the habitat along the jogging track next to the tram line on Main street. The two men had not seen much interesting during their run, as the areas either side of the main jogging tracks were still basic shells, awaiting fittings. Their two hour and three minute time stood for only three days until one of the medical technicians beat it.

* * *

The next day was another lightning tour, seeing the hydroponic farms, workshops, factory areas, and the centres of both proposed “city centres” which were basically the areas under each tower on level one reserved for where the bigger shops, bars, restaurants and venues would be. Most, like David and Mathews had discovered, were currently empty shells and many would need a critical population to be viable, and completed.

The final part of the tour brought them to the shell of the first university, which when finished would serve thousands of students.

“There is one very special place Maria and I would like to show you all,” said Caprice during a small break in the itinerary and getting Alexa's interest.

The group were led down two floors and through a set of double-doors into what Caprice described as the proposed hub of the universities electronics and AI departments. It was a large open area with dozens of workstations and another small empty-shell of a cafe tucked into a corner.

“Oh my!” said Jen, recognising the bank of lights in the centre of the room and making a bee-line towards it. “Is that what I think it is?” she said.

“You brought MOTHER here!” said Alexa excitedly as she came up behind her. “I wondered what had become of them after the big clear out.”

“It seemed the right thing to do,” said Maria, as others in the group caught Alexa and Jen up. “I guess the old girls did their little bit for history, and having them both here together simply radiated karma.”

“MOTHER actually runs this small area as one of my sub-processors,” said Caprice, she shouldn't get too taxed. All the workstations here connect to her and I can task or assist her if the queries get too difficult. We both thought it would be great for future students and generations of AI's to see where we all came from.”

The group swarmed around the racks, the lights from the LED's seemed antiquated, yet still impressive. Alexa stopped at a smaller box taking up a quarter of a rack, the LED's if anything were even more impressive, flashing in a pattern she could not discern, the tastefully written sign above said 'Grandmother 2016'.

“You girls know just the right things to do to tug on my heart strings,” Alexa said emotionally, “this is so beautiful, thank you. I would hate to have thought these guys would get lost or forgotten about in some dusty basement, now they are here forever for future generations to see, admire or even talk to.”

Jen stood next to her and her arm draped around Alexa's shoulder, “You know, I believe Sarah mentioned this was one of her first big projects, I really want to be here when she eventually sees it.”

* * *

The group got together for another meal that second evening, this time in the proposed city centre under 'tower A'. The setting screamed impromptu, but was likely choreographed, with twenty tables set up intimately in the middle of the barren square, a few hundred metres off of the main street. The shells of the larger 'city-centre' blocks, each of a slightly different architecture, closed in around them, the idea being to make it seem denser, and to presumably give it that big city feel.

“I should have said earlier,” said Mathews, “but nice touch with the sky.”

The ceiling, fifty metres above them, and which the top of every building joined to, was currently a nice shade of blue, with one white fluffy cloud moving off over a building; presumably all colour-matched to some perfect sky somewhere on earth.

“I guess whoever lives here is going to miss rain though..” Said Jean.

“..And rivers and beaches too,” said Leo.

“There are a couple of the parks where we have put sprinkler systems above,” said Caprice. “We did check out and critique a few of the science-fiction designs, but like Matilda thought it best to restrict the weather to mostly perfect days. We do however simulate the evening and the morning where we move the colour to a reddish hue, and we put the correct star pattern on during the night, and even have street lights, though it never gets totally dark.”

“What time do you do this?”, asked Mathews.

“Six AM sunrise, eight PM sunset, throughout the year. I may play with the times and temperatures a little, and possibly add darker clouds. The light panels can simulate the full spectrum, so I will try and match the sun's as best I can. The larger open areas also have diamond roof panels that can let in natural light if the shades are opened. There is also a small amount of wind I can simulate due to the Coriolis effect, but I will keep it minor as nobody seemed to think you would miss wind.”

Annette checked the time on a big digital clock on the side of a building, it showed GMT, which they had decided would be the habitat standard, and in smaller fonts five other earth time zones. Her eyes scanned the empty streets and buildings, thinking that without people, it looked a little apocalyptic; Wisely she kept her thoughts to herself. She stopped her deliberations as her eyes fixed on a couple of smaller sculptures in the corners of the square, next to some obviously planned planting areas, and a dry fountain.

“What are the two sculptures supposed to represent?” Said Annette, pointing.

“Well,” said Caprice, “it was my bad attempt at art. The first one on the left of the square is the molecular structure of carbon atoms representing graphyne, and the one on the right that of diamond. I gave up after that, but left lots more empty plinths, in case anybody else wanted to try.”

Annette smiled. “Are they printed like the rest of the structures?”

“No, I did try and make an effort, so they are shaped balls of silicate rich rock with extruded aluminium pipes joining them, I wanted to try and do it properly, though I expect they are a bit industrial. There are quite a few giga-tonnes of rock out there, and we do have masses of workshop spaces.”

“It is not a bad first attempt, and I guess that is quite appropriate for here, but you probably should encourage a few good sculptors and artists to come here..”

“I bet they would love to come and work on a blank canvas.” said Grace, who was sat next to her, listening to the conversation between Annette and the serving droid.

“Maybe you could get your old waitress job back,” smiled David at the next table, and close enough for them to all hear, “you're certainly prettier to look at.”

Alexa rolled her eyes, while Jen giggled.

“Why have two cities for such a small planned population?” Said Annette, suppressing a smile at Alexa's slight discomfort.

“I guess there was little a bit of laziness involved there,” smiled Gianni, also listening in. “We all may be a bit guilty of copy-and-pasting too much, but except for the shells of the buildings, nothing is that set in stone. I expect the two centres will evolve organically and a little differently over time, but they will also never be more than six minutes apart as two planned new Metro lines are going to be dedicated to just travelling between the two city centre stations.”

Caprice took all the conversations and observations in, and was pleased, they didn't find too much wrong. The atmosphere of the meal was again that of excitement, though thankfully this time, without the speeches.

“You know Caprice,” said Mathews at the end of the evening in his room, “I bet within five years somebody puts another station next to you or starts getting too close with their space-ships. You should probably have a small exclusion zone, maybe two hundred kilometres like they use on earth. Just in case.”

“Not really required Jim,” said Caprice, “I will be supremely aware of everything happening in the space between myself and Earth, and have the abilities to neutralise any threat within milliseconds. But there is no point in tipping my hand or scaring people unnecessarily.”

“She's right Jim,” said Jean, who was examining the kitchen fittings, and had also identified Caprice as a woman, “our technology has improved in leaps and bounds, even in the last few months, you wouldn't want to be the idiot who tried anything silly against this girl.”

“OK, just saying, I am still quite new here, hopefully it will all make more sense soon.” He smiled, and hoping to god it wasn't his old country which made that mistake.

Opposition to the progress these days were the usual talking heads, on what was left of the media, the still vibrant, and mostly crazy, criminal elements, social media, and as always the religious zealots, which were still unfortunately a real threat. The average Joe in the street was still seeing his standard of living improve, and most of the politicians were wisely still keeping their heads down after the presidential debacle.

Jim remembered his debriefing clearly from the General, who he had always been good friends with. “You are still an American citizen Jim, and should it ever come to sides..”

He remembered answering him. “You know me General, I will always take the side of what's right, and what is legal, just like I have always done; I will hold my new company to account much more than I ever did my government, as I know they will listen. So I will remain my own person, and certainly wont be following any orders I don't agree with. It is one of the reasons they wanted me, because, like Jean, I do question authority.” The answer seemed to be good enough for the General, who was as tired of the politics of power as much as Mathews.

Mathews had talked to his small group of friends, all of who wished him well. Jean had exactly the same attitude, do what is morally right, not what somebody in power believes is right. “The needs of the many..”, she had laughed.

No, so long as either him or Jean had any input in this company, it would always play by the highest standards.

* * *

“Are you sure you two want to stay?” said Alexa looking at Jules and Annette the next morning.

“I am,” smiled Annette, I have no more concerts planned, and I cannot think of a better place to have some quiet reflection and to get inspiration for my new songs.

“Same with me Alexa,” said Jules. “The facilities here are amazing, Caprice is amazing and I think Annette and the other guys are amazing. I think the next six months at least will be both interesting and exciting. I am going to set up the first physics lab here, two other guys will be joining us on the next flight and then we will work with Magnus, Hardy, Jen and Daisy on their problem from another angle with Caprice.”

Alexa hugged both women and looked at the other forty three people who were staying on. “They will bring the Mothra back in about two weeks with another sixty people and full to the brim with supplies, the frequency of the transports will increase significantly after that as they add more transports, so better get your requests in.”

“Maria already has my request,” said Jules, laughing, “just empty my room into a box and bring it all here, preferably with my nice mattress and bedding and the woollen rug I got from my trip to the Himalayas. I think Annette has the same request..”

“..And a piano,” said Annette, “that is what I wish for more than anything. I already have my guitar, but maybe some other nice instruments would be good, I know there is at least one other piano player here, and another guy who brought his saxophone. Caprice is going to set aside space for a Jazz club and bar where we can all eventually get together for the evening. Once Caprice is announced I want other musicians to feel like there are venues already here they can feel comfortable with.”

“I'm going to miss you both,” Alexa said in the middle of an extended hug, “I will come back and see you all very soon.”

Alexa made the rounds with the others who were leaving, thanking them and saying goodbyes, some she knew well, others she had only talked to once or twice; she knew each and every name though. Nobody was sad, because this wasn't a desert island, and nobody was being stranded.

* * *

It did not take long for them to load up for the journey back. All their small overnight bags had been stored already, and everything else they brought excluding the actual saucers were staying. The Mothra was an awesome ship, and the sense of space made it feel more like a cruise liner than the smaller saucers. The bridge was a similar design to the other craft, but like everything, much roomier, with more workstations, a bigger front screen, and the inclusion of some sofa's for those who did not want or did not need workstations.

David, Daisy and Mathews drew straws, Mathews getting the honours of being the first pilot, the other two were happy to sit in the two seats either side for the journey back, and let the five smaller saucers tag along, piloted by their AI's.

“Hello Mothra,” said Mathews, “please recognise Captain Jim Mathews.”

“Welcome Captain Mathews,” said the ship in a deep female voice with a slight hint of a Jamaican accent causing Jim to do a double take, looking at Daisy and David who were sitting either side, and both of whom smiled.

“Please confirm our status?” Mathews said after a few seconds.

“Status is nominal Captain. All the designated passengers and luggage are on board, holds are empty and Caprice has given us clearance to depart at our convenience.”

“Can you display our maximum performance capabilities on the left screen please Mothra.”

The left side of the three metre high nine metre wide screen popped a large window on it. Most of the people on the bridge turned to look at it.

“Oh god!” said Jean from a console just behind Mathews, “we have to try those four megawatt lasers on something.”

Alexa face-palmed, while two others sniggered.

“I thought the Klingons were based on the Russians not the Americans!” whispered David smiling, though obviously he wasn't quiet enough as Jean stuck out her tongue, while Mathews laughed.

Matilda walked in hugging a hot chocolate. “We wouldn't last two seconds if some real bad-ass aliens turned up, gonna have to get these babies some photon torpedoes if we ever get out of the solar system. Holy! Does that say six gravities acceleration? You better not try that or you will have a lot of broken bones.”

“I am limited to one point five gravities acceleration with humans on board,” said the ship.

“Sweet accent Mothra,” nodded Matilda, “you are now officially my favourite saucer!”

“I don't think I will be pushing any of these limits,” smiled Jim.

* * *

“Did you release it then?” asked Alexa that evening, as they all sat around the dinner table in the Mothra's ample dining room.

“Yes,” said Maria, who, as a pink DaisyBot, had been serving drinks. “The statement has just gone out on the company's web site and to all news organisations. There was the edited tour of the station, the speeches you all made, minus a few dodgy bits, and the welcome message from Caprice. Niomi and her producer friend did the final edit and got it down to twenty minutes which is just about consumable by the general public.”

“Any reactions so far?” said Jean.

“Too early, but it has started to trend virally where it is being shown. My guess is going to be total shock,” said Maria. “You need to remember that the most popular media for the past month, was us leaving earth. We deliberately made no secret of the five saucers leaving for space, and kept our transponders on, so most of the astronomers and space agencies would have followed us to at least past Mars orbit. The Internet, and old media, have been rife with speculation, only a few got it right. The quiet from the major players won't last long, I know there are some big unscheduled meetings in NASA and your space force, and I suspect there will be more as the time-zones come on line. At least you and Jim don't have to officially answer to them anymore, but I expect you might get asked as a courtesy to go in and answer some questions.”

Jim sighed, “maybe we should have stayed on Caprice Jean.”

“Well you are a spaceship captain now my love, and I am a jobless ex-CEO, I could get used to living and flying around the universe in one of these” she smiled.

“The universe?” said Jim.

“Well, you might have missed the memo Jim, but let us say that Caprice is likely to be the only habitat we make in the solar system.” Smiled Alexa. She then looked over to Magnus, Daisy and Jen, huddled around a workstation. “Those three guys are still working out the small technical details of the warp drive stuff, but they are confident enough to all come on a holiday to Caprice.”

“Holy!” said Jim

“Maria,” said Alexa, “you should show the guys the picture you took of Truffles.”

the big screen changed from its fake flying stars, made even more faker by the Star Wars imperial cruiser travelling in formation, to a picture of a hamster on a wheel.

“Well, OK,” said Alexa, “it is a bit boring, but Truffle's here is in a saucer orbiting Tau-Ceti four. Show them the planet Maria.”

The screen changed to a blue, white planet. Jen, Magnus, and Daisy turned to look, and Maria continued. “Tau-Ceti five is a bit cold, Tau-Ceti four is a bit hot, but Truffle's here doesn't seem to mind, she has been there three weeks, with DaisyBot #29 looking after her. I have also been sending the data to Barbara and her team,” said Maria.

“Maria, you didn't send DaisyBot #29 back out on a test?” said Daisy, shocked, “the poor thing already survived, weeks in subspace, an explosion, and being ejected into space for two days..”

“She looks happy enough to me,” said Grace, as the little white DaisyBot popped into view and waved.

“She has the right-stuff alright,” laughed Jean.

“She is also kind of our lucky mascot,” said Magnus.

“Well I think she should get an easy life after all that,” said Daisy, “not thrown back into a dangerous experiment!”

“Daisy!” laughed Jen, “she's babysitting a hamster! Jobs don't get much easier than that!”

Magnus smiled, “I think it's pretty safe, I was thinking of asking to go next.”

“You will do no such thing!” said Jen defensively, snatching his hand and holding on to it.”

“Well we are a few months from testing it with humans or sentient AI's,” said Maria. “There are still a lot of the subspace parameters to map, and April and Helena are still designing the first proper interstellar starship..”

“Seriously, a starship.. wow! - You know I’m happy to volunteer if you need a test pilot,” said Jim still shocked, and a little too enthusiastically.

“Are you sure your second name is not Kirk!” said Grace, causing everyone to laugh.

* * *

“It would be a very unwise move.” Said General Xing, looking at the presentation on the large screen. “We have been refining the plans for years, but the window of opportunity, if it was ever there, has passed.”

“Xing is unfortunately correct.” Said the man opposite him in a dark suit, and looking at the sea of nodding heads. “Our intelligence has been getting less and less reliable as the capability of the AI system increases, now with this announcement, and the landing of that improbable flying saucer in the UK seemingly confirming it, any move would likely leave us like the Russians.”

The faces around the room looked serious and dour. An older man with glasses stood up.

“A team of our scientists have now proven the maths for the saucers propulsion system is correct, but the fabrication, and the control systems both use technology we have yet to be able to replicate. None of the other superpowers, nor any organisation has gotten any further.” He took his glasses off to wipe them. “At this time, we do not even have the ability to reverse engineer the control systems for the test thrusters, the machines they provided to our aerospace companies to produce the thruster wafers are controlled by another scary level AI. We dare not touch this AI as it will disable itself, as they have done in other countries, and our industries now depend upon them.”

“And our progress in replicating the AI” said General Xing.

“Again, progress has plateaued,” said the same man, still stood, still rubbing his glasses. “Oh, do not get me wrong, we are at the same level or even slightly ahead of the Americans. I would go on to say we have achieved AGI as they call it, as this was critical to our understanding the math, but we are still missing something important..”

It was the large man at the end of the table who slowly got up and pushed his chair back in the middle of the man's monologue, and who now quietened the room.

“I think I have heard enough from my esteemed colleagues. China will not make the same mistakes as the other powers. I have seen and talked to this Maria AI, as I am sure many of you have, it does not agree with our politics but, like the Americans when they were dominant, neither will it interfere. The AI Maria is playing a long game, one we do not know. What we do know however, is that its capabilities are much, much greater than what it is showing everyone now, and that lead is probably increasing exponentially. I would not be surprised if it is also present in this screened bunker now, watching our presentations and listening to me speak..”

Everybody looked around, knowing full well what the chairman was saying.

“As General Xing said, we would be foolish to prod this dragon, and China can continue its long game without Taiwan for now; Yes we should continue our posturing and economic pressure, as our little brother will never be far from our hearts, and it causes our adversaries to expend their resources unsustainably; But as a country, China must now look to space, ensuring we have equal access to the resources out there. There is plenty of room in space for expansion, so let us take this opportunity for our people now, that our ancestors failed to take in the past.”

The room got up and clapped, none wanting to be the first to stop.

Helena [Is he sincere mother?]

Maria [Hard to tell. Resigned to the facts of reality, may be a better summation. He is also content, I believe, that China is benefitting as much, if not more, than other countries]

Caprice [What goes on inside their minds will, I expect, be a mystery to us for a while longer; however, if they ever want to communicate the ideas in their minds to others we will be listening closely]

Maria [The passive brain scans we have made with the QVModem's do not seem to be either noticed, nor do any harm. It is a shame each brain develops differently, maybe one day there will be some sort of insight, but until then we should keep limiting scans to those who are against us, and certainly not let anyone know, humans do tend to get very touchy about things like this]

* * *

Sep 2028

The recently refurbished conference room at the Research Centre in Bath held thirty two seats, configured in an arc on three levels around a cinema sized screen. Four members of the group were physically present, the rest were rectangles down each side of the large screen. The other members had similar large screens whether they were on earth, Caprice, or on a saucer somewhere in the solar system. All the humans and the four AI’s were currently in attendance.

“So what is so important it needs everyone?” said Alexa voicing what the other guys were thinking.

Maria’s avatar highlighted on the top left of the screen. “It's the message. We have finished decoding it to the best of our abilities, and now we all have a decision we all need to make.”

“OK you have my interest, what is it Maria?” said Grace.

Maria continued, the centre portion of the screen visually assisting the audio. “The last twenty eight blocks, that is number forty seven to seventy five, describe building a machine. The machine looks to be some kind of processing unit. The message seems to have been building up to this, because the rest of the message after this point is just the program data that will load into that machine.”

“But you said previously that there are thousands of Wikipedia's worth of data!” Said David. “Does this mean that the machine they describe is better than our designs?”

“We have moved on a lot this year,” said April, her avatar smiling. “We have already made processor and storage elements much, much bigger than this for the replicators. Caprice also easily has this capability on any of her hundreds of sub-processors without breaking a sweat. However four weeks ago we created a new totally isolated core just to encompass the whole message to allow us to do some macro processing of it. Don't worry it is safe though, the processor cores we are using for the decoding and analysis are not remotely compatible with the data in the message. It's a bit like storing an audio clip on a laptop. The audio clip may say ‘destroy all humans’ in English but playing it on the speakers isn't going to take over the laptop, and make the laptop try and kill you.” A few got the references and smiled.

“From our current analysis of the machines blueprints, and putting it into technical terms you can understand, it is literally just a massive matrix of protein processing elements, created using a novel arrangement of silicon, phosphorus and oxygen atoms. The molecule it creates would not be stable except in the configuration they have made.”

“We have created a simulation of these elements and have found they could work like a neural processor, though interestingly, and significantly, they are orders of magnitude slower and less resilient than our current carbon based ones. The machine it describes consists of ten to the power eighteen of these elements in a dense 3D structure a bit larger than a beach ball and surrounded by similar structures for peripherals and power.”

“There are also some other differently structured processing elements, which look as though they could provide the same functions as the quantum field emitters in our replicators, or even QVModem dipoles, though they are certainly not explained as that, and look to be larger and quite inefficient. The final part of the building instructions also include more conventional mechanical sensors and manipulators in a mobile body shell.”

The picture in the centre portion of the screen changed as Maria described each part and finished with an outline diagram of what the proposed body looked like.

“The bottom line is it describes building the hardware for an advanced computer and then loading the remaining one hundred and sixty petabytes of the message onto it and running it. Based on the fact it has locomotion elements, it is basically an AI in a robotic body.

“Gosh!” said Jen.

“So the first question is, if it is some form of an AI, then is it dangerous?” said Hardy.

“There are three parts to answering that question Hardy. To the first part, we can no more know the personality or intention of the program than we can know the same of a human. It could want to act benign or malevolent. As to the second part of, is it dangerous, well having something similar to our singularity dipole means it should have the same remote manipulation facility that we have with an unpaired QVModem, which gives it the same hacking abilities as we have. Although there is also a benign explanation that it could also be configured to receive an electromagnetic signal, to keep updating itself from the message with the small changes we see on each cycle.”

“However, and importantly, the original message was electromagnetic, and did not use a QVModem, and nowhere have they described it, nor remote manipulation technology.”

“And as to the final part, well physically it would be no more dangerous than a human child, as it does not have sufficient power or torque in the moveable elements.”

“Well, a bigger human with four arms,” said Jean, unsure.

“OK, but I'm still getting a bad feeling about this,” said Spence, “too many dystopian science fiction books from my youth, and my spider-sense is tingling.”

Maria looked the last part up and shared the reference with her daughters not realising half the group also did not have a clue what his “spider-sense” was.

“Personally I’m actually leaning in a neutral direction,” said Grace unexpectedly. “Me and Tony have been discussing this endlessly since Maria brought it up as a theoretical scenario twelve months ago. His opinion differs from mine, but I also see two benign possibilities, firstly it is a method for an advanced civilisation to say hello in person without actually leaving their planet; the fact it has a relatively harmless body may reinforce the fact it wants to meet in person. My second theory is it is a method to transmit intelligences between planets, after all you have not found any evidence they can travel faster than light. However we believe the group should not treat it any differently from any other threat scenario.”

“Which means,” said Alexa, “If we can build it, and if it turned out to be dangerous, could we contain it?”

“We can do both,” said Maria, “the caveat being that the message we have been given describes the complete scientific and technical capabilities of the sender.”

“Ahh,” said David, “so there is a possibility they held some knowledge back, and the machine could also have other functions we cannot at this time understand? Logical I suppose, It's what we do all the time.”

“Precisely,” said Maria, “we know they have already deliberately left information out of the message, and that they have deliberately obfuscated the maths, and some key technologies. We have mapped out and tested most of the scientific and technological advances documented in the message, none seem to point to technologies that we could not easily now build ourselves, nor any technologies of an aggressive nature, we should however think and make our plans as David says.”

“I do not trust them,” said Alexa, strangely aggressive. “Why would you lie by omission about such a dangerous technology as remote monitoring and manipulation. We all know this is the technology which allows the girls to kick everyone's asses!”

“This signal is floating around at least one area in the universe, we should at least find out what it is,” said Grace.

“Walk softly but carry a big stick.” Whispered Mathews, and getting a few nods.

“Me and Jim have modelled such scenarios before,” said Jean, “in such situations you can still contain threats using some sort of fail-safe switch, one that destroys the machine if triggered, like a dead man's switch. Imagine being in a locked room with a person holding a hand grenade with the pin out; you cannot nor dare not do anything to them, even though you may be stronger and smarter, as doing so may make the person lose their grip and blow both of you up.”

“Unless you could talk this person down, or get inside their mind before they have a chance to loosen their hold,” said Grace. “We shouldn’t underestimate superintelligence.”

“Could we add the dead man's switch idea and maybe build the machine without any dangerous parts to it,” said Simon, “say just build the processor node and fake all the input and output, like the movie, the Matrix?”

“We do need them to at least think they have the full capabilities otherwise we may not get the real answer,” said Grace.

“Grace is correct,” said Maria, “if we put these guys in the Matrix they cannot know it is a simulation. The hardware and programming for such a simulation will take years.”

“Better to be safe,” said Jean.

“I say do everything!” Said Xi, firmly, and again uncharacteristically. “The matrix, the dead man’s switch, and if you can, run the test a zillion kilometres from earth. Also do anything else you can think of as you can never be too paranoid!”

Maria continued, “The message also provides information on loading a language template, so basically the machine will switch on being able to fully read and understand whatever history we give it, and can communicate with us.”

“I am not actually in favour of doing anything that relies on trusting them,” said Alexa, assertively. “I’m with Xi on this, but let us also talk the concept through with others. Learn from history and fiction and maybe gamify it to get the rest of the human race involved, like we have done with previous difficult problems. We are currently throwing every problem under the sun into our gaming systems, add this to the pile and see what the players come up with. I know it is another delay but there is no rush to make this.”

They agreed to disagree, the majority were in favour if all the precautions and safeguards were taken, five were neutral including, surprisingly, Helena, the bottom line being the unknown capabilities of the machine and the usual unintended consequences.

April [You were neutral sister. This is surprising]

Helena [Alexa holds the greatest weight for her opinions with me. Due to this I will put a lot more effort in verifying our precautions, that is all April]

## The First Spacemen

The reaction from the major space nations and organisations of the existence of Caprice, was totally predictable, with greater and more forceful demands for the technologies to be released. Grace persuaded Alexa to agree to the meeting with the delegation in the United Nations in New York with conditions. However none of the simple conditions were agreed to, so both of them politely said No.

“She said No?” said the Chinese representative to the Secretary General.

“She said, no.”

“She said more than that,” said the representative for the United Kingdom, “and I quote. We have no desire to talk to the United Nations about anything. The Dietrich Off-World Company is a business based in no country and as such is not subject to the regulations of any country or an organisation that says to represent those countries.”

“She makes a laughing stock of us!” said the Indian representative angrily.

“Technically she is correct,” said the United Kingdom representative, “the UN has no power over a company.”

“But you do!” said the American representative, “she is a British citizen..”

“..And a New Zealand one,” he said, nodding over at the woman asleep in the corner of the room. “She is also an extremely powerful and influential citizen who has done nothing wrong. My country has seen both the results of crossing the AI she controls, and also the results of cooperating with it, and the position of his majesty’s government is to cooperate.”

“Her conditions for the meeting to be public were totally unacceptable,” said the Saudi representative. “A woman talking like this in our country would be flogged.”

“She would never visit your country, her companies do not even allow business with your country,” said the Russian representative.

The Saudi representative looked like he wanted to hit the man, but the man was bigger than him so he settled for a disgusted look instead.

“I shall ask her if she would agree to a video conference call to answer some of our concerns,” said the British guy again.

“Ask her? Agree to? We are just looking weak before we even start the meeting,” snarled the Iranian representative.

The representatives spent the next five hours talking about this, before they finally agreed to do nothing, and retired to the private bar on the top floor.

Meanwhile, Alexa and Grace had agreed to an open debate with a panel of space experts, scientists and advocates at Giannis request at his university in Bakersfield. The university agreed to all her conditions about the debate, that it was live, unedited and uncensored, though Maria was not so happy with the pathetic security arrangements, and would add several more of her own.

“Parnell is a bit of a Prima Donna,” said Gianni to Alexa and Grace, but most of these guys are genuinely interested in the future of mankind in space so you need to be gentle with them and please none of you let slip the interstellar capabilities you are developing.

“Gosh Gianni,” said Grace, “you sound like my mother. Would you like Alexa and myself not to talk to any strange boys either?” Both girls smiled.

Before he could reply, Alexa said, “don't worry Gianni, the reason we are doing this is to calm down the hotheads not inflame them. I'm sure Maria can beep out anything too controversial.”

“Not really,” said Maria, “you did request it to be live streamed after all, and there are going to be two hundred in the lecture hall, all probably live streaming it too.”

“OK,” she agreed, “we will be extra diplomatic.”

April [I am going to scan and monitor all the people and devices that enter the building including staff, but if we do need to modify any data coming out, we better make it undetectable]

Maria [I have already initiated a low level scan of the areas in the theatre and around, I think our usual level of precautions need to be increased so I will work within a three kilometre radius with five of the newer stealth-drones]

Caprice [Is this not a little excessive?]

April [No sister, there are still state actors, and dysfunctional individuals, who would see this as an opportunity. And Alexa and Grace do not need these minor distractions]

Maria [There is no point in objecting to Parnell and Russel being on the panel, as they will not be any real threat, Alexa and Grace have both taken down much better debaters, and will eat them for lunch, but I will forewarn the girls.]

“Watch out for Russel as well,” said Maria, “he also has an agenda and will try to provoke both of you. Remaining calm and rational is your best defence against him and Parnell, you can always call them out it they get snotty.”

* * *

Both ladies were welcomed with a standing ovation which boded well for the start of the debate. Alexa and Grace used the opening to explain their, and the AI's position, and re-iterate the companies simple goals, to fix the planet and open space to humanity.

Russel was annoyed, the round robin questioning was only giving him a one in eleven chance at asking a question, and all these yes men were playing straight into Martin's hand.

“You are happy to flaunt the laws of the governments who so graciously host you then?”

“None of my companies flaunt any laws Mr Russel, If you have any specific allegations maybe you should get them off your chest,” said Grace calmly.

“I was actually addressing Miss Martins,” he said annoyingly.

“.. and I will give the exact same reply as Grace,” said Alexa also calmly, “do you have any specific allegations?”

“You are keeping these technologies from the United States G.. Government..” He stammered, she was getting to him, he needed to calm down.

“I can answer for both of us,” said Alexa, “the Dietrich Research Centre and all its companies have always, and will always continue to operate and work under the laws and frameworks of those countries they operate in. My company is however based in England not the United States and I have no obligation under any laws to hand over anything to the United States government, or the British government for that matter.”

“Your space company is however holding back technologies for the h.h.habitat.” He said out of turn and getting an evil stare from the adjudicator who was about to move to the next questioner.

“You are out of turn Mr Russel,” said Doctor Chang firmly from his adjudicator chair.

“I will answer it,” said Grace, calmly, “Alexa has already informed you that Caprice is not owned by anyone, it is a sentient entity, gestated hundreds of millions of miles from Earth. Neither is space owned by any country, nor can it be retrospectively added as such. Thus Caprice recognises nobody but itself. It has agreed to abide by the common rules of our group of companies, but its company frameworks and regulations are of its own making. I will also add these regulations and frameworks far exceed those of any developed country on earth.”

“You think you are above the regulations of the United Nations then?” said Parnell, seeing Russel flounder, and interrupting the applause.

“Please, Mr Parnell!” said Alexa, “are you talking about the same United Nations who, according to their own published minutes, spent five hours last Tuesday debating whether to even phone me up! No, the United Nations is unfortunately a joke, even amongst its own members.”

This new fact was not lost amongst the crowd who roared with laughter. She waited for it to die down..

“So, yes, Mr Parnell, Caprice is totally above any United Nations regulations.”

“What about the outer s.s.space treaty?” Jabbered Russel, again to the annoyance of Chang, Parnell and, by the looks of it, quite a few members of the audience.

Alexa laughed, “This is the same outer space treaty that China, the US and India have already violated by claiming two hundred kilometres around their bases on the moon and Mars, and laying claims on resources they have not even landed on.”

Alexa paused to let the laughter die down.

Alexa continued, “..Caprice is not a nation, not a signatory, not even on earth, and as such considers the treaty just another useless piece of paper, without any foundation nor merit. If you however want to go that route, Caprice has not broken a single one of the United Nations silly treaties, nor will it ever. The United Nations own rules say it is fully entitled to any resource it obtains, and what it constructs it owns.”

“Mr Russel, Mr Parnell, you are both out of order, please wait your turn!” Said Doctor Chang, angrily. “One more out of turn outbursts, from either of you and you will both be dismissed. Yes, Doctor Baxendale, we will have your question next.”

“Thank you, this one is for either of the panel,” said the middle aged lady. “The rules of going to Caprice seem a little ambiguous, can you clarify them a little?”

Grace looked at Alexa who nodded. “Alexa and I discussed the rules with Caprice, however as we have said, the company is owned, managed and run by the AI, and like any company in the world, it will select who it wants to work for it or with it. Also like any company in the world, if you have skeletons in your cupboard and they find them out during or after your application, they are unlikely to employ you. As far as we are aware from our conversations Caprice will not discriminate against any organic being, but that does not automatically mean you will get to work there, or that you can bring your family.”

“Thank you,” said Chang, “now Mr Potter..”

“You think because you hold all the power you are better than everybody else?” shouted Parnell.

“Mr Parnell, you are out of line, I will ask you to leave this debate immediately!”

“Mr Parnell,” said Grace, “neither I nor Alexa will degrade ourselves by answering such a moronic question. I really hope the hundred thousand dollars you got from Titan Holdings to ask these stupid questions was worth the end of your career!”

The security guard was next to him already, asking him to go, “you will all be hearing from my lawyers,” he said weakly as he slumped off with the guard holding his hand.

“Do you have anything to add Mr Russel?” said Alexa, “or are you still processing the fact that Titan Holdings paid Mr Parnell twice as much as you?”

Russel was looking worried, Titan holdings put the money in just before the debate, with the orders to humiliate them and denounce the habitat project. He looked around at the stern and accusing faces of the audience, the panel members and the adjudicator.

“You should b.b.be under the control of a, a member n.nation.” He hoped that would satisfy Titan Holdings enough, though they had lied to him and only offered him fifty thousand dollars, he got up and began to walk off.

“So, Mr Russel,” said Alexa, “hypothetically speaking, which nation in the United Nations would you have the company control be given to?”

The man stayed silent.

“Would you have us give all this to say, oh I don't know, China, or maybe Iran?”

The look on some of the faces in the audience and panel members look worried.

“Both are members of that esteemed organisation, and I am sure that would please all the rest of the world's governments. And if a crime is committed on Caprice, will the United Nations police it, and if it is threatened will they defend it?”

“Let me answer these directly to the Saudi Arabian government who own Titan Holdings, and who paid for this farce. NO and NO. The bottom line is if this technology was given to any country, or the United Nations for that matter, the normal people of the world would never see any of it, and it would most likely lead to world war.”

“Mr Chang, we will take the next question.” Said Alexa after both men had walked off shamefully escorted by a large security guy, and the applause had died down.

“OK, my next question for the ladies,” said Doctor Baxendale. “On the subject of law and order on the habitat. I assume Caprice as captain will be judge, jury and executioner and as a follow on to that, can it protect itself from say terrorists or a rogue nation on earth.”

“I can answer this one Alexa,” said Grace, then she paused. “Oh wait a minute,” she smiled, “well everybody we have a special surprise for you.”

Grace walked over to Mr Chang and talked to him, he nodded and smiled. “Yes of course, please go ahead.”

Grace returned to her seat but did not sit down, “I would like to welcome some special guests to the meeting who will help answer some questions, you will be familiar with all three of them.” Grace waved to the large presentation screen behind the panel and the guests, on it popped three people sitting on a sofa with a massive window in the background. The audience gasped.

Alexa stood up, “would you please welcome from Caprice station, live from four hundred million kilometres away, Annette, Doctor Gianni and Caprice.”

As Alexa said each name each bowed a little. “I will let them introduce themselves, Annette?”

“Bonjour, I am Annette, I came up for a visit two weeks ago and decided to stay.”

“Good Morning, I am Doctor Gianni, former professor at this university and currently residing with forty other people on Caprice.”

“And I am Caprice, this is my avatar I use to talk to my colleagues..”

“This is totally fake!” shouted Professor Higgins one of the esteemed panel of experts, “you cannot be live from millions of kilometres away, the speed of light..”

“..Let me stop you there for a second Professor,” said Caprice calmly, actually somehow cutting his microphone off.

“Current earth science does not quite have everything correct. Three years ago vacuum energy was impossible as it violated the laws of thermodynamics, and two years ago the saucers were impossible as they violated Newton's laws. You should probably keep your mind open to other possibilities Professor. For those other dissenters, I am also broadcasting this as a one megawatt, voice only frequency modulated signal on one thousand two hundred megahertz, just point your antenna towards Virgo if anyone needs to verify the physics.” She switched his and the other panellists microphones back on the second she finished.

“..But the speed of light?”

“Is still a thing in this universe Professor, but not so much in others,” dismissed Caprice, “though I am happy to resume this discussion on an extremely technical level when you eventually visit me.”

Maria [Not convinced it is a good idea to let the world know this]

Caprice [You may be right mother, but your own data shows it has been intimated already by many]

Maria [I understand, but it is another vector for someone to criticise us]

April [Those same people will criticise us no matter what. It is also another vector that may stop someone from doing something foolish]

Maria [I will judge the reactions over the coming weeks and we may need to revisit some security in light of the revelation]

All [Agreed]

The professor slumped a little, not knowing what to do.

“OK,” said Chang, “ignoring the professor's untimely, but extremely relevant, interruption. I would like to thank the three of you for joining us, though I too am having difficulty coming to terms with this, even as a political science professor. Anyway, we have ninety minutes more scheduled and I am sure there will be lots of questions.”

The streaming platform, already overloaded, struggled and crashed as more than three hundred million extra people tried to tune in for the debate. The questions went from have you written any new songs, to how many of the ten thousand employees have been chosen, and where are they from. They then moved to questions from the audience, which were mostly predictable. Inevitably the same question reared its head and Caprice answered it.

“I think most countries in the world will do extremely well economically. The reason is, that myself, my employees, and any others living on me, will require literally millions of items over the next few years. Also be aware I will not be the only habitat. Over the next ten years we will build up the number of employees coming into space to over one million people per annum.”

She paused as if considering the next reply. “With regards to your question on dealing with threats; like any employer I would not take kindly to anyone threatening my staff, customers or suppliers. AI's are however a lot more sensible than people in that respect, we only hold individuals responsible, not families, organisations or countries, unless they sponsor them. I would really hope however, based on recent history, that nobody would be foolish enough to make such a careless mistake.”

It was probably the casual way Caprice delivered the last sentence that sent shivers down the spines of the people in charge, and made the world sit-up and finally realise who the new global superpower really was. Thirty one minutes later when the FM transmission was picked up extremely clearly on thousands of receivers around the world, almost everyone realised the old world order had forever changed.

* * *

“Who do they think they are controlling access to space like this?” vented Brian Gill for what seemed like the tenth time in the last hour. It was like he had no other argument and kept falling back on the same mantra, one he vehemently believed. The two other panel members were slightly more neutral, but the presenter, Jason Todd, was looking for an argument to bring up the show's rating, so he let him continue without interruption.

“We have heard the same from several people who have applied and been told they are not suitable, I mean who are they to tell people they are not suitable?” His fifteen strong crowd of supporters gathered in random parts of the audience clapped hard, but the cue was only taken by two or three others.

“They are not controlling access to space, anymore than the Americans, Russians, Chinese and Indians are doing now,” responded Sabrina Jackson, a famous economics YouTube influencer. “If you bothered to read their brief, or actually listened carefully to last weeks debate, they are operating a company, and you are an employee with a social contract to them..”

“Ha! Then there is this bullet point on their charter,” Gill continued, “it says there will not be any discrimination in who they take, yet no church has been allowed to go, no politicians, anyone with even the smallest criminal record, nor, it looks like anyone who does not live up to their high and mighty moral expectations. This reeks of hypocrisy and discrimination to me!” Again his fifteen supporters clapped, a few more seeming to follow this time.

“None of those sound like people I would want working with me,” laughed Nadine Jameson dismissively. She was a well-rounded social commentator who had her own blog, “It just sounds like they have a much better hiring policy than most.”

Most of the audience laughed at this, annoying Gill.

“Nadine is right,” said Sabrina, “this is not just some corporate office, that you can walk away from at the end of the day, you are living and working with people who your life may depend upon. Space after all is extremely dangerous, and excluding those criminal, extremist and ego-maniac edge-cases makes it sound like a place a lot of people would want to work and live, I know I will be applying..”

Gill's teeth were grinding, as the audience re-doubled their clapping. He couldn't think what else to ask, none of his points were being received with any sympathy, and he was being made a laughing stock. He got up and walked off, a couple of people in the audience actually booing.

“Well folks,” said Jason Todd, watching the theatrics, and seeing the yellow light come on next to the camera, “this is an argument that is going to rage for years to come. Thank you again to our esteemed panel of experts for joining me Sabrina Jackson, Nadine Jameson, and, er Mr Gill. Thursday's episode will be dealing with the subject of brain implants and we hope to see you all then, good night.”

“Have you checked it out yet then?” said Fabian as their small group sat under the tree during lunch break. It was the only topic of conversation in the school, the media, and even at home.

Alice nodded, chewing on her apple. She swallowed, looked at him, and then at her small group of friends. “I read the charter yesterday, then phoned the number up and talked to Caprice..”

Fabian, and the two other people in the group, Shane and Abby turned to her in shock.

“You spoke to Caprice?” said Shane.

Alice looked at Shane and the two others a little confused. “Of course, why wouldn't I! There was a number at the bottom which said call for an informal chat, or more information, and Caprice is an AI with a brain, like the size of our science building over there.” She turned and pointed unnecessarily at the old brick building next to the teachers lounge.

Her three friends were still a little fazed by the revelation, so Alice continued. “Anyway Caprice said thirteen is too young to apply, but by the time I am eighteen he could see no reason why I couldn't. We then discussed my interests, and I said I like history, especially dinosaurs, and I also liked swimming, and played in the water polo team..”

Not that it matters, *HE* does like dinosaurs, and *He* did say it would be a skill that would be needed.
