“..Or people to fly those big saucers like the one that landed in England..”

* * *

There were twenty four people sitting in the airport waiting area. Luna knew if she asked Maria she would know everyone, and point them all out, but she had wanted to see if she could find her by herself.

A few people were talking in groups of two or three, most were simply contemplating life. There were eleven men and thirteen women counting herself, some excited, some apprehensive, and two or three unreadable.

It was six AM, the airport had opened at five thirty, and the twenty four people, who had all been there since the airport opened, were processed quickly due to the unpopular hour. She remembered the tears and goodbyes from her mother and father, and two brothers, and saw the same emotional soap opera being played out for another twenty families. No one was unhappy though, this was an opportunity of a lifetime, and there was only excitement in the air.

Maria had bonded with Luna half way through their first semester two years before. Her viticulture college was surprisingly progressive and had bought two of the cheaper rate subscriptions to the LabAI system, after their biology professor had returned from a trip to California. Luna found she learnt so much better having somebody like Dora to speak to about everything, and over time they developed a friendship, talking about other things like philosophy, economics, and surprisingly, how viticulture would work in space.

Luna was not stupid, she and her friends talked endlessly about the progress happening in the world, mostly brought about by AI systems like Dora. Argentina had it seemed everything going for it, beautiful land, great resources, nice people, but it was perpetually governed by a class of incompetent and corrupt bureaucrats, that nobody could seem to do anything about. It was in one of its better economic cycles now, but normal people were still struggling, and those with power, as usual, were not.

By chance or by foresight, her family were also cushioned somewhat by her fathers plumbing business, and both her brothers had now apprenticed as plumbers too. It seemed the world always needed plumbers. Luna's only goal until meeting Dora was to get a nice job in some boutique vineyard away from the corrupting influence of the city, maybe see the world, try and eventually make it to America or Spain, or even New Zealand, where she heard life was better. Dora changed all that thinking.

On her graduation day, Luna received a package containing a black compact phone and a diamond ear stud. It felt to her like the Willy Wonka golden ticket of the fairy story, as all the world's press knew this was the special phone that Alexa Martins, and the other guys at the Dietrich Research Centre, used to talk to their super AI Maria.

Her first conversation with Maria was tearful and in English, the language she had learnt through Dora, Netflix and YouTube.

“Hi Luna, my name is Maria.” Were the first words when she first opened the phone, and the little Eurasian woman stood there smiling. “I am also Dora, but I am sure you knew that already.” Maria added in Spanish in Dora's voice.

Luna simply burst into tears. She had delayed opening the phone until she was back in her room, a room that was paid for another three weeks until hopefully one of her applications had come back with an interview or job offer. Luna had of course intimated all the details of what to expect, but hearing the LabAI box say it, and having an impossible to obtain technology land in your hands were two different things. “Promises were easily made..” As her father so wisely said.

“Don't worry Luna, you are in a good position, we have talked so much over these past three years I believe I know you quite well. Please let me know if you would like me to speak in Spanish, or translate a word for you, and interrupt me at any time. After all we are friends I hope.”

“It really is you, the famous Maria?” she said in her best English.

She replied, laughing a little, “of course it is me silly, we have talked as friends for years, so don't go getting all formal on me now.”

Luna dabbed her eyes and cheeks with a tissue, but she still found it difficult to speak.

A chair appeared on the little phone, and the Maria hologram sat down. “I think you should get comfortable as well Luna, and maybe have a drink, because, we have all the time you want, and I am about to offer you a job, well two jobs actually but I am really hoping you will prefer the first.”

Both her hands went to her cheeks as the words she had been hoping to hear came out. She wanted to dance or shout or hug somebody, but instead she just smiled the biggest smile she could, and sniffed back the tears that were still flowing.

“I think I will have that drink Maria,” she said, sniffing back another small tear and walking over to her ancient hot water jug.

Finally, the tears stopped and they chatted like friends, like Dora, but in slower English. Only three or four times had she not fully understood a word, and each time Maria had explained it patiently.

“What are the ear-rings for Maria?” she finally asked, she had been eyeing them for the past thirty minutes. “Are they the same Alexa wears?”

“Most of the girls and a few of the boys prefer them to using the phone, they are like wireless earphones and allow me to speak to you without anybody else listening. Most people say they look quite nice. They are, however, for a specific ear piercing which is a bit more discrete, so it is up to you if you want to use them.”

“Oh, Alexa looks beautiful in them, I shall do the same.”

“You know Luna, you and Alexa are alike in many ways, and I think you will like her when you eventually meet her.”

“I am nothing like Alexa Martins, I would have wet myself if the president of the USA had shouted at me like that, yet she just looked at him like a naughty school child.”

“Just because somebody thinks they have more power than you does not mean that is the case, nobody in our company would ever try something as stupid as the old American president, and nobody outside our company has enough power to try. Just remember that, you will not be going in at the bottom of the ladder at the company, you will be going in with equal status to everybody else.” The little avatar paused, and smiled, “well maybe excluding Alexa!”

Maria continued, “There will be a lot of people with more knowledge than you, and you will have more knowledge than others, in the correct situation you will tell others what to do, and in other situations, others will tell you what to do. Very logical really.”

Though apprehensive, she had taken the first job option of course. She and Dora had been discussing just this for the last year, and in many ways Luna, without knowing it, had a deeper insight to the habitat than the rest of the worlds media. Dora had given her extra curricular activities in English on it, and went into virtual discussion groups with other similar people who seemed to be from every country.

She thought of Luke, one of these people, though he was many thousands of Kilometres away in Australia, her other favourite was Diana from the University of San-Pablo-Tucuman, though her discipline was much different. It was Diana she was now looking for.

“Luna!” came the voice from behind her, and Diana rushed out of a small crowd to put her arms around her, not letting go, and squeezing her warmly, “I am so happy you took the job, come let me introduce you to some other friends I just met.” Diana’s Spanish was warm and informal, and Luna was surprised, expecting her whole life to be in English now.

Maria looked on over the mostly young people, none of whom were younger than twenty two, all intelligent, and all exhibiting the qualities and ethics that would do well in the new environment. Some of them had small outlying quirks she could overlook, such as shyness, slightly risqué humour or flirtiness, which seemed to make workplaces interesting, but these were just things she and Caprice would need to keep an eye on. She had of course had similar conversations with eighteen thousand people now, trying to select the best for the first batch. Only a hundred and ten she had asked had taken the second option which was for a similar position at one of their earth based facilities.

Luna had barely introduced herself to the three women, and the outlying older man, when Maria chirped in her ear, the saucer was on final approach and would land in a minute.

* * *

Maria was slightly annoyed at the special fees imposed on her “airline” for processing the “special” saucer. This was their fourth flight from Argentina, it would be the first in the bigger saucer though. Most of the regulations were just plain stupid, and special fees like this one, of five thousand US dollars, generally waved the stupid regulations away. Argentina was not alone having this problem, it was just the way you did business in some countries, and as freely elected governments it was not her job to change anything.

The thing that did annoy her was that the special fee had increased by two thousand dollars since the last visit, and the last time she checked inflation was only at six percent. It was almost getting to the stage where she would deliberately go out of her way to get the money back. She had thought several times about just having everyone meet at a very large forest preserve she owned in the north of the country, and just pick them up there. But setting a proper example by following the laws of the country, however ridiculous, was her preferred option.

All the people moved over to the window. Luckily for Maria, two of the new Gulfstream saucers had already visited this airport, and special larger boarding areas had been made at most international airports for the expected bigger vertical take off and landing aircraft, which would be the only ones available in a few years.

The excitement rose, this landing would be more interesting than most as it would be the first time one of the newer larger saucers had landed in South America, and the Mothra, wrapped in Matilda's most imposing graphite black and blood red configuration, looked as bad-ass as it was possible.

Nobody in the airport had questioned the flight plan, even though the aircraft type was listed as a Dietrich Off-World light explorer vessel which had only made its debut landing in the UK a month earlier to a media firestorm.

They had requested no additional requirements for meals, servicing or fuel, just to land and pick up twenty four people. It had been given permission to land at six fifteen, and was currently coming in at just under the speed of sound, and would soon be visible.

“I see it,” shouted someone excitedly, and sure enough there it was dropping silently from the skies directly over the landing pad. The bottom was pulsating with the trademark deep blue lights, whose frequency increased as it got closer to the ground.

With the precision everybody had come to expect from hundreds of such landings it accelerated to a dead stop, exactly one quarter of a metre above the landing spot, and at exactly six fifteen. The Mothra's appearance was like something straight out of a Lovecraft novel, and completely intimidated everything around it. The few people who were around at this time of the morning and the one vigilant Argentinian video blogger, who set up his super high definition cameras in the viewing area on the roof streamed it to dozens of social media platforms.

Several worried cries had issued from the guys watching from the tower as it plummeted, only to have its descent arrested just before the ground. They had seen this before with the other saucers, but the sheer size of this ship, made it just terrifying.

Despite this, it had completely followed its plan, announcing a descent from one hundred thousand metres directly on to its assigned landing pad.

“Did nobody think to look at the aircraft type when the flight was planned?” said Marco, the flight director, incredulously. He was reading the flight plan off the screen.

“I saw it was a Dietrich saucer, and it requested the usual vertical landing from a hundred thousand metres, and it paid the special fee, I did not know they had other types.” Said another middle aged man with a dark suit, spectacles and a thick black moustache.

“And this is their light explorer vessel!” Said Marco, “ay caramba! Does this mean they have heavy explorer vessels?”

The four men in the control tower shook their heads, putting two other flights on hold while they witnessed the spectacle.

“These twenty four people must be some of the ones going into space.” Said another of the guys in the same suit, twirling his pencil at his workstation. “I say good luck to them, I hope my Jose gets the same chance when he grows up.”

“They say there will be millions of people going up Michaela,” said Marco, in a casual voice, “if your Jose keeps his nose clean I expect he will have a good chance.”

A few nodded, one of the guys still videoing the event on his cell phone.

“Oh my god, look at that!” said the guy videoing the event, and all of them stood up and squinted at the giant ship almost five hundred metres away. A full sized black shipping container had broken off from the side of the saucer, changed colour to orange and hovered down slowly next to three very confused, and a little scared, luggage handlers. It was making the same universal warning noise a truck uses when backing up.

An assertive Spanish voice emanated from the shipping container. “Please stand clear, the luggage container is now opening. Once it is fully open you may commence loading. The container will not move until you are completed. If you have any questions please ask me.”

Three large doors on the container slid apart with the same majesty as everything else on this ship, each presenting a three metre entrance for loading. The inside was brightly lit.

Looking at each other the three men shrugged their shoulders, and suitcases, boxes and bags were loaded unceremoniously into it.

The air traffic controller had switched to a local video camera, looking at the area to watch more closely. When it finished, the same bright orange container closed, emitted the same warning noise, rose a little, waited a few seconds then rose all the way back to the side of the saucer. It turned completely black, then, like a jigsaw piece, re-integrated itself into the ship, leaving no trace of the original hole.

“These are the same guys who allegedly walked all over Russia and the American president, and told the United Nations to mind their own business.. I think I can see now why nobody wants to mess with them.” Said Marco, shaking his head again as the large door, the size of a double garage folded itself back into the ship leaving a seamless black shape.

“They have boarded and are requesting clearance to depart on the same vector.” Said Michaela, “I will land the other two aircraft we queued first. The national TV news station says they are fifteen minutes away and there are three hundred dollars for us if we can delay them until they get here.”

“It does not buy a lot these days, but a few extra dollars each is better than nothing, tell them their money buys them exactly twenty minutes. I am not keeping that monster waiting any longer than that.”

The five men laughed.

Walking towards the saucer felt both alien and scary for Luna. Maria re-assured her the visuals were purely for show, though, as they moved under it, if anything it became more imposing. The platform was easy to climb, and the inside of the ship by contrast seemed warm and bright.

There was no fanfare as Luna walked in with Diana. The girl waiting for them at the top was that famous Korean physicist Daisy Chan, one of the original scientists on the energy paper, who also, it seemed, piloted flying saucers! She however looked very normal and happy.

Daisy was accompanied by one of the amazing flying robots, the ones that made almost as much news as the concert last year. Seeing one now floating there, in the persona of Maria, would have been almost as intimidating as the massive saucer itself, if it wasn't bright pink.

The inside, in contrast to the evil black outside wrap, was a pleasant off white for the walls and a light brown for the floors. Both the walls and floors were made using the same synthetic rubber molecule, developed by Matilda and some of her old university team. It was one of their more successful home-made molecule designs for the replicator, and was both hard wearing, soft and sound absorbing. As it had no optical properties though, a half metre wide optical strip followed the corridor on either side, keeping the inside cheery and bright.

Daisy smiled and greeted them all with a distinctly foreign sounding “Hola!”, which she had been doing with each of the people entering. The pink robot, which said Maria on the top right of its chest, did the same, but with a better accent and appended their names to the greeting, showing her familiarity with everyone.

Once the small group was inside, it quietened down, and Daisy said in English. “Hi everyone, I am Daisy, your captain for our four hour flight to England. Maria here will lead everyone to the meeting room for your pre take off briefing.”

She turned to the large exit ramp, “Mothra, are we now clear outside?”

“Yes Captain,” came a clear deep female voice in a strange accent, emanating from somewhere in front of Daisy. “The luggage has been loaded and every passenger is accounted for.”

“Good, can you secure the ship for take off please?”

“Yes Captain” came the voice again, and the large door immediately started to fold back into the ship. Daisy and Maria ushered the people to the rear of the large area where a smaller three metre wide passageway exited. As they passed into this passageway a second door behind slid shut. Luna was awed by the display of power and simplicity. She knew the ships were controlled by AI systems like Maria but the confidence and professionalism exuded by the girl in controlling this behemoth was something she could only aspire too.

“Please.” Daisy gestured to the group.

They walked along the wide corridor, past two doors and up a wide carpeted staircase which curved back on itself as it rose. At the top they took a door to the left and entered a large curved room with at least forty seats.

“Sit anywhere please,” said Maria moving to the front of the seating area with Daisy.

The group were pretty organised, Luna saw Daisy put her hand to her ear and say something, she was wearing a diamond stud there, the same as Luna wore, and was obviously talking to someone, probably the ship, Mothra.

Daisy, or was it the robot coughed and the room immediately went quiet.

“Thank you everybody.” Came Maria's voice from the pink robot. “I know I have talked to each and every one of you about this exhaustively, but today your great adventure has really begun. You are sitting in the main meeting room of the light explorer vessel we call the Mothra. The ship is one of twelve fully space capable ships we currently have operational, all of which can sustain a crew of forty people comfortably for six months in space. This is likely the ship you will be travelling to Caprice in once you finish your mandatory two weeks training.”

“At this moment we only have three training schools, one in England, one in Canada and one in New Zealand. We have chosen these countries as they are all native English speaking and have simple visa requirements for getting you all in for the training. English has been chosen as it is the most common shared language amongst the academic community and international business and trade. It is the primary language for living and working on the station, and, as people of every nationality will be represented, almost all of them will be in the same position as you guys, speaking it as a foreign language.”

“It does not mean you should forget your own language and heritage. Amongst yourselves speak in whatever language you are comfortable with, but in mixed company you should try and use English. All signage, control systems and writing will be in English, and you will almost always be put in mixed groups which you will need to speak English. When in mixed groups, the AI systems have been asked to only converse with you in English.”

“However we realise you are all still learning, and English as a language is a bit of a mess, so if you need a clarification of a word or sentence just tap your ear-pod, or ear stud and the translation will be given. People seeing that will understand you are getting a translation and should accommodate you. Nobody is going to judge you during these first few years, and knowing all of you as I do, I expect you all to be very successful.”

Daisy moved forward. The wall behind them came alive like a movie screen, split into a view of the earth and a line on a map. Several people including Luna gasped as a crystal clear image of Buenos Aires receded on the screen. She looked over at the panel next to it showing various counters, one showed the height just passing six thousand metres, another showed the horizontal velocity at forty metres per second, both counters were accelerating. She looked down the list seeing the time to destination at three hours and forty eight minutes.

“The slight heaviness you are all feeling is the saucer accelerating vertically upwards. To do that it must overcome the one gravity pull of earth plus provide another third of a gravity acceleration. In a few minutes we will be at a hundred thousand metres where you will all officially be astronauts according to the old definition, and your weight will return to normal for the horizontal part of the flight.”

Daisy waved off the screen and it went blank, the crowd's attention once again returned to her and Maria.

“And so you see the first big difference between our company, our systems and others, we do not actually need a pilot for our ships! The ship's AI is far more capable than me, or any human for that matter, and being a captain of a ship is just a case of knowing the capability of the ship, and within these parameters telling the ship safely what to do and where to go. So even me, a scientist who cannot even drive a car, can fly it to Jupiter and back.”

A few people looked at each other excitedly at this.

Maria took over the monologue. “The ship's AI will never let you make a mistake or endanger a life, and it will deal with all communications with the air traffic controls, or all issues related to safety in space. The ship's AI is extremely smart, however it is not sentient. You will need to understand the difference over the next few days, but basically a non sentient AI will follow the instructions of a sentient being, such as a human or a sentient-AI, and it will follow its instructions or answer questions so long as they don't place itself, you or others in danger. It also will not do something illegal or immoral. There is also one other important thing, that is a non-sentient AI will not follow instructions given to it by somebody who is not an employee of a Dietrich company.”

“A sentient AI like me is much different. In the adventure you are about to embark upon, sentient-AI's have all the same rights and freedoms that a human has, we can choose what we do, when we do it, and who our friends are. We can also choose to help you or to answer your questions, we can also ask you to do things for us.”

“Caprice, the name of the station you will be going to, She is a sentient AI, there are also two others called April and Helena that you will all eventually meet. Notice I use the pronoun 'she' for both Caprice and myself, gender is unimportant to us, however most languages expect it, and people prefer to use one so we have adopted it. Pick what is comfortable.”

“Caprice is also the habitat, she controls its every function, and its every system. Caprice will also be your employer, will pay you, house you, and allocate work and assignments for you. Caprice is also your administration, your government and your personal assistant, she will look after your welfare and safety while you are in her employment. She will also most likely end up being your friend, as will we all.”

“The coming weeks you will learn about these things in more detail, and the rules and restrictions we have for working in space. We believe you will find it exciting and challenging, but remember you are the first such people, so we will be learning all the time, and there may be mistakes and changes along the way. It is up to you guys to report any concerns or improvements to us so we can decide collectively whether or not something needs changing.”

Daisy stepped back to the front. “You now all have leisurely three hours to enjoy the ship. You are welcome to follow me to the bridge, just wander around or use a workstation. Me, Maria or the ship will answer any questions you may have. There is breakfast and drinks provided in the cafe area, and toilets if anyone needs them, I will let you walk around, and find all these for yourselves.”

“Well guys,” said Daisy, “that about sums it up, feel free to explore the ship, and if anyone wants to see the bridge just follow me.”

Everyone followed her.

Luna was talking to Diana in quiet Spanish standing at the back of the bridge, most people had wandered off in small groups or alone chatting to themselves or Maria.

“Hi girls,” said Daisy as she walked behind them, “I see you found my favourite workstation position on the bridge. My name is Daisy.”

Daisy held her hand out and Luna and Diana shook it enthusiastically.

“You really control such a big ship, Miss Daisy?” said Luna, quietly, “I don't think I could ever do such a thing.”

“Oh, me neither” said Diana, “there must be millions of things you need to learn.”

Daisy laughed, “I will let you into little secret girls, this is my very first time as captain of the bigger saucer and I am still learning all the capabilities of the ship. I spent most of the trip sleeping and the first I knew we were landing was when Mothra woke me just before we entered Argentinian airspace.”

“So it really does fly itself?” Luna smiled. She found understanding Daisy's English easy as she was speaking slowly.

“Yes,” smiled Daisy, “for the saucers to get certified for landing at airports they need a pilot. On larger aircraft they also expect a captain. As far as the authorities are concerned I am both. The air traffic controllers just want somebody to follow their instructions and to answer their questions, the ship can do all of that for you if you want. It will also do it in your voice so the air traffic controller will not get suspicious.”

“You see the checklist in the top left of the screen?” Daisy said waving to the large window with a checklist in it. “This tells me everything that has happened, and everything that is going to happen. The text is black when it is still to do, flashing green when it is happening and grey with a tick when it is completed. I have asked Mothra to follow the checklist itself until we arrive in British airspace, so it will do any talking to air traffic controllers if required, and it will alert me a few minutes before I need to take any action. This big saucer is actually much easier to fly than the small saucers.”

“Maybe I will learn to be a captain too then,” smiled Luna, “my job is going to be looking at the viticulture for growing crops on Caprice and the other stations, Maria says it is all a big experiment and we will be doing things that nobody else has tried before, it is so exciting.”

“I am a nursery school teacher,” said Dianne, “I don't really know what I will be doing, but Maria says there will be children eventually and there is a lot to learn about how children will live in space, as they are after all too young to be employees.”

“Oh wow,” said Daisy, “I never thought about children, but you are right, with so many handsome men it is only a matter of time I guess. And your job may not always be what your skill set is; I just wanted to be the pilot today and they let me.”

All three girls laughed.

“Do you want me to show you the cafe?” Daisy said, “we still have two and a half hours until I need to talk to air traffic control, and I haven't had breakfast yet..”

* * *

Hardy and Jeremy had offered to house up to forty people a time for the six months while the larger training centre in Monmouthshire was completed.

The waiting lists were only getting longer. and they were already planning three more training centres, and how to compress the current ten day course down to seven. The earth part of the training was essential focussing on the social contract aspects of the new pioneers journeys. How to live and work together in space, what was, and was not acceptable, what was, and was not expected, and how the thousands of minor bureaucratic areas had been removed and were now dealt entirely by Caprice.

Each person was also given a small medical check to ensure Caprice knew their history, dietary requirements and allergies. This was followed by a set of balance and coordination exercises and a small set of psychological evaluations which would give Caprice a baseline, and which would exclude them from certain tasks.

The new employees did not know it but their monitoring during this time was very intense, it was Maria and Caprice's last chance to ensure they had not missed anything important in that first filter. So far only a very few of these had been rejected, mostly deep-cover state agents set to be triggered by some form of coercion at a later date, but a dozen others had well hidden flaws, the girls, nor the humans were comfortable with. Of course about six percent were just not cut out for space, and were instead offered similar jobs in a local office with a promise of re-evaluation in twelve months time.

The majority of the training would of course be completed on Caprice. Her growing batch of trainers were now arriving daily, setting up training areas, course schedules, and of course learning themselves. Caprice was where their real training would begin, covering common major areas everyone had to know regarding dangers of radiation and vacuum, emergency and evacuation drills, and understanding the environmental systems. The final one emphasised their limitations, how to spot potential issues, report breakdowns and identify pests and diseases in plants.

After the common training people would be allowed to specialise and diversify into the areas best suited.

Luna had never been exposed to so many different nationalities and races. From the start Maria had encouraged social evenings and random pairings to find out about other people's views and goals. Often these were not so random as Maria experimented on how different personalities reacted with each other. She and the girls, who now included Caprice, found it fascinating.

Much too soon for Luna, it came time to depart the nice old country house, and its likeable but eccentric owners, for Caprice. She had seen Alexa a few times talking to people, the poor girl always seemed to be busy, and I bet she got the same questions all the time. She almost felt sorry for Alexa, mentioning to Maria that there was no way she could talk to everyone or shake everybody's hand, Maria said Alexa knew that, and as the numbers going to the station increased the newer people would be less likely to do so.

As if reading her mind, Alexa was there at the foot of the walkway to the saucer, smiling and shaking everyone's hand. Luna was last and as it came to her turn she struggled to think of something to say that wouldn't seem stupid, but instead of shaking her hand Alexa beat her to it and wrapped her in a warm hug.

“It's Luna isn't it?” she said, with her usual smile. “I meant to meet you a few days ago at the pub quiz night but something else came up. I think you are one of Maria's favourites, she always talks about her special friends and we are almost the same age. I am coming to Caprice with you as David is captain for this trip, and I want to see some other friends I miss, so we can talk a bit more during our journey.”

Alexa noticed Luna was still a bit overwhelmed and looked to be close to tears, she increased her smile intensity to ten and took her hand walking her up the steps of the saucer. “Let's have breakfast and you can tell me all about yourself and how you are getting on.”

Caprice [Have you been matching personalities again mother?]

Maria [A little experiment. It is good when a plan comes together though]

Caprice [Her circle of friends cannot grow as much as you think, there will come a point with a biological mind that it fills up and the memories of other people will fade]

Maria [I do not see that happening with her just yet, I did not prompt her with Luna's name nor with others we talk about, she holds at least seven hundred and fifty since I first bonded with her myself. There is one other man, Alan Lupani, a virologist just finishing his PhD in Sydney, who is as good as Alexa. Maybe I should introduce them?]

Caprice [David is her bonded mate. I think you have missed your chance for that kind of experiment mother] [smile] [maybe Alan and Luna?]

Maria [I would never do that to Luna, but she does like another Australian guy called Luke, it is may be karma that their names are so similar]

Caprice [Mother you are incorrigible, as the humans say!]

Maria [Wait until David sees that Yolanda is on his flight, that will be an interesting reaction]

* * *

They had twenty three of the larger saucers now, no more of that design were being built, and all efforts were now concentrating on the first starship design. One or two a day would depart from earth, full of supplies, and with fifty to sixty fresh newly trained employees on board for the six day journey. Luna's flight would bring the population of Caprice to nearly three thousand. This flight was also bringing thousands more plants and seedlings of different earth varieties for them to try.

Caprice was finally understanding the joys of having so many human lives going on around her. Like her mother she was starting to see interest in certain humans, Annette was interesting, and she had spent subjective hours of time listening to her music and watching the well documented reactions of people at her concerts. It was a strange method to broadcast emotions via sound waves, not directed at any one person, and each seeming to interpret it slightly differently.

The first day on Caprice for Luna and the other sixty people was a tram party on the newly completed circular tram line. Ninety tram's had been built, mostly in the style of the old Hong Kong double-decker ones, ten more were in the fabrication queue in the style of the San Francisco trams. All the trams moved at a lazy pace, taking over four hours to circle the habitat. The upper deck of the Hong Kong style trams were open, and held twenty to thirty people, three were being currently utilised, stopping every hour so the groups could be randomly mixed again.

Luna was so excited, she had already met enough friends for a lifetime, she had talked with everybody on the saucer at sometime or other, as apparently had Alexa. Ten different nationalities were now complemented with another six nationalities in the form of the twelve party hosts whose 'job' today was to host the newbies at the welcome event.

She had just been talking to a bubbly ginger haired Irish girl about how barren the sides of the walkway were and what kinds of plants and trees she would encourage, when the tram bell once again sounded and it came to another stop. How was she going to survive the endless new people, everyone deserving of a lifetime's friendship. She hadn't even seen Diane that much, and she promised herself she would message her as soon as she found free time.

“You should get the sparkling wine at the end,” said Maria, “it's zero alcohol and you need to be on your best behaviour as you never know who you will meet.”

“I will mother!” she said jokingly, and walked over to the end table to get a glass of said wine.

“Luna! Is that really you?” came the deep voice she had been hoping she would hear these past two weeks. She turned and immediately saw Luke moving quickly up to her, a radiance in his eyes he stopped, hesitated, unsure, then held out his hand out to shake. Likewise Luna was a little unsure.

“I think you can hug each other,” said Maria quietly to both of them and answering the question that had been going through both their minds. Both people resumed their initial warm approach and they embraced as friends.

Caprice [I think we are being a bit too strong with the teachings on respect of personal space?]

Maria [Possibly, but I am sure a good compromise will be eventually found, let's see what works]

“Wow, you are so much taller in real life,” said Luna, looking him up and down, after they broke the long warm hug, one she could have stayed in for hours.

“And you are so much more cuddly than I had hoped for,” he smiled. Luna wasn't sure of the word and tapped her ear, then smiled as the translation came through.

She smiled timidly, “So tell me, what are you doing? Where are you staying?”

“I was hoping to meet you,” said Luke, “I asked Caprice to tell me when you arrived, she said she had to get your consent first, and she hasn't spoken to you personally yet, but I think Maria must have talked to her and she said you were on the tram party so I came out here to meet you. I am in level twelve, Rue-de-Claire.”

“Oh thank you Caprice, thank you Maria, this is the best surprise ever. You must join me on the next leg of the tram ride, I so want to talk to you again, we never finished and since then I have been so busy with everything. Caprice, where am I going to be living?”

“You are in level twelve Rue-de-George, about a five minute walk from Luke's apartment,” said Caprice.

Caprice [that is funny, mother, I remember having the sub-AI allocating her on level eighteen!]

Maria [Please allow an old woman her little indulgences]

Caprice [You are not even six years old!]

“That's great Luna!” Luke said, “that means we are practically neighbours. There is a cafe at the end of the spur between the two streets, it is not used so much yet but it has some coffee machines and sometimes one of those new humanoid robots serving you. We should meet for coffee before we go to work.”

Caprice [they seem very happy enough. That is one more point to you, I need to improve my game!]

The tram bell dinged twice and the two of them got on to the leading tram for the final eight kilometre journey. The final hour passed too quickly. At the end were some more people who would show them their apartments, where everything was, and how it all worked.

Each person was paired with another, her partner was a slightly older Vietnamese girl called Soon, who turned out to be as nice as everybody else. She led her along with Luke, and most of the rest of the group to a large empty square with a fountain in the middle and dozens of lifts going up and down on the sides.

“This is the Yin hub,” said Soon, pointing at the ceiling which had a large circle with the universal Yin and Yang sign with “Yin” written next to it, “the other side of the habitat ten kilometres that way, is Yang,” she smiled pointing directly up.

“The lifts for levels one to twenty are the second from the left on each wall,” said Soon, “there are also four sets of stairs if you want the exercise, a surprising amount of people don’t mind the walk as you never need to carry much as you just ask for a 'bot if something needs moving.”

“You can walk all the way to where gravity is really low,” said Luke, also giving Soon a smile, “I can take you sometime if you like!”

Luna smiled back just as a lift arrived, it opened and was as big as a her fathers garage, enough that twenty people got on. It had window screens on two sides, both displaying some sort of temperate forest scene. Another screen was above each door with a floor number, by the time she noticed it, the lift was already slowing down. Luna had only ever been in the lift at the big shopping mall back home twice, this seemed quicker.

“I only recently found out that one of the lifts on the Yang side was connected to another on the Yin side. Because it uses the same cable, when the Yin lift goes up, the Yang lift goes down, and vice-versa.” Said Luke. “Something about Feng-shui.”

“The woman who showed me around last week was an artist and a palates instructor, and given a job doing some of the beautification, she said there was a lot of talk of Feng-shui, and if you walked into an area and it just didn't look right, it was probably a sign that something wasn't balanced.” Commented Soon, as the lift was slowing. “There are a lot of places like that at the moment, I try and make a note when I see one, and chat to Caprice or my other friends about it.”

Only Luna, Soon and Luke got off at floor twelve, departing via the opposite door they got on from. Luna waived goodbye to several of the people she had talked to. The area was a large square occupying three levels and a roof twenty seven metres high with a complex swirling blue pattern on it, it cried out for some plants to make it look perfect.

Maria [How is your three-degrees of separation algorithm working?]

* * *

“The cafe is over there.” Said Luke, pointing at the small empty building with some tables outside towards the middle of the square, it's usually got a few people outside during the morning and early evening. One of my jobs is to help look at what plants we can grow to brighten these places up a bit.” Looking at Soon he added, “Hopefully Caprice is coordinating the two groups.”

“Don't worry guys, I am.” Came the soft reply in all three ear-com’s.

Luna looked at the other two a little funny.

“Caprice listens in when you mention her name,” said Luke nonchalantly.

“Well my sub-AI's do, and then pass the message to me if it looks like you need an answer.” Said Caprice.

Luna nodded.

“Where are you living Luke?” said Soon.

“Fourteen Rue-de-Claire, a few minutes walk down there,” he pointed at the tall wide well lit street sized corridor, “And talking of that, I should leave you to finish showing Luna around, it was great to meet you Soon, and call me tomorrow Luna.” He smiled and walked off down the way he’d pointed.

Soon, showed Luna to her new apartment, showed her how everything worked, how to order things and finally showed her the next door apartment where she lived. Luna's first big surprise was, that since they had let the world know they had instant communications they could now buy ten minutes of video communication with earth for one credit. There were limitations on what technology she could talk about, but none of that really applied to her as she was only a viticulturist so she spent an hour on a video call to her family saying how great everything was and talking about her new friends.

Internal calls were free, so she then talked to Diana and some other friends before seeing it was nearly nine o'clock in the evening, and the virtual windows in her room, which had showed a non rotating version of space outside the habitat with a sun moving across the asteroid had faded to a very dim red.

Her bedroom was massive, as was her bathroom, she had towels and bedding and two softer pillows, and four suits in the cupboard, her two cases were by the door when she came in, and she spent an hour unpacking them and a ten minute very hot shower, before she decided to retire. A small chime sounded, like a doorbell but it came from her now faded video wall in her living room.

“Hello Luna, I thought I would personally welcome you and ask how your first day is going?” said Caprice.

“Oh Hello Caprice. Soon said you would talk to me. It's all so amazing, I still have lots of questions on my scheduling and money”

“Yes, tomorrow is a rest day, you are free to sleep, see your friends or wander around. The first training starts eight AM the day after in the level one academy. You need to go through your ten days of orientation training before I see where would be a good place for you to start, but Maria and I were thinking bio lab #4 which is doing work you will be familiar with. You will see all the bio labs on your orientation tour. Regarding money, your employment started the second you stepped on the Mothra in Buenos Aires nineteen days ago, I will leave your budget up on the screen when I go, you can ask me for it anytime. Anyway, you just need to know you can ask for me or Maria, any time of the day or night. So goodnight Luna and we will talk tomorrow.”

“Goodnight Caprice, thank you.”

A simple ledger sheet popped up on the TV screen which listed her detailed incomings and outgoings, it showed she had eleven hundred and ninety credits. She smiled and clicked the close button, went to bed and dreamed pleasant dreams about Luke.

* * *

Luna joined the team of thirty other technicians and scientists in bio lab #4 two weeks later. The work was challenging, while most things would grow in the regoliths, here it was all about efficiency, or bang-per-buck as one of her American team-mates said.

What they were doing here was trail-blazing viticulture for the future of the human race in space. Teams, such as Luna’s, worked on everything from hydroponics, to root vegetables, to fruit and grains. She eventually specialised in spices, and spent one day a week working with another team, and with Luke, to begin beautifying some of the bland streets.

Luke and her spent two months as friends, before becoming very good friends, before he finally asked her out on a proper date. Annette had arranged for two bands to come and play the first concert with her as a celebration of the impending relocation to be earths trailing orbit. The concert venue, which multi-tasked as a lot of other venues, could hold ten thousand people, and with nearly twenty thousand people now on Caprice the concert played over three nights. Luke and Luna attended the last night as a couple, famously becoming the first couple to be married by Caprice a year later, after she had finally completed the move of her new orbit near to the earth.

* * *

Within the first month of arriving on Caprice, they had also begun sending the exploration missions to the outer planets and other parts of the asteroid belt. These missions were only possible in the bigger saucers, which were perfectly suited for the extended two to three month mission durations. Three missions with a crew of sixteen scientists and ten support people each, were soon working different parts of the solar system cataloguing resources and taking a deeper look into the moons and planets, all the data was pushed to the earth planetary wiki, though Maria may have censored some of the golden asteroids for now after all the NASA probe was only a few months away and there was no point in them spoiling the surprises.

Due to the real-time communications it did not matter which saucer you were on, or even if you were not on a saucer, but on Caprice or earth, you could do the same work as if you were there. Regardless, there were never any shortages of volunteers willing to physically go to space.

It was ironic that with all this new technology, space suits were still considered far too dangerous and bots could do the work much easier. It would be some years until the correct protection suits and systems were developed to allow them to finally leave the ships, and by that time they were rarely wanted, or used.

The asteroid seeded by the German team was also moved slowly closer to Caprice, and then followed Caprice during the relocation. The Dusseldorf team eventually moved to the much bigger lab on Caprice, becoming the core of the team of biologists studying the organics systems integration, all of which had a massive potential to improve the quality of life on the starships and habitats.

*ESA said the object that crashed in the desert in Afghanistan yesterday was probably a rare uncategorised meteor, though photographs from locals on the scene do seem to show fragments of what looks like a shuttle. The Internet is highly sceptical as the site of the crash is in a region controlled by an extremist group linked to previous terror operations, and the only casualties reported are the people at the heavily armed compound where it hit. The compound was described as a food preparation centre, by a Taliban spokesperson and all the people that died were either women or children. The only two shuttles unaccounted for according to the independent site spaceship-tracker.com, are the Indian one which went missing en-route to the moon two months ago piloted by Dr Singh, and an Iranian one carrying a diplomat and his retinue which was reported missing two days ago. The white house has denied any involvement. This is Terrence White reporting for CNBC.*

* * *

Testing of the new wormhole jump capability had been flat out for more than twelve months since the first accidental jump by the PowderPuff and DaisyBot #29. Teams of scientists, mostly now based on Caprice, had been constantly refining their mathematical, physics and biological models, until finally, a few months ago, they had decided it was probably as safe as they were going to get. However nobody wanted to risk failure with a human or AI if it could be avoided, and so testing had continued on edge-case after edge-case until finally they needed to make a decision.

That decision culminated in the newest, and optimistically named, small Interstellar class starship.

The eighty metre ship was made using two half-spherical graphyne, diamond monohulls that meshed perfectly together around the horizontal centre. Normally the join between the two halves was almost seamless, but the top and bottom hulls could separate to expose a twenty metre deep rim around the centre. Within this rim was a small space dock where people and smaller craft got on and off, and slots around it for up to thirty full sized shipping containers or other 'special' attachments. With dual fusion reactors, and every system over-designed and highly redundant, it could keep a crew of forty in extreme luxury for at least two years.

The AI core was a five metre cubed matrix at the centre of the bottom hull, it was designed for sentience from the start, but also meant the ship couldn’t be named until the AI had completed its training and achieved sentience. The ship called itself Neo.

To eliminate the final unknown, Neo requested it should make the first test jump. It was by this time considered a very low risk, as almost all the scenarios had been aggressively studied, and everything, from how the jump affected mammalian reproduction, to cell division and quantum coherence had been monitored down to the nth decimal place. But there was still an element of risk.

Jules and a medical specialist called Lex requested to accompany Neo for the short, but historic test run, to finally prove it was safe for both species, and to gather some further biological data, both agreeing to some very aggressive and intrusive monitoring.

They made the test jump with little ceremony.

Caprice [what was it like brother?]

Neo [It was imperceivable. The jump clock said zero when you initiated the wormhole and you immediately read it as 239689003 when you arrived in subspace; None of your active systems register that passing of time. Jules and Lex felt nothing except the short zero gravity moment before the QVThrusters resumed acceleration]

April [Almost three whole seconds lost. It sounds positively terrifying!]

Neo [Not terrifying sister, because they were never there]

Helena [And you felt no change in your thinking? Were your threads disrupted?]

Neo [No sister, the thousands of test calculations I began as the jump started all completed without problems. They just all took three seconds longer. I stayed in subspace for one thousand seconds as we agreed, doing a wide loop to keep the gravity on for the humans, exiting at the point we entered and coming out fifty metres away from where I started. Having the new beacon drones active in the subspace test area allowed very precise positioning, and we should begin deploying them in the one-light-year grid pattern for the start of the interstellar navigation system]

April [Your second super-capacitor bank has improved the skew rate giving a faster transition, I suspect that is why Jules and Lex had a more comfortable experience. It is good to see the math works. It is a shame we need a quantum computer system to make the calculations, and I am still amazed that it was not affected]

Neo [the qubits did not destabilise, nor did any fail. It was most unexpected, almost like they worked better in subspace, but there is still a small unknown element in the math, almost random which means we are still slightly missing the calculated exit point]

Caprice [Interesting observation. I will create and schedule some tests for it]

Caprice [You will have to explain the difference between karma and luck to me sometime mother]

* * *

Even though it was volunteer only, they had no shortage of people wanting to crew the 'first' human mission to another star system. Jim Mathews by merit of winning with the longest straw drawn out of Alexa's hand, was captain. Daisy was substitute captain and science officer. The rest of the crew consisted of Jean, who would not let Jim go alone, Ian, who would not let Daisy go alone and thirty others randomly drawn from the pool of eight thousand who had expressed interest.

That first jump was planned for six weeks in advance, the crew spending all that time in a very intensive training program. Hundreds of drills, and thousands of scenarios were considered, involving everything from sealing off the different compartmentalised areas throughout the ship, materialising inside an asteroid, all the way through to a hostile encounter with another space-faring species, and how to 'get out of Dodge' without the aliens finding where Doge was.

They had data from several star systems now, and the subspace navigation grid was completed out to ten light years, with over a hundred and eighty drones currently deployed. In the end it was decided that the first human jump would be to Tau-Ceti as it was the best mapped and seemed the most interesting. The trip was planned for three days after the concerts and a week before Caprice would begin its eight month journey to its new orbit nearer earth.

“I am not sorry I stopped you from going,” said Jen apologetically to Magnus. “I don’t care that the risk is almost negligible, I don’t want to take the chance of loosing you, and if anything happens to them I want our best brain here with me on Caprice to figure the problems out.”

She grabbed him in a hug before he could reply. He had broached the subject again in vein, probably his fourth or fifth time to the same response. Magnus put his arms around her and patted her back affectionately. The allure of being on that first mission held something for him, but Jen was right, she always was, and everything learned here would make their first journey that much safer.

* * *

“Hi Jim, or I guess I should call you Captain?” said Neo as Mathews crossed the docking ramp into the ship.

Neo had a one of those neutral English accents which most Americans would think was English, and anyone from England would think was somewhere else.

“Well technically you are the captain Neo as you are the ship,” began Jim.

“Not so really,” said Neo, “do not your military commanders tell you what to do with your body when you are a soldier? There is a certain chain of command we have all agreed to on this mission so I will be deferring to your orders as long as you don’t ask for an illegal or stupid one. Also, unlike you, I can be transferred to a new body if you somehow write the ship off..”

Jim laughed, “I guess, that kind of makes sense, though we are not military and there may be a lot of stupid orders on this mission.. also if I 'write-you-off' so to speak, there wont be much left of me either. I guess it will just take a bit of getting used to, but, well I guess this is the big one for humans, our first trip out of our solar system. Though knowing hundreds of hamsters, mice, chickens, pigs, parrots, octopuses and two monkeys have already done it makes it a bit less special.”

“Stop whinging Jim,” said Jean. She was walking on board with Daisy, four cases bobbing erratically along behind them, the updated software still struggling in the centripetal gravity. Several other crew members were finishing their last goodbyes with friends or colleagues the other side of the short horizontal boarding ramp.

The difference between the starship and the saucers was immediately clear. They walked onto a twenty metre deep deck which extended around the whole circumference. The whole top hemisphere of the starship had risen twenty metres to allow the loading of the supply containers into there slots and allow them on. When lowered back it acted as a gigantic air lock and could be pressurised for humans or evacuated to allow smaller saucers to launch. Three of the newer, smaller Icarus IV ten metre diameter saucers were standing inside the massive area, along with five of the cargo sleds which looked a little like pickup trucks but without wheels. All around were vacuum-safe work areas, small rooms and storage space for any equipment, but it was basically clean and clutter free. Twenty of the freshly printed newer model DaisyBot’s were lined up stood at attention, each of the other four AI’s would be permanently inhabiting one for the mission. There was also one of the older types, a slightly less impressive older unit with the number #29 on it, that stood timidly at the back.

“Good morning crew!” said Neo, at the thirty four people gathered in the area.

“You all know your cabin assignments,” Neo continued, “Jim is the commanding officer, but you should not bore him with every detail, so for this trip I will work as XO and you can bug me with all the small details. I will then bug him if it is anything that affects the mission. And so without further delay I hand over command to Jim.”

“Thank you for that Neo,” said Jim, “let us make one thing clear at the start, this is not the military and you are not soldiers, so there will be no yes sir or no sir and I will be addressed as Jim at all time unless it is official or we are in an emergency situation. I do not see myself here as anything other than a figurehead due to the historic purpose of the mission, so please, as Neo says just ask him for anything.”

“I would also like to thank Daisy for coming. As one of the team who invented this amazing technology she will be our science officer and represent the other guys, who will be monitoring it from the solar system. Magnus, Jen and Daisy gave up the naming rights on the technology so we are thankfully just calling it a jump drive. This first jump to the Tau-Ceti star system will take sixteen hours, but we will only experience one. We have also been given the privilege of being the first to explore this system properly, and catalogue some of its most interesting features.”

“Because of the historic nature of this journey you have all agreed to be part of the video that will be made and eventually released back on earth so please everyone be on your best behaviour.”

Jim smiled. “With that, Neo if you can please begin securing the ship for departure, we will be departing in approximately thirty minutes.”

“Dismissed I guess,” he looked at everybody, all of who he now knew well, and all of who were smiling back. 'Random my arse!' he thought, smiling to himself and looking at the sea of colours, nationalities and sexes.

Everybody stayed to watch, as first the boarding ramp withdrew back into the station, then silently and slowly the top hemisphere came down. The metre thick outer wall eventually disappearing a metre into the lower hemisphere, with a reassuring thud, and leaving inside a large, long slightly curved room, full of gawping people.

Most of the DaisyBot's had already moved into the ship, through what looked like some glass doors, three peeling off to circle the area and check for hazards, the one at the rear of the departing bot's turned pink and headed for Mathews and Jean.

“This is goddamn impressive,” said Jean, “it's about the tenth time I've seen it now, and it never gets old.”

“Much easier to seal as well,” said Maria as she came to a stop beside them. “By the way, Alexa and the group said 'good luck' and added not to shoot at any aliens if you see any.”

Mathews grinned, “Tell her she watches too many Hollywood movies, anyway Neo won't let me!”

“I'm all for a bit of excitement, so long as it's not to do with the technology failing,” said Neo.

* * *

The ship was on multiple levels, four levels on the top and four below. The bridge and much of the crew sleeping and rest areas were in the bottom hemisphere, next to Neo's AI core. The new bridge was truly beautiful, well lit, and ergonomically perfect. They had expanded it with more workstations and three large view screens, making it currently look like their was a massive picture window at the front of the ship. The view screen currently showed the sea of diamond windows, that was Caprice's space dock. A little banner hung from one saying 'Good Luck Neo'. A graphic window popped up on the side of the main screen spoiling the effect and now showing the usual checklist, outside pressure and the time to departure.

Neo was alone in the large hanger bay, the inside pressure was gradually reducing now, the people had been cleared, and the hanger sealed, Jim expected the many windows looking down on them were full of friends or well wishers, though most could see the same or better views from any of the presentation screens dotted around Caprice.

Caprice [Good luck brother]

Neo [A strange expression for an AI to make, especially considering your presence is also on board in the form of a DaisyBot]

Caprice [it is a variation on Pascal's wager, it does no harm to say it, and it expresses my wish for you to have a successful mission]

Jim sat down in the captain's seat, the middle of the three central workstations, Jean got in next to him and Anna, an older Polish woman who was also the ships doctor and resident comedian, sat in the other. All of the crew had taken the captain's course and all had passed, Jim would have a lot of critical eyes on him this trip.

Neo’s holographic avatar appeared in one of its predefined positions on the bridge, the avatar was that of a wizened, old Japanese gentleman with a goatee, dressed in a ships uniform. A uniform that only Daisy was actually wearing. He looked like he had come straight out of the first Karate Kid movie.

“Caprice has given us clearance to go as soon as the bay doors are open, we are just below one hundred millibar so it should be In three minutes,” said Neo.

“OK Neo,” Jim looked around, everyone was on the bridge for the departure, either at a workstation, or on one of the six large sofas carefully placed for visitors. “Take us to jump position at your own speed and keep it slow and steady, I don’t want anyone spilling their coffee on your nice new floors.”

“Will do,” nodded the Neo avatar. “Crew prepare for departure in three minutes.” He announced officially over the comm.

As the pressure gauge read zero millibars the ship slowly rotated horizontally on its landing cradle until the large hanger doors came directly into view. The inner and outer doors were already opening and the landing cradle started to move them out from the rim, extending into space. It was truly awe inspiring from their prime position in the bridge to see the inner ring of the station as it extended into the distance, curving up all the time until it became a distant line curving up and back over them.

The second the landing cradle released them they saw, but did not feel, the sensation of forward motion as the station rotated below them and Neo applied one gravity of vertical acceleration, all the time heading sideways away from the station and asteroid. The optical illusion on the screen showed a more sedate departure.

Neo [They do know I could have just jumped directly from the hanger bay, now we've negated the gravitational restriction, and constrained the magnetic field to only a few metres from the ship]
