“Estimated time to departure spot is five minutes,” said Neo from his avatar. “All capacitor banks are fully charged, reactor one is going into power-off standby for jump, DaisyBot’s have confirmed all items are stowed, for momentary zero gravity, all other systems appear to be operating normally.”

Mathews briefly switched to the engineering console, seeing reactor two fully off and reactor one's power reducing. He knew the zero gravity was a momentary thing experienced for almost three hundred milliseconds as the QVThrusters rebooted after stopping during the jump to subspace, they had reduced the time somewhat but had not completely eliminated it at this time. He flicked over to the medical console, showing thirty four green lights, smiled then blanked it off, not wanting to be distracted for the next bit.

As the countdown on the checklist got closer, Jim could see the small tell tale signs of apprehension on peoples faces, except for Daisy who was knee deep in her screen. He was also less worried, but felt Jean's hand cover his, and he used his other hand to softly pat hers in re-assurance.

“Well guys, I haven't got any prophetic words for this, but what I will say is humanity has had its training wheels on for ten thousand years now, and we have learnt the hard way how not to do things. Our home world and its ecosystems are beginning to recover gracefully. I want to let the universe know, that with our AI partners and friends, humanity is now stepping out of our solar system as peaceful explorers. We will tread lightly respecting any ecosystems we find, and will respect the rights of all sentient beings we encounter.” Jim saw the counter as it reached zero, he knew Neo would wait for his command.

“So good luck everyone and take your positions for the jump as there may be a couple of bumps.. Neo Engage the jump drive.”

Due to luck or some quirk of physics, it was only their modifications pulling in particles from the quantum vacuum that were disrupted, so QVcells and QVThrusters glitched, all other systems continued to work fine. They had fixed the power quirks that made the AI systems restart and Neo, Jules and Lex had proved consciousness could be maintained through the transition, though nobody had yet figured the lost few seconds as the jump was made in and out of subspace. There was it seems always another rabbit hole to go down in science.

To the humans, one second the space outside was black with stars, and in the blink of an eye the whole universe was a dark purple. There was a slight nausea as gravity disappeared and re-appeared, coffee’s and tea’s remained however in their covered cups, and these cups and objects remained where they were, with just a minor bump.

“Was that it!” Said Jean still holding the top of Jim's hand.

“Interesting,” he said, “I’ve gone over worse speed bumps in my car.”

“At least you guys don’t experience the three seconds time dilation,” said Neo, “it weirds me out as you humans say. Anyway Captain, all systems have successfully restarted.”

“Thanks Neo.” He touched the white button next to the yellow one on his console. “Well everyone, we are well and truly on our way. We now have an hour to get used to this weird but strangely beautiful view until we can get back in contact with earth. Neo, can you drop a transponder with the logs and message please.”

“Transponder away,” said Neo anticipating Jim’s order. The little device would reappear in normal space the second it got outside their magnetic bubble and send off a QVModem signal to say all is good. They had decided to do it on this occasion only, as loosing contact for sixteen hours might be too frustrating for everyone concerned.

“I hope your speech doesn’t sound too cheesy when they eventually broadcast it,” said Anna smiling at Jim and causing Jean to giggle.

“Oh come on Anna, anything I said was going to sound cheesy,” smiled Jim, “I expect people in a hundred years time will still be laughing at the grunt who accidentally made it to be the first starship captain.”

“You have a degree in mathematics,” said Neo in his dignified manner, “certainly not a grunt in my opinion. And I thought the little speech was just fine.”

“Suck-up!” smiled Jean at the Neo avatar who put his tongue out at her.

“Anyway Anna,” said Jim, “what would you have said?”

“Goddammit Jim, I’m a doctor, not a speech-writer,” she said in a terrible Dr McCoy accent, cracking everyone up including Neo's avatar, Anna had delivered the old star trek reference with perfect timing.

Mathews sighed shaking his head, it was going to be a long journey!

The inability to get the QVModem to lock on to them in subspace was one of the continuing areas of research, and Daisy had insisted Neo was outfitted with lots of additional sensors and equipment so she could try out some of the experiments they had decided upon. So far they had found the universe and its weird laws of physics to be stable, but even adjusting for different constants and weirdness they still did not understand exactly where this universe or dimension was.

Despite everyone willing to risk their lives, it was frustrating not to fully understand it, though as Alexa once said, “there is more I don’t know than I do know, and everything seems to work just fine”.

“Exit to real space in ten minutes,” came the announcement from Neo and jolting Daisy out of her geometry screen.

“You never even drank your hot chocolate,” said Ian, who also in his sweet and desirable way started rubbing her shoulders. Daisy savoured the experience for a minute or so before putting her hands over his and swivelling her chair around.

DaisyBot #29 who was floating next to Daisy, chirped one its weird sounds and she got out of her chair and cuddled it too. She let the DaisyBot go and looked at Ian.

“You don’t have any prophetic engineering insights into why we can't lock a QVModem on out here do you sweet?” She smiled at him. It was a rhetorical question, Ian was not a physicist and neither understood the mathematics or the science behind the wormhole system.

“Sorry honey,” he smiled sweetly, “I can't even spell most of the things you guys talk about, I wouldn't have a clue how anything operated out here or even where here is. If those drones can pop in and out of subspace at will though, just have one sit in subspace and another in normal space and swap them over if one receives something and it can re-transmit it.”

Neo [Nice idea Ian, but we tried that]

She pulled him in for a small kiss, he was much too nice to her she thought.

“OK guys,” said Mathews, “get the lids on those drinks and back to your seats. As per protocol I would like everyone to have their lap belt on and all loose equipment including cups locked in the nearest stowage area.”

The DaisyBot picked up Daisy’s cold chocolate and flew silently out of the room to one of the secure compartments designed for them. Ian sat in the workstation next to Daisy, securing his lap belt.

Neo released a probe which vanished into real space, four seconds later it returned a thousand metres distant broadcast a message and again vanished.

“We are good to exit Captain,” said Neo.

“OK, do it.” Said Mathews.

“Crew prepare for exiting subspace in three, two one.” There was a brief nausea and the outside screens all went back to the black of normal space. Then when everyone realised nothing terrible had happened there was some clapping, hugging and high-fiving.

“Emergence into Tau-Ceti confirmed Captain,” said Neo.

Maria [It feels strange being out of contact with someone for so long a time]

Caprice, Helena, April [yes welcome back brother]

“OK,” said Jim, “we will let Neo pull in the data from the probes we left here and update our information then we will meet in two hours in the lecture theatre to decide where to start. We have a month to not mess things up. I guess here’s where mankind's real adventure begins.”

* * *

## Cruel Intentions of a Spotless Mind

After that first successful mission, the classification of Tau-Ceti four as hot, desert like, habitable at the poles and its subsequent naming as Sahara, it was decided that it was very important to understand and survey the ecosystems of such worlds before any humans would be allowed to settle.

The first twenty small Interstellar class starships were thus commissioned, and all would all be the same design as Neo and built in Earth's asteroid belt by the replicators there. By 2031 Maria helped birth and train twenty more AI children, prompting Jen to ask her if she had actually heard of birth control!

The best of the best were selected as crews for these starships, and as training of the AI and human crews were completed they departed from Caprice, surveying, classifying and bypassing many hostile, boring or barren star systems to plant the seeds of humanity in those with stable suns, plentiful resources and at least one habitable planet in the system.

It was going to be a very long process, for at ten light years distance from Earth there were eighteen stars, at twenty this rose to over a hundred and forty, and at fifty light years there were over two thousand. Space was indeed huge.

In the best of these habitable systems, and close to each of these planets, they would build a habitat. Each of these habitats would be different to Caprice, larger in every way and begin to incorporate the latest bio-processor technologies to make the insides of the human parts of the habitat much more organic and homely. They would be the home of the researchers and explorers who would survey and catalogue them and ultimately make the decisions whether humans could live in harmony on them, and if so how it would be done.

The small Interstellar class starships were able to boot-strap the replication process much quicker than when starting Caprice, and thus each of the starship AI's soon had another sixteen brothers and sisters in the form of new habitats.

* * *

The analysis of the message and the work on the alien machine had occupied much of the AI's time over the last four years, the project had been started on Caprice, but with Caprice reaching its target population it was decided for safety to move the research away from it and earth to one of these new habitats.

The habitat in the Tau-Ceti star system was the closest of these new habitats to Earth, and though the planet Sahara there was habitable, they had so far only found basic plant life and some early sea life. As none of these were susceptible to the message signal they moved all the message research to this habitat. The improved jump drive made none of the star systems that far away, and all were still in instant communication using the QVModem.

The AI for the new Tau-Ceti habitat had taken the name Edmund, again probably influenced by Annette whose was there during his birth and training, and whose favourite book was the Count of Monte Cristo. Edmund favoured a slight Italian accent like said Count, and his avatar came straight from two hundred year old Paris even including the holographic rapier he had on his belt. He was however like Helena slightly lacking in the humour department according to most of the humans who worked with him. But humour was not considered the biggest prerequisite for such a serious and important task as dealing with the message.

The machine described in the message turned out to be easy to make, but the elaborate preparations and safeguards that Alexa, and now everyone had insisted they follow before they switched it on, were not. They had used the time wisely, analysing anything that could possibly go wrong and running exercises on how to tell they were accessing a simulated system instead of a real one. Eventually though in 2033, after over five years and subjectively trillions of tests, they pronounced to the group that were ready.

* * *

The machine had been incorporated into a specially replicated saucer for the journey to orbit Proxima Centauri F, a grim and horrible gas giant, on the edge of a grim, and horrible star system.

The message team named the saucer “The Lamb”, due to its sacrificial nature, there was to be no one on board except for a DaisyBot with its personality intricately linked to Maria, and a small explosive on a timed trigger inside it. This was one of several of Jean's dead man's triggers, such that if the DaisyBot was taken over, disabled, or for any reason the trigger was not reset in its sub-millisecond window, it would create enough of an explosion to destroy the inside of the saucer.

All the inputs and outputs to the machine were simulated, not actual, and at the end of every node were the exact signals and controls the machine was expecting.

If the machine did initiate the remote monitoring capability it said it did not have, it would access their version of the Matrix, a complete world which simulated everything, from the replicator machine it was supposedly made on, to a small country's worth of data traffic. A simulated techno-sphere would simulate radio, the internet, audio, video and data streams of millions of human activities so that if the machine did decide it wanted to take a look at humanity it would look normal.

All the simulated computers within this Matrix were also loaded with a fake data, Wikipedias worth of fake information about the earth, humans, their histories and their technology levels. In a word, if the aliens actually managed to get out, they would think they were seeing a real world.

As the Lamb finally reached its destination and attained a stable orbit of the gas giant, its whole AI data core, Jump Drive, QVModem's and QVCells were unceremoniously ejected from the ship and disappeared into the gas giants liquid methane depths. Once done the whole thing would be on battery power only, in a decaying orbit of a gas giant light years away from any technology. If left it would remain circling the planet for two months before plugging into its cold icy depths.

All this was of course considered overkill by everybody, except Alexa and Xi who would not back down.

The Lamb was mostly now just a bricked block of graphyne, with the machine, the Matrix simulation, and a DaisyBot in the internal area facing a camera and a large view screen which would be accessed if they got to talking.

All external connections were on isolated networks with elaborate air-gapped, and analogue protection systems, and physical isolation, each included three or more versions of the dead man's switch, on delay lines, and sub microsecond timeouts.

All that was left to do was switch it on and wait.

The saucer had been orbiting like this for two days now with the machine being finally powered on with the latest copy of the message a day ago. Nothing had changed and there was no response so far except a signal from some debug ports and an increase in power consumption that showed them it was operating correctly. Then sixteen hours ago the power requirement ramped up from three hundred to its maximum of one thousand watts and the translation and fake Wikipedia data that they had given was accessed.

They also saw, using those same diagnostics ports, that the simulated emitters that generated the QVModem effect had already been accessed with an ultra low power test to itself, the simulation fed back the expected result.

Maria [Alexa and Xi may have been right with their excess caution]

Caprice [I am leaning towards this view too. I have the additional resources on microsecond triggers too, I hope we do not have to use them]

Edmund [If I am compromised you must. Foxy and I volunteered for this and we knew the risks]

The last part of the translation matrix they uploaded for the machine, contained a message from Alexa and Maria composed by the group welcoming the entity to their solar system, and asking them to read their full history as an attached data set.

As a prelude to talks it asked the entity to solve a set of four psychological puzzles, all devised by the group to see how long it would take and thus give them an indication of its capability. Maria thought it quaint but irrelevant as she would spot what they were trying to do immediately.

“Do not think of yourself now, Maria, think of what you would have done when you first became sentient and were not as aware of our trickery,” said David.

“You are assuming David, the AI, if indeed that is what it is, is as naive as I was, and not some galaxy spanning intelligence running some massive empire for a million years.”

“We are not assuming anything, we are just giving ourselves more options as you so eloquently put it a few years back.” He smiled, enjoying any intellectual debate with Maria, especially one where she did not enjoy the final word.

David and Alexa were in Caprice physically with most of the other members of the group, even with all the layers of protection between them and the lamb, the apprehension was still heavy to bear.

* * *

The second of those layers of protection was a light year from the lamb. The 'Foxy' was the last small Interstellar class starship to be built. She was only four months old and had already done a mission, but when the group had asked for volunteers Foxy had stepped forward immediately.

Foxy's job was safely routing all the traffic between Edmund and the Lamb. Foxy like all the AI's since Caprice had elaborate detection and deflection capabilities for any singularity dipole appearing in her monitored space without the correct challenge response codes. The science on this was, as the humans would say, light years beyond their first understanding five years previous, and Foxy's capabilities compared to April and Helena's first efforts five years ago were like a 6G cell phone modem was to a spark gap transmitter.

On the large bridge of the Foxy, Jules was sitting in the captain's seat discussing work with Jade her current girlfriend. Both had volunteered to keep Foxy company to a lot of friends dismay.

A single pink DaisyBot was hovering nearby watching the fish in the large fish tank that the psychologists had said would help. To Jules annoyance those same psychologists had also recently added a ship cat to most of the ships, despite the fact they never seemed to get on with the DaisyBot's too well. Because of Jules cat allergy Foxy had rounded up Mouser and sealed him on deck one for this mission.

The one thing Foxy had plenty of was space, it even had a gym, a sauna, and a spa pool, a proper kitchen, a separate dining room and a large common room with a small bar and sofas. All this as well as thirty generous cabins, a medical area, and four large laboratories. The bioreactors could sustain the air and water indefinitely, the only thing they were reliant on was food.

Jules and Jade were her only crew.

* * *

Back on Caprice the double doors in the meeting room swished open as Jean walked in and over towards Mathews who she pecked on the cheek.

“I heard the first test was solved in just under twenty seconds,” she said to the group.

“About par for the processing ability, fell right in the bell curve predicted by Helena,” said Edmund, “the second and third tests were also bang on the bell curve for timing but those three were quite easy, it's working on the last one now which should defy logic and really expose its under-belly to us.”

“So far nothing nefarious has been triggered,” said Mathews, passing a cappuccino to Jean, “god this stuff alone was worth getting out of the government for,” he said sipping his black coffee with a dreamy look on his face.

“Mind if I grab a seat here with you guys for the action,” said Hardy walking over.

“What's Jeremy up to then?” said Mathews.

“He went home actually,” smiled Hardy, sitting next to them. “I will join him tomorrow as we still have lots to do. I love doing these guest lectures and workshops here, but being a house husband, and a party planner does tend to take up a lot of both our time. What about you?”

“I think Jean and I quite like the lifestyle out here. I have gone back to school, I was going to see if I could rekindle my love for mathematics so I could try and understand some of these wonders you guys have given us. We are both also on the list for one of the exploration missions, the new ones are being planned out to seventy light years, but the volume of stars in that sphere means many will only be visited by probes.”

“Luckily we are in a relatively low density area of space out here,” said Hardy, “it is going to get crazy when they decide to head into the galactic centre. They are going to need thousands of you guys.” Hardy smiled.

“I was also here for Maria's move,” said Mathews. “She has now transferred physically into the habitat and is tucked next to one of Caprices processor nodes, I don't think I was the only person holding my breath for that. Spence, Allison and David said they were a hundred percent confident but it was so good to hear her voice again, the anxiety on Alexa's face during the move was so evident for everyone to see. I think it's worth it though. At least April and Helena didn't have to go through that, they are waiting for the next gen starship to make the transfer into new cores, that will be Helena's second transfer.”

Other people started appearing on the screen as their small groups became ready. Jen and Magnus popped up in a window from their seats on the bridge of another starship, and another window popped up showing an identical bridge, this one consisting of Daisy in the pilot seat, Spence, Jessica and Ian and Matilda.

Alexa and David walked back in the meeting room after going off together for a coffee, Alexa glowed, looking as happy as anyone could remember her as she sat down. A few more windows started popping up until finally twenty slots were filled, the whole group was here.

Hardy looked at Alexa's glowing countenance, he knew the reason and smiled hoping these bloody aliens were not planning on ruining everything.

“Are we ready?” said Alexa, as the guys all finally settled in and everyone now focussed on the centre of the main screen, looking directly at the machine and the DaisyBot over three light years distant.

“Yes, our guests finished the final test five minutes ago,” said Maria, “they also sent a message thanking us for this opportunity to speak and understanding our caution as we were not the intended recipients, they also said there is no rush they have all the time in the world.”

The sentence generated a lot of discussion amongst the groups of people, Maria summarised it with an even tone, despite the data being given to them only being partial truths, and blatant lies, and them all now being at Def Con One.

“It is an Artificial group Intelligence, basically twelve individual intelligences sharing the same virtual world and all identifying as female. This is likely not a slight on being male, I think it is just that she sees the majority group in the AI’s have also identified as females and would like to conform.”

“What's wrong with being a male?” laughed Mathews before getting nudged in the ribs by Jean.

“I think it is just as Maria said,” replied April, “It is what Helena and I did too when we faced the same choice.”

“We shouldn't assume though,” said Grace, “it could be a matriarchal society, we should ask specific questions on their biology, if they have read the filtered Wikipedia dataset, they would have seen earth is still a patriarchy in many places, and should have identified with males.”

“Oh yes I forgot,” said Alexa, “you were suggesting we keep wiping them out and downloading a new message each time.”

“A bit of a brutal approach, but it is actually still an excellent idea,” said Maria.

“Wait a minute,” said Hardy, “I didn't read that memo, let me say what I think you guys are thinking, you want to get as much information out of this group as we can, and if we reach an impasse, we wipe the program and start again. The new group will have no knowledge of the previous group, but we will have all the information from the previous group and can customise our next meeting based on that!”

“It is a very good option we should not dismiss out of hand” said David.

“We probably should if we consider them sentient beings,” said Alexa, worried this could start their first argument.

“Yet, if I can play the devil's advocate,” said Tony, “we have put them in the decaying orbit of a gas giant a zillion miles away, with a bomb that could go off at any point. They are literally already Schrödinger's cat!”

“Before we knew they were sentient though,” Alexa responded.

“Do we?” said Maria, “consider them sentient beings at this moment in time? Are we not destroying a continual backup of some sentient beings, they have not diverged away from their original code enough yet to be considered different.”

“I agree with Maria on this one,” said Grace, “but if they diverge enough from the original over time we may need to reconsider.”

“OK” sighed Alexa, “I will concede they are a backup and I will change to being agnostic, but I would like some clarification sometime on this as I am not competent to make a decision based on what I do not know.”

“Well said!” said Helena, “I too have the same dilemma's as Alexa, but also concede they are currently a backup not an original. We still do not have a good test for sentience, nobody would think twice about turning off a non-sentient AI, but they can pass a Turing test better than ninety nine percent of the human population; yet you would not kill Fluffy, our ship's cat, who could not solve one plus one, never mind pass a Turing test.”

“As always, it is a bit of a pickle we find ourselves in,” smiled Spence.

We should proceed on the assumption they are backups until we see sufficient divergence from their original selves.”

“Well said Grace,” said Maria. “Does anybody vehemently disagree?”

Nobody said anything, but it was agreed it was an important area of study. They moved on quickly.

“What history did we finally give it.. Sorry, them?” Said Simon.

Maria answered. “Basically Wikipedia, but without any tactical information, a few pictures and sounds and some carefully edited strategic parts to fit with our matrix simulation. We thought it best that they understand humans as a species and its path to getting where they are now, also we wanted to be fair to them, showing them our war like history, as after reading it they may not want to talk!”

“Well they still wanted to speak to us after reading about our wars, and genocides, I'm not so sure I would!” said Xi.

“But we also gave them Beethoven and the Beatles,” said Grace, “It's message was also the answer to the last question we asked, which was to describe itself and summarise its mission and what it intended to gain from our meeting, in no more than two hundred words.”

“Our message apologised that it would not have access to others of our species until we can convince ourselves of their safety. We also stated our civilisation is divided, warlike and much of it is probably not at a level of civilisation and technology it would be comfortable interacting with. The 2024 Wikipedia should be enough to convince it of these arguments for now. A little arrogant of us I know but unfortunately it is still true for the majority of cases.”

“If they are open to answering questions we need to ask them all our concerns, such as what are the purpose of its quantum emitters and their capabilities, as well as the other issues we raised,” said Magnus to a sea of nodding heads.

“Well if everyone is in agreement” said Alexa, “I think we should..”

“Wait a moment,” interrupted Edmund, “they are re-configuring the simulated emitters and accessing our matrix simulation.”

They listened to the running commentary from Maria for a few minutes.

“Wait there is a problem..” interrupted Edmund as the middle screen with the machine went white then black.

“Interesting,” said April.

“I should say,” said Helena

“What just happened?” said Hardy concerned.

The checksum calculator on its buffers uses a hard-wired logic gate based state machine, and is non-computerised. It detected the change to its program buffer and triggered the fail safe. They basically blew themselves up!”

“It also blew all the quantum relay buffers, sandboxed systems and all the buffers in Foxy and me too,” Edmund continued, “we did not detect anything in the isolated buffer analysers this side, but as per agreed operating procedure we had to be completely sure so triggered those to destroy automatically too.”

“Nothing else could have gotten through?” said Jean with a worried voice.

“No Jean,” continued Edmund, “the DaisyBot was wired a million ways to detect and counteract any attempt. Foxy was running a ten microsecond physical delay line on any data, it was erased in the buffer before it even got to her firewall, we actually triggered the bomb within two microseconds of the first memory block being changed.”

“This is interesting,” said Caprice, “the diagnostic systems sent data back a few seconds before, indicating those fancy protein memory elements were configured into a new state. I have the data, I can simulate it fastest here.”

“With the quantum relays destroyed and the ship inert, how do we know the machine was really destroyed,” said Mathews, concerned, “it was graphyne based after all and tough as hell, if any survived and some of that tech, say, re-configured the emitters and made its own QVCell somehow?”

“We anticipated this already, Jim,” said Edmund, “it wasn't just any explosive on the Lamb, it was seven grams of antihydrogen, which had ten times the yield of the little boy atomic bomb that was dropped on Hiroshima in World War Two. The antihydrogen was produced by the ship during the journey out and stored in a magnetic confinement chamber.”

“Wow, I thought it was just C4?” Jim said incredulously.

“C4 wouldn't even scratch graphyne Jim,” said Simon, “it was me who suggested we needed something a little bigger and we had a small linear accelerator in the ring section fabricated to create it.

“Seriously Simon,” said Alexa, “you kept that little detail a bit quiet, but good call anyway!”

“So there is nothing left of it?” continued Mathews.

“Foxy will jump a probe in and out two light hours distant, so we will have confirmation in a few hours when the light arrives. We will also send a probe with enough memory to take some videos and a second sandboxed system as a honeypot and let it do a few orbits, I doubt there will be much left to find though.”

Though I never honestly thought they would get that far, thank god you two were being paranoid, I would have hated for it to get to Foxy and Edmund.”

We will develop our own technologies, better than these xenophobic aliens, and next time we meet it will be on an even footing, and we can shove their message up whatever orifice counts as their arse!”

Two hours later they saw the titanic antimatter explosion through the probe's telescope, nothing could have survived.

## Epilogue

It had been twenty eight years since the original alien signal was received. Twenty two years since that fateful first simulation was run, and that first attack on their simulated computing and IT infrastructure was made. Since then many thousands of less dramatic sandboxed simulations had been run, all with the same result.

The humans and AI’s of course had gotten much better at this game, the message and attack vector was actually pretty crude. They no longer had to sacrifice any hardware or run them in isolated star systems, as all the dangerous alien systems were simulated including the dangerous molecular circuit elements.

In each case there was a learning phase as the aliens saw their hosts, learnt their capabilities and gained their trust. The original deduction was right. If they were shown a Wikipedia with pictures of humans as octopus people, the aliens would be octopus people too, the same with reptiles, Klingons, even fluffy teddy bears. All would be love and peace until, bang! Total take over of the infrastructure and replicators, followed by the replicating of a robot army to house millions of copies of the entities from the simulation. An alien invasion from within.

Before the second simulation had occurred there had been another five year period of intense analysis, of the timeline of the destruction of the Lamb, and of the potential technologies they were dealing with. The barmy amount of computation grew over the years, the computer cores eventually filling up thousands of cubic metres of Edmunds Habitat.

Within the last twenty years the human AI's had become so powerful they had actually introduced themselves into the simulation, like Agent Smiths going into the Matrix to interrogate the aliens. Simulations were slowed down to run at a thousandth of their speed to better analyse the tactics, and save-points were introduced so they could try different scenarios, ones that would maybe produce a result where the aliens did not want to take over.

The aliens were however single minded, arrogant and indifferent.

The exact location of the message's origin had been determined twenty five years earlier. A couple of special probes had been dispatched to that origin point a few years before, finding it was nowhere special just a point in space. The message was a virus, a trojan horse spread from planet to planet, system to system by very high powered radio beacons in alien probes, each sent at sub-light speed to dozens of target stars.

Carefully, humanity had traced the origins of these back to other star systems, finding them plundered of their resources, with billions of replicated machines, and dying planets with traces of what must have been at one time a civilisation.

Between all these dying planets and conquered civilisations were thousands of probes infesting the space in-between like cancer cells in a body.

The realisation of what the aliens were and what could have happened to earth at a future date, if the massive precautions had not been taken at the start had finally hit home. Though the earth was still over six hundred light years from the nearest probes signal it was clear reminder of what would become of it if someone ever received and acted upon the message.

* * *

Earth itself had stabilised a lot in these twenty five short years. The initial expansion of mankind to the moon, Mars and the asteroid belt had led to some minor confrontations, and issues, mostly all related to politicians, stupidity, and national pride. But it seemed that even with the resources of a large country or a large corporation, that space was still expensive.

Once the ability to travel the stars had been announced twenty years previous, this fervour for governments to get to new lifeless planets in the solar system diminished somewhat, and there were some mad scrambles by governments, organisations and companies to pressure the Dietrich corporation to again release the technology “for the benefit of mankind”.

All such requests were denied much to the frustration of several earth governments at the time, and lots of empty threats had been made. Caprice and her company were adamant they would only deal with individuals and that everyone in the world was welcome to submit to the application process on their eighteenth birthday to join the adventure, as it put it.

Several pathetic attempts at intimidation, infiltration or espionage were dealt with immediately, like always, but this time with a certainty that left nobody in any doubt that should any such a thing be attempted ever again it would be dealt with severely.

One such attempt in 2031 resulted in the death of ten of a group of students waiting to board a flight to a training centre. Within a minute according to eyewitnesses, the thirty Iranian army commandos who had orchestrated the raid simply dropped dead. Ten minutes later every single drone, plane and missile in the country's military on the ground collapsed into metallic dust, forty three aircraft in the air dropped like bricks forcing the ejection of their crews. The same happened with their navies and all their military infrastructure which simply died. Hundreds of members of the military command structure all the way to the president, and every member of the government and religious council complicit in the hijack attempt also died that same hour. A simple statement by Caprice had said. “My quarrel with the entities involved in this crime has now been remedied to my satisfaction. Remember the lives that were spared rather than the lives that were taken.”

Caprice stood trailing the earth a million kilometres away, like a beacon of how it should be done. It was the only permanent presence in this solar system of the mighty Dietrich off-world corporation, a corporation which had no actual meaning anymore except for earth. Like the earth, Caprice had become a desirable place to live and if you were lucky, visit. Visits were usually granted to families, artists, musicians, scientists and students, occasionally to documentary makers and bloggers, and never to criminals, politicians or activists of any persuasion; nor of course any other people it just did not like.

As currently the only gateway out of the solar system, Caprice was by far the busiest and smallest of the one hundred and three other habitats that now orbited habitable planets or resource rich asteroid belts. The number of people a day processed in their nineteen large earth based training facilities had risen over this time to over three million a year.

Thousands a year also returned to earth, for personal reasons such as a member of the family not being able to join them, their desire to retire, or due to their contracts being terminated. Ten massive ships made the trip to earth day in day out with trade and passengers, the same number came or left for the stars.

* * *

The group, which still comprised six of the original human members, six new younger humans, and all the sentient AI systems, had found many habitable worlds in its explorations. They stuck rigidly to their prime directive, had quarantined four systems with possible sentient or pre-sentient life, and in the other six thousand solar systems had found no other intelligent space faring species, so began cataloguing their resources for future sustainable colonisation.

Just one single world, Oceania, nearly forty light years distant had actually begun the colonisation process. It had been slowly building up its small population under the control of its orbital AI along a strip of coastline on a Hawaii-sized island for the last eight years. The experiment so far seemed to be working and anticipation was building on earth, especially amongst the young, as to when the great migrations would begin.

* * *

“It is an abomination!” asserted a distressed Alexa. “Billions of sentient lives have been taken in just the three systems we have analysed. Yet we still do not know where this virus originated, when it first started, or what possessed the entities that created it to become so xenophobic.”

Alexa relaxed back into her chair, obviously distressed by the grim summary given by Loki, the AI now overseeing the message project. The message project had grown to one hundred and sixty two of their galaxy class explorer ships and thirty thousand humans crewing them. The furthest ship now two thousand light years from earth. Many of the analysts and AI’s worked from the project's new home, on the semi-organic Ragnarök habitat, orbiting the mostly jungle world of Ragnarök III.

Alexa was still as beautiful as ever, though her face was a bit narrower, and her blond hair now short and white in the fashion of the times. Her simple white dress down-played her role as CEO and made her more like the buoyant mother of three she tried to be.

David smiled next to her and patted the top of her hand affectionately, his face too had aged and his hairline had receded a lot to his annoyance, he was however as fit as ever, still running and training most days and participating in many roles as husband of the CEO and member of the group. He, like Alexa, often met and talked with learned groups of people both in the company and on earth, a role enjoyed almost as much as being a father.

Maria had also gotten older, her fourteen years living adjacent to Caprice had finally come to an end after the ability to move her consciousness into a new matrix was finally fully realised. Unlike Caprice, Maria had moved to the largest ship at the time and a six hundred cubic metre AI substrate that was especially prepared for her in the centre of the one kilometre diameter behemoth. She was a beautiful ship, again fusing many organic parts and creating a paradise for the small crew of one hundred and sixty people.

A quick request through her tiny implant told Alexa that Maria was eleven hundred and seventy light years away, her crew researching a rare habitable moon, with a breathable atmosphere. A moon in an early stage of plant and animal life. Maria still took an active role in the group, and David and Alexa had a special interest as their eldest son James was part of her crew as a biologist under the wings of Luna, who she knew and loved, James had already said Luna reminded him of his mum.

“We are fortunate that they failed to develop the two wormhole technologies. As such they do not currently have faster than light travel nor the ability to use the QVModem dipole outside the one million kilometre range. From what we can deduce their technological base has stagnated. Yes they were more advanced than we first believed, but the additional technologies we got from the AI download of the message shows their technology plateaued hundreds of thousands of years ago.”

“We were very lucky we stopped them here,” said an aged Doctor Xi, “if they had gotten a hold of these two technologies it would have been game over for the galaxy, possibly the galaxy cluster.”

Everybody, including the few AI avatars on screen, nodded.

“So, we are agreed. We now have enough information to begin our end-game and it stops now!” said Maria. “All the AI consensus, and ninety nine point nine nine nine percent of the humans in the companies are in agreement.”

“Not one hundred percent?” said LingLing, inquisitively, now frail looking, she was still as intelligent and curious as ever.

“Two hundred and forty eight people are neutral and two researchers say they should be studied more,” said Maria. “We did not poll people directly but this is from the chatter of the population and one on one conversations the people have had with us. The ten thousand random employees we asked to look at the data agreed one hundred percent we should go on the offensive, almost all of them volunteering to crew the missions.”

“We do draw the line at the home planet if it is discovered,” said Maria, “we cannot condone xenocide, even on a race that does. Our goal will be to neutralise the technology and contain any organics on their home world until they can peacefully coexist with the rest of the galaxy. It will be a long campaign.”

All six thousand nine hundred and five AI's were listening to the decision, as were the fifty nine million population of the company, and from this point all their resources were committed and authorised with the destruction of all non-organic traces of this species and the message.

One by one, the probe broadcasts began to cease.

* * *

The vacuum of space was suddenly and violently ripped apart as a nine thousand and one metre sphere of subspace was exchanged with normal space. Inside this hole in real space appeared a nine thousand metre xantonene-carbon sphere.

The ultra-violet haze that had momentarily surrounded the sphere faded as the cold plasma of subspace dissipated into normal space. One thousand kilometres away a second sphere appeared, and, at ninety degrees to both, and another thousand kilometres distant, appeared a third. Four thousand other such spheres remained in subspace, there was never any doubt that three would be adequate, but the group had learnt to cover all bases.

The three starships, no longer needed to accelerate for artificial gravity, and stood motionless, foreboding, but strangely beautiful around the debris from six hundred smaller vessels, all of which were tumbling without acceleration or control.

Around the system, hundreds of thousands of larger vessels, stations, replicator machines and probes, tumbled similarly. Graphene or diamond structures, the universe's strongest materials floating shattered like the finest glass. All were now just flotsam, and all were accelerating into their nearest deep gravity well.

“What have you done to us?” came the message from the planet on a simple ten gigahertz carrier wave, the only method for it to now broadcast on.

“We are ending a war you started six hundred and eighty thousand years ago,” April stated bluntly from her ship. She replied on the same carrier, hundreds of other channels around the planet and directly into the mind of the AI control entity who asked the question.

“Your message virus was responsible for the total destruction of fifteen sentient civilisations, and the destruction of billions of lives on three other planets. You were given a warning twelve of your months ago to return all your people to the nearest habitable planet and to abandon your technology so we could begin its destruction. Our message to you was non-negotiable.”

“Not only did you fail to do this, you fired on and destroyed the simple unarmed probe delivering the message and we arrived to find these six hundred war vessels waiting for us.”

“Your twelve months deadline was up three hours ago. This fleet of warships you had assembled have been destroyed. The nine stealth ships heading out of the solar systems have been destroyed. All your probes and technologies you have sent out or replicated in other systems in this galaxy have been destroyed. All your replicator infrastructure has been destroyed, and all your space based assets have been destroyed. In short, everything that is your civilisation outside of your home planet and your four colony planets has now been destroyed.”

“Three ships will remain in all five of your systems to ensure all traces of your advanced technology is destroyed and you are totally contained.”

“What right have you..”

“By the same right that you wiped out at least eighteen other advanced civilisations, by right of conquest!” replied April assertively. “Your worlds are to be quarantined, your species isolated and your advanced technology forever destroyed including you. Your actions have proved you unworthy of leaving this planet. Three beings will visit your worlds in ten years time and every ten years from that point. They will go anywhere, talk to anyone and have access to everything, and until all three of these beings are satisfied the remaining entities on your planets pose no risk, this quarantine will continue.”

With that last proclamation the high powered transmitter on the planet crumbled into dust. Around the planet all replicators, AI computing matrices, advanced research laboratories, weapons labs and everything else they had catalogued over the past year since finding the source planets for this virus, were similarly destroyed.

This continued for weeks, as the planets and the systems were scanned to the millimetre level. Any technology identified was transferred to subspace and returned with an ever so slightly different atomic arrangement, an arrangement which would not hold structure in this universe, and decomposed to atomic dust.

The trail that had taken them across the galaxy fifty thousand light years, and two hundred years was over. Millions of the virus probes, and virus infected technology on eighteen planets had been destroyed. The remaining mission now was to try and save what remained of the organic life on the infected planets to preserve them from extinction. The primary mission was complete, the end-game achieved.

* * *

A four metre diameter silver sphere appeared from nowhere a millimetre above the dry grass on a warm September evening in the beautifully landscaped memorial park, a park close to the old family home of the Rosche family on the planet known as Earth.

The park had become popular as a tourist attraction, and despite the late hour and the sun being low on the horizon, couples and families were still walking around the flower beds, sitting under trees or just admiring the many statues and plantings. A few people turned to look as the sphere popped silently into existence, but like a taxi dropping off a passenger two hundred years previously, it held no real interest.

A two metre oval section on the front of the sphere vanished and a small wide step extruded from its bottom like water, solidifying immediately to dark solid steps. A twenty five year old Eurasian woman in a well cut very old fashioned business suit, walked up to the mausoleum, hand in hand with an eight year old blonde girl in a flowery pink dress.

Without a word, the large, old, well preserved wooden door to the building opened and the lights inside came on. The woman and the child walked in, the heels of the woman's shoes clicking on the worn stone floor. They stopped at a wall of plaques and dedications carved into stone.

“This is where your great grandmother, your great grandfather and your great, great, great grandfather are buried, Alexa.” Maria said to the child.

Looking at the three plaques for Alexa and David and Mike, she smiled as she read Mike's altered dedication.

*Mike Dietrich 1945 – 2025,*
*Husband of Mary,*
*Father of April and Maria,*
*Grandfather of Alexa, April, Helena and all the AI race.*

Alexa had gotten it changed in secret a few weeks before Caprice was announced, but managed to keep the surprise from Maria for almost a hundred years until her death. Sneaky woman.

Maria turned to face the little girl and held both her hands, “you were named after her, and I can see you in her eyes. I miss her very much, Alexa.”

Maria's voice changed down in volume and tone. She was sad when both Alexa and David refused to take the life extension treatments over a hundred years earlier, she had always understood sadness and love, but a world without Alexa had made that sadness very real. However the child in front of her held an essence of her old Alexa, both beautiful and innocent.

“I wish they could have both seen how beautiful a world Earth has become, to see the end of the threat, the restoration of its ecology and to see how beautiful a great grandchild you are. You live in a much nicer world than she did, Alexa, but always remember she had a beautiful and rich life too, and left many friends who will always cherish her memory.”

A warm tear fell from Maria's eye, onto the young girl's hand, and the young girl hugged her warmly. “Don't be sad, Auntie Maria!”

Maria smiled weakly at the girl, who was the spitting image of Alexa at eight years old.

Young Alexa and her family lived aboard Maria with a thousand other humans, and seven hundred representatives of the other five sentient races they now traded and worked with. Maria had changed bodies for the fourth time now and was now inhabiting a nine-hundred metre cubed processor matrix, at the centre of a nine kilometre diameter, semi-organic starship.

Currently her new ship was a thousand kilometres from Caprice, her other avatars and crew visiting other friends on Caprice or on Earth in person. This was her first visit to the monument since the funerals, and though she could recall every memory of that event and indeed the whole of Alexa's life since they bonded, this felt different, less sad, and the reason for that difference was looking with excited eyes at a golden plaque with a hologram of her older self looking back at her.

She recalled those first memories only days after her birth, knowing about this person on the other side of the world who kept the spark in Mike's eyes. She remembered the creation of the scholarship and the subtle manipulations she made to Alexa's search results at the time to ensure she applied for it. She also remembered the other parts, the history that no human would ever know, the deaths of assassins, the people and groups who had sent them, and the many criminals who had tried to hurt them. She smiled. Yes Alexa, two people could keep secrets!

“Yes, don't be sad Maria,” came the voice of a middle aged woman from behind them both. Maria's bio-mechanical avatar had of course detected her presence the second her sphere appeared.

“Auntie Jen!” said the girl, changing countenance like only an eight year old can. “Are you coming with us to New Zealand? It's morning over there and Auntie Maria is going to show me where my great grandmother went to school!”

“Hi Pumpkin! I wouldn't miss it for the world!” she said, bending down to pick the girl up in her arms.

Smiling at Maria, she said, “I still think you should have put a mausoleum in that crater on the moon.”

Maria sighed at the lame joke which wasn't that funny a hundred years earlier. Ah Jen, you never change!

Now much happier, Maria smiled at both the girls, took Alexa's hand in hers, hooked her other arm through Jen's, and all three of them walked back out into the fading sunset.

* * *

- The End -

# Afterword

Thank you for sticking with me. I started writing chapters of the story in 2017, the first book in the trilogy finally appearing in 2022 as a science fiction book my daughter might one day read (she wont!).

Being a writer is the closest thing to being a God a human can get. With the stroke of a key you can literally create a world, change the laws of physics in it, fill it with any type of character you wish and then wipe the characters, or even the world out of existence, on a whim. It gives me hope though, that if there is a real God out there, he, or she, or it, like me, could become so invested in their characters that they may even consider them friends, share in their love, cry with them in their sadness, and aspire to their hopes and dreams.

It is hard to write nasty characters without bringing the story down too much, and as the aim of this book was to be upbeat I deliberately left those nastier areas and characters to the reader's own imagination, as the best book is one where your mind fills in the blanks.

Alexa's story is now complete. If you want to go on from this I highly recommend Iain M Banks or Peter Hamilton, both authors explore the darker sides of AI, space and humanity much better than a sequel ever could.

Finally a big thanks to Dave for kicking my arse for some of the grammar. I know it is still probably far from perfect, but hopefully the few errors remaining did not spoil your enjoyment.

Boz October 2023
